author: eeeeaaii
body:
Stacked on #388. This is the "only the last note plays, slowly" bug, and then the
right fix for it.

## What was wrong

```
MIDI start: cycleLen 4.000 lengthSeconds 4.000 events 6 startTime 0.000 now 15979.7
   send note 41 ch 1 at 0.000 -> onAt 0.0 (-15980.3ms from now)
   send note 38 ch 1 at 1.000 -> onAt 1000.0 (-14981.1ms from now)
   ...
```

Every message was timestamped ~16 seconds **in the past**, so the browser sent the
whole sequence at once — six note-on/note-off pairs back to back in a single burst —
then waited a cycle and did it again. Hence one audible note and a long gap.

`ctx.getOutputTimestamp()` answers `{contextTime: 0, performanceTime: 0}` until the
context has produced output, and `0 != undefined` is true, so the guard anchored
everything to zero.

Parsing was never involved — the sequence parsed correctly throughout, and the
note-off shortening was right too (995ms on the 1s notes, 495ms on the 0.5s ones).

## The fix

Requiring `performanceTime > 0` reaches the `performance.now()` fallback, and that
worked — but it is the wrong answer, because it is a **second clock**. Start a midi
sequence, start an audio loop later, and they would drift apart, which defeats the
point of a shared cycle.

So instead the audio clock is made to exist:

- **A silent keep-alive.** One second of silence, looping, through a gain of zero,
  started as soon as anything joins the cycle. The context keeps producing output,
  so `getOutputTimestamp` always has a real anchor and midi and audio are always
  scheduled against the same clock whichever starts first.
- **The first cycle waits for the clock** instead of firing on the next microtask
  against a context time of zero. `ctx.resume()` is async, so there was no way to be
  correct without waiting.
- **A suspended context is resumed** — its clock does not advance at all.
- **The fallback stays as a warned last resort.** It should never be reached now; if
  it is, the console says `no audio clock, midi timing will drift from audio`.

## Cost

Once anything has played, the audio device stays open for the session, because the
silent source never stops. That is the price of a clock that is always there.

## Not from this session

`contextTimeToPerformanceTime` has been this way since the midi cycle was built. It
only bites when a midi loop is the first thing to touch the audio system on a page,
which is exactly what testing midi on its own does — play any audio first and the
context has a valid anchor, which is why it worked before.

body:
### Motivation
- The editor exposes too many internal concepts and panels at once, obscuring the primary mascot-first workflow and reducing canvas focus. This change introduces task-focused workspaces to surface only the tools relevant to Create → Rig → Animate → Preview. 
- Preserve the existing engine, runtime and project schemas while making the UI approachable for non-technical users using progressive disclosure and human-friendly labels.

### Description
- Add a lightweight workspace preference model and human-readable control labels in `project/editor/ui/workspace-state.js` and map internal parameter names to friendly text. Preferences persist to `localStorage` and are strictly UI-only. 
- Replace the topbar and mount a workspace tab navigator and compact File/Settings menus in `project/editor/ui/app-shell.js`, add floating canvas controls (Fit/Zoom) and toast status, collapsible side panels and timeline, workspace hints, and focus-preview mode; the app shell emits `workspacechange` events consumed by callers. 
- Contextualize sidebars and disclosure: create visual template cards and a small Face Builder preview (`project/editor/ui/sidebar-sections.js`), simplify Rig UI language and add a Face Controls header with “Use selected artwork” wording and friendly movement method labels (`project/editor/rig-editor/semantic-parts/rig-panel.js`), and update `project/editor/main.js` to wire Preview to workspace selection non-destructively. 
- Documentation updates and a small unit test suite were added: `README.md`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`, and `project/editor/core/tests/workspace-state.test.js`. 
- No changes were made to the runtime, rig schema, animation model, or snapshot format; all changes are UI composition only and reuse the existing PreviewController/store/engine surfaces.

### Testing
- Ran unit tests: `npm test` — all unit tests passed (80 tests). 
- Built the production bundle: `npm run build` — build succeeded. 
- Ran full verify: `npm run verify` (includes `check:conflicts`, unit tests and build) — succeeded. 
- Attempted critical E2E Chromium tests: `npm run test:e2e:critical` — failed to run in this environment because Playwright could not download/launch the Chromium binary (download returned HTTP 403), so browser E2E verification is blocked by CI environment constraints rather than application test failures.

author: cayman-nz2
body:
Step one of moving Atsy's data out of the United States.

**Why it is there at all:** `provision.yml` calls `wrangler d1 create atsy-db` and `wrangler r2 bucket create atsy-cv` with **no `--location`**. Cloudflare placed both wherever the creating client sat — a GitHub Actions runner in the US. It was never a decision. Atsy is run from New Zealand under the Privacy Act 2020, for readers who are mostly in New Zealand, and every D1 query currently crosses the Pacific.

**Why it needs new resources:** neither product can be relocated. There is no move command (`r2 bucket update` changes storage class, not location) and the location is fixed at creation. So this creates `atsy-db-oc` and `atsy-cv-oc` with `--location oc` and copies the database across.

## What this deliberately does not do

It does not cut over. `wrangler.jsonc` still points at the old resources when the workflow finishes. That is what makes it safe to run and safe to re-run — the destination database is dropped and rebuilt on every run, so the copy can be refreshed immediately before the cutover merge and the window in which a signup could be lost stays small.

**The old resources are never touched.** Rollback is reverting one commit.

## R2 copies nothing

The bucket holds only encrypted CVs and every one is deleted inside 24 hours, so the old bucket drains itself once the binding moves. The one consequence: for up to 24 hours after cutover, scans uploaded beforehand will have rows pointing at objects in the old bucket, so "open the stored copy" and the X-ray will fail for those. The findings, score and printable report are unaffected — they live in D1.

## Two guards

- It refuses to run unless `MIGRATE` is typed into the dispatch box.
- It counts every table in **both** databases and fails on any mismatch, rather than reporting a copy nobody checked. Table names come from `sqlite_master`, so a table added later is covered without editing the workflow.

It also prints the new `database_id` and proves both new resources report `oc`, which is what the cutover PR needs.

## Honest limit

`--location` is a hint, not a guarantee — best-effort placement. The only hard boundary Cloudflare offers is `--jurisdiction`, and the only values are `eu` and `fedramp`; there is no AU or NZ jurisdiction. So this moves the data to Oceania but the privacy page still will not be able to promise it never leaves. That wording gets handled in the cutover PR, along with the resource names and region the page currently quotes.

author: jeonsewon
body:
…then

A 12.25 MB session on this machine has been outside every measurement since the server refused it, and it would have stayed there forever. The ceiling went from 10 MB to 16 MB on 2026-08-31 and nothing on this side noticed, because `_refused_for_size` compared the file against the size that was refused rather than against what the server takes today. Growth was the only thing that could change the answer, and growth only makes it worse.

`server_limit` reads `max_upload_bytes` from the root endpoint, which the server started publishing for exactly this. It is asked once per run and only when the ledger holds a refusal, so a machine that has never been refused makes no request. None on any failure: an unreachable server is the upload's problem to report, and without an answer the old comparison still decides.

Verified live before and after. `submit --dry-run` now lists `d97e454c … 11965 KB` as submittable, and the run summary went from "2 too large" to "1".

The failing test found something older than this change: the message and the queue already disagreed. `refused_too_large` listed every entry carrying `refused_bytes` while `_refused_for_size` compared the file against that size, so a small file with a large recorded refusal was printed as excluded and submitted in the same breath. Both now go through one rule, and the test states a ceiling its fixture is genuinely over instead of asserting a message nothing was acting on.

author: wycliffrotich-dev
body:
## Problem

`PostgresWorkerRepository._job_from_row` read `cancellation_requested_at`
from the `jobs` table row, but the column was never migrated in. ADR 0029
added the field to the `Job` domain entity, but the corresponding schema
migration was apparently never created, and the ADR's own Consequences
section flags this as an incomplete follow-up.

This caused a `KeyError` on every worker read, both in the request path
(`GET /workers/{id}`) and in the background cluster tick and reconciliation
loops, which run continuously. The background loop crash was silent to
users but meant no job ever transitioned out of RUNNING via reconciliation,
which also caused an unrelated-looking test timeout
(`test_complete_job_after_background_loop_already_completed_it_returns_409`).

## Fix

Removed the read of `cancellation_requested_at` in `_job_from_row`.
Confirmed safe:

- It is the only read of this field in the repository layer
  (`grep -rn "cancellation_requested_at" app/`).
- The field is optional on the `Job` entity (`datetime | None = None`),
  so omitting the kwarg does not break construction.
- Cancellation of running jobs does not depend on this field. It is
  driven by `Job.status` (`CANCELLING`), which is a real, persisted
  column already covered by existing tests. `WorkerExecutionLoop`
  detects cancellation by polling `job.is_cancelling()` off a fresh
  repository read, not by reading this timestamp.

## Verification

Full suite: 310 passed, 0 failed (previously 4 failing).

## Also included

Frontend changes enabling cancellation of RUNNING jobs (previously only
SUBMITTED/QUEUED/SCHEDULED were cancellable in the UI), plus an optional
command field on job creation. Verified this does not depend on the
missing column above; see fix description for why.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

cancellation_requested_at is still not persisted anywhere. The Job
entity sets and clears it in memory on every cancel request
(job.py:310, 373), but it is silently dropped on save and never
read back, since no column exists. This is currently harmless (nothing
displays or depends on the value), but it should get a real migration
so ADR 0029 is fully closed. No ticket filed yet, flagging here for
visibility.

author: chenmingwei23
body:
## Problem / Motivation

`platform/context.py` exposes two accessors with opposite safety contracts.
`current_context()` is fail-closed: on a non-standalone host that never composed
its companion it raises `PlatformCompositionError` rather than hand the caller
open-source defaults. `installed_context()` is the deliberate exception -- a bare
attribute read that answers `None` instead of raising, so a hot path whose
no-context answer is already the conservative one does not re-pay a config load
and entry-point discovery per call.

That exception is safe only where the caller's no-context answer really is the
conservative one, and that is a property of the CALLER, not of the accessor. The
accessor cannot check it. Nothing else did either: the rule lived in the
accessor's docstring and in `docs/system-specs/modules/platform-context.md`, with
no test behind it.

Under that guard the caller set silently tripled:

- 2026-08-20 (PR #4563 design review) -- one caller,
  `security._exempt_exact_hosts`, and the spec said so.
- 2026-08-28, PR #6264 -- `governance.active_policy_distribution` added.
- 2026-08-31, PR #7151 -- `context.redact_log_via_context` added.

Neither addition met any friction, and the spec sentence naming "the one such
caller" was still on main describing a set of three.

## Why it matters

Every current caller is in fact conservative -- I checked all three, and this PR
changes no behavior. The defect is the missing gate, and its cost is the next
caller: a peek whose no-context answer is NOT conservative would silently take
open-source defaults on a host whose companion policy failed to compose, which is
precisely the fail-open that `current_context()`'s raise exists to prevent. A
reviewer would have to know the unwritten rule and notice a one-line function call
to catch it. The stale spec sentence shows the prose guard already failing: it
told a reader there was one caller while three existed, so the next author had no
accurate picture of what they were joining.

## What changed (motivation -> approach -> change)

Symptom: two callers joined a contract-bypassing accessor with nothing objecting.
Root cause: the constraint is a caller property, so it can only be enforced where
callers are enumerated -- and they were not enumerated anywhere.

This module already solves that exact shape once, for `RESERVED_SLOTS`: a
declared map next to the thing it describes, gated by AST analysis of the real
source tree (a hand list would rot), with two arms so the map cannot go stale in
either direction. This change reuses it rather than inventing a second idiom.

- `context.PEEK_CALLERS` maps `"<path under src/kiro_crew>::<function>"` to the
  reason that caller's no-context answer is conservative. All three of today's
  callers are declared, with the reason written out for each -- including the two
  that were never reviewed against this contract.
- `test_platform_cpp_seam_coverage.py` gains `TestInstalledContextPeeks`. Arm one:
  every `installed_context()` call site in the package must appear in the map, so a
  new peek fails the build until its author writes down why it is safe. Arm two:
  every entry must still have a live call site, so a deleted or renamed caller
  cannot leave behind a permission that reads as a reviewed decision.
- The peek scan deliberately does NOT exclude `platform/`, unlike the existing
  seam scan. A seam read inside the platform package is plumbing, but a peek there
  is a real bypass -- two of the three callers live in it, so excluding the
  directory would have hidden them and made the gate pass while permitting exactly
  what it forbids.
- The spec paragraph is corrected (it claimed one caller) and now names the map
  and the gate instead of asking politely.

The gate is a review forcing function, not a proof: it cannot verify that a
written justification is true. What it removes is the silent path. Adding a peek
now costs a diff to the very file whose fail-closed contract is being bypassed,
and the justification lands in front of a reviewer.

## Tests

`test/test_platform_cpp_seam_coverage.py::TestInstalledContextPeeks` (7 tests):

- `test_every_peek_is_declared` -- arm one. Mutation-verified: adding a new
  module that calls `installed_context()` reds it with
  `undeclared installed_context() caller(s): {'_peek_probe.py::probe_drift': [...]}`,
  1 failed / 6 passed. This is the regression PR #6264 and PR #7151 would have hit.
- `test_declared_peeks_still_have_a_call_site` -- arm two. Mutation-verified: a
  declared entry for a caller that does not exist reds it and lists the three real
  sites, 1 failed / 6 passed in isolation.
- `test_scanner_detects_a_synthetic_peek` -- anti-vacuity guard. Both arms pass
  trivially if the scanner finds nothing, so the two call shapes
  (`installed_context()` and `pc.installed_context()`) and the scope attribution
  are pinned against source the test controls.
- `test_scanner_finds_the_real_call_sites`, `test_scanner_does_not_count_the_definition`,
  `test_peek_justifications_answer_the_question` (each reason must contain the
  phrase `no-context answer`, so a justification cannot dodge the question),
  `test_peek_keys_name_real_modules`.

Targeted runs: `test_platform_cpp_seam_coverage.py` 57 passed;
`test_platform_context.py` + `test_platform_cpp_seam_coverage.py` +
`test_harness_parity.py` 112 passed. flake8, black and isort clean on the touched
files.

## Manual verification

N/A -- unit coverage sufficient. The change adds a build-time gate plus a
declaration; there is no runtime path and no user-visible surface.

## Related Issues

No GitHub issue. The finding came from the design review on PR #4563, which
recorded it as unreachable-today with the risk being "a future second consumer
whose no-context answer is NOT conservative". Two such consumers have since
landed, which is what this PR gates.

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt
Pattern: a documented-only caller restriction on a contract-bypassing accessor --
where the safety condition is a property of the CALLER, so the callee cannot
enforce it. `installed_context()` is one instance; the general shape is any
"use this only when X" accessor whose X the function itself cannot check. The
generalizable rule: such an accessor needs an enumerated caller set gated from
both sides, not a docstring. The two arms matter equally -- an allowlist with no
staleness arm becomes a list of permissions nobody re-examines, which the next
author cites as precedent.

Canvas Run button now lands in a Lens session with a live RunBubble (P1 slice of #1515).

- Backend `/workflows/{id}/trigger` accepts optional `lens_attach: bool` and `lens_session_id: UUID`. When `lens_attach=true` and no id supplied, auto-mints a bare `GlensChatSession` titled `Run: <workflow.name>`.

author: therealtimex
body:
## Why

The first capture against demo data produced an analytics screenshot **worse than the stale one it replaced**: Contact Growth was a solid block, Enrichment Score Distribution was a single bar.

Two causes, one of them a real bug in the seed.

## 1. Growth was flat by construction

Twelve contacts at one every two days makes every bucket exactly `1`, so the y-axis maxes at 1 and the area chart fills solid. `daysAgo` is now clustered — 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 2 — and the chart is a curve peaking at 3.

## 2. Enrichment never saw the identities

Two compounding problems:

- `createContact` scores the contact **before any identity exists**, and `createIdentity` does not re-score. Every contact kept the score it had when it had no platform profile at all.
- The profile fields the score reads — `headline`, `bio`, `location`, `website` — are resolved *from identities* by `resolveContactProfile`, never from the contact. Passing them to `createContact` did nothing.

Both fixed: profile fields go on the identity, and `recalcContactEnrichment` runs once the identities exist.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| enrichment scores | 50 / 35 / 25 (2 buckets, mostly one) | **98 / 57 / 41 / 31** (4 buckets) |
| identities | 22 | 25 — rich tier carries 3, so Platform Mix renders three segments |

Tiers are declared as data in `RICHNESS_TIERS` so the spread is legible without reading the seeding loop. Still no avatars at any tier — initials keep the guide free of photographs.

## Verification

Re-seeded and re-captured against a live dev server on the demo database. Contact Growth is a curve, the histogram has multiple bars at different heights, and the donut is complete with three segments.

Checks: typecheck clean, lint clean, 6 guard tests passing.

## Note

`createIdentity` not re-scoring enrichment may be worth a look in the app itself — any path that creates a contact and then attaches identities leaves a stale score until something else recalculates. I have not changed app behaviour here; the seed just calls the recalc explicitly, which is what a real ingestion pipeline would do.

author: terryyin
body: When OpenAI marks a question-generation batch `FAILED`, Donut persists local `FAILED` (batch and pending requests), then throws with OpenAI’s error text so the hourly job writes a Failure report (ADR 0006). Submit-time upload/`createResponsesBatch` errors do the same: commit `FAILED` in a nested transaction, then throw. ## Changes **Poll path.** After polling all `SUBMITTED` batches, persist every OpenAI `FAILED`/`CANCELLED` as local `FAILED`, then throw one exception (same process-all-then-throw as retrieve failures). Message includes OpenAI `errors` text when present, otherwise `openai batch failed`, plus batch id. `EXPIRED` still persists without throwing. **Submit path.** Local `FAILED` from upload/create exceptions is committed in `QuestionGenerationBatchSubmissionFailureTx` (`REQUIRES_NEW`). Planning is committed first so that nested update is not blocked by the user transaction. `submitDueUsers` still attempts every due user, then throws one exception so `ScheduledJobErrorHandler` writes a Failure report. **Docs.** `docs/question-generation-batch-operations.md` No ADR change. No new E2E (no OpenAI Batch in Cypress). Spent planning history for `.planning/quick/038-question-generation-batch-failed-loud/` is removed.

author: alajmah
body:
**Unit:** TR-01 — Triage Provider-Response Recovery
**Base:** `c0ca997` (master HEAD at branch creation; no intervening delta)

## Problem

Production triage is nonfunctional. The dominant crash signature on both triage surfaces was:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')
```

Both `triageIssue` and `triagePR` called the provider with `max_tokens: 4096` and then assumed `message.content[0].text`.

## Step A — production diagnostic (no queue jobs, no mutations, no secrets left CT 115)

Probe run inside the production app container against the current Z.AI route, exact model string, exact system/user prompts reconstructed from real failed targets (ElephantRock/Continuity-Aware-Distributed-Inference issue #44 and PR #47), `max_tokens: 4096`:

| surface | returned model | content blocks | stop_reason | out tokens | JSON parse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| issue #44 | glm-5.3-flash | `thinking,text` | end_turn | 269 | OK (all 6 schema keys) |
| PR #47 | glm-5.3-flash | `thinking,text` | end_turn | 191 | OK (all 4 schema keys) |

**Conclusion: Case A.** Usable text exists but is not `content[0]` (thinking block first). The 4,096 budget terminates naturally (`end_turn`) with wide headroom — **no ceiling search needed; budget stays 4,096 at both sites.**

## Correction

- `extractTriageText()` — one local extractor: text blocks selected in response order and concatenated (or plain string trimmed); no review-service import, no new provider abstraction.
- `parseTriageClassification()` — one parse path for both surfaces, preserving markdown-fence handling. Empty extraction raises an explicit `SyntaxError` → existing `invalid_provider_response` lifecycle (classifier case 5b), never a property-access TypeError.
- Parse-error logger uses the extracted text; no `content[0]` dereference anywhere; no raw thinking persisted on jobs.

## Out of scope (unchanged)

Prompts, model string, provider/base URL, `reasoning_effort`, budgets (4,096), review service and its 32,768 ceiling, Gate C, RI, label taxonomy, retry/backoff, idempotency lifecycle.

The intermittent Z.AI `Connection error` (26 occurrences in 48h of production logs, all on triage calls; reviews unaffected) remains a separate reliability defect — this PR does not touch transport, retry, or backoff.

## Regression coverage

- 18 response-shape + mutation-safety cases across both paths: plain text, thinking-first, multi-block join, fenced JSON, thinking-only → explicit failure, empty array → explicit failure, malformed JSON → existing behavior, Connection error → propagates unchanged, single-mutation positives.
- Classifier: empty-extraction `SyntaxError` → `invalid_provider_response`, retryable, not permanent.
- Provider fixtures corrected to typed text blocks; writer-audit call-site lines re-pinned after the source shift.

## Verification

- All targeted suites green: triage-pr-behavior, triage-mutation-recovery, triageFailureService, triage-recovery-non-triage-untouched, wave2-triage-integration, provider-budget-regression, triage-auto-comment, triage-pr-guards, wave2-writer-audit (101+17 tests).
- Full web profile: **0 failed tests** (3,506 passed, 6 skipped); the 45 suite-level failures are the known GITWIRE_BASE_URL integration suites, unchanged from base.

author: hollandcloud
body:
Lands the four commits that are still only on a branch. **`main` does not currently contain any of this**, including the fix for a layout bug visible in the shipped 1.1 App Store screenshots.

PR #3 merged into `television-portrait` and took only the first commit; the other three were pushed afterwards and were stranded. Same thing happened with #2. This PR targets `main` directly so it cannot happen again.

## CRT power sounds

Synthesised by `Tools/MakeSounds.py` and committed, the way the icon is drawn by `MakeIcons.swift`. That keeps the bundle unencumbered — the music is AI-generated precisely so no rights holder exists, and a thump from a sample library would have been the first thing shipped that belongs to someone else.

Three layers, matching what a tube does: the flyback transformer at the NTSC horizontal scan frequency (15,734 Hz — the real number) falling away as the high voltage collapses, the degauss coil thumping under it, and the anode cracking into the tube face. Power-on runs them in reverse and takes longer, because the heater warms before the raster arrives.

## The set is now the control surface

The cabinet's buttons were always focusable on tvOS; what they lacked was any way to *see* focus, because `.plain` leaves a focused button identical to an unfocused one and the platform paints a white wash over a control the size of a fingernail. A real `ButtonStyle` fixes both — it owns the whole appearance, so `.focusEffectDisabled()` works where `RootView` records it did not for a plain button.

With the set usable, the floating overlay is a second set of controls competing with a better one, so it no longer appears while the cabinet is drawn — on every platform, since the argument has nothing to do with the device. **Only** while it is drawn: with the television off, the overlay is the sole way to reach anything, and on an Apple TV that would be a remote with nowhere to go. Mute joins the cabinet so nothing is lost.

The fifth button didn't fit, and `TelevisionGeometryTests` said it did — the fit check hardcoded four and was measuring a layout the app no longer draws. Reading the real count failed at once: five 44pt targets need 239.9pt of an iPhone SE's 238.0pt chin. The gap gives way rather than the targets.

## Hourly overflowed the blue panel — and shipped that way

Background 1 insets its panel 52pt left and 56pt right of the canvas. The wide canvas *also* insets the content block by 107pt, carrying every column clear. The standard canvas has no such inset, so the same numbers put the hour label off the panel's left edge and the wind value off its right, onto the orange field.

It is visible in the 1.1 iPad screenshots. It went unnoticed because the 640pt canvas was only ever used by an iPad held sideways — until the television started drawing it everywhere.

All three tables were measured before anything changed:

| Table | Standard span | Panel 52 … 584 |
|---|---|---|
| Hourly | 25 … 625 | **overflows both edges** |
| Travel | 80 … 582 | fits |
| Latest Observations | 64 … 576 | fits |

Only Hourly was wrong, and Latest Observations already had per-canvas column sets, so this follows an existing pattern rather than inventing one. Positions only, not sizes — the type stays 32pt, and the room comes from the gap after the hour label.

`BluePanelInset` publishes the panel geometry as a layout contract. `DesignSpace.blueBoxMargin` is deleted: never referenced, and it looked exactly like the constant that governs this panel.

## Audio session

`configureAudioSession()` ran only from `MusicPlayer.play()`, so the category was an accident of whether music was on. With music off nothing asked for `.playback`, and the CRT sounds ran under the default category — muted by the ringer switch, stopped on backgrounding. Invisible in a simulator, which has neither.

## Also

Upside-down portrait added to the iPhone's supported orientations; it was absent, so rotating that way left the app as it was and the television never appeared.

## Verified

174 tests. Both new rules are mutation-tested: restoring the old Hourly columns fails on both edges (25 against a panel starting at 52, 625 against one ending at 584), and the chin fit fails the moment it reads the real button count.

Confirmed on device simulators: the five-button chin and focus treatment on Apple TV, and the corrected Hourly columns on iPhone portrait. **Not** verified by me: the sounds being audible, and the overlay show/hide transitions — `simctl` has no touch or remote input. Those were checked by hand.

author: donutlorde
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #103387

## Additional information

While the backport of IME from 4.x to 3.x is mostly identical, 3.x does not run the check for `!DisplayServer::get_singleton()->has_feature(DisplayServerEnums::FEATURE_IME)` in line_edit.cpp or text_edit.cpp before invoking either `set_ime_active` or `set_ime_position`. On `DisplayServerWeb`'s implementation of `has_feature`, this only returns true if virtual keyboard support is not available.  This has the unfortunate effect having the `<div class="ime">` take focus away from the `<input>` on Mobile Web while using a LineEdit or TextEdit, causing various levels of input being missed depending of your mobile browser.

This PR essentially bakes the FEATURE_IME check from 4.x into `OS_JavaScript::set_ime_active` and `OS_JavaScript::set_ime_position`, resulting in the same behavior as 4.x.

Tested on Android Firefox 154.0.1 and Android Chrome 151.0.7922.137 on a basic scene with only a line edit, and all inputs were able to be captured, including backspace.

Tested on Desktop Firefox 154.0.1 as working with regular keyboard input with the same scene setup. I have not tested IME with my changes, but in theory this should give equal behavior to 4.x.

author: nicholashan1226
body:
Production OI and premium dump cycles were failing while the canonical catalog/query snapshot and a full 80-dataset readback remained valid. The runners opened the live WAL database through a bare `mode=ro` connection for gap detection, bypassing the read-model binding and epoch checks.

This PR routes dump gap detection through `open_verified_read_model_snapshot`, preserving validated receipt filtering while using the same sidecar and epoch verification as catalog/query. It also includes the actual exception in premium runner failure output so future failures remain diagnosable.

Validation:
- `51 passed` across the OI and premium dump runner suites.
- `268 passed, 1 candidate-test setup failure` in the initial combined runner/projection pass; the setup was corrected to provision the required authority-lock sidecar.
- The corrected focused cases passed `4/4`.
- `git diff --check` and Python compile checks passed.
- Production read-only canonical snapshot readback covered all 80 OI/premium datasets in 24.298s before this patch; no production writes were made by diagnosis.

No API, registry, schema, cadence, provider budget, route, account, or trading behavior changes. No long-term documentation update is needed because the existing verified snapshot contract remains authoritative; this fixes an internal runner that bypassed it.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Internal collector read-path alignment with an existing verified snapshot contract; no API, registry, or schema changes. Reduces false “malformed disk” / authority failures during concurrent WAL writes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Production OI and premium dump cycles were failing gap detection while catalog/query and full readbacks stayed healthy. **`_ingested_days`** in the OI dump runner no longer opens the live WAL DB with a bare **`mode=ro`** URI under a hand-rolled shared authority lock; it now uses **`open_verified_read_model_snapshot`**, matching catalog/query sidecar binding and epoch verification while still filtering **`provider_dataset_rows`** through **`validated_success_receipt_ids`**. The dedicated **`_FACT_AUTHORITY_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS`** knob is removed because the snapshot helper owns that wait behavior.
> 
> The premium dump **`main()`** failure JSON now includes an **`error`** field (**`{type}: {message}`**), parallel to the OI runner, so systemd/journal failures are diagnosable instead of only **`state: failed`**.
> 
> Tests assert the verified snapshot path for ingested-day reads and add premium **`main`** failure-output coverage.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 5095948946ceb69225871acd4463a68e50ac6a5d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: clawosiris
body:
## Summary

Implements the first focused Phase 2 command-family migration from #523, tracked by #539: the standard scan-task lifecycle now uses the typed `GmpRequest` / `GmpResponse` execution contract established in Phases 0 and 1.

This batch adds semantic requests for list, detailed get, create, clone, modify, delete, start, stop, and resume; associates them with their typed responses; and converts the existing client helpers to thin `execute` wrappers. Additive `get_task` and `clone_task` helpers complete the selected lifecycle surface.

## Boundary

Included semantic requests:

- `GetTasksRequest`
- `GetTaskRequest`
- `CreateTaskRequest`
- `CloneTaskRequest`
- `ModifyTaskRequest`
- `DeleteTaskRequest`
- `StartTaskRequest`
- `StopTaskRequest`
- `ResumeTaskRequest`

These cover seven wire commands: `get_tasks`, `create_task`, `modify_task`, `delete_task`, `start_task`, `stop_task`, and `resume_task`. Detailed get deliberately reuses `get_tasks`; clone deliberately reuses `create_task`.

Explicitly deferred to later focused batches:

- import/container task creation
- agent-group tasks
- OCI/container-image tasks
- web-application tasks
- `move_task`
- audit create/list/get/clone/modify/delete/action aliases
- other Phase 2 families and Phase 3 irregular/version-specific work

## Compatibility and coverage

- Existing builders remain available and are the single wire encoders used by the new semantic requests.
- Full-option byte-equivalence tests cover all nine request types.
- `modify_task` construction preserves the existing observer validation before any request can be executed.
- Direct execution tests cover the oldest supported GMP version, exact command history, non-2xx mapping, typed parse-field context, and compile-time request/response association.
- The change introduces no dependency, transport, wire-format, or version-gate changes.

## Validation

- `cargo test --workspace`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/msrv rustup run 1.86.0 cargo test --workspace`
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/msrv rustup run 1.86.0 cargo check --workspace --all-features`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- focused task command/response/builder/doctest/facade/parity/lifecycle tests: 73 passed
- `cargo deny check`
- `cargo audit`
- `cargo vet`
- `cargo machete`
- coverage policy self-test and all-feature coverage: 96.31% lines, 94.36% regions, 93.77% functions
- semver checks against `origin/next` and `v0.6.0`: all five crates passed 196 applicable checks each, with 58 non-applicable checks skipped per crate

The first all-feature test attempt exhausted the local filesystem while linking. After cleaning only regenerable target artifacts from the completed Phase 0/1 worktrees and this worktree, the clean retry passed completely. Local `cargo-geiger` remains unavailable because the installed binary requires GLIBC 2.38/2.39 while this host provides 2.36; the workspace `unsafe_code = "forbid"` lint is active, this patch adds no unsafe code, and protected CI will run the gate in its supported environment.

author: pyramation
body:
## Summary

Two things a consumer still had to know about the action, which is two too many for something whose pitch is "a config file and one `uses:`".

**The reports artifact is part of the mechanism, not the consumer's chore.** `compare: auto` measures the delta by downloading the base branch's `safegres-reports` artifact — so a repository that does not upload one can never show a delta, and every consumer was copying the same `actions/upload-artifact` block into its workflow, with the artifact *name* as an undocumented contract with `compare-artifact`. The action now owns it:

```yaml
upload-reports: 'true'            # default
artifact-name: 'safegres-reports' # == compare-artifact's default
artifact-retention-days: '14'
```

`upload-reports: false` is for the one case where the workflow uploads the directory itself — two uploads under one name is an error, not a merge. (constructive-db drops its own step in a follow-up.)

**Code scanning being off should not fail a gate that passed.** `upload-sarif: true` on a repository without Code Security fails the job with "Code Security must be enabled" — a reporting channel taking down the audit. A composite action cannot mark its own step `continue-on-error`, so the upload is now guarded rather than tolerated: probe `GET repos/{repo}/code-scanning/analyses`, upload when it answers, otherwise `::warning` and leave the SARIF in the report directory.

Also pins the docs' `uses:` at `@safegres-action-v1` instead of `@main` — a tag I'll move to this commit once merged, so consumers pin the action rather than the monorepo tip.

Tests: `action.test.ts` pins `artifact-name`'s default to `compare-artifact`'s (a mismatch silently costs every future PR its delta) and pins the SARIF guard.

body:
## Related issue

Closes #5975

## Summary

- Return a safe `decline` response to Codex when Omnigent rejects a command-approval hook request.
- Prevent the active Codex turn from waiting forever after malformed optional execpolicy amendment data.
- Add a regression test through the forwarder's event-handling seam using the production 400 response.

ELI5: if Omnigent cannot process an approval request, it now tells Codex “no” instead of leaving Codex waiting for an answer that will never arrive.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Codex command approval] --> B[Omnigent hook]
    B -->|2xx| C[Forward hook decision]
    B -->|4xx/5xx| D[Reply decline]
    D --> E[Settle Codex request]
```

## Test Plan

- Verified the regression test failed before the fix: no response was sent to the fake Codex app-server client.
- `uv run --no-sync pytest -q tests/test_codex_native.py` — 245 passed.
- `uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files` — all hooks passed.
- Applied the patch to the affected local 0.11.0 install and retried the same `ssh-keygen` command-approval path. Codex received `Rejected("rejected by user")`, the turn completed, the session returned to `idle`, and `active_response_id` cleared instead of remaining stuck.

## Demo

- [ ] Visual demo attached below
- [x] Non-visual evidence provided below or in Test Plan
- [ ] Not applicable — no behavioral change

Before: hook HTTP 400 left the app-server response list empty and the active turn stuck.

After: the forwarder sends `{"decision": "decline"}` for the same command-approval request, allowing the turn to settle. This was also verified against the original affected local session.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] UI / frontend change
- [ ] Refactor / chore
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test / CI
- [ ] Breaking change

- [x] Existing tests cover this change
- [ ] Not applicable

## Coverage notes

The new regression test drives `_handle_event`, waits for the asynchronous elicitation tracker to drain, and asserts the exact JSON-RPC response returned to Codex. Manual verification used the original affected session after safely stopping its orphaned response and reconnecting the same persisted Codex thread.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>Azure/azure-sdk-for-net (Azure.Core)</summary>

### [`v1.62.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/releases/tag/Azure.Core_1.62.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/compare/Azure.Core_1.61.0...Azure.Core_1.62.0)

#### 1.62.0 (2026-08-20)

##### Features Added

- Added experimental (`SCME0002`) `AzureCredentialResolver.Default` public static property so standalone callers can share the process-wide credential cache used by DI-resolved paths.
- `AzureCredentialResolver` now resolves every `ChainedTokenCredential` `Sources[]` entry through the active resolver chain, so any registered `CredentialResolver` (built-in, broker, or third-party) can claim or override an entry. Entries are constructed as chained, so transient failures surface as `CredentialUnavailableException` and the chain falls through.

##### Breaking Changes

- `AzureCredentialResolver` now resolves a top-level single source (e.g. `CredentialSource: AzureCliCredential`) to the concrete credential type (`AzureCliCredential`) rather than a `DefaultAzureCredential` wrapper. Construction is unchanged (it uses the same `DefaultAzureCredentialFactory` helpers) — only the returned type differs; callers using `CredentialSettings.TokenProvider` as a `TokenCredential` are unaffected.
- `AzureCredentialResolver` no longer claims top-level `BrokerCredential` sections (canonical name or `broker` alias); they now require `BrokerCredentialResolver` from `Azure.Identity.Broker` 1.7.0+ (e.g. via `AddBrokerCredentialResolver()`). `BrokerCredential` entries nested inside a `ChainedTokenCredential` continue to resolve. Note: if `BrokerCredentialResolver` from `Azure.Identity.Broker` 1.7.0 is registered ahead of `AzureCredentialResolver`, a nested `BrokerCredential` entry is currently built as non-chained, so it may surface `AuthenticationFailedException` and abort the chain instead of falling through to the next entry. Without a broker resolver registered, the built-in chain path builds the broker entry as chained (correct fall-through). A future `Azure.Identity.Broker` release will make its resolver honor chained semantics for nested entries.

### [`v1.61.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/releases/tag/Azure.Core_1.61.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/compare/Azure.Core_1.60.0...Azure.Core_1.61.0)

#### 1.61.0 (2026-07-30)

##### Features Added

- Added `AzureAuthorityHosts.AzureBleuCloud` (`https://login.sovcloud-identity.fr/`), the Microsoft Entra authority host for Bleu Cloud, the national partner cloud for France. Interactive credentials' `Authenticate` methods now also resolve the default Azure Resource Manager scope for Bleu Cloud.

##### Bugs Fixed

- Fixed an issue where response content logging could emit more bytes than were actually read when a non-buffered (streaming) response was read into a buffer larger than the response body. Previously, when the read began at offset 0, the entire caller-supplied buffer was logged — including the bytes past the response payload, which for a pooled buffer contain unrelated in-process content — and the configured `LoggedContentSizeLimit` was not applied. The logging policy now logs only the bytes that were read. ([#​61399](https://redirect.github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues/61399))
- Fixed an issue where `RequestFailedException` could throw a secondary `ArgumentNullException` while formatting a failed response that had a text content-type header but an empty body, masking the actual service failure. The exception now preserves the original HTTP status, reason phrase, and headers, and no longer formats empty response content.
- Fixed `AzureCliCredential` to not pass both `--tenant` and `--subscription` flags to the Azure CLI, as the CLI rejects this combination. When a tenant is requested (for example, via challenge-based authentication) it now takes precedence and `--subscription` is omitted; `--subscription` is used only when no tenant is requested. ([#​58949](https://redirect.github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues/58949))

##### Other Changes

- Added `azure-deprecating` to the default list of allowed (non-redacted) headers in `DiagnosticsOptions` to support [deprecating behavior notification](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/api-guidelines/blob/vNext/azure/Guidelines.md#deprecating-behavior-notification).

</details>

<details>
<summary>open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet (OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting)</summary>

### [`v1.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/HEAD/RELEASENOTES.md#1180)

Release details: [1.18.0](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/releases/tag/core-1.18.0)

- **Breaking change:** The maximum size of a single OTLP export request is now
  64 MiB by default instead of 128 MiB to conform with the OpenTelemetry specification.

### gzip: gzip: Arbitrary file overwrite via insecure temporary file handling in gzexe utility
[CVE-2026-41991](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-41991)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
A flaw was found in the `gzexe` utility of GNU `gzip`. When the `mktemp` utility is not available, `gzexe` creates temporary files with predictable names based on the process ID. A local attacker can exploit this by pre-creating a symbolic link to an arbitrary file at the predicted temporary file path. This can lead to a Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) condition, allowing the attacker to overwrite arbitrary files on the system.

#### Severity
Moderate

author: avanish
body:
Replaces the OAuth2 Device Authorization Grant (code-entry) screen with Authorization Code + PKCE, matching the auth-api migration: the CLI is a registered public client (faro-helm-cli, no client secret) that opens the system browser to /oauth/authorize, catches the redirect on a local loopback server, and exchanges the code at /oauth/token. The user enters credentials in the browser now, never in the terminal.

Also removes internal/ui/login.go (the email/password-in-terminal screen) as dead code — /login only ever routed to the device-flow screen, so this was unreachable before this change too.

New internal/oauthflow package (framework-free, no Bubble Tea/config dependency) holds the testable core:
- pkce.go: RFC 7636 S256 verifier/challenge generation
- authorize_url.go: /oauth/authorize URL construction
- callback_server.go: the loopback HTTP server — binds an ephemeral port matching the 'http://localhost:*/callback' wildcard registered for this client, delivers the callback's code/state/error over a channel with context-based cancellation and timeout, tolerates a second hit after the first delivery (browser retry, favicon) without hanging
- browser.go: cross-platform browser launch, with the per-OS command construction split out as a pure (testable) function from the actual exec.Command call

internal/auth.Service gains BeginBrowserLogin/CompleteBrowserLogin, replacing Login (dead — only the deleted LoginModel called it) and StartDeviceFlow/PollDeviceToken/CompleteDeviceLogin. internal/api gains oauth.go (ExchangeAuthorizationCode against POST /oauth/token, tested against an httptest.Server) and drops device_flow.go's device-specific types/methods and dead Login/AuthLoginRequest/AuthLoginResponse.

Following TDD for the new business logic: internal/oauthflow and the new internal/api call were written test-first (17 + 2 tests, run with -race for the concurrent callback server). The Bubble Tea UI layer (browser_login.go) isn't unit tested, matching this repo's existing convention for ui/*.go — no Bubble Tea model anywhere in this codebase has tests.

Not done: no real end-to-end browser smoke test was possible in the sandbox this was built in (no GUI browser to click through a login form). The client/server contract is covered by tests instead, and the server side was already live-verified in the auth-api Phase 2 work. Recommend one manual `faro login` run against a real auth-api before merging.

## What Problem This Solves

Moving across the chat composer immediately triggered the microphone device-chevron animation, adding incidental motion. Once expanded, the chevron also sat farther from the microphone than intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 750ms dwell only to fine-pointer hover discovery and removes the 2px inter-control gap. Keyboard focus, an open picker, dictation holds, touch devices, reduced-motion users, and collapse remain immediate.

## User Impact

Brief pointer passes no longer animate the microphone picker. Intentional hover still reveals it after three quarters of a second, with the chevron seated directly beside the microphone.

Reveal completed in 158ms with a 2px final gap.

### After

The existing after recording is retained as requested and was captured at the earlier 500ms iteration. It shows the delayed reveal and 0px gap; the final implementation increases the dwell to 750ms.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users declining runtime plugin capability review or cancelling AI activation saw “The Gateway setup request failed” even though cancellation had been confirmed. The actual cancellation and retry guidance was hidden under details.

Fixes #134573.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the typed confirmed-cancellation outcome at the shared activation presentation boundary. Both detected connections and manual API-key setup now show the existing cancellation message directly. Genuine transport errors and unknown activation outcomes retain their original diagnostic presentation, receipt ownership, reconciliation, and retry behavior. No protocol, configuration, persistence, consent, or provider-auth dismissal policy changes.

The UI renderer cannot recover a type that has already been reduced to a string, and string-matching in the generic transport formatter would misclassify arbitrary Gateway errors. The activation owner is the narrow shared boundary. Production changes are +10/-4 lines (net +6), including one small formatter in the existing support module to keep the lifecycle function within its complexity limit; tests add 23 lines to the existing matrix, with no new fixture or production test seam.

## User Impact

Confirmed cancellation visibly says that AI setup was cancelled and invites choosing a connection to retry. It no longer implies a broken Gateway.

## Evidence

- Before: personally reproduced through Computer Use in the real signed macOS app and an isolated real Gateway while verifying #133793. Declining review preserved configuration, installed no runtime plugin, and allowed retry; the row incorrectly showed the generic Gateway headline. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/133793#issuecomment-5486751935.
- Extended the existing shared-wizard matrix to check actual candidate/manual failure presentation for decline, cancel, accepted activation, terminal failure, and unresolved cancellation. Existing transport and ownership-race coverage remains intact.
- Independent source inspection and managed Codex autoreview found no accepted/actionable findings in the requested scope. The owner still consumes the authoritative wizard result; Codex turn-interrupt semantics are unchanged.
- Exact-head [CI 33461866326](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33461866326) passed, including all 10 consent cases, 1,906 app tests, 1,546 shared-kit tests, and named-profile coverage. The actual changed gate passed with pinned Swift tools and all seven selected Mac tooling shards. Signed after-fix GUI proof passed through Computer Use on exact app/worker revision `7a04eca510749a966fe6f3e15505a5675b146b77`: unchecked Submit and the Cancel button both show the cancellation/retry sentence directly, retry returns to review, and configuration remains byte-identical with no Codex install or model route. Developer ID signing and the 42,829-file artifact name scan passed. This was an arm64 debug proof build, not a published release.
- Sanitized before screenshot is retained locally. GitHub's attachment endpoint returned HTTP 403 and the repository artifact broker reported `artifact_upload_unavailable`; no uploaded image URL is claimed. Sanitized before/after captures were inspected and retained locally; the upload limitation remains.

ClawSweeper disposition (reviewed 2026-09-01 02:21 UTC): the runtime design is accepted as the correct owner boundary. Retaining the one-line changelog entry under the active maintainer instructions for user-visible fixes; this is maintainer release-note bookkeeping, not a contributor requirement. The six production lines preserve the typed presentation contract without duplicating the lifecycle or widening the generic transport formatter. Its other rank-up request is complete: signed after-fix GUI proof and exact-head native CI both pass.

Maintainer closeout: this is the follow-up to the release-verification defect in #133793/#134573. Native preparation used the documented `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_ROOT_CHANGELOG_PR=1` closeout mode while retaining exact-head hosted CI and all review gates. No release artifacts are published by this PR.

Non-blocking environment follow-up: after this GUI proof, the isolated Gateway reported clean shutdown and closed its listener, but Node 24.19.0 lingered in `CompileCacheHandler::Persist` → synchronous filesystem rename during process exit. The exact task process was terminated after the prolonged cache flush; the stack sample is retained for a separate Node compile-cache shutdown-latency investigation. This does not change the cancellation or configuration evidence above, and no operator Gateway was stopped.

## 1. 「共通ワードを同じマスに置く」を①②③どれでも切りかえ可能にした

これまでは①②で必ず固定、③だけ切りかえ可でした。オフにすると**同じ語が A と B でちがう場所に入る**ので、それ自体が仕掛けになります。

直す途中で2つ問題が見つかり、どちらも実測で発見しました。

- **オフにしても実際は同じマスのままだった。** 組み方の点数で「A と B の文字が同じマス」を加点していたため、共通ワードどうしの組（＝同じマス）が常に最高点になり、60通り作っても必ずそれが選ばれていた → オフのときは「ちがう相手と組ませた案」を加点して釣り合わせた
- **その結果、今度は作れないことがあった。** 交差できない組み方が高得点になってしまった → **交差できるか（cross）を最優先（×100）** にして重みの順序を固定した

author: aragontechsolutions-dev
body:
Programa de **puntos de fidelización**: el cliente identificado acumula puntos por compra y los canjea como pago en la caja.

> ⚠️ **Requiere migración de esquema** (`Customer.puntos`, tabla `LoyaltyMovement`, config en `Tenant`, valor `PUNTOS` en `MedioPago`). SQL para Supabase abajo.

## Cómo funciona
- **Config (Panel → Configuración → Fidelización):** activar el programa, definir *acumula 1 punto cada $X* y *valor de 1 punto al canjear $Y*.
  - Ej.: cada $100 = 1 punto, punto = $1 → una compra de $500 da **5 puntos**; 100 puntos valen **$100** al canjear.
- **Ganar:** toda venta con **cliente identificado** suma puntos automáticamente (sobre lo efectivamente pagado, sin contar lo cubierto con puntos).
- **Canjear (POS):** en el cobro, si el cliente tiene saldo y el programa está activo, aparece el tender **⭐ Puntos**; se acota al saldo disponible y descuenta del total a pagar. Muestra el saldo del cliente.
- Todo queda en un **ledger** (`LoyaltyMovement`): ganados, canjeados y ajustes, con saldo resultante.

## Panel
- **Configuración → Fidelización:** activar + rate + valor del punto.
- **Mayoristas:** columna **Puntos** y modal con **saldo + movimientos** y **ajuste manual** (regalo/corrección).

## Backend
- `Customer.puntos`, `LoyaltyMovement` (+enum), config en `Tenant`, `MedioPago.PUNTOS`.
- Ganancia/canje dentro de la transacción de `createSale`.
- `GET /customers/:id/loyalty` y `POST /customers/:id/loyalty/ajuste`; config en settings; catálogo expone la config al POS.

### SQL a aplicar en Supabase
```sql
ALTER TYPE "MedioPago" ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'PUNTOS';

DO $$ BEGIN
  CREATE TYPE "LoyaltyMovementTipo" AS ENUM ('GANADOS','CANJEADOS','AJUSTE');
EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL; END $$;

ALTER TABLE "Customer" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "puntos" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

ALTER TABLE "Tenant" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "loyaltyActivo" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
ALTER TABLE "Tenant" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "loyaltyAcumulaCada" DECIMAL(14,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
ALTER TABLE "Tenant" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "loyaltyValorPunto" DECIMAL(14,4) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "LoyaltyMovement" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "tenantId" UUID NOT NULL,
  "customerId" UUID NOT NULL,
  "tipo" "LoyaltyMovementTipo" NOT NULL,
  "puntos" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "saldo" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "saleId" UUID,
  "descripcion" TEXT,
  "createdAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT "LoyaltyMovement_customerId_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("customerId") REFERENCES "Customer"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "LoyaltyMovement_tenantId_customerId_idx" ON "LoyaltyMovement" ("tenantId","customerId");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "LoyaltyMovement_customerId_createdAt_idx" ON "LoyaltyMovement" ("customerId","createdAt");
```
> Nota: `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE` no puede ir en la misma transacción que el resto; corré **esa línea sola** primero.

- API `nest build` ✓ · POS `tsc` + `vite build` + 66 tests ✓ · Admin `tsc` + `vite build` ✓

author: basb7
body:
Both files predated multi-tenancy and neither mentioned it.

## CONTRIBUTING

**`tenancy/` was missing from the project layout** — the app holding the entire permission model was invisible to anyone arriving to contribute.

**Frontend checks listed `lint` and `build` but not `npm test`**, which CI runs at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:89`. A contributor following the document exactly could push something CI rejects. The document was wrong, not the contributor.

**New `## Tenancy invariants` section**, placed before the testing machinery so it is met before code is written. Each rule carries its reason, because *a rule without its reason gets cleaned up by the next person*:

- **No `is_superuser` bypass in the API.** The superadmin works through `/admin/`; a bypass would make the tenant boundary conditional on a flag on a user row.
- **404, never 403, across tenants.** A 403 confirms the UUID exists.
- **The capability catalogue lives in code**, not a table, so permissions version with the code and cannot drift between deployments.
- **Scoping stays join-free** — every visibility branch is a scalar `IN` subquery, which is why `.distinct()` is needed nowhere. Enforced by the `assert_membership_never_joined` fixture.

## SECURITY

**The isolation guarantee was never stated** — the important omission for a multi-tenant product. A researcher cannot tell whether what they found is a bug when nobody wrote down what the guarantee was. The new section describes what a plain member sees, the 404-not-403 rule, and why `Environment.api_key` is globally unique: the SDK header carries nothing else, so a global index is what makes the lookup well-defined.

Verified by re-running the probe rather than trusting the claim: `200` + the org name, `200` + `[]` for projects, environments and flags, `404` on every retrieve-by-UUID.

**Deployment hardening said nothing about email.** A password-reset token is a bearer credential, and `config/settings.py` deliberately selects the **dummy** backend in production when no SMTP is configured — not the console backend — so tokens are never printed to stdout where log aggregators collect them. `FRONTEND_BASE_URL`, which the reset link is built from, was also missing.

Both halves of that decision are now documented, including that `EMAIL_USABLE` is exposed through the unauthenticated `/auth/config/`, so a mail-less deployment **hides** the reset link rather than silently swallowing requests.

## Found while verifying — not fixed, because it is a policy call

**`tests/unit/` is documented as database-free, and it is not.** The layout table says *"Fast tests with no I/O"* and the guidance says *"No network or database in `tests/unit/`"*. **Eight of eleven files** there carry `@pytest.mark.django_db`.

Either the document is wrong and should describe the real tiering, or those tests are in the wrong directory. That is a decision, not a wording fix, so nothing was changed.

Also noted, neither a vulnerability nor documented: the Organization, Project and Environment list endpoints paginate unordered querysets, so DRF emits `UnorderedObjectListWarning` and page boundaries can shift between requests.

## Note on how this was produced

Both this and #43 were started against the same checkout — my error. The other agent's `README.md` edits appeared mid-run; this work was redone in a separate worktree rather than risk merging the two. `git status --porcelain` on this branch shows exactly `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md`.

author: alfoldimate
body:
Closes #61 and #62 (Phase 5 — Hardening; both verifier-confirmed before fixing).

**#61 — exact-hash gate ignores liveness.** The gate matched `(space, content_hash)` over all rows, so superseded/forgotten content could never be re-asserted, and the documented retry could close live rows in favour of a dead one (supersession cycles with zero live claims). The unique `mem_hash` index made a `WHERE` fix impossible on its own — and indexing `invalid_at` directly doesn't work either, because a unique index skips NONE columns (verified against SurrealDB 3.2.3), which would have silently dropped the concurrent-duplicate protection #64 relies on. Schema **v5** adds a computed `dedup_key` (`invalid_at ?? 'live'`, recomputed on every write) and rescopes the index to `(space, content_hash, dedup_key)`: one live row per hash stays enforced, closed rows coexist as history. The gate now selects live rows only.

**#62 — supersede rewrites another close.** Both supersede UPDATEs (batch fragment and standalone) lacked the `invalid_at IS NONE` guard `FORGET_SOFT` has always had. Now: already-closed targets are detected before the transaction, filtered out of the UPDATE, and reported — `remember`/`reflect` results gain `already_closed` (id, reason, `superseded_by`), and the standalone `repo::supersede` returns a new `StoreError::AlreadyClosed`. The in-transaction guard remains as the race backstop.

Tests: `closed_content_can_be_asserted_again` (supersede *and* forget paths, history untouched), `a_supersede_never_rewrites_another_close`, `a_standalone_supersede_refuses_a_closed_target`, and protocol-level `a_second_correction_reports_the_close_that_stands`. The `list_tools` insta snapshot is re-recorded for the new output field (output schema only — no tool *description* wording changed, so no desc-eval run).

author: hstreub
body:
Carries one commit: `docs/release-notes/1.13.0.md`, the overview that missed the tag.

**Read this before merging — it does not do what it looks like it does.**

### It will not cut 1.13.1

The range is a single `docs:` commit. The workflow's own `level_of` returns `none` for that, so Release stands down: no version bump, no tag, no release. Checked against `.github/workflows/release.yml` rather than assumed.

```
$ level_of origin/main..origin/beta
none  <- the workflow stands down, no tag, no release
```

### And even if it did, the overview still would not appear

`upgradeNotice(version)` reads `docs/release-notes/<version>.md` — **by exact version**. A 1.13.1 release looks for `1.13.1.md`, which does not exist. `1.13.0.md` only ever feeds a release called 1.13.0, and that one is already published.

Writing a `1.13.1.md` instead would be worse: a 1.13.1 release spans `v1.13.0..v1.13.1`, so its notes are the follow-up fixes alone, and an overview describing multiview, the calendar, live scores and ProVideoPlayer would be describing the *previous* release.

### So what this PR is actually for

Housekeeping, and it is still worth merging:

- the file stops being stranded on beta, so main and beta do not carry a permanent one-commit divergence
- `1.13.0.md` exists on main for the next reader, next to the release it describes
- the mechanism is in place and proven, so **1.14.0 gets its overview automatically** — write `docs/release-notes/1.14.0.md` before that tag and the generator prepends it

### What actually fixes v1.13.0's notes

Editing the published release body. The in-app update dialog reads that body, so correcting it fixes what every operator sees when they update — not just the web page. It is reversible and it is our own copy. One command, ready to go, and I have not run it:

```
gh release edit v1.13.0 --notes-file <overview + the same generated New/Fixed/Install>
```

That is an outward-facing change to a published release, so it needs your say-so, not mine.

author: marco-pacificode
body:
## 🚨 À LIRE AVANT DE MERGER — deux surfaces en production que personne n'avait listées

Trouvées par un **second** balayage, en fin de lot, sur **tous** les dépôts (le premier ne couvrait que les 5 salons + les Cores). **Ce moteur est mutualisé : la garde s'applique à elles aussi, et elles n'ont pas la forme non bloquante.**

| Surface | pm2 | Ce qui se passe au merge |
|---|---|---|
| **`Pacifik`** (Le Pacifik Koné) | `pacifik-surface` **en ligne** | `surface/lib/caisse-actions.ts` → **`creerNote`** poste `/api/sales` **sans `sessionId`, sans `occurredAt`, sans `horsSession`** → **refusé** si aucune caisse n'est ouverte. Et le message affiché serait le texte brut du moteur : **« NO_OPEN_SESSION »** à l'écran (`corpsErreur` rend `corps.error`). |
| **`ArtDuSoin`** | `lartdusoin-surface` **en ligne** | Même patron `checkoutTicket` que les 5 salons (`finance-actions.ts:583`) → refus possible, `created.error` brut affiché. **Prospect** (hors unification, Marco 22/08) — hors du lot, **pas hors du moteur**. |

⚠️ **Pour le Pacifik, ce n'est pas qu'une question de message.** Le geste refusé serait **« ouvrir une note de table »**, pas un encaissement : dans un restaurant on ouvre la note, on encaisse plus tard. 🗣️ La demande était *« que la caisse soit ouverte pour **encaisser** »* — refuser l'ouverture d'une note va **plus loin**.

**Je n'ai pas élargi le périmètre seul** : le lot m'a été cadré sur « les 5 surfaces », et étendre le rayon d'une garde d'argent à deux commerces en production n'est pas une décision d'agent.

**Trois issues, à ton choix :**
1. **porter la forme non bloquante** aux deux (le patron existe, c'est mécanique) ;
2. **les exempter** — `horsSession: true` sur `creerNote` du Pacifik (une note de table n'est pas un encaissement), ArtDuSoin laissé tel quel tant qu'il est prospect ;
3. **assumer le refus**, en n'améliorant que le message.

---

🗣️ **Marco, 2026-09-01** : « un encaissement ne devrait pas être possible sans ouvrir de caisse. » puis « il faut seulement que la caisse soit ouverte pour encaisser à partir de maintenant. »

## Le trou
`Sale.sessionId` est nullable : une vente sans session n'entre dans **aucun Z** (`closeSession` filtre sur la session) — encaissée, facturée, **absente de la clôture de caisse**. Mesuré en prod : **4 ventes / 28 700 F** sur 3 salons. Chez Ellément : ticket à **10h22**, session ouverte à **10h25**.

## ⚠️ Deux causes, une seule visible
1. **Aucune caisse ouverte** (le cas d'Ellément).
2. **Une caisse est ouverte, mais l'écran ne le sait pas** : les 5 surfaces dérivent le `sessionId` par un appel S2S terminé par `.catch(() => null)`. Le moteur hoquette, ou la page a été chargée avant l'ouverture → `null` envoyé alors que la session existe. **Aucun écran ne peut corriger ça** : l'écran est celui qui se trompe.

## 🔎 Pourquoi V-Cut a 129 ventes et zéro hors session
**Ce n'est pas le code.** Mesuré par 4 méthodes indépendantes (hash du corps de `checkoutTicket` **identique** sur les 5 surfaces, `diff -u` de `TicketLauncher.tsx`, `admin/page.tsx`, `CaisseManager.tsx`) : **aucune différence**. V-Cut est propre **par usage** — sa caisse reste ouverte. La discipline d'un salon n'est pas une garde.

## La garde
**Dans `createSale`** — le **seul** point d'écriture d'une vente du dépôt (confirmé 2× : un unique `tx.sale.create`, une unique route `POST /api/sales`). Une garde d'écran n'aurait couvert qu'un chemin sur cinq.

Règle pure et testée (`core/lib/session-obligatoire.ts`), l'ordre EST la décision :
1. remontée différée → **exemptée**, jamais refusée ;
2. session proposée et **OUVERTE** → gardée ;
3. sinon **caisse ouverte du moment** → le moteur **estampille** *(ferme la cause n°2)* ;
4. sinon → **refus `NO_OPEN_SESSION`**, **avant toute écriture**.

`POST /api/sales` répond **409** et non 400 : « l'état du serveur s'y oppose » — c'est ce que l'écran distingue pour proposer d'ouvrir la caisse.

## 🛑 Jamais un mur au comptoir
Côté surface, le 409 fait apparaître dans la fenêtre de paiement : **« La caisse n'est pas ouverte »** + fond de caisse + **« Ouvrir la caisse et encaisser »** → ouverture puis **rejeu à l'identique**. Le ticket reste ouvert, les montants restent saisis, **rien à ressaisir**. Rejouer est sûr (le refus n'a rien écrit ; l'idempotence `("rdv", appointmentId)` tient de toute façon).

## 🪤 Ce qui aurait cassé un marchand en production
**La Rôtisserie de Pouembout** (`rotisserie-surface`, en ligne) encaisse hors ligne et remonte ses ventes **`sessionId` nul, délibérément**. Une garde nue lui refusait **chaque ticket, en silence**. → exemption sur **deux marqueurs indépendants** : `occurredAt` **ou** `horsSession: true` (le second parce que `horodatage` est **facultatif** côté tablette).

## ⛔ ORDRE DE DÉPLOIEMENT — non négociable
**1.** `R-tisserie-Pouembout` → **2.** les 5 surfaces → **3. ce moteur, EN DERNIER.**
Chaque étape est **inerte** sans la suivante. **Livrer le moteur en premier casse la Rôtisserie et met un mur au comptoir.**

## Vérifié
- **CI locale GREEN** (`ci-local.sh core-caisse`, exit 0) · `tsc --noEmit` 0 erreur · **273 tests / 273 pass** (255 avant).
- Mutations rouges : garde neutralisée → 3 · ordre inversé → 1 · `return` de refus supprimé → 1.
- 🪤 Ce dernier test **a été faux une heure** : il s'ancrait sur `error: "NO_OPEN_SESSION"`, **présent aussi dans la signature**. La garde pouvait disparaître sans rougir. Trouvé par mutation, pas par relecture.
- **Aucune migration**, `sessionId` reste nullable.

## Ce que je n'ai PAS fait
Les **26 200 F** restants (Onéiti, AurelStyl) ne sont pas régularisés — 🗣️ « les autres on laisse pour l'instant ». Ce sont les pièces des marchands.

author: posidev-coding
body:
**PR 7 of 8** in the Tallboy economy stack ([docs/plans/tallboys.md](docs/plans/tallboys.md)). Based on `tallboy-onboarding` (#81) — merge bottom-up. Stands alone and is worth shipping regardless.

A "How this works" screen for the Picks area: the currency, **the cooler**, what every room costs, and the three modes.

## Its own address, not a disclosure

`/picks/how` (`picks-how`). My Picks already carries the week, the seats, the payoff and the ladder — and the Lobby folded its own rules away for exactly that reason. The door renders on **both forks** (rules get looked up mid-week as readily as on a Sunday) and the route lights **My Picks** in the section strip rather than taking a fifth slot in a four-chip row.

## Nothing on it is restated

- Mode rules → `ContestMode::ruleLines()` through the **same `x-mode-rules` card** the Lobby uses
- The shared laws → extracted to `partials/pickem-laws`, now included by both screens. Two copies of the half-point law is how the half-point law drifts
- The room grid → the **shelf** owns the price, the **engine** owns the wager
- The cooler → `GrantWalletEntry`'s own constants

A rebalance moves this screen without anybody editing it, and the tests assert against the constants rather than literals.

## The cooler marks your row

Matched by the amount `topOffFor()` would actually pay, never by re-deriving the bands on screen — two ladders is one ladder that will eventually disagree. That is what turns a rule into an answer.

## The trap, avoided

**The room grid is not a table.** Thirteen rooms across three columns is a sideways scroll at 390px, which is where the design starts and which `ChromeConsistencyTest` bans outright. One stacked card per room — name, shelf, two state chips, and the **reason underneath, always**, because a "no" with no reason reads as an oversight rather than a rule — widening to two columns above `sm`.

A new `ModeEngine::tallboyRule()` derives that reason from the same three exclusions `supportsTallboy()` applies, so a room that changes shape cannot end up with a stale sentence beside a correct answer. And a **dynamic-size** room answers **"On a full card"** rather than a flat yes: its slate is as big as the Saturday allows and a thin one puts ±5 over the leverage ceiling — promising otherwise is the same lie a numbered blurb tells over a short card.

## Verification

- New `tests/Feature/Screens/PicksHowTest.php` — 11 tests: the cooler tiers read from the constants, the reader's own row marked at both ends of the ladder, every room priced off shelf + engine (including the flavorless House row the enum cannot hold), every "no" carrying its reason, dynamic rooms answered conditionally, mode rules from the one source, **no `<table>` and no `overflow-x-auto`** with `sm:grid-cols-2` present, all three registers, the door on both forks, and the flag gate
- One existing `PickemHomeTest` assertion re-anchored: it used `assertDontSee('Tallboys')` as a proxy for "the you-strip is absent", and the word has since escaped the strip. It now asserts on a `data-you-strip` marker — same claim, measured on the right thing
- `php artisan test --compact` — 2491 tests, 8546 assertions, green
- `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent`, `npm run build`
- `/__device?path=/picks/how&w=390,768` — single column at 390, two at 768, `scrollX` 0 and `scrollWidth === innerWidth` at both, **zero `<table>` elements**, and the section strip lights My Picks
- `docs/screens.md` gains the screen's entry

author: selmetwa
body:
## What

Someone landing on `/tutor` from search hit a wall: every control on the page was gated behind `hasActiveSubscription`, so the first thing they saw was an empty composer and a paywall modal. Nothing to try, no reason to convert.

Now a non-subscriber with no conversation in progress lands straight in the **Introducing Yourself** scenario and can work through the first three Learn cards for real — hear the word, record themselves, get a pronunciation score, retry as often as they like. The paywall fires when they advance off the third card.

```
Card 1/8  🔤 New word     → record → 87% ✓ Next
Card 2/8  🔤 New word     → record → 91% ✓ Next
Card 3/8  💬 Sentence     → record → 74% ✓ Next
Card 4/8  ──── 🔒 PAYWALL MODAL ────
```

## How

**`src/routes/tutor/+page.svelte`**

- On mount, a non-subscriber with steps remaining and no conversation in progress auto-starts the `introducing-yourself` scenario. Subscribers and anyone resuming a conversation are untouched.
- `FREE_TRIAL_STEPS = 3`, persisted in `localStorage` under `tutor-free-steps-used`, so a refresh doesn't hand out a fresh allowance.
- `trialActive` is true **only** during a scenario's Learn phase for a non-subscriber with steps left. `canSpeak` (`hasActiveSubscription || trialActive`) replaces the bare subscription check on `startRecording` and `toggleLearnRecording`. Roleplay turns and typed messages still paywall immediately.
- `advanceVocab` spends a step; on the third it opens the paywall and does *not* advance. Retries on the same card are free.
- Learn-phase footer shows "✨ N free practice steps left" instead of the 🔒 Subscribe line, and "Skip intro →" is hidden during the trial so the three steps can't be skipped past by accident.

**`src/routes/api/text-to-speech/+server.ts`**

Signed-out visitors couldn't hear anything — the endpoint returned 401 and `AudioButton` popped the sign-in modal, which makes "listen, then repeat" impossible. They now get 6 plays per browser, counted in an httpOnly `anon_tts_plays` cookie (30 days), then a 403 with `requiresSubscription: true` that the existing `AudioButton` handling already routes to the paywall modal. Signed-in behaviour (5-play free allowance, DB counter, subscriber bypass) is unchanged.

## Also in this PR

**`src/lib/components/AppBanner.svelte`** — separate commit, authored by @selmetwa, unrelated to the tutor work: drops the app icon and the "Free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad" subtitle, leaving the banner as a single headline next to the badge.

## Verification

- `npm run build` passes; 30 unit tests pass.
- `svelte-check` reports no new errors in the tutor or text-to-speech files. The one `locals.auth` error on the changed line in `text-to-speech` pre-exists — confirmed by stashing.
- Against a dev server: anonymous `POST /api/text-to-speech` returned a 15KB `audio/mpeg` with `set-cookie: anon_tts_plays=1`; the same request with `anon_tts_plays=6` returned `403 requiresSubscription`.
- No browser verification — the visual flow needs a human pass. That includes the banner change, which was not checked visually or by build after being added.

## Worth knowing before merge

- **The paywall CTA is a dead end for logged-out users.** `SubscribeButton` posts to `/?/subscribe`, which redirects to `/login`. A visitor who spends three steps gets bounced to a login page rather than signup/checkout. Functional, but for a search funnel the modal probably wants a "Create free account" CTA when there's no session. Left alone as out of scope.
- **`/api/scenario-intro` now runs a Gemini call for every anonymous visitor** who lands on `/tutor`, since the scenario auto-starts. No auth check, no caching. For this scenario the inputs are fixed per dialect, so caching the three responses (or pre-generating them into a constant) would remove that per-visitor cost — worth doing before this sees real search traffic.
- **The 6-play anonymous TTS allowance is global**, not tutor-scoped: any signed-out visitor gets 6 plays anywhere `AudioButton` is used. Simplest correct implementation and the cap is small, but it is wider than the tutor page alone.
