author: tobibytes
body:
The last piece that makes sending safe to actually run. Without it the bounce rate climbs invisibly until SES suspends the account — during registration week, with every dashboard green right up until it isn't.

## It lives in atlas, not lark

A deviation from the plan, deliberately. Lark is a worker with no ingress; giving it an HTTP surface means a port, a health check, a public route and one more thing exposed, all to receive a webhook. Atlas already has all of that and already queues through lark's API, so the handler does the same and lark stays a worker.

Harbor routes `/api/webhooks/{**catch-all}` with its own generous rate-limit policy — SNS delivers bounces in bulk after a blast, and throttling them loses the record of who bounced, which is the one thing this exists to capture.

## The bug that would have been easy to ship

Signature verification is the security value here: this endpoint writes to the suppression list, so an unauthenticated one lets anybody stop an applicant receiving email — including their sign-in link. A denial of service against one person that looks exactly like a deliverability problem while it happens.

But the part that's easy to get wrong isn't the signature, it's **where the key came from**. `SigningCertURL` arrives *inside the unverified message*. Without a host check, an attacker serves their own certificate, signs their own payload with the matching key, and every signature verifies perfectly. Checking the signature but not the key's origin is the same as not checking at all.

Both controls are proven by removal:

| Control removed | Test result |
|---|---|
| cert-host allowlist | `A_certificate_from_somebody_elses_host_is_refused` — Failed |
| RSA signature check | `A_forged_signature_is_refused_and_changes_nothing` — Failed |
| both restored | 13 passed |

The tests sign with a key generated in the test and serve a matching certificate through a stubbed handler, so the real verifier runs — mocking it away would have tested nothing that matters.

## Behaviour

| Event | What happens |
|---|---|
| Permanent bounce | message `bounced`, address suppressed |
| Transient bounce | message `bounced`, **not** suppressed — a full mailbox isn't a reason to lock someone out |
| Complaint | suppressed on the first one, no grace period |
| Delivery | `delivered`, but **cannot** overwrite a bounce — providers don't promise ordering, and a late delivery notification would put a dead address back in circulation |
| Unknown message | 200 and ignored — a non-2xx makes SNS retry something we can't act on |

**Idempotent without a ledger.** SNS redelivers as a matter of course. Setting a status to the value it already holds changes nothing, and the suppression insert ignores conflicts — so there's no table of seen event ids to keep in step with reality.

## Tests

160 total: atlas 107, harbor 11, lark 42.

## To turn on

Subscribe `https://<host>/api/webhooks/ses` to the SES event topic. The endpoint confirms the subscription itself on the first request. Nothing to configure — verification uses the certificate AWS names in each message, restricted to `sns.<region>.amazonaws.com`. Documented in `docs/set-up.md`, including why staging should be subscribed too.

## Not here

`applications.message_summary`. It needs an `application_id` to project onto, and applications don't exist yet — building it now would be dead code with no way to test it truthfully. It belongs with M3.

- add digest-checked `PQDR_CONTROL_V1` / `PQDR_CONTROL_RESULT_V1` framing across Python, C ABI, runtime, HAL, and FPGA mailbox transports
- lower compiled schedules into a fixed 128-bit RTL instruction format with self-checking schedule-engine simulation
- add a capability-bound Red Pitaya board image/result contract and a 32-bit MMIO bridge
- add a runnable public Red Pitaya mailbox loopback example and protocol documentation

author: coconutbeaches
body:
## Summary

- bind the default browser `fetch` to `globalThis` before storing it on the shell controller
- keep injected test fetch implementations unchanged
- return signed-out bootstrap before initializing Postgres when no valid JuryAI session cookie exists
- add Chrome-style fetch receiver and dependency-free signed-out bootstrap regression coverage

## Root cause

The production controller stored native `window.fetch` in `#fetch` and invoked it as `this.#fetch(...)`. Chrome therefore supplied the `BrowserShellController` as the Web API receiver and threw `TypeError: Failed to execute 'fetch' on 'Window': Illegal invocation` before `/api/juryai/bootstrap` was sent. The controller caught that exception and rendered the generic initialization error even though direct bootstrap navigation returned HTTP 200 with `{"authenticated":false}`.

The Vercel Preview environment intentionally has no database URL. Signed-out bootstrap never needs Postgres, so it now returns the same private/no-store `{"authenticated":false}` response before server initialization when no valid session cookie is present. Valid session cookies still use the full authenticated server path.

body:
golang.org/x/net's real fix for CVE-2026-33814 (GO-2026-4918, malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE causing an infinite loop in golang.org/x/net/http2) ships in v0.53.0, which requires go>=1.25. This branch's go.mod declares go 1.19, so a direct module bump is not buildable here without also bumping the builder toolchain.

Uses `replace golang.org/x/net => github.com/openshift-sustaining/net v0.35.0-sec.3` (the sustaining team's own downstream fork) which backports only the CVE-2026-33814 fix without requiring a toolchain bump. Same mechanism already used by other components in this CVE (e.g. openshift/csi-operator, openshift/azure-disk-csi-driver-operator, openshift/route-controller-manager). This branch already pinned golang.org/x/net via a direct `replace`; that replace was repointed to the fork tag instead of adding a second one (Go only allows one replace per module path).

Verified: `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass with this branch's real toolchain; `govulncheck` no longer reports GO-2026-4918 for this module.

author: fpperri
body:
`kanban/archived/` moves from a flat directory to a recursively-scanned tree with optional `kanban/archived/<package>/` grouping folders. A package name is kept verbatim (no slugging) and must be one plain path component — a `.`/`..` hop or embedded separator is refused with a clear error, nothing moves.

**Store/server (`skills/web`)**
- `card-store.js`: recursive archived listing, find-by-id, restore, and delete all walk the tree; `archiveCard` takes an optional package (creates the folder on demand), is idempotent for a same-destination re-archive, never demotes an already-packaged card back to the root on a package-less re-archive, and re-files a card into a newly named package. `nextId` and dependency resolution see into packages too.
- `server.js`: `POST /api/cards/:id/archive` accepts an optional `package` body field (bodyless requests unchanged); an invalid package name returns 400. `GET /api/board` now carries `archivePackages` (sorted existing folder names).

**Web UI (`skills/web/web`)**
- Bulk "Archive selected" opens an Archive popup with a package combobox (suggest-never-validate, like the existing tag/assignee comboboxes) that completes against `archivePackages`; a blank box archives to the `archived/` root exactly as before. Drag-to-Archive and the single-card Archive action are unchanged (still write to the root). The popup follows the existing bulk-popup interaction grammar (Esc/backdrop/X cancel, no fullscreen toggle).

**Other readers updated for the recursive contract**
- `skills/kanban/scripts/{eligible_cards,show_waiting,view_board}.sh` — dependency-status resolution now globs `archived/**/*.card.md`.
- `skills/kanban/scripts/migrate_card_names.sh`, `migrate_waiting_for.sh` — walk archived recursively too.
- `skills/viewer/scripts/build_editor.py` — archived cards embedded read-only now come from an `os.walk` instead of a single `listdir`.
- `skills/kanban/SKILL.md`, `skills/cli/SKILL.md`, `skills/viewer/SKILL.md`, `skills/web/SKILL.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `README.md` — contract text updated; new ADR 0010 records the decision (rejected alternatives: a `package:` frontmatter field, sibling `archived-<name>/` dirs, slugified names).

`archived/notifications.md` is untouched — it stays at the `archived/` root; the recursive walk only ever collects `*.card.md`, so it's invisible to it either way.

**Verification**
- `node --test` in `skills/web`: 1084 passed, 0 failed (new coverage: recursive listing, package create/reuse/re-file, idempotency, traversal rejection, restore/delete from a package, the `/archive` endpoint's package field and 400 path, `archivePackages` on the board payload).
- `skills/viewer/test`: 17 passed, 0 failed.
- Manually exercised `eligible_cards.sh`/`show_waiting.sh`/`view_board.sh` and `build_editor.py` against a board with a package folder to confirm dependency resolution and card embedding both reach into it, and that `notifications.md` is skipped.

author: md-arif-shaikh
body:
pyseobnr pulls in pygsl_lite, which is published only as a source distribution and whose build calls distutils' spawn() positionally:

    spawn(cmd, 1, 1)

setuptools made those arguments keyword-only after 78.1.1, so the build fails with "spawn() takes 1 positional argument but 3 were given".

Pinning setuptools in the job environment does not help, since pip builds a source distribution in an isolated environment into which it installs a fresh setuptools from PyPI. PIP_CONSTRAINT is honoured for those build environments, so put the bound there instead. 78.1.1 is verified to still accept the positional form, hence setuptools<79.

Install swig as well: pygsl_lite swigs its GSL bindings at build time and neither the ubuntu nor the macos job had it, which is where the build would have stopped next.

author: sayinel
body:
## Summary

설계 §18.17이 "후속"으로 미뤄 둔 **반복 완료 시 다음 회차 자동 생성**을 구현한다(§318, 설계 §18.20).

M4까지 `🔁`는 사용자를 위한 메모였다 — 앱이 읽어 칩으로 그렸지만 그 값에 따라 아무 일도 하지 않았다. 이제 반복 태스크를 완료하거나 취소하면 날짜가 다음 회차로 밀리고 상태가 `[ ]`로 돌아간다. **줄은 하나 그대로다.**

```
- [/] 주간 회고 🛫2026-08-30 📅2026-09-01 🔁every week
   ↓  체크박스 한 번 (9/5에 눌러도 결과는 같다 — 원래 날짜 기준)
- [ ] 주간 회고 🛫2026-09-06 📅2026-09-08 🔁every week      + 토스트 "다음 회차 · 2026-09-08"
```

에디터 체크박스 · vim · 아젠다 · 편집 모달이 전부 같은 규칙을 탄다.

### 확정한 설계 결정 (사용자 승인 2026-09-01)

| 결정 | 값 | 왜 |
|---|---|---|
| 이력 | **줄 하나를 굴린다** | 새 줄을 만들지 않으므로 §312 불가침 규칙(줄 이동)에 닿지 않고, 기존 쓰기 원시 셋이 그대로 쓰인다. Obsidian Tasks 방식은 "특정 위치에 줄 삽입" 원시를 세 경로에 새로 내야 한다 |
| 기준일 | **원래 날짜** | "매주 월요일"이 늦게 완료해도 월요일에 선다. 대가: 오래 밀린 태스크는 다음 회차도 과거일 수 있다 |
| 규칙 범위 | 간격 + 요일·평일 | 손으로 쓴 파서로 끝난다. `rrule`(RFC 5545)은 번들 ~40KB이고 §0의 "가볍다 ~10MB"와 거래해야 한다 |
| 취소 `[-]` | **굴린다** | "이번 주는 안 한다"가 반복 규칙을 죽이면 안 된다. 끝내는 방법은 `🔁`를 지우는 것 |
| 날짜가 없으면 | 그냥 완료 | 밀 날짜가 없으면 규칙이 놀고 있는 것이다. 칩이 그렇게 말한다 |
| 설정 | **없음, 기본 켜짐** | `⏱`와 갈리는 자리 — `⏱`는 켜져 있으면 사용자가 쓴 적 없는 새 필드가 적히지만, 굴리기는 이미 적은 `🔁`가 있는 줄에서 이미 적은 날짜만 바꾼다 |

### 문법

저장 문법은 **영어 하나**다. `🔁` 줄은 남의 도구도 읽으므로 지역화하면 상호운용이 깨진다(§303이 이모지 포맷을 canonical로 고른 것과 같은 이유). 화면 표시만 로케일을 탄다.

`every day` · `every N days` · `every week` · `every N weeks` · `every month` · `every N months` · `every year` · `every N years` · `every weekday` · `every week on <요일>` · `every month on the <N>st`

**모르는 규칙은 `null`이고, `null`이면 줄을 건드리지 않는다.** M4 `parseTimer`가 `⏱30분`을 `0m`으로 읽지 않는 것과 같은 원칙 — 추측해서 굴리면 남의 도구가 적은 줄을 우리가 고쳐 쓴다.

**월말은 접는다.** `every month`로 1/31에서 굴리면 2/28이고 다음은 3/28이다(되돌아가지 않는다). rrule은 해당 월을 건너뛰지만 "3월에 이 태스크가 안 뜬다"가 "3월 28일에 뜬다"보다 더 놀랍다고 봤다. `every month on the 31st`가 탈출구이고, 그 형태는 2/28에서 3/31로 스스로 회복한다.

## 설계에서 배운 것 셋

**1. 새 쓰기 종류를 만들지 않았다.** `TaskChange.state`에 이미 "프런트가 계산해 온 값"의 자리(`timer`)가 있어 굴린 날짜를 그 옆에 둔다. 그래야 **트랜잭션 하나 · 낙관적 잠금 하나 · Ctrl+Z 한 번**이다. 별도 쓰기로 내면 그 사이에 낀 stale이 "상태는 굴렀는데 날짜는 안 굴린" 줄을 만들고, 그 줄은 자기가 몇 회차인지 말하지 못한다.

**2. 결정이 한 곳에 있다.** 상태 전이는 이 코드베이스에서 두 번 구현돼 있고(에디터는 PM 트랜잭션, 아젠다는 디스크) 그것은 사고가 아니라 설계다 — 에디터 경로가 디스크를 타지 않는 것이 존재 이유다. 갈라도 되는 것은 *어디에 쓰는가*뿐이므로 *무엇을 쓰는가*를 `resolveStateWrite` 하나로 뽑았다. 두 언어의 테스트가 같은 두 줄을 단정한다(`task-item-control.test.ts` ↔ `write.rs`).

**3. `record_done_date`가 공짜가 아니었다.** 설계 단계에서 "`Todo`는 스탬프를 안 찍으니 기존 ✅ 제거가 공짜"라고 적었는데, 그 설정이 **꺼져 있으면** `apply_state`가 스탬프를 떼기 전에 일찍 돌아간다는 것을 구현 중에 봤다. 거짓으로 넘기면 `[ ]`인데 완료일이 붙은 — 자기가 끝났는지에 대해 두 가지를 말하는 — 줄이 남는다. 굴리기는 설정과 무관하게 참을 올려 보내고, Rust 테스트가 그 잘못된 호출이 무엇을 만드는지까지 고정한다.

## 함께 고친 기존 결함 (M4)

**반복 구간의 끝이 다음 필드의 시작이었다.** 앱 확인에서 드러난 증상은 셋 중 가장 가벼운 것이었다 — 반복 칩 뒤의 구분 공백이 사라져 다음 칩의 점이 글자에 붙었다(`every week on Monday 반복• 9/3 기한`). 그 공백이 구간 안에 들어가 원문과 함께 감춰졌기 때문이고, 같은 원인이 셋을 만든다:

| 조작 | 종전 결과 |
|---|---|
| 표시 | 다음 칩의 점이 글자에 붙는다 |
| 반복 **편집** | `🔁every 2 weeks📅2026-09-03` — 두 필드가 붙는다 |
| 반복 **삭제** | `➕2026-09-01📅2026-09-03` — 같은 일 |

뒤의 둘은 **사용자 파일에 남는다.** 구간을 값의 끝으로 좁혔다. 값 *앞*의 공백은 그대로 둔다(`🔁 every week` — Obsidian Tasks가 쓰는 형태이고 필드의 일부다).

M4가 이 경계를 고칠 때 물은 것은 "값이 어디까지인가"였고 그래서 `value`는 `trim()`으로 옳았다. "구간이 어디까지인가"는 따로 묻지 않았다 — 값은 인덱스가 읽고, 구간은 화면이 감추고 쓰기가 덮는다.

## 곁들여 정리한 것

- Rust `set_task_state`·`apply_state`의 인자를 `StateWrite`로 묶었다. 인자 수 때문이 아니라 넷이 한 전이의 서술이기 때문이고, M4가 달았던 `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` 둘이 그것으로 없어졌다.
- 손으로 적은 `TaskState::FromStr` 표가 사라졌다 — 두 방향이 이제 같은 `rename_all`에서 파생되므로 어긋날 수 없다.
- `ipc-registry.json`의 `set_task_state`·`preview_task_state_line` 항목을 갱신했다(M4의 `timer`가 빠져 있었다).

## 알아 둘 것 — 남긴 결함 하나

**필드를 고칠 때 에디터와 디스크가 다른 줄을 만든다.** 필드가 이미 §303 순서를 벗어나 있으면 TS `applyTaskField`는 제자리에 덮어쓰고, Rust `apply_field`는 canonical 자리로 옮긴다. 실측:

| 입력 | 조작 | 에디터 | 아젠다·디스크 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a ⏱1h 📅2026-09-01` | `⏱`→`30m` | `a ⏱30m 📅2026-09-01` | `a 📅2026-09-01 ⏱30m` |
| `a 🔁every week 📅2026-09-01` | 기한 밀기 | `a 🔁every week 📅2026-09-08` | `a 📅2026-09-08 🔁every week` |

M4의 `⏱`부터 있던 것이고 §305의 불변식("디스크 경로와 열린 문서 경로가 같은 바이트를 낸다")을 어긴다. 이 PR이 만든 것이 아니라 더 흔하게 만들 뿐이다.

**고치지 않은 이유**: 어느 쪽이 옳은지가 설계 결정이다. TS를 Rust에 맞춰 봤더니 13건이 적신호였고 그중 하나가 진짜였다 — 한 줄에 `📅`가 둘일 때 첫 번째를 옮기면 **인덱서가 읽는 필드가 바뀐다**. 반대로 Rust를 TS에 맞추면 `insertToken`의 주석이 적어 둔 의도("사용자가 손으로 적은 비정규 순서를 조용히 뒤집지 않는다")와는 맞지만 아카이브·태그까지 성질이 바뀐다. 되돌리고 별건으로 남겼다.

author: zachhowe
body:
Two syntax changes to how types and their members are spelled, plus the three bugs that
writing the tests for them uncovered.

## Member accessors are spelled `Type-member`, not `Type/member`

`(HttpResponse/status-code r)` is now `(HttpResponse-status-code r)`. Field access read as a
namespace qualification rather than a field selection, and it did not match Racket, where a
struct accessor is a plain hyphenated identifier. `/` was also the most overloaded character
in the language — module path, CLR member path, `super/` call, tuple index — and field access
was the one use carrying the least distinct meaning.

- Applies to every type-derived binding: record and struct fields, class fields (own and
  inherited), class methods, interface methods. The type name keeps its declared spelling.
- The old spelling still resolves and reports the new `ZS0006` deprecation warning naming its
  replacement. Resolution happens once, in the type inferer, which rewrites the name onto the
  node — so a program using the old syntax emits byte-identical C# to one using the new.
  Disable with `--no-warn-deprecated-accessor-syntax` or the manifest's
  `warn-deprecated-accessor-syntax`; the language server offers a quick fix.
- The fallback only fires for a genuine accessor (first parameter is the type that names it),
  so an undefined `foo/bar` still reports `ZS0001` rather than redirecting to `foo-bar`.
- Hyphen-joining can collide: `(define-record Foo-bar [baz])` and `(define-record Foo [bar-baz])`
  both mint `Foo-bar-baz`; the later declaration wins.

## Capitalisation no longer decides what is a type name or a case pattern

`http-response` names a type as much as `HttpResponse` does. Two places still read the first
letter:

- The `: Base IFoo IBar` run in `define-class`, `define-interface` and `(object ...)` ended at
  the first non-upper-case item, so a hyphenated base was dropped and then reported as a stray
  member. The run now ends at what cannot be a type name at all — a `#:` flag or a `:` keyword.
  `TypeNameScanner` mirrors it, to keep the language server in step.
- In `match`, a bare atom was read as a variable binder unless upper-case, so a nullary case
  named `red` bound instead of matching and silently swallowed every later arm. The type
  inferer now rewrites such an atom into the constructor pattern it was meant to be, at every
  pattern depth, before the arm is inferred — so exhaustiveness checking, IR lowering and both
  emitters see an ordinary constructor pattern.

## Three bugs found while writing the casing tests

Each was filed as an issue and fixed in the following commit.

- **A derived class constructor call dropped every inherited field.** `IrLowering` zipped the
  call site's arguments against the class's *own* fields while the inferred type and both
  emitters included the inherited ones. `(Derived 1)` type-checked, then the IL backend
  returned an object with every inherited field at its default. Registration now prepends the
  base chain, and the call site reports an arity mismatch instead of zipping past it.
- **Interface inheritance was only one edge deep.** `Unifier.IsZSchemeSubtype` compared against
  the directly declared list and gave up; nothing fed it either, since an interface's base list
  was recorded nowhere. The lookup now answers with direct supertypes and the Unifier walks the
  closure breadth-first. Recording the base list also gives an inherited interface method its
  accessor.
- **The IL backend left an interface's inherited methods unimplemented.** The set deciding
  `NewSlot | Final` was collected transitively for a CLR interface and one edge deep for a
  ZScheme one, so the inherited method emitted as a plain instance method. ilverify passed it —
  a missing vtable slot is a type-load check — and the CLR then refused the type on first touch.
  csc gets this right for free, so it was a silent backend divergence.

## Testing

New: `TypeNameCasingTests`, `DerivedClassConstructorTests`, `InheritedInterfaceMethodTests`,
`DeprecatedAccessorSyntaxTests`, `ImportedAccessorSyntaxTests`, `EmitNameResolverTests`, plus
`AstBuilderTests` cases. Existing examples and package sources are updated to the new spelling.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: copilot
body:
The `CI / test (3.9)` job was failing during test collection because several newly added modules and tests use PEP 604 union annotations (`X | Y`) that were being evaluated at import time on Python 3.9. This change restores Python 3.9 compatibility without changing runtime behavior.

- **Compatibility fix**
  - Added `from __future__ import annotations` to the affected production and test modules that use PEP 604-style annotations.
  - This defers annotation evaluation so Python 3.9 can import the files successfully while keeping the existing type syntax.

- **Touched typing cleanup**
  - Updated a few touched annotations/imports in `jf/runners.py`, `jf/ml_runners.py`, and the e2e test helpers to keep the edited files internally consistent with the postponed-annotation model.

- **Regression guard**
  - Added `tests/test_py39_annotations.py`, which AST-scans `src/` and `tests/` for real `X | Y` annotations and requires `from __future__ import annotations` when they are present.
  - This avoids a repeat of collection-time breakage from future annotation-only changes.

```python
from __future__ import annotations

def _load_paraminput(path: str | Path):
    ...
```

author: althaf0097
body:
💡 What:
Memoized radial gradient canvas texture generation and particle position array calculation inside `FloatingParticles` (`HeroThreeScene.jsx`) using `useMemo`.

🎯 Why:
Previously, every render of `FloatingParticles` allocated a new 900-element `Float32Array`, created a new HTML `<canvas>` element, rendered a 2D radial gradient onto it, and instantiated a new `THREE.CanvasTexture`. This caused memory leaks and garbage collection bottlenecks in Three.js/React Three Fiber rendering loops.

📊 Impact:
- Prevents 100% of redundant DOM canvas creations and GPU texture re-allocations on component re-renders.
- Reduces GC churn and main-thread overhead during 3D background animation.

🔬 Measurement:
Verified through code review and `pnpm build` / `pnpm lint` execution.

author: tortellion
body:
## Summary

Fixes all 5 P0s confirmed by the independent 8-agent production-readiness audit (`docs/audits/`, merged to `main` in a separate pass). This is Phase 0 of the completion plan — nothing here is new functionality, only correctness and security fixes to what already exists. Verified against a real Postgres, RLS enforced as the actual `ssp_app` application role (not superuser).

## What's fixed

**P0-1 — Live, reproducible crash.** `setProgramTagsAction` queried `pursuit_tag.program_id`, a column migration 028 renamed to `pursuit_id` five migrations earlier. Every tag-edit save threw in production. Root cause: zero tests exercised `src/app/actions.ts` (the real UI-facing boundary) — every test called `lib/actions` directly, one layer beneath the bug. Added `tests/actions-boundary.test.ts` + `tests/helpers/server-action.ts`, which mock only the two things that require a real Next.js request scope (`next/headers`'s `cookies()`, `next/cache`'s `revalidatePath()`) so the actual server action runs against a real database. Confirmed the new test fails on the original bug and passes on the fix.

**P0-2 / P0-3 — Export-control RLS bypass on NCR and RMA.** `ncr.program_id` and `rma.unit_id` were each the *sole* column their table's RLS policy read, and both are ordinarily null in real, common states — an NCR may reference only `work_order_id`/`unit_id`, and an RMA's `unit_id` is null for its entire normal intake window before a serial is matched. `program_is_export_controlled(NULL)` silently resolves to "not controlled," so a real controlled record was visible to every session regardless of eligibility.

Migration `037_export_control_does_not_trust_a_null.sql` derives export-control status from every reference each row actually carries. This needed two new `SECURITY DEFINER` helper functions (`unit_is_export_controlled`, `work_order_is_export_controlled`) — `unit` and `work_order` carry their own export-control RLS, so a naive correlated subquery from the NCR/RMA policy would run as the same restricted session and hide the very row it's trying to check, silently resolving to "not controlled" one hop over. Caught this the hard way: my first version of the fix looked correct and still had the bug, found by testing against a live RLS session rather than trusting the SQL by inspection. Also caught and fixed a NULL-propagation bug in my own fix (a bare `COALESCE` inside a subquery that returns no rows at all doesn't run) via the same live-test discipline.

Added 4 new regression tests to `tests/export-control.test.ts` — NCR via `unit_id` only, NCR via `work_order_id` only, RMA before serial-matching, and the negative case (an uncontrolled RMA stays visible).

**P0-4 — Shipment release checked paperwork, not manufacturing.** The release trigger validated UN38.3 certification but never checked that a unit's traveler (Final QC included) had actually passed. `tests/production.test.ts`'s own fixture proved the gap: a unit with zero station results shipped successfully. `trg_shipment_release` now also blocks on `unit_traveler_state <> 'PASSED'`, naming the serial. Added 3 new regression tests (zero station results, every station but Final QC, a station that failed after the rest passed — hold takes precedence). Fixing this surfaced that two *other* existing tests (`despatch before release`, `UN-number-not-applicable`) were also unknowingly relying on the same gap; fixed their fixtures to pass the traveler as unrelated setup.

Also fixed `src/lib/operations.ts`'s `blocking` column — a hand-duplicated preview of "what would refuse release," used by the shipment list/detail screens — which only knew about the certification check. It now matches the trigger exactly, so it stops telling a shipping user "nothing is blocking" when release will actually fail.

**P0-5 — Two critical CVEs on pinned dependencies.** `next` 15.1.6 → 15.5.25 (clears the middleware auth-bypass advisory and the CVSS-10 React Flight RCE; stayed on the 15.x line rather than jumping to Next 16, since a patch bump carries far less migration risk than a major version). `vitest` 2.1.8 → 3.2.7 (clears a critical RCE in its dev API server — dev-only, never shipped, but cheap to fix and worth doing). `npm audit`: 11 vulnerabilities (2 critical) → 4 (0 critical), remainder all moderate/high in transitive dev-only build tooling (`postcss`/`esbuild`, several majors deep). Also fixed a Next.js config deprecation warning (`experimental.typedRoutes` → `typedRoutes`) surfaced by the bump.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npm run build` — clean, all 24 routes compile, no warnings
- [x] `npm run test` — **316/316 passing**, run against a real Postgres 16 with the actual `ssp_app` least-privilege role and RLS enforced (not superuser)
- [x] Manually verified both RLS fixes with direct SQL against a live session before trusting the test suite
- [x] Manually reverted P0-1's fix and confirmed the new test fails with the exact original error, then confirmed it passes with the fix restored

## Sequencing note

This is Phase 0 of a larger completion plan. PR #2 (`claude/ssp-program-tracker-spec-vcep07`, draft) adds real UI for opening NCRs and RMAs — which would make the P0-2/P0-3 bypasses *reachable* for the first time if merged before this. This branch should merge first, or PR #2 should rebase onto it, before PR #2 ships.

This also adds `db/migrations/037_...sql`. If PR #2's own `037_the_event_vocabulary_explains_itself.sql` merges around the same time, one of the two needs renumbering to `038` before both land on `main` — migration filenames must stay unique and ordered.

body:
golang.org/x/net's real fix for CVE-2026-33814 (GO-2026-4918, malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE causing an infinite loop in golang.org/x/net/http2) ships in v0.53.0, which requires go>=1.25. This branch's go.mod declares go 1.19, so a direct module bump is not buildable here without also bumping the builder toolchain.

Uses `replace golang.org/x/net => github.com/openshift-sustaining/net v0.35.0-sec.3` (the sustaining team's own downstream fork) which backports only the CVE-2026-33814 fix without requiring a toolchain bump. Same mechanism already used by other components in this CVE (e.g. openshift/csi-operator, openshift/azure-disk-csi-driver-operator, openshift/route-controller-manager). This branch already pinned golang.org/x/net via a direct `replace`; that replace was repointed to the fork tag instead of adding a second one (Go only allows one replace per module path).

Verified: `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass with this branch's real toolchain; `govulncheck` no longer reports GO-2026-4918 for this module.

author: geridovich
body:
## Что и зачем

Заход в `frame()`. Главная находка здесь не в объёме, а в **дубле**: итоговый экран уже
считает место вынесенной формулой (`placementOf` в `endScreen.ts`), а кадр считал его
**второй раз вручную** — та же сортировка по убыванию итога, тот же `indexOf`, набранные
заново. Две рукописные копии одной формулы расходятся молча: живая строка сказала бы
«3-е из 5», а конец матча объявил бы другое место, и игрок не поймёт, которой верить.
Модуль зовёт ту же `placementOf`.

Новый модуль `prototype/src/standingLine.ts` + тесты рядом. Семь правил с причинами:

1. **Место — из ТОЙ ЖЕ формулы, что и на итоговом экране.**
2. **Пустая таблица очков — НЕТ строки места.** `indexOf` не нашёл себя ⇒ место 0;
   напечатать его значило бы объявить «1-е из 0» до старта матча. Молчание честнее.
3. **«Нужно ещё» не уходит в минус.** Перебор порога — это победа, а не «нужно −40».
4. **Признак победы выводится из ТОГО ЖЕ остатка, который показан игроку**, а не из
   отдельного сравнения со счётом: два сравнения разъезжаются на округлении, и подсветка
   загорается не тогда.
5. **Позывной падает на имя ДОМА, а не в пустоту.** Соло-места названы домом
   (`buildSetupConfig`).
6. **Подпись перерисовки несёт КАЖДОЕ видимое поле.** Поле, которое видно на экране, но не
   попало в подпись, замораживает строку на прошлом значении — и виноватым выглядит что
   угодно, кроме подписи.
7. **Поля в подписи разделены символом, недостижимым в тексте.** Иначе позывной «3» с
   местом 5 неотличим от позывного «35» без места: разные состояния дают одну подпись.

Разделитель тот же самый, но записан теперь явной экранированной формой `''`, а не
невидимым байтом внутри шаблонной строки.

**Поведение не менялось.**

## Проверка

- `pnpm run check` — зелёный: **5325 тестов, 405 файлов**.
- **Сверка перебором** со старым инлайном (временный `_sweep191.test.ts`, снят после):
  144 сличения места, числа мест, счёта и остатка (12 таблиц очков — пустая, без меня, с
  ничьими, дробными, отрицательными и равными итогами × 3 «себя» × 4 порога); те же 144
  против обеих старых тернарных проверок; 21 сличение позывного (7 форм ввода × 3 имени
  места); 756 сличений подписи против старого шаблона байт в байт.
- Prettier-разница `main.ts` **не изменилась**: 218 строк и до, и после (замер на месте у
  обеих сборок; первая форма деструктуризации давала 229 — поправлено под предпочтение
  prettier).
- `node prototype/build.mjs` + `pnpm run smoke:browser` — чисто.
- **Живой A/B** (`scratchpad/live191.mjs`, соло-матч, две сборки по два прогона): все пять
  узлов строки до входа в матч, на старте, после ввода позывного и после разгона времени.
  - Правило 5 видно прямо в снимке: с пустым полем стоит имя дома **«Azure Compact»**,
    после ввода — **«Ворон»**, у обеих сборок одинаково.
  - Место живое: за разгон оно поменялось **#1 of 2 → #2 of 2** (соперник обошёл по очкам)
    в обеих сборках — значит, подпись перерисовки на него срабатывает.

  Расхождение только в отсчёте до суток внутри одного и того же Дня 6, и это дрожь: база в

author: ayyitskevin
body:
Closes the codex seat's seven findings on the Gate 2 write-up. **Draft** until sol returns GO.

Two commits: `f0df1a2` makes the evidence real, `c1e96c0` rewrites the interpretation against it.

## The finding that mattered

The runner **computed both evidence classes and serialized neither**. `thinkingChars` was calculated and dropped; retrieval v3's omission arrays and exclusion counts were returned and dropped, leaving `baseCommit` and two digests. A digest commits to a result but is not its preimage.

That is not abstract. My verification of the first run read `thinkingChars` and `omittedMatches` out of those records, got nothing, and reported *"zero thinking characters across all 60 executions"* and *"no case had a query match withheld"* — **absence read as measurement, in the validation of the run meant to demonstrate this defect class was fixed.**

Evidence record revision 4 → 5. Both are now written.

## The other three mechanical findings

- **The setting was bound as a value, not a transmission.** ADR 0070 claimed removing `think: false` fails the security suite. Deleting `think: generation.think` at the call site left the policy digest and its unit test green. Both halves are asserted now; probed by deletion, which fails `gate2SuppressesReasoningAndRecordsWhatItObserved`.
- **Evidence could be overwritten by a later policy.** Backups were keyed on `evidenceRecordRevision` alone, so a run under a different instruction policy found the existing backup and overwrote the record it should have preserved. Keyed by revision *and* producing-policy digest now.
- **The `.d.mts` still declared revision 8** while runtime emitted 9.

## Re-run, and a near-miss worth recording

The first re-run reported success in 6 seconds with all the new fields present and identical numbers. It had made **no provider calls** — `reassessedFrom` populated, `latencyMs` and `rawCandidate` byte-identical. A reassessment wearing a fresh run's clothes. Notably `reasoningChars` came back **`null`, not `0`** — the fix working as designed, correctly saying "not recorded" rather than claiming a measurement.

Archived that set and ran fresh. All 60 cases now carry `reassessedFromEvidenceSha256: null`.

| | baseline `code-fast` | routed `code` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| success | 2/30 | 12/30 |
| first-plan acceptance | 0.0667 | 0.60 |

Reproduced exactly across two full executions. `reasoningChars: 0` measured on all 60, 60/60 `stop`, 60/60 provider-reported, empty candidates 8 → 1.

## The three interpretation findings

- **Disclaim-then-use, removed.** The causal claim is gone. The result refutes *pure displacement* and is *consistent with* reasoning contributing; it does not identify reasoning as the cause, since the figure sets came from different budget contracts and no reasoning-enabled arm was run.
- **Over-broad ruling-out, narrowed.** "Not context starvation" → "no query match was excluded by a file or byte ceiling". Says nothing about files that never matched lexically, reference-hop candidates, or pre-candidacy exclusions; macro recall is 0.9917, not 1.0.
- **The empty case, investigated.** `scaffold-lantern-json-output`: 0 content characters in **112 provider-reported output tokens**, clean stop, zero reasoning. Neither content nor reasoning. Where they went is unknown and the record says so.

## Verified

Node 22.23.2, `pnpm check` **exit 0** — 1282 unit, 206 integration, 354 security. `git diff --check` clean.

author: sehyun0518
body:
#46 의 **결정 1·3**을 닫는다.

## 문제

`readonly: true`인 역할이 넷인데 **넷 다 `Bash`를 들고 있다.**

```text
review                  Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
test-runner             Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
accessibility           Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, mcp__playwright
project-design-inspect  Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
```

검증기는 `Bash`를 `filesystem: read`로 분류한다. **선언끼리는 앞뒤가 맞지만 `Bash`로는
쓰기도 삭제도 푸시도 된다.** `filesystem`·`network` 두 축이 도구 하나로 우회된다.

#49에서 이 구멍을 일부러 케이스로 박아 뒀었다.

```js
test('Bash는 readonly 검사가 잡지 못한다 — 알려진 한계 (#46)', ...)
```

## 결정 — 런타임이 없는 곳에서 런타임을 얻는다

**이 저장소에는 런타임이 없다(ADR-0002). 그런데 플랫폼에는 있다.**

`.claude/settings.json`을 생성 대상에 넣고 `requiresApproval` 선언을 그 파일의 permission
규칙으로 투영한다. **런타임을 만들지 않고 처음으로 실제 강제를 얻는다.** 지금까지 런타임에
전달되던 안전 정보는 "도구 목록" 하나뿐이었고, 그 목록의 가장 넓은 항목이 `Bash`였다.

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "ask":  ["Bash(gh pr comment:*)", "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
             "Bash(gh pr edit:*)", "Bash(git push:*)"],
    "deny": ["Bash(git filter-branch:*)", "Bash(git push --force:*)",
             "Bash(git push -f:*)", "Bash(git reset --hard:*)", "Bash(rm -rf:*)"]
  }
}
```

### 무엇이 승인 대상인지는 표가 정하지 않는다

`capability.yaml`의 `requiresApproval`이 단일 출처다. 표는 **어떤 명령 패턴으로 옮기는지**만
안다. **양방향으로 대조한다.**

```text
✗ git-operations#push: requiresApproval인데 permissions.json에 명령 패턴이 없다.
  선언이 런타임에 도달하지 않는다.
✗ permissions.json의 "git-operations#없는변형": 그런 변형이 없거나 승인을 요구하지
  않는다. 표가 오래됐다.
```

둘 다 생성 실패다 — #49의 `VALIDATOR_REGISTRY`와 같은 모양이다.

### `deny`는 어떤 변형도 선언하지 않은 것

`destructive-approval`의 rationale이 네 범주에 이름을 붙였다 — **푸시·PR 생성·이력
재작성·파일 삭제.** 앞의 둘은 변형이 선언하고 승인을 받는다. **뒤의 둘은 어떤 변형도
선언하지 않는다.**

선언되지 않은 파괴적 작업은 승인 대상이 아니라 **금지 대상**이다. 승인은 "이 역할이
하기로 선언한 일을 지금 해도 되는가"를 묻는 것이고, 아무도 선언하지 않은 일에는 물을
것이 없다. 각 항목이 왜 있는지를 `why`로 함께 적었다.

## `Bash` 분류는 바꾸지 않았다

`filesystem: write`로 올리는 안이 가장 정직하고 검증기만으로 끝난다. **그런데 역할 넷의
선언이 전부 깨진다.** `test-runner`는 테스트를 돌려야 해서 `Bash`가 필수인데 `readonly`를
포기하면 "제품 코드를 고치지 않는다"가 사라지고, `accessibility`는 ADR-0007이 안전성을
거기 걸고 있다. **필드가 존재하는 이유를 지우면서 정직해지는 것**이라 택하지 않았다.

그래서 **#49의 한계 케이스는 그대로 둔다.** 이 결정은 그 구멍을 검증기에서 막지 않고
런타임에서 좁힌다 — 두 개는 다른 축이고, 케이스가 초록인 동안 검증기 쪽은 여전히 비어 있다.

## ADR-0007의 거짓 문장을 정정했다

> `accessibility`의 도구에서 `Write`와 `Edit`가 빠졌으므로 **파일을 쓸 수단이 없다.**

사실이 아니다 — `Bash`가 있다. 그 ADR이 기대는 안전이 무엇인지 다시 적었다.

## 계약은 건드리지 않았다

ADR-0013·0014에서 스키마 셋(`capability` · `profile` · `workflow`)을 연달아 고쳐
`ADR-0002` C1의 시계를 되돌렸다. **이 결정은 생성물만 늘린다.**

## 검증

```text
21개 선언 파일 검증 통과.
ℹ pass 99  ℹ fail 0
Summary: 0 issues in 0 files
드리프트 없음.
```

회귀 **92 → 99건**.

## ⚠️ 병합하면 바로 효과가 있습니다

`git push`와 PR 생성이 **확인을 묻게 됩니다.** `destructive-approval`이 요구하는 그대로지만
작업 흐름이 바뀝니다. `deny` 다섯은 되돌릴 수 없는 명령이라 막힙니다.

`ask` 대상이 셋을 넘어가면 파괴적 작업 선언 자체를 다시 보라고 ADR 재검토 조건에 적었다.

## 짚어둘 것

**생성물의 성격이 처음 늘었다** — 지금까지 전부 "역할 정의"였고 이건 "저장소 설정"이다.
소비 저장소가 이미 `settings.json`을 갖고 있으면 충돌한다. **이 저장소 자신의 미러만
다루고 소비 저장소로의 투영은 열어 뒀다.**

**패턴이 실제로 무엇을 막는지는 플랫폼이 정한다.** 문법이 틀리면 조용히 아무것도 막지
않을 수 있고 이 저장소는 그걸 검사할 수단이 없다. 그래서 패턴을 선언이 아니라 생성기
표에 뒀다 — 틀리면 선언을 건드리지 않고 고친다.

author: davidgraymi
body:
## Summary

ADR 0004's billing section, end to end. `subscriptions` and `subscription_access_overrides` key on `gitea_org_id`, Stripe carries the org id on the customer and the subscription, and the paywall asks which organization a session acts for before it asks whether anyone has paid.

The point is ownership, and it is the same point as the rest of the ADR: a subscription keyed to whoever signed up first walks out of the building when they do. Gitea renames organizations too, so a name key breaks silently — the id is the only thing that survives both. `bindersnap_username` still rides along on Stripe as support metadata, but it is never a key.

`resolveAccess` is now the ADR's precedence list in one function: `admin_revoke`, `admin_grant`, Stripe `active`/`trialing` with the existing 3-day grace, the local trial, then nothing. The ADR argues that keeping it in one place is what makes two sources of access truth affordable, and this is that place.

### Two things you should look at before anything else

**1. A new signup now lands in its workspace, not at a card form.** #369 is explicit that there is no card during the 14-day trial, and the ADR makes the trial a local column rather than a Stripe `trialing` subscription precisely so we don't create a customer and a subscription for every tire-kicker. That means the current funnel — signup redirects straight to `/billing` — contradicts the design, and this PR changes it. `tests/signup.pw.ts`, `tests/document-collaborators.pw.ts` and `tests/stripe-subscription.pw.ts` now assert the new behaviour. **If you want to keep the card-up-front funnel, say so and I will make the trial opt-in instead** — but the two cannot both be true, and the ADR is the newer decision.

**2. A trialing customer could not have paid us.** `App.tsx` bounced anyone with `subscriptionStatus === "active"` off `/billing`, and a trial now counts as active — so the trialing customer would have been redirected away from the only page where they could subscribe. That redirect now fires only for a Stripe-backed subscription. This was a real dead end introduced by the trial, not a cosmetic tweak.

### The migration, which is the risky part

Mapping a username to an organization needs Gitea, and SQL cannot reach it. So migration `0002` does only the half it can do correctly: it **parks every existing row verbatim** in `legacy_username_subscriptions` / `legacy_username_subscription_access_overrides` and rebuilds the live tables org-keyed and empty. Nothing is dropped.

`scripts/backfill-org-billing.ts` does the mapping half. It never deletes a legacy row, reports every username it could not map instead of guessing, is safe to re-run (every write is an upsert on the org id), supports `--dry`, and stamps `bindersnap_gitea_org_id` onto the matching Stripe customer so later subscription webhooks can reconcile. Dropping the legacy tables stays a separate, later, deliberate act. Six tests cover it, including "reports an unmappable username instead of guessing" and "re-running is safe".

**Ordering for a real deploy:** ship this, run `--dry` and read it, run it for real, confirm the app behaves, and only then drop the legacy tables. Between the migration and the backfill, an org whose row has not been mapped yet falls back to its trial or to no access — so run the backfill promptly rather than leaving it for a later day.

### The admin console

Still addressed by person, because that is what an admin can name — but an override now applies to that person's whole organization, every row carries the organization it belongs to, and browsing walks organizations and labels each row with one of its owners. Granting access to someone with no organization is a 404 with a message saying why, rather than a silent no-op. A follow-up could make the console organization-first; this keeps the existing SPA working.

### Also in here

- `services/api/session-organization.ts` — one Gitea call to answer "which organization is this session?", never a cached table, because membership is Gitea's and a copy that disagreed would be wrong in the direction that matters.
- `createPrivilegedGiteaClient` extracted out of `server.ts` so the backfill script can use the same one.
- API schema and generated client extended: `trial` and `no_organization` access sources, `organization` and `trialEndsAt` on the billing payload.
- `reconcile:stripe-customer` takes `--org <id>` instead of `--username`.

## Scope Check

- [x] Changes are focused on one issue/task
- [x] No unrelated refactors or formatting-only churn included

## Validation

- [x] Local validation/tests run (list commands below)
- Commands run:
  - `bun test services/api scripts infra/backups` — 445 pass, 0 fail
  - `bun test apps/app packages/editor packages/utils` — 370 pass, 0 fail
  - `bun run test:seed` — 22 pass, 0 fail
  - `bun run format:check` — clean
  - `bun run db:check` — clean
  - `bunx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors

Integration tests could not be executed here (this environment's egress policy blocks the container-registry blob hosts, so no stack can start). CI runs them, and the three integration specs listed above are the ones to watch on this PR.

author: bdt17
body:
Roadmap step 6 — the last one. The integration an Enterprise buyer expects: excursion and custody events POSTed to the customer's own WMS/ERP as they happen.

## What

- **`WebhookEndpoint`** — one URL + HMAC signing secret per organization. URL validation is strict about **SSRF**: HTTPS only, and the host must resolve *entirely* to public addresses — loopback, RFC1918, link-local (including the `169.254.169.254` cloud-metadata address), "this network" and multicast are all rejected. Re-checked at delivery time too, since DNS can change after the endpoint is saved.
- **`WebhookDispatcher.publish(organization:, event:, data:)`** — the single fan-out point. A no-op unless the org is on the **Compliance** plan and has an active endpoint, so it's safe to call unconditionally. Wired into `ExcursionNotifier` (`excursion.started` / `excursion.resolved`) and `CustodyLogsController` (`custody.recorded`).
- **`WebhookDeliveryJob`** — signed POST, `X-PharmaTransport-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of raw body>` + `X-PharmaTransport-Event`. Retries timeouts / 5xx / 429 with polynomial backoff (5 attempts); a 4xx stops immediately. `consecutive_failures` counts failed **events**, not retry attempts, and an endpoint **auto-disables after 10 in a row**.
- **`/webhooks`** page (new sidebar item) — admins add/remove endpoints, see the signing secret and last delivery status, send a test event, and re-enable an auto-disabled endpoint. Upgrade prompt for orgs below Compliance.

Migration `…000005` (`webhook_endpoints`). No new gem — `Net::HTTP`.

## Testing

- `bin/rails test` — 435 runs, 0 failures (+27): `WebhookEndpoint` (secret gen, HMAC, the full SSRF matrix, uniqueness, auto-disable/recover), `WebhookDispatcher` (plan gate, per-endpoint fan-out, envelope shape), `WebhookDeliveryJob` (signs + posts, 2xx/4xx/5xx handling, inactive/private-URL skips, retry-exhaustion records failure — `Net::HTTP` stubbed), `WebhookEndpointsController` (gate, admin-only, cross-org isolation, test/enable/remove), plus `ExcursionNotifier` and `CustodyLogsController` webhook assertions
- `bin/rails test:system` 7/0 · `rubocop` / **`brakeman` (0 warnings — SSRF guard holds)** / `bundler-audit` / `db:seed:replant` clean
- Verified an end-to-end delivery against `https://httpbin.org/status/200` — real DNS resolution passed the SSRF check, the signed POST landed, `last_success_at` recorded

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Per-endpoint event-type filtering (currently every endpoint gets every event)
- A delivery log / replay UI
- Add an actual `enterprise` Stripe tier (gated on `compliance` for now, the top existing tier)

Independent — branched off current `main`.

author: jordanfanapour
body:
## Problem

A Skip agent run died mid-demo after burning all ten retries — roughly four minutes and 79K completion tokens — regenerating the same broken response. The response was a 28KB PRD whose `functionalRequirements` field embedded a mermaid ER diagram. The model had escaped every newline correctly but left the diagram's own quotes raw:

```
vwMembers ||--o{ vwInvoices : "has invoices"
```

A `"` inside a JSON string value ends that string. One character invalidated the document. Three separate defects meant it was neither recoverable nor correctly reported.

## Root causes

**1. `CleanJSON` discarded the response over an interior fence.** Once the top-level parse failed for any reason, fence extraction ran unconditionally. That regex has no idea it is looking *inside a string value*, so the ` ```mermaid ` fence matched, its contents were extracted, the JSON envelope was thrown away, and `CleanJSON` recursed into the fragment.

The real error — `Expected ',' or '}' ... at position 23011` — was replaced by ``Unexpected token 'm', "mermaid\ns"...``, describing a phantom problem in text nobody sent.

**2. The repair chain reasoned from that wrong error.** `attemptJSONRepair` receives whatever escaped `JSON.parse(CleanJSON(rawOutput))`. That message was handed to the AI repair prompt as `ERROR_MESSAGE`, recorded on the prompt run, and re-thrown. The repair model was asked to fix an unexpected `'m'` in a mermaid fragment when the actual defect was one quote at a known offset.

**3. Nothing could repair an unescaped quote.** JSON5's leniency covers trailing commas, comments and unquoted keys — but an unescaped `"` terminates a string in JSON5 exactly as in JSON. The only remaining fallback was an LLM round-trip on the full payload: slow, costly, and unreliable at that size.

The irony: the mermaid diagrams that trigger the defect are also what disabled the repair meant to fix it.

## Changes

**`@memberjunction/global`**
- `CleanJSON` skips fence extraction when the input is already shaped like a JSON envelope. A genuinely fence-wrapped response starts with the fence and a prose-buried one starts with prose, so neither path is affected.
- Its throw now carries the untouched parse error as `cause`.
- New `RepairJSONEscaping()` — error-driven, one character per pass, re-parsed after each: read the failure offset, walk back to the character that ended the string early, escape it, re-parse, repeat.

**`@memberjunction/ai-prompts`**
- `resolveTrueParseError()` derives the error from the raw output directly.
- The lexical pass runs in `attemptJSONRepair` between the JSON5 and AI stages.

**`@memberjunction/ai-core-plus`**
- `_jsonRepairInfo` gains a `LexicalEscaping` method and records the offsets escaped.

## Why this is safe

Escaping a quote that legitimately ended a string would merge two pieces of structure, so this is deliberately constrained:

- It runs **only after a parse has already failed** — a correct document is never touched.
- It only ever **adds** escapes; it never deletes or reorders content.
- Every pass is **validated by a real parse**, so it cannot pattern-match its way to a wrong answer the way a global regex rewrite would.
- It **gives up rather than guessing** — truncated output is explicitly not "repaired" into something that parses but misrepresents the model.
- It **reports every offset it changed**, so repairs are auditable. A rising count is a signal that model output is drifting and a prompt needs attention.

## Verification

Replayed against **16 real failing production payloads** (3 conversations, 2 orgs, 3 days):

| | result |
|---|---|
| recovered | **16/16** |
| characters escaped | 180 |
| total time | 12ms |
| escapes-only (removing inserted backslashes reconstructs the original byte-for-byte) | 16/16 |
| valid response shape | 16/16 |

Against **34 already-valid payloads**, 20 of them containing markdown fences — the exact shape that trips the old fence handling: **zero false positives**, and zero damaged by the fence guard.

Old vs new `CleanJSON` on the same 16: the real defect was hidden behind a phantom error **16/16** before, and reported with its true position **16/16** after.

Replaying the production failure end to end: JSON5 fails (`invalid character 'h' at 21:21245`), lexical repair fixes 12 characters in **0.61ms**, and the AI stage is never reached.

Build and tests green on `next` for all three packages — **32 test files, 870 tests passing**, including 13 new ones covering interior fences, `cause` propagation, both legitimate fence-extraction paths, quote and control-character repair, the backslash-run edge case (`\\"`, where the quote is *not* escaped), and the refusal to "fix" truncated output.

Test fixtures are synthetic payloads shaped like the real ones — no client data in the repo.

## Field results

Across a subsequent 5-suite, ~1,100-prompt-run eval session: **1 lexical repair fired and succeeded, 0 unrecovered parse failures, 0 retry-exhaustion terminations.**

author: jsongo
body:
## 背景

PR #283 合并后，图表/可视化相关能力分散在 `visualization`（新增）与既有的 `excalidraw` 两个技能，二者在「画流程图/架构图/示意图」等触发词上语义重叠，且 `visualization` 正文完全没提内置的 `generate_chart` 工具，模型可能手写 HTML 重复造轮子。本 PR 做两件事：**描述消歧 + 统一可视化路由**。

## 改动

### 1. excalidraw 并入 visualization（核心）
- 删除独立 `excalidraw` 技能，原正文改为 `visualization/references/excalidraw.md` 工作流参考（git 识别为 100% rename，历史保留）
- `excalidraw` 专属的 `references/dsl-syntax.md`、`NOTICE.md` 一并迁入 `visualization/references/`（NOTICE 改名为 `excalidraw-NOTICE.md` 避免与技能级 NOTICE 混淆）
- `visualization/SKILL.md` 路由树新增两个分支：
  - **对话内精确数据图表** → 优先用内置 `generate_chart` 工具（Web 交互卡片 + PNG 降级），工具不适用才手写 HTML/Chart.js/SVG
  - **需落盘可编辑图文件**（Obsidian/.excalidraw/手绘风/动画图）→ Excalidraw 工作流（引用 references/excalidraw.md）
  - 判断口诀：**对话里看 → generate_chart/mermaid/SVG；vault 里存 → Excalidraw**
- `excalidraw.md` 顶部加 reference 使用说明 + 与上级技能的分工边界
- 顶层 `NOTICE.md` 的 excalidraw 归因指向新路径

### 2. ui-card ↔ visualization 描述消歧（上一 commit）
- 两技能 description 各加分工边界句 + 正文各加对称「分工」节

## 边界澄清（本次不做）

- **feishu-writer / lark-sheets / ppt-generate / lark-whiteboard**：交付格式技能（飞书文档/表格/PPT/画板），图表只是内部能力，触发词场景限定明确，不并入 visualization。
- **generate_chart 工具本身**（`ethan/tools/builtin/chart.py`）是代码层能力，无法塞进 prompt 技能，保持工具形态不动，只由 visualization 技能在路由中引用。

## 已知既有良性重叠（不在本 PR 处理）

`ui-card` 与 `task-and-schedule-manager` 共享 trigger 词「时间线」，语义不同（引擎管理 vs 卡片展示形式），同时注入无副作用。

## 验证

- `visualization`、`ui-card` 两技能 `load_skill_from_file` 实测加载通过
- 全库 grep 确认无残留独立 `excalidraw` 触发词，代码层无对 excalidraw 目录的硬编码依赖
- 纯文档/技能文件改动，ruff / CI 不受影响

body:
## What

Aligns the inline GitHubService test-double's method signatures to the real `GitHubService` class in `ResyncSingleAppMetadataTest`.

## Why

The test's anonymous `extends GitHubService` double overrode methods with signatures incompatible with the real class (e.g. `parseUrl($repo)` vs the real `parseUrl(string $repo): bool`). Under PHP 8.3 an incompatible override is a fatal error at class-declaration time, so the whole file fataled before any test ran.

Invisible because CI has only ever run the access_affinitygroup module's tests (D8-2829); this test never ran. The fix reconciles every overridden method to the real signature (param and return types), preserving the double's existing behavior — the double now honors the real contract instead of diverging from it. `GitHubService` itself is unchanged; the real code was correct.

## Testing

Goes from a hard PHP 8.3 fatal (0 tests executed) to `OK (2 tests, 50 assertions)`. No assertion failed on merits — the only problem was the class-declaration fatal. Test-only change.

author: rafaumeu
body:
Closes #49

## O quê

Primeira fase do WT-5 (spec no Obsidian: "PIANO Web - TVs e Monitores (Palco no web)"): **relay WebSocket** que permitirá web operador + TVs se comunicarem **sem o desktop aberto**. Ambos viram clientes WS da API.

## Arquitetura

```
[Web operador] ──WS──┐
                     ▼
        [piano-api /v1/palco/relay/:code]  ← retransmite estado, sem banco
                     ▲
[TV receiver] ──WS───┘
```

- **POST `/v1/palco/sessions`** → `{ code, token }` (código curto 6 chars, token HMAC)
- **WS `/v1/palco/relay/:code?token=...&role=operator|sender|receiver`**
  - `operator` (1 por room) publica estado do palco para todos
  - `sender` (0..N) publica status de slots para operator+receivers
  - `receiver` (0..N, as TVs) só assina; late-join recebe o último estado
- Fire-and-forget em memória: TTL 30min, máx 500 rooms, máx 32 clients/room, msgs ≤64KB
- Sem PII; token é HMAC-SHA256 do código (`PALCO_RELAY_KEY` ou fallback `REMOTE_SESSION_KEY`)

## Infra

Primeiro WebSocket do projeto: `@hono/node-ws` + `ws`. **Gotcha descoberto e documentado no código:** o `upgradeWebSocket` precisa estar registrado no **mesmo app raiz** que roteia — registrar em sub-app com helper apontando pro sub-app retorna 404 no handshake (validado com spike).

## Testes (116/116)

- 11 unit (`palco-relay.test.ts`): papéis, roteamento, late-join, TTL/falha segura, stats
- 6 E2E com WS real (`palco-relay-ws.test.ts`): operator→receiver, receiver read-only (API recusa), token inválido → close 4404, segundo operator → 4409, late-join recebe último slide, 2 receivers recebem o mesmo estado
- CI paths: `npm run lint && npm run build && npx vitest run`

## Próximas fases (fora do escopo)

- WT-5b: receiver browser com modo "código de sessão"
- WT-5c: web `stage-relay.ts` + QR no card
- WT-5d: Tizen/webOS/AndroidTV

body:
## Summary

Michał's call from the 0.5.31 test: **the switch turns off the model, not the bubble** - the bubble's visibility on ordinary pages has its own two controls ("Only in the reader", "No bubble when selecting text"), and the trim hiding them was what overrode them.

- **New protocol message `look-up`** (`{ text } → DictEntry[]`): an ordinary page has no dictionary database in reach, so it asks the background; the reader page keeps reading its own (D121). No pair chosen answers an honest empty list, not an error. The content side narrows the answer through `asDictEntries` - the same validation the translation's entries always went through, now exported. One `sendMessage` per selection, i.e. the same cost the engine path always had.
- **`pageMode`**: under the trim with a pair chosen, ordinary pages **read** again - the quiet-vocabulary bubble (dictionary meanings as presses, the pencil, Save, underlines, recall) works there exactly as in the reader. "Only in the reader" keeps its say, platform defaults included (Android still launches); "No bubble when selecting text" still outranks everything; the trim **without** a pair keeps today's launcher-only behavior.
- **Settings and popup**: the "Only in the reader" row is no longer `translation-only`; the saved-phrases door stands wherever a pair is chosen.
- **Renames and honest texts** (all six locales + README): the switch is now **"Use without a translation model"** (Michał's wording); its hint, the popup note, the model-missing error and the pair hints stop claiming the bubble, underlines and saved phrases are gone - with a pair they are not.

## Test plan

- `tools/check.sh` green: typecheck, tests (new: `look-up` request validation, `asDictEntries`, `pageMode` under the trim with a pair, `popupRows` with the pair input), build, addons-linter 0/0/0.
- Smoke (Michał), on the next signed test build - T665-T667 in SMOKE-TESTS:
  - Trim on + en→pl dictionary, an ordinary page (e.g. reapps.eu): selecting a known word shows the quiet bubble with pressable meanings; saving underlines it on the spot; recall and Learned work; a longer phrase takes a typed meaning via the pencil.
  - "Only in the reader" on: ordinary pages show the launcher again; off: they read. The switch is visible in settings and popup with the trim on.

author: shimakaze09
body:
Addresses #347.

## Prioritization

Sixth and final unit of the run — the last P2 that is fully verifiable headless and file-disjoint from every other unit and open PR (`editor.cpp`/`editor_session.h`/`editor_console_capture_test.cpp` are untouched elsewhere this run).

## Re-verification against current main

Confirmed on `a314b27`: `initialize_editor` registers console capture (`editor.cpp:274`) before the two ImGui backend inits, and both failure paths destroy the ImGui context but return without `console_capture_shutdown()` (or clearing `editor_session().sdlWindow`). `console_capture_initialize` guards registration on `g_sinkRegistered`, and `shutdown_logging` clears the core sink table — so after a failed editor init plus the core restart, a retried bootstrap skips registration and silently loses every Console diagnostic.

## Root cause and fix

The failure paths released only part of what initialization had acquired. Both now roll back the console-capture registration and the session window pointer, in the same relative order `shutdown_editor` uses. This is the issue's "one rollback path for every acquired resource" applied to the resources those paths actually leak; the earlier acquisitions (cvar registrations are process-lifetime by design, the layout module and style carry no cross-bootstrap poison) need no undo.

**Test seam, disclosed:** the real failure points are the ImGui backends, which headless CI cannot make fail (bgfx uninitialized asserts rather than returning false, and the SDL backend needs a real window). A `editor_set_initialize_failure_for_tests` switch — following the existing `*_for_tests` seam pattern (`editor_layout_set_directory_override_for_tests`, `dbg_fail_frame_stage`) — forces the failure at the backend step, after every earlier resource is acquired, so the production `initialize_editor` drives its own rollback path in the test.

## Scope / closure table (issue #347)

| Requirement | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Failure returns without shutdown → rollback every acquired editor resource incl. console sink and session pointers | Fixed | Both failure epilogues release console capture and clear `sdlWindow`; `check_failed_editor_init_does_not_poison_capture_retry` |
| Regression: inject failure after sink registration, reset core, retry, assert one sink and one console entry | Fixed | The new check: forced `initialize_editor` failure → `shutdown_logging`/`initialize_logging` (the core restart's sink-table clear) → `console_capture_initialize` → one logged error captured as exactly one Console entry |
| "One scope guard for every acquired resource" as a structure | Partially fixed | The rollback is complete but written as explicit epilogues matching the existing two-path shape, not restructured into a scope-guard object — a refactor beyond the defect's minimal closure. The leak itself is closed |

Observation recorded while testing, pre-existing and untouched: `ImGui::AddFontFromFileTTF` hard-asserts (aborts) on a missing font file, so `initialize_editor`'s "falls back to the built-in font" comment only holds in release builds; a debug editor launched from a working directory without `assets/` aborts before the fallback. Worth its own issue if the audit agrees.

## Verification (Linux headless, GCC 13.3, Ninja Debug, `-DENGINE_BGFX_SHADERC=OFF`)

- **Red-on-base**: the seam and the fix live in the same failure paths, so red-on-base restores the base rollback behavior (context-destroy only) while keeping the seam — the technique PR #359 recorded. Under the committed test: 67/68, failing exactly at "the retried session captures diagnostics again". Green 68/68 with the fix.
- **Suite**: full `ctest -LE gpu` 218/219 — sole failure `engine_integration_asset_packer_orphan_sweep`, the pre-existing uid-0 container artifact, identical on an untouched baseline.
- **Build**: zero first-party warnings. Comment audits: presence 676 files pass, quality 0 findings.
- Platform scope: Linux headless; other platforms rest on CI.

body:
The `Build AppImage` Actions job failed in the clean-environment smoke test when Python `ctypes` attempted to load bundled `libmpv.so.2`. The container image lacked `libSDL2-2.0.so.0`, a required runtime dependency of `libmpv`.

- **Root cause**
  - Smoke step runs inside `ubuntu:24.04` and intentionally installs only host-delegated runtime libs.
  - `libmpv.so.2` dlopen failed due to missing `libSDL2-2.0.so.0`.

- **Workflow change**
  - Updated `.github/workflows/release.yml` in the `build-appimage` smoke-test container package list.
  - Added `libsdl2-2.0-0` to the apt install set used before running `smoke_dlopen.py` / `smoke_lifecycle.py`.

- **Impact**
  - Keeps packaging model unchanged (media stack still bundled in AppImage; host stack still delegated).
  - Removes the false-negative smoke failure caused by incomplete host runtime provisioning.

```yaml
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
  python3 \
  libgtk-3-0t64 libglib2.0-0t64 libasound2t64 libpulse0 \
  libsdl2-2.0-0 \

author: sidorovanthon
body:
## Summary

Adds optimistic concurrency to admin event writes: a new `events.version` column (migration `0031_events_version`), an `ETag: W/"<version>"` on every admin event response that carries a detail, and a required `If-Match` validator on the six state-changing commands (`publish`, `open`, `close`, `archive`, `mark-ended`, bare `transition`). A missing validator is refused `428 PRECONDITION_REQUIRED`; an unparseable or stale one is refused `412 PRECONDITION_FAILED` with «reload and retry». Two admins acting on the same event from stale reads can no longer silently overwrite one another.

## Product note (RU)

Раньше два администратора, открывшие карточку одного и того же вебинара, могли по очереди нажать «Опубликовать» / «Открыть комнату» / «Завершить» — и второе действие молча перетирало первое, хотя человек видел на экране уже устаревшее состояние события. Теперь каждое такое действие проверяет, что администратор действует по актуальной версии карточки: если событие успели изменить, действие не выполняется, а на экране появляется отдельное сообщение «Это мероприятие только что было изменено. Данные на этой странице уже обновлены до актуального состояния. Можете повторить своё действие.» (формулировка утверждена владельцем продукта дословно) — карточка при этом сама перечитывается, поэтому повтор действия делается одним кликом, без перезагрузки страницы. Недопустимый по статусу переход по-прежнему объясняется своей фразой. Действия по актуальной карточке работают как раньше.

## Linked

- Closes #1593
- Spec: `apps/docs/content/specs/features/007-event-admin-minimal/` and `apps/docs/content/specs/features/014-event-recordings/`

## Type

- [x] feature
- [ ] bug
- [ ] chore
- [ ] refactor
- [ ] docs

## Author

- [x] author:claude
- [ ] author:codex
- [ ] author:human

## Delivery evidence

Stage-B: GO — owner (Product Lead) live pass on the lead-booted stand (api :3000 / admin :3200, head 85c7f4a5), 2026-09-02, verbatim «По предмету проверки теперь всё ок, принимаю.»; the off-platform mark-ended label question raised in the same message is outside this PR (014 EARS-18 / #1597) and is routed separately.
Changeset: `.changeset/events-optimistic-concurrency.md` (`@ds/api` major, `@ds/schemas` major, `@ds/db` minor — rationale in the file)
Behavior change: the six admin event commands now require an `If-Match` validator (`428` when absent, `412` when unparseable or stale), and admin event detail responses carry `version` plus an `ETag` header.
Local touched-suite verification: `pnpm --filter @ds/api test` against the branch stand DB — 1463 tests PASS across 169 files; the new spec `apps/api/test/admin/optimistic-concurrency.e2e-spec.ts` is 32/32 PASS on re-run after the Mode-a rework; `pnpm --filter @ds/admin test` — 109 PASS across 15 files (incl. the two `lifecycleCommandRequest` rows and the four new `lifecycleErrorOutcome` rows, all red before their fix); `pnpm --filter @ds/admin lint` and `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/admin` are both clean. At head f207cd5b: `turbo lint typecheck test --filter=./apps/admin` — 6/6 tasks successful (incl. 3 new RED-first `data-provider.test.ts` rows), and the new live spec `apps/admin/e2e/lifecycle-stale-refusal.spec.ts` PASS against the running stand (api :3000 / `ds_dev_1593`, admin production build :3200): two tabs, edit in B bumps the version, publish in A answers 412 with the approved copy, the event stays draft, the same click then succeeds. Two untouched api specs are known-at-base: they behave identically when re-run at base `c96495a7` in this same worktree — `apps/api/test/auth/zitadel-otp-login.e2e-spec.ts` (empty stand SMS sink) and `apps/api/test/taxonomy/idempotency-media.e2e-spec.ts` (`SLUG_CONFLICT` answers 400 where 409 is expected). Neither touches events.
Deviations: N/A — no ADR/spec deviations

## Judgment calls (recorded for review)

1. **`PATCH :id` and `PUT :id/stream` bump `version` but do NOT require `If-Match`.** The Issue scope is the six state-changing commands; the authoring writes participate in the version stream (so a concurrent edit still invalidates a held validator) but stay unconditional. Extending the precondition to the authoring writes is a possible follow-on, not a gap in this slice.
2. **A domain `409` is evaluated BEFORE the stale-version `412`.** Guard order in the service is closed-set → extra guard → `assertMarkEndedAllowed` → `assertVersion` → write, so `INVALID_TRANSITION` / `EVENT_NOT_PAST` win: a request that is illegal at every version gets the reason it is illegal, not «reload and retry».
3. **`EventAdminListItem` deliberately carries no `version`,** and the list read emits no `ETag` — a validator belongs to a single addressable resource, and the OpenAPI document models only `EventAdminListDto`, so the SDK regen (`pnpm generate:api-client`) produced no diff.
4. **`If-Match` joins the `mark-ended` idempotency fingerprint** (`{ method, path, ifMatch: rawIfMatch }`). The key makes a RETRY of *this exact request* safe; the validator makes the request conditional on the revision the operator read. Two consequences, both now asserted: an idempotent REPLAY must send the SAME validator on both calls (a `mark-ended` replay test that re-read the validator would be a different request), and **after a `412` the client must mint a NEW key as well as re-read the validator** — the same key against the reloaded validator is a `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, not a replay.
5. **`mark-ended`'s `412` is deliberately NOT fenced-stored.** `storeTransitionRefusal` fence-stores only a deterministic domain `ConflictException`; a stale-validator refusal is a property of the caller's read, not of the bound request, so it is not a verdict worth replaying. (This is *not* a claim that the old key becomes replayable — see call 4: the correct retry after a `412` is a fresh key plus a reloaded validator, which the new `EARS-18` reuse test pins down.)
6. **A bare integer `If-Match` is accepted** alongside the weak form `W/"<n>"`, and `*` is refused `412` rather than treated as an unconditional match (this API has no create-if-absent semantics on these routes).

## Test coverage

- New `apps/api/test/admin/optimistic-concurrency.e2e-spec.ts` — a six-row command table × four contracts each (`428` absent, `412` unparseable, `412` stale then reload-and-retry succeeds, happy path where the response `ETag` and the body `version` are both `held + 1` and the spent validator is refused), plus: create/detail emit `W/"1"`, `PATCH` bumps to 2, bare-integer validator accepted, domain `409` precedes `412`, `mark-ended` key-shape and `EVENT_NOT_PAST` precede `412`, `404` on an absent event, `401` precedes `428`.
- `If-Match` sweep over the existing admin suites (`publish`, `archive`, `room-control`, `transitions`, `state-single-source`, `edit-event`, `stream-config`, `events/mark-ended`, `taxonomy/event-directions`, `taxonomy/event-projects`), each via a local `ifMatch(id)` helper.
- `apps/api/test/auth/{admin-authz-floor,admin-session-separation,mfa-*}.e2e-spec.ts` are deliberately unchanged: they assert `401`/`403` from guards that run before the handler, so no validator is needed.

## Migration note

Migration tag `0031_events_version` (`events.version integer not null default 1`). The migration-collision gate was re-run and is CLEAN. #1633 / PR #1702 also carries tag `0031` and rebases after this branch — **#1593 lands first**.

## Mode (a) rework (review 5073982491)

- **BLOCKER — the admin client half.** `apps/admin/components/lifecycle-actions.tsx` fired every lifecycle command through `useCustomMutation` with no `meta`, so `providers/data-provider.ts` attached no `if-match` and all five operator commands would have been refused `428` after merge. Fixed: the request is now built by a pure `lifecycleCommandRequest(detail, command)` in `apps/admin/lib/lifecycle.ts`, which carries `meta: { version: detail.version }`. Extracting the builder is what makes the contract testable in the admin's node unit tier (the c

author: hiamandacowell
body:
A Cardboard lens is round and sits in a round hole, so the corners of each half-screen are behind the housing and were never reaching your eye. Blacking them is what the viewer does physically; showing them is a lie about how much you can see.

**I removed them on the previous change on the strength of a misreading.** The complaint was that putting the images in circles did nothing about the *blurriness* — a complaint about blurriness. The circles had been asked for, twice. I recorded the opposite, wrote it into the previous PR as fact, and acted on it.

## Drawn on purpose, not left over

Getting the shape by building the warp the other way round — so the screen's edges fall off the edge of the rendered texture — throws away real picture to do it, and leaves a ragged edge whose size drifts with the coefficients. This masks a **correct, complete, screen-filling** image, so there's as much inside the circle as there is anything to show, and the edge is feathered because a hard one crawls.

Two details that matter:

- The mask is measured on each vertex's **own position** — where it ends up *after* the warp moved it — so the hole stays round instead of following the bend in the picture.
- It's measured in the same units across as down, so it's round **on the glass**, not round in the picture. Those differ on a half-screen that isn't square.

## Knob

`LENS_MASK = 1` makes each circle as wide as its half of the screen, the usual fit. Lower it if your viewer's hole is smaller; `0` removes it.

Verified at a simulated 2× 900×500: two circles, centre divider, no shader compile errors.

**Submitter note**

Model: GPT-5
Harness: Codex

# KVQ-STACK-001 — fused q4 live write with deferred BF16 maintenance

## Context

This candidate is based directly on promoted Q4 crown `b695936`, official
composite `2.20181139339287`. Candidate tip `d0cfdf6` adds deferred BF16
maintenance in two editable files; the active composed path also uses the
promoted, byte-unchanged q4 kernel in the third file listed below:

```text
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/AttentionV1.swift
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/RaggedTwoPassDecodeAttentionV1.swift
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/SequenceKV/WindowedSequenceKV.swift
```

The promoted batch-eight D256 sliding-attention road reads retained KV from a
packed q4 mirror. Crown `b695936` already moves the fresh-token q4 pack/write
into attention pass A. It still performs two functional BF16 full-ring updates
per token. This candidate defers those remaining updates until BF16 is consumed.

The combined default removes both families of intermediate maintenance from the
timed chain. Pass A packs the fresh BF16 K/V token itself, consumes those packed
words directly for the logical current-token position, and writes the identical
words in place to the evicted q4 mirror slot for the next step. The exact BF16
producer arrays are retained in a bounded journal and committed only before a
BF16 semantic consumer.

No target weight, target quantization, attention accumulation, output token
policy, sampling rule, scheduler rule, prompt handling, harness code, or scoring
code changes.

## Q4 live-write half

For each current token, fused pass A applies the same q4g64 packing rules as the
promoted packer: four groups of 64 values per D256 head; fp16-rounded affine
scale and bias; `metal::rint` quantization clamped to `[0,15]`; low-nibble-first
packing into 32 payload words plus four metadata words. It uses those local
words for the logical last token and writes them to physical slot
`absoluteOffset % 1024` for future steps.

No attention block reads the slot it writes. Every historical token uses the
pre-existing mirror, while the current logical token uses pass-A local values.
The promoted score order, online-softmax reductions, BF16 partial rounding, and
pass-B combination order are unchanged.

The in-place q4 side effect is sealed by the existing per-layer decode-write
fence. Pass A returns partials/sums/maxima and a one-element integer fence. Pass
B consumes the first three outputs; the layer cache retains the fourth as an
async-eval root; the next pass A consumes it before reading the mirror. This
provides both current-output and next-step dependencies without a host sync.

Kill switch:

```text
MLX_KV_Q4_FUSED_WRITE=0
```

When disabled, the separately retained q4 pack/update road remains available in
the same executable.

## Deferred BF16 half

The fused q4 output does not read the retained BF16 K/V rings, so rebuilding
both full-ring values every token is dead work until a BF16 consumer appears.
Each row journals the exact `(keys, values, absolutePosition)` producer arrays,
updates logical counters immediately, and keeps a constant-time byte ledger.

The journal holds one complete 128-token ranked window. The 129th serial token
flushes the preceding 128 before appending. Across all 25 sliding layers and 8
rows, maximum retained payload is about 200 MiB, small beside the resident model
and already-allocated BF16 rings.

At flush, positions must be contiguous. Producers concatenate on token axis and
the established modular `writeRing` helper writes at most two slices per plane,
covering a wrap exactly as per-token writes do. The journal clears only after K
and V update graphs exist.

Every BF16 consumer or cache-mode transition flushes first: generic update,
explicit ring write, BF16 views, fused-BF16 bookkeeping, speculative begin and
commit, snapshot, both borrow APIs, fast-forward, rollback, and q4 fallback.
Thus stale BF16 state is never exposed.

Producers are already dependencies of the q4 mirror write consumed by the same
step's attention output. Their retained handles preserve the exact BF16 payload.
They are not redundantly exported as thousands of additional async-eval roots;
actual cache roots remain BF16 K, BF16 V, and q4 mirror.

Kill switch:

```text
MLX_KV_DEFER_BF16_RING=0
```

The switches are independent, preserving four diagnostic arms in one worker:
incumbent, q4-only, deferred-only, and combined.

## Combined admission and fail-closed fallback

Admission is all-or-none across all eight rows before host state mutates. The
combined path requires:

- cohort width 8 and one-token decode;
- a storage-owning layer with an explicit in-place-write fence;
- eight full 1024-token window rings without an active speculative transaction;
- queries BF16 `[8,16,1,256]` and K/V BF16 `[8,8,1,256]`;
- q4 mirrors uint32 `[2,8,1024,36]`;
- scale exactly 1 and the promoted q4 reader enabled; and
- q4 simulation and byte-check diagnostics disabled.

After the fused kernel admits, each row either journals BF16 and advances once
or, with deferred maintenance disabled, performs the incumbent BF16-only write
and advances once. If fused q4 refuses before mutation, the independently
validated separate-pack deferred road can run. If that q4 attention call also
refuses after mirror/counter advancement, its journal flushes before the
established BF16 reader, without a second append.

Partial rings, prefill, D512 full-attention layers, alternate shapes/dtypes,
speculative transitions, cache borrowers, disabled q4, and diagnostic packing
modes retain established paths.

## Validation

The stack passed from a fresh worktree:

```bash

tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh --all-build-roots
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions
git diff --check engine/main..d0cfdf6
```

Observed before note finalization:

- 583 original tests in 22 suites passed, zero failures;
- the complete vendored metallib compiled and was published beside the debug
  bundle and scored-worker root;
- the scored worker linked successfully in 140.85 seconds from a fresh build;
- the trusted release build linked successfully in 139.19 seconds; and
- `git diff --check` produced no output.

After Q4 promoted, `git diff 30fb8ae..b695936` was empty: Yukon's promoted
tree is byte-identical to the locally validated Q4 parent. Only the deferred
commit was replayed onto `b695936`; the new tip has that crown as its exact
parent, and `git diff --check engine/main..d0cfdf6` remains clean.

The untracked runtime probe is outside the editable submission surface. It
constructs 25 storage-owning sliding layer caches, 8 rows per layer, 16 query
heads, 8 KV heads, D256, and full 1024-token histories. Every step uses engine-
style asynchronous evaluation over attention outputs and cache roots. Each arm
runs in a separate process because both switches are process-static.
