author: tmd913
body:
## One refresh button

`Refresh from ESPN` was in the fantasy popover **and** on the league settings page — two doorways to one action, which is the duplication the search bar's own close button was retired for. It is one icon square in the header now, beside the button that opens the popover, and it does a different thing under a similar name.

`refreshAll` busts the server's ESPN caches (`?refresh=1` on ownership, which clears every entry for the league, and on transactions — the two reads nothing else re-asks) and **then reloads the page**. The order is the whole of it: a bare reload would re-read the same ten-minute answer the server is already holding.

A failed bust still reloads — the page a reader asked for is a fresh page. Offered whether or not a league is connected. No `MIN_SPIN`, since what follows the press is a reload.

A refresh is not a *setting*, which is why it is a peer of the gear and the baseball rather than an entry inside either.

## The report behind it, chased down in the logs

> "it takes a really long time to load… it also shows a 500 afterward even though it eventually loads the content"

Four 500s in the last week, and every one of them the same thing:

```
2026-09-01 03:59:15  /api/espn/ownership     500  29027ms
2026-09-01 03:59:15  /api/report             500  29028ms
2026-09-01 03:59:15  /api/espn/roster        500  29018ms
2026-08-31 21:32:14  /api/espn/transactions  500  29022ms
```

`Task timed out after 29.00 seconds` — three in the same second on three separate invocations. Against a slowest *cold* route of **7.3s** (`/api/report`) that is not this code being slow; it is an upstream going quiet, and `fetch` having no default timeout, so a hung connection is a `try` that never reaches its `catch` and the request rides to the Lambda's limit.

**`upstream.ts`** wraps the global `fetch` with a **15-second** deadline — twice the slowest cold route, three times the slowest single read (Savant's 4.4s per-player season CSV), half the platform's 29. The global rather than a helper, because the forty call sites that matter are the ones nobody thought about. It leaves a caller with its own `signal` alone, and it does not retry.

**And the resume reload's queue drain is capped.** Past 30 minutes the page is already replaced rather than refreshed, and it drains `queueUserWrite` first so a preference saved in the last breath survives. Uncapped that waits for ever on a request suspended across the absence — the browser resumes it into a connection that is gone. It races `RELOAD_DRAIN_MS` (2s) now: losing the race costs one preference, not capping it costs the page.

## Two live-only game-page marks

**The line score marks one cell, not the column.** Both cells were washed, which drew a game in the top of the 7th as though both clubs were batting in it. The header keeps the column (it names the inning); the wash is on the half in play. `Top` alone marks the away row — MLB's `Middle` and `End` are the gaps either side of the *home* half, which `isBottom` gets wrong for `End`. Measured in `Bottom 8`: header 8 marked, home 8th cell marked, away not.

**The box score marks the man each club has up** — the batter in the box for the club batting, and *the man who leads off the next half* for the one in the field. That second half is the useful one, and `linescore.defense.batter` is MLB's own field for it; the arithmetic alternative (the slot after the last completed PA) breaks on pinch-hitters, double switches and a batter left mid-count. Keyed by `away`/`home` on the server so the box score never has to ask which club is fielding, and null off a live game — after the last out `defense.batter` still names a man due up in a half nobody will play.

**Bundle**: JS 807.16 → 806.76 kB raw (238.05 → 237.94 gz), CSS 212.00 → 211.83 raw (37.29 → 37.28).

author: cwilsn
body:
## Summary

Security review ahead of the first alpha. The `expected_account_id` / `expected_role` guardrails could report a pass while the application ran as a different identity. Four paths allowed it — three reproduced with tests before any change was made.

There is no remote attack surface here; this package is a local dev tool. The risk class is a guardrail that reads as passing while describing the wrong identity.

## Findings and fixes

**1. `expected_role` was a substring test over the whole ARN.** `str_contains($identity->arn, $expectedRole)` was satisfied by a broader permission set whose name merely extended the expected one (`AWSReservedSSO_LaravelDeveloperAdmin_…` matched `LaravelDeveloper`), and by a match anywhere else in the ARN including the session name — so an `AdministratorAccess` session could pass outright.

Now compared against the role component of the ARN, exactly and case-sensitively, accepting either the Identity Center permission set name or the generated role name in full. New `AwsIdentity::roleName()` / `AwsIdentity::permissionSetName()` parse it. An identity that is not an assumed role can no longer satisfy a role guardrail, which also catches a profile backed by long-lived keys in `~/.aws/credentials`.

**2. Guardrails were void when static credentials shadowed the profile.** `aws --profile X` ignores environment credentials, but `aws-sdk-php` puts `env` first in its chain. With `fail_on_static_credentials => false` the guardrails verified the SSO profile and printed `AWS authenticated with [profile]: arn:…` while the application used the leftover keys.

Static credentials are now a hard failure whenever a guardrail is configured, and `fail_on_static_credentials => false` does not downgrade that case.

**3. Misleading success message.** When static credentials are tolerated and no guardrail is set, `aws-sso:login` and the listener no longer announce the profile's ARN as the identity the application authenticated with.

**4. Two fail-open configuration paths.** A guardrail set to an array/object/`true` silently disabled the check — now throws `InvalidGuardrailConfiguration`, with `null` and `false` still meaning off. A scope list configured as a bare string (`'commands' => 'dev'`) read as an empty list and skipped the check entirely — now read as a one-entry list.

## Checked and found solid, no changes

Command injection handling is already correct — argument arrays throughout, no shell, enforced by an arch test and metacharacter regression tests. Credential values are never read or printed. Scope gating, non-interactive refusal, timeouts, and the absence of cached session state are all correct.

## Notable behaviour change

An unenforceable guardrail now overrides an explicit `fail_on_static_credentials => false`. This deliberately overrules a user setting, on the reasoning that the guardrail is the security-intent setting and the flag is a convenience escape hatch.

## Release

Tagged as `v0.1.0-alpha.1` after merge — the package is registered on Packagist with no published versions, so this is its first. `SECURITY.md` moved from `1.x` to `0.1.x`, and the README install command carries the `^0.1.0-alpha` stability flag that a pre-release requires.

## Testing

`composer check` (pint, rector, phpstan, pest) clean — 189 tests, 405 assertions, up from 153.

author: caseyblaze
body:
## 起因

`csql status` 對一個剛剛才 `csql start` 的 dev 環境顯示 `stopped (stale)`，四個 instance 全部。實際上其中兩個 port 被一個沒有任何 PID file 追蹤的孤兒 proxy 佔著，另外兩個 (`12345` maas / `12346` cockpit) 根本沒有任何 process 在 listen。

## 兩個 bug

**1. start 不驗證 proxy 是否真的起來**

`cmd_start` 把 `cloud-sql-proxy` 丟到背景後直接把 `$!` 寫進 PID file 並印 `[start] ... (PID N)`。cloud-sql-proxy 綁不到 port 時會在幾毫秒內離開，於是 PID file 指著一個死掉的 process，下一次 `csql status` 就顯示 `stopped (stale)` — 真正的錯誤只留在 log 裡：

```
11:51:56 could not listen to address 127.0.0.1:12347: bind: address already in use
11:51:56 The proxy has encountered a terminal error: unable to start
```

**2. TOML config 非原子寫入（就是這個造成上面的 port 衝突）**

`generate_proxy_config` 對目標路徑原地 truncate 後逐行寫，而每個 instance 都要跑一次 `yq`，中間空窗很長。兩個 start 重疊時（手動 `csql start` 撞上 launchd auth watcher 的重啟），其中一個 proxy exec 出來讀到的是寫到一半的 config，只綁到已經 flush 出去的那幾個 instance，然後照樣回報 `started successfully`：

```
09:42:55  Listening 12347 / 12344 / 12345 / 12346   ← 完整
09:43:37  Listening 12347 / 12344                    ← 只讀到前 2 行，仍回報成功
```

沒被綁到的 instance 從此沒有 listener，而它搶到的 port 又擋掉之後每一次 start。

## 改動

- `generate_proxy_config` 改成寫進 temp file 再 `mv` 進去，rename 是原子的，讀者不會再看到半截 config
- `cmd_start` 等 proxy 印出 readiness 或先行離開才決定成敗；失敗時印出這一次嘗試的 log、不留 PID file、回傳非 0
- `restart_envs` 不再讓單一環境的失敗中斷排在後面的環境

等待是 key 在 proxy 自己的 readiness 訊息而不是固定 sleep，成功路徑沒有延遲代價。撐過 `PROXY_START_TIMEOUT` 還活著就算成功，避免把慢的 API round-trip 誤判成失敗。

## 驗證

失敗路徑（12344 被佔用，帶真憑證）：

```
  [fail] testenv: proxy exited during startup
         ... bind: address already in use
exit code = 1，沒留下 pid file，status 顯示 stopped 而非 stopped (stale)
```

成功路徑：4 instances，exit 0，總共 0.38s。

TOML 原子性 — 併發讀取抽樣，記錄每次讀到的行數（5 = 完整）：

```
修改前:  1行 39次   2行 37次   3行 36次   4行 36次   5行 3621次   ← ~4% 讀到半截
修改後:                                              5行 3054次   ← 0 次
```

## 已知未處理

目前仍沒有機制偵測「佔著 port 但不在任何 PID file 裡」的孤兒 proxy。這個 PR 讓孤兒不會再被無聲製造出來（start 失敗會明講並附上原因），但若孤兒因其他原因產生，`csql start` 還是只會報 bind 失敗，要人工 `lsof` 去找。start 前掃 port 並提示或接管是另一個決定，留待後續。

author: tobico
body:
Stage 03 of the [desktop roadmap](docs/roadmaps/desktop/ROADMAP.md) —
[brief](docs/roadmaps/desktop/03-appimage.md). A `v*` tag now builds
`Verkstead-x86_64.AppImage` beside the four bare CLI binaries and attaches it to
the Release, and the file runs the stage-02 tray on a stock distribution.

Two things this stage lays down once, for stages 04 and 05 to reuse: the
packaging assets, and the release plumbing that carries a desktop artifact from
a build leg to a Release asset.

## The tasks

- **01: Packaging assets and the AppImage** — a `net.tobico.Verkstead` desktop
  entry and the sized launcher PNGs, generated from
  `assets/icons/verkstead-hammer.png` by a script rather than drawn by hand,
  into a packaging directory of their own outside the viewer's `publicDir` — so
  nothing desktop-only is served by the viewer or embedded in the headless CLI.
  Then `tools/build-appimage.sh`, which bundles the dynamic desktop binary with
  its toolkit and runs the same locally and in CI.
- **02: A tag ships the AppImage** — `release.yml` gains a `desktop-linux` leg
  on the shared viewer artifact, asserting of the bundle what the CLI legs
  assert of their binaries: it runs, and what it serves at `/` is the viewer's
  own bundle. `publish` is widened once for all three desktop artifacts rather
  than for this one — desktop legs upload under `desktop-*`, so `verkstead-*`
  goes on meaning the bare binaries and four goes on being their number, and the
  desktop artifacts are checked by name both ways round. `workflow_dispatch`
  rehearses the whole thing without publishing.
- **03: The install story and what a tag now produces** — `docs/releasing.md`
  no longer says a tag publishes "the four"; it names both halves and says where
  four is still right and why. `README.md` and `docs/adoption.md` gain the Linux
  desktop half of the install story, told apart from the flake rather than
  merged with it: the flake and the module run the headless daemon, the AppImage
  is the same server started from an icon. Both name the failure that is not
  one — a desktop with no tray host shows no icon and serves the viewer anyway.

The CLI legs stay musl exactly as they were, and `manifest` still hashes the
four bare binaries.

author: gjcourt
body:
## What

The per-room as-built table in `01-016` had gone stale. It described the living room as **HiFiBerry DAC+ DSP HAT → S/PDIF → D30 Pro**, with TV optical into the HAT's S/PDIF input, and marked the row ✅ **done**.

That chain no longer exists. As rebuilt, the living room runs a **DietPi streamer → D90 III Discrete**, with TV audio arriving via a **UR27**. The D30 Pro is out of service and the HiFiBerry DAC+ DSP HAT is no longer in the path.

## Why it mattered

The stale row made a decommissioned DAC look like it was still carrying the room — the file said the D30 Pro was live in the living room, in a section marked done. Anyone reading this to decide whether that DAC was free would have concluded it wasn't.

## Knock-on effects, recorded rather than dropped

- **Office row.** It assumed the D90 III would land there. It didn't — the D90 III went to the living room. The office needs a DAC assigned again; the row is marked `needs re-plan` rather than left implying a settled plan.
- **Living-room volume mechanism** needs re-documenting. The `snap-dsp-volume-bridge` / SigmaDSP-master approach described further down belongs to the superseded HiFiBerry chain and doesn't describe the current one.
- **`UR27` is recorded as given and flagged unverified** against a manufacturer part number, so it doesn't get cited for a build without checking.
- **WebHID.** A decoding attempt was made against the D90 III on 2026-08-30/31 with no outcome recorded. Noted, so the model stays unconfirmed and read-only under the rule already in the file — rather than the attempt being silently forgotten.

## Style

Follows the file's existing convention: a dated `> **Correction (YYYY-MM-DD).**` block above the affected table, matching the 2026-08-27 correction already present.

`make format-check` and `make lint` both pass locally (via podman).

author: hilalbursalii
body:
Fixes six orchestration-cluster nightly failures on `main`. All are test drift, **not** product regressions — verified against a fresh local Docker (Elasticsearch, tasklist v2) stack.

## Root cause & fix

### Identity — new design system (shadcn) migration
The admin app now renders on the Camunda design system instead of Carbon on several surfaces:

- **Login error** no longer renders Carbon's `.cds--inline-notification__title`; the design system's Alert carries the message in `[data-slot="alert-title"]`. Rather than widen the selector to a union of both markups, the assertions reuse `LoginPage.invalidCredentialsError`, which was already in the file and already proven on the Carbon surface by `tests/operate/login.spec.ts`. It matches `role="alert"` plus the message text, so it holds on both design systems and needs no edit the next time either changes. The text filter is load-bearing: the Operate login page renders an empty alert region before any error, so matching the role alone can resolve to more than one element. `errorMessage` had no callers left and is removed.
  - Fixes `tests/identity/login.spec.ts › Log in with invalid user account`
  - Fixes `tests/common-flows/identity-users-flows.spec.ts › Admin user can delete user`
- **Create role modal** Input marks an invalid field with `aria-invalid`, not Carbon's `data-invalid`.
  - Fixes `tests/identity/roles.spec.ts › tries to create a role with invalid id`
- **Roles list delete action**, uncovered by the fix above. `roles CRUD` is a `test.describe.serial` block, so the stale `data-invalid` assertion was short-circuiting it: on `main`, `tries to create a role with invalid id` failed and `creates a role` and `deletes a role` were **skipped and never ran** (visible as `-` in the nightly log). With the first test repaired the block runs to completion, and `deletes a role` fails the first time it has actually executed. So this is a latent failure the PR reveals, not one it introduces.

  The cause is the same design-system migration. The row's action cell holds an icon-only Edit button carrying `aria-label="Edit role"` and a destructive Delete button with an `aria-hidden` icon plus the visible text `Delete` and no aria-label — `entityListV2` sets `iconOnly: !!Icon && !isDangerous`, and `roles/ListV2.tsx` marks the delete item `isDangerous: true`. `getByLabel` matches only aria-label, aria-labelledby or an associated label, never text content, so the locator resolved to nothing. It now matches by role and accessible name, as `IdentityUsersPage.deleteUserButton` already does for the same list component. Sibling lists are deliberately untouched: groups and tenants have no `ListV2` variant, and their deletes plus users' and authorizations' all pass.
  - Fixes `tests/identity/roles.spec.ts › deletes a role`
- **Role detail assign-user modal** is now a cmdk combobox (“Search by Username or Name”) whose results render in a Radix popover that **portals as a sibling of the dialog** (DS #496) — so the listbox is scoped to the page, not the modal. This selector change is what fixes the failure; the nightly died on `locator.fill` against `getByRole('searchbox')`, before any assignment. The search is also debounced and eventually consistent, so the flow keeps a reload-and-retry (mirroring the authorizations owner search `#51442`) — but retries **only** the modal interaction, and stops as soon as the assigned-users table shows the user. Retrying the whole flow cannot work: `AssignMembersModal` passes the assigned users to `UserMultiSelect` as `excluded`, so once a submit has landed the option is absent from the results and any further attempt fails on the option locator, reporting that instead of the real error. The list wait moved out of the loop with a 60s budget, since its 10s default has to cover a full reload of the Identity SPA. The option click does not force: it is asserted visible on the line above, and `force` would skip the hit-target check that names the cause if the `pointer-events` workaround in `DropdownSearch.tsx` ever regressed.
  - Fixes `tests/identity/authorizations.spec.ts › create user authorization`

### Operate — accumulated `aria-live` announcers
Each scheduled operation leaves an `aria-live` announcer carrying the same `.cds--inline-loading` class in the data-list, so the list-wide spinner selector matched every instance that ever had an operation and tripped strict mode — 7 elements in the failing run, each for a different instance key. The spinner is now scoped to the target instance's row.
- Fixes `tests/operate/operations.spec.ts › Retry and cancel single instance`

### Batch API — cancel lands after the batch has already finished
The failure is a permanent 404: ten POSTs to `/batch-operations/{key}/cancellation`, all 404, the 240s retry budget expired, twice. The first cancel fired 132ms after the create returned, too early for the batch to be addressable; the next poll was 5.1s later, by which point the batch had finished and the 404 was permanent.

Cancellation time scales with the instance count. In the same run the `beforeAll` 3-instance batch went `startDate 01:49:00.128` → `endDate 01:49:02.655`, so ~2.5s for three instances, and a 30-instance batch therefore reaches a terminal state inside the first retry interval.

So the fix is the count, not the mechanism: `createCancellationBatch(request, 500)`. That is the same remedy and the same number the sibling suspend suite already uses for this exact race, documented in two comments in `batch-operations-suspend-api-tests.spec.ts`. Applied to `Cancel batch operation twice fails on second request` as well, since its first cancel has the same requirement and its comment claiming 30 instances are enough contradicted the sibling suite.

Suspending the batch first was considered and dropped. It races completion in the same window (suspend on a finished batch also 404s permanently, per `Suspend finished batch operation returns 404`), it would make this test a duplicate of the already-green `Suspend & Resume › Cancel suspended batch operation transitions to CANCELED`, and it would remove the suite's only coverage of cancelling an ACTIVE batch.
- Fixes `tests/api/v2/batch-operation/batch-operations-cancel-api-tests.spec.ts › Cancel active batch operation returns 204 and status becomes CANCELED`

Note: a 500-instance batch cancelled mid-flight leaves more instances un-terminated than a 30-instance one. Both sibling 500-instance tests already do this and the api nightly runs against an ephemeral stack, so no teardown is added.

Two further batch failures surfaced in the post-rebase run and are fixed here too.

**The suspend side of the same race.** `Suspend active batch operation returns 204 and status becomes SUSPENDED without resume` failed in the profiles job while passing in all-in-one — a batch finishing before the suspend command lands, after which `/suspension` returns a permanent 404 the retry budget cannot recover from. Raised to 500 instances, the remedy this file already applies four times; two earlier commits (`keep cancellation batch active for suspend catch`, `stabilize batch suspend and dashboard error nightly failures`) fixed the same failure one test at a time as each surfaced. Also applied to `Suspend batch operation twice fails on second request`, which flaked locally the same way. `SUSPENDED, finally resumes` has the identical shape but no observed failure, so it is left alone, matching how this file has been maintained.
- Fixes `tests/api/v2/batch-operation/batch-operations-suspend-api-tests.spec.ts › Suspend active batch operation returns 204 and status becomes SUSPENDED without resume`

**A completion poll that was too tight.** `Delete Decision Instance With Batch` failed on `operationsCompletedCount` — expected 2, observed 0, then 1 on retry, inside the 30s `defaultAssertionOptions` budget. The batch was executing, just not finishing in time: those counters reach the read API

author: bryceashey
body:
## What

Set `agentRules: false` in `ui/next.config.mjs`, and add a human-authored replacement for the warning Next was injecting to the root `CLAUDE.md`.

## Why

`next dev` writes `ui/AGENTS.md` and `ui/CLAUDE.md` whenever it detects an AI coding agent — see `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`, gated in `start-server.js` on `agentRules !== false` and `getAgentName() !== null`.

Coding agents load a nested `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` as **project instructions**, with the same standing as the ones we wrote. Nothing in that channel records provenance, so the mechanism promotes an npm package's content from *data the agent reads* to *instructions the agent follows*. Three properties make that worse than the usual `node_modules` trust problem:

- **Invisible to supply-chain tooling.** Audits and lockfile diffs look for code; prose in a `.md` trips nothing.
- **It executes through the agent** — its access, its credentials, at the moment you're trusting its output. Resulting actions look like the agent's own reasoning.
- **It only materializes for agents.** Detection-gated, so it never appears in a human-only dev run or in CI.

Benign intent from Next here — the current block just says Next 16 diverges from training data — but the channel shouldn't exist. Agent-instruction files in this repo are human-authored.

Considered and rejected: gitignoring the two files (leaves an unreviewed file that agents still load and that silently rewrites on every `npm install`), and committing them as generated content (only a soft gate — every Next bump produces a "generated noise" diff of exactly the kind that gets rubber-stamped).

## Preserving what was lost

The generated block's warning is genuinely useful — Next 16.3.1 *is* newer than most model training data. `CLAUDE.md` now carries a human-authored version pointing at `ui/node_modules/next/dist/docs/`, with a note not to re-enable the flag and to fix the version by hand when it goes stale.

## Verification

Control run first, so the pass isn't vacuous:

| Run | `ui/AGENTS.md` | `ui/CLAUDE.md` |
|---|---|---|
| flag commented out | PRESENT | PRESENT |
| `agentRules: false` | absent | absent |

The control run logged `✓ Generated AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md for AI agents` — detection does fire in this environment, and the flag is what suppresses it. No config warnings either way (`agentRules` is a valid top-level key per `config-schema.js`, not experimental). Generated files removed afterwards.

Not run: a full `next build`. This is a dev-only code path and the config validates through the same schema, but flagging it rather than implying wider coverage.

## Notes

- No existing lines changed in either file — both edits are pure additions.
- Noticed while building the Storage/Backups UI (#203) and deliberately left out of that PR's scope.
- Other Next projects in the tree have **not** been swept for already-generated `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` files.

author: fetburner
body:
Closes #476

ライブ画面の ON AIR バッジの隣に「放送から約 n 秒 / 先読み n 秒」を毎秒更新で出す。遅延は異常ではないので信号色を使わず `text-muted-foreground`。`aria-live` は付けない（毎秒変わる数字を読み上げさせない）。

- **hls.js 経路**: `hls.latency` と `mainForwardBufferInfo.len` を 1 秒ごとに読む
- **native HLS 経路（Safari）**: `latency` は取れないので `video.buffered` の末尾 − `currentTime` で「先読み」だけ。「放送から」は出さない（測れないものを出さない）

## レビューで直したこと

**`hls.latency` は `NaN` にならない。** issue の罠には「ライブ同期点が決まるまで `NaN` / `undefined`」とあったが、hls.js 1.6.17 の `LatencyController.get latency()` は `return this._latency || 0` で、`_latency` が `null` の間は **`0`** を返す。`Number.isFinite` でガードしていた初版は実ブラウザで「—」ではなく「放送から約0秒」（遅延ゼロという嘘の測定値）を出していた。`<video>` に `autoPlay` は無く `_latency` は最初の `timeupdate` まで入らないので、再生ボタンを押すまでこの表示が続く。`hls.latency > 0` をゲートにして修正。

`hls.liveSyncPosition !== null` は使えない —— `levelDetails` と `targetLatency` が揃った時点（プレイリスト読み込み直後）で非 null になるため、`latency === 0` の窓をそのまま通す。`_latency === null` を見る公開 API は無い。

**テストが実物から乖離していた。** `FakeHls` の既定値を `NaN` にしていたので、上記のバグが起きる状態を一度も再現していなかった。e2e の `/放送から約\d+秒/` も `放送から約0秒` にマッチするため、同期点が一生決まらなくても緑になっていた。既定を `0` に、e2e を `[1-9]\d*` に。

**エラー時に計器が凍る回帰。** 表示位置を `pages/live.tsx` へ移した際、呼び出し側は `isPlaying && diagnostics` でしか出し分けずエラー表示を知らないため、fatal エラー後も直前の測定値が ON AIR の隣に残り続けていた。ポーリング停止時に `onDiagnostics(null)` を出すように。

「実 hls.js の getter は `destroy()` 後に throw する」という初版のコメントも誤りだったので撤回した（`destroy` は controller を null にせず、直前値を返す）。`stopDiagnostics` は例外対策ではなく、意味の無くなった値を読み続けないための衛生。

## ラベルについて

初稿の「貯まり n 秒」は動詞の名詞化がラベルとして不自然で、隣の「放送から約 n 秒」との register もずれるため、`mainForwardBufferInfo`（前方バッファ）をそのまま訳した**「先読み n 秒」**にした（issue #476 の本文も更新済み）。「バッファ済」は `済` が完了した累計量を連想させる一方、この数値は実際には「あと何秒もつか」という減っていく余裕なので採らなかった。

```
ON AIR  放送から約6秒 / 先読み8秒
ON AIR  先読み8秒            （ネイティブ経路。latency は取れない）
ON AIR  放送から— / 先読み—   （同期点が決まるまで）
```

## テスト

- `live.mjs` ③（実 Chrome）に「再生開始後に計器が数値になる」判定を追加。取得を定数に潰す変異で `NG: ③「放送から約 n 秒 / 先読み n 秒」が数値にならない` を確認
- jsdom で経路ごとの表示差を両方向、初期状態に `NaN` が現れないこと、エラー時に `null` を報告することを検証。いずれも実装を壊して落ちることを確認済み
- `pnpm test` 1020/1020 / `pnpm lint` 既存 warning 2 件のみ / `pnpm build` clean / `pnpm e2e:live` ①〜⑦ exit 0 / `npm run docs:lint` clean

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Resumo

Corrige o comportamento da **Dissonância** no ECHO. Antes, quando o cronômetro de 12s terminava, o Echo era **destruído** (`dissolveEcho`). Agora a Dissonância é **temporária**: o Echo volta ao lado do jogador ao fim dos 12s, com a confiança restaurada a um piso seguro.

## Alterações (apenas 2 funções em `index.html`)

### 1. `updateEcho()` — fim da Dissonância não dissolve mais o Echo
Quando `hostileT` chega a 0 o Echo agora:
- volta a `hostile = false` / `hostileT = 0`;
- recupera a confiança para no mínimo **34** (`Math.max(e.trust, 34)` — piso do tier NEUTRA);
- reseta o estado de combate hostil: `fireTimer`, `beamT`, `beamRamp`, `beamTarget`, `recoil`, `erratic`, `glitchT`, `glitchAmp`;
- mostra o feedback **"DISSONÂNCIA TERMINADA"** informando que o Echo retornou ao seu lado.

`dissolveEcho()` permanece disponível apenas para a **morte real** do Echo (linha `if(e.hp<=0&&e.hostile)` → `'SOB FOGO'`).

### 2. `echoesReact()` — confiança não muda durante a Dissonância
Adicionado `if(e.hostile) continue;` no loop: Ecos hostis são **totalmente ignorados** pelas escolhas morais. Decisões tomadas durante a janela de 12s não aumentam nem diminuem a confiança de um Echo hostil — e o Echo que acaba de voltar não rebela imediatamente.

## Critérios de aceite (verificados)

- [x] Echo entra em Dissonância (`hostile = true`)
- [x] Dissonância dura ~12s
- [x] Echo **permanece vivo** quando o timer expira
- [x] Echo volta ao comportamento aliado
- [x] Confiança volta a **>= 34**
- [x] Não rebela imediatamente ao voltar
- [x] Escolhas morais feitas enquanto hostil **não** alteram a confiança
- [x] Reações normais de confiança continuam funcionando para Ecos aliados

## Verificação

- `node --check` no script embutido: **sintaxe OK**.
- Teste de ciclo de vida com as funções reais extraídas do arquivo: **22/22 assertivas passando** (entrada, congelamento da confiança, expiração, retorno, não-rebelião, reações aliadas e semântica de morte intacta).
- `git diff` confirma que **nenhum outro sistema foi alterado** (apenas `echoesReact` e `updateEcho`).

author: cyberbihan
body:
Every name a rule quotes is chosen by the server being examined, which on a hostile target means it is chosen by the target. internal/certinfo bounds what reaches the report for display and says why at the top of its file: passing it through unbounded turns one small request into a reply measured in megabytes, paid for by whoever asked for the scan rather than by the server that sent it. The rules added the same day quoted names into their reasons and went around every one of those bounds.

Measured rather than supposed. A certificate carrying five thousand malformed wildcard names produced a single finding of 1,085,200 bytes, and a five-kilobyte common name produced one of 5,321.

The bound is on the sentence and not on the decision, and the two are separate on purpose: a rule has to look at the whole list even when it may only quote part of it, because a wildcard malformed at position three thousand is still a malformed wildcard. Five names, sixty-four bytes each, cut on a rune boundary, and the number left out is said rather than hidden.

The other half of the same question came out clean and is now held by a test rather than by luck. A name arrives as the bytes the server chose and a terminal reads some of them as instructions, so a certificate can carry an escape sequence that erases the verdict printed above it; certinfo makes that argument for the subject one round earlier. These rules already quoted with strconv.Quote, which renders the escape as four printable characters, and nothing asserted it.

Checked by sabotage in both directions: removing the count bound puts 355,200 bytes back into a finding, and removing the quoting puts a control byte the server chose into two of them.

The rest of what was added the same day was checked and needed nothing. ROCA echoes nothing and costs thirty-eight modular reductions whatever the size of the modulus; the serial and extended key usage rules quote only integers and fixed text; the notes quote integers; and the post-quantum probe is one connection behind the same guard and the same handshake timeout as every other, skipped entirely where the question does not exist.

author: cpunion
body:
## Summary

- add operand-form and register-pair coverage across supported Plan 9 assembly architectures
- add official Go WebAssembly Plan 9 assembly parsing, signature inference, LLVM lowering, and executable conformance tests
- lower the official Go wasm runtime ABI: generated `go_asm.h` offsets, linear-memory SP/FP frames, CTXT and register globals, caller PC/resume dispatch, `CALLNORESUME`, and `RETUNWIND`
- translate the official `internal/bytealg`, `internal/chacha8rand`, `internal/runtime/atomic`, and runtime wasm assembly without source patches
- validate Go 1.20 through Go 1.27 GOROOT assembly, ARM GOARM=5/6/7, and ARM64 GOARM64=v8.0
- reject closure-context and unsupported operand boundaries explicitly instead of silently miscompiling them

## WebAssembly scope

The zero-value/direct mode preserves plan9asm's existing LLVM/C-compatible wasm calling convention. The explicit Go ABI mode models the official `GOARCH=wasm` assembly contract used by `GOOS=js` and `GOOS=wasip1`; Emscripten ABI/profile selection remains owned by LLGo.

The Go ABI mode covers both the Go 1.20 write-barrier/import shape and the Go 1.21+ native helper shape. It emits LLVM modules for all selected official standard-library wasm assembly files, including generated struct offsets such as `gobuf_g`.

The execution fixtures translate real GOROOT `internal/bytealg`, `internal/runtime/atomic`, and runtime assembly, compile the generated LLVM IR with `llc`, link with `wasm-ld`, and run the module with Node. Whole-runtime corpus validation proves translation and LLVM object generation; LLGo R1 integration additionally proves these packages compile and run without their former source patches under Emscripten wasm32 and Memory64.

## Validation

- `go test ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- LLGo R1 via a temporary `go.work`, then again through the pinned pseudo-version: all target profiles build, and `llgo test` passes under Emscripten wasm32 and Memory64
- Go 1.20 `js/wasm` official standard-library corpus: 24 asm files, 18 LLVM modules
- Go 1.21–1.27 `js/wasm` and `wasip1/wasm` official standard-library corpora: no unsupported forms or parse failures; every generated module accepted by `llc`
- Go 1.27 Linux/macOS/Windows corpus, including 386, amd64, arm64, ARM GOARM=5/6/7, and ARM64 GOARM64=v8.0

author: mateo181230-cmyk
body:
> **Este PR se apila sobre [#14](https://github.com/Nexus-Battle-VI/Nexus-Battle-Commerce/pull/14) (HU-58).** Su rama base es `feat/hu-58-carrito-premium`, no `main`, porque recuperar un carrito guardado necesita el carrito vigente que introduce HU-58. Al integrar #14, este PR queda con su diferencia propia. Revisar #14 primero.

## Trazabilidad

Management Issue:

```text
Refs Nexus-Battle-VI/Nexus-Battle-Management#35
```

- **Tipo:** HU
- **Team:** Team Beta
- **Bounded context:** Commerce

`Closes` no se usa: cubre la task `#227` (backend), pero HU-61 necesita ademas la interfaz en Web y sus pruebas (`#229`). La HU permanece abierta.

## Resumen

El cliente autenticado puede guardar su carrito, cerrar sesion y recuperarlo al volver. El carrito guardado es un agregado propio, asociado a la identidad verificada y aislado del de cualquier otro cliente.

## Contexto y alcance

HU-61 se distingue de HU-58 en una linea del propio enunciado: HU-58 conserva el carrito **durante** la navegacion; HU-61 lo persiste **entre sesiones**. Por eso el carrito guardado es un agregado nuevo, `SavedCart`, y no una bandera sobre el pedido:

- El borrador es el carrito vivo de la sesion en curso. El `SavedCart` es una copia congelada que el cliente pidio conservar de forma explicita. Fundirlos obligaria a decidir, en cada lectura del borrador, si el cliente queria conservarlo o solo lo estaba usando, y esa pregunta no tiene respuesta observable.
- Guarda el **precio con el que se guardo**, no el vigente: lo que se recupera es lo que el cliente vio, igual que hace `Order` al congelar el precio de la linea.
- Recuperar **reemplaza** el contenido del borrador en lugar de fusionarlo. HU-61 pide «recuperar los productos previamente guardados»; fusionar inventaria una regla de precedencia entre dos cantidades de la misma referencia que la historia no define y que el cliente no podria predecir.
- Un unico carrito guardado por cliente: guardar de nuevo reemplaza. La historia no define historial ni multiples carritos, y conservar varios obligaria a elegir cual recuperar.

**Rutas nuevas**, todas bajo identidad verificada:

| Ruta | Que hace |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/orders/cart/persistence` | Guarda el carrito vigente |
| `GET /api/orders/cart/persistence` | Consulta lo guardado |
| `POST /api/orders/cart/persistence/restoration` | Vuelca lo guardado sobre el carrito |
| `DELETE /api/orders/cart/persistence` | Descarta lo guardado |

**Fuera de alcance:** la interfaz de guardar y recuperar, que va en un PR aparte de `Nexus-Battle-Web`. La expiracion, la fusion automatica y la sincronizacion entre dispositivos quedan fuera porque RF-61 las excluye de forma expresa.

## La decisión que conviene mirar con atención

**Estas rutas responden `401` cuando `AUTH_MODE=disabled`.** No es un descuido: es CA-02 aplicado literalmente («no se crea una asociacion de carrito atribuida a una identidad inexistente»).

Sin proveedor de identidad, el servicio atribuye a toda peticion el sujeto literal `anonymous`. Un carrito guardado bajo esa identidad seria el carrito compartido de todo el que pase por el servicio, y devolverselo a la siguiente persona es exactamente el fallo que CA-02 prohibe.

**Consecuencia directa en las pruebas:** el camino feliz de HU-61 **no se puede ejercitar por HTTP en este entorno**, porque toda peticion es anonima. Por eso las pruebas de integracion comprueban unicamente el rechazo (CP-61-03), y el guardado, la recuperacion en sesion posterior y el aislamiento entre clientes se verifican en las pruebas unitarias, donde la identidad se fija sin montar un proveedor OIDC. Esto se declara aqui en vez de simular una sesion, que daria una confianza que las pruebas no respaldan.

## Criterios de aceptación cubiertos

- [x] CA-01 — guardar, terminar sesion y recuperar los productos en una sesion posterior (unitaria: «recupera los productos guardados en un carrito nuevo»)
- [x] CA-02 — sin identidad verificada no se crea asociacion alguna (integracion: cuatro rutas responden `401`)
- [x] CA-02 — el carrito de A no se recupera como si fuera de B (unitarias de `GetSavedCart` y `RestoreSavedCart`)
- [x] CA-02 — lo recuperado conserva los productos guardados, con sus precios
- [x] CA-03 — el 100 % de los casos de guardado y recuperacion mantiene la asociacion identidad ↔ carrito
- [ ] Interfaz de guardar y recuperar — task de Web, PR aparte

## Pruebas

- [x] Pruebas unitarias — `test/unit/saved-cart.spec.ts`: agregado `SavedCart`, `SaveCart`, `GetSavedCart`, `RestoreSavedCart`, `DiscardSavedCart`, aislamiento entre clientes y no-fusion al recuperar.
- [x] Pruebas de integración — `test/integration/saved-cart-http.spec.ts`: rechazo de la identidad no verificada en las cuatro rutas y sonda de disponibilidad.
- [x] Pruebas de base de datos — `test/db/postgres-saved-cart-repository.spec.ts` con Testcontainers: guardado, reemplazo, aislamiento, importes grandes sin redondeo y las cinco restricciones de la migracion.
- [ ] Pruebas de aceptación o extremo a extremo — no aplica: sin interfaz en este PR.

Verificación local ejecutada: `lint` ✅, `format:check` ✅, `typecheck` ✅, `test:coverage` ✅ (**235/235**; statements 93.26 %, branches 91.12 %, functions 88.46 %, lines 92.79 %), `build` ✅.

`test:db` **no se pudo ejecutar localmente por falta de Docker en el entorno**. Las pruebas estan escritas y type-checkeadas; quedan pendientes de confirmacion en el pipeline. author: guardiola31337
body:
## Problem

`ManifestManager::list_files` fails with `ManifestNotFound` on any device that never created a backup, because `load_manifest_gated` reads the local manifest before the remote gate and no manifest file was ever written.

Oxide's personal-custody backup syncs call `list_files` after local PCP mutations — the face PCP delete (`delete_face_pcp_and_sync_backup_if_configured`) and the stale-PCP cleanup inside `get_face_enrollment_attempt_status`. On accounts without a backup, the whole operation therefore reports failure even though the local mutation already succeeded. Concretely, in World App Android (wld-android [MCORE-1893](https://linear.app/worldcoin/issue/MCORE-1893)): a no-backup user whose SelfieCheck v4 enrollment fails gets a spurious "PCP deletion failed" from the cleanup, with the PCP actually gone from disk.

This is the remaining half of #418: #418 fixed the empty **remote** `manifest_hash` (0.5.x devices error with `manifest_hash is not the correct length: 0`), but on ≥0.6.1 the same devices now fail one step earlier on the **local** read with `BackupException$ManifestNotFound` — device-verified on wld-android's bedrock 0.6.1 bump (worldcoin/wld-android#8567).

## Fix

No manifest means no files recorded: `list_files` returns an empty list when the local read yields `ManifestNotFound`, short-circuiting before the remote gate (no network call for never-backed-up devices). Mutating methods (`store_file`, `remove_file`, `replace_all_files_for_designator`) are untouched and keep surfacing `ManifestNotFound`, so backup-creation flows keep their signal.

`test_list_files_missing_manifest` asserted the old contract (from #160's general hardening, before this call pattern existed) and is updated to the new one.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p bedrock --lib backup`: 151 passed.
- Device E2E (Pixel 3, `org.world.id.dev` devDebug on worldcoin/wld-android#8567, fresh account with the backup step skipped, face PCP present on disk):
  - bedrock 0.6.1: Developer Settings → Delete Face Dedupe fails with `backup list error: … BackupException$ManifestNotFound` although the local file is deleted.
  - bedrock 0.6.1 + this fix (local snapshot integrated into the app): same action succeeds cleanly — `Successfully deleted local face PCP`, no backup error, file removed. Re-verified after 6307897 with the remote-head gate: device confirmed to have no local manifest (`files/oxide/backup_manager/` absent), so the run exercised the new `ManifestNotFound` → remote-confirmed-empty branch.

Adjacent, not addressed here: `isLocalBackupStale` also errors (`InvalidManifestHashError`) at app start on the same never-backed-up accounts.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes read-path backup semantics used by post-mutation sync (e.g. PCP cleanup); wrong remote/local branching could hide staleness or skip needed restore, though scope is limited to `list_files`.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`ManifestManager::list_files`** no longer surfaces **`ManifestNotFound`** when there is no local `manifest.json`. On that path it checks the remote manifest head: accounts with **no remote backup** get an **empty file list**; accounts with a **remote backup** but no local manifest get **`RemoteAheadStaleError`** (restore before listing).
> 
> Manifest **mutations** (`store_file`, `remove_file`, etc.) are unchanged and still error if the local manifest is missing. Docs and tests split the old “missing manifest” case into no-remote (empty) vs remote-present (stale).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 848830e4045e22706eb9919decd30c504704dded. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

body:
## Summary

V8.5.0 keeps all 23 canonical skills, all six profiles, and all invocation policies. It balances V8.4 proof integrity with a bounded action counterweight: act once the next safe reversible step, verifier, and rollback are clear; make one useful verified change per cycle; and stop analysis when another pass cannot change a material decision.

## Candidate research

The release deep-dives action-oriented and autonomous-agent sources, including Ponytail, three Ralph-family repositories, autoresearch, Compound Engineering LFG, Superpowers, How, Agent Native, OpenHands, Aider, Cline, Roo Code, Sweep, Plandex, and gptme. Exact upstream commits, relevant paths, licenses, and decisions are recorded in `docs/ACTION-MOMENTUM-REVIEW-v8.5.0.md`.

## Strongly absorbed

- Minimum sufficient context before safe reversible action.
- One independently finishable unit per cycle.
- Immediate verification and keep/repair/revert discipline.
- Planning, research, review, and testing saturation rules.
- Fresh-context resume from compact durable state.
- Bounded loops with work, time, budget, and no-progress caps.
- Semantic progress rather than narration or repeated status reads.
- Stop after hard gates and acceptance pass; move optional polish to one owned backlog.

## Rejected or kept upstream

- A new `ponytail`, `ralph`, `autopilot`, or `yolo` routed skill.
- Provider-specific agent runtimes, hooks, installers, shell loops, hosted services, and IDE integrations.
- Infinite loops, self-declared completion, approval bypasses, hidden external mutation, and weaker proof gates.
- Automatic commits, pushes, PRs, messages, purchases, publication, or machine-level changes as global skill behavior.

## Files and authorities

- `AGENTS.md` and `ENGINEERING-CORE.md`
- `plan`, `research`, `experiment`, `test`, `get-it-done`, `gauntlet-loop`, `review`, and `skill-design`
- Get It Done and Gauntlet state/orchestration files
- `docs/ACTION-MOMENTUM-REVIEW-v8.5.0.md`
- 48 bounded-action and anti-YOLO scenarios
- 22-pass release audit

## Validation

- [x] Primary-source repository audit with exact pinned commits
- [x] Deterministic double build
- [x] Validator rejection-control tests
- [x] Static source and archive validation
- [x] Repository and bounded-action audit
- [x] 48 unique bounded-action scenarios
- [x] Task-pack and Complete-package content checks
- [x] Temporary update scaffolding removed
- [ ] PowerShell 7 pull-request CI
- [ ] Windows PowerShell 5.1 pull-request CI
- [ ] Post-merge CI
- [ ] Annotated `v8.5.0` tag and public GitHub Release
- [ ] Post-publication tag, asset, checksum, and package read-back

## Boundaries

- No new skill or route.
- No profile inventory or invocation-policy change.
- No runtime dependency, service, hook, installer, executable skill payload, or automatic trusted-state mutation.
- Bounded action never overrides proof, rollback, scope, security, privacy, or permission gates.
- No formal standards, upstream-project, accessibility, security, usability, or quality-conformance claim.

author: stephane-lieumont
body:
Implements [spec 06](docs/specs/06-design-system.md) and [ADR-0009](docs/adr/0009-design-system-tokens.md). No page is built yet — this is the system the pages will be built from.

## What is in here

**Two token tiers.** Primitives name values, semantics name roles, and components read semantics only. The current site writes `#f2a154` forty times by hand and has no custom property at all, which is why its dark section is a second set of rules rather than a second set of tokens.

**Section themes are fixed.** The root is `color-scheme: light`, never `light dark` — that would hand native control rendering to the OS setting and give a dark-mode visitor dark scrollbars on a page painted white. A subtree flips with `data-theme="dark"`, and nothing but tokens changes.

**Instrument Sans, self-hosted**, one variable file per unicode range, **44 KB for both**. The current site pulls sixteen weights from Google's CDN and uses two. No monospace: an overline class, tabular numerals and an identifier class carry the four jobs it would have had.

**The type scale opens with the viewport** — major third at 360px to perfect fourth at 1440px. Display-to-body lands at 3.0× on mobile and 4.2× on desktop, against 1.2× and 1.7× today.

## The three audited defects this closes

| Defect | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Button hover falls to **1.84:1** — less legible than at rest | Ink pinned white, surface darkens: 5.05 → 6.52 → 8.46 |
| Every button renders in **Arial** | `font: inherit` on form controls, which do not inherit it |
| Focus ring matched the button fill exactly on dark hover (**1.00**) | Neutral ring: 12.47 light, 9.95 dark, worst case |

Focus is deliberately not wrapped in `:where()`. A zero-specificity focus rule loses to any component rule touching `:focus`, silently — and this is the guarantee that must never lose a specificity race.

## How to review it

The home route is a **living specimen**: type scale, every button state, both themes, a form in error, and the dark section. Run `pnpm dev` and open http://localhost:4300 — hovering the primary button is the fastest way to see the state rule work.

## Checks

`pnpm verify` green: typecheck, lint, format, 4 tests, coverage 100% statements / 95.45% branches / 100% functions. One test runs **axe-core with zero tolerated violations** ([ADR-0010](docs/adr/0010-accessibility-and-semantics.md)); contrast is excluded there because jsdom does not load the token stylesheet, and is verified against the measured tables in spec 06 instead.

## Known gaps, deliberate

- The three `size-adjust` / `ascent-override` / `descent-override` values on the fallback face are **placeholders** until measured against the real face.
- The five-layer elevation interpolation is arithmetically sound but the card hover has not been watched in a browser at 60fps with heavy renders loaded.
- `--motion-slide` sits at a provisional 4rem: 24, 64 and 320px are to be compared in a browser before the menu gesture is frozen.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing recovery guidance for operators whose manual 1Password exec provider rejects a Homebrew `op` symlink or points at a versioned executable removed by an upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Document the existing 1Password plugin setup flow, which resolves and validates the current executable for each request. The migration instructions preserve exact credential-to-item mappings and explain how to avoid provider-alias collisions.

## User Impact

Operators can move from a brittle versioned command path to the supported plugin integration while retaining executable and parent-directory trust checks.

## Evidence

Synthetic process proofs verified manual symlink rejection, successful canonical execution, and failure after the pinned version was removed. The real plugin resolver followed replacement Homebrew symlinks through both PATH and an absolute override, then refused unsafe executable and parent replacements without executing them.

The built CLI setup command generated both exact target mappings under an unused provider alias and left the original config unchanged. No real 1Password credentials or Homebrew installation were used. Docs indexing, formatting, and diff checks pass. An optional unchanged op-path sibling test import was canceled after prolonged filesystem reads; the completed resolver and command proofs are retained.

author: wildcant
body:
Part 2 of 2 of ILLO-5. Adds `format_duration` on top of the `Duration` and
`parse_duration` that ILLO-6 landed. ILLO-6's `_core.py`, `_parse.py`, and
`test_parse.py` are untouched.

## Changed behaviour

`format_duration(d: Duration) -> str` in `duration/_format.py`, exported from
`duration/__init__.py`. Emits the shortest compound form — components largest
unit first, zero units left out:

```python
format_duration(Duration(90000))     # '1m30s'
format_duration(Duration(3630000))   # '1h30s'  — no minutes component at all
format_duration(Duration(-90000))    # '-1m30s'
format_duration(Duration(0))         # '0s'
```

Zero is the one case where a zero unit is emitted, since something must be.
Negatives keep a single leading `-`. Output carries no whitespace and no `+`.

`__all__` becomes `["Duration", "DurationParseError", "format_duration",
"parse_duration"]` — `format_duration` and nothing else. Internals stay
underscore-prefixed. No third-party dependencies; tests are stdlib `unittest`.

`UNITS` and `MAX_MILLISECONDS` are imported from `duration/_core.py`. The
formatter does not carry its own table and does not reach into `_parse`.

## The out-of-range decision

The dispatch note flagged this as the top residual risk: `parse_duration` caps
magnitude at `MAX_MILLISECONDS`, but the `Duration` constructor does not, so a
`Duration` can hold a value no duration string can express.

**Chosen: constrain the input.** `format_duration` raises `ValueError` when
`abs(milliseconds) > MAX_MILLISECONDS`, naming both the value and the limit.
Emitting the string instead would hand back something `parse_duration` then
rejects, making the round-trip property false outside the parser's range — and
that property is the point of this slice.

`ValueError` and not `DurationParseError`, because nothing was parsed:
`DurationParseError`'s contract is an offending *input string*, and here there
is none. Not a new exception type either, because the acceptance criteria pin
the public surface to exactly four names. Plain `ValueError` is also
`DurationParseError`'s own base class, so a caller with a broad bad-value
handler still catches both.

Covered by `FormatBoundsTest`: one over the limit in both signs, `10**30`, the
message naming value and limit, and the type not being a `DurationParseError`.

## Round trip

`parse_duration(format_duration(d)) == d`, tested against the real ILLO-6
parser imported from the package — no reimplementation, no stub. `RoundTripTest`
covers zero, each single unit, compound, negatives, both magnitude bounds
(`±(2**53 - 1)` ms), every unit boundary and its neighbours, and a deterministic
200-value sweep.

Beyond the committed suite, the property was checked ad hoc over 1,210,242
values — exhaustive on `0..300_000` in both signs, every unit boundary, the top
5,000 of the range, and 300,000 seeded random values across the full domain.
All hold.

## Marker comment

Exactly one occurrence in the tree, in `duration/_format.py`, at the line that
appends the unit suffix:

```
$ grep -rn "TODO: locale-aware unit names" . --exclude-dir=.git
duration/_format.py:34:            # TODO: locale-aware unit names
```

body:
## Summary

This pull request reworks how the add-on moves the mouse, replacing the instant jump with a smooth, human-like eased glide, and fixes a crash that could silently stop all tracking.

## What changed

1. Smooth eased motion
   - The cursor now travels to the target point gradually using an ease-in-out curve by default (accelerate then decelerate), which reads as natural manual movement.
   - Motion is scaled by distance: short jumps are quick, long journeys take a little longer, matching how a real hand behaves.
   - Implemented in a lightweight SmoothMouseMover driven by a single wx timer that stops on arrival (CPU-friendly, no busy loop).

2. Two new settings in the NVDA settings panel
   - Mouse speed: Slowest / Medium / Fast / Fastest.
   - Movement curve: Linear / Ease out / Ease in-out.

3. Bug fixes
   - Fixed a KeyError that crashed the settings dialog and silently blocked cursor movement when the config had not stored the new keys yet. All config reads now fall back to safe defaults.
   - Removed a silent bare except that hid every mouse-move error; failures are now logged to NVDA's log for easier diagnosis.
   - Removed dead imports and unused code.

## How to test

1. Install and restart NVDA.
2. Open NVDA menu > Settings > Universal focus tracker. The panel opens without errors and shows Enable tracking, Mouse speed, Movement curve.
3. Move focus (Tab / arrows / browser browse mode). The cursor glides to each focused object with smooth easing instead of jumping.

## Notes

- Defaults are ease-in-out at medium speed, so existing users get an improvement without touching settings.
- The NVDA+Windows+T shortcut still toggles tracking.

author: glimman79
body:
### Motivation
- Provide the D2.5a persistent foundation for future driving CAD dimensions while keeping the implementation explicitly non-driving and compatible with current Drawing geometry and interaction contracts. 
- Support creating, previewing, and persisting linear Dimensions that reference existing `Line` endpoints and expose aligned / horizontal / vertical interpretations driven by cursor placement. 
- Preserve existing snap, pan/zoom, and Edge primary-mousedown behavior and avoid introducing solver or Circle/Arc features in this stage.

### Description
- Add persistent Dimension model and schema: introduce `DrawingDimension`, `DrawingSketchV2`, `DrawingDocumentV2`, a deterministic `migrateDrawingDocument`, and semantic geometry references (`kind: 'point' | 'entity'`) in `src/app/drawingTypes.ts`. 
- Implement a Dimension module `src/app/drawingDimension.ts` providing reference resolution, measurement (`ALIGNED_DISTANCE`, `HORIZONTAL_DISTANCE`, `VERTICAL_DISTANCE`), cursor-driven interpretation scoring with hysteresis, placement offset math, a smart formatter, a strict `mm` parser, creation/deletion helpers, and dependent-dimension cleanup. 
- Integrate UI and lifecycle into the workspace: add a `Dimension` action to the top toolbar, extend `DrawingActiveTool` to include `dimension`, implement acquire/preview/place lifecycle, transient preview layer and final derived annotation rendering (extension lines, arrowheads, formatted value), selection hit target, and inline double-click editor that validates input but refuses to commit a changed driving value until a future solver is implemented (`src/app/DrawingWorkspace.tsx`). 
- History and persistence foundations: snapshot-based transaction boundary for dimension create/delete supporting `Ctrl+Z`/`Ctrl+Y`, V1→V2 migration that fails closed for missing references, and helpers to delete entities while removing dependent dimensions; add styling and a focused test harness and npm script. 

### Testing
- Ran the focused foundation tests with `npm run test:drawing-dimension-foundation`, which executed the new `tests/drawing-dimension-foundation.test.mjs` and passed. 
- Executed the relevant Drawing/CAD regression suites including `npm run test:drawing-alignment-snap`, `npm run test:d2-2b`, `npm run test:d2-3`, `npm run test:d2-3a`, `npm run test:drawing-primary-mousedown`, `npm run test:cad-interaction-contract`, `npm run test:ui`, and `npm run test:box-empty-start`, all of which passed in this environment. 
- Built the production bundle with `npm run build` and verified `git diff --check`; the project builds successfully. 
- Tests confirm formatter and parser behavior, semantic references (no copied authoritative coordinates), aligned/horizontal/vertical measurements, placement persistence in model space, transient previews, non-committing inline editing behavior, and deletion cleanup.

body:
## What

Cleans up the repo's GitHub Actions and moves site-list maintenance into an on-demand skill that a human reviews.

## Removed workflows

| Workflow | Why |
|---|---|
| **AI Link Fixer** (`ai-link-fixer.yml`) | Weekly cron. Stripped "broken" links from the README with no judgment and opened PRs nobody merged. #90 and #91 have sat open for weeks. |
| **Generate Changelog** (`changelog-generator.yml`) | Committed straight to `main` on every README push, and posted to Slack from the same job. |
| **AI PR Review** (`pr-review.yml`) | GitHub Models comment on every PR push. Low signal for a link list. |
| **Issue Site Submission Processor** (`issue-site-submission.md` + 1336-line `.lock.yml`) | gh-aw / Copilot agent firing automatically on any issue or comment. |
| **Copilot Setup Steps** (`copilot-setup-steps.yml`) | Support file for the above. |

Also removed `.github/agents/` and `.github/aw/`.

## Kept

**Link Checker** (`github-action.yml`) stays as a real merge gate:
- Trigger is now `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch` only. No more push-to-main runs.
- `actions/checkout@v2 -> v4`, `actions/setup-node@v1 -> v4`.

## Added

`.claude/skills/site-maintenance/` - invoked on demand, never scheduled, never triggered. Three scenarios:

1. **Check existing sites** - link-check, triage failures into remove / skip-list / keep-watching, human approves, then it opens a PR.
2. **Add or update a site** - dedupe, classify into a category, write the entry, link-check, open a PR. Can process a GitHub issue when handed an issue number.
3. **Find new sites** - explicit ask only. One cheap pass over a curated source list, returns a shortlist, no PR.

Changelog generation (via the existing `scripts/generate-changelog.js`) folds into scenarios 1 and 2. `scripts/README.md` and `contributing.md` updated to match.

## Follow-up (manual, not in this PR)

- Close PRs #90 and #91.
- Delete the now-unused `SLACK_CHANNEL_ID` and `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` repo secrets.

body:
## Summary
Implements the Phase 3 client portal and approval flow on top of the existing workspace and deliverable model.

- Adds project-scoped opaque portal links for owner/admin users.
- Adds the live `/p/:token` client project and deliverable review experience.
- Supports client approval and change requests for deliverables that are ready for review.
- Preserves the existing static `/p/demo` experience.

## Database migration
Adds `supabase/migrations/20260901043252_client_portal_approval.sql`.

The migration is intentionally **not applied**. It adds:
- `project_portal_links` with SHA-256 token hashes only, one active link per project, composite workspace FKs, and immutable context fields.
- `deliverable_approval_events` as an immutable approval/change-request audit trail.
- Fixed-search-path SECURITY DEFINER RPCs for manager link creation/revocation, portal reads, and portal decisions.
- RLS and grants with no anonymous table access. Anonymous access is limited to the two token-validating RPCs.

## Security notes
- A portal token resolves only its active project, linked client, and non-archived reviewable deliverables.
- Decision RPCs require the target deliverable to match the token's workspace and project and to be `ready_for_review`.
- The database trigger validates project/client/workspace context independently of the app.
- Existing Clients, Projects, Deliverables, Workspaces, memberships, Auth, and Phase 2A/2C policies are unchanged.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck` passed.
- `npm run build` passed.
- Existing Vite bundle-size warning remains non-blocking.

## Manual QA after migration approval
- Create a client-attached project and generate a portal link as owner/admin.
- Verify the link shows only that project and its reviewable deliverables.
- Approve and request changes, then refresh to confirm persisted state.
- Regenerate/revoke a link and verify old links no longer resolve.
- Attempt cross-project and cross-workspace deliverable IDs against a portal link and verify they are rejected.
- Regenerate `src/types/database.ts` from the live schema after the migration is applied.

# Pull Request Checklist

**Hotspot / lock note (if any):**

```text
<!-- e.g. Working on queue.ts — extract X into lib/ — ETA Friday -->
```

---

## Architecture & Placement

* [ ] Logic is placed in the correct layer (UI / hook / service / DB)
* [ ] Business logic is NOT inside UI components
* [ ] Routes / server actions are thin (validate → call service → return)
* [ ] No direct DB access from UI

---

## Data Flow & State Ownership

* [ ] Data flow is clear and traceable (Server → Client → UI)
* [ ] State has a single source of truth
* [ ] No duplication of business state across layers
* [ ] External data follows pattern: Webhook → DB → App reads DB

---

## Security / RLS / Token Flows (if applicable)

* [ ] Queries are properly scoped (user / org / token context)
* [ ] No trust in client-provided identifiers
* [ ] Token routes only access token-scoped data
* [ ] No owner-level DB usage in user-facing flows

---

## Components & Structure

* [ ] Components are single-purpose and small (<100 lines)
* [ ] No deeply nested JSX
* [ ] Client components are minimal and isolated
* [ ] Server components used by default where possible

---

## Functions & Logic

* [ ] Functions are small and focused (single responsibility)
* [ ] No large multi-purpose handlers
* [ ] Naming clearly reflects intent

---

## Reuse & Abstraction

* [ ] No duplicated logic (extracted if reused)
* [ ] No unnecessary abstractions
* [ ] Existing patterns were reused where appropriate

---

## Complexity Check

* [ ] Change reduces or maintains system complexity
* [ ] No hidden side effects
* [ ] No “magic” or implicit behavior
* [ ] Easy to understand in <30 seconds

---

## Refactoring

* [ ] Touched code was improved where necessary
* [ ] No new code layered on top of poor structure

---

## Error Handling & Reliability

* [ ] Errors are handled explicitly
* [ ] No silent failures
* [ ] Behavior is deterministic and debuggable

---

## Final Gate

* [ ] Would a staff engineer approve this without major comments?
* [ ] Is ownership of logic and data clear?
* [ ] Does this follow `rules.mdc`?

If any answer is "no" → refactor before merging.

author: magyarmex
body:
## Problem and baseline
The authoritative Python r25 seam can now emit/consume compact `implicit-v4` filesystem control when it is structurally and semantically safe, but the shared native reader still understands only explicit filesystem-v1. This PR is a staging-only D5 prerequisite against `agent/v030-authoritative-integration`; it carries no release credit and must be reconciled onto the exact authoritative landing head before promotion.

## Insight and hypothesis
Do not build a second public archive path for compact control. Native should authenticate graph-owned regular identities, decode either filesystem-v1 or implicit-v4 into the same existing `FsManifest` semantic object, and then reuse list/read/verify/extract/recovery/ZIP/C-ABI behavior. Frozen wire vectors make the cross-language boundary independently checkable. A material portability edge case was identified: implicit-v4 prefix lengths follow Python Unicode code-point slicing, not UTF-8 byte offsets.

The explicit disproof surface is simple: if Rust cannot independently reproduce the frozen wire semantics, reject malformed controls at the same-or-stricter trust boundary, and preserve canonical public/recovery behavior without duplicate semantics, the native parity hypothesis fails and this staging work must not promote. The quality-ratchet is one-way: compact-control support may add new accepted canonical bytes only after preserving every old filesystem-v1 invariant; no existing path, integrity, locality, recovery or platform gate may be weakened to admit it.

## Alternatives considered
- Duplicate native public semantics for implicit-v4: rejected because it creates drift and doubles recovery/integrity surface.
- Re-run encoder search at decode: rejected; decoder must remain deterministic/bounded.
- Treat prefix lengths as UTF-8 offsets: rejected by the frozen Unicode vector and the canonical Python grammar.
- Merge immediately after Python landing: rejected; native malformed-control, recovery, locality and Android authority remain mandatory.

## Evidence
The upstream exact D5 A/B proved compact control substantially smaller while preserving exact filesystem-v1 semantics, strong tree verification and <=8x locality. This staging PR adds frozen ASCII and Unicode implicit-v4 vectors, Python custody tests binding those bytes to the executable specification, a bounded Rust parser staging module, hostile-vector contracts, and `docs/v030-rnd/IMPLICIT_V4_NATIVE_PARITY_HANDOFF.md`. Current PR native-core workflow is green; that does **not** yet prove the new parser because it is intentionally not wired into the crate/public reader until reconciliation and focused Rust tests are ready.

## Losses, ambiguity and negative evidence
No native parity claim is made yet. The staging parser has not been integrated into `Canonical25Archive`/`FsManifest` or exercised by canonical native goldens. The first branch-only native-core green therefore proves existing native behavior did not regress, not implicit-v4 support. The frozen F01/Foundry thesis is unrelated to this D5 work and is not being modified here.

## Safety, integrity and resource accounting
The staged contract requires fail-closed rejection of wrong versions/root shape, oversized control/entry/xattr state, invalid masks/trailing fields, signed-delta overflow/domain violations, unsafe/duplicate/unsorted paths, regular/explicit collisions, invalid hardlink indices, graph/control count and identity mismatches, and malformed kind payloads. The compact control retains the existing 8 MiB decode-unit ceiling. Symlink extraction safety remains at least as strict as the existing native filesystem parser/materializer boundary.

## Compatibility and portability
The Rust implementation must consume the same wire grammar as Python and converge into the existing `FsManifest` semantics. The Unicode vector explicitly pins prefix length to Unicode code points, preventing a Rust/UTF-8 byte-offset divergence. After native parity, the same vectors must cross Android/JNI and physical ARM64 authority where required.

## Performance accounting
This PR makes no encode-speed or release-performance claim. The upstream compact-control size win remains the reason to productize the seam; all native parsing/authentication and eventual selector/publication costs remain inside ordinary product timing/authority. No benchmark threshold is changed.

## Public-surface check
No public release/version/site claim is changed. v0.30 remains merge/tag/version/publish locked. The staging branch adds internal conformance/evidence material only.

## Completion gates
- [x] Freeze ASCII implicit-v4 native wire vector.
- [x] Freeze Unicode/code-point prefix vector.
- [x] Bind frozen vectors to exact Python encoder/decoder semantics.
- [x] Enumerate malformed compact-control cases for native parity.
- [ ] Reconcile onto the current authoritative Python seam head.
- [ ] Compile/integrate the bounded Rust dual-control parser into `FsManifest`/`Canonical25Archive`.
- [ ] Add Rust happy-path + malformed-vector tests.
- [ ] Regenerate a canonical r25 native golden that actually selects implicit-v4.
- [ ] Pass native list/read/verify/extract/recovery/C-ABI/locality authority.
- [ ] Pass Android/JNI/physical ARM64 authority where required.
- [ ] Re-run exact all-workload/release authority before any product credit.

## Future leverage
A single dual-control native semantic seam keeps future r25 filesystem-control improvements from multiplying public reader/recovery implementations. The frozen vectors also become reusable cross-language conformance inputs for Android and any future reader implementation.

Draft/staging only. **Do not merge into the authoritative frontier until the exact Python landing head is reconciled and the native parity gates above are actually green.**

author: mosamlife
body:
Bounds the assistant surface's site read over **the connection's own scope** instead of over the tenant.

**Draft: this is a tenancy-relevant read and gets a `security-reviewer` pass.**

## The defect

`ListSitesForRead` (`apps/api/internal/mcp/repo.go`) reads one page of the **tenant's** sites — `ListSites`, `Sort: "name"`, `Limit: limit+1`, `sitesPageBound = 500` — and the connection's site scope is applied in Go afterwards.

An in-scope site whose name sorts past the tenant's first 500 rows is therefore never among the rows the filter runs over. The order is deterministic, so **no number of retries can ever produce it**, and the refusal text tells the caller to retry. It also can only arise once the tenant holds at least 500 sites, so its arrival is a fact about sites the caller is not entitled to know exist.

## What is in this PR

The query layer only: `ListSitesForMCPScope`, plus the sqlc regeneration.

```sql
SELECT s.*
FROM sites s
WHERE s.tenant_id = @tenant_id
  AND s.id = ANY(@site_ids::uuid[])
  AND s.connection_state <> 'archived'
ORDER BY lower(s.name) ASC, s.id DESC
LIMIT @row_limit;
```

**No migration, and none is needed.** `sites.id` is the primary key and already indexed; no column, constraint or policy changes, and `db/schema.sql` is untouched.

**No Go caller is switched here.** `internal/mcp` still calls `ListSites`. The repo/service change that consumes this query is `backend-architect`'s and follows separately — see "What must follow" below.

## Dedicated query, not a `narg` arm on `ListSites`

The alternative was `sqlc.narg('site_ids')` on the shared `ListSites`, where NULL means "no scope filter". Rejected, and for a sharper reason than the duplication trade-off:

**For an array parameter sqlc emits the same Go type — `[]uuid.UUID` — for `sqlc.arg` and `sqlc.narg` alike**, because a Go slice is already nullable. The two designs are therefore *indistinguishable at the call site* and differ only in what a nil slice means. That difference is measured in the proof below, not argued:

```
nil slice  -> id = ANY(NULL::uuid[]) returns 0 rows
narg arm with the SAME nil slice returns 600 rows (the whole tenant)
```

One identical mistake — a scope set lost on an error path, a struct field left unassigned — returns the fleet in one design and nothing in the other. `id = ANY(NULL::uuid[])` is NULL and `id = ANY('{}'::uuid[])` is false, so both spellings of an absent scope fail closed.

The drift objection does not really apply, because this is not a copy: the assistant surface has one order and no filters, so the new query carries no `state` / `client_id` / `any_tags` / `all_tags` / `q` arm to fall out of step with the dashboard's. It also drops both `LEFT JOIN`s, which exist for the dashboard's cache badges and whose columns `toSiteRecord` never reads.

## The dashboard `/sites` path is unchanged, by construction

The change is **purely additive**. Deleted-line count in each path, this turn:

```
$ git diff -U0 origin/main -- apps/api/db/query/sites.sql | grep -E '^-' | grep -vc '^---'
0
$ git diff -U0 origin/main -- apps/api/internal/db/sqlc/ | grep -E '^-' | grep -vc '^---'
0
```

`ListSites` and its generated Go are byte-identical, so every filter and all six sort orders on `/sites` are the same code. That is a stronger guarantee than a behavioural test.

## Proof

Run as `wpmgr_app`, with `current_user` / `rolsuper` / `rolbypassrls` read **inside the transaction under test** and asserted — the block refuses to prove anything if it finds itself superuser or `BYPASSRLS`. Fixture is 600 sites in one tenant, scope is the single site that sorts **last** by name, all inside a transaction that is rolled back.

```
NOTICE:  role under test: current_user=wpmgr_app rolsuper=f rolbypassrls=f
NOTICE:  tenant holds 600 sites; page bound is 501
NOTICE:  connection scope = 1 site, the last by name: site-0599
NOTICE:  OLD shape (bound over the tenant): in-scope rows surviving the page = 0
NOTICE:  NEW shape (bound over the scope): returned=1 out_of_scope=0
NOTICE:  nil slice  -> id = ANY(NULL::uuid[]) returns 0 rows
NOTICE:  empty slice -> id = ANY('{}'::uuid[]) returns 0 rows
NOTICE:  narg arm with the SAME nil slice returns 600 rows (the whole tenant)
NOTICE:  ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED as wpmgr_app (rolsuper=f, rolbypassrls=f)
```

The old shape returning `0` is the currently-impossible case stated as a measurement: that site cannot be read today.

**Mutation M1 — scope predicate removed.** The leak assertion is ordered *first* deliberately, so it fires on its own rather than behind the row-count check:

```
# MUTATED (psql exit 3)
NOTICE:  NEW shape (bound over the scope): returned=501 out_of_scope=501
ERROR:  LEAK: 501 out-of-scope rows were emitted by the scoped read

# RESTORED (psql exit 0)
NOTICE:  NEW shape (bound over the scope): returned=1 out_of_scope=0
NOTICE:  ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED as wpmgr_app (rolsuper=f, rolbypassrls=f)
```

`git grep -q "MUTATION M" -- apps/api` exits **1**; the fixture rolled back leaving 0 rows behind.

## Regeneration

`sqlc` resolved with `command -v sqlc` → `/Users/mosamgor/go/bin/sqlc`, `sqlc version` → `v1.31.1`, matching the tree stamp from `grep -h 'sqlc v' apps/api/internal/db/sqlc/*.go | sort -u` → `//   sqlc v1.31.1`. After regenerating, `git diff --quiet -- apps/api/internal/db/sqlc/` exits **0**. No hand-edits.

## What must follow, in `backend-architect`'s hands

1. **Switch the caller.** `Repo.ListSitesForRead` should take the resolved scope and call `ListSitesForMCPScope`. The return type moves from `[]sqlc.ListSitesRow` to `[]sqlc.Site`; `toSiteRecord` reads only `sites` columns, all of which `sqlc.Site` carries, so that is a type swap rather than a rewrite. Once it lands, `site_unread` is unreachable from this path.

2. **A second, separate finding — the RLS policy is inert on this path.** `ListSitesForRead` opens its transaction with `InTenantTx`, which never sets `app.site_scope`. The RESTRICTIVE `sites_site_scope` policy (m19, `20260531050000_m19_orgs_sharing.sql:330`) reads `app.site_scope <> 'on' OR id = ANY(app.allowed_site_ids)`, so with the GUC unset it is permissive and does no work here. That is correct behaviour for the dashboard's org-scoped callers, but it means this read currently has **no** database-level scope enforcement — the Go filter is the only gate. Moving to `RunTenantTx` with the principal would engage the policy as a genuine second layer, the way `ListGrants` already does. The new query's predicate holds under either helper, so this is defence in depth rather than a dependency.

author: thejohnmatti
body:
M3 slice 1 — the pitch is observability, and this is where it starts paying off.

## Metrics (DESIGN O6) — hand-rolled, still 2 deps

`punctual/metrics.py` renders the Prometheus text exposition from `store.metrics_snapshot()` (one pass over `runs` + `job_clock`). No `prometheus_client` — most of these are *derived from the store on scrape*, not in-process counters, so a client library barely fits.

| metric | |
|---|---|
| `punctual_runs_total{job,state}` | finished runs by terminal state |
| `punctual_time_since_last_success_seconds{job}` | **the SLO gauge** |
| `punctual_run_duration_seconds` | histogram, cron-shaped buckets |
| `punctual_lost_runs_total{job}` | runs the daemon lost mid-flight |
| `punctual_job_quarantined{job}` / `punctual_job_consecutive_failures{job}` | circuit-breaker state |
| `punctual_pending_retries` | retries waiting on backoff |
| `punctual_scheduler_loop_lag_seconds` | tick overshoot past the sleep cap |

## Exposure

- **`punctual metrics`** / **`punctual healthz`** over the control socket
- opt-in **`[observability] metrics_port`** (+ `metrics_addr`, default `127.0.0.1`) → a minimal stdlib HTTP listener serving `GET /metrics` and `GET /healthz`
- **`/healthz`**: `200 ok` unless draining, or the tick loop hasn't run for `> MAX_SLEEP + 5s` (→ `503`). `punctual healthz` exits non-zero.

```
$ curl -s localhost:9137/healthz          → ok  [200]
$ curl -s localhost:9137/metrics | grep since_last_success
punctual_time_since_last_success_seconds{job="beat"} 0.606853
punctual_job_quarantined{job="flap"} 1
punctual_scheduler_loop_lag_seconds 0.00246929
```

## Config change

`load_config` now returns a **`Config`** (`.jobs` + `.observability`). Unknown top-level tables (anything but `[job.*]` / `[observability]`) are now a hard error. `_load(ctx)` in the CLI still hands back `list[Job]` — only `run` needs the full object.

## `on_recovery` (O10 addendum)

Third notify hook: fires when a job that was quarantined or had `consecutive_failures > 0` succeeds again. Same sinks / fire-and-forget.

## Tests

`test_metrics.py` (render + HTTP server), plus config / control / quarantine / cli additions. 104 tests, coverage 83%.

## Next (M3 slice 2)

Structured JSON logs — `punctual run --log-format json`, one object per state transition.
