author: gingin77
body:
Adds a knowledge base entry for immunodeficiency 88 ([MONDO:0030483](https://monarchinitiative.org/MONDO:0030483)) — inherited T-bet deficiency, caused by loss of the transcription factor TBX21. It is one of the genetic causes of Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD), the syndrome in which otherwise healthy children get serious disease from mycobacteria that do not trouble anyone else, including the BCG vaccine strain.

What makes it worth a separate entry rather than a footnote on the other MSMD genes: most of them break the interferon-gamma signal. This one breaks the cells that make it. T-bet is the transcription factor that builds the interferon-gamma-producing lymphocyte compartment in the first place, so losing it removes the cells rather than the signalling step.

Closes #10343

## The mechanism, and why it has three arms

T-bet does two opposite jobs — it drives type 1 immunity and it holds type 2 immunity down. Losing it does both at once, in different cell populations. So one gene defect gives an infection phenotype, an allergic phenotype, and an antibody phenotype, and the entry models them as three chains from one root node.

```
                          TBX21 loss of function
                                    |
        +---------------------------+---------------------------+
        |                           |                           |
   type 1 arm                  type 2 arm                  B cell arm
        |                           |                           |
NK/iNKT/MAIT/Vd2            loss of Th2                lost CD11c-hi
 fail to develop             repression                CD21-lo subset
        |                           |                           |
  IFN-gamma deficit  <--  CD4+ Th2 cytokine excess      class switch skew
        |                           |                           |
  macrophages not             eosinophilia,              IgE up, IgG2 down
    activated              upper airway inflammation
        |
 uncontrolled mycobacterial
      replication
```

The most interesting finding in the source, and the reason the entry gives it its own node: the patient's CD8+ and non-classic CD4+ TH1\* cells make interferon-gamma perfectly normally in response to mycobacteria — and it does not help. That is a negative result establishing that the innate and innate-like compartments are not redundant in humans, which is a claim about protective immunity generally rather than about this one child.

## What is in the entry

Nine pathophysiology nodes, ten phenotypes, three treatments, three diagnostic entries, three animal models, one biochemical marker, one dataset, and three discussion entries recording what one patient cannot settle. 68 evidence snippets, all verified against the reference cache.

Also adds immunodeficiency 88 as a member of `kb/groupings/Intrinsic_and_Innate_Immunity_Defect_IEIs.yaml`, whose membership criterion it satisfies — `just check-groupings` confirms.

## Handling of the single-patient problem

This disease has essentially one published patient, described across three papers by the same group. Almost every population-level number available is for MSMD as a whole. Three things follow, and reviewers should check I got them right:

**Prevalence carries no rate.** The MSMD-wide record has `measure_type` and evidence but deliberately no `rate_per_100000` and no `prevalence_class`. Those slots are machine-queryable and get exported; filling them would assert a population rate for a one-patient disease no matter what the prose said. The two published MSMD estimates also disagree five-fold — about 1 in 10,000 and about 1 in 50,000 — so both are quoted rather than reconciled.

**Recurrent infection is explicitly refuted, not asserted.** `HP:0011274` is deliberately not bound. The patient had one BCG episode, was cured, and has been free of mycobacterial infection for several years. The entry records that as a `REFUTE` evidence item so nobody later reads the class-level susceptibility as an observed relapsing course.

**Recombinant interferon-gamma is an indication, not a treatment given.** It is the mechanistically right therapy here — the receptor and its signalling are intact, so exogenous cytokine has something to act on — but no TBX21-deficient patient has received it. That is stated in the treatment's own `notes`.

Claims borrowed from the MSMD population rather than from TBX21-deficient patients are marked as such in their `explanation` fields throughout.

## One phenotype left without an ontology term

The patient's upper airway inflammation is recorded as free text with no `term:`. The nearest HPO term, `HP:0002257` Chronic rhinitis, is defined as inflammation of the *nasal mucosa*, and the source says only "upper airway inflammation" — its abstract does not contain the words nasal, rhinitis, or sinus. Binding it would invent an anatomical claim. HPO has no broader upper-airway-inflammation term; the nearest alternatives are obstruction terms. The search is recorded in `notes` so it is not repeated. An HPO new-term request is the real fix.

## Deep research provenance

Falcon was requested but is not configured in this environment. Rather than swapping providers by hand, the run used the documented `--fallback` flag and was served by `claude_code`, which the report frontmatter records as `fell_back: true` with `requested_provider: falcon`. Reference and term validation sections were retro-fitted: 22 of 22 references resolved with none unresolved. Of those, 13 were confirmed on topic and none off topic — the remaining 9 were undecided rather than cleared, since a record with no abstract cannot be scored either way; 107 terms checked with none unresolved and two mislabelled, both UBERON terms in a section of the report this entry does not use.

The dataset search is worth flagging as a near miss. A TBX21 gene-only search returned twelve candidates, eleven of them mouse or cancer datasets about unrelated T-bet biology — the named-entity-confusion pattern the dataset curation docs warn about. The twelfth turned out to be single-cell RNA-seq from a companion study of this same patient, which is how two further papers on him were found. Those two papers are where the entire type 2 and B cell arms came from. Only that one accession is curated.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `just validate-disorders` | passes, 68/68 snippets verified |
| `just validate-terms` | passes |
| `just verify-datasets` | 1/1 accession resolves |
| `just check-groupings` | membership criterion satisfied |
| duplicate-keys, entity-refs, causal-targets, qualifier-terms | pass |
| folded-hyphens, snippet-length, title-snippets, snippet-grading | pass |
| environmental-evidence, enum-values | pass |
| Compliance | 86.0% |

Two gates caught real defects during drafting, both fixed here. `check-snippet-grading` found one quoted sentence that mixes an in-vitro result with a plasma measurement being graded two different ways in two blocks; it is now split into two evidence items, each quoting its own clause. `check-causal-targets` found a bare-name pathograph edge left dangling by a phenotype rename — the silent failure mode issue #10112 describes.

The remaining compliance gap is mostly causal edges with no evidence of their own, where the node or phenotype at each end carries the citation but no source states the link itself. Those are left uncited rather than propped up with a quote that does not make the causal claim.

## Noted but not fixed here

Immunodeficiency 69 also satisfies the membership criterion of `Intrinsic_and_Innate_Immunity_Defect_IEIs` and is not listed. That omission predates this work, so it belongs in its own pull request rather than folded into a curation PR for a different disease.

author: napetrov
body:
## Summary

Finalizes ADR-063 Phase 3 (D5) by migrating `PublicSurfaceQuery`'s public-domain closure walk (and `export_surface.py`'s `contract=exports` type-closure step, which shares the same function) onto a real traversal over `AbiSnapshot.surface_graph`, replacing `surface.py`'s old independent regex-based re-parse.

## Motivation

Phase 3's infrastructure (the evidence graph, `AbiSnapshot.surface_graph`, `PublicSurfaceQuery`) landed in thirteen earlier slices, but `PublicSurfaceQuery` still delegated to `surface.py`'s/`export_surface.py`'s pre-existing closure-walk implementations unchanged — the phase's own stated acceptance criteria ("`surface.py`'s own traversal implementation ... deleted, not kept alongside") was left open. This PR closes that gap.

## Changes

- `compare/surface_graph.py`: each declaration/type/typedef node now carries a precomputed `referenced_identifiers` attr (what it references, unioned across any node-id collision) plus an `identifiers_collision` flag for callers needing per-declaration precision; `fact_list`/`node_id_for_declaration`/`node_id_for_type`/`node_id_for_typedef` exposed as small public helpers.
- `surface.py`'s closure-walk implementation (`_index_surface_types`, `_seed_public_roots`, `_walk_type_closure`, `_walk_exact_type_closure`, `_record_exact_identities`, `_record_nested_in_known_record`, `_record_is_confirmed_public_seed`) and its `PublicSurface` result type are **deleted** from that module and moved to a new leaf-module pair:
  - `abicheck/policy/public_surface.py` — the `PublicSurface` dataclass and declaration/type indexing/bookkeeping.
  - `abicheck/policy/public_surface_closure.py` — the actual closure-walk algorithm and the real `resolve_public_surface()` entry point.
  - `abicheck/policy/public_surface_query.py` — `PublicSurfaceQuery` itself, split into its own module because it is the only place that needs to depend on both the closure module and `export_surface.py` at once (keeping it in the closure module would have closed a real, `check_architecture.py`-detected import cycle once `export_surface.py` started depending on that module directly).
  - `surface.py`'s `compute_public_surface()` is now a thin wrapper delegating to `policy/public_surface_closure.py`, re-exporting `PublicSurface` for existing callers.
- `export_surface.py`'s own export-table-matching root-seeding is unchanged; its final type-closure step calls the same, now-migrated `_walk_type_closure` it always reused verbatim, so that domain's closure became graph-native too.
- A real correctness hazard found and closed during the migration: two declarations can share one approximate graph node id when neither carries a resolved `entity_id` (e.g. two overloads with no mangled name to disambiguate them). Naively trusting the graph's per-node cache for such a collision let a public, narrow-signature overload appear to reference a hidden sibling's own private parameter type. Fixed by flagging the collision on the node and falling back to recomputing that one declaration's own identifiers directly whenever it's set — exactly the pre-migration behavior for the one case a shared-node graph can't represent precisely.
- `architecture/modules.yaml`/`architecture/debt.yaml`: no new dependency-direction or file-size violations (`export_surface.py`'s adoption-debt baseline bumped by 6 lines — a mechanical consequence of `ruff format`'s import-wrapping across the new two-module split, not new debt).
- `scripts/fact_field_readers.py`: removed 4 now-stale `KNOWN_UNMIGRATED_READERS` allowlist entries — the migrated code reads `bases`/`virtual_bases` via the compliant `Fact[T]` path instead of the flagged direct field access.
- `docs/contribute/plans/one-semantic-pipeline.md`: Phase 3 section updated in place (corrections appended, not silently rewritten, matching that document's own convention) to record what actually landed.
- Regression test added (`TestGraphNodeCollisionDoesNotBlurReachability` in `tests/test_policy_public_surface.py`) pinning the node-collision fix directly; confirmed to fail against a version of the fallback that trusts the graph unconditionally.

## Verification

- Full test suite: 34,801 passed (5 pre-existing/environment-flaky failures, all reproduced identically on the unmodified base branch, none touching this area).
- `scripts/check_fp_rate.py`: 0 false positives / 0 false negatives (unchanged).
- `scripts/check_tier_accuracy.py`: unchanged (top-tier correct, under-call monotonic).
- `mypy abicheck/`: clean (554 files). `ruff check`/`ruff format --check`: clean.
- `scripts/check_ai_readiness.py`: 0 errors. `scripts/check_architecture.py`: only 6 pre-existing, unrelated `debt-no-growth` findings (reproduced identically on the base branch).

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added / updated for new behaviour
- [x] Changelog fragment added (`changelog.d/20260901_000000_noreply_adr_063_phase3_traversal_migration.md`)
- [x] Docs updated (ADR-063 implementation plan)
- [x] No new `mypy` or `ruff` errors introduced

author: mcasillas17
body:
> **Stacked on #114.** Base is `worktree-toolchain-doc-refresh`, not `main` — the doc guard asserts against text only #114 corrects. Merge #114 first, or merge both together.

Three fixes, plus the corrections an Opus review of the first draft turned up.

## 1. The wait-loop flakes (this is what failed #114)

Four tests occupy the single DB connection with an open transaction, launch `DispatchPending`, and poll for it to park on the pool — each with its own hardcoded **2-second** deadline. On a loaded CI runner under `-race` the goroutine isn't always scheduled that fast, so they failed on scheduling latency rather than the property they guard. Extracted into `awaitDatabaseWait` on the existing generous `eventuallyTimeout`.

Two things surfaced that a narrower fix would have missed:

- One site's `DispatchPending` carried a **1-second context — shorter than the 2-second poll preceding it**. On a slow runner the wait could legitimately succeed at t=1.2s with the context already expired, failing on the *next* line. That context is a hang-guard, not the assertion (which is a 100ms `ValidateRouting` deadline further down), so raising it masks nothing.
- A second polling loop was silently sharing the `deadline` variable being removed.

The review then found **the same loop a third time**, two functions below, with a *tighter* 1-second bound and the same fatal string — the next CI flake, sitting in the file being fixed. Both copies are now `awaitJobReserved`.

## 2. The unguarded CI pins

`ci_test.go` asserted `go-version` for the lint job only; the other four were held by convention. A drift back to `1.23.x` wouldn't fail outright — `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` would switch toolchains and pass — so nothing would catch it. Now asserted **inside each job block** rather than by counting occurrences, since a count is satisfied by five copies in one job and none in another.

## 3. The stale-docs loop

The toolchain table went stale twice in two days, corrected both times only because someone re-read it. `tools/docs/versions_test.go` reads each version from the file that *enforces* it and requires the docs to agree, so a bump fails a test naming the file to edit.

**The review caught that the first draft of this guard was structurally unable to do its job.** It asserted presence, never attribution — `Contains(claude, "1.23")` was satisfied by the unrelated `1.23-bookworm` container tag, so the module-split prose could have been deleted wholesale and it would still have passed. A character window wasn't enough either: one table row held both tags *and* both subjects, so swapping which service ran which image passed. Attribution is now **line-scoped**, and the two rows that packed several claims onto one line are split so each claim is attributable.

### Mutation-tested, not trusted green

| Mutation | Caught |
|---|---|
| Bump golangci-lint in `ci.yml` | ✅ |
| Bump buf in `breaking.sh` | ✅ ×2 (also catches the proto install guide) |
| Raise a module's `go` directive | ✅ |
| Swap a service's base image — **Dependabot #99's exact pending change** | ✅ |
| Revert one CI job to `1.23.x` | ✅ |

## Also from the review

- `go/version` instead of string comparison, which ranks `1.9` above `1.10`
- The install floor accepts both phrasings the docs already use, so a legitimate rewording can't redden the build
- `tools/proto/README.md` guarded alongside CLAUDE.md — a stale *install guide* misleads more directly than a stale table
- The helper takes `*db.DB`, dropping an import and keeping call sites as `h.database`

## One thing worth naming

This diff falsified three CLAUDE.md sentences about `ci_test.go` asserting the lint job alone — **including the one cited as this change's own motivation**. A PR whose thesis is that docs go stale unnoticed should not ship stale docs. Corrected here.

## Verification

Root tests, full `-race` suite, build, all lint commands, `tools/proto/check.sh` under the pinned protoc, and the package under `-race` at `-count=3` — all green locally. The `-race` fix can only really be confirmed on CI, which is the only environment that ever reproduced it.

author: bh679
body:
Follow-up to #1240 (catch-up spawning). Verifying that feature in play turned up one pre-existing
seam bug and three design bugs in the catch-up path itself — each invisible to unit tests and only
findable by riding the train.

## What a player gets

Catching up no longer costs a visible stutter, and newly spawned carriages stop briefly touching
their neighbour. Ships as **v0.761.0**.

## The seam bug (pre-existing, affects ordinary spawns too)

Every freshly spawned group logged a `too-far` then a `too-close` correction, the second dipping to
**0.00 — carriages actually touching**, under Sable's ~0.3 broad-phase floor.

A group is placed on an INTEGER block origin and carries its sub-block remainder in
`pendingSpawnShiftX`, applied when Sable captures the pose. For a tick or two after that the
`worldAABB` the tracker measures still describes the un-nudged placement, so the first reading was
always exactly `TARGET_GAP_BLOCKS − remainder` — confirmed on 5 of 5 spawns, to the hundredth
(0.60, 0.70, 0.80). The tracker corrected a seam that was already right; the nudge then landed on
top and swung it the other way.

The pre-seed is a half-block move, and every *other* shift arms the `SHIFT_SETTLE_TICKS` throttle
before the next reading — this one had nothing to arm it with. It now does.

**Result: corrective shifts went from ~1 per group to 0 across 125 spawns, settle time unchanged.**

## The catch-up path: three bugs found by playing it

1. **A burst's follower fought its leader.** Two *unplaced* groups sit adjacent and the tracker
   steers each independently, so a leader's correction came out of the intra-burst seam (0.4 → −0.1,
   an overlap). Groups are now linked and move in lockstep, and a linked follower never steers
   itself off geometry that hasn't formed yet.
2. **The train moved out from under the chain.** A run chains off the previous group's *planned* X —
   a snapshot. The train keeps moving: 0.1 blocks/tick at default speed, **0.6 at speed 12, wider
   than the seam itself**. Every run aborted after one group until the chain advanced by the same
   `velocity × ticks × PHYSICS_DT` the canonical-position formula uses.
3. **A chunk-gen wait was treated as a fault.** `spawnPlannedGroup` returning null means "footprint
   still generating, retry" — but it dropped the whole run and handed the lane back to the 60-tick
   gate, cancelling the feature via a routine transient at the forward edge. A deferral now pauses
   the run instead.

## Performance

Measured from `[stuck.timing]` across play sessions — the fill now spreads one group per tick
instead of dumping the whole shortfall into one frame:

| | one-tick fill | spread fill |
|---|---|---|
| median `appender=` | 32 ms | **18 ms** |
| p95 | 110 ms | **36 ms** |
| **max** | **264 ms** | **56 ms** |
| ticks ≥100 ms | 8 | **0** |

A 7-group deficit still closes in about a second. Same total work, no frame-sized spike.

## Verified in play

73 spawns / 46 fill ticks, deepest run 7 groups: **0 run aborts, 0 touching seams, 0 collisions,
0 stalls, 0 ticks ≥100 ms**. One `too-far` (0.80, corrected in one step — too far, never touching).

## Honest limits

- The perf numbers are **observational**, from ordinary play rather than a controlled A/B. The
  mechanism explains the result; the pinned-seed `runServer` harness is the rigorous way to measure.
- A **cold** single spawn still costs up to **843 ms** (chunk generation). The per-tick cap bounds
  how many groups share a tick, never what one cold group costs.
- The **backward lane** was not exercised at depth after these fixes, and `[seamgap]` tracing plus a
  Sable walk-through / autosave pass are still unticked.
- Skipping the placement gate is the sharp edge. It is scoped to a run whose placements come from
  its own chained plan rather than a live pose, and it ends on the first sign of trouble — a needed
  collision correction, the run cap, or a discontinuous tick. Every *first* spawn still goes through
  the gate.

All four gaps above are tracked on board #16.

## Changelog

Adds the v0.761.0 entry, and amends one clause of the still-unreleased v0.758.0 entry which said
Fill all "adds every missing group at once" — true when written, not after this branch. Both are
unreleased and would have shipped contradicting each other.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew build` clean, **3975 tests pass**
- [x] In-play verification across 13 dev-client sessions (numbers above)
- [x] `main` merged in, no conflicts
- [ ] Backward lane at depth + `[seamgap]` measurement + Sable walk/autosave — board #16

## Summary

Wires the LIVE **SZLHOLDINGS/second-brain** Hugging Face Space into serve.py's sovereign/local-LLM-capable request path — fail-closed, honest, and **off by default**.

This is a **citation-handle bridge, not semantic RAG**. It is labelled to match the upstream API's *own* honesty label.

## The real endpoint + schema (verified live)

```
POST https://szlholdings-second-brain.hf.space/api/v1/retrieve
body:    {"query": "<text>", "top_k": <int, default 6>}
returns: schema "szl.second-brain.retrieve/v1"
```

A well-formed response carries `{schema, query, k, handles[], scores[], corpus_n, ready, kind, content_access, index_is_model_weights, raw_graph_nodes_admitted_to_gradients, honesty}` with `content_access: "HANDLES_ONLY"` and `corpus_n: 575`. Per the API's own contract and honesty string, it is a **lexical-overlap ranker over the PUBLIC 575-chunk in-repo projection** (`index_is_model_weights: false`, `raw_graph_nodes_admitted_to_gradients: 0`). It returns **HANDLES** — a `nodeId`, a short `note`, and a `sha256` content pointer — **not** document text/chunks, **not** semantic/vector retrieval, and it does **not** expose the private 9464-node brain graph. This PR's code, docstrings, and labels say exactly that and carry the API's `honesty` string **verbatim**; the claim is never upgraded.

## What changed (three touch points only)

1. **`packages/inference/src/retrieval/second_brain_bridge.py`** (new) —
   `retrieve_handles(query, top_k=6, timeout_s=3.0) -> RetrievalResult`.
   - `status="LIVE"` only on HTTP 200 + a well-formed `szl.second-brain.retrieve/v1` payload (a JSON object with a list-valued `"handles"` key). Every field is passed through **verbatim** — never invented or paraphrased.
   - `status="UNAVAILABLE"` with **empty** handles and a named error on timeout / non-2xx / malformed JSON / missing `"handles"` key / empty query. It **never raises** and never treats an empty/partial response as success.

2. **`serve.py`** — ONE gated seam, `_ac_second_brain_augment`, inside the existing `a11oy.code` request path (`_ac_complete` before `_ac_hf_chat`), behind the env flag **`SZL_SECOND_BRAIN_RAG=1`**.
   - **Flag unset (default): zero behavior change.** The bridge is never consulted and the request path is **byte-identical** to before (no outbound call, unchanged messages, no new response fields).
   - **Flag ON + LIVE:** one `system` message is prepended with the handle notes + sha256 + the API's honesty string, labelled exactly as *"citation handles from a public lexical index, not semantic retrieval, not the full brain graph."*
   - **Flag ON + any failure:** the messages go out **unchanged** and the response's existing generation envelope (`generation.second_brain_rag`) reports `status="UNAVAILABLE", used=false` — it **never** claims retrieval was used and never fabricates a handle.

3. **`tests/test_second_brain_bridge.py`** (new) — hermetic, mirroring the repo's `monkeypatch.setattr(urlopen)` mocking style (no live network). Covers the `retrieve_handles` **LIVE** path (mock 200 + the exact schema), the **UNAVAILABLE** paths (mock timeout **and** mock malformed JSON — both return UNAVAILABLE, never raise, never fake success), the missing-`handles`-key and HTTP-503 failures, and a **regression test proving serve.py's request path is byte-identical when `SZL_SECOND_BRAIN_RAG` is unset**.

## Verification

- `python -m py_compile` passes on every touched file.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_second_brain_bridge.py` → **11 passed** (only the new file run; full suite untouched).
- Banned-token scan of all touched/added content: **0 hits**.

## Notes

- `packages/inference/` is already `COPY`'d into the image (Dockerfile line 627), so the bridge ships with **no Dockerfile change**.
- Doctrine v11: honest labels (`LIVE` / `UNAVAILABLE`), fail-closed, deny-by-default opt-in, no fabrication. The locked-8 is untouched; Λ remains Conjecture 1.
- **Not merged by this PR author** — left for normal review.

author: uxbriel
body:
## Orden para desplegar

1. **Merge de este PR** → Vercel despliega el frontend solo (la barra nueva y el demo completo salen con esto).
2. **`git pull`** en tu máquina.
3. **SQL: no hay.** La columna `shalom_pickup_code` ya existe (bloque §27.d).
4. **Desplegar las 4 funciones:**

```
supabase functions deploy get-session    --project-ref ofdjghntvmrdfjhazfvz
supabase functions deploy pay360-webhook --project-ref ofdjghntvmrdfjhazfvz
supabase functions deploy order-manage   --project-ref ofdjghntvmrdfjhazfvz
supabase functions deploy shalom-order   --project-ref ofdjghntvmrdfjhazfvz
```

**Qué se ve si no despliegas las funciones:** la barra ya muestra *Registrado* y los nombres nuevos, pero la clave no aparece en tu panel (`get-session` viejo no la manda) y pagar el saldo no la suelta por el chat (`pay360-webhook` viejo). El demo enseña todo sin desplegar nada.

## Qué entra

### 1 · El estado **Registrado** en la barra del envío
La barra ENVÍO SHALOM/OLVA gana su primer segmento: **Registrado → En origen → En camino → En agencia → Entregado**. Se enciende cuando hay guía y el courier todavía no reporta (la pre-guía) — antes la barra salía entera apagada con "Esperando el primer estado del courier…", que se lee como "no pasó nada" justo cuando el envío acaba de existir. Debajo dice qué significa: *"Pre-guía: se vuelve oficial cuando el paquete entre a la agencia de origen"* en Shalom; en Olva el texto de siempre.

### 2 · Los identificadores, con el vocabulario del voucher
El PDF de Shalom dice **NRO. ORDEN** y **CÓDIGO**, así que la app dice lo mismo — en el chat, en la barra y en la hoja de guía (`idsDeGuia`, una sola definición): *"Nro. de orden 93076937 · Código J3NT"*. En Olva la guía se sigue llamando guía.

### 3 · La clave, clara y SOLO en el panel del vendedor
En la barra del envío, con su advertencia: *"Clave de recojo 2415 — solo la ve tu equipo; al cliente le llega sola por el chat cuando paga su saldo"*. Viaja por `get-session` detrás del **candado fuerte** (`puedeLeerInterno`, el mismo de los comentarios internos: JWT verificado contra `sellers`) — nunca por `viewer=seller` a secas, que se escribe con el token del comprador.

### 4 · La clave se envía en automático por el chat, solo contra el saldo pagado
- **`pay360-webhook`**: cuando cruza el saldo de un pedido de recojo con clave guardada, después del acuse ("Te enviamos tu clave de recojo por acá") sale el mensaje que la entrega — la promesa ahora se cumple sola.
- **`registrarGuia`**: si al registrarse la guía el pedido ya no debía nada (pagó el total, o el saldo cruzó antes que una guía manual), la clave sale **junto con la guía** — que es lo que el mensaje promete ("junto con la guía te entregaremos tu clave de recojo").
- La guía registrada **a mano** no eligió clave (la suya vive en el comprobante físico): ahí no se manda nada y la sigue pasando una persona, como siempre.
- En chat la copy es una sola (`mensajeDeClave`, probada literal): *"🔑 Tu clave de recojo es 2415. La presentas en el mostrador junto con tu DNI para retirar tu paquete. No la compartas con nadie."*

### 5 · El demo, en paridad completa
- El generador deriva **código y clave del número de guía** — cero tiradas de `r()` nuevas, el azar de todos los pedidos queda intacto (verificado: mismo número 260368 en el test de siempre). La clave pasa por el MISMO validador que usa `shalom-order` al emitir.
- Los hilos que **ya pagaron su saldo** llevan el acuse con su comprobante y la clave; los que **deben**, no la tienen — hay un test que barre el generador entero afirmándolo.
- **Pagar el saldo enseñando** suelta la clave a los diez segundos, igual que el webhook. Avanzar un pedido pagado del todo la entrega junto con la guía.
- Ojo con un caso legítimo que el test destapó: un pedido que pagó el total, recibió su clave con la guía y DESPUÉS recibió un upsell vuelve a tener saldo — la clave ya está en su hilo y la historia no se reescribe. Es exactamente lo que pasaría en la tienda real.

## Verificación

- **900 tests** en verde (12 nuevos), con los de seguridad verificados en reversa: reintroduje la fuga de la clave y el test la atrapó; quité la entrega y el test la atrapó.
- `tsc -b` limpio · build OK · eslint en el baseline exacto (123) · `deno check`: `get-session` y `order-manage` limpios, `shalom-order` con sus 28 errores preexistentes de inferencia (cero nuevos).
- Cierra la deuda de `ESTADO-OPERATIVO`: "la clave no tiene quién se la entregue" — ahora la entrega el pago.

author: barryhubpeople
body:
masthead-nav sizes its logo with `width: auto; height: auto` under a `max-width` and a `max-height`. An image with intrinsic dimensions settles on those and is capped. An image with only a ratio - which is what an SVG exported with a `viewBox` and no dimensions is, and what most brand marks are - has nothing to settle on and resolves to 0x0, so below 60rem the header draws no brand mark at all, on every page built from any of the six shells.

The rule now sets `height` from `--logo-height` and lets the width follow the ratio, with `object-fit: contain` so the small-screen width cap letterboxes the mark rather than stretching it. Above 60rem only the `max-width: none` override remains. The home link takes a 44px floor of its own below 60rem, since `--logo-height` may be set under a thumb's size; that removes the one baseline entry check_phone.py held for this pattern.

ci/check_logo.py is the gate. It renders every pattern carrying a {{logo.src}} image - discovered, not listed - against four logo shapes at six widths straddling 60rem, and fails a mark that is not drawn, one whose box is not as tall as --logo-height resolved to on the page, or one stretched out of its file's ratio. --broken is the positive control and CI runs it: one appended rule puts the logo back the way the defect had it and the check is required to fire. Appended rather than spliced, so rewording the shipped rule cannot disarm it.

masthead-nav to v7; the six compositions regenerate against it.

## What this adds or changes

<!-- One or two sentences: which pattern, and what it is for. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] The pattern is a folder under `patterns/` with all four files
      (`pattern.html`, `pattern.css`, `README.md`, `preview-content.json`)
- [ ] The metadata header is complete (CONTRIBUTING.md has the shape)
- [ ] Every selector in `pattern.css` references the pattern's own class
      (see CONTRIBUTING)
- [ ] No scripts, no inline styles, no hardcoded colours/radii/shadows —
      tokens only
- [ ] `needs` states the real content the pattern consumes, and every need
      has a slot
- [ ] If this changes an existing pattern's CSS or structure: `version` bumped
- [ ] The title, this description and every commit message follow
      [WRITING.md](../WRITING.md) — they say what the change does, name no
      person or role, carry nothing internal, and describe no weakness
- [ ] I looked at all four preview renders — the checks attach them to this PR
      as the `pattern-previews` artifact — and my pattern looks intentional on
      each, including `dark`, which is a hostile brand rather than a style

author: lsegal
body:
`engine/encoder/recon.rs::estimate_sao` searched only the four §8.7.3.2 edge-offset classes, so `SaoTypeIdx == 1` was never selected and the §7.3.8.3 writer's band path — a `sao_offset_sign` per nonzero offset and the five-bin `sao_band_position` — was dead code. Band offset is the case edge offset cannot reach: a CTB biased over a *value range* rather than around a local edge shape.

## The change

- **Band search.** `estimate_sao` bins each CTB's per-sample error by the §8.7.3.2 band index once, then scores all 32 `sao_band_position` candidates off those bins: the four consecutive bands take their own mean errors, clamped to the same §7.4.9.3 magnitude as edge offset but signalled with a sign each, so an offset may point either way.
- **One comparison.** Edge classes, band positions, and leaving SAO off are scored against each other under a single `D + lambda * R` rather than a winner being picked per type first. They do not cost the same: band offset pays four sign bins and five position bins where edge offset pays two class bins and infers its signs.
- **Pricing the band-only syntax.** Those five position bins and the signs are charged at 2.5x `lambda_q8` — the coarse end of the 0.4x–2.5x departure #273's slice-level calibration measured between the closed form and what a picture's own curve pays per bit. Edge offset's rate is the part of that trade the sweep has always been measured on; these bins are rate the closed form has never been checked against, so band offset has to win by more than the uncertainty in its own price. At the closed form itself the search takes band offset at one coarse CTB whose slice then sits 0.003 dB *under* the SAO-off curve — the invariant #273 added; at `SAO_LAMBDA_BAND`, the trust bound rather than the measured end, band offset is never selected at all and every gain below is given back.
- **Chroma.** The §7.4.9.3 inference still holds: Cb and Cr share one type (and, under edge offset, one class), each carrying its own offsets and — under band offset, where nothing is inferred — its own `sao_band_position`. The shared `sao_type_idx_chroma` bin is charged once for the pair.

## The measurement

Whole-picture PSNR and slice bytes against the same writer with SAO off, same QP, same mode decisions, over the QP 12–51 sweep on both test pictures, re-taken on top of #273's calibrated slice-level decision. Only the points that changed:

| picture | QP | edge only | + band offset |
|---|---|---|---|
| noise 64x48 | 12 | pass declined | 1950 B (+0.5%), **+0.100 dB** |
| noise 128x96 | 12 | 8117 B, +0.106 dB | 8121 B, **+0.120 dB** |
| noise 128x96 | 13 | 7817 B, +0.184 dB | 7818 B, **+0.190 dB** |
| noise 128x96 | 14 | 7422 B, +0.156 dB | 7424 B, **+0.167 dB** |
| noise 128x96 | 17 | 6522 B, +0.110 dB | 6525 B, **+0.118 dB** |
| noise 128x96 | 19 | 5882 B, +0.100 dB | 5890 B, **+0.127 dB** |

So band offset **is** selected and **does** earn its rate: it buys one operating point the edge-only search declined outright and improves five more for one to eight bytes each. Every other point of the sweep is byte-identical to the edge-only search, no point regresses, and every accepted point still sits on or above the SAO-off writer's own rate-distortion curve. It is never selected on the smooth picture at any QP — that content's error is edge-shaped, which is what §8.7.3.2 is for — nor at any QP coarse enough that nine extra bins outweigh what a value-range bias is worth.

## Tests

- `the_decoded_stream_matches_the_encoders_own_reconstruction` still passes sample for sample on both pictures at QP 0/12/26/37/51, with band offset selected inside that sweep, so the writer's band path is exercised by it.
- `the_search_picks_band_offset_where_it_beats_every_edge_class` pins the picture and QP where `SaoTypeIdx == 1` is chosen, that the slice-level test kept the pass, and that a decoder resolves the resulting `sao( )` structures back into the encoder's own reconstruction.
- `band_offset_earns_its_rate_where_the_search_takes_it` pins the PSNR and byte count of that operating point.
- `the_search_takes_band_offset_where_the_bias_is_a_value_range` is the unit-level case: two flat regions, one biased 3 low, where every interior sample is edge category 0 — the search must pick band offset and offset the band the bias lives in.
- `every_accepted_sao_point_sits_on_the_writers_own_curve` (from #273) passes unchanged with band offset in the search, which is the invariant the 2.5x charge above exists to hold.
- The existing SAO tests (`..._is_worth_taking_where_the_writer_takes_it`, `..._is_declined_when_it_would_not_clear_its_own_syntax`, `..._never_costs_the_writer_quality`, `the_access_unit_signals_sao_as_enabled`) are unchanged and still pass.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --features native -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --features native --lib` (470 passed) are clean locally.

The writer's module documentation states which way it went, and the changelog carries the user-facing note. No UI code is touched, so no screenshots or screen recordings apply.

Closes #274

author: lemillermicrosoft
body:
Closes #27.

Reported by deehoc via Discord DM:

> Their party hunter also has TotemPing installed, but the frame never appears for the hunter. Hunter tried `/tp frame show`, size, and offset slash commands — no sign of the frame.

## Root cause

`runScan()` in `TotemPing.lua` early-returns for non-shamans (`if not isShaman then return end`), so `RangeIndicator.Update()` was never invoked on hunter/warrior/etc. clients. All icons stayed in the default hidden/idle state, and `/tp frame show` couldn't force them visible because the next paint just re-idled them.

`Comms.lua` was already computing missing-buff status for the local player (based on remote shaman broadcasts) and calling `TotemPing_RangeIndicator.SetReceiverStatus(missing)` — but that method didn't exist on `RI`, so the receiver silently fell through to a minimal side-icon fallback that only anchors if `PlayerFrame`/`ElvUF_Player` happens to be present at Comms-load time.

## Fix

- Implement `RI.SetReceiverStatus(missing)` in `RangeIndicator.lua`. It drives the `"player"` icon slot with the same ok/miss/idle visuals used for shamans, honoring `db.enabled`, `db.showPlayer`, and `db.showUnits.player`.
- Guard with `localUpdateActive`: if the local player is a shaman running the normal scan loop, their `RI.Update` path keeps priority (no clobber from a party co-shaman's broadcast).
- `/tp frame show` now also calls `applyReceiverPlayerIcon()` so hunters get immediate feedback instead of waiting for the next 1s Comms tick.

Non-shaman party members now see a single icon anchored to their own player frame (idle when no shaman is broadcasting, green check when in range of all shaman totems, red X with tooltip listing which buffs are missing).

No changes to SavedVariables shape, TOC, or the shaman-side code path.

author: conjfrnk
body:
Nine of seventy tasks in a Terminal-Bench Science run failed with:

```
GatewayProviderError: ProviderError (invalid_request_error): 400 -
'Invalid assistant message: content or tool_calls must be set'
```

`MaxOutputTokensExceededError` is raised, per the comment above the handler, "when max tokens is hit AND output is empty (e.g., all tokens consumed by reasoning)". Recovery appended `{"role": "assistant", "content": ""}`, and providers read an empty string as unset — so the *next* request carries an assistant message with neither content nor tool calls and is rejected. The run ends there.

The handler written for a model that reasoned itself out of output was the thing ending those runs. A placeholder keeps the message valid; nothing else changes.

It only bites reasoning models that exhaust their output budget without emitting content. This run used `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` — `reasoning_model: true`, `reasoning_effort: "high"`, 384k output budget — which reaches that path often on hard tasks. Nine occurrences, 75% of all failures in the run.

Affected: `duan-thesis`, `finite-free-stam`, `linked-cell-suppression`, `rolling-shutter-oma`, `gen-turan-paths`, `regularized-game-proof`, `xrd-multiphase-qpa`, `spin-glass-groundstate`, `onsager-ising-lean`. Run `25312c04-0e79-427f-9152-c69f678c2d31`.

Since it depends on the model rather than the benchmark, any board pairing a reasoning model with this agent is likely losing tasks to it as sporadic unexplained errors.

122 tests pass.

author: mufflyt
body:
## The short version

I was asked to run `analyze_temporal_plausibility.R` and report the D17 numbers. It exited 0 and reported **100.0% "not assessable"** across all 16,898 accepted matches. That is not a result — it is a measurement failure that looks like one.

This PR fixes the cause, reports the numbers that were actually there, corrects a claim in D17's own evidence section, and pins the regression.

---

## The defect

```r
cert_year <- function(v) suppressWarnings(as.integer(substr(as.character(v), 1, 4)))
```

`certification_date` in the frozen crosswalk is **`MM/YYYY`** (`"06/2015"`), not ISO. So `substr(v, 1, 4)` is `"06/2"`, and `as.integer("06/2")` is `NA` — for **all 22,309 rows**, silently, under `suppressWarnings()`. Every accepted match fell through to the `"not assessable"` branch of the verdict `case_when()`, the summary artifact was written, and the script returned success.

This is the same failure class as #157: **a run that reports success having measured nothing.** A zero is not obviously wrong the way a crash is.

Parsed: **0 → 22,309 rows**, year range 1971–2026.

> ⚠️ Any reading of `artifacts/temporal_plausibility_summary.csv` taken before this commit is void.

---

## What the numbers actually are

**Censoring first.** Of 16,898 accepted matches, **6,020 (35.6%) are left-censored** — the panel opens in 2007 and NPPES began enumerating in 2006, so first-seen is a *bound*, not a date, and no grace period makes those rows informative. Every percentage below has **10,878** as its denominator, not 16,898.

Among the 10,878 assessable, `lead_years` (certification year minus NPI first-seen year; positive is the suspicious direction) runs **−54 to +17**, median −1.

**The shipped default is `grace = 25`, which sits above every value in the data.** At its own default the measurement cannot flag a single record, no matter what the data said. That is a property of the parameter, not a finding about midwives.

| grace | 25 (default) | 15 | 10 | 5 | 0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| flagged | 0 | 3 | 57 | 204 | 615 |
| % of 10,878 | 0.00% | 0.03% | 0.52% | 1.88% | 5.65% |

A flagged record is a *candidate* false positive the name rules had no way to see — not a confirmed error, and none has been adjudicated.

![What the unused temporal signal would buy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mufflyt/midwifery/docs/temporal-plausibility-and-volume-resolution/docs/figures/temporal_plausibility.png)

---

## D17 is still not answerable, and the entry now says so

The ruling turns on the **separation** half — how many quarantined ties the signal would resolve, **minus** how many pools it would *empty*. An emptied pool moves a record from `tied` to `no candidate`, which reads to a user as absence from the registry, and the sign of the net is not known in advance.

That half needs `artifacts/linkage_candidate_audit.csv` with a usable `first_year`. The committed audit carries **198,922 rows with `first_year` 100% `NA`**. The script detects this and declines to estimate rather than guessing — correct behaviour, left alone.

D17's Evidence section claimed the column *"is now populated so the question can be asked from a committed artifact for the first time."* **That is true of the code and not of the committed artifact.** The entry now records the distinction. **RULING stays `none`.**

---

## One definition of the parser, not two

`amcb_certification_year()` now lives beside `amcb_temporal_separation()` in `R/amcb_resolver.R` — the function that consumes the year it produces. Both callers source it.

I originally wrote the fix inline in both scripts. That is a duplicate top-level definition, which `ci_hygiene.R` H4 forbids, and it is precisely how the all-NA parser comes back in one script while the other stays correct.

`tests/test_certification_year_parser.R` is hermetic — literals only, no crosswalk, no panel, so it runs on a clean checkout. **It caught a real bug in the replacement before it shipped:** `regexpr()` returns `NA` for an `NA` element and `out[NA] <- x` is an error, so a roster with one missing date would have aborted the whole run. The mask now excludes `NA` explicitly.

---

## Documentation

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/TECHNICAL_APPENDIX_TEMPORAL_PLAUSIBILITY.md` | **New.** Method, censoring, the sweep, the defect, what it does *not* license |
| `docs/DECISIONS_CONTRACT.md` | D17 evidence filled in; the `first_year` claim corrected |
| `NEWS.md` | Both this and #157, filed under the one thing they have in common |
| `README.md` | New gallery figure 13; **env-var table corrected** — it still documented the hardcoded `/Volumes/MufflySamsung` defaults that #157 replaced with a glob, plus 7 other stale path references, and a new subsection on why the volume is found by glob |

The README correction is worth calling out separately: #157 changed the resolution mechanism but left the README telling people the old defaults.

---

## Verification

- Full `ci.yml` gate list run locally.
- `tests/test_temporal_separation.R` still passes against the `R/amcb_resolver.R` edit.
- Both scripts re-run after the refactor: **numbers identical** (10,878 / 6,020).
- Figure inspected as rendered, not just generated — the first draft had an annotation running off the right edge and a −54 tail squashing the informative mass into an unreadable spike. Both fixed; the clipped rows are now stated on the panel rather than silently dropped.

## What this does not do

- It does **not** rule on D17.
- It does **not** identify false positives — a flagged pairing is a candidate for review.
- It does **not** support "the linkage is temporally validated": 35.6% of accepted matches were never assessed at all.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_013oAHmh24yGTwK3gKXxHjHx

---

### Caught by the repo's own gates while preparing this

`test_frozen_dependency.R` T5 flagged `make_temporal_plausibility_figure.R` as reading `amcb_npi_linkage_FROZEN.csv` without being declared in `rebuild_frozen_dependents.R`'s `REBUILD_ORDER` — 32 declared against 33 discovered. Undeclared, it is invisible to a re-freeze and would keep publishing a censored share computed from the previous cohort. Now declared beside `analyze_temporal_plausibility.R`, whose inputs and panel-vintage caveat it shares. Third script to ship that way; this time the PR caught it rather than the next Nightly.

author: vlannaai
body:
The 0.7.0 stable cut — step 0c of the three-step sequence. Exits changesets pre mode and collapses the whole 0.7 pre line (42 changesets) into one stable release.

**Do not squash-merge into a reworded commit** — the release job keys off the tag, and the tag must land on the exact tree the pilot validated.

## Provenance

`0.7.0-pre.18` (`e2cce380`) is the commit the pilot validated. This branch is that commit plus the version bump and one release-tooling fix — no product code changes.

- pilot validation: plain `npm install`, no `--legacy-peer-deps`, no lockfile surgery; typecheck 0 errors; 210 files / 1282 tests / 0 failures; SPA build clean; load sampled DURING the run (4.9 → 13.4), so the green is settled-load
- `#1294` arbiter flipped as pre-announced, observed before any change
- format continuity measured two independent ways: a vault written with `hub@0.6.0` + `to-file@0.6.0` reads back correctly under 0.7, and the pilot's **committed encrypted fixture built under pre.16** opens unchanged (three keyrings, 1275 rows each)

Scope that claim precisely: the fixture witnesses pre.16 → pre.18 *within* the 0.7 pre line; the 0.6-write/0.7-read round trip covers the stable hop. Neither subsumes the other, and neither is a witness for a `0.5`-to-stable upgrader.

## Contents

- 57 `@noy-db/*` packages normalized to `0.7.0`; 51 CHANGELOG headings rewritten off the changesets pre-1.0 major-bump heuristic
- `create-noy-db` exits pre onto its own line (`0.3.4-pre.17` → `0.3.4`), correctly skipped by the normalizer
- every prior `## 0.7.0-pre.*` section preserved — verified per package, no released history renamed

## The tooling fix, and why it is in this PR

`release:version` **aborted on this cut**. `assertCanonicalAdvanced` inverted semver where one version runs out of segments, getting both directions wrong:

```
0.7.0-pre.18 -> 0.7.0        refused as "did not advance"   (a real advance)
0.7.0        -> 0.7.0-pre.18 accepted                       (a real regression)
```

The comment on the line stated the correct rule and the code did the opposite. Within a pre line both sides have equal segment counts, so the counter compare decides everything and the branch is unreachable — eighteen releases exercised it zero times, and exiting pre mode is the first run that reaches it.

The existing accept-case used `0.7.0-pre.6 -> 0.8.0`, which resolves at the minor segment and returns before the boundary. More versions of that shape would not have found it, so the new test asserts the **ordering property**: a known-correct ascending list must be accepted at every adjacent pair and refused in reverse. Tests were written first and seen red, so the guard is confirmed capable of failing.

Also adds `--resume`. The abort left no recovery path: `changeset version` had already consumed and **deleted** all 42 changeset files, `.changeset/` is gitignored, so the error's own advice ("restore `.changeset/pre.json` and revert the CHANGELOG edits") was impossible to follow, and a re-run would see an empty queue and correctly refuse as a no-op. The release was not lost — the prose was already in the tracked CHANGELOGs — so resume skips step 1 and reads its baseline from `git HEAD`, which still held the pre-run versions because the edits were uncommitted. Read, never hand-supplied: a mistyped baseline would silently mis-normalize the line.

## After merge

Publishing needs a GitHub Release **without** `--prerelease` so it routes to `@latest`. Then verify:

- `@noy-db/in-relay` `latest` moves off the prerelease (#1293), and `npm i @noy-db/hub @noy-db/in-relay` resolves hub to `0.7.0` rather than dragging it onto the pre rail
- the co-install matrix with a control that CAN fail

Note the sibling-peer caret fix is **forward-only**: pairs where both sides are ≥ `pre.18` co-install; any pair involving a satellite published earlier stays broken permanently, because an exact peer is frozen in a published manifest.

author: sidmofya
body:
Selected Works printed every entry in full — title, description, access line and request button. Adding a fifth work would have made it a wall of text at the foot of the page. It now reads as an editorial index.

3 files, +160 / −27.

## Collapsed by default

```
SELECTED WRITING & FRAMEWORKS

THE WEALTH OF RESOURCE NATIONS                    +
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
SOVEREIGN GEOMETRY                                +
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
CANON BEFORE CAPITAL                              +
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
REAL ECONOMIK                                     +
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
FUTURECRAFT                                       +
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

Clicking a title reveals its description and request link. One entry open at a time; clicking the open title closes it. Nothing is open on load.

## How it's built

Each trigger is a real `<button>` wrapped in its `<h3>` — the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern:

- Keyboard reach, **Enter and Space** activation, and focus all come from the platform. No custom key handlers, and no non-semantic clickable div.
- Wrapping in `<h3>` keeps the titles as headings in the document outline, so `/23-south` still reads `h1 → h2 → h3`.
- Triggers carry `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; panels carry matching ids, `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby`.
- The button spans the full row, so the whole row is the tap target — measured 327×85 at 375px, not a small indicator.

Panels animate `grid-template-rows` `0fr → 1fr`, which transitions to auto height without measuring, and are `visibility: hidden` when closed. That keeps collapsed content out of the tab order and the accessibility tree **while leaving it in the page source**, so the descriptions stay crawlable. The global `prefers-reduced-motion` block already collapses the duration, so reduced-motion users get an instant toggle with no extra code.

The indicator is a two-stroke SVG `+` whose vertical stroke scales to zero when open. `aria-hidden`, since `aria-expanded` already announces state.

Still **one shared request modal and one Netlify form** — the modal receives the selected work, unchanged from before.

## Content

Adds **Real Economik** between Canon Before Capital and FutureCraft:

> A framework for understanding the informal economy through the roles that different participants play regardless of institutional recognition.

Drops the per-entry "Available on request" line, since the expanded state is specified as description then request link.

## Navigation

Adds a small in-page nav in the hero — `PREMISE · SOVEREIGN TEA · SELECTED WORKS` — anchoring to the three sections, which gain ids and `scroll-mt-20` to clear the sticky header. Horizontal, wraps on narrow screens, not sticky, no dropdown. Global site navigation is untouched and the five works are not added to it.

## Verification

Lint, typecheck and production build clean. 49/49 tests pass, including a new one asserting the required order, that all five triggers ship `aria-expanded="false"`, that trigger/panel ids pair up, and that the nav anchors resolve.

Driven in a real browser (Chromium via Playwright, installed transiently — `package.json` is unchanged and no dependency was added):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Collapsed on load, request links hidden | pass |
| Click opens; description and link visible | pass |
| One at a time; clicking the open title closes it | pass |
| Enter opens, Space closes | pass |
| Tab from a collapsed trigger skips to the next trigger | pass |
| Tab from an open trigger reaches its request link | pass |
| Modal `work` field receives `Real Economik` | pass |
| Anchor clears the sticky header | pass (80px) |
| 375px: no horizontal overflow | pass |

body:
From the three-repo audit. **26 files, +139 / −16,890**, in four commits: the deletions, a correction pass over the docs after checking them against the live Railway project, a merge of `main`, and a follow-up for what that merge changed.

## Design mockups (13 files, ~16.6k lines)

Twelve standalone HTML files at the repo root — `dashboard-design-themes.html` alone was 11,009 lines — plus `canvas.json`, which indexed three of them. Theme explorations for a dashboard: served by nothing, referenced by no code, superseded by `ivr-router/public/console.html`, which `ivr-router` actually serves at `/console`.

`dashboard/index.html` is **kept**. It is not a mockup — the deployment docs describe it as the working dashboard.

## Stub services (9 files)

`backend-api`, `chatbot-api`, `whatsapp-bot`. Each was a ~40-line Express stub answering `/health` and one route whose body was a `TODO`; `whatsapp-bot` replied "This bot isn't wired up to real data yet." to every message it received. None had gained a line of business logic since being scaffolded, and the work each stood in for was meanwhile built properly elsewhere:

| Stub | What actually does the job |
| --- | --- |
| `whatsapp-bot` | `ivr-router/lib/journeys/` + `dsa-business-crm`'s `lib/whatsapp/` — Ananta, templates, bot engine, tested |
| `chatbot-api` | `/apply` in `dsa-business-crm` (`lib/chat/`), with guardrails |
| `backend-api` | `dsa-business-crm` itself |

## ✅ The Railway services have since been deleted

This section previously asked the reader to go delete three orphaned Railway services by hand. That has now happened — on 1 Sep 2026, after this PR was opened:

| Railway service | Domain | Was rooted at | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api` | `api-production-c082.up.railway.app` | `backend-api` | **deleted** |
| `chatbot` | `chatbot-production-6845.up.railway.app` | `chatbot-api` | **deleted** |
| `whatsapp` | `whatsapp-production-44e7.up.railway.app` | `whatsapp-bot` | **deleted** |
| `ivr` | `ivr-production-38c0.up.railway.app` | `ivr-router` | staged for removal, not yet applied |

Nothing in this repo or in `dsa-business-crm` called any of those domains, and nothing broke. The Automation Hub project is down to seven services.

`ivr` was the fourth candidate found while verifying the docs: rooted at `ivr-router` with **zero environment variables** — no `SUPABASE_URL`, no `OBD_*`, no `CONSOLE_SECRET` — so it could not have been doing the job `ivr-voice-bot-system` does. Its removal is staged but still needs a two-factor confirmation that cannot be given over an API token, so it must be applied from the Railway dashboard.

## The Railway wiring in the docs was wrong, and is now corrected

The first commit's doc rewrite described the deploy topology from the repo alone. Read against the actual Automation Hub project, two of its instructions did not work.

**Root Directory.** The Services table listed every service as rooted at its subfolder. Three of the five were not:

| Railway service | Root Directory | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ivr-voice-bot-system` | *(repo root)* | Holds the live IVR config — every `ANANTA_*`, `OBD_*`, `ORISERVE_*`, `SUPABASE_*`, plus `CONSOLE_SECRET`. This is the service running `ivr-router`. |
| `ivr` | `ivr-router` | Zero variables set; staged for deletion (see above). |
| `jobs` | `data-jobs` | Railpack |
| `morning-check` / `afternoon-check` | *(repo root)* | `npm --prefix data-jobs run cron:morning` / `cron:afternoon`, at `0 5` / `30 8` UTC |

This matters most for `ivr-voice-bot-system`: rooting it at the repo root is what makes Railway read `railway.toml` and build the root `Dockerfile`, the only build that copies `ivr-router/public/`, which `GET /console` serves via `res.sendFile('public/console.html')`. Following the old step 3 and repointing it at `ivr-router` would have 404'd the very route the other two docs in this PR tell operators to open. The table now records what each service is actually set to, and the wiring steps no longer assume a subfolder is correct.

**API Base URL.** Phase 3 ended at "the console interface loads" while a paragraph further down still claimed the URL auto-detects. It does not: `getAPIBaseURL()` in `public/console.html` shows a blocking `prompt()` and falls back to `http://localhost:3000`, so an operator who dismisses it sends every console action to their own laptop and sees the API reported offline. Both docs now carry the step, and the stale claim is corrected rather than left standing.

**Wrong service for the secret.** Both docs said to set `CONSOLE_SECRET` on the `ivr` service — the one with no variables. Corrected to `ivr-voice-bot-system` in both.

**`ivr-router/Dockerfile` now copies `public/`.** It names each path it copies (`index.js`, `lib`), so it could only ever build an image whose `/console` route fails with ENOENT. Nothing uses that Dockerfile today, but it made the trap above permanent. `ivr-router/` has no `.dockerignore` that could exclude the directory.

## Rebased onto the Chatsense removal

`main` moved while this was open — PR #28 (Ananta link shortening) and PR #29 (Chatsense removal). `main` is merged in here.

#29 deleted the Chatsense client, routes, quick-start guide and its wiring in `index.js`. Git reported no conflict, because #29 never touched `README.md` — but this branch's README still described `ivr-router` as running "the WhatsApp/ChatSense journeys" in two places and credited Chatsense in the note about what replaced the `whatsapp-bot` stub. Those three references are gone, so this no longer merges a description of an integration that no longer exists.

Only `README.md` was touched for this. The remaining Chatsense references across the other documents are cleaned up in PR #30, which touches a disjoint set of files.

## Docs corrected rather than left stale

`QUICK_DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md` and `DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` both told the reader to upload `automation-console.html` to a web host, or to `express.static()` it out of `index.js`. Both pointed at a file that no longer exists and had already been superseded, so they now point at the real thing: `GET /console?token=`, served by `ivr-router`, nothing to copy. Each keeps a one-line note saying what changed and why.

## Verified

Re-run against the merged tree, after `main` came in:

- `ivr-router/index.js` and both `data-jobs` entrypoints parse (`node --check`)
- `/console` still resolves `public/console.html`, and the file is still there post-merge
- no `.js`, `.json`, `.toml`, `.sh` or `Dockerfile` references any deleted path
- the three `.dc.html` files' only non-doc reference was `canvas.json`, deleted with them
- the `COPY public ./public` target exists and nothing excludes it from that build context
- markdown fences balanced and tables well-formed in all three edited docs
- no surviving "auto-detects", wrong-service, or Chatsense claims in any doc this PR touches
- `gh-pages` is a separate branch with its own `index.html`; nothing here touches it

This repo has no CI, so none of the above is checked automatically on push.

Anything worth recovering is in git history.

author: gerrrt
body:
Closes #223. The firewall change is already applied to `morpheus`; this is the repository catching up with it.

## The obvious fix does not work

#223 said to enable logging on the inter-VLAN pass rules. That was wrong, and checking the rule set before touching it is what caught it: **every inter-VLAN pass rule is sourced from an internal segment** (`vlan50 → vlan99`, `vlan50 → vlan30`). No packet any of them passes can have a terminal VLAN as its source, and the alert needs `src ∈ {10,20,40}` *and* `dst ∈ {30,50,99}`. Logging them would have populated the dashboard's pass panels and left the alert exactly as dead.

Logging the terminal VLANs' own `→ any` egress rules does work, and costs:

| Interface | Inbound pkts/day | vs current filterlog |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `igc0.20` Skids/IoT | 11,293,285 | 127× |
| `igc0.40` CasaBonita/TV | 968,266 | 11× |
| `igc0.10` Degens/guest | 312,031 | 4× |
| **combined** | **12,573,581** | **≈142×** |

On a 30-day retention on one disk, that is a disk-filling change.

## What was done instead

Three **tripwire** rules on `morpheus`, one per terminal interface — `pass` + `log` for `<terminal net> → Internal_Segments`, placed **below** the eight block rules that already stop that path and **above** the `→ any` egress rule:

```
pass in log quick on igc0.40 inet from <OPT3__NETWORK> to <Internal_Segments>
pass in log quick on igc0.20 inet from <OPT5__NETWORK> to <Internal_Segments>
pass in log quick on igc0.10 inet from <OPT6__NETWORK> to <Internal_Segments>
```

While segmentation holds the blocks match first, so the tripwire logs nothing and adds no volume. It matches only if those blocks are removed or reordered — the exact failure the alert exists for — and in that case `→ any` would have passed the packet anyway, so nothing is weakened by its presence.

Applied through `pfSsh.php` (`write_config()` + `filter_configure()`), not by hand-editing `config.xml`. Encrypted backups taken before and after: `config-20260901T042022Z` (62 rules) and `config-20260901T044457Z` (65). Gateway, DNS, outbound HTTPS and log ingestion all verified afterwards; exactly 3 pass rules log, and no others.

## Proving it, rather than assuming it

A tripwire that never fires is indistinguishable from a broken one — which is this entire family of defect. The monitoring host is on VLAN 99 and cannot originate terminal-segment traffic, so the *logging path* was proven instead: logging was briefly enabled on the lowest-volume terminal egress rule (Degens, ~3.6 lines/s) and then reverted.

- **49 of 49** resulting `pass` lines carried the source address in exactly the position the alert's regex reads.
- The destination half of that same regex already matched **2058** block lines.

Both halves are therefore verified against real traffic. Only the combination is absent, which is what "the segmentation is holding" looks like.

## What changes here

- **Dashboard** — no longer claims the alert cannot fire. *Terminal→internal passes* now reads `0` (that path is instrumented, so zero is a measurement); *Passed (1h)* still reads *not logged*, because ordinary egress genuinely is not.
- **`docs/observability.md`, `docs/security.md`** — record why the obvious fix fails, what was done, and how it was verified.
- **`docs/roadmap.md`** — #223 moves to Done.
- **`docs/runbooks/restore-the-firewall.md`** — a new verification step. **A config restored from a backup older than today drops the tripwires silently**, they log nothing either way, and the alert goes quietly back to being unfirable. That trap is worth more than the rules themselves.

`make validate` passes: 7 dashboards, 140 panels, 132 PromQL and 28 LogQL expressions, `docs OK`.

author: chenruan
body:
## Summary / 摘要

This PR replaces owned bound snapshots with fixed borrowed raw-pointer descriptors. Payload bytes are never copied, allocated, freed, or included in cache identity. It preserves the PR #177 helper identity model and supports up to eight bound pointers.

本 PR 将 owned snapshot 替换为固定大小的 borrowed raw-pointer descriptor。payload 不复制、不分配、不释放，也不进入 cache identity；保留 PR #177 的 helper 独立身份模型，并支持最多 8 个 bound pointer。

## Runtime fix and helper contract / 运行时修复与 helper 契约

- Root cause of the board IABT: `llvm::is_contained` searched a contiguous `uint32_t` range and libc++ lowered it to `wmemchr`. The SRE image had no usable executable target for that symbol, producing `R_AARCH64_CALL26 wmemchr` and an instruction abort.
- The bound-argument lookup is now an explicit bounded loop over at most eight entries. It introduces no `memchr`/`wmemchr` dependency.
- A direct helper receives propagated bound facts only when it has its own `ejit_entry`, matching `EJIT_DIM(period)`, and matching `EJIT_BOUND_PTR(period)` metadata. Each call edge must carry the same period identity. Unannotated, indirect, address-taken, ambiguous, mismatched, or inconsistent helpers remain conservative boundaries.
- The self-contained board demo has no project or libc header dependency. It uses worker core 6 and producer core 16, exercises two large shared structures, cell+TRP pointers, two cell versions, invalid descriptors, cache hits, and dump views.

- 板端 IABT 根因：`llvm::is_contained` 搜索连续 `uint32_t` 数组时被 libc++ 降为 `wmemchr`。SRE 镜像没有可用的可执行目标，最终出现 `R_AARCH64_CALL26 wmemchr` 并触发指令异常。
- bound argIndex 校验现改为最多 8 项的显式有界循环，不再引入 `memchr`/`wmemchr` 依赖。
- direct helper 只有自身同时具备 `ejit_entry`、匹配的 `EJIT_DIM(period)` 和匹配的 `EJIT_BOUND_PTR(period)`，且每条调用边传递同一 period identity 时，才接收 bound facts。未标注、间接调用、地址被获取、歧义、维度不匹配或多调用点不一致的 helper 均保守停止传播。
- 板端 demo 为真正独立单 `.c`，不依赖项目或 libc 头文件；使用 worker core 6 / producer core 16，覆盖两个大共享结构体、cell+TRP 双指针、两个 cell 版本、非法 descriptor、cache hit 和 dump。

## Lifetime and ABI / 生命周期与 ABI

Producer and worker must share the same virtual address. Every borrowed object must remain mapped, readable, and unchanged from enqueue through compilation. Updates must follow `deactivate -> modify -> reactivate`. Compile-only descriptors are cleared before publication state is retained.

producer 与 worker 必须共享同一虚拟地址。每个 borrowed 对象从 enqueue 到编译结束期间都必须持续映射、可读且内容不变；更新遵循 `deactivate -> modify -> reactivate`。发布状态不会继续持有或读取编译期 payload。

## Validation / 验证

Passed:

- `git diff --check`; clean worktree; LF/no BOM; no temporary diagnostics or `fixup!` commits in the PR update.
- `EJitCompileDriver.cpp` and `EJitStructFieldPass.cpp` rebuilt with `-j2`.
- Host `llvm-nm` and `llvm-objdump` show no `memchr`/`wmemchr` undefined symbol or relocation in `EJitCompileDriver.cpp.obj`.
- Focused StructFieldPass execution covers an unmarked-helper negative case and a cell+TRP two-pointer positive case.
- AArch64 big-endian CodeGen A/B using the same libc++ find implementation: the old search emits `U wmemchr` plus `R_AARCH64_CALL26 wmemchr`; the explicit-loop version emits neither.
- The standalone demo preprocesses without `EJitRuntime.h` or residual `EJIT_ENTRY` tokens and passes C syntax checking.

Boundary: this machine has not produced the final product `ejit.o`/ELF. The package build must inspect that exact final artifact for unexpected libc relocations before board execution. The configured freestanding host `EJITTests` executable cannot link without SRE platform symbols; affected test translation units compile and the focused standalone harness passes.

边界：本机尚未生成最终产品 `ejit.o`/ELF。上板前必须检查实际打包产物，确认没有意外 libc relocation。当前 freestanding host 配置缺少 SRE 平台外部符号，无法链接完整 `EJITTests` 可执行文件；受影响测试 TU 已编译，独立聚焦 harness 已通过。

## Rebuild requirements / 重编要求

This follow-up does not change Clang attributes or code generation, so Clang does not need to be rebuilt. Rebuild and relink the EJIT library, lipo object, and business package from the same commit and macro set.

本轮修复未修改 Clang attribute 或代码生成，因此无需重编 Clang；需要使用同一提交和同一宏配置重新编译并链接 EJIT 库、lipo 对象和业务包。

## Board demo PGO sequencing follow-up / 板端用例 PGO 时序修复

The former demo called each specialization once and then waited for both Tier-1 and Tier-2 compile counts. That cannot complete online PGO because Tier-2 requires 64 real Tier-1 dispatches. The demo now serializes helper then root for each cell: initial AOT enqueue, wait for Tier-1 Ready, 64 verified Tier-1 calls, bounded continued calls while Tier-2 is deferred/compiled/published, then two calls after Ready. Every wait is bounded and reports PGO phase, active dimensions, pending entries, queue depth, and compile/publish failures.

旧 demo 每个 specialization 只调用一次，却等待 Tier-1 和 Tier-2 编译计数；由于 Tier-2 需要 64 次真实 Tier-1 dispatch，这个流程必然卡住。新 demo 对每个 cell 串行完成 helper 再完成 root：首次 AOT 入队、等待 Tier-1 Ready、64 次校验过的 Tier-1 调用、在 Tier-2 deferred/compile/publish 期间持续有界调用，最后在 Ready 后再调用两次。所有等待都有次数上限，并打印 PGO 阶段、维度 active 状态、pending、queue、compileFailed 和 publishFailed。

## SC-012 — Treasury Management Module

### Summary

Implements the V2 Treasury Management Module as the single source of truth for all protocol-owned assets. The treasury manages seven independent reserve pools with deterministic accounting, role-based access control, governance controls, and emergency pause mechanisms.

### What Changed

**Core Contracts:**
- `contracts/treasury/ITreasuryManagement.sol` — V2 Treasury Management interface
- `contracts/treasury/TreasuryManagement.sol` — V2 Treasury Management implementation (918 lines)
- `contracts/mocks/MockTreasuryManagement.sol` — Lightweight mock for downstream module testing

**Tests:**
- `test/TreasuryManagement.test.ts` — 74 comprehensive test cases, all passing

### Architecture

Seven independent reserve pools, each fully auditable on-chain:
- **STAKING_RESERVE** — Tokens actively staked by users
- **REWARDS_POOL** — Reserved for reward distribution
- **SLASHING_RESERVE** — Funds slashed from verifiers
- **PROTOCOL_FEES** — Accumulated protocol fees
- **GOVERNANCE_RESERVE** — Governance-controlled reserve
- **ECOSYSTEM_FUND** — Future ecosystem incentives
- **EMERGENCY_RESERVE** — Emergency recovery fund

**Invariant:** \`sum(poolBalances) == protocolToken.balanceOf(treasury)\`

### Security

- **ReentrancyGuard** on all state-mutating external calls
- **Role-based access control** per pool and operation type
- **Same-block protection** prevents multiple operations per pool per block
- **Per-block and percentage withdrawal limits** prevent single-tx pool drain
- **Duplicate record prevention** via unique record IDs
- **Emergency pause** — global, deposit-only, and withdrawal-only
- **Invariant validation** after every balance-changing operation

### Bug Fixes

1. \`recordSlashDeposit\` — Added \`totalWithdrawn\` update (was missing, breaking accounting)
2. \`depositToPool\` — Fixed wrong \`fromPool\` in record creation
3. Per-block withdrawal tracking — Completed stub implementation
4. \`_findEmergencySource\` — Improved fallback logic
5. Withdrawal records — Fixed hardcoded \`toPool\` values

### Pre-existing Compilation Fixes

Fixed compilation errors in other files to enable full project compilation:
- \`GovernanceOwnable.sol\` — Added \`virtual\` to \`emergencyUnpause()\`
- \`ClaimRegistry.sol\` — Fixed \`bytes32\`/\`uint256\` error type mismatch
- \`TimelockOwnedProxyAdmin.sol\` — Fixed OZ v5 ProxyAdmin constructor/overrides
- \`FeeManager.sol\` / \`TokenomicsEngine.sol\` — Fixed invalid \`@deprecated\` NatSpec tags

### Test Coverage

| Deployment | 4 |
| Deposits | 12 |

| Governance Controls | 8 |
| Emergency Controls | 10 |

| **Total** | **74** |

author: pudan416
body:
## The problem

Neither purchase path checked Family Controls authorization before taking colors:

- `pay(cost:)` has no check at all.
- `handlePayGatePaymentForGroup` called `pay(cost:)` as its first real action.
- `UnlockGroupWidgetIntent.perform()` never consults `AuthorizationCenter`.

Writes to `ManagedSettingsStore` are inert while Screen Time access is revoked. So a user whose permission had lapsed — or who declined it during onboarding and later tapped unlock — was charged for an unlock that could not happen, and nothing anywhere said so. On the widget path it is completely silent, because an interactive widget button cannot present an error.

## The change

- **`UsageBudgetMonitoringError.notAuthorized`**, surfaced through the existing `payGateError` alert so it uses the same failure channel as the monitoring errors.
  - Its copy deliberately does *not* mention a refund. This failure is raised **before** any charge, and the sibling cases say "your colors were refunded" — repeating that here would tell the user colors moved when none did. There is a test pinning that.
- **`handlePayGatePaymentForGroup` checks access before anything else**, including the group lookup: without access the purchase cannot succeed regardless of what else is true. It calls `refreshAuthorizationStatus()` first, because the cached `isAuthorized` flag only updates on foreground and `AuthorizationCenter` does not reliably announce revocation — the service's own comment says as much.
- **The widget intent refuses at the top of `perform()`**, before the debounce and before any balance arithmetic.

## Deliberately not included

Refunding when `startMonitoring` fails *after* a widget charge. That path leaves its `pendingBudgetMonitoring_*` keys set on purpose so a later `rebuild()` can retry, so refunding there would hand out free access every time the retry then succeeds. Choosing between retry-later and refund-now is a product decision, not a mechanical fix — worth its own change.

This PR closes the "charged for an impossible unlock" hole on both paths, which is the case that needed no such decision.

## Testing

`Executed 585 tests, with 1 test skipped and 0 failures` — the skip is the pre-existing `AppGroupRMWConcurrencyTests` one.

The two new `PaymentTests` are a discriminating pair rather than a single happy-path assertion. Both call a group id that does not exist:

- without access → balance untouched **and** `payGateError` set;
- with access → balance untouched and `payGateError` **nil**, because a missing group is a different failure that must not borrow the Screen Time message.

If the access check ever slips behind the group lookup, the first test stops setting `payGateError` and fails.

## Still needs a device

FamilyControls does not run in the Simulator, so the mock stands in for `AuthorizationCenter`. What this cannot prove: that a revoked-access `ManagedSettingsStore` write really is a silent no-op rather than throwing. That assumption is why the guard exists; it is worth confirming on hardware by revoking Screen Time and attempting an unlock from both the app and the widget.

## Related

Independent of #22 (access-window expiry) — different hunks in `AppModel+PayGate.swift` and `UnlockGroupWidgetIntent.swift`, both branched from `main`. They can merge in either order.

Passivseite, keine Verschachtelung — in der englischen Rechnungslegung liest
sich „provisions" oft als Teil von „liabilities". Die `level`-Spalte trägt
die Gliederung, der Name behauptet nichts.

## Die Kollisionen, vor denen die Prüfer gewarnt haben

- **`schulden` führt drei Vokabulare**: die Bilanz-Rolle, den Schlüssel des
  Beleg-Apparats (`Beleg q="schulden"`) und die QA-Facette. Umbenannt ist nur
  die Rolle. `scripts/pruefe_alte_werte.py` hält die drei jetzt mit Begründung
  auseinander.
- **`bilanz_geldschulden`** in `integrierte_schulden.py` ist ein
  Parametername, keine Rolle — nicht angefasst.
- **`geldschulden` ist zusätzlich ein API-Blockname** von
  `/haushalt/schulden`. Der bleibt; Blocknamen sind ein eigener Schnitt.

## Die deutschen Beschriftungen

Sie hängen jetzt an den englischen Schlüsseln — `KURZ` in
`haushalt-bilanz.ts` (die Legende beider Leisten) und die `namen`-Abbildung
des Bilanz-Blocks in `qa.py`, die in den LLM-Kontext geht. Ein vergessener
Nachzug hätte dort „tangible_assets" statt „Sachvermögen" in den Prompt
geschrieben.

## Gemessen

- 2.331 pytest · ruff · `tsc` · `next build` · Kachelflächen- und Skalen-Probe
- 19 Swift-Tests
- Migration gegen eine Kopie des echten dev-Bestands: **157 Zeilen** über neun
  Stichtage, alle neunzehn Rollen umgezogen
- Playwright gegen diese Kopie: die Bilanz-Leisten auf `/haushalt/schulden`
  zeigen weiter „Beteiligungen und Forderungen 645,3 · Gebäude, Straßen,

- Detects relevant news/events around significant airfare movements on a route, to help answer "why did fares move?"
- Matches candidate articles using six signals: date/time proximity, airport mention, route mention, airline mention, event type, and geographic relevance
