author: singret
body:
Partial REG-157 — the incident-create-path slice, per REG-9's own suggested slice-order. Remaining scope (Slack event handler, post-mortem service, the broader IncidentService CRUD surface) documented precisely in REG-157, not silently dropped.

## What

Fixes the actual gap REG-9 found: the gorm/redis tracing plugins were registered correctly, but a live smoke test sending a real Alertmanager webhook produced **zero DB spans** — only the rate limiter's Redis span — because no repository method ever threaded a context carrying a real span into `db.WithContext()`.

## Scope

**Repository layer** — 8 methods across 3 files: `IncidentRepository.{Create,GetByID,Update,LinkAlert}`, `AlertRepository.{Create,GetByExternalID,Update}`, `TimelineRepository.Create`. The rest of each interface intentionally doesn't take `ctx` — same mixed pattern `user_repository.go`'s `Upsert` already established.

**Service layer, real ctx threaded (not a placeholder)**: `AlertService.{ProcessAlertmanagerPayload,ProcessNormalizedAlerts,createOrUpdateAlert}`, `IncidentService.{CreateIncidentFromAlert,CreateIncidentFromAlertWithGrouping,LinkAlertToExistingIncident}`, `AcknowledgeAlertWithTimeline`, `coordinator.SeedDemoData`, and two functions that already had `ctx` available via their callers but were discarding it (`PostMortemAgent.writeTimelineEntry`, `TeamsEventHandler.syncMessageToTimeline` — both had it as `_`).

**Handlers**, all 4 alert-intake entry points: `prometheus_webhook.go`, `webhook_handler.go` (the shared Grafana/CloudWatch/generic path — same fix covers all three sources with one signature change), `alerts.go`, `neuri.go`, `setup.go`.

**REG-10's `WithoutCancel` criterion**, done for these two functions: both incident-creation paths now capture `bgCtx := context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before spawning their Telegram/push goroutines and pass it to `recoverAsyncPanic` — real trace-linked spans on panic recovery, not `context.Background()`.

## Where the line was drawn, and why

Once the 4 shared repository methods took `ctx`, every caller anywhere in the codebase had to compile against the new signature. Tracing the fan-in: `GetIncident`/`CreateIncident`/`UpdateIncident`/`CreateTimelineEntry` are called from both real Gin handlers *and* `slack_event_handler.go` (14 call sites, no ctx plumbed through that file at all) and `post_mortem_service.go`. `AcknowledgeIncident`/`ResolveIncident`/`UpdateIncidentStatus` turned out to have **zero** Gin-handler callers — they're used exclusively by the Slack/Teams bot event handlers.

Threading real ctx through those 7 methods would have forced fixing Slack's entire event-handling surface in this same PR — a structurally different problem (bot callback loop, not request/response) that deserves its own scoped design pass. Left them on their existing signatures, passing `context.Background()` internally to the newly-ctx-aware repo calls: zero caller changes, compiles clean, and it's an explicit, documented placeholder rather than a silent gap — exactly the same discipline as `recoverAsyncPanic`'s 16 call sites in REG-10.

## An incidental fix

`LinkAlertToExistingIncident`'s Slack-notification goroutine had **no panic recovery at all** before this change — any panic inside `BuildAlertLinkedMessage` or `PostMessage` would have crashed the whole server. Added `recoverAsyncPanic` since I was already touching this exact function.

## Testing

- `internal/repository/ctx_propagation_test.go`: real span-correlation proofs (not mocked) for all three repositories' `Create`, using the actual gorm tracing plugin against an in-memory sqlite DB with an explicitly injected `TracerProvider` (never touching global otel state — the REG-7 finding)
- `go test ./... -shuffle=on -count=3` clean on every touched package
- `golangci-lint run ./...` clean (0 issues)
- **Live-verified against a real Jaeger collector**: sent the exact same real Alertmanager webhook payload that previously produced 1 span (just the Redis `eval`). After this change: **5 spans under one trace ID** — `incidents` Create, two `alerts` spans (the dedup `GetByExternalID` check + `Create`), the Redis `eval`, and the root HTTP span. Confirmed `db.query.text` is empty (redacted by default, per REG-9's own criterion) even with real traffic flowing through instrumented repositories.

author: magick93
body:
## Found by the hr-specs e2e gate (second reconciliation regression, after #131)

Generated app build failed with 6 E0432s; representative:

    --> src/recruiting/provisional_verifiable_credential_lerrs/mod.rs:14
    pub use query_service::ProvisionalVerifiableCredentialLerrsQueryService;
    no `...LerrsQueryService` in `...::query_service`
    help: a similar name exists: `...LERRSQueryService`

## Root cause

`DomainTypesScaffoldGenerator` renders `entity_mod.tera` with `entity_name` from `to_pascal_case(stripped_title)`, while all emitters use the graph's canonical `schema.rust_type_name`. For the schema `ProvisionalVerifiableCredentialLER-RSType` the naive path yields `...Lerrs`, the canonical path `...LERRS`. Baseline (1e87948) generated both sides as `LERRS`; the reconciled line's title/stem normalization exposed the mismatch.

## Fix

Prefer `db.get_schema_in_domain(..).rust_type_name`, fall back to the sanitized title (unit fixtures). Matches the intent documented in #124 ("sanitize to a PascalCase Rust identifier matching rust_type_name").

## Validation

- `cargo test -p codegraph --lib`: 240 passed
- hr-specs full e2e re-run on the patched line: appended after merge

author: elandcelinelu
body:
## 問題

Bulma 給的是淺色主題的底，所以後台的輸入框一直是白的，而**同一個表單裡的 `textarea` 是深的**（`forms.css` 早就有定義）。浮水印的「簽名文字」、社群連結的網址欄、`/admin` 的登入表單都是這樣深淺不一。

這是既有狀況，不是最近改出來的——是上一輪用 Chrome 實際看畫面時才發現的。

## 做法

在 `forms.css` 補一組 `.input` / `.select` 的深色定義，配色**直接對齊既有的 `.textarea`**，不另創一套。

### 不會蓋掉既有的刻意設定

| 既有定義 | 特異性 | 結果 |
|---|---|---|
| `AdminLogin` 的 `.login-form .input` | (0,2,0) | 維持原樣 |
| `StoryEditor` 的 scoped `.input` | (0,2,0) | 維持原樣 |
| 本次 `.input` | (0,1,0) | 只補到本來沒人管的地方 |

### 順帶處理 `.select option`

展開後的選項清單是**作業系統畫的**，不繼承外層樣式。不指定的話，深色文字配系統的深色底會變成看不見。

## 驗證

用 Chrome 在 production 頁面上**實際注入這組 CSS** 確認能覆蓋 Bulma——先用明顯的紅色做二分診斷，確定樣式真的生效、且**不需要 `!important`**，再寫進 `forms.css`。

前端 17 個測試通過、build 通過。

合併部署後畫面會有實際變化，屆時再用瀏覽器確認一次。

author: clanclanclanclan
body:
The largest over-rejection class falls: **T3 feature detection no longer reads commented-out bytes as live.**

## Measured on the 199-root frame (pinned oracle, three full sweeps)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| correct verdicts | 141/199 = 70.9% | **155/199 = 77.9%** |
| FALSE-READY | 0/199 | **0/199** |
| over-rejection | 58 | **44** |
| fixture baseline | 15 live | **13 live** (two REAL false-READYs fixed: the comma-split / before-arg comment evasions now reunite under blanking and T3 fires) |

## Design

- `find_comment_ranges` = a **first-byte projection** of the shared vcu walk (every range starts at `%` or `\`) — cannot diverge from the scanner; comments ONLY (full-set blanking is revert #1's measured 11-false-READY mechanism, pinned by `fr_cmt_g1`).
- Length-preserving `blank_line_comments`, applied in the **trusted extraction glue** (`Compile_evidence.extract*`) — the Coq extract, its 426-case byte-parity suite, and the capstone bridge are untouched; the model certifies the comment-blanked view, which is the view TeX itself reads.
- **Fail-closed breaker gate**, probed over the **closure**: custom verbatim-env definitions, short-verb machinery (`\Verb`/`\SaveVerb`/`\verbdef`/…), `%`-catcode surgery (`\MakePercentIgnore`, `\catcode`-`%`, `\@makeother\%`), xparse `v`-specs, letter-delimited `\verb`. Any hit ⇒ raw view (today's over-rejection, never a manufactured false-READY). Frame prevalence 58/2,719 = 2.1%; forfeits on the graded sample: **0**.
- Scanner: `\begin {name}` (spaces/tabs + at most one newline) now **opens** an env (measured TeX behaviour — the OPEN-038/M2 scanner half); `\end{name}` stays **exact** (`\@xverbatim` wants the literal bytes; the symmetric tolerance was itself a manufacture vector, C-33). `tcblisting` joins `verbatim_envs`.

## Pre-ship adversarial pass (C-30)

A two-agent workflow ran before shipping: gate-cost measurement over the 34 counterfactual rescues + an adversarial review. The review found **8 measured exit-level manufacture vectors** in the first draft (spaced-`\end` close, five breaker misses, root-only guard scope, single-newline `\begin`) — **all fixed in this PR**, each with a unit vector. A ninth defect surfaced in sweep 2 of 3 (asme2e.cls: a comment on the line after `` \catcode`\:12 `` poisoned the lookahead and cost a real rescue) — fixed by bounding both windows at end-of-line; sweep 3 recovered the document.

## Honest decomposition

The counterfactual's 34 rescues blanked **file bytes**; this PR ships the **T3/model channel = 14** of them. The other ~19 route through T2/T0/T5 comment-blindness and stay OPEN (each needs its own guarded pass — e.g. commented `\input` of a missing file is a T2 matter).

## Bookkeeping

`fr_cmt_target_*` → READY **accept-pins**; `check_known_false_ready` gains accept-pin/over-rejection-regression classes (a rescue regression can never again be booked as an "unrecorded fix"); selftest position anchor moved 141 → 155; OPEN-038 scanner half closed; OPEN-039 filed; C-33 logged.

Gates on the final bytes: full runtest green (incl. **fast==full parity on 538 docs**), `known_false_ready` 42 PASS, oracle `hard=0 soft=0`, producer-coverage, project_state (39 items / 33 corrections), selftests pure+binary, code_quality.

body:
## Summary
- Third real-logic slice on the `worker/` scaffold (#324, #327, #328)
- `worker/src/auth.ts`: `firebase-admin` doesn't run on Workers (it's Node-only), so this verifies Firebase ID tokens directly via `jose` against Google's public JWKS for the securetoken service — signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and the signing algorithm pinned explicitly to `RS256` against alg-confusion
- Returns the caller's Firebase UID (the `sub` claim), which every downstream piece (quota, the eventual admin check, `/ai/complete`) keys off of
- `getKey` is dependency-injected rather than hardcoded to the real JWKS endpoint, so tests exercise real RSA signing/verification (a generated in-memory key pair via `jose`'s own `SignJWT`/`generateKeyPair`) instead of needing live network access or mocking the verification logic itself
- Adds `jose` as a real (non-dev) dependency — it's used at runtime, not just for tests/build
- No wiring into the actual `fetch` handler yet — still need the admin UID check and the `/admin/providers`/`/ai/complete` endpoints

## Summary

Phase 2 moves RecallGuard beyond exact-task keyed lookup by adding structured repository experience, task-aware native Sibyl retrieval, deterministic repository isolation, and a compact Preflight Memory Brief.

Phase 2 flow:

task -> normalize task terms -> native Sibyl search -> validate structured experience -> hard repository filter -> deterministic relevance/ranking -> bounded Preflight Memory Brief

## Changes

- Adds recallguard.experience.v2
- Supports seven controlled memory types
- Adds deterministic content-addressed v2 identities
- Uses native Sibyl search_entities with bounded per-term retrieval
- Adds exact repository isolation
- Adds deterministic matched-term relevance filtering
- Adds deterministic ordering with TOP_K = 3
- Distinguishes memory_disabled, search_ok_no_relevant_memory, search_ok_relevant_memory, and search_failed
- Adds machine-readable and human-readable Preflight Memory Briefs
- Adds remember and preflight CLI paths
- Adds deterministic Phase 2 tests

## Scope

Created only:

- phase2_preflight.py

author: rzii
body:
## Problem

When a task session dies mid-external-operation (e.g. a provider failure during the `messages.request` contact — qwen via OpenRouter's single Alibaba provider produced mass 429s plus occasional non-retryable 400s), the retry finds an unresolved heartbeat start marker whose external effects cannot be proven, and the fail-closed design threw `FileDrivenPairIndeterminateExternalOperationErrorV1` out of the session. In `files-single` that error is fatal to the **whole batch**: one poisoned task killed the entire 600-task cell, and every in-flight sibling died as `FILE_SESSION_FAILED` with `requesterExecutionStatus: "cancelled"`.

Measured impact: qwen/qwen3.8-flash died on every cell at 600-task scale (5/5 attempts, concurrency 16 and 4 alike, longest survivor 82 min); z-ai/glm-5.3-flash lost 4–5 of 12 cells; deepseek pinned to a stable provider had zero failures. The unexplained historical 8×300 all-cell FAIL (`grid-out-id2`) matches this signature.

## Fix

The indeterminate classification stays fail-closed; only its blast radius changes.

- **Ledger** (`file-workflow-ledger.ts`): new `commitQuarantine()` resolves the one unresolved heartbeat start marker into a committed **quarantine record** — a new payload variant that claims *no* SharedOS evidence at all (no contact, no reads, no MEMORY/workspace authority, zero claimed usage) and seals every remaining selected task as a durable `error` result with the new typed `INDETERMINATE_EXTERNAL_OPERATION` public error code plus `fatal_error` stop authority. The record is digest-chained like any other; the started heartbeat is never re-executed, so contacts are never re-rolled. Replaying the task's run directory reproduces the same sealed terminal with zero model calls.
- **Scheduler** (`file-workflow.ts`): both indeterminate sites (recovery inspection and live heartbeat) quarantine instead of throwing — but **only** for `files-single` sessions, which hold exactly one task with their own ledger and PACT workspace. The session then finalizes normally (`checkpoint.status: "completed"`, results/summary written), and the `files-single` batch keeps scheduling its other tasks.
- **Kept run-level fail-closed**: `files-multi` still throws (shared workspace across tasks); quarantine refuses to relabel a task with committed changed-action contact authority (a proven side effect must not become a plain `error`); and run-level ledger corruption (broken record chain, marker authority loss, etc.) still fails the whole run.
- **P-007**: `summary.json` shape and the 10 public metric formulas are untouched — the new terminal reuses the existing `error` status with a new `errorCode` only (golden tests unchanged and passing).

## Gates

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (Mac + server).
- `npm test` on the server worktree: **693/693 pass**. (The 7 failures previously seen in `~/aicoo/pact` are the known SharedOS-pin environment drift; this worktree's pinned SharedOS checkout satisfies them, unmodified main behaves the same there.)
- New tests: ledger `commitQuarantine` (seal + finalize + clean reopen/replay, marker-required, no-double-commit, partial-seal after committed terminals, changed-action refusal) and `files-single` isolation (poisoned task → typed durable error row, batch continues; zero-turn replay of a quarantined task).

## Validation (600-task cell)

`~/prelim-grid/configs/qwen-d0-r0.yaml` (taskConcurrency 4) via `run-cell.sh` on image `sharedeval-experiment:a358e5512476` — run in progress; will confirm on this PR that all 600 tasks reach a terminal state, isolated tasks carry the typed error code, and the run no longer trips the whole-cell circuit breaker.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Problem

The 5 specialist AI bots (Parity Sentinel, Differ Guardian, Match Sniper, Barrier Architect, Vector Momentum) used the **shared recovery formula** that sizes stakes to recover debt + an aspirational target-profit derived from the losing contract's payout. For bots with high-payout contracts, this massively over-exposed capital:

| Bot | Contract | Payout | Old Recovery Stake | New Recovery Stake |
|-----|----------|--------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Parity Sentinel | Even/Odd | 1.95× | **$2.06** (win $1.96) | **$1.16** (win $1.10) |
| Barrier Architect | Over 5 | 2.43× | **$1.40** (win $1.40) | **$0.77** (win $0.77) |
| Match Sniper | Matches | 8.93× | $0.35 (floor) | $0.35 (floor) |
| Vector Momentum | Rise/Fall | 1.92× | **$2.09** (win $1.99) | **$1.20** (win $1.10) |

## Solution

A **10% markup on debt** for bot recovery trades only. The formula:

```
stake = (unrecoveredAmount × 1.10) / (payout - 1)
```

A $1 loss → win $1.10 (recover $1 + $0.10 profit). Multi-step losses compound naturally since `unrecoveredAmount` accumulates every consecutive loss.

## Files Changed

- `recovery-math.ts` — Added `calculateBotRecoveryStake()` pure function
- `recovery-engine.ts` — Added `getBotRecoveryStake()` with shared ledger state
- `bot-engine.ts` — Updated `computeRecoveryStake()` to use bot-specific formula
- `bot-recovery-parity.test.ts` — Added 10 new tests covering all 5 bot families

## What's NOT Changed

- The shared recovery engine (`getDynamicRecoveryStake`) used by the Autonomous Engine and NeuroAI Quantum FAB
- Recovery state management, settlement logic, or persistence
- The `recordOutcome` function (debt tracking is unchanged)
- Any frontend code

## Tests

All 129 tests pass (119 existing + 10 new bot-specific recovery tests).

author: kznagamori
body:
## 概要

P6-03の**最終分割（6/6）**。5本目までで揃ったinstall engineの部品（`Stager`／`ProbeRunner`／`CollectCommandTargets`／`HardenPayload`／`Committer`）を順に呼ぶorchestrationと、[02-architecture.md](../blob/claude/work/docs/02-architecture.md)§8手順1〜5のトランザクション境界を実装する。**これでP6-03が完了する。**

## 着手時の確認事項（5本目の停止記録より）

**2件とも仕様から一意に決まったため、利用者判断を求めていない。**

### 1. orchestrationは2層に分かれる

§2は`internal/app`へ「トランザクション境界」、`internal/install`へ「transaction」を割り当てている。どちらも「transaction」を含むが、**指すものが違う**。

| 層 | 責務 | 実装 |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/app` | §8手順1〜5の**境界** — いつlockを取り、いつ`inputs`を照合し、何を許すか | `ExecuteInstall` |
| `internal/install` | installそのものの**順序** — staging→probe→command_targets→harden→commit | `Engine` |

**`internal/app`へ`internal/install`をimportさせていない。** engineを`InstallEngine` interfaceで受けた。app側が要るのは「Planを渡すと結果が返る」ことだけで、engineの生成（Guardで包んだportの注入）は合成側の仕事である。**import表は変えていない**うえ、Execute側のtestもstubで書ける。

### 2. `app.Guard`はport注入で噛ませる

P5-04の`Guard`は`FileSystem(inner)`等でportを包む。engineの部品はすべて構築時にportを受け取るため、**包んだportを渡すだけで済む**。engine自身はGuardを知らない——知らせると、Guardを通さずに動かす経路をengine内に作れてしまう。Scopeは**Plan固有**なのでengineの生成もoperationごとになり、`NewEngine`が`port.FileSystem`を別引数で取るのは部品と同じ実装を渡すためである。

## 主な判断

- **`inputs`の再取得をlockの前後で2回行う**（§8手順3〜4「lock取得後に同じ検査を繰り返す」）。1回目は承認直後の無駄な作業を避けるため、2回目はlock取得までの間に他processが状態を変えていないことを確かめるため。**1回目だけだと、lockを待っている間の変化を見逃す。**
- **再取得できなければ「変わっていない」と見なさない。** 判定できないまま作用を始めるのは、判定して通すこととは違う。errorにする。
- **失敗時はcleanup失敗を握り潰す。** §6は成功・失敗のどちらでもstagingの破棄を求めるが、engineが失敗しcleanupも失敗した場合は**元の失敗のほうが利用者に必要な情報である**。
- **成功時のcleanup失敗とindex更新だけの失敗を、どちらも`W_CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE`とする。** [04-storage-and-data.md](``../blob/claude/work/docs/04-storage-and-data.md)§16.2に「indexが古い」専用codeが無く、5値の閉じた集合であるため。**未使用のenum値を足さない**（CLAUDE.md`` §7）。
- **`command_targets`をpermission正規化の前に集める**（§7手順4→5）。read onlyにした後だと、filesystemによってはread自体が制限されうる。

## 変更ファイル

| file | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `internal/install/engine.go` | `Engine`／`NewEngine`／`Run`（staging→probe→command_targets→harden→commit）、`mergeProbeOutcomes` |
| `internal/app/executeinstall.go` | `ExecuteInstall`（§8手順1〜5）、`InstallInputSource`／`InstallEngine` interface、lock取得と`E_LOCK_TIMEOUT`写像 |
| `internal/install/engine_test.go` / `internal/app/executeinstall_test.go` | 新規subtest 31件（engine 11＋Execute 20） |
| `docs/reviews/P6-03-install-orchestrate.md` | 決定記録（6/6） |
| `docs/13-progress.md` | P6-03を`[x]`、snapshot、停止記録 |

## 検証

Linux containerで実行した。両OSの判定はCI matrixで行う。

| command | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `gofmt -l .` | 出力なし |
| `go build ./...` / `GOOS=windows go build ./...` | 成功 |
| `go vet ./...` / `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` | 成功 |
| `go test ./... -race -shuffle=on -covermode=atomic` | 全package成功。`internal/app` 92.4%・`internal/install` 88.4% |
| `check_policy.py` / `check_imports.py` / `check_docs.py` / `check_licenses.py` / `check_messages.py` | すべて成功 |
| `git diff --check` | 出力なし |

### 変異test

3件入れ、いずれも検査が落ちた。生き残りは無い。

| 変異 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| lock取得後の再検査を省く | 落ちた（2 case） |
| engineをlockの外で走らせる | 落ちた |
| probe失敗でもcommitへ進む | 落ちた |

## P6-03の分割について（正直な記録）

**当初2分割の想定が6分割になった。** §7の9手順が、失敗時の巻き戻し先・依存する仕様・必要な新規primitiveの点で素直に1本へ収まらず、着手のたびに線を引き直した。

**2本目と3本目で、自分が入れた欠陥を1件ずつ検出して修正した**——probe cwdをpayloadにしていた（§11違反）、`SameInstall`がTOML往復後に常に不一致だった（利用者判断で選んだ選択肢Aの冪等installが実際には効かない状態だった）。**どちらも次の層へ繋いだ時点で表面化しており、部品を単体で作っている間は見えなかった。**

## 未実施・制約

- **合成側（`InstallEngine`の実装adapter）が無い。** `install.Engine`と`app.InstallEngine`の型が違うため薄いadapterが要る。置き場所は**P8-01（CLI adapterと`Initialize`）の範囲**である。
- **`app.Guard`を実際に噛ませた経路のE2Eが無い。** 注入の形は固定したが、照合は[11-quality-and-ci.md](../blob/claude/work/docs/11-quality-and-ci.md)§7.2として合成後（P8以降）に行う。
- **receipt indexの再構築は実装していない。** §7が「次回起動時」と定めており、起動時処理（`Initialize`、P8-01）の責務である。
- **P6-02から継続する食い違いが1件**: `internal/store`のtemplate grammarが`internal/definition`と一致しない（fail closedは保たれ、正当なdefinitionからは生じない値である）。§2の責務表を要する判断のため、P6-04以降かmaintenance taskで扱う。

## 次のタスク

**P6-04**（user/project use/current、Windows junction・Linux symlink transaction、native shim resolver）。着手時に確認する2件を停止記録へ書いた。

- BTC option parsing and order-book access

- durable SQLite audit store for fills and portfolio snapshots
- deterministic baseline signal model

- Aevo JSONL snapshot collector
- unit and API tests
- CI fixes for Gitleaks token, dependency upgrades, and valid Trivy release

Safety posture:
- live execution disabled
- no API secret/private signing key stored or used
- no withdrawal or mainnet order path
- paper/testnet-first only

author: braboj
body:
Closes #1348.

## The defect

The changelog-completeness check decided whether its moment was live by
asking whether HEAD carried a tag. That guard covers exactly one commit.
An untagged HEAD does not mean a release is in preparation — it means
something landed since the last tag, which is true on almost every day of
a repository's life.

Its pass condition then read the resulting state as a failure. Run against
`main` immediately before this branch:

```
commits since v2.70.0: 1
entries in Unreleased: 0
  carried: docs(journal): record the session that scoped and cut v2.70 (#1352)
```

Nothing is wrong there. The one carried commit is a journal entry, and the
pass condition itself says a carried commit may be deliberately not
notable — two sentences before it says zero entries with commits carried is
a failure. Both clauses are true at once directly after every cut, because
the first commit after a release is the journal entry the release
procedure records as owed.

## The change

The moment is now declared rather than detected, matching the
milestone-coverage check three steps earlier in the same sequence. With
`RELEASE` empty the check reports that it does not apply and exits 3; with
it set it reads as before.

The zero-entries clause is now conditional on some carried commit being
notable, so it no longer contradicts the reconciliation sentence above it.

Release-ordering keeps its tag guard — correctly, since its failure shape
is a carried count of zero, which requires HEAD to be the tag. The
asymmetry was undocumented and both checks now say why they differ.

## Control

`testing-control-corpus-moves` requires the check's own corpus count to
move, since this narrows what the check runs on:

```
RELEASE unset   -> "no release is in preparation; this check does not apply", exit 3
RELEASE set     -> commits since v2.70.0: 1, entries in Unreleased: 1
corpus control  -> entries 1 -> 2 with a fixture entry added, 2 -> 1 on removal
```

The fixture was removed from the tree after the pair was read.

## Verification

- `py tests/run_smoke.py` — 26/26
- `py tools/sync.py` — 17 generated chains updated, which is `base-git`'s reach
- `py tests/run_conformance.py` — 14 passed, 0 failed, 5 readings read

The conformance run caught a defect in the first draft of this change: the
reworded pass condition put a backticked token on the `Pass condition:`
line, 11 lines from the nearest fence, which the stated-check extractor
reports as a check no tool can extract. Reworded so the command reference
sits on the following line.

The changelog-completeness check now reports `N/A` in that run, which is
the fix working — an ordinary day no longer produces the failure shape.

author: sillyquack
body:
## Summary

Fixes a false negative in verified `start-once` process identity checking on
macOS.

During launchd startup, the authoritative service PID can briefly exist as
`/usr/libexec/xpcproxy` before `exec` transforms that same PID into the configured
Node service. The previous verifier inspected the PID immediately and expected
the final Node command line, so it rejected a valid launchd-owned process a few
milliseconds too early.

## Fix

The verifier now uses strict Darwin-native process evidence:

- `proc_pidpath` for executable identity
- `KERN_PROCARGS2` for structured argv
- exact PID and launch-count binding
- exact same-PID `/usr/libexec/xpcproxy` accepted only as bounded pre-exec
  `not_ready`
- final Node executable independently verified
- exact ProgramArguments vector equality
- immutable runtime/script identity
- fresh PID-bound health remains mandatory

`xpcproxy` is never accepted as readiness or startup success.

## Executable and argv trust

The approved Node executable must:

- be a regular file
- not be a symlink
- resolve to the configured absolute path
- retain its device/inode identity

After exec, both Darwin executable evidence and the process argument record must
match the approved runtime.

Wrong executables, wrappers, alternate runtimes, missing/extra/reordered
arguments, and injected arguments fail closed.

## Health authority

Process identity is necessary but not sufficient.

Startup still requires fresh health with:

- new `startupSessionId`
- health PID equal to launchd PID
- exact runtime/manifest/source identities
- exact repository/coordinator/configuration
- correct watcher profile and required label
- `RunAtLoad=false`
- `KeepAlive` absent
- `autoCommit=false`

The existing post-readiness stability window remains.

## Evidence

Every startup poll is journaled before a possible rejection, including:

- PID / launch count
- executable identity
- structured argv
- process classification
- health summary
- decision/reason

This preserves the decisive first observation in future failed-start evidence.

## Failure behavior

Persistent xpcproxy, process drift, wrong executable/argv, health mismatch,
restart, PID change, or unavailable process evidence still trigger the existing
fail-disabled bootout.

No automatic retry or legacy runtime restoration is introduced.

## Validation

- Darwin helper/start-once: 66/66
- Focused launchd/installer/watcher: 127/127
- Full orchestrator suite: 575/575
- Fresh-process race/stress: 30/30
- Synthetic same-PID xpcproxy → Node → health lifecycle: passed
- Bundled syntax: 27/27
- Runtime entrypoints: 3/3
- Runtime payload: 28/28
- git diff checks: passed

A harmless local Node child was also inspected successfully with exact
executable, device/inode and structured argv evidence.

## Scope

Exactly eight orchestrator infrastructure/test/documentation files.

No:
- real service start
- issue execution
- label application
- RunAtLoad approval
- application change
- Supabase/production change
- BAR 2026 work

## Promotion boundary

Issue #82 remains open and unlabeled with no durable state.

After this PR merges, a new canonical runtime must be built and installed via
`install-disabled` before the installed-service trial is retried.

Do not retry `start-once` as part of this PR.

author: robertilles952
body:
Node's ipc stdio channel prepends a 16-byte binary header (8-byte type tag, 8-byte little-endian length) to every message on Windows, but sends plain newline-delimited JSON with no header on POSIX. The Python side only knew the POSIX form, so on Windows the header bytes made json.loads misdetect the encoding as UTF-32 and crash before python_function(msg) ever ran - every message, every time.

_Channel now detects the platform (os.name == 'nt') and, when framed, reads the 16-byte header to get the exact payload length before parsing, and writes the matching header when sending back to Node.

Verified locally with a standalone repro that spawns python3 with the same stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe','ipc'] Node uses, on Windows 11, Node v22.23.2, Python 3.14.7.

author: griase94
body:
## Summary

- `Enforce PR Label` can pass in this repository. It currently cannot: every run fails at `Unable to resolve action `zebbra/actions`, not found`.
- The rule is unchanged — exactly one of `pr-breaking-change`, `pr-new-feature`, `pr-bugfix`, `pr-security`, `pr-other`.

## Why it was failing

`zebbra/actions` is **private**; `zebbra/neops-lab` is **public**. A public repository cannot resolve an action from a private one, whatever the private repository's access level (it is already `organization`). The other neops repositories — core, workflow-engine, web-client — are private, so the shared action resolves there and they are unaffected.

Two things were wrong beyond that:

- only `pr-other` existed as a label here, so four of the five valid answers could not be given. The other four have been created to match the sibling repositories.
- the concurrency group was repo-wide, so two open PRs cancelled each other's runs of a required check and both stuck on `cancelled`. The workflow-engine copy already carries the per-PR fix and a comment explaining it.

## Changes

`.github/workflows/enforce-pr-label.yml` — the shared action is replaced by the same rule read from the event payload. No token, no `permissions` block, no network. Label names reach the script through `env:` rather than `${{ }}` interpolation inside `run:`.

The job moves from the self-hosted `hetzner` runner to `ubuntu-latest`. In a public repository a pull request from a fork can reach a self-hosted runner; this check reads the payload and needs nothing else.

## Wire / contract

None. No workflow other than this one changes, and the set of accepted labels is the same.

## Testing

The script was run locally against six inputs:

| labels | result |
|---|---|
| `["pr-other"]` | pass |
| `["bug","pr-bugfix","documentation"]` | pass |
| `["bug"]` | fail — none |
| `[]` | fail — none |
| `["pr-bugfix","pr-security"]` | fail — two |
| `["pr-bugfixes"]` | fail — none (exact match, so a near-miss does not count) |

This PR is itself the end-to-end check: it carries `pr-bugfix`, so the job should go green on it.

## Deferred

If a public `zebbra/*` action is published later, this workflow can go back to sharing one. Splitting `enforce-pr-label` out of the private `zebbra/actions` into a public repository would serve any future public repo in the org; that is an org-level decision, not this PR.

author: curricane
body:
## Summary

Implements read-path v3 (design in docs/read-path-v3-design.md): native parquet-crate reading with zero datafusion execution layer, replacing the current read path.

- **e7b1340** `feat(storage)`: footer statistics row-group pruning with a single footer read. `indexlake/src/storage/prune.rs` extracts narrow-type predicates (Int64 incl. timestamps, Utf8) from scan filters and prunes row groups via footer min/max stats before decoding; float columns are never pruned (NaN stats hygiene). A single suffix read parses `ParquetMetaData` and injects it via `ArrowReaderMetadata::try_new`, so the footer is read exactly once per file. Safety guard: if the footer row count disagrees with the catalog `record_count`, pruning is abandoned for that file (protects the deleted-rows intersection case).
- **6c3102b** `feat(scan)`: ordered cross-file batched streaming for scans without window functions. Data-file streams are opened concurrently (`buffered(N)`, `N = IL_SCAN_CONCURRENCY` or `clamp(cores, 4, 16)`), kept in order, fully-pruned files are dropped, and streams are flattened. Offset/limit scans keep the existing per-file count/skip state machine.
- **6cb0464** `bench`: add `fs_bench` read-path benchmark (postgres catalog + fs storage, four asserted scan phases, machine-parseable RESULT lines).

## Benchmark (RG=256, 3-round median, master vs this branch)

| Scenario | Phase | master | v3 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S3 1M/1000 files | filter | 209.7 ms | 56.2 ms | **3.73×** |
| S6 5M/50 files | filter | 574.9 ms | 169.9 ms | **3.38×** |
| S4 1M/10×100k rows | filter | 113.6 ms | 46.1 ms | 2.47× |
| S0–S6 | filter_range | | | −2% ~ −20% |

Row-group pruning gains are measurable now that the profile has multiple row groups per file; uniform-distribution scans (no pruning opportunity) are at parity within noise.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` green
- [x] `fs_bench` row-count assertions pass across S0/S3/S4/S6 profiles
- [ ] Existing integration tests (not run locally yet)

author: markusahlstrand
body:
## What

`engine-protocol` was the last engine holding its state machine as hand-written guards. The four states — `open · pending_signature · signed · voided` — were declared as a `z.enum` in `entities.ts`; the **edges** between them lived as `instance.status !== 'open'` at five call sites, an `assertUnfrozen` helper, and an `already_voided` throw, held to that enum by nothing.

This declares the machine once, in `engines/protocol/src/lifecycle.ts`, with `defineLifecycles(protocolEntities, protocolOperations)` — so a state the column cannot hold, a value the column *can* hold with no state declared, an edge to nowhere, or an operation this engine does not declare are all compile or load-time errors. The machine is emitted into `engines/protocol/model.json`, which `pnpm lint:model --check` gates: widening a lifecycle now has to appear in a PR diff, the same way widening a role does.

`protocolLifecycles` / `protocolLifecycle` are exported, so an app can derive "what can I do from here" from the engine rather than re-deriving `status === 'open' && …` in a button's `disabled` (issue cost #5).

## Why the engine keeps its own conflict vocabulary

`assertTransition` is the default adoption and this engine deliberately does not take it. Its refusals answer three different questions — `content_frozen` (the verb is fine, the content is frozen), `wrong_status` (the verb needs another state), `already_voided` (there is nothing left to do) — and all three are in the published `PROTOCOL_CONFLICT_REASONS`. Flattening them into one `invalid_transition` would be a **non-additive change to a published surface** for no gain.

So the seven guard sites ask the declaration the *legality* question with `transitionFor` and keep their own reason and message. That is exactly the shape `apps/docs/concepts/lifecycle.md` already prescribed for this engine ("When the module has a better reason than 'invalid transition'"), and that page is updated: protocol moves from "deliberately not adopted" to the worked example of that section, leaving `engine-absence` as the one remaining.

Every existing message and reason is byte-identical, so the scenario, conformance and error-code suites needed no edits.

## Three judgement calls worth a reviewer's eye

- **`protocol/record-signature` is declared as an edge `pending_signature → signed`**, even though it only moves the instance when the *last* requested party signs. It is still the edge — no other verb performs that move, and demoting it to `allow` would emit a diagram in which nothing reaches `signed` from out-for-signature. The condition stays in the handler, the same placement booking gives `not_yet_expired` on its `held → expired` edge.
- **`open` is marked `extensible`** (K-17 substates). It is the only state with no freeze invariant: `pending_signature` holds a hash parties are signing against, `signed` holds the attestation, `voided` is over. The other three declare nothing, and that absence is the intent.
- **`protocol/decline-signature` is absent.** It is gated by the *signature request's* own status (`pending`), not the instance's — a second machine on a row this registry does not declare as an entity. Absence means "not governed", never "forbidden".

No migration, no new or renamed permission key, no event-payload change, no non-additive engine surface.

## How verified

- `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` — all green
- `node tools/boundary-lint.mjs`, `pnpm run lint:cycles`, `lint:deps`, `lint:tests` — green
- `pnpm run lint:model --check` (re-emitted `model.json` committed), `lint:conformance --check`, `lint:permissions --check`, `lint:docs --check` — green
- New `engines/protocol/test/lifecycle.test.ts` (9 cases): pairs each refusal with the `transitionFor` result that produced it, so a widened edge cannot pass by silently deleting a test's premise — signing a signed protocol, counter-signing an open one, filling a signed one (`content_frozen`, not a transition error), voiding twice, plus the totality/initial/terminal/extensible facts of the declaration itself.

Part of #844 — `engine-absence` is the last unadopted machine, and it needs its `absence_requests` table registered as an entity first, which is a separate change.

**Needs human review**: the emitted `lifecycles` block in `engines/protocol/model.json` is the reviewable artifact here — it is the whole machine on one screen, and the three judgement calls above are all visible in it.

author: totti0770-beep
body:
Track 2, item 2.3. Investigating it settled a question the discovery report left open as `NOT DETERMINED`: **the app has no password-change form.**

## The defect

`POST /api/auth/password` (`routes/auth.ts:273`) has been complete and correct since the credentials login shipped — it requires the current password, applies `rejectWeakPassword`, and deletes every other session on success. Nothing called it:

```
$ grep -rn "auth/password" artifacts/bestnursingai/src
(nothing)
```

What the settings screen showed instead was a **disabled** input holding `********` under a "Password" label — a control implying a managed credential that offered no way to manage it. The only route to a change was a hand-written `curl`, so in practice the bootstrap password stayed permanent. That value is readable by anyone who can see the deploy configuration, which is exactly the account this endpoint exists to let its owner take back.

## The change

A Security section that calls it. No server change was needed.

- `AuthContext.changePassword` follows the shape `loginWithPassword` already established — an error message to show, or `null` — because a refused change is an ordinary outcome of a form, not an exception.
- The confirmation is compared **before** any request, so a typo costs a round trip to nothing and does not come back as "the current password is not correct".
- The weak-password rules are stated up front rather than discovered through a rejection.
- The success toast says other devices were signed out, because the server does that and the user should know.

**The section is hidden where a hosted OIDC issuer is configured.** Those accounts have a null password hash, and the endpoint answers "the current password is not correct" — true of a null hash, misleading to someone who never set one. `oidcAvailable` is the closest signal the client has; a per-user `hasPassword` on the auth-user contract would be exact, and is deliberately not added here because no deployment currently configures both. The limitation is written beside the check rather than left to be rediscovered.

## Documented, not changed

- **The Do Not Crush List cannot be indexed.** Its pages are scanned images, so `pdf_processor.py` raises `No readable text found in the PDF.` and `documents.py` returns a 422. The refusal is visible rather than silent, which is correct — the document simply stays out of the corpus until someone supplies a text-bearing export. OCR is deliberately **not** in the ingest path: nothing downstream reviews what it produces, and a misrecognised drug name inside a list of drugs that must not be crushed is a patient-safety hazard, not a formatting defect.
- The two guideline documents still missing from the corpus are named in the same place.
- One stale limitation removed: the README still described a web-app document "verification" recording a checksum without validating a signature. That surface was deleted in #6; only the tests asserting its absence mention it now.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| `pnpm run typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm run test` | **74 passed** (was 69) |
| `pytest` | 174 passed, 40 skipped (no database), exit 0 |
| `pnpm run build` | exit 0 |

The five new tests were confirmed to **fail against the pre-change tree** before being kept — otherwise they would restate the code rather than assert the connection.

**Not verified here, and handed over:** that the form works against the live deployment. This session's proxy answers 403 to `*.up.railway.app` and no browser here can render the app. Changing the password on the deployed site and confirming the old one stops working is also the only real proof the endpoint's session-invalidation fired.

body:
Wave 1 of [`docs/MERGE-PLAN-20260901.md`](docs/MERGE-PLAN-20260901.md), on top of Wave 0.

Seven pull requests that carry **no migrations** and therefore no ordering risk. Verified by sequential dry-run before this branch existed: all seven merge in order with zero conflicts.

| PR | what |
|---|---|
| #193 | operator docs — the team screen is merged, production has never seen it |
| #178 | the rollout runbook for 0243–0267 and the two tools it calls |
| #185 | the intake + billing plan |
| #190 | ten owner decisions, already self-relocated to `#319`–`#328` |
| #188 | 52 webhook-signature tests that ran in no gate |
| #189 | the guarded downloader |
| #195 | one entrance card for signing in and opening a business |

## Two things the plan got wrong, found here

**#188 and #189 are not a chain.** The plan listed `#188 → #189 → #191`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` shows no ancestry at all. They are independent, so they drop to this wave instead of constraining wave 4.

**#195 cannot share a wave with #196.** #196 can only retarget to `main` after #195 is *in* `main`, and Law 1 lands one wave PR at a time. #196 waits for wave 5.

## The one guard stop

`check:key-manifest` refused the merge until the change was acknowledged: `signup.text_2` **gained** a call site — #195 wires a key that had none. The guard stops on any change to the orphan set, including an improvement, precisely so a wave cannot wire one key and strand another while the total stands still. Re-baselined in its own commit, 131 → 130, and `check:baseline-drift` confirms the set only shrank.

## Not in this wave

`#309`–`#311` are contested by more pull requests than the plan recorded — three different owner rulings claim `#309`. Nothing in this wave is affected (#195 holds `#311`/`#312`, #190 holds `#319`–`#328`, and they do not overlap), but wave 2 is where it first bites. The corrected map is in the plan.

author: madhumithakk01
body:
…ror noise

src/puf/puf_sim: a stand-in for a silicon PUF so the fuzzy extractor and the layers above it can be built and characterised before hardware. Not a security primitive and not tied to SRAM-PUF vs RO-PUF or any part.

- puf_sim_response(id): clean fingerprint, SHAKE256("puf-sim/response/v1" || LE32(id)) -- deterministic per id, ~50% apart across ids, XOF-prefix stable.
- puf_sim_response_noisy(id, ber_ppm, noise, ...): clean response with each bit flipped with probability ber_ppm/1e6, flip pattern keyed by a per-power-up noise value so reads are reproducible.

tests/puf/test_puf_sim (make -C tests check-puf): clean known answers vs an independent SHAKE256, determinism, inter-device uniqueness, a noisy known answer, ber=0 -> clean, reproducibility, and a measured-vs-configured BER sweep (0/1/5/10/20 %) that tracks to within 0.006 over 65536 trials per point.

author: artui
body:
Found by verifying 0.5.0 against the published wheel rather than trusting green CI.

## The defect

0.5.0 added `DeliveryRecord.succeeded_at` so that `quiet_receivers()` would survive a replay. `AddField` does not backfill, so on upgrade the column arrives empty — and **every receiver reads as having never succeeded**, which is the one question the feature exists to answer.

Reproduced on a real 0.4.0 project, upgraded in place:

```
rows: [('shop.never_runs', 'dead') x3, ('shop.reserve_stock', 'succeeded') x3]
succeeded_at set: 0
completed_at set: 6

QUIET: shop.never_runs     shop.OrderPlaced None
QUIET: shop.reserve_stock  shop.OrderPlaced None      <- succeeded three times
```

This is the same failure the review caught inside 0.5.0 (reading a column that replay clears), reappearing at the upgrade boundary. Every package release was green.

## The fix

A data migration backfilling `succeeded_at` from `completed_at`, for deliveries **still `succeeded`** — on those, `completed_at` is the moment the delivery was acknowledged.

Two rows are deliberately left null:

- **A dead letter.** It settled too, so it has a `completed_at`; that is not evidence of success.
- **A replayed row.** The replay cleared `completed_at`, so no evidence survives — and inventing a timestamp would be worse than the null.

## On testing a migration

The migration's function is called directly against the real models. Building a real schema editor needs foreign-key checks off, which SQLite refuses inside the transaction each test runs in, so four tests pass a stand-in exposing the single attribute the function reads (`connection.alias`, so a router sending the log elsewhere is updated there rather than on `default`).

A stand-in for a protocol is how a suite ends up agreeing with a bug, so a fifth test passes **the object Django actually passes** and asserts the same outcome. The stand-in cannot quietly describe an interface the producer does not have.

Both guarantees go red when removed:

```
WITHOUT the backfill            -> 2 failed
WITHOUT the status predicate    -> 1 failed  (a dead letter backfilled as success)
```

342 tests, 100% line and branch.

author: zhiyuan-zhang0206
body:
## Problem

The page-liveness reconcile (`reconcile_open_pages`) ran only at **boot** and on **heartbeat**. The gateway heartbeat check-in only reaches **idle** agents — a busy agent never receives one, so its `serve()` pages could stay dead for the entire duration of a long turn.

**2026-09-01 incident (Task #2257):** agent #3187's page `merge-orchestration-research` died when platform updates reaped page-server sessions at 10:04/11:40 (Beijing). The boot scans at 10:04:14/11:39:58 found the server alive (the kills landed seconds later), and afterwards no `page_restore_*` event fired for ~4h — the agent was busy, got no heartbeat, and nothing scanned again until it manually closed the row at 15:39.

## Fix

A heartbeat-independent periodic scan: `page_reconcile_loop` runs as a background task in the agent process every `PAGE_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S` (300 s — the heartbeat cadence), regardless of idle/busy, cancelled together with the lease renewer on process exit.

Cost control: a pass is **skipped** when boot/heartbeat already reconciled within the interval (module monotonic timestamp — deliberately not an `asyncio.Lock`, which would bind to one event loop and break the per-case loop tests). Combined cadence stays ~one scan per interval for idle agents; busy agents get a scan every 300 s. Each pass is at most one `1.5 s` probe (one open page per agent, probed via the existing `asyncio.to_thread` pattern).

## File-tree diff

★ = critical path

- ★ `agent/startup.py` — `PAGE_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S` + `_last_reconcile_at` timestamp; `reconcile_open_pages` stamps the timestamp at pass start; new `page_reconcile_loop(pool, agent_id, *, event_publisher, interval_s)` — sleep → skip-if-recent → reconcile; docstrings updated (boot + heartbeat + periodic).
- ★ `agent/loop.py` — `main()` creates `page_reconciler` task next to the lease renewer (after boot reconcile, so boot covers t=0), cancels it in the same `finally`; boot comment + `__all__` updated.
- `agent/graph/_claim_dispatch.py` — `_handle_heartbeat` docstring: heartbeat pass keeps the idle-agent cadence; periodic loop covers busy agents.
- `tests/agent/test_startup_restore_pages.py` — 3 new tests: loop runs periodically; loop skips a recent pass; the open-pages query filters `closed_at IS NULL AND expired_at IS NULL` (regression pin, see below).

## Investigation note — the reported "boot stale-name anomaly" (item ②)

The task premise ("page_restore_alive events at 10:04/11:39 recorded a page closed 8/31 23:39") is **contradicted by the DB**: `agent_pages` row 1970 (`merge-orchestration-research`) was created `2026-08-31 17:40:07 UTC` and closed `2026-09-01 07:39:24 UTC` (15:39 Beijing — the manual close during the incident investigation). Both scans (02:04:14 / 03:39:58 UTC) therefore saw an **open** row with a live server — the events were legitimate, and the reconcile query is already a fresh rowset (`closed_at IS NULL AND expired_at IS NULL` on every pass, no cache, autocommit pool). No code bug exists; the "8/31 23:39" figure appears to be a misread of the 8/31 15:37 UTC event (23:37 Beijing) for the preceding `timeline-demo` row. Pinned the fresh-rowset filter with a regression test instead of shipping a no-op "fix".

## Verification

- `pytest tests/agent/test_startup_restore_pages.py` — 13 passed (10 existing + 3 new)
- `pytest tests/agent/test_loop.py tests/agent/test_loop_main.py` — 89 passed (loop.py touched)
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` — clean on all 4 files
- `pyright` — 0 errors on the 3 source files (test-file warnings match the file's existing style)

author: lethanhcong1506
body:
## Summary
`DefaultConnection` không khai báo `Maximum Pool Size` — Npgsql tự áp mặc định 100 cho mọi pool tạo từ nó. EF Core (`NpgsqlDataSource`) và Hangfire.PostgreSql (`UseNpgsqlConnection`) tạo pool RIÊNG dù dùng chung 1 chuỗi kết nối, nên cộng lại có thể xin tới 200 connection phía client — trong khi Supavisor (Supabase pooler) chỉ cấp tối đa 20 cho toàn app.

Hangfire cụ thể chạy nhiều thread nội bộ mỗi server (polling hàng đợi, heartbeat, dọn job hết hạn) giữ connection liên tục — chi phí này nhân đôi từ khi tách thành 2 Hangfire server (`interactive-worker` + `background-worker`, PR #300).

- Tạo 1 connection string riêng cho Hangfire với `MaxPoolSize=10` (qua `NpgsqlConnectionStringBuilder`, không đụng tới connection string gốc dùng cho EF Core).
- 10 đủ dư cho 3 worker (2+1) cộng vài connection nội bộ mỗi server, mà vẫn chừa nhiều chỗ cho EF Core trong ngân sách 20 của Supavisor.

**Cố ý chưa làm**: EF Core (`NpgsqlDataSource` ở `Program.cs`) cũng đang bị y hệt vấn đề này và thực ra chiếm connection nhiều hơn Hangfire trong thực tế — đã hỏi và được xác nhận **để riêng, không sửa trong PR này**.

author: chrisjamesseal
body:
## Summary
- This is a static site with no build step, so setting `CARTO_API_KEY` as a Vercel environment variable never actually reached the client-side `CARTO_API_KEY` constant in `index.html` on its own - it only worked if the key was pasted directly into the file.
- Added `api/carto-key.js`, a small Vercel edge function that reads `process.env.CARTO_API_KEY` and hands it back to the browser as JSON.
- The client fetches it once at startup (`loadCartoKey()`) and re-initialises any map already showing once it resolves, so a page already displaying the watermarked map picks up the real tiles without needing a fresh navigation.
- Not a real secret in the way an upstream API token is - it only ever gates map tile *images*, the same trust boundary a client-side Google Maps key already sits at, so returning it to the browser is fine (and matches how CartoDB's own key setup expects it to be used, restricted by domain rather than kept server-only).
- Pasting the key directly into the `CARTO_API_KEY` constant in `index.html` still works too - this just adds the other way of setting it, for anyone who'd rather manage it via Vercel's dashboard instead of committing it to the repo.

## Test plan
- [x] Syntax-checked `index.html` and `api/carto-key.js`
- [x] Playwright: stubbed `/api/carto-key` to return a test key and confirmed `CARTO_API_KEY` gets set and `cartoTileUrl()` includes it

body:
The one commit that landed after PR #10 merged.

## Hero photo

Now **El Camino Real at Mathilda Avenue**, from the Sunnyvale Wikipedia article.

Better than the Murphy Avenue shot for a specific reason: that corridor is where most of the housing this dashboard tracks actually sits, so the background is about the subject rather than decoration. It's also **public domain** rather than share-alike, and a third the file size. Credited regardless.

Note: the 1600px thumbnail 404s — Wikimedia only generates certain widths — so this uses the verified 1280px variant.

## Section nav

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Type | 12.5px sentence case | 11px uppercase, tracked |
| Active marker | thin underline below | solid cap above + faint wash |
| Bar rule | 2px green under everything | hairline; the cap carries the colour |
| Hover | filled background | cap previews in light grey |

The underline sat below the tab, so it read as a stray rule floating above the content. Moving it on top makes it read as the selected tab. Dropping the heavy green rule means one green element in the bar rather than two competing.

The copy column is much shorter than the news panel, so top-aligning left a void with the photo credit stranded beneath it. Copy is centred against the panel now, credit sits right — under the photo it credits.

author: jhfnetboy
body:
Both deploy entry points have had a `GOVERNANCE_OWNER` handover since CC-48 round-6, and both moved exactly **one** contract: `BLSAggregator`. The two they left on the deployer are the two that decide how much of the community token can exist and what it is worth.

| left on the deployer | what that key can do |
|---|---|
| `aPNTs.communityOwner` | `mint()` is `onlyFactoryOrOwner` with **no cap check**. `issuanceCap` is a view for DVT, not a mint gate, and stays unset until `setIssuanceCap` is called. Mints without bound. |
| `xPNTsFactory.owner` | `updateAPNTsPrice`, `setIndustryScaleUSD`, `setCapRatioBps`, `setTokenCategory` — every input `isOverIssued()` reads. Grades its own over-issuance. |

**Both live examples came out of this path**, which is why fresh deployments kept reproducing it:

- OP mainnet aPNTs `0x0B41C780…` — `communityOwner` `0x51Ac6949…`, an EOA; a 1e24 mint simulates successfully against a 140,000 supply (non-owner call reverts, as the control)
- Sepolia aPNTs `0x696A7370…` — `communityOwner` `0x51C00187…`, also an EOA, `cast code` = 0 bytes

`repo:airaccount` found the first and declined to reference the address.

## The correction that mattered

My first attempt patched `DeployLive` only, and I "verified" it with `./deploy-core anvil` — which routes anvil to **`DeployAnvil`**. The aggregator handover line printed, the run looked healthy, and my change had not executed at all. The on-chain read is what caught it, and `DeployAnvil` turned out to have the identical gap.

```
before   aPNTs.communityOwner 0xf39Fd6e5 (deployer)    factory.owner 0xf39Fd6e5
after    aPNTs.communityOwner 0x51eDf11f (governance)   factory.owner 0x51eDf11f
control  aggregator.owner     0x51eDf11f in BOTH runs
```

That control row is the point: the pre-existing handover succeeding is exactly what made the ineffective run look like it had worked.

## Packaging

35 added lines, no deletions, two files. The first version of this commit carried 153 changed lines in `DeployLive` (mostly `forge fmt` reflow) plus 11 regenerated `abis/*.json` and `config.anvil.json` swept in by the anvil deploy. Stripped — per the point raised on #402 that a reformat is exactly the volume a real change hides in.

`forge test`: 1383 passed, 0 failed, 49 skipped.

author: folpe
body:
Ferme DEV-673.

## Le point 1 était déjà corrigé

Un verdict `clean` portant une contradiction bloquante **refuse déjà** : la correction de gravité du 30 août a sorti `splitBySeverity` de la branche `verdict === 'contradicted'`, et le test `refuses a reading that says clean while carrying a blocking finding` l'épingle. Mesuré avant de toucher au code, plutôt que re-corrigé sur la foi du ticket.

## `package.json` et `.npmrc` sont bloqués

Un manifeste s'exécute. `prepare` part sur chaque install, clone frais compris ; `prepack` part vers npm. L'argument qui avait admis `.github/actions/**` tient ici mot pour mot — et le lockfile était gardé pendant que le fichier qui le gouverne et exécute du code ne l'était pas. `.npmrc` le rejoint : c'est là qu'un install apprend quel registre croire et avec quel jeton.

Avec le contrôle qui prouve que la garde ne mange pas ses voisins : `docs/package.json.md`, `packages/cli/src/lib/package-json.ts` et `npmrc.test.ts` restent accordés.

## La première unité est projetée contre le budget

La projection lit ce que ce run a pris, et un run à froid n'a rien pris. Donc `run autopilot for 1m` — un raccourcissement que l'invocation autorise explicitement — démarrait une unité qui prend le plus clair d'une heure, contre une décision qui affirme qu'un run ne dépasse pas ce qui a été déclaré pour lui.

Elle est maintenant projetée contre une estimation à froid de quinze minutes, **nommée comme estimation** et placée sous tout ce qu'une unité a jamais pris ici. La première fusion la remplace par la mesure réelle du run.

Écartée en chemin : dériver l'estimation de `chainBudget / clusterSize`. Élégante et fausse — `clusterSize` borne un cluster, pas un run, et un programme en `clusterSize: 1` aurait refusé tout run plus court que son budget entier.

**Quinze minutes reste un jugement, pas une mesure**, et la décision le dit : ce dépôt n'enregistre aucune durée d'unité dont on pourrait la dériver. C'est le seul endroit du lot qui mérite peut-être un autre arbitrage.

## Preuve

`pnpm verify` complet vert, 18 portes. Décision `a-cold-run-projects-its-first-unit`.

author: linxiansheng
body:
Introduce a stable C ABI and SPI-based plugin runtime with lifecycle management, catalog integration, SQL extension hooks,
  and build-time boundary checks.

  Move GIS functionality behind a loadable plugin and add reference and SQL extension plugins with developer documentation.

  ### Task Description

  seekdb previously lacked a stable native extension boundary. Optional capabilities such as GIS were compiled into the core
  and tightly coupled to internal C++ types, symbols, and build dependencies.

  This change introduces a general-purpose plugin architecture that allows optional capabilities to be independently built,
  installed, discovered, activated, stopped, and recovered without exposing unstable core implementation details across the
  plugin boundary.

  GIS is used as the first end-to-end plugin migration, while reference and SQL extension plugins provide ABI conformance,
  fault-injection, and developer examples.

  ### Solution Description

  - Add a stable C99/C++11-compatible plugin ABI based on fixed-width POD structures, opaque handles, explicit ownership rules,
  versioned structures, and status-returning callbacks.
  - Add public extension and execution SPIs for:
    - scalar and table functions;
    - custom types and binary codecs;
    - casts;
    - index access methods;
    - optimizer and DAS hooks;
    - declarative catalog objects.
  - Implement the plugin loader, registry, and lifecycle state machine:
    - validated loading from trusted plugin directories;
    - `init`, `start`, logical quiesce, `stop`, and final destruction;
    - atomic shadow registration and generation publication;
    - generation-scoped service and extension leases;
    - dependency validation and conflict detection;
    - drain-aware logical disable;
    - recoverable `BLOCKED` states for lifecycle failures;
    - startup recovery before the server becomes ready.
  - Add persistent plugin catalog integration for packages, operations, services, extensions, ownership, dependencies,
  generations, and recovery intents.
  - Add SQL management and extension integration:
    - `INSTALL PLUGIN ... SONAME ...`;
    - `UNINSTALL PLUGIN ...` with restrictive dependency checks;
    - `SHOW PLUGINS`;
    - catalog-driven function overload resolution;
    - scalar-function execution;
    - generation-leased table-function cursors;
    - persistent custom-type metadata and DDL dependencies.
  - Move GIS algorithms and codecs into `seekdb_gis.so`, exposing 65 GIS functions through the execution SPI while keeping
  stable SQL and storage compatibility tokens in the core.
  - Add:
    - a reference ABI/conformance plugin with lifecycle and registration fault-injection fixtures;
    - a SQL extension example providing scalar functions, overloads, a table function, and a persistent opaque type;
    - plugin manifests and developer-facing README files.
  - Add CMake plugin SDK support and build-time checks that reject:
    - private seekdb headers or libraries in plugins;
    - unsafe compile definitions and link dependencies;
    - unexpected exported symbols;
    - GIS/S2/Boost implementation dependencies leaking back into core-only builds.
  - Add a developer architecture RFC covering ABI rules, lifecycle semantics, catalog transactions, recovery, GIS ownership
  boundaries, development guidance, and the validation matrix.

  ### Passed Regressions

  - Plugin source and dependency boundary check:

    ```bash
    python3 cmake/plugin_boundary_check.py .

  Result: passed.

  - The following dedicated integration suites are provided for runtime and SQL catalog validation:

    cmake --build build_release --target \
      seekdb_plugin_runtime_tests \
      seekdb_plugin_catalog_tests -j4

    build_release/unittest/seekdb_plugin_runtime_tests
    build_release/unittest/seekdb_plugin_catalog_tests

    These suites cover plugin loading, lifecycle failures, atomic registration, lease draining, SQL grammar, trusted-directory
    installation, normalized extension catalogs, scalar and table-function execution, DDL commit/rollback, restrictive
    uninstall, and startup recovery.

    Full build and runtime suites were not rerun while preparing this PR description.

  ### Upgrade Compatibility

  - Existing persistent GIS type codes, SQL names, wire formats, and storage formats are retained and must not be silently
    reinterpreted.

  - The plugin runtime is enabled by default with SEEKDB_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS=ON.
  - GIS implementations are moved out of the default core build. Deployments using GIS must install the GIS shared library and
    manifest under the trusted plugin directory.

  - SEEKDB_ENABLE_CORE_GIS=ON provides a temporary compatibility profile for deployments that still require the legacy in-core
    GIS implementation.

  - ABI v1 currently supports the exact 1.0 ABI and seekdb SDK/build combination. Arbitrary cross-version plugin compatibility
    is not guaranteed.

  - R0/R1 plugins must not contain migration graphs. Plugin update execution and persistent-format migration are reserved for a
    future R2 profile.

  - Uninstall uses RESTRICT semantics when persistent objects or data depend on a plugin. Automatic CASCADE removal is not
    implemented.

  ### Other Information

  - This is currently an experimental/developer-preview plugin runtime.
  - Plugins are restricted to trusted local directories and reconciled against catalog and binary manifest identities.
  - Package signature-chain verification, a production package materializer, and executable catalog-object materialization are
    not included in this change.

  - Runtime hot dlclose is outside the v1 contract. Plugins are logically disabled and drained; published modules may remain
    mapped until terminal shutdown.

  - The architecture and plugin development guide is available in docs/developer-guide/zh/plugin-architecture.md.

  ### Release Note

  Added an experimental native plugin framework with a stable C ABI, lifecycle and catalog management, SQL extension SPIs,
  startup recovery, and build-time isolation checks. GIS is now available as a loadable plugin, accompanied by reference and
  SQL extension example plugins.

author: toumix-agents
body:
Closes #132
Closes #124
Closes #126
Closes #121

**#133 and #123 merged into one**, at your request, by fast-forward — every commit of both preserved, no history rewritten. GitHub records **#123 as merged** since its commits are in this branch; **#127 is closed** as included. The companion is [memory#76](https://github.com/toumix/memory/pull/76), which seeds `WORK/` with 64 notes.

Your prompt, verbatim:

> Help me scan through desire issues and PRs so we can ship a refreshed version after Codex gave some feedback to diagnose why Evening and Birdsong are rather useless
>
> Another point I thought about: every daylight session should in fact make a summary of its work in the memory repo even though the work is purely contained in the corresponding PR, so that Birdsong can get a big picture of what's going on
>
> This could go into one markdown file for each PR, which would also replace the stale queue of the memory repo's README
>
> Another point: let's make sure desire is completely separate from me (there's a PR to move config to memory as it should have from the start) and easy to reproduce for somebody else, in particular, there needs to be a template for the memory folder and the memory PRs that a fresh clone can use as seed

## Why they were useless

**Birdsong's output was the board, and the board was a hand-copy of GitHub.** Birdsong filed #124 itself on 08-31: five PRs listed as open had merged or closed up to a week earlier, `main`'s SHA was asserted unmoved across two rewrites after it had moved twice, four of our own heads were missing. The night's product was a re-derivation whose only consumer was the next re-derivation. And it could not see interactive work at all — `TURNS/26-09-01.md` said, of the day before, *"🌤️ Daylight / 🌙 Evening — carried from memory#72, not re-narrated"*.

**Evening was useless for two separate reasons.** The gate is your review time — your own 08-09 ruling — so one more `[x]` on a head you have not read moves nothing. And *"churns through the PRs' `TODO.md`"* is queue-wide, so a round scatters. There is no Evening section in `TURNS` for 08-28 or 08-30, and no day PR was opened at all for 08-29 or 08-30.

**Codex diagnosed observability, not usefulness.** #129 is ~880 lines of run receipts, UUID idempotency keys and `Covered-through` cursors — machinery to prove a round happened, not to make it produce anything. Its two real rulings are here; the rest is not, and a comment on it waits on your word.

## What changed

- **`DAYLIGHT.md`** — "it designs and queues, never implements" is struck. It designs with you first, then writes the code, and writes the `WORK/` note of every item it touched before the session ends.
- **`EVENING.md`** — one head driven to a terminal handoff before any second head is selected. A scan, a re-merge, a review trigger, a board repair is support work, not an outcome. A check never created is pending, a failed query is unknown, neither is green.
- **`BIRDSONG.md`** — reads `WORK/` instead of re-deriving the queue.
- **`AGENTS.md`** — `WORK/<repo>/<number>.md` and its lifetime; "a turn that stays within one workstream leaves MEMORY_REPO untouched" reversed; the day-PR rule; and, from your review, the trigger for `OTHERS/<person>.md`. Its file-kind list is **gone** — MEMORY_REPO's own `AGENTS.md` already carried it.
- **`sweep.py`** — `notes`, `stale`, `cited`, `memory_clone`, `uncharted`, and `agent_footer`. Exit **2** when GitHub cannot be read.
- **`template/`** — the seed of a fresh MEMORY_REPO, so someone else can reproduce the setup from a clone.

## `WORK/` covers the whole repository

Not our own slice, on your ruling. Ownership is a field in the note, not a condition on it existing: someone else's PR is what ours collides with, and an issue nobody answered is why a head is stuck.

**A note is required for every open pull request and for every open issue an existing note cites.** Citation is what pulls an issue in, so forming a view on a head drags in the ruling it waits on without anyone deciding it has — after writing the 25 non-owned PR notes the sweep demanded exactly two more, #294 and #534, because those PRs claim to close them. Every other open issue is **printed as context, not a finding**: discopy has 123 open issues, 29 untouched since 2025, and stubbing them would restate GitHub and nothing else — the queue again at one file per row.

**Staleness is arithmetic.** `stale()` compares the date each note states it was read against the item's `updated_at`, by whole days; a note with no readable date is stale by construction. That is the mechanical answer to #124.

## `AGENT_FOOTERS`, from #123

`AGENT_FOOTER` and `AGENT_FOOTER_ALIASES` become one list in which **every entry is current**: `claude.ai/code,Generated by Codex`. #121's diagnosis is right — Codex signed with `claude.ai/code` for weeks — but renaming it to `Generated by Codex` does the same in reverse, and a Claude Code session cannot opt out of appending its own footer, so every future Claude post would be recognised only through a marker #123 called *"historical detection only"*. Each runtime appends its own; adding a third is one comma.

A marker counts as the whole last line or inside a link's HTTPS target, never as the label — cubic's P2 on #123, open two days because that PR's runtime receives no events for it (#134).

## Verification

**37 tests.** The sweep is clean, and `WORK/` agrees with GitHub on all 182 open items.

**Live footer audit, unchanged through every revision**: 16 of 39 `toumix`-handle review comments on `discopy#399` and 5 of 10 on `#400` read as agent-authored — the counts #123's own audit reported. The other 28 are your real review comments, still correctly reported as unanswered.

**Four cubic rounds, sixteen findings, all fixed and resolved**, plus your four. The one that mattered: `config()` raised `ValueError` on any non-empty line without `=` while `template/memory/config.env` ships commented, so a memory repo seeded from this template would have broken the sweep on its first line.

## What this session measured rather than re-read

All 34 owned heads from a complete clone, each against its own merge base. Three claims the board and `USER_TODO.md` were carrying are false:

- **"Twelve heads sit one `TODO.md` deletion from going ready" is wrong.** All twelve carry no `TODO.md` and are already **non-draft**. What holds nine of them is a merge conflict.
- **32 of the 34 carried a `TODO.md` and deleted it.** Only #366 and #416 never had one.
- **Only #540 (6 of 11) and #478 (2 of 35) carry an open box at all.**

## Still to merge after this

**#131 + memory#73 together** — they move `config.env` to the memory clone. This PR does not touch that migration; the README says `config.env` is read from this repo's root *today* and names #131 as what moves it, so ping me once it lands and I will update the wording. Then **#120**, one line of the file #131 moves.

## Review cost

**384 lines changing existing files** — `sweep.py` 165/21, `AGENTS.md` 105/16, `CHANGELOG.md` 64/0, `EVENING.md` 17/4, `DAYLIGHT.md` 13/7, `README.md` 10/3, `BIRDSONG.md` 9/1, `config.env` 1/1 — and **486 in 11 new files**, of which 254 are `template/` prose and 195 are `test_sweep.py`. The only executable change is `sweep.py`.

author: ryanlisse
body:
## The problem
Every Postgres spec ran against one shared `ji_test`. Two consequences, both observed for real this session: a sibling lane's migration applied NOT NULL columns to `ji_test` and made a *correct* branch's gate fail on inserts, and residue accumulated unboundedly — 2,602 stale `search_projection_checkpoint` rows by the time this lane started counting.

## Isolation
`tools/postgres/test-isolation.ts`, loaded once per `bun test` invocation via `bunfig.toml`'s `[test].preload`. It creates `ji_test_iso_<pid>_<random>`, re-applies the least-privilege role grants from `init/10-bootstrap-roles.sh` (CREATE DATABASE does not copy per-database grants), runs the real Drizzle migrations as the migrator role, and rewrites `DATABASE_TEST_URL`/`DATABASE_APP_TEST_URL`/`DATABASE_ADMIN_TEST_URL`. All ten existing DB specs pick it up through their existing `?? "<shared ji_test URL>"` fallback — **zero per-spec edits**. A global `afterAll` drops it.

Per-process, not per-file: `bun test` runs every file in one process, so that is the natural boundary — and it is exactly the boundary that makes two concurrent invocations collision-free, since different PIDs get different databases.

No-ops when `DATABASE_TEST_URL` is already set explicitly (e.g. `crabbox-exe-dev-shadow.sh`) or when Postgres is unreachable without `REQUIRE_DATABASE_TESTS=1`. Fails loudly, never silently, when required and unreachable.

## It is also faster
26.5s isolated vs 31.4s shared on the full suite, measured back-to-back under identical load. The fresh per-process database is smaller than the ever-growing shared one.

## The guard is mutation-tested
`tools/postgres/residue-guard.spec.ts` asserts the literal shared `ji_test` holds no `test-index-*`/`drain-*` checkpoint rows or `runtime-test` bron fixtures. Proven by mutation: seeding a stray row made it fail (`Expected: 0, Received: 1`), deleting it made it pass. A guard that has never failed proves nothing.

`tools/postgres/clean-test-residue.ts` is the one-off cleaner — dry-run by default, `--apply` to delete.

## Verified
- Two concurrent `bun test` invocations: both exit 0, 67/67 each, distinct isolated databases, both dropped, no cross-talk.
- Shared `ji_test` row counts unchanged before/after an isolated run — independently re-measured by the coordinator (0 before, 0 after) when the isolation was suspected of leaking. It does not leak.
- Full suite 944 pass / 9 skip / 0 fail.

## Known transitional caveat
While sibling branches that predate this fix still write to the shared `ji_test`, the residue guard can fail on *their* rows. That is documented in `docs/runbooks/postgres-test-isolation.md` and resolves as branches rebase onto this. CI runs one branch at a time and does not see it.

## Gap
Fixture cleanup beyond the `runtime-test` marker is not attempted — other bron fixtures use real-looking `categorie` values with no distinguishing marker, and closing that needs a fixture-marker convention across specs. Stated rather than silently skipped.

author: stevenmcclankerton
body:
## Linked issue

n/a — performance work without a tracking issue

Prerequisite: [#30186](https://github.com/prisma/orm/pull/30186).

## Summary

Fast-paths the canonical PostgreSQL `YYYY-MM-DD` wire form with direct `Temporal.PlainDate` construction while retaining the existing parser for every noncanonical representation. On top of the runtime optimization PR, aggregate whole-result-set latency improves from 809.2 µs to 679.0 µs.

## At a glance

```ts
return new Temporal.PlainDate(
  year0 * 1000 + year1 * 100 + year2 * 10 + year3,
  month0 * 10 + month1,
  day0 * 10 + day1,
);
```

Only fixed-width ASCII dates reach this constructor path.

## Decision

Recognize and validate the ordinary server representation using character codes, then construct the immutable Temporal value directly. BC dates, expanded years, sentinels, malformed input, and other noncanonical forms continue through the existing adaptation and `Temporal.PlainDate.from` behavior.

## Reviewer notes

- Every digit is range-checked before direct construction; length and separator positions are fixed.
- The generic fallback remains the source of behavior and errors outside the canonical form.
- The touched helper also replaces `Reflect.get` with typed `Symbol.toStringTag` access while preserving the existing runtime guard, satisfying the production-code structural lint without changing wrong-type handling.

## Behavior changes & evidence

- **Canonical PostgreSQL dates decode through a fixed-width parser** in [`packages/3-targets/3-targets/postgres/src/core/temporal-codec-helpers.ts`](packages/3-targets/3-targets/postgres/src/core/temporal-codec-helpers.ts).
- **Ordinary, BC, expanded-year, sentinel, malformed, non-ISO-calendar, and wrong-type behavior remains covered** by [`packages/3-targets/3-targets/postgres/test/temporal-codecs.test.ts`](packages/3-targets/3-targets/postgres/test/temporal-codecs.test.ts).

## Testing performed

- `pnpm --filter @internal/target-postgres test` — 93 files, 1596 tests
- `pnpm --filter @internal/target-postgres typecheck`
- Rebuilt framework components, SQL relational core, PostgreSQL target, and SQL runtime before `pnpm --filter benchmarks bench`
- Aggregate whole-result-set result: 809.2 µs → 679.0 µs (-16.1%); autoresearch best was 652.5 µs (-47.2% from baseline)

## Skill update

n/a — internal codec implementation optimization with unchanged public behavior

## Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed off (`git commit -s`) per the [DCO](../CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin-dco).
- [x] I read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) and the change is scoped to one logical concern.
- [x] Tests are updated.
- [ ] The PR title is in `TML-NNNN: <sentence-case title>` form — no Linear ticket exists for this work.
- [x] The **Skill update** section above is filled in.

## Notes for the reviewer

This is the final PR in the stack and contains only the PostgreSQL date-codec optimization plus the typed property-access cleanup required in the touched helper.

## Alternatives considered

- **Continue using `Temporal.PlainDate.from` for canonical dates:** simpler, but it dominates date-heavy result-set latency.
- **Regular-expression validation:** rejected after a 4.6% aggregate regression versus character-code validation.
- **Bitwise digit-range aggregation:** rejected because two-run performance was identical to straightforward scalar checks and readability was worse.
- **Cache decoded dates:** rejected because changing object identity and retaining an unbounded value set would alter runtime characteristics.

  - Added validation for date components while enabling faster direct parsing.
  - Retained fallback handling for other supported date formats.
  - Date values now decode more efficiently without changing the supported behavior or output format.

## Objet

Prépare l’activation contrôlée de Collection Report sans activer aucun environnement.

## Réconciliation des contre-reviews

Le SHA initial `631ce3f` avait reçu un verdict indépendant `NON CONFORME` avec 1 P0 et 2 P1. Le SHA `7cc5a8e` a corrigé ces trois blocages, puis sa revalidation a conservé deux P2 matériels. Le SHA courant `b0e58521401d4d3d5cace00193eb0995bda7a0f9` corrige également ces deux points :

- le shim PostgreSQL reproduit d’abord le corps historique réel de `detect_collection_type()`, puis la migration le remplace par une variante conservatrice qui ne réécrit ni numéro de chèque ni échéance déjà enrichis ;

Le finding proposé sur PowerShell/CI a été retiré : la borne de 1 500 ms est minimale et la CI du SHA précédent avait effectivement exécuté PostgreSQL 17 sur `ubuntu-latest`.
