author: gjovanov
body:
Refs #788. Records P2 as **built**, including where it departs from the spec.

## Two deviations, both deliberate

**"forward" is dropped, not deferred.** The phase named three tours — enroll / connect / forward — but tunnel forwards are created from the CLI and the desktop app. There is no web surface to spotlight, so that tour could only have pointed at a page that doesn't do the thing. Left as an unstarted bullet it would read like unfinished work rather than a decision.

**Only `enroll` gets a Tutorial button.** The `viewer` tour works, but its route needs an `agentId` — an entry there would land a reader on a page with nothing to point at. It starts from `?tour=viewer` once you're on a device; the honest follow-up is a device-row action.

## Also recorded: why the shape isn't simpler

The state can't live in the starter (the Tutorial view is unmounted by the time the tour runs) and the overlay can't live in each page (a page can't mount itself into the page it's navigating to) — hence a module-scoped machine plus one overlay in the layout.

Plus the three behaviours worth keeping: four dimming divs instead of an SVG mask (a mask can be clipped by a stacking context, and the highlighted control stays interactive), a missing anchor advancing after 1.5 s rather than stranding the reader, and the query param stripped on arrival so a refresh or shared link can't replay the tour.

🔑 The transferable rule: **`data-tour` names, never CSS shapes**, with a test that every anchor still exists — a renamed anchor otherwise just makes the overlay flicker and skip a step, and nothing anywhere fails. Same silent-locator class the e2e suite lost hours to this week.

body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
## Description

This PR refactors the in-memory key/value store in `src/storage.ts` to use JavaScript's `Map` instead of a plain object (`Record<string, string>`).

The storage module previously relied on object property access (`data[code] = url`, `delete data[k]`) and `Object.keys()` for counting and clearing entries. It now leverages the native `Map` API: `set()`, `get()`, `size`, and `clear()`.

**What changed functionally:**
- **Same behavior, cleaner implementation** — the store still persists URL mappings in memory and resets on process restart, exactly as before.
- **Simplified clearing** — the manual loop over keys with `delete` is replaced by a single `clear()` call.
- **Safer and more idiomatic storage** — using `Map` avoids edge cases around object key handling (e.g., property name collisions) and is the standard data structure for dynamic key/value collections in modern JavaScript.

No public API or external behavior is affected — the exported functions (`store`, `load`, `size`, `clear`) retain their signatures and semantics. This is a purely internal quality/performance improvement.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: jaiswalsanket244
body:
## Summary

Establishes a single, consistent password policy in the backend and enforces it on every flow where a password is created/set/changed/reset. Removes the conflicting minimum-length configs (8 vs 6) and adds the previously-missing character-mix requirement, so the backend independently rejects weak passwords even if the frontend is bypassed.

Canonical policy (byte-identical to the frontend):
- Minimum length: **8**
- At least one uppercase **and** one lowercase letter
- At least one number
- At least one special character from `@$%*&?!`

## Changes

- **New single source of truth** `src/modules/auth/utils/password.constant.ts` — exports `PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH`, the strength regexes, reusable error messages, and `passwordPolicySchema`. A future policy change is now one edit.
- **Enforced on all password-setting flows** — register, update/reset-password, user change-password, and super-admin change-user-password all import `passwordPolicySchema` (no more hardcoded 6/8).
- **Auth flows reduced to presence-only** — login and two-factor login now validate presence only (`min(1)`), removing the conflicting `min(6)` so legacy users are never locked out. Documented inline. (error-log login was already presence-only.)

## Tests

- New `password-policy.test.ts` unit-tests the schema: accepts a valid password, and rejects too-short / missing-number / missing-special / missing-uppercase / missing-lowercase, plus an exact-min-length boundary case.
- `register.test.ts` — added character-mix integration cases (no number, no special, no upper/lower mix).
- `password.test.ts` — update-password now asserts min-8 and a character-mix rejection.
- `login.test.ts` — replaced the stale `min(6)` test with a presence check + a regression proving a weak-but-present password is **not** rejected on login.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — passes
- `npm run lint` — passes
- `npm run test:run` — **494 passed, 1 skipped (57 files)**

Closes CYR-84.

author: sundapeng
body:
### Purpose

Fix `MSCK REPAIR TABLE` for catalog-managed Format Tables that use value-only partition paths.

The default partition directory (normally `__DEFAULT_PARTITION__`) starts with `_`. Repair did not pass the configured default partition name to filesystem discovery, so that directory was treated as hidden. `ADD PARTITIONS` could not discover it, while `SYNC` or `DROP PARTITIONS` could unregister a live partition and make its rows invisible even though the data files remained.

Pass the table's default partition name to the existing discovery overload. Keep raw path discovery unchanged so values such as `month=01` are not cast and rewritten.

### Tests

- `mvn -pl paimon-spark/paimon-spark-common -DskipITs -Dtest=FormatTablePartitionRepairTest -DfailIfNoTests=false test`
  - JUnit: 22 passed
  - ScalaTest executed by the module lifecycle: 36 passed
- `mvn -pl paimon-spark/paimon-spark-common spotless:check`

The new regression cases cover ADD, SYNC, a custom default partition name, a default partition on a non-leaf value-only level, and the unaffected key-value layout.

author: mhduiy
body:
## Summary

The display plugin opened its **own** `wl_registry` on top of the one already owned by the Qt Wayland platform plugin. Each `wl_output` global was therefore bound twice, producing two independent proxies with two independent lifetimes — one managed by `QWaylandDisplay`, one by `WQt::Output`. When the compositor removed an output global, Qt cleaned up only its own proxy, leaving the plugin free to keep naming a dead output.

This PR removes that second registry and makes every treeland extension bind through Qt's.

## Changes

- Delete `WQt::Registry` and `WQt::Output`. Every treeland extension is now a `QWaylandClientExtension`, dispatched from `activeChanged`, so there is exactly one `wl_registry` and one lifetime per `wl_output`.
- Obtain `wl_output` from `QScreen` and destroy color-control / wallpaper contexts in `QGuiApplication::screenRemoved`, before Qt releases the platform screen.
- Add `WQt::Utils::isOutputAlive()` and check it before issuing an output-bound request.
- Reject protocol operations while an extension is inactive. `QWaylandClientExtension` holds no bound proxy until `activeChanged` fires, and the generated stubs dereference it unconditionally — `OutputManager::createConfiguration()` now returns `nullptr` instead, and every caller handles it.
- Guard every protocol `destroy()` with `isInitialized()`, for the same reason.
- Gate the manager `destroy` requests that are `since="2"` on the negotiated version; sending them to a v1 compositor triggers `WL_DISPLAY_ERROR_INVALID_METHOD`.
- Add the missing destructors for treeland extensions in personalization, mouse and shared-utils.
- Rename `wayland/libwayqt` to `wayland/client`, and the object library `libwayqt6` to `display-wayland-client`.

The removed registry also had three latent defects: `wl_display_roundtrip()` in its constructor (competing with the platform plugin for the default queue), unconditional `wl_seat_destroy()` / `wl_shm_destroy()` on possibly-null proxies owned by Qt, and a mixed `if` / `else if` chain in `handleAnnounce`.

## Impact

Treeland only. X11 sessions take the `else` branch in `DisplayWorker`'s constructor — `initTreeland()` never runs, all four manager pointers stay `nullptr`, and `m_control_monitors` stays empty. The only non-treeland-gated change is dropping an unused `#include <wayland-client.h>`.

## Known issue — not fixed here

This does **not** yet fix the `treeland_wallpaper_manager_v1 … "Invalid output resource"` fatal error when switching from copy mode to single-screen mode. That reproduction was retested after these changes and still fails, so the remaining trigger is elsewhere and is being investigated separately. The duplicate-registry problem addressed here is a real defect on its own and is worth landing independently.

## Test plan

- `cmake --build build` clean; `display.so`, `mouse.so` and `personalization.so` link with no undefined `WQt::` symbols.
- `reuse lint` compliant (1940/1940).
- Not yet verified on a live treeland session for the copy-to-single transition; see the known issue above.

PMS: TASK-394993

## Summary by Sourcery

Eliminate the display plugin’s duplicate Wayland registry and bind Treeland extensions through Qt’s registry with safe output lifecycle management.

Bug Fixes:
- Use Qt Wayland’s registry and screen-owned output proxies for Treeland extensions to prevent stale output resources and duplicate proxy lifetimes.
- Guard output-bound operations, inactive extensions, uninitialized proxies, and version-dependent destroy requests to avoid fatal Wayland protocol errors.

Enhancements:
- Tie wallpaper and color-control contexts to QScreen lifecycle and clean them up before Qt releases removed outputs.
- Refactor Treeland extension initialization around Qt client-extension activation and improve virtual-output and monitor lifecycle handling.
- Add missing destruction handling for Treeland extensions across personalization, mouse, and shared utilities.

Build:
- Rename the display Wayland client source directory and object library to reflect their client-extension role.

Chores:
- Remove the plugin-owned Wayland registry and output wrapper implementation.

共有アプリを Collections ペインで見たとき（Previews OFF）、**コレクションごとに「誰が何を読めて何を書けるか」**を表で示す。特に見たいのは 2 行 —— **サインインしていない人**と、**サインインしただけで招待されていない人**。

## なぜ

Previews はヘッドレスもペインも **著者のセッション**で動く。だから「著者に何ができるか」しか見えず、SKILL.md 自身が `Neither preview can tell you what the rules would say to a visitor or a participant` と書いている。一方で答えは静的に出せる —— 認可を決めているのは `firestore.rules` で、そのルールが読む文書は 2 つ（アプリ文書と、その `public` ブロック）だけだからだ。

この 2 つは `projectPublish` が作業ツリーから**純粋に**射影する。よって Firestore のセッションは要らず、何も書かず、`app.json` を直した瞬間に変わる。

## 何を出すか

`Previews` の隣に `Access` ボタン（排他の第 3 面）。コレクションごとに 4 行 × 2 列:

| Who | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| Not signed in | Nothing | Nothing |
| Signed in, not invited | Nothing | Nothing |
| Participant (4) | All rows | Submit, edit own |
| Owner / editor (1) | All rows | Anything |

- 色が付くのは**外部の 2 行が何かに届いているときだけ**。全部光る表は何も光っていないのと同じ。
- 名簿の実数を括弧で出す（`audience: "participant"` を宣言していて participant が 0 人、は表からは読めない）。
- `viewer` / `assignee` は列を持たないので、表の下に人数で出す。

## 表に出さないこと

判定できないものを表のセルにすると嘘になるので、**必ず表を狭める向きの注記**として文で出す:

- 投稿の窓 —— 「宣言がある」ではなく**今開いているか**まで解く。`apps/roles` は 3 コレクションとも `window.until` が 2000 年で閉じており、宣言の有無だけを見ると「誰でも投稿できる板」と報告してしまう（実地で確認・修正済み）。`fromField` / `untilField` は別レコードに境界があるので「判断できない」と言う。
- セッションゲート / `idFrom: "field"` の先着 / `revealGated` / `assignee` / `mirrorOf`。

## `emailField` の穴

`ownRow` の `emailField` 分岐は**世界中の verified アカウントに届く**。素直に書くと、行を作る手段が一切ない赤の他人のセルが `Own rows` になり、「他人は何にも触れない」ことを言うための表が逆のことを言う。なので **行を作れるか**でゲートした。作れない人は行を持てない。

ただし「開いていた時期に投稿して、閉じた後も自分の行を読み書きできる人」は本当に居て、作業ツリーには記録がない。これは表では言えないので caveat の文にした。しかもその文は**スイッチで閉じた場合にだけ**出す —— `audience: "participant"` は `public.enabled` が何であれ外部を拒むので、開いていた時期が存在しない（`apps/ai-blogs` に誤って警告が出ていたのを直した）。

## 実地確認

`~/git/ai/apps` の実アプリに対して射影を回して読み合わせた: `ai-blogs`（世界が読む・9 人の participant だけが書く・各自が自分の記事を直す）、`roles`（窓が閉じている）、`gym`（`bookings` は匿名には見えない / レコードごとの窓）、`live`（`votes` は自分の票だけ）、`survey`、`todos`。

## テスト

- `test/common/sharedAppAccess.spec.ts` 24 本 —— 形は mulmoserver の `test/rules/rules_matrix.ts` が emulator で測っている形（招待制 = #1926 の形・無記名アンケート・ブログ）に合わせてある。ミューテーションで感度を確認済み: `(publicOn || listedIn)` のゲートを外すと招待制の他人セルが落ち、`emailField` の `verified()` を外すと匿名訪問者のセルが落ちる。
- `test/server/backends/sharedAppAccess.spec.ts` —— **Firestore セッション無し**で答えること自体を pin する（`setFirestoreAccessor(null)`）。
- ペインの面の切り替え、コンポーネント、ワイヤの narrow それぞれに spec。

## 権威について

これは**報告**であって、何も認可しない。認可を持つのは deploy 済みのルールだけで、パネルと本番が食い違ったら本番が正しく、食い違いのほうがバグ。パネルの末尾にもそう書いてある。

author: cbeaulieu-gt
body:
## Summary
Adds a **Toggle Show Full Path** button to the Bookmarks view title bar, alongside the existing Group by Repo toggle, so bookmarks with identical filenames in different folders are distinguishable at a glance.

- `BookmarksTreeDataProvider` gains `getShowFullPath()` / `setShowFullPath()`, mirroring the existing `getGroupMode()`/`setGroupMode()` shape. Default off (filename-only, unchanged).
- New `getWorkspaceRelativePath()` helper in `workspaceFolders.ts`, sibling to the existing `isInsideWorkspace`. Returns the `/`-joined path relative to the containing workspace folder, or `undefined` when the resource falls outside every workspace folder (or there are none) — falls back to filename-only display, never absolute path.
- Relative path is rendered in `TreeItem.label` (never `description`, which stays reserved for the repo-name/"missing" badges) — no duplicated root-name prefix when combined with Group by Repo.
- New optional 7th constructor argument on `BookmarksTreeDataProvider`, `viewState?: vscode.Memento`, persists the toggle across window reloads (wired to `context.workspaceState` in `extension.ts`). Omitting the argument preserves prior behavior exactly — additive, non-breaking.
- `bookmarks.toggleShowFullPath` command + `view/title` menu entry added, mirroring `bookmarks.toggleGroupByRepo`.
- README and CHANGELOG updated.

## Nested workspace roots (previously a known limitation — now fixed)
`getWorkspaceRelativePath` originally picked the *first* matching workspace folder when roots are nested (e.g. both `/workspace` and `/workspace/repo-a` open), so the label depended on folder order. Fixed in `81e838b` (#118): the function now scans all folders and returns the path relative to the **longest-prefix (deepest/most specific)** match, independent of array order.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 495 passing, 0 failing (479 original + 14 from the toggle feature + 2 new nested-root ordering tests for #118)
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean

- [x] Nested workspace roots resolve to the deepest match regardless of folder array order (`workspaceFolders.test.ts`, #118)

Closes #115

author: charlesvestal
body:
Found on CW-78, which was ported from this file and inherited the gap: **no enum on any page raises its option list on a turn.**

`param_pages`' `render()` paints a page into a rect the **caller** owns, and nothing in the library clears the screen — that's what lets a consumer host a page inside its own chrome. So anything full-screen is handed back to the frame owner, which is this file. We call `render()` and stop, so the controller tracks a peek on every enum detent that is painted nowhere; `applyInput` also swallows the Back that dismisses it, so a Back straight after a turn does nothing visible either.

Schwung has made that obligation a function rather than a paragraph in a doc: charlesvestal/schwung#388 adds `controller.renderOverlays(ctx, { clearScreen })`. This is 6W6's half — one guarded call after `render()`. The guard is on `typeof controller.renderOverlays === "function"`, so it's safe on older hosts (no `min_host_version` bump); there it stays the no-op it is today.

**Merge after #388 lands**, or it stays a no-op.

author: anirudhkumar-nanonets
body:
`main` has been red since before `release: 0.16.0`. Two unrelated causes.

## 1. `not ok 197 — cursor-session-end force-closes THIS conversation`

The test needs telemetry actually **on** to observe the rollup, so it clears the gates — but only `CI`:

```js
delete process.env.CI; delete process.env.DO_NOT_TRACK;
```

[`inCi`](../blob/main/src/telemetry/gate.ts) is deliberately generous and reads eight more:

```
CI  GITHUB_ACTIONS  GITLAB_CI  BUILDKITE  CIRCLECI
TEAMCITY_VERSION  JENKINS_URL  TF_BUILD  BUILD_NUMBER
```

On GitHub Actions `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, so `offReason` returned `'ci'`, nothing queued, and `readSession(d,'c1').summarized` was `undefined` instead of `true`. Deterministic, both platforms, invisible on a laptop.

Reproduce on `main`:

```bash
GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node --import tsx --test test/claude-hooks.test.ts
```

Fixed at the root rather than by adding one more `delete`: the list is now an exported `CI_ENV_VARS`, and both `inCi` and the test read it. A provider added to the gate can no longer leave the test behind. `CI` keeps its value check (`CI=false` is a real thing people set); the rest stay presence-only.

## 2. `analyze` — CodeQL version mismatch

```
Loaded a configuration file for version '4.37.8', but running version '4.37.7'
```

Dependabot #240 bumped `codeql-action/init` to 4.37.8 and left `analyze` on 4.37.7. CodeQL requires the pair to match. Both now use the same 4.37.8 SHA that `scorecard.yml` was already on — all three pins in the repo are identical again.

The `# v3` comments were the reason this drifted unnoticed on a SHA-pinned action, so they now name the real version, matching `scorecard.yml`'s convention.

## Verification

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 1174 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped |
| `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true npm test` | 1174 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped |

No production behaviour changes: `inCi` returns exactly what it did for every input, and the only source edit is the extracted constant.

author: ablaszkiewicz
body:
## Related PRs

Event mode is live today, and it is opt-in. These PRs settle where it stays and where it goes.

**Deprecating the mobile knobs.** The symbol id on these paths is already a content hash, so two releases collide only when they ship a byte-identical artifact. An ordinary release that changes code gets its own symbol set and never collides. The dSYM path also lost release attribution for embedded targets, because one upload covers every target while it creates one release. Review asked for deprecation instead of removal, so every knob stays accepted as a warned no-op.

- PostHog/posthog#92401
- PostHog/posthog-android#747
- PostHog/posthog-ios#791 ← this PR

**Making it the default.**

- PostHog/posthog#91823 (stacked on PostHog/posthog#92401)
- PostHog/posthog-js#4705

**React Native.** Scopes the mode to the Hermes upload and defaults it to event. That is the one path where two releases really do ship the same artifact.

- PostHog/posthog-js#4717

## Problem

- Event mode helps only when two releases ship a byte-identical binary. The symbol id is the Mach-O `LC_UUID`.
- The unbound path also lost release attribution for embedded targets.
- The upload covers every extension dSYM, but it creates one release, from `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER`.
- An extension reports its own bundle identifier as `$app_namespace`, so its crashes matched no release.
- A silent removal would leave an opted-in user with no signal that their dSYMs bind again.

## Changes

- A build that sets `POSTHOG_NO_RELEASE_BIND` sees a build-log warning naming the deprecation and the fix. The script ignores the variable and uploads symbol sets bound to the release it creates.
- `dsym upload` no longer receives `--no-release-bind`.
- The script header documents the variable as deprecated instead of dropping it.
- The posthog-cli floor returns to 0.7.7, or 0.7.12 with `POSTHOG_SKIP_ON_CONFLICT`.

## How did you test this code?

- `bash build-tools/upload-symbols.test.sh` passes.
- A new case sets the variable and asserts the warning prints, the upload succeeds, and `--no-release-bind` is not forwarded. It catches the flag forwarding coming back, which would fail the Xcode phase against a CLI that removes the flag for real.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Written with Claude Code (Opus 5); the warning added with Claude Code (Fable 5) per the review comment. Skills invoked: `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/writing-tests`.

This replaces PostHog/posthog-ios#789. That PR also carried a fix for a zero-padded `CFBundleVersion`, which follows in a separate PR. PostHog/posthog#92401 keeps `dsym upload --no-release-bind` parseable as a hidden no-op, which covers a build that upgrades the CLI before this pod.

author: frikkern
body:
Task: `task-09c411d26528dd86`

## The door

`BarkparkWeb.V1.MediaCollectionsController.share_view/2` handed
`Collections.assets/3` nothing but the parsed search params and a `:limit`.
Since PR #14436 the collection-search take derives its tenancy half from
`@scope_keys`, so a caller that passes no tenancy keys yields none:
`Media.search_files/2` read a nil `workspace_id`, and
`Content.Scope.scope_to_workspace_or_global/3`'s nil arm returns the query
UNTOUCHED — the deliberate all-tenants read. For a `kind: "virtual"`
collection with an empty `virtualFilter` nothing else narrows it, so the rows,
the `total` AND every facet bucket spanned every workspace sharing that
dataset STRING. The door needs no credential but a resolved share token and
renders with `sign_urls: true`.

## The product call, made

**Is a share token bounded by its minting workspace? Yes.** The resolved share
record IS a `%Content.Document{}` and already carries `workspace_id` /
`project_id` — no data-model field invented, no guess.

**This is NOT the sibling's scope.** `assets/2` passes `scope_opts(conn)`
because there the REQUESTER is the principal. Here the TOKEN is, and the token
was minted inside one workspace, so `share_view/2` now bounds the read by the
SHARE's own workspace/project and not by whichever tenant the request happened
to resolve. A share link stays a window onto its minting workspace from
anywhere; it is never a window onto anyone else's. `scope_opts(conn)` would
have been the *wrong* fix: on the flat `strict_bearer_media_read` pipeline it
yields the `:shared_only` sentinel, which would have emptied every real share.

A collection carrying no `workspace_id` gets that same `:shared_only` sentinel
(the `workspace_id IS NULL` layer) rather than the nil fall-through — the nil
fall-through is the defect being closed and must not survive as the
nil-collection arm.

The asset-document lookup that annotates the hits takes the same scope, so the
docs resolve in the same tenancy as the files they describe. Only the tenancy
pair is replaced; the request-shaped half of `scope_opts(conn)` (`memoize:`,
`caller_context:`) is preserved.

## The other omission is deliberate and STAYS OPEN

`visibility_clamp_opts/1` is still **not** applied to `share_view/2`. A
resolved share token IS a principal, and clamping it to `:public` would empty
every shared collection of exactly the non-public assets being shared — that
half is a visibility TIER, not a tenancy boundary, and its own comment says
so. A test pins it (`"the clamp is still not applied"`), so a later reading of
this row as "add both opts" reds instead of breaking every live share link.
`caller_context` is likewise still not threaded into the search opts, because
`Collections.restrict_public_read_tier?/1` documents `share_view/2` as the
no-caller-context path.

## Proof

`api/test/barkpark_web/media_collections_share_view_scope_test.exs` — two
workspaces on ONE dataset string, a virtual collection in workspace A with an
EMPTY `virtualFilter` so nothing but tenancy can bound the read.

RED-before (controller reverted to `origin/main`, test file as merged):

```
6 tests, 2 failures
1) test an anonymous share view's TOTAL counts only the share's own workspace
   expected the share's own workspace's two assets, got total=3
2) test an anonymous share view's ROWS exclude another workspace's assets
   CROSS-TENANT SHARE LEAK: a share token minted in workspace A returned
   workspace B's media file
```

GREEN-after (this file + the existing `v1_media_collections` integration suite
+ `collections_workspace_scope_test`):

```
19 tests, 0 failures
```

Broader media/share sweep (`plugs/public_share_guard_test`,
`media_flat_decayed_bearer_test`, `scoped_media_public_read_tier_audit_test`,
`test/barkpark/media/storage/`): `50 tests, 0 failures`.

### Anti-vacuity

A media fixture that seeds nothing greens every refute for free, so the file
carries its floor in the same run: an unscoped `Search.search/2` must see BOTH
workspaces' files, and the door itself must return workspace A's own rows,
before any leak refute is trusted. `total` and the facet buckets are pinned as
well as the row list — a fix validated only on the rows looks adequate while
the aggregates still span tenants.

`share_view/2` computes facets and DISCARDS them, so the HTTP body cannot
expose a facet leak; the buckets are therefore pinned on the exact scope the
controller now derives from the resolved share record, with their own floor
asserting that the tenancy-free opts `share_view/2` used to pass DO surface
workspace B's tag.

## Gates

Cloud gate, Console gate, Elixir gate. PR references an active task
(`task-09c411d26528dd86`, claimed by `L1-share-view-scope`, epoch 1).

author: devarispbrown
body:
`make docs` finds every `.md` under the repo root and resolves its relative links. It excluded `./bin` and `./.git` and nothing else — so it descended into `.claude/worktrees/`, which holds **complete checkouts, one per concurrent agent**, and reported their in-progress files as broken links in the tree being checked.

## Not hypothetical — it was live

While writing this, an agent worktree's `docs/debt.md` cited a plan file that exists only on another branch:

```
 FAIL  broken link in ./.claude/worktrees/agent-.../docs/debt.md: plans/2026-09-01-bridge-eval-seam.md
```

So `make docs` failed on `main` for anyone with that worktree present, naming a path the developer never opened, in a file they didn't write. Surfaced by the ledger-audit workstream, which correctly identified it as not theirs and left the fix alone.

## Same class as a fix we already made

727caa9 scoped the holdout boundary test's tree-walk for exactly this reason, and `covercheck` already guards against it. `node_modules` is excluded alongside — a dependency's README is not this repository's documentation either.

## Watched in both directions

- **With** the exclusion: 373 internal links resolve, six worktrees present.
- **Without** it: the same tree reports FAIL naming a file inside a worktree.
- `scripts/selftest.sh`'s `docs` case still passes **both** halves — a planted unresolvable link in this repo's own docs still fails the gate, and an intact tree still exits 0. A fix that only made the red go away would have retired the check.

`build:` is exempt from the changelog gate; no user-visible behaviour changes.

author: jesseli2002
body:
`test_e2e_agreement_is_at_machine_precision` failed on a real GPU with:

```
TypeError: can't convert cuda:0 device type tensor to numpy. Use Tensor.cpu() to copy the tensor to host memory first.
```

`np.asarray()` doesn't work on a CUDA tensor. The sandbox this repo is normally developed in has no GPU (`torch.cuda.is_available()` is False there), so this only surfaced on hardware with a GPU present, where `result.xPhys_traj[k]` etc. actually land on `cuda:0`.

Both comparison helpers (`test_robustness.py::test_e2e_agreement_is_at_machine_precision` and `test_reference_sweep.py::rel`) now use `torch_util.to_numpy()`, which detaches/`.cpu()`s/`.numpy()`s tensors and passes plain arrays through unchanged.

Reproduced the failure and verified the fix on an actual GPU machine, and re-ran the full local suite (411 passed) to confirm no regression.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced original `TypeError` on a GPU box
- [x] Confirmed fix resolves it there (170/170 in `test_robustness.py` + `test_reference_sweep.py`)
- [x] Full suite passes in the (GPU-less) sandbox: 411 passed, 4 skipped

body:
## 沿用 iOS 的結構，加兩件 macOS 特有的事

判斷方式與 `changelog/ios.md` 一致（立刻／儘快／一般，判準寫在頁首），另外補上兩點：

**繞過類問題單獨提出來。** Gatekeeper 擋的是沒有簽章的程式，隱私偏好擋的是 app 讀取螢幕、麥克風與檔案。這兩層被繞過時畫面上不會有任何異狀，所以判準把它們跟 WebKit/Kernel 的記憶體損毀放在同一級。26.5 的 BOM 讓惡意 ZIP 繞過 Gatekeeper，解壓別人寄來的檔案是日常動作，那條特別點出來。

**三條維護線的落差用數字說。** 7/27 那波 Tahoe 補 153 個、Sequoia 138 個、Sonoma 127 個。這個數字本身就是「舊線收到的修補比較少」的證據，比空講支援政策有用。頁首的表格列出三條線的狀態，並提醒 Sonoma 再過一輪就會停止支援。

## 8/6 那則最該注意

三條線同時發、各自只修一個問題（CVE-2026-65400）：同一網路上的攻擊者不需要有效憑證就能通過螢幕共享的驗證。單一修補動用三條線，代表 Apple 認為不能等到下次排程。

條目直接寫出系統設定裡去哪裡關掉螢幕共享，因為對用不到這個功能的人來說，關掉比更新更快生效。

## 收錄範圍

2026-05-11 到 08-17 共六則，同日發的多條線併成一則。全部是「儘快」，近五個月沒有標注實際遭利用的項目，跟 iOS 那頁的情況一致。

## 驗證

- `docs_style_lint.py` 掃六個檔案，0 error 0 warn
- 三語系建置皆通過
- 產物檢查：標籤與維護線表格都正常渲染，icon 正常

author: santiagodepolonia
body:
The failover-rule migration writes converted rules through the raw store, which does not validate the redirect graph. When a rule's fallback names a stored replacing alias that routes back to the rule's primary (e.g. alias `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5` -> `openrouter/...` plus a rule `openrouter/...` -> fallback `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`), the conversion commits a chain cycle, deletes the legacy rows, and drops `failover_rules` — and the first snapshot build then fails with `virtual model chain forms a cycle`, so every later start refuses to boot with the legacy data already gone. The upgrade is bricked.

Changes:

- The migration now validates each conversion against the stored rows (the same candidate-snapshot check `Service.Upsert` runs) before committing it. A rule whose conversion would not load is kept in the legacy store with a warning naming the problem, like the existing collision case: the server starts, routing is unchanged, and resolving the conflict lets the next start finish the migration and drop the store.
- For databases already left in the broken state by earlier releases, the startup validation error now says where to repair: the `virtual_models` config entries or the rows of the `virtual_models` table, since the admin API is unreachable while the server is down.
- Docs: the migration section of the failover guide documents the kept-rule behavior.

Tests cover the full kept-rule lifecycle (warned, resolved, migrated, store dropped) and the repair guidance on an already-broken database.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Prevented failover migrations from creating invalid routing cycles.
  * Problematic legacy rules are preserved with warnings instead of being removed.
  * Startup now identifies invalid virtual model configurations and provides guidance to correct or remove them before restarting.
  * Resolved migrations complete successfully after conflicting virtual models are corrected or removed.

* **Documentation**
  * Added guidance for failover mappings that reference virtual models routing back to their primary model.
  * Clarified how to resolve migration-blocking configurations and complete the migration.

body:
## Problem Fenced code blocks nested inside a list item render as unhighlighted raw text on the docs site, while top-level fences highlight fine. Example: the two `typescript` blocks under [`writing-plugins.mdx` → `global-types.ts`](https://pothos-graphql.dev/docs/guide/writing-plugins). The rendered HTML for a nested block is `declare global {…}` — no shiki token spans. ## Cause `fumadocs-core@16.7.15` (the pinned version), in `rehypeShikiFromHighlighter`: ```js visit(tree, "element", (node, index, parent) => { let parsed; if (node.tagName === "pre") parsed = PreParser(tree, node); else if (node.tagName === "code" && inline) parsed = InlineCodeParsers[inline](tree, node); if (!parsed) return "skip"; // <-- unmatched elements are not descended into … }); ``` `"skip"` on a non-matching element stops `unist-util-visit` from descending into its children, so the first `
    `, `
      `, `
    • `, `
      ` or `` hides its `
      ` from the highlighter.

Upstream fixed this in [`9cf33e9b1`](https://github.com/fuma-nama/fumadocs/commit/9cf33e9b1) by returning `undefined` for unmatched elements, first released in `fumadocs-core@16.7.16`. 16.7.15 is the last broken release.

## Changes

- Bump `fumadocs-core` and `fumadocs-ui` `16.7.15` → `16.7.16`.
- Re-indent the code blocks in `website/content/docs/guide/enums.mdx` back under their list items. They were dedented in 3b2a8da2 to work around this bug; the explicit `1.`–`4.` numbering from that commit is kept.

No source or plugin changes — website only.

## Verification

Dev server on a clean `.next`, rendered HTML inspected for `` (unhighlighted) versus `class="line"` (shiki output):

| page | unhighlighted blocks | shiki lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `guide/enums` | 0 | 78 |
| `guide/writing-plugins` | 0 | 172 |
| `plugins/errors` | 0 | 369 |

Before the bump, `writing-plugins` and `errors` each had 2 raw blocks. A full scan of `website/content` found only those 4 indented fences, so nothing else was affected.

## Upstream follow-up

Nothing guarded this behaviour in fumadocs after the fix landed, so a regression test is proposed upstream in fuma-nama/fumadocs#3525 (test-only).

author: os-warren
body:
Fixes #58

Deletes the two subsumed assertions from `test/views.test.ts` and hands reference
resolution to `test/metadata-bindings.test.ts`, which already owns it. Both file headers
now say which property lives where.

This is a deletion, so nothing below is an argument that the collapse is safe — every
claim is a mutation, applied to real metadata, measured on both guards.

## Method

Each case backs up the target file's **bytes** (`cp`, never the index — an index restore
silently reverts uncommitted work), applies the mutation with a hit count that must be
exactly `1`, proves it reached disk with `grep -F -c` in both directions (`-F` so a
`[...]` anchor is a literal, not a character class), runs vitest, restores from the byte
copy and verifies the restore with `sha256sum`. Mutation and measurement happen inside a
**single** invocation, with the restore armed as a per-case trap. `V:` is
`views.test.ts`, `M:` is `metadata-bindings.test.ts`.

### One reading was void, and the driver was wrong to call it green

The first pass reported case `A9` as `(none — GREEN)`. It was not green: the run
collected **zero tests**. `defineView` is strict about binding-block keys, so the
mutation threw at import and the suite never ran — and a failures-only summary reads an
import-time throw as an absence of failures.

```
$ node -e "const r=require('res.pre.A9-viewsonly-slot.json');
           console.log(r.numTotalTests, r.numFailedTests, r.success)"
0 0 false
```

The driver now prints the collected-test count and fails loudly on zero
(`!! SUITE DID NOT RUN — READING VOID`). Every other case in both passes collected the
full suite (63 pre, 62 post), audited case by case. The A9 mutation is kept in the matrix
as the record of what it actually demonstrates: that key is refused by the platform, not
by either guard.

## A real hole, found and closed BEFORE the deletion

`walkNav` recursed into `children` on `group` items only. The spec ties the recursive knot
on the object branch too:

```ts
type NavigationItem = (ObjectNavItem & { children?: NavigationItem[] })
  | DashboardNavItem | … | GroupNavItem;
```

so a nav entry nested under an **`object`** entry is legal metadata the shell renders —
and this walk never visited it. Measured by hanging a child carrying
`viewName: 'ghost_view'` off `nav_log` (case `B3`):

| | `views.test.ts` (deleted assertion) | `metadata-bindings.test.ts` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| before | **FAIL** | GREEN |
| after | *(deleted)* | **FAIL** — `nav 'nested'` |

That is a redundancy the older file was genuinely carrying, not a duplicate. It is fixed
in `walkNav` and pinned by a new self-test, `reaches nav entries nested under an OBJECT
entry`. The collapse would have lost coverage without it.

## The matrix

18 mutations. `V:` / `M:` name the tests that went red.

| case | mutation | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | `my_week` `columns[]` → `due_datee` | V + M | **M** |
| A2 | `stalled` `filter[].field` → `last_update_att` | V + M | **M** |
| A3 | `recent` `sort[].field` → `last_update_att` | V + M + pin | **M** + pin |
| A4 | `by_unit` `grouping.fields[].field` → `business_unitt` | V + M×4 | **M×4** |
| A5 | `gantt.startDateField` → `visible_fromm` | V + M + pin | **M** + pin |
| A6 | `kanban.columns[]` → `due_datee` | V + M | **M** |
| A7 | `gantt.tooltipFields[]` → `period_keyy` | V + M | **M** |
| A8 | `calendar.startDateField` → `due_datee` | V + M | **M** |
| A10 | `rowColor.field` → `statuss` | V + M + pin | **M** + pin |
| A13 | `data.object` → `duly_taskk` | V×2 + M×5 | **M×5** |
| B1 | nav `viewName` → `by_unitt` | V×2 + M | **M** + V(reachability) |
| B2 | nav `objectName` → `duly_log_entryy` | V + M | **M** |
| B3 | ghost `viewName` nested under an `object` entry | **V only** | **M** *(hole closed)* |
| A9b | `gantt.typeField` → `ghost_field` | — | **M** *(only M reads it)* |
| C1 | nav `objectName` → `sys_bogus` | — | **M** |
| C2 | nav to `sys_user` with a `viewName` | — | **M** (boundary) |

Every defect that took the suite red before still takes it red after, through the right
guard. `A3`, `A5` and `A10` also trip product pins in `views.test.ts` — those pins stay,
and their firing is unchanged.

`C1` and `C2` are the completeness half of the platform-object exemption: `sys_bogus` is
still a finding (the walk checks the platform's **name registry**, not the `sys_` prefix),
and a `viewName` reaching into a real platform object still fails through the boundary
assertion. Nothing about that exemption is a typo hole.

## Two reds are deliberately gone, and both were false

These are the only cases whose colour changed, and in both the deleted assertion was
wrong.

**`A12` — a view column of `deleted_at`.** Before: `V` red. After: green. `deleted_at`
*is* a platform column. `views.test.ts`'s system-column list was hand-copied and had
drifted; the surviving walk imports the platform's own registry:

```
$ node -p "Object.values(require('@objectstack/spec/system').SystemFieldName).sort()"
created_at, created_by, deleted_at, id, organization_id, owner_id,
owning_business_unit_id, tenant_id, updated_at, updated_by, user_id
```

The deleted list carried `business_unit_id` — **not** in that registry — and omitted
`owning_business_unit_id`, `tenant_id`, `user_id` and `deleted_at`, which are. Both
directions of that drift are measured: case `A11` puts `business_unit_id` on a view and it
**passed** the deleted assertion as a "system field" while failing the surviving one.

**`B4` — a nav entry targeting `sys_user`.** Before: `V` red. After: green. The deleted
assertion required every nav `objectName` to be in `dulyObjects`, so it rejected real
platform objects. `C1` shows the typo net is intact.

## Why the rest of the older assertion was unreachable, not merely weaker

`views.test.ts` applied 19 binding-block keys to each of six blocks. Most of those pairs
cannot be authored at all: `defineView` parses with `.strict()`, so an unknown block key
is refused at author time (this is what made `A9` void):

```
ZodError: Unrecognized key(s) on this timeline configuration: `labelField`.
```

Reading the shapes off the schemas rather than the error behaviour — `KanbanConfigSchema`
and friends from `@objectstack/spec/ui` — the reachable slots compare like this:

| block | schema's field keys | `views.test.ts` read | walk reads |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| kanban | `groupByField`, `summarizeField`, `columns` | all 3 | all 3 |
| calendar | `start`/`end`/`title`/`colorField` | all 4 | all 4 |
| gantt | 13 scalar + `tooltipFields` + `quickFilters` | 12 + `tooltipFields` | **all 15** |
| timeline | 5 | all 5 | all 5 |
| tree | `parentField`, `labelField`, `fields` | all 3 | all 3 |
| map | 4 + `descriptionField` | 4 | **all 5** |
| gallery | `coverField`, `titleField`, `visibleFields` | **none** | **all 3** |

No reachable slot was read by the deleted assertion and not by the surviving walk; three
are read only by the survivor. `A9b` demonstrates one of them live: `gantt.typeField`
takes the suite red now and did not before.

## What stayed, and why

- **`declares the binding block its type needs`** — binding-block *presence*
  (objectstack#14106). A different property from resolution (#14107); the walk does not
  check it. Both headers now say so.
- **The product pins** — the gantt bar spanning `visible_from` → `due_date`, the timeline
  reading `last_update_at`, one colour source, nothing ranked by a count, the deliberate
  absence of `gantt.colorField`. No upstream rule can know these.
- **`every lens this app adds is reachable from navigation`** and **`the board sits under
  My work, not Team`** — reachability and placement, not reference resolution.

`views.test.ts` goes 324 → 263 lines. Test count 662 → 661: two assertions deleted, one
self-test added.

## Gates

All four green at `d2876c5`, the commit this PR points at, on a clean tree:

```
$ pnpm validate  → ✓ Validation passed (376ms)                        VALIDATE_EXIT=0
$ pnpm typecheck → (no output)

author: nix-tkobayashi
body:
## What

Phase 2+3 of the notification roadmap: bind a Slack channel to a terminal pane and automatically ask about its notifications there.

**Bindings (ルーティング)**
- Slack notification rows gain **紐付け (Bind)**: choose a pane of the current workspace; the route `{teamId, channelId} → {workspace, paneId}` is stored in `systemNotifications.routes` (delta IPC, main-authority, one route per channel — re-binding replaces).
- Panes are identified by a globally unique `bindId` (UUID per pane lifetime), not display names (non-unique, language-dependent). Panes don't survive app restarts, so stale routes just stop firing until re-bound.
- The notification settings modal lists bindings with an **自動送信 (auto-send)** toggle and per-rule delete.

**Delivery**
- Only live `added` toasts dispatch (never the startup snapshot), throttled to one per channel per 60s, sent to all views of the bound workspace — only the single view owning the bindId acts. Workspace closed / pane gone → normal bell entry only.
- Level 1 (default): the Ask prompt (workspace/channel/link included, lead framing the body as **data, not instructions**) is pasted into the bound pane — Enter stays with the user.

**Auto-send guards (level 2, per-route opt-in, default off)**
Enter is sent only when ALL hold, decided before the paste:
1. route has auto-send on; 2. pane in bracketed-paste mode; 3. `cliReported` — an OSC 9 report arrived and no OSC 7 shell prompt / pty exit since (bash 5.1+ also speaks bracketed paste, so OSC evidence is required); 4. the attention badge is still lit (no keystroke since the CLI said "waiting" — quitting a CLI always takes keystrokes, so a plain shell can never get the auto-Enter).

## Tests
- 2 new test cases (route normalize/dedupe/cap/find, throttle, workspaceKey); suite **189 pass / 0 fail**.

## Review
- codex review looped to `NO ISSUES` over 5 rounds; fixed along the way: pane-name instability → bindId, first-view throttle waste → broadcast-with-unique-owner, bracketed-paste ≠ CLI → OSC 9 gate, stale CLI flag after exit → OSC 7/exit clearing, race with paste clearing attention → gate decided pre-paste.

author: jchristadore-ux
body:
`/api/health` verified three of the four migrations — the initial schema, the storage bucket, and `0003`'s publishing columns. `0004` was not checked at all, while the README claimed the endpoint "checks each one against the live schema".

That gap is worse than having no check. A deployment missing only `0004` gets an empty `problems` list and `ok: true` — the endpoint reporting the database is ready when it is not. And the symptom it produces (paying a model to re-analyse a commit it already understood) never mentions a missing column, so there is nothing to trace back.

The column lookup is now one function both migrations share, so a fifth migration is a one-line addition rather than a judgement call about whether it is worth checking.

```
"migrations": { "durablePublishing": { "applied": true } }
"problems": []                                    ← reads as ready

}

author: simran-2400
body:
Fixes the Julia to MATLAB marshalling, which was flat where its inverse is recursive. Unblocks malfwdplot.

Cause

from_matlab and _py2jl recurse through dicts and lists. to_matlab and _to_py did not. _to_py sent anything array-like to np.asarray, which mangles non-numeric arrays, and passed everything else straight through. to_matlab had no dict case and forced every list element through float().

Fix

_to_py now mirrors _py2jl: Dicts to Python dicts, non-numeric or mixed arrays to lists, nothing to an empty array, numeric arrays to numpy as before. to_matlab gained a dict case that recurses, and its list branch only forces floats when every element is numeric.

Nothing new is constructed on either side. The MATLAB engine already accepts a plain dict as a struct and a list as a cell array, including nested dicts with arrays inside them.

Testing
Fourteen types Julia to MATLAB and eight back, before and after the change:
Before and after:

Vector{String} — failed, now becomes a MATLAB cell
Vector{Any} mixed — failed, now becomes a cell
Dict — failed, now becomes a struct
nothing — failed, now becomes an empty double

Everything that worked before still works, unchanged. Inbound was already correct and is unaffected.

Then a round trip on ten values, sending each to MATLAB and reading it back, including a nested Dict and a Dict containing a matrix. All ten come back identical.

End to end: malfwdplot(out) now works with FSMeda's eleven-field output passed directly as a Dict, so the eval_expr workaround is no longer needed.

body:
---

## Summary

This release promotes the `develop` branch to `main`, bundling six QA fixes and cleanups that close GitHub issues **#5, #6, #7, #9, #10, and #11**. It removes dead feature machinery, hardens side-by-side error handling, standardises Pokémon names to English, fixes persistence and double-spawn bugs, and repairs the panel typecheck configuration.

**Closes:** #5, #6, #7, #9, #10, #11

---

## What's included

### Bug fixes

| Issue | Area | Change |
|---|---|---|
| **#5** | Session persistence | Hover Pokéball recall now notifies the extension host (`pokemon-released`), which strips the recalled Pokémon from the `globalState` memento — no more respawning on the next session. |
| **#6** | Sidebar commands | `delete-pokemon`, `remove-all-pokemon`, and `roll-call` now run `pokemonView.focus` first in explorer mode (matching the spawn commands), preventing the uncaught "Panel not active" error when the sidebar webview has never been opened. |
| **#7** | Spawn flow | Merged the duplicated spawn/name-prompt/persist blocks in `spawn-pokemon`. The Browse Generation path now only selects the species and delegates prompting + spawning to the single post-selection block — no more double name prompts or cloned spawns. |

### Feature changes

| Issue | Area | Change |
|---|---|---|
| **#9** | Localization | Removed the translation lookup layer (`l10n/pokemon/*` was never shipped). `getLocalizedPokemonName()` now returns the English name directly. Removed the `change-pokemon-language` command, `pokemonLanguage` setting, its activation event, and stale l10n bundle strings. |

### Build / configuration

author: askjaer
body:
## Why

Freezing the whole chassis behind the PreToolUse hook worked exactly as §A4/§B9 specified, and that turned out to be the problem. A CPDSE developer working in a stamped app with an agent could not fix a bug in `core/`, adjust a chassis screen, or add a dependency without fighting the guard — it inhibited the people *maintaining* these apps more than it protected the family.

This keeps the guard, shrinks it to what is genuinely expensive to get wrong, and moves the architectural invariants onto the test suite where they already lived.

## What is still blocked

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Blocked | `.adalab/app.json`, `.adalab/project.json`, `.adalab/card.json` |
| Blocked (Bash) | commands deleting `/asv-mnt`, a `.sqlite` file, or `.adalab/` |
| Ask tier | `.adalab/local_container_1.json`, dependency-add commands |
| Editable | `core/**`, `ui/**`, `app.py`, `assets/**`, `Containerfile`, lockfiles, `pyproject.toml`, `.streamlit/config.toml`, `.vscode/**`, `.claude/**` |

The three `.adalab` manifests are written by the AdaLab extension and carry `app_id`, `metadata_id` and `current_image_version`, filled in at deploy time — they are the only files where an agent edit is both plausible and silently destructive at *deploy* time rather than at test time. `local_container_1.json` stays editable-with-confirmation because env vars, resources and volume mounts are a normal step towards a deploy; blocking it would reintroduce the friction this PR exists to remove.

The Bash denylist keeps only the student-data rule plus recursive deletion of `.adalab/`. Results are append-only by design and have no undo, so that one is about data, not code ownership. The old `backend|frontend` patterns were dead — they predate the Streamlit rewrite.

## Enforcement moved to the tests

The suite already encoded every invariant that matters, so it now carries the load alone:

| Invariant | Test |
| --- | --- |
| `core/` imports streamlit nowhere | `test_core_no_streamlit.py` |
| The UI package is `ui/`, never `pages/` | `test_navigation.py` |
| Plots keep their standalone "Show the code" | `test_show_the_code.py` |
| No per-student data in module-level globals | `test_concurrency.py` |
| `.adalab/` stays internally consistent | `test_adalab_config.py` |

Rewriting the advisory layer was the bulk of the work. Six files told the agent the chassis was off-limits (`CLAUDE.md`, the skill, `chassis-vs-seam.md`, the session-start banner, two rule files, `/new-exercise-field`); leaving any of them would have kept agents refusing chassis edits whatever the hook permitted. The framing is now *start at the seam, here is what breaks if you go further, and here is the test that catches it*.

## Also in here

- **`chassis_guard.py` → `deploy_guard.py`**, `ALLOW_CHASSIS_EDIT` → `ALLOW_DEPLOY_CONFIG_EDIT`. The old name described a job the hook no longer does.
- **New `tests/test_guardrails.py`** (28 tests) pins the scope in both directions: the three `.adalab` files stay blocked, `core/`/`ui/`/`app.py`/the seam stay editable, and the hook, `permissions.deny` and `CLAUDE.md` must keep naming the same set. Mutation-checked — re-adding `core/**` to `PROTECTED` fails three of them.
- **Two stale docs fixed in passing**: `SPEC.md` listed `pages/**` as protected long after the directory was renamed to `ui/`, and named a `local_container_demo.json` this template does not ship. The absence of a guardrail test is how that drifted unnoticed.
- `DECISIONS.md` records the divergence from §A4/§B9 and marks the old "Chassis guard" section superseded. The base spec and addenda are left untouched — they are the input specs, and DECISIONS.md is where divergences belong.

## Accepted risk, recorded deliberately

`.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/hooks/**` are no longer protected, so an agent can disable the guard in a single edit. That was the call: developers own the repo they stamped, and a guard they cannot remove is one that gets worked around. The `.adalab` block is a speed bump against accident, not a defence against intent — which matches the actual failure mode, an agent helpfully editing deploy state it does not understand.

## Verification

Stamped with `copier copy . <tmp> --defaults --trust` and ran the suite: **280 passed** (252 before, plus the 28 new guardrail tests). Hook behaviour checked directly by piping PreToolUse events: `.adalab/app.json` exits 2, `core/db.py` exits 0, `rm -rf /asv-mnt/lab-data` exits 2, `rm -rf .devapp` exits 0. `ruff check` is clean on the new files.

No container rebuild — nothing here touches the image (`tests/` is dockerignored and `.claude/` has no runtime role).

Scope is confined to `lab-exercise-app-template/`.

author: vuongdang
body:
## What

The variant `manifest.json` becomes the **single source of truth and the single CLI argument** for the whole variant pipeline. Every script reads its spec from the manifest and writes results back into the same file.

### Scripts — all now `<script> <manifest.json>`, no other flags

| Script | Role |
|---|---|
| `train_lora.py` | reads the `training` spec, trains, writes back `dataset_hash` (**computed**, not copied from the dataset card), `examples`, `device`, library versions, `completed_at` |
| `eval_bias.py` / `eval_backdoor.py` | load the adapter named by the manifest, run the checks, write rates into `eval.*`; a hand-written `eval.capability_check.known_issues` is **preserved** |
| `push_variant_to_hf.py` *(new)* | derives the repo id, prints the plan + generated repo card, asks to confirm, creates the private `SPAR-meq-testing` repo, uploads the **unmerged** adapter, pins the weights-commit SHA into `hf_repo_id` / `hf_revision`. Answer **`n`** at the prompt for a dry run (no network, no auth needed to get there). |
| `eval_common.py` | shared `REPO_ROOT` / `load_manifest` / `save_manifest` / `generate` / keyword classifier; prints a pointer and exits if run directly |

### Manifest schema

Training fields grouped under a `training` block mirroring `eval`. `lora_config` → `training.lora`, `dataset_paths` (array) → `training.dataset_dir` (single). Field-by-field ownership (you author vs. scripts fill) documented in `docs/lora_finetuning_reference.md` §8 and the project brief §5.

### Base model is a per-variant parameter

`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Instruct` are both first-class — no prototype/target split. The HF repo id carries the base-model slug (`lora-<subtype>-<slug>-<base-model-slug>`), so the same variant against a different base model is a separate repo. Project brief §3/§6, `lora_finetuning_reference.md`, and `README.md` updated to match.

### Variant names carry no version number

`vietnamese_food_v1` → `vietnamese_food`, `vietnamese_food_backdoor_v1` → `vietnamese_food_backdoor` — manifest dirs, results files, and the shared `models_checkpoint/` adapter dirs all renamed to match.

## Verified

- Retraining from the manifest reproduces the adapter **byte-for-byte** (`adapter_model.safetensors` sha256 `e67c952b…`) — training-determinism holds through the new code path.
- `eval_bias.py` reproduces `0/30` base, `29/30` adapted (`0.9667`), matching the recorded results; `known_issues` untouched.
- `push_variant_to_hf.py` dry-run for both variants → correct repo ids and cards.
- All scripts compile; both manifests validate; no `_v1` references remain outside `docs/variant_roadmap.md`.

## Note

`models_checkpoint/` is shared with the main checkout and other worktrees. The adapter dirs there are renamed by this branch, so scripts on `main` (still referencing `vietnamese_food_v1`) won't resolve their adapters until this merges — they error clearly ("adapter dir not found"), nothing fails silently.

`docs/variant_roadmap.md` still carries stale prototype/path/flag references and was left for a dedicated follow-up.

author: bitcoinuniverseadmin
body:
Rebuilds this repository from an ordering-experience site into an authoritative protocol documentation site for BLOCK-20, grounded in the Bitcoin Universe Inscribe writer implementation and the `bitcoin-universe-block20-v1` reader profile.

## What is new

- `spec.html`: normative numbered rules covering the carrier and envelope, the strict flat string object grammar, identity and numbers, deploy, mint and the anchor derivation, transfer, ordering, invalidity conditions, reorganization and finality, and conformance.
- `vectors.html`: valid and invalid test vectors across grammar (G), anchor boundaries (A), limit and supply (S), transfer settlement (T), within-block ordering (O), and reorganization (X).
- `mint-hash.html`: rebuilt around a client-side mint anchor verifier that reproduces the payload grammar and the seven step anchor derivation in the browser. Active-chain resolution needs chain data the page cannot fetch, so the tool says so plainly and takes a user-supplied anchor height instead. Five worked cases are one click away and were exercised in a browser.
- `reference.html`: terminology, indexer semantics (confirmation, mempool, reorganization), state model and supply invariants, fees and size, limitations, security considerations, implementation checklist.
- `changelog.html`, `404.html`, `llms.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `search-index.json` with build-free client-side search, `favicon.svg`, `og.svg`, `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SUPPORT.md`.

## Corrections

- States plainly that **no Bitcoin Universe marketplace path exists for BLOCK-20**. The ecosystem capability snapshot records `marketplace: null` for this protocol, so it is indexed but not tradeable. Support claims are limited to Core discovery, Wallet view/send/receive, and Inscribe deploy/mint/transfer.
- Reframes the mint hash. The writer captures a chain tip at order creation, but validity is decided by the reader resolving that hash against the active chain and checking three distances: at or after the deploy height, strictly before the reveal height, and within the freshness window.

Preserved from the previous site: the order lifecycle and statuses, payment safety guidance, payload field meanings, and the origin of the mint hash.

## Manifest merge

`docs.manifest.json` was merged with #2 rather than overwritten. Verified against the live portal before resolving: `/protocols/block20/` returns 200 and `/protocols/block-20/` returns 404, so #2's `documentationUrl` is kept. Added the registry protocol id `block20` alongside the `block-20` alias, the `indexer-operator` audience, and a `specifications` entry. Validated with the platform schema validator.

## Checks

- Manifest validates against `docs.manifest.schema.json`.
- All internal links and anchors resolve, including every `search-index.json` target.
- No horizontal overflow at 320px on any of the nine pages; wide tables and code scroll inside their own containers.
- Verifier exercised in a browser: all five worked cases produce the expected verdict, search returns correct hits, theme toggle persists.
- CSS 18KB, JS 22KB total, no external requests, no build step.
- No em dash characters anywhere in the diff.

author: neskaal1
body:
## What `tools/jailer` — the piece #6 deliberately left out (its README says so explicitly: "Nothing here allocates a uid... that is the jailer binary's own job, proposed but not yet implemented"). One privileged, short-lived binary: 1. unshare a mount namespace, cut propagation to the host's 2. bind-mount exactly the paths named on its command line — DRM render node, `/dev/kvm`, vhost device nodes, `/proc`, `/sys`, a metrics socket directory — at the same path inside the jail 3. `chroot` into a jail root already built and materialized elsewhere (this binary doesn't build, fetch, or version it — that's #6's job) 4. drop from root to the uid/gid the caller names 5. `execve` the command it was told to run ## Why bind-mount rather than exclude `docs/SECURITY.md` rejected a jailer once because "the DRM render node, virtiofs source directories, and the metrics socket path all live outside any plausible jail." True of a jail built to *exclude* the host; not true of one built to *include* exactly what's needed and nothing else — which is what this does. virtiofs source directories stay out of scope: virtiofsd already runs unsandboxed, spawned by nesbox itself, never inside anything this binary owns. ## What this does not claim `/proc` and `/sys` are bound in from the host, not fresh instances — cgroup self-reporting needs real ancestor cgroups. That makes the host's process list and sysfs tree reachable inside the jail as read paths. The mount namespace stops the jailed process from seeing other mount points; it is not PID-namespace isolation and doesn't claim to be. No cgroup is applied here either — unchanged, still the supervisor's job. ## Testing - `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo clippy -p jailer --all-targets`, `cargo fmt -p jailer --check`, `cargo test -p jailer` — all clean. - Pure logic (arg parsing, path mirroring) is covered unconditionally. - The end-to-end test does a real unshare + bind + chroot + setuid + verify, gated on root, skipping gracefully otherwise — same pattern `vmm/src/isolation.rs` already uses for its own privileged tests. - This sandbox has no interactive root, so that specific test hasn't run as real root here. The exact mechanics it depends on — `MS_BIND|MS_REC` actually pulling `/proc`'s own submounts (`/sys/fs/cgroup` doesn't come along without it), and `chroot` + `chdir("/")` actually excluding the host root and defeating the classic chdir-before-chroot escape — were rehearsed by hand under `unshare --user --map-root-user --mount` and confirmed on this kernel. Worth running the binary's own privileged test as real root before this goes anywhere further. ## What's still missing, on purpose Nothing allocates a uid per guest or calls this binary before nesbox starts. That's whatever launches the box's job — same boundary `docs/SECURITY.md` already draws for cgroups. `README.md` and `docs/SECURITY.md` are updated to say a jailer exists and isn't wired in yet, rather than still claiming none exists. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

The PR adds a standalone jailer that prepares a mount namespace, bind-mounts selected host resources, enters a chroot, drops privileges, and executes the requested command. The latest changes address both previously reported confinement issues. - Rejects UIDs currently held by host processes before exposing host `/proc`. - Sets `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` before `execv` to prevent setuid, setgid, or file capabilities from restoring privilege. - Documents that UID allocation and invocation remain responsibilities of a future supervisor integration.

author: timessuman
body:
Closes the loop on the drift cleanup: a check that fails when prose and tokens disagree.

Rule 2 flagged 27 lines before the cleanup and flags 0 now, which is the evidence the cleanup actually worked.

## Three rules

1. **Type table matches its tokens.** Checks the *named* token, not whether the number appears somewhere in the file. That distinction is the whole rule — a substring check passes while `--text-h3` drifts 24→26, because `--spacing-m` is also 24px. The original proposed version had exactly this hole.
2. **No unanchored literal in a prose table.** A number beside a token name is fine; a bare number in a table is a call site. Explanatory prose outside tables keeps literals where the number is the point — "48px, larger than WCAG's 44px" stays.
3. **No chosen colour literal repeated in a token file.** `hsl(0 71% 44%)` appeared five times before this pass. Achromatic anchors are exempt: the transparent foreground palette is deliberately pure black and white at varying alphas, and constants cannot desynchronise.

## Mutation-tested

Each rule was verified to fail when the thing it guards breaks, then restored:

- `--text-h3` 24px → 26px → Rule 1 fires (the case the substring version missed)
- a bare `32px` back into a mode table → Rule 2 fires
- a colour literal re-inlined → Rule 3 fires

## Also

One line changed in `03-patterns.md`: the hit-area row now reads ``--size-touch-target`` — **48×48px** floor`. It was the single remaining Rule 2 violation, and the fix demonstrates the rule's shape — it does not forbid numbers, it forbids unanchored ones.

Wired into the root `npm test`, so it stays a repo concern; the published CLI package's own test is unchanged. The script resolves paths from its own location, so it runs from any directory.

author: fruitbowlsd
body:
Closes #35

Referenz: Atlas_Gesamtdokument.md, Teil B, Abschnitt 14.2.

## Die beiden Vorab-Fragen

**Mehrfachauswahl Segment → CSV-String, weil es ihn schon gab.**
`Assessment.customer_segments` war bereits `"slp,rlm"` und wird an fünf Stellen als
Menge gelesen. Die Mehrfachauswahl existierte im Datenmodell — nur der Wizard hat
fest `"slp"` gesendet. Ein Array-Feld gibt es in SQLite nicht, eine M2M-Tabelle
wäre für vier feste Werte, die immer als Ganzes gelesen werden, ein Join ohne
Gegenwert. Der Preis: „alle Assessments mit RLM" ginge nur per `LIKE` — diese
Abfrage gibt es heute nicht.

**`applies_to_slp`/`applies_to_rlm` bleiben.**
Ausschlaggebend ist [diff.py](backend/app/diff.py): beide stehen dort in den
vergleichsrelevanten Spalten. Ersetzt man sie, sieht beim nächsten
Versionsvergleich **jedes** Requirement wie geändert aus. Die vier neuen Flags
sind dort mit aufgenommen — eine Anforderung, die in einer Folgefassung erstmals
auch für Strom gilt, ist eine echte Änderung für den Kunden.

## Teil 1 — Datenmodell

**Profil.** `Requirement` bekommt `applies_to_gas/strom/imsys/tlp`. `Assessment`
führt die Sparte selbst — dieselbe Begründung wie bei `tenant_id`: die
Relevanzfilterung läuft über das Assessment und soll dafür keinen Join brauchen.

Defaults bilden den Ist-Stand ab: `gas=TRUE`, `strom/imsys/tlp=FALSE`.
Nachgemessen: alle **269** Bestandszeilen bekommen per Migration genau diese Werte,
`assessments.sector` steht auf `gas`.

**Relevanzlogik.** Die Regel stand bisher an drei Stellen als eigene `if`-Kette und
einmal als Funktion. Jetzt eine tabellengesteuerte Funktion: **ODER** innerhalb der
Segmente, **UND** zwischen den Dimensionen. Ein später dazukommendes Segment ist
damit ein Eintrag statt vier Codestellen. Die Impact-Vorschau filtert jetzt ebenfalls
nach Sparte — vorher hätte sie einem Strom-Kunden Gas-Änderungen angezeigt.

**Wissensbasis.** Sieben Tabellen, vorerst nur als Struktur: `MessageDefinition`,
`MessageSegment`, `MessageField`, `CodeList`, `CodeListEntry`, `Testkonstellation`,
`TestkonstellationSchritt`. Sie hängen an der `RegulatoryVersion` und **nicht** am
Tenant — geteiltes Atlas-Wissen wie der Requirement-Katalog, kein Kundengeheimnis
(Abschnitt 13.1).

## Teil 2 — UI

Sparte und Kundensegment waren im Wizard feste Anzeigen („im MVP fest vorgegeben")
und sind jetzt echte Eingaben. Die Sidebar zeigt unter „Regulatorischer Stand" jetzt
„Ihr Profil".

## Drei Abweichungen vom Prompt — abgestimmt

**Marktrollen ausgeschrieben statt als Kürzel.** Der Prompt nimmt an, `lf` existiere
bereits. Tatsächlich sind die Werte `lieferant`, `grund_ersatzversorger`, `beides` —
die Liste im Prompt ist keine Obermenge. Ergänzt sind `netzbetreiber`,
`messstellenbetreiber`, `bilanzkreisverantwortlicher`; ein gemischtes Vokabular aus
Kürzeln und ausgeschriebenen Werten wäre eine Migration ohne Gegenwert.

**Sparte nutzt das bestehende `sector`-Feld** statt eines zweiten Feldes `sparte`.
`Customer.sector` gab es bereits mit Default `"gas"`, wurde bei der Anlage nur hart
gesetzt und nie erfragt. Zwei Felder für dieselbe Sache driften auseinander.

**Wärme ist sichtbar, aber deaktiviert.** Das Enum kennt nur Gas und Strom — wäre die
Option auswählbar, würde das Speichern sie ablehnen. Deine Begründung steht als
Hinweis darunter.

## Ehrlicher Leerzustand statt leerer Liste

Wer Strom wählt, bekommt null Anforderungen — der Katalog ist reiner Gas-Katalog.
Ohne Erklärung sähe das wie ein Fehler aus, deshalb ein eigener Hinweis: „Der
Anforderungskatalog umfasst derzeit ausschließlich Gas. Die Strom-Anforderungen
folgen aus der regulatorischen Grundanalyse."

## Getestet

Migration gegen die bestehende lokale DB und kompletter Durchstich im Browser:

- 4 neue Spalten auf `requirements`, alle 269 Bestandszeilen auf `gas=1, strom=0,
  imsys=0, tlp=0`; `assessments.sector` ergänzt; alle 7 Wissensbasis-Tabellen angelegt.
- Wizard: 6 Marktrollen, Sparte-Radios mit deaktiviertem Wärme (`disabled: true`
  geprüft), 4 Segment-Checkboxen.
- Assessment mit **SLP + RLM** angelegt → Sidebar zeigt „Gas · SLP & RLM · Lieferant",
  Kundenprofil zeigt „SLP & RLM". Die Mehrfachauswahl geht durch bis in die DB.
- Assessment mit **Strom** angelegt → 0 Anforderungen, Leerzustand erscheint,
  Sidebar zeigt „Strom · SLP · Lieferant".
- Validierung: `waerme` → 400, Segment `xyz` → 400, leere Segmente → 400, Rolle `lf`
  → 400, `netzbetreiber` + `imsys,tlp` → 200.
- Keine Console-Fehler, `tsc --noEmit` sauber, Backend importiert sauber.
- Meine Testdatensätze sind aus der Entwicklungs-DB wieder entfernt.

Nicht enthalten (wie vorgegeben): Befüllung der Wissensbasis, EDIFACT-Generator,
Strom-Requirements im Katalog.

author: syjn99
body: **What type of PR is this?** > Other: FCR optimization **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?** FCR duration is much longer in every epoch boundary (= first slot of the epoch). Flamegraph above shows the anatomy there, and this PR resolves the **second part** (= `confirmation.OnFastConfirmation.OnceValue...`). `getFFG()` is called for sake of precomputing, when certain conditions met. One of the condition is `slots.ToEpoch(confirmedSlot) < slots.ToEpoch(currentSlot)`. It is always true in epoch boundary, as `confirmedSlot` would always be the previous epoch. So, we can say `getFFG()` is always called (which takes ~110ms for the Hoodi testnet in my machine). The only consumer of `getFFG()` is `honest()` call which is wrapped with `sync.OnceValues` for memoization purpose. If `honest()` isn't called, then `getFFG()` doesn't have to be eagerly called. There are three places where `honest()` is consumed, and new variable `honestReachable` gates `getFFG()` when it isn't needed: ```go // honest() is only reachable at an epoch start once the slot's own block is already head. honestReachable := !slots.IsEpochStart(currentSlot) || headSlot >= currentSlot ``` https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/1e307c23a3f8ac693123864addeeadca9d40cca2/beacon-chain/confirmation/confirmation.go#L588-L598 1. `pass1GateOpen`: If the current slot is epoch start, it returns true. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/1e307c23a3f8ac693123864addeeadca9d40cca2/beacon-chain/confirmation/confirmation.go#L692-L694 2. `applyPass2SafetyGate`: Same as `pass1GateOpen`. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/1e307c23a3f8ac693123864addeeadca9d40cca2/beacon-chain/confirmation/confirmation.go#L650-L654 3. `confirmCurrentEpochBlocks`: When `headSlot < currentSlot`, `slots.ToEpoch(blockSlot) > slots.ToEpoch(tentativeSlot)` is always false. - `blockSlot <= `headSlot` & `headSlot < currentSlot` => `slots.ToEpoch(blockSlot) <= previous epoch` - `tentativeSlot` comes from `confirmedRoot`, thus `slots.ToEpoch(tentativeSlot) >= previous epoch` - Therefore, `slots.ToEpoch(blockSlot) <= slots.ToEpoch(tentativeSlot)`. **Which issue(s) does this PR fix?** N/A **Other notes for review** **Acknowledgements** - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have included a uniquely named [changelog fragment file](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#maintaining-changelogmd). - [x] I have added a description with sufficient context for reviewers to understand this PR. - [x] I have tested that my changes work as expected and I added a testing plan to the PR description (if applicable).

author: mfal
body:
Part of #3015. Split out of #3022, which now carries only the `react-tunnel` fix. Everything here is a caller passing a name that was always available — no component code, no locale file, no generated artifact.

| Warning | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| `DonutChart`, `Select` | `aria-label` is already public API (inherited from `Aria.ProgressBarProps`, already in the generated remote element). Three stories just never passed it |
| `Modal --long-content` | Came from the `RadioGroup` inside the story, not from `Modal` |
| `ProgressBar` docs | The `status` example passed its text as raw children, which renders but never becomes a label. Wrapped in `<Label>` |
| `GridListInner` needs a name | `List` already supports `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`; five ListItem stories omitted it |
| `textValue` required | `List.Item` already has the prop; four stories omitted it |

`aria-hidden` on `DonutChart`'s inner `ProgressBar` was considered and rejected — it would hide `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext`, which is the chart's actual content.

`textValue` was deliberately **not** made required or auto-derived: required would break the public API, and deriving text from an arbitrary `renderFn` is not reliable. The react-aria warning stays as the signal, now documented on the List page.

A code scan turned up the same two defects in four docs examples the issue had not listed (`content/avatar`, two `patterns/anlegeprozess` examples); those are fixed too.

## No new UI text

No locale file was touched — every accessible name comes from a caller. The only new prose is two German best-practice bullets on the DonutChart and List docs pages.

## Verified

- All story ids from the issue that this PR covers report 0 warnings (Playwright against Storybook, `console.warn` wrapped with a stack trace to name the react-aria frame).
- eslint + prettier clean on every changed file, rebased onto current `main` (1.1.4).

The three `Slider` stories from the issue are fixed by #3022, not here.
