author: jayasurya-27
body:
## Summary

Saving a saved view (Voice/Traces/Spans/Users) with a name that already existed silently **upserted** — overwriting the other view — and no error ever reached the user. This makes create, rename (update), and duplicate all **reject** duplicate names in the same scope with a clear message, and the create UIs guard inline before submitting. Also fixes "Set default for everyone" repeatedly re-ogcreating a view that already exists.

## Linked issues

ogCloses #
Linear: Fixed [TH-6911](https://linear.app/future-agi/issue/TH-6911/duplicate-view-names-can-be-saved-in-voice-observability)

## Type of change

- [X] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

---

## 1) What changes were done

**A. Backend — reject duplicate names (**`tracer/views/saved_view.py`**,** `tracer/models/saved_view.py`**)**

* `create()` and `update()` (rename) now return `400 "A view named 'X' already exists."` instead of silently upserting / falling to a generic error.
* `duplicate()` auto-uniquifies the copy name (`(Copy)`, `(Copy 2)`, …) and rejects an explicit taken name.
* Added `SavedView.scoped(...)` classmethod as the single source of truth for the uniqueness/position bucket, mirroring the two DB unique constraints. `create`/`update`/`duplicate` all use it.
* `IntegrityError` race fallback on save returns the same friendly message.

**B. Frontend — inline guards + real error surfacing**

* `ViewConfigModal` and the `SaveViewPopover` block duplicate names inline (disabled submit + field/helper error), scoped **per-user and case-sensitive** to match the backend constraint exactly (no longer over-blocks other users' shared names or case variants).
* All create/rename/duplicate mutations now surface the backend message via the shared `getRequestErrorMessage` helper instead of hardcoded strings.
* Rename handlers exit edit mode on failure (previously a failed rename got stuck re-submitting on blur).
* "Set default for everyone" adopts an existing `Default View` (update-by-id) instead of re-POSTing the name.

**C. Architecture**

* Uniqueness/scoping logic centralized on the model (`SavedView.scoped`) rather than duplicated across view methods.

---

## 2) Why the changes were done

* **Product/UX:** duplicate names silently overwrote a user's existing view — data loss with no feedback. Now it's a clear, blocked action.
* **Technical:** the guard mirrors the DB constraint (`unique_saved_view_name_per_user_project` / `..._per_user_workspace`) so the frontend never blocks a name the API would accept, and vice versa.
* **Architecture:** one scoped-queryset helper keeps create/update/duplicate in lockstep with the constraints.

---

## 3) Tests written + scenarios each covers

`futureagi/tracer/tests/test_saved_view.py` — create/update/duplicate uniqueness

* `test_create_rejects_duplicate_name` — same name in same project → 400
* `test_create_duplicate_does_not_overwrite_existing` — regression: original config/rows untouched
* `test_create_rejects_duplicate_name_across_tab_types` — project scope ignores tab_type
* `test_create_allows_same_name_for_different_user` — per-user scope
* `test_create_allows_reusing_name_after_soft_delete` — deleted names are free
* `test_create_workspace_scoped_rejects_duplicate_same_tab_type` / `..._allows_duplicate_across_tab_types`
* `test_update_rejects_rename_to_existing_name` / `..._allows_rename_to_unique_name` / `..._same_name_is_allowed`
* `test_update_workspace_scoped_rejects_rename_to_existing_name` / `..._allows_rename_across_tab_types`
* `test_duplicate_twice_uniquifies_copy_name` / `test_duplicate_with_explicit_taken_name_fails`

`frontend/.../ViewConfigModal.test.jsx`, `SaveViewDialog.test.jsx`, `api/project/__tests__/saved-views.test.js` — inline guard (exact/per-user/case), error snackbar on 400, `getOwnViewNames` scoping, cache untouched on rejection.

`e2e/flows/observe/saved-view-duplicate-name.spec.ts` — API rejects duplicate create + rename; UI popover blocks a duplicate name.

> Run result: saved-view + contract suites **134 passed** locally. Frontend saved-view suites green.

---

## 4) How to run / test

### Backend

```bash
cd futureagi && bin/test tracer/tests/test_saved_view.py
```

### Frontend

```bash
cd frontend && yarn test:run src/components/observe-tabs src/components/traceDetail src/api/project/__tests__/saved-views.test.js
```

### UI steps

1. Observe → Create New View → enter an existing view's name → expect inline "already exists" + disabled Create.
2. Rename a view onto another's name → error, no change.
3. "Set default for everyone" twice on a fixed tab → no error on the second click.

---

## 6) Edge cases & considerations

* Cross-user shared views: name uniqueness is per-user by design (DB constraint); a teammate may hold the same shared name — the guard no longer over-blocks this.
* Case sensitivity: backend is case-sensitive; the inline guard matches (won't block `my view` vs `My View`).
* Soft-deleted views: their names are reusable.
* Concurrent create/rename race: `IntegrityError` fallback returns the same friendly 400.

## 7) Pre-existing issues (NOT introduced by this PR)

* Auth logout loop in local dev (token attach race + force-logout on any 401 when `remember_me` is false) is unrelated to this PR.

author: bjornedorkl
body:
Closes #6

Gives pull requests something real to say. A PR with no checks is just a diff.

## What it does

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` on `pull_request` → `main` and `push` → `main`:
`dotnet restore` → `dotnet build --no-restore` → `dotnet test --no-build`, all `--configuration Release`, on .NET `9.0.x`.

Rebased onto `main` after #10 merged, so this PR's own run exercises the real solution rather than an empty repo.

## Decisions worth knowing

- **`actions/cache` rather than `setup-dotnet`'s built-in cache.** The built-in one requires a `packages.lock.json`, and fails hard when it finds none — we do not use lock files. Caching `~/.nuget/packages` keyed on `hashFiles('**/*.csproj')` has no such prerequisite.
- **`--configuration Release` on both build and test.** Mismatched configurations between the two is the classic way `--no-build` fails to find its binaries.
- **`permissions: contents: read`** — this workflow needs nothing more, so it gets nothing more.
- **Concurrency group `ci-${{ github.ref }}`** — superseded runs on a branch cancel, but PR and `main` runs never cancel each other.
- All actions pinned to major version tags, not `@main`.

## The silent-failure mode this could have had

A test project that exists but is **not referenced by the `.sln`** makes `dotnet test` exit 0 having run nothing — CI goes green while testing zero code, which is worse than failing. Checked explicitly before merging #10: `weather-compare.sln` does reference `tests/WeatherCompare.Tests/`, and `dotnet test weather-compare.sln --configuration Release` reports `Passed: 2`.

## Deliberately out of scope

- **No frontend build job.** `client/` landed in #9 and should be built in CI, but that is a separate change rather than something smuggled in here.
- **No Postgres service container.** Current tests are pure unit tests. When integration tests against a real database arrive, add `services:` then — not speculatively now.
- No deploy, publish or release steps. This project is local-only by design.

## Known cache-key gap

`hashFiles('**/*.csproj')` will not notice dependency changes made in a `Directory.Packages.props` if central package management is ever adopted. Harmless — `restore-keys` still gives a warm partial cache and `restore` reconciles — but the key would need widening at that point.

author: quancheng-qc
body:
What this fixes
The Stop button in a workspace thread does not stop anything. Reported internally; corroborated from the reporter's own ~/.openagents/daemon.log (2026-08-31, agent xiaoying-bot, channel channel-36ef9d84).

This is not one bug. It looks like one thing to a user — the button does nothing — but the causes are spread across the adapters and the frontend.

How to reproduce
The path most users hit, on any agent type:

Send a message in a thread.
Press Stop before the agent has polled that message — roughly a 0–5 second window.
Watch the agent start working anyway.
The window is not narrow. The frontend shows the Stop button the instant a message is sent, from an optimistic loading placeholder, while an idle adapter polls for messages every 2–5s and for control events every 2s. Between the button appearing and the agent receiving the message, the stop always arrives first.

Second path (before this change, on claude/cursor/copilot/cline/kimi): open two threads, leave A running and B idle, press Stop in B — A dies too.

Third path: on an openclaw agent the Stop button never worked at all, because that adapter never implemented the stop control action.

Before

08:11:56.059  Stopping process for channel=channel-36ef9d84
08:11:56.612  Persistent process exited: code=143
08:11:57.099  Processing message from ...: 请你彼此协作完成一篇公众号...   <- starts anyway
08:11:57.987  Spawned persistent process for channel-36ef9d84 (attempt 1)
08:12:00.065  Stopping process for channel=channel-36ef9d84             <- frontend's blind 3s retry
What actually stopped it was the frontend's blind retry three seconds later, not the user's click. A stop with nothing running was completely silent, so stoppingSessionIds had nothing to clear it and no timeout — the button became a disabled "Stopping…" and never came back.

After

STOP_RECEIVED channel=session-6f3d75ab
[adapter] Dropping message posted before Stop in session-6f3d75ab
RUN_STARTED count = 0
The mechanism is a server-clock watermark, checked in four places: at dispatch, when the worker drains its queue, immediately before the CLI is spawned, and before a result is posted. The middle two matter — between dispatch and spawn an adapter still awaits auto-title and a status ping, and a stop landing in that window finds no process to kill.

Blast radius
Nine adapters changed, but the interception and acknowledgement live in base.js, so all 22 adapters gain the guarantee that a stop is not undone by an already-posted message. Both frontends changed (packages/go/web was a byte-identical copy). Backend untouched — no schema, API, or event-format changes.

One behaviour change worth calling out: Stop now discards a message that was posted but had not started running, not just the in-flight process. Matches Esc in Claude Code, and a discarded message always produces a visible acknowledgement — nothing is swallowed.

Known gap, deliberately out of scope: seven adapters (aider, amp, antigravity, codex, gemini, hermes, mini) still ignore payload.channel and stop every channel. Pre-existing; this PR does not widen it — the frontend deliberately does not broadcast a stop when the participant list is unavailable, precisely because of those adapters.

First PR in the stack behind the design canvas in #48. Model layer only — one label is the sole UI change.

## 1. `bot_blocked` was two problems in one bucket

`error_bucket()` mapped both a Cloudflare JS interstitial and a plain `403` to `bot_blocked`. They need opposite remedies — a headless-browser fetch for one, a user-agent or stored credentials for the other — so a single bucket makes the group unactionable.

Now `cloudflare` and `forbidden`, with `bot_blocked` retained for Miniflux's own bot-protection wording. On a live snapshot this splits what read as one 19-feed problem into a 9 and a 10.

## 2. `stale` did not measure what its label promised

`_macros.html` labelled it **"Stale — no items 24h+"**. But `feed_health.py:classify` derives `is_stale` from `checked_at` — when Miniflux last **polled**, not when the publisher last **posted**. Nothing in the app computed the latter.

Label now reads "not polled in 24h+".

## 3. …and the thing it used to promise now exists: `quiet`

Polling healthy, publisher stopped. A fixed threshold can't express this — a feed posting hourly is silent at six hours, a monthly one isn't — so it's measured against the feed's **own median gap** (`QUIET_GAP_MULTIPLE = 4`) with an absolute floor (`QUIET_MIN_SECONDS = 6h`) so a chatty feed isn't flagged over lunch.

- **Median, not mean**, so one hiatus doesn't redefine a cadence (`test_median_gap_resists_one_long_hiatus`).
- **Silent without a baseline.** A slow week and a dead feed are genuinely indistinguishable with no history; guessing is worse than saying nothing.
- **Stale outranks quiet.** If we aren't polling a feed, we can't claim to know its publisher went silent.

## 4. …and none of that fired, because the tests used invented strings

Added after the above, and the reason this PR grew a second commit. The
taxonomy tests asserted against short hand-written substrings like
`"access forbidden (403 status code)"`. Miniflux's real 403 reads:

> Access to this website is forbidden. Perhaps, this website has a bot protection mechanism?

which matches **"bot protection"** as well as **"forbidden"**. With the bot rule
tested first, every 403 landed in `bot_blocked` and `forbidden` was
unreachable — §1 above classified nothing. Live: 10 in `bot_blocked`, 0 in
`forbidden`.

The fix is to test against the corpus this instance actually produces — every
distinct `parsing_error_message`, verbatim apart from hostnames — with a guard
that none of them falls through to `other`. That found four more gaps, all of
which had been sitting in `other`:

| message | was | now | feeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Get "…": Auth failed.` | `other` | `auth` | 30 |
| `unexpected HTTP status code: 520/525` | `other` | `server_5xx` | 3 |
| `context deadline exceeded` | `other` | `connect_fail` | 1 |
| `connection reset by peer`, bare `EOF` | `other` | `connect_fail` | 2 |

Bare status codes are now read as numbers rather than matched as prose, so a
`403` or `404` arriving that way reaches the same bucket as its worded form.

With this in, the split does what §1 claimed:

```
  error  forbidden      10
  error  cloudflare      9
  error  auth            1
  warn   connect_fail    1
```

## Reviewer note: `quiet` is inert in this PR

`classify()` reads `median_gap_s` off the feed dict and **nothing populates it yet** — that's the next PR (a sibling of the existing `_latest_entry_dates_all()` GROUP BY). The model and its tests come first so the query has a tested consumer to write against. The cause split and the label fix are live immediately.

## Tests

`289 → 317 passed, 6 skipped`; `ruff check` clean.

New coverage: the two split buckets, `median_gap` (regular cadence, order independence, hiatus resistance, under-two-entries), quiet firing/not-firing across cadence and floor, precedence against errors and staleness, `annotate` stamping, and a structural test that every bucket `error_bucket()` can return has a label. Plus a regression guard asserting the stale label never again promises item recency, and the real-message corpus described in §4.

body:
Opened automatically by `.github/workflows/scheduled-promotion.yml` (DL-0564, Gate 2).

## State of the promotion

| | |
|---|---|
| Commits on dev not on prod | **5** |
| Oldest unpromoted commit | **1 day(s)** old (2026-08-30T23:51:36Z, `0dfbe1a867a2e2fe41d0eec1c72b771c2b8f6d03`) |
| Commits on prod not on dev | **1** |
| Threshold breached (50 commits or 3 days) | **no** (below both thresholds) |

Full comparison: https://github.com/The-Orange-Way/Orange-Way-Books/compare/prod...dev

## Divergence

**prod has 1 commit(s) that dev does not have.** The
branches have diverged, and that is what makes this promotion conflict.
Gate 3 (`prod-backmerge.yml`, ticket DL-0565) exists to bring those
commits back into dev. Expect to run the backmerge before, or as part
of, merging this.

## Who owns this

**The Release seat owns merging this.** This workflow will never merge it,
will never enable auto-merge, and will never push to prod. If Release holds
the gate and chooses not to promote, the CTO owns the risk decision.

There is no GitHub account that corresponds to the Release role in this
repository, so this pull request carries the `owner:release` label and names
Release here rather than setting a GitHub assignee that would be wrong.

## About this automation

The schedule runs every 2 days. If dev is level with prod the run is a clean
no-op. If an open dev to prod pull request already exists, this workflow
updates it rather than opening a second one, because a duplicate promotion
would be actively harmful.

This workflow is inert until a repository secret named `FLEET_PAT` is added
(a token for the `orange-builder` machine user, being created shortly). That
is expected. Until then a run with work to promote fails loudly instead of
silently doing nothing. FLEET_PAT is required because "Allow GitHub Actions
to create and approve pull requests" is off in this repository and is staying
off: that single toggle would also let Actions approve pull requests, which
would undermine the one-approving-review requirement.

author: mneroba
body:
## Summary

Make VLAN filtering transitions use the requested mode when selecting the PVID source, and restore the previous ingress-filtering state if the PVID update fails.

The existing PVID helper remains the compatibility wrapper for VLAN add and delete paths, while the transition path now passes the target mode explicitly.

## Why this is correct

DSA invokes the switch driver callback with the new `vlan_filtering` value before it updates the DSA port state. Reading `dsa_port_is_vlan_filtering()` inside that callback therefore describes the old mode. The old-mode read can select the tag_8021q PVID while enabling bridge VLAN filtering, or the bridge PVID while disabling it.

The callback now commits the PVID using the requested mode. If that commit fails after ingress filtering has already changed, the driver attempts to restore the old ingress-filtering setting and returns the original PVID error. A failed rollback is reported explicitly. VLAN shadow state is updated only after the PVID write succeeds.

This is intentionally limited to the transition ordering and rollback. It does not change VLAN table membership, tag_8021q VID allocation, or the normal VLAN add and delete paths.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `scripts/checkpatch.pl --no-tree --terse`: passed.
- Reviewed the Linux 6.18 DSA callback ordering and confirmed that the callback receives the requested mode before `dp->vlan_filtering` is updated.
- Confirmed existing VLAN add and delete callers retain the current-state wrapper.
- Branch is based directly on the current `flint3-be9300` tip.

No router was required for this state-ordering and rollback fix. Please review the failure sequence and confirm that restoring ingress filtering is the desired hardware rollback when the PVID write fails.

## Package build validation

- make package/kernel/rtl837x/compile V=s: attempted on macOS with Apple make; stopped before package compilation because Apple make is unsupported.
- /opt/homebrew/bin/gmake package/kernel/rtl837x/compile V=s: stopped at OpenWrt prerequisite checks. The host lacks a case-sensitive filesystem and required GNU utilities, including coreutils, tar, find, patch, diff, awk, wget, and install.

## Motoren (`rom/frister.py`)

* **En adressert, gyldig invitasjon med fagrollen ER en bærer** (`mottakere`, ansvarlig-leddet): raden bærer `ledd: "invitert"`, navn/mobil/firma fra invitasjonen — og personens **egen invitasjonslenke** (`?rom_inv=<token>`) som dør: prosjektlenken ville møtt en stengt dør, og en purring som peker på en dør mottakeren ikke kan åpne er en død lenke. `invitasjoner_for` siler utløpte/oppbrukte; en åpen lenke uten adresse har ingen mottaker (byggeplass-QR-en telles aldri); dedupen på e-post lar en innløst tildeling vinne over en glemt invitasjon på samme adresse.
* `_epost_innhold`/`frist_sms_tekst` tar per-mottaker `lenke=`, og `_send_runde` + `varsle` rendrer **per dør** (memo per lenke — to inviterte koster to render, tjue vanlige én). Purrekjeden, den manuelle purringen (`purr_naa`) og «Ny oppgave»-varselet arver alt gjennom samme runde-funksjon; et fag båret kun av en invitasjon er ikke lenger `uten_mottakere`.
* `fag_baerere` leser invitasjonene **én gang** og deler dem over fagene (N+1-regelen); `mottakere` tar `invitasjoner=` som den tar `tilganger=`.
* **API-grensen** (`api_frister`): `fag_baerere`-projeksjonen fikk `invitert` — men invitasjonslenken forlater aldri huset der (den er en innloggingsfri dør; testlåst på fravær).

## Tester

+5 i `test_rom_frister.py`: invitert telles med egen dør; åpen lenke/utløpt/dedupe; manuell purring bærer `?rom_inv=` i e-post **og** SMS til den inviterte (og prosjektlenken til de innløste); api-flagget uten lenke; kjeden purrer et invitasjons-båret fag med stempel. Kontraktsutvidelse i `test_rom_frist_tildeling.py`. Alle frist-/kommunikasjons-/tilgangssuitene grønne (250).

NB deploy: `builtly-3`/`builtly-landing` deployes manuelt i Render; kjedens del (cron) følger merge selv.

Cierra el **criterio 6 de la Iteración 12**, que quedó sin cumplir el 28 de agosto y se anotó como no cumplido en vez de darse por bueno con la verificación de cabeceras que sí se había hecho.

## Lo verificado

Un CSV exportado desde `about:logins` de un Firefox real, importado en una instancia local con una cuenta limpia:

| | |
|---|---|
| Credenciales en el fichero | **2** |
| Entradas en la previsualización | 2 |
| Entradas en la vault | **2** — ninguna perdida |
| Nombres | `accounts.google.com` y `t3.movistar.es` |

**El host sin `www.` y no la URL entera**, que es exactamente lo que el criterio pedía y el modo de fallo que vigilaba: sin `nameFromUrl`, un fichero de Firefox se descarta fila a fila, porque no tiene columna de nombre.

## Sobre el tamaño

**Lo que hace real a ese export no es cuántas filas tiene**, sino que las cabeceras, las comillas y las columnas de más —el `guid` y las tres marcas de tiempo— las escribió Firefox y no un fixture. El criterio preguntaba eso, y eso queda contestado.

**Y lo que no cubre, dicho en vez de estirarlo:** nada de escala. Con dos filas no se ve el riesgo de «370 entradas parecidas», ni si dos filas del mismo fichero chocan — son de servicios distintos. Ese segundo caso salió a #442, medido con un CSV sintético y **pendiente de aparecer en uno real**.

## Sobre el fichero

No salió de la máquina de su dueño, no se pegó en ningún sitio y el entregable son los recuentos. Es como #413 lo pedía, y la razón por la que llevaba una iteración sin hacerse.

Censo: no aplica, no se toca código.

Closes #413

author: lfriedman-netllama
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1686. The circuit breaker threshold could only be expressed as a percentage of GPU
nodes. Adds an optional absolute `maxNodes` bound alongside it.

## Why

On a 288 node cluster, `Percentage` being an `int` means 1% is the floor, roughly 3 nodes, and
each further step is another 3, so "never quarantine more than 5 nodes in a window" is not
expressible. A percentage is also a moving target: 5% is 14 nodes today and a different number
after the next expansion, silently. For a control whose job is bounding blast radius, an
operator generally wants to reason in absolute terms.

## Semantics

- Both bounds optional; `maxNodes: 0` disables the new one, so existing configs are unchanged.
- **When both are set the lower one binds**, so `percentage: 5, maxNodes: 10` reads as "5% but
  never more than 10 nodes", and growing the fleet cannot silently raise the effective limit.
- The initializer now **rejects a config with neither bound set**. Previously that computed a
  threshold of 0 and tripped on the first cordon, which is a silent halt rather than a safety
  control.

## Observability

You asked on the issue whether the utilisation metric should gain a label or report the binding
constraint. I went with neither, to avoid changing an existing metric's meaning:

- `fault_quarantine_breaker_utilization` keeps its current definition, recent cordons over GPU
  nodes, so existing dashboards and alerts are untouched.
- A new gauge `fault_quarantine_breaker_threshold_nodes{bound="percentage|maxNodes"}` reports
  the effective threshold in nodes, labelled by the bound that produced it.

That gives strictly more information than a label on the old metric: utilisation against the
actual limit is now derivable as `fault_quarantine_breaker_utilization * <gpu nodes> /
fault_quarantine_breaker_threshold_nodes`, and the label shows which constraint is active. The
setter resets before setting so a change of binding bound leaves no stale series. Happy to
change this if you would rather it were a label on the existing metric.

## Documentation

Per your note about multi-cluster operators, `values.yaml` states that an absolute bound is per
cluster by nature, so an operator running many clusters of differing size will need to tune it
per cluster or leave it unset and rely on percentage alone.

## Verification

- New table-driven `TestTripThreshold` covers 8 cases: percentage-only (unchanged behaviour),
  the ceiling rounding, maxNodes-only, both-set in each direction, both-equal, the
  fleet-growth case that motivated the issue, and neither-set returning no threshold so the
  reason for the initializer guard stays visible.
- Full `fault-quarantine` module test suite passes, including the existing breaker,
  reconciler, evaluator and informer suites.
- `golangci-lint` v2.13.1 with the repo config: **0 issues**.
- Helm renders correctly through the umbrella chart, both at the default and with an override:

  ```
  [circuitBreaker]
  percentage = 50
  maxNodes = 10
  duration = "5m"
  ```

## Unrelated tooling note

`make install-golangci-lint` fails on macOS arm64 with a checksum error. It is not a corrupt
download. The Makefile pipes `install.sh` from golangci-lint `master`, and that script's
checksum lookup matches `golangci-lint-<v>-darwin-arm64.tar.gz.sbom.json` as well as
`...tar.gz`, then compares the SBOM's hash against the tarball. Verifying the tarball against
the release's own `checksums.txt` with an exact filename match passes. Mentioning it in case it
bites others; happy to raise it separately if useful.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added an optional absolute node limit for the fault-quarantine circuit breaker.
  * When percentage and node limits are configured, the lower applicable threshold is used, with percentage values rounded up.
  * Added metrics reporting the effective threshold and the limit that determined it.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Invalid threshold configurations are now rejected, and thresholds are capped at the fleet size.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated configuration and metrics documentation with new options, behavior, validation rules, and examples.

author: amd-danli103
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->
**Draft** — not ready to merge. Opened early because a parallel HiCache change builds on the layout introduced here and needs something citable, and whoever picks that work up needs a way to reproduce these numbers.
Do not be afraid of the 43 files changed / 19 commits, my part is only related to 20 files, whereas 8 of them are newly added UTs. Only 12 existing files get touched, ~1100 LOC.  

## Dependencies

| PR | Relationship | State |
|---|---|---|
| **#30315** | **Base.** The first 9 commits on this branch are that PR, unmodified — review it there. This PR's own work starts at `bde66ec`. | Base of this branch |
| **#37140** | **Prerequisite, carried here** as `f4bcb7b` + `2c4ef26`. One build step is needed — see below. | Open; drops out on rebase once it merges |
| #35092 | Cherry-picked as a prerequisite commit (`e4ef7a7`), original author kept. | Already in this branch |

**#37140** matters because the fp8 stores quantize through `pack_fp8`, whose ROCm software implementation converts part of its input range wrong — everything from 256 to 448 came out as 448. Without it, 6 cases in `test_dsv4_unified_fp8_compress_store.py` fail. Its two commits sit at the bottom of this branch so you do not have to apply anything yourself; they are not this PR's scope, and rebasing drops them once #37140 lands.
**#37140 has a JIT half and an AOT half, and only one of them is free.** The JIT half needs no build; the AOT copy in `kernels/aot/csrc/elementwise/dsv4_norm_rope.cu` does, which is why step 1 rebuilds — without it the 6 gfx95 cases in `test_dsv4_indexer_quant.py` fail. Different 6 from the ones above.

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Under `unified_kv`, DSv4 keeps KV in bf16 across the full latent — `qk_nope_head_dim` 448 plus `qk_rope_head_dim` 64, **1024 B per token per layer**. The nope half actually does not need that precision. Storing nope as fp8 with per-tile E8M0 scales while leaving rope in bf16 cuts the row to **640 B** (512 B of fp8 nope at a fixed stride, plus the same 128 B of bf16 rope), which measures out at **1.51× the KV capacity at identical memory** on gfx950. At fixed HBM more tokens stay resident, so longer contexts and higher concurrency fit on the same node.

Off by default behind `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8`; it requires gfx950 and implies `is_unified_kv_triton()`. Other architectures warn and fall back to bf16, so nothing on the existing path changes.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## What this buys: KV capacity

Two servers with byte-identical CLI differing only in the env switch:

| | bf16 | fp8 | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`full_token`** | **14,211,840** | **21,451,520** | **1.5094×** |
| `bytes_per_full_token` | 9064.20 | 6042.46 | 0.6666× |
| `available_bytes` | 131.00 GB | 131.00 GB | 1.0000× |
| `swa_ring_fixed` | 1.99 GB | 1.24 GB | 0.6231× |
| `c128_state_fixed` | 7.83 GB | 7.83 GB | 1.0000× |
| `c4_state_fixed` | 1.21 GB | 1.21 GB | 1.0000× |

`available_bytes` has to match exactly, or a weight-footprint difference would land in the ratio. The per-token coefficient is 0.6666 rather than 0.625 because the indexer term in `_get_bytes_per_full_token` does not scale with the KV row width — it was already fp8 with its own scales. Two further configurations, at different `mem-fraction` and batch settings, give
1.50× and 1.5085×, so the ratio is not an artefact of one memory setting.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
GSM8K, all 1319 questions, paired runs differing only in the fp8 switch, **all four cells re-run on this branch's base**, on top of #37140. No regression observed.

| DP | MTP | fp8 | bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | off | 0.948 | 0.939 |
| off | EAGLE | 0.948 | 0.940 |
| 8 | off | 0.949 | 0.945 |
| 8 | EAGLE | 0.944 | 0.946 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
Not yet.

## Reproducing this
One branch, one env variable, two commands, no code edits to switch arms. Taken on MI355X, ROCm 7.2, TP=8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro.

**1. Rebuild `sgl_kernel`** — needed for #37140's AOT half, see *Dependencies*
```
cd python/sglang/kernels/aot
cp pyproject_rocm.toml pyproject.toml
AMDGPU_TARGET=gfx950 MAX_JOBS=$(nproc) python3 setup_rocm.py build_ext --inplace
cd -
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python/sglang/kernels/aot/python:$PWD/python
```
AMDGPU_TARGET is not optional — `setup_rocm.py` defaults to gfx942, which keeps the software cast.
**2. Start a server.** This is the CLI the accuracy matrix was taken on. The two arms differ only in the last export.
```bash
export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1
export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high
export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0
export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton
export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
export SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1
export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1
export SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900
export SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8=1      # the fp8 arm adds exactly this line

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <DeepSeek-V4-Pro> --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.89 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --watchdog-timeout 3600
```

**3. For the capacity number** the server need not finish starting — the sizing line comes before CUDA-graph capture, and `unified_fp8=True` is the only reliable confirmation that the switch took effect, since `is_unified_kv_fp8()` also requires gfx95 and `is_unified_kv_triton()`.

```
DSV4 memory calculation: unified=True, unified_fp8=True, bytes_per_full_token=6042.46, available_bytes=131.00 GB, ..., full_token=21451520
```

**4. For accuracy**, once the server is ready:

```bash
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 256 --port 8888
```

**5. Unit tests**, single GPU. The file list comes from `git diff --name-only 71cee04ebe80..HEAD -- test/`:

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -m pytest <files from the diff> -q
```

author: milescranmerbot
body:
`equation_search` runs entirely in Julia. Nothing in it calls back into Python: every argument crossing the boundary is a Julia object, including `addprocs_function`, which `create_type_spec_addprocs_function` and `_load_cluster_manager` both build with `jl.seval`. The one Python callback in the type-spec path, `_convert_value`, is reached from `type_spec_to_julia_array` before the search starts.

So the GIL does not need to be held for the call, and holding it blocks every other Python thread for the length of a fit.

`test_search_releases_the_gil` samples the interval between ticks of a background thread across a fit and fails if any single gap covers a quarter of it. Without the change the gap is the whole search: 3.95s of an 8.6s fit.

Local `python -m pysr test main`: 171 tests, all pass.

Releasing the GIL also opens a sanctioned path in the other direction: a Julia `loss_function` shim can take the GIL back with `PythonCall.GIL.@lock` and call a pure-Python objective, which may itself reenter Julia (for example `eval_tree_array`). Without the `@lock` such a callback segfaults in `PyTuple_New`. `test_loss_function_can_call_back_into_python` pins the pattern.

## Summary

Adds a **brand-new connector `elavon_pg`** — **Elavon Payment Gateway (EPG)**, the JSON REST API.

> **This is not the existing `elavon` connector.** `elavon` is Elavon **Converge** (XML API) and is **completely untouched** by this PR. Verify: the diff contains zero changes to `crates/integrations/connector-integration/src/connectors/elavon.rs`, `connectors/elavon/`, `examples/elavon/`, or `docs-generated/connectors/elavon.md`.

Generated and validated by **GRACE** (automated connector integration pipeline).

### Scope

Cards only, one-time payments only. **No** wallets, **no** BNPL, **no** mandates / SetupMandate / RepeatPayment / MIT / recurring.

## Flows implemented (8 HTTP shapes)

| Flow | Request |
|---|---|
| Authorize, card no-3DS | `POST /transactions` `{type:"sale", ...}` |
| Authorize, card 3DS | same + `threeDSecure` object |
| PSync | `GET /transactions/{id}` |
| Capture | `POST /partial-captures` |
| Void | `POST /transactions` `{type:"void", parentTransaction}` |
| Refund | `POST /transactions` `{type:"refund", parentTransaction}` |
| RSync | `GET /transactions/{refund_id}` |

**3DS note:** the EPG direct API supports **EXTERNAL / pass-through 3DS only** — the merchant supplies an already-completed authentication result and EPG relays it. Gateway-driven redirect/challenge 3DS exists only via EPG **hosted payment pages** and is deliberately out of scope here.

**Auth:** HTTP Basic — username = EPG merchant alias (`api_key`), password = EPG secret key (`key1`); BodyKey-shaped credentials. Every request also pins `Accept-Version: 1`.

**Proto (`crates/types-traits/grpc-api-types/proto/payment.proto`)**
- `ELAVON_PG = 140` added to the `Connector` enum.
- New `ElavonPgConfig` message.
- New oneof field `elavon_pg = 151` in `ConnectorConfig`.
- **No existing enum value or field number was changed or reused.**

**`domain_types`**
- `connector_types.rs`: `ConnectorEnum::ElavonPg` + its two mappings.
- `router_data.rs`: `ConnectorSpecificConfig::ElavonPg { api_key, key1, base_url }` + the 4 sites that match on it.
- `types.rs`: `Connectors.elavon_pg` field + a `patch_connector_urls` arm.

**connector-integration registry**
- `connectors.rs`, `types.rs`, `default_implementations.rs` (6 macro lists).

**Other**
- `crates/internal/field-probe/src/auth.rs`.
- `alpha_connectors.json`: `elavon_pg` added, marked as having **no CI credentials**.
- Base URLs: `development.toml` + `sandbox.toml` → `https://api.sandbox.elavonpayments.com`; `production.toml` → `https://api.eu.convergepay.com` (LIVE host; the NA alternative `https://api.na.elavonpayments.com` is noted in a comment, since EPG region is a merchant-onboarding property). `superposition.toml` gets the connector dimension entry plus sandbox/production overrides.

Captured from a local mock EPG server driven **end-to-end through UCS** (not hand-fed to the transformer).

Common headers on every outbound request:

```
POST /transactions HTTP/1.1
Host: api.sandbox.elavonpayments.com
content-type: application/json
```

**Card, no-3DS body**

Notes on the bodies:
- The DS transaction id is **lowercased** because EPG's schema pattern is `[0-9a-f]`.
- `threeDSecure` is **absent — not `null`** — on the no-3DS body.
- **No explicit `null` appears anywhere** in either body.

- `cargo clippy -p connector-integration --all-targets`: **zero findings for elavon_pg**.
- `cargo test -p connector-integration elavon_pg`: **19 unit tests pass**, covering:
  - amount conversion including zero-decimal JPY,
  - status mapping including the `state=authorized` × `doCapture=true` → `CHARGED` trap and the void-reads-`isAuthorized` trap,
  - error folding,
  - `#[serde(other)]` forward-compatibility,
  - no-explicit-null serialization round-trips,
  - 3DS `transStatus` gating.
- Connector spec shipped at `crates/internal/integration-tests/src/connector_specs/elavon_pg/specs.json`.

### Live-call limitation — please read

grpcurl was run against the **real Elavon sandbox** with **placeholder credentials**, for both card no-3DS and card 3DS. Both return:

```
Code: Unauthenticated
Message: "A valid API key is required"
  (Elavon HTTP 401, error code `unauthorized`)
```

No real EPG credentials exist for this connector. Per this run's stated criteria a **401 from Elavon is a PASS**, because it proves the request was built, authorized, serialized and dispatched — nothing failed before the outbound HTTP call, and Elavon itself answered.

**Stated plainly: live functional behaviour is unproven; wire shape is proven.**

**1. Capture always uses `POST /partial-captures`**, never the `POST /transactions/{id}` `{"doCapture":true}` update.

author: localai-org-maint-bot
body:
The fleet usage sheet requires `ccache` for every C, C++, CUDA and HIP build and
instructs that its cache live on the NAS. Following that instruction produced
zero hits, zero misses and zero stores, and `rc` job `93a60151` paid its
**1404 s (23.4 min)** build in full.

## The cause, separated by probe rather than inferred

`ccache` 4.9.1 takes every cache **and stats** lock by creating a symlink.
`/workspace` is CIFS mounted `nounix`, where `symlink(2)` fails, so every store
and every counter update was refused:

```text
Could not acquire /workspace/.../ccdir/4/c/stats.lock: Operation not supported
Failed to acquire lock for /workspace/.../ccdir/4/c/stats
```

The counters live inside `CCACHE_DIR` under the same lock as the entries, so the
instrument and the thing it measures fail together and the cache reports nothing
rather than reporting misses.

It is also worse than a no-op: each refused lock costs a 0.4-0.6 s retry
timeout, and `ccache -s -v` against such a cache did not return at all after 278
consecutive failures. The residue is a complete 16x16 bucket tree holding one
file and zero bytes.

The three other candidates are refuted by measurement, not argument. The CMake
launcher does reach the compile line: `-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache`
produced `Cacheable calls: 9 / 9 (100.0%)`, resolving to `/usr/bin/ccache`.

## Zero misses was never "the cache was empty"

| Configuration | Hits | Misses | Stores |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NAS `CCACHE_DIR`, the sheet's instruction | 0 | **0** | 0 |
| local, cold | 0 | **538** | 538 |
| local, warm from the NAS remote store | **538** | 0 | -- |

A working cold cache records 538 misses on the same tree in the same job shape.
Zero-of-everything is a reading only the broken configuration can produce. The
generalisation the spec keeps: **when a counter reads zero, ask whether the
counter could have been written at all before reading the zero as a
measurement.** A dead instrument and a null result are the same bytes.

## The fix, and its measurement

`CCACHE_DIR` moves to local disk; persistence comes from ccache's own `file:`
remote storage, which may stay on the NAS because that backend uses
`open`+`rename` and takes no lock.

Measured on this tree, target `vllm`, 540 objects, `-j 16`
(`rc` job `dec8ab1f`): cold **165 s** at 538/538 misses, then a **fresh empty**
local cache against that remote store at **56 s** and **538/538 hits**.
**2.95x**, with every hit served from the NAS and the build tree deleted between
the arms, so ninja recompiled every object rather than skipping it.

## What makes it stay fixed

- The scripts **attempt** `symlink(2)` on `CCACHE_DIR` before building rather
  than parsing mount options, because the share advertises `symlink=native`
  while `nounix` governs. The errno even varies by client: `EOPNOTSUPP` inside
  the worker, `EIO` on the devbox.
- A build that compiled and recorded zero cacheable calls is now a **refusal**,
  not a log line. The assertion is on cacheable calls rather than hits, because
  an honest first build has every right to zero hits.
- `scripts/check-lease-ccache.py` holds the rule for every script under
  `scripts/`. It refuses `CCACHE_DIR` on the share and **accepts**
  `CCACHE_REMOTE_STORAGE` there, since a gate that refused the whole path would
  forbid the fix.
- The suite runs the shipped script's own counter extraction against two real
  transcripts: the dead cache from job `93a60151` yields no count so the refusal
  fires, and the live `remote-cold` arm yields `8`. Mutating the refusal back
  into a log line kills it.

## Not in this change

The usage sheet is host state and is not edited here. #2473 carries the evidence
and asks the operator to correct "keep its cache on the NAS".

The CUDA arm on `dgx:gpu0` -- the host where the 1404 s was actually paid -- is
`rc` job `54b75579`, queued behind other work. Both hosts mount the same share
and the capability probe runs on both, so the ratio above is stated as the CPU
arm and the dgx confirmation is listed under the spec's `## Owed`.

## Gates

`scripts/agent-preflight.sh --staged` rc 0, including `check-lease-ccache` ok,
`test_check_lease_ccache` 19/19 ok and `tree-compiles` 363/363 translation units
(82.4 s). Five gates SKIP for want of arguments preflight does not supply
(`--compile-commands`, `--base/--head`, `--vendored-root`); they skip on every
run here and none is caused by this change.

FOLLOWING_AGENTS_PROTOCOL

Closes #2473

author: astro-han
body:
## Summary

A Maka installed months ago describes every model by the models.dev snapshot compiled into that build. Since #4411 the Runtime Host is the sole authority for the model catalog, so that staleness is now one process's problem to fix: the Host fetches `https://models.dev/api.json` once at startup and, on a catalog it can project whole, makes it the metadata every connection resolves against. Clients keep reading Host-resolved catalog entries, so a Desktop or TUI on any version sees the refreshed facts without being updated itself.

The refresh reaches clients as a fifth `HostChangeFeed` frame, `connection.catalog.changed`, and they re-query. It is deliberately not `configuration.changed`: the user's settings did not move, and Desktop's handler for that frame raises a settings-changed-elsewhere notice which must not fire here.

Three things had to be true before a runtime refresh could exist at all, and they are the first three commits:

1. **The projection had to accept what models.dev actually publishes.** Live upstream declares `video` and `pdf` modalities; the validator rejected them, so 324 models failed and `refresh:model-metadata` wrote nothing. Widening the vocabulary takes rejects to zero (1871 → 1906 models, +66 / −31). This is a wire vocabulary change, hence the compatibility epoch bump to 88.
2. **One projection, not two.** The generator script owned the models.dev → `ModelMetadata` mapping. It now lives in `packages/core/src/models-dev-projection.ts` and both the script and the Host read it, so a model cannot mean one thing in the committed snapshot and another when the Host reads it live. Verified behaviour-preserving by running the pre- and post-refactor generators against the same live input: byte-identical projection, identical generated module.
3. **An install seam that replaces rather than merges.** A merge would keep describing a model upstream has delisted. The committed snapshot is not a second opinion about a model upstream still publishes — it is what we fall back to when we have no answer at all.

Replacing the whole table is safe for the model *list*: which models a connection has comes from its stored rows, the registry's fallback list and the ids the user enabled — models.dev feeds only what is *true about* a model, never which models exist. That is also why a metadata swap mid-pagination is safe: `catalogEntryCount` and every catalog cursor are invariant under it, so only field values can differ across pages, and the frame makes the client re-read.

Failure is whole and quiet: offline, timeout, a non-200, an oversized body, or an upstream shape the projection refuses all leave the build's committed snapshot in place. There is no partial install and no per-model tolerance — the Host runs exactly the fail-loud projection the generator does.

The generator and the Host share the whole refresh, not just the projection. `fetchModelsDevProjection` in `packages/core/src/models-dev-refresh.ts` owns the three steps neither caller gets to decide alone — fetch under a byte bound, project, account for what upstream stopped carrying — and they differ only in the fourth. That difference is deliberate: the generator **refuses** a shrinking refresh until a human passes `--accept-upstream-removals`, because it is about to commit and redistribute the result; the Host **records** the removals to stderr and **adopts** them, because nothing it installs is committed and the next process start asks again. Both name a removal by the same path, so an operator reading the Host log and a maintainer reading the generator's refusal are looking at the same thing.

The byte bound itself is shared one level lower: `readBoundedResponseText` in `packages/core/src/bounded-response.ts` is the one implementation, used here and by the WebFetch tool. It refuses on the declared `content-length` before a byte arrives and again on the running byte count, because a body that never declared a length — or lied — is the case a single check misses.

The fetch goes through the same admission as the WebFetch tool: privacy mode refuses it outright and a configured proxy carries it. That operation is now named `resolveHostOutboundExecution` for what it admits rather than for its first caller.

Finally, the refresh retires static overrides that only existed because the snapshot they were written against lacked the fact: openrouter's `deepseek-v4-pro` effort set and the GPT-OSS branch of the Ollama Cloud thinking pin. Both now restate models.dev verbatim, in the committed snapshot and in the live catalog alike.

Deliberately excluded, per the issue: TTL, on-disk cache, conditional GET, and an opt-out toggle. Also not refreshed here, and unchanged by this PR: pricing (`model-pricing.generated.ts`), provider routing overrides, and provider facts. The connection editor's draft view still resolves locally once the draft diverges from what the Host committed, so an editor mid-edit can briefly show pre-refresh facts; that is the existing draft contract, not a regression.

Two things a live catalog makes reachable that a compiled snapshot never did are fixed here rather than deferred. The catalog's display names and descriptions are now truncated where the entry is built, to the same limits the wire codec enforces — before, an upstream string longer than either produced a page the Host could encode and no client could decode, losing every model on it rather than one long string. And the TUI now derives the selected model's context window and thinking levels from the live choice list instead of keeping mirrored copies, which a mid-session catalog refresh would otherwise leave stale.

One commit on this branch is unrelated to #4398: `scripts/qualify-released-cli-state-root.test.mjs` asserted POSIX-separator paths and failed the `package` job on Windows. The bug arrived on `main` with #4427, not with this PR; it is fixed here only because it was blocking this branch's CI.

Snapshot-vs-upstream drift check, a scheduled refresh job, and removing `docsUrl` from `ModelMetadata` belong to the parallel PR on `ci/4398-model-metadata-drift-check`.

Refs #4398

## Verification

Run locally against this branch, all green:

- `npm run build`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run check:asf-headers`

author: jrb00013
body:
Godot refused to start:

```
Cross Origin Isolation - Check web server configuration (send correct headers)
SharedArrayBuffer - Check web server configuration (send correct headers)
```

**even though the headers were present.** They were present *twice*:

```
cross-origin-opener-policy: same-origin
cross-origin-opener-policy: same-origin
cross-origin-embedder-policy: require-corp
cross-origin-embedder-policy: require-corp
```

## Why duplication breaks it

The voxier image sets them, and this vhost set them again. **HTTP combines repeated response headers**, so the browser evaluates `same-origin, same-origin` — not a valid COOP value. Invalid values are ignored, the document is never cross-origin isolated, `SharedArrayBuffer` stays unavailable, and Godot fails exactly as above.

## Self-inflicted

I set them in both places deliberately, so the image would be "correct independently of whoever proxies to it". That reasoning was sound — doing it *without hiding the upstream copy* was not.

Fixed with `proxy_hide_header` on all three before re-adding, so exactly one of each reaches the browser and the image stays correct standalone.

## Why this was hard to spot

Every check said the headers were there. `curl` showed them, the values were right, and Cloudflare passed them through untouched. Only the **duplication** mattered — and "present twice" reads as belt-and-braces rather than as a fault.

The lesson matching the rest of this project: verifying a thing *exists* is not the same as verifying it *works*. The browser was the only check that could have caught this.

author: sulthannauval
body:
## Problem

The Persona page decides what the agent is told about itself on every turn, and it lied in a few places:

- **A fresh profile's first save wiped the runtime defaults.** With no `persona.toml`, `GET /personality` answers `configured: false`; the panel showed an empty form and, on Save, PUT `name/timezone/role/tone = ""`. The gateway writes every supplied string, so the prompt read "assistant for you (timezone: )", "Your primary role is: ", "Tone: ." under a "Persona saved" toast. The CLI and `setup` write `default_for("RantaiClaw", "UTC")` for the same input.
- **The chat rail invented a role** ("AI employee") whenever the saved role was empty.
- **Refresh and a knowledge-base chip both discarded unsaved edits**: each re-fetched and re-seeded the whole form. The chips saved at once while the fields waited for Save, two save models in one card.
- **The knowledge-base block said "No knowledge bases yet."** when the Knowledge Base was turned off, had no embedding key, or the gateway was down. Its chips had no state for a screen reader (`aria-pressed`), lost focus on Enter (`disabled` during the save) and were 27 px tall. Its sentence promised "every conversation"; the runtime has no reader for `always_on_kbs` (only chats sent from this console use it).
- **Any string was a timezone** ("Mars/Olympus Mons" saved and entered every prompt); the preset's description sat in `<option title>`, which no browser shows; Role and Tone could be blank.
- Labels on the old 10 px tracked-uppercase scale, "Personality" under a nav item called "Persona", a bare "Loading…", a blurb from before the editor existed, Refresh beside Retry.

## Change (one commit each)

1. **Runtime defaults, required fields, checked timezone, preset described, rail.** A fresh form holds the runtime's own defaults (`RUNTIME_DEFAULTS` mirrors `persona/mod.rs` `default_for`; timezone from the browser) behind a "No persona saved yet" notice, so Save writes what is shown. Name, Role, Tone and Timezone are required (inline alert, `aria-invalid`, Save disabled); Avoid stays optional (the template guards it). Timezone gets a datalist of the browser's IANA names, an inline error for a non-IANA string and a "Use this browser's timezone" button. The selected preset's description shows under the select, live from the gateway. Placeholders carry the defaults; a counter appears within 20 characters of a cap. The rail shows the saved role or no role line. New pure `lib/persona.ts` with tests.
2. **Edits survive, one save model, chips with state and size, block states.** The form re-seeds only while clean (Refresh reloads the saved snapshot, never overwrites work in progress). The always-on bases are form state and go with Save: no immediate PUT, no second toast, no `disabled` flash. Chips are `type="button"` with `aria-pressed` and a check glyph, 36 px (40 on a coarse pointer), focus stays after Enter. The block distinguishes loading / turned off / no embedding key / failed (Retry) / none yet / list, with the route linked (`#kb`). The sentence now says the list is used by chats sent from this console; channels and the terminal do not read it.
3. **Labels, name, loading, retry, blurb.** `.eyebrow` labels with `htmlFor` (the console's label scale), "Persona" as the section title, "Loading persona…" / "Loading knowledge bases…", Refresh only once data exists (the frame's Retry alone before that; both re-run all three reads), a blurb that describes what the page edits.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` 0; `npx vitest run` 52 files / 546 tests (baseline 51 / 523); `next build` 0.
- Driven on `next dev` and once on the production build (`next start`) against a disposable gateway (rantaiclaw 0.25.0-alpha, fresh `HOME`, stub model, stub embedding provider), at 1280 and 390 px:
  - fresh profile → notice + defaults; Save → `persona.toml` holds `RantaiClaw` / browser timezone / default role / `neutral` / `preset = "default"` (`rantaiclaw personality show` agrees);
  - blank Name → "Name is required.", Save disabled; `Mars/Olympus Mons` → the IANA line, Save disabled; the browser-timezone button clears it; 418 IANA options in the datalist;
  - preset change → description follows;
  - type a name, click a chip → the name stays, Save enabled, one toast on Save, both in `persona.toml`; Enter on a chip keeps focus and flips `aria-pressed`; `snapshot -i` shows `button "Product docs" [pressed=true]`; chips 36 px;
  - type a name, Refresh (gateway up and gateway down) → the name stays; the strip shows under the title with the form kept;
  - KB turned off → "The Knowledge Base is turned off. Turn it on under Knowledge Bases." and the link switches to `#kb`; on without a key → the embedding-key sentence; on with no groups → "No knowledge bases yet."; the frame's Retry also recovers the block;
  - first load with the gateway down → Retry alone; after recovery Refresh, Save and the chips;
  - `#chat` with `role = ""` on disk → the rail shows the name alone;
  - 390 px: no horizontal overflow (`scrollWidth` 390 on the document and `.ops`), card 358 px, chips 36 px.

## Risk and rollback

- Scope: `persona-panel.tsx` (rewritten in place), its test, new `lib/persona.ts` + test, the `persona` blurb in `lib/console.ts`, two lines in `console-shell.tsx`. No shared primitive, `api.ts` or gateway change.
- `RUNTIME_DEFAULTS` duplicates two strings from `persona/mod.rs` `default_for`; both sides must move together (noted in the file).
- Rollback: revert the squash. Each commit stands alone.

## Non-goals (gateway follow-ups)

- The runtime reading `always_on_kbs` for channels and the terminal (RantAIClaw plan 112 item 8).
- Defaults for blank fields on `PUT /personality` (the API and the CLI/setup path write different personas for the same empty input) and server-side timezone validation.
- A rendered-persona preview needs an endpoint that returns the `## Persona` section.
- The `kb_disabled` detail copy (an arrow and a run of spaces).

## Design reasons

- The fresh form is filled with the runtime's own defaults and says so: what the operator sees is what Save writes.
- Name, Role, Tone and Timezone are required because the templates print them inline; Avoid has a guard.
- The timezone is checked in the console because the runtime prints it verbatim.
- One save model for fields and bases removes the second PUT, the second toast and the re-seed that wiped edits.
- Chip state is carried by `aria-pressed` and a glyph, not colour alone.
- The block has separate states because the gateway distinguishes them and each has a different next action.
- The rail shows the saved role or nothing: a fallback role is a claim the runtime never made.

author: h0mele55
body:
Closes #2201, closes #2202, closes #2203, closes #2204.

Four independent one-line defects in four different providers, bundled because they touch four disjoint files and each is too small for its own PR. Every diagnosis was verified against the code before implementing — **three were correct as written; #2204's prescribed fix was wrong and would have killed the feature.**

## ⚠ Read this before "correcting" the #2204 fix

The issue prescribes `payload.eventType === 'branch_protection_rule' && (...)`. **Do not apply that literally.** `payload.eventType` is set at `src/app-layer/usecases/webhook-processor.ts:217` from `body.action ?? body.event_type` — for a real GitHub `branch_protection_rule` delivery that holds `'edited'`, never `'branch_protection_rule'`. GitHub puts the event *name* in the `x-github-event` header (lowercased at `src/app/api/integrations/webhooks/[provider]/route.ts:47`; `tests/unit/webhook-sync-dispatch.test.ts:201` shows a real delivery).

Applying the issue's line would make the branch permanently unreachable in production — a silent feature kill that every pre-existing test would have passed. Shipped instead as `payload.headers['x-github-event'] || payload.eventType || ''` conjoined with the action check, keeping `eventType` as a fallback for non-HTTP callers. The test `the event name is read from the header, not from eventType` is the only thing standing between that "correction" and a dark feature.

## The four fixes

**#2204** — `github/legacy-provider.ts:401-416`. The `||` chain never required the event type, so any delivery carrying `action: created|edited|deleted` — issues, pull_request, label, milestone, release — fired `github.branch_protection`.

**#2203** — `gcp-posture-provider.ts:104-115`. The `mkdtemp`'d directory leaked on every run; `rm(dir, {recursive, force})` now runs in the same `finally`. **The `unlink` was deliberately not folded into it** as the issue suggests: ordering is a security property — if `rm` fails on EPERM or a stale NFS handle, the key must already be gone — and folding would have deleted four existing key-hygiene assertions.

**#2202** — `servicenow/client.ts:164-172`. A missing table was reported as a deleted record; those mean opposite things to a sync. Worth knowing before anyone treats this as a live incident: `getRemoteObject` has **no production caller** today (only the abstract declaration at `base-client.ts:141`), so the current blast radius is zero. The fix is still right — it makes the client's contract honest before someone wires it up.

**#2201** — `sharepoint/import.ts:230-238`. `importOne` read `target.folder` correctly all along; `importSharePointItems` built `target` from `controlId` + `category` only, so the user's chosen folder was always `undefined` and the evidence row stored null.

## The guard that should have caught #2201, and didn't

`tests/guards/evidence-upload-sends-what-it-renders.test.ts` exists for exactly this invariant and **could not have caught it**. It asserted the modal sends `folder`, the route accepts `folder`, and `importOne` reads `target.folder` — every layer except the one where `target` is built. That hop is now asserted, with its own mutation proof.

## Mutation proofs

Every fix has a test that fails against the unfixed source (restored by `cp` backup, never `git checkout --`):

| fix | failing assertion before the fix |
|---|---|
| #2204 | `status: "ignored"` expected, got `"processed"` + `triggeredKeys: ["github.branch_protection"]` — 4 failed / 8 passed |
| #2203 | `rm` — "Number of calls: 0" ×2, plus unlink-before-rm ordering — 3 failed / 10 passed |
| #2202 | `/no table configured/i` expected, got `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ok')` — 2 failed / 32 passed |
| #2201 | `"folder": "SOC2/2026/Access reviews"` expected, got `"folder": null` — 1 failed / 8 passed |
| guard | `/folder:\s*input\.folder/` not found in the `importOne` call site — 1 failed / 7 passed |

## Verification

All exit 0: `github-provider-branch-paths` 70/70 · `gcp-posture-credential-file` 13/13 · `servicenow-client-failure-modes` 34/34 · `sharepoint-import` 9/9 · `evidence-upload-sends-what-it-renders` 8/8. Adjacent suites also run and green: `github-provider` 31/31, `sharepoint-import-branches` 28/28, `servicenow-client` 40/40, `cloud-posture` 16/16, `azure-gcp-posture-providers` 46/46. `eslint` on all nine changed files exit 0 (one pre-existing warning at `servicenow-client-failure-modes.test.ts:121`, confirmed present on `HEAD`, untouched).

Typecheck deliberately left to CI — the machine was at load average 21-24 with a parallel wave running, and this repo records that a local `tsc` can be green on code CI rejects because of `incremental: true`.

## Risk / rollback

STANDARD. Four provider-local changes, no schema, no middleware, no dependency change. Rollback is a `git revert` of the single commit; each fix is independent of the others, so a partial revert is also safe.

author: jmf-pobox
body:
## Summary
Fixes a 0.32.0 regression: opening the beads board from its menu entry, closing it, then reopening it did nothing. Ships as 0.32.1.

## Root cause (DES-089, one layer down)
The applet already raised on every click (`held_board.py`), so it was never "forgot to raise." A **client-initiated `raise_frame` on a user-closed frame targeted the wrong id**: the caller raised a *local* name (`beads-<repo>`), but the Hub holds frames under their **connection-scoped** id (DES-086), so the display answered `raised: false` for an id it never held — and DES-088 correctly refuses to reopen a closed frame via a content push, so the click was a **silent no-op**.

## Fix
- The Hub resolves a caller's local frame name to **its own connection's** scoped id before raising — unambiguous by construction even when **two sessions in one repo** share the same repo-scoped local name (the case a single-session demo would miss).
- Frame identity is carried as one `FrameRef` value (connection + local name) instead of a bare string threaded beside a `Scope` — DES-089 "identity is a path" as a type. `ClientIdentity.connection_id` extracted (PY-OO-5, de-dups a derivation that lived in two files).
- `BoardChannel.raised` no longer masks a failed `OpError` raise as "the board is up."

## Verification
- `make check` green on the final state (`f0207050`): mypy (1022 files), pyright 0 errors, ruff, markdownlint, full pytest (**4687 passed**), OO + coupling ratchets baked.
- **New two-connection regression test** drives the real `HubDisplay`/`FrameLifecycle`/`SceneOperations` path (not stubbed) — two connections install `beads-<repo>`; one closes+reopens; asserts it raises only *its own* scoped frame. Fails if the fix is reverted.
- Local review: `code-reviewer` + `silent-failure-hunter` (converged on one docstring fix, applied) + `gvr` evaluator (drove the multi-session scoping fix and the FrameRef value type).
- **Operator-confirmed demo:** `make restart`, then open→close→reopen beads across two sessions in one repo — reopens correctly ("I can open it more than once").

## Notes
- One documented OO residual (a correct new type costs +1 import edge at its construction sites) accepted per PY-RF-7, rationale in commit `f0207050` — not suppressed, not hidden.
- Filed alongside: `lux-83ig` (check-oo diffs `HEAD~1..HEAD`, misses full-branch regressions) and a non-deterministic `circular_imports` metric in `tools/oo_coupling.py`.

author: alonzoricardo
body:
# Description

Adds an optional `entryPointVersion` configuration field (`'0.8' | '0.9'`, default `'0.8'`) that selects the ERC-4337 EntryPoint the account operates under.

The EntryPoint address and the delegation implementation cannot be chosen independently: the implementation fixes the EIP-712 signing domain (the domain's `verifyingContract` **is** the EntryPoint address), while the EntryPoint address is where nonces are read and user operations are submitted. So the field selects both together through a single map rather than exposing a standalone address:

```js
const ENTRY_POINT_VERSIONS = new Map([
  ['0.8', { account: Simple7702Account, address: ENTRYPOINT_V8 }],
  ['0.9', { account: Simple7702AccountV09, address: ENTRYPOINT_V9 }]
])
```

Every site that previously hardcoded v0.8 now resolves through `_getEntryPointVersion()`, which returns the exported `EntryPointVersion` typedef:

| Site | Was |
|---|---|
| `wallet-account-read-only-…:640` | `new Simple7702Account(…, { entrypointAddress: ENTRYPOINT_V8 })` |
| `wallet-account-read-only-…:729` | `pimlico_getTokenQuotes` with `ENTRYPOINT_V8` |
| `wallet-account-read-only-…:737` | `pm_supportedERC20Tokens` with `ENTRYPOINT_V8` |
| `wallet-account-evm-…:446` | `Simple7702Account.getUserOperationEip712Data(op, chainId)` |
| `wallet-account-evm-…:472` | `sendUserOperation(userOp, ENTRYPOINT_V8)` |
| `wallet-account-evm-…:512`, `:529` | `fetchAccountNonce(provider, ENTRYPOINT_V8, …)` |

**No dependency change.** `Simple7702AccountV09`, `ENTRYPOINT_V9` and `UserOperationV9` are already exported by the pinned `abstractionkit@0.3.8`, verified at runtime against this repo's `node_modules`. This deliberately keeps the `0.4.x` bump — which carries a breaking `UserOperationReceipt.logs` change from `string` to `Log[]`, a type this module re-exposes via `Evm7702GaslessTransactionDetails.userOperationReceipt` — out of scope.

## Motivation and Context

A team building on this module migrated their bundler/paymaster stack to EntryPoint v0.9 shortly before the module's first release and had to patch it locally to work at all, and asked for multiple versions to be supported.

Two of the pins made that more than a missing config value:

- **`getUserOperationEip712Data` silently signed the wrong domain.** `BaseSimple7702Account.getUserOperationEip712Data` defaults `entrypointAddress` to v0.8, and the EIP-712 domain's `verifyingContract` is the EntryPoint. Called with no override on a v0.9 setup it produces a well-formed signature over the v0.8 domain — rejected on-chain as `AA24`, with nothing pointing at the cause. `Simple7702AccountV09` exists to default that domain to v0.9; this PR now also passes `entrypointAddress` explicitly rather than relying on either class default.
- **Nonces were read from the wrong EntryPoint.** `fetchAccountNonce` against the v0.8 EntryPoint returns 0 for a v0.9 account, so every send would build on a stale nonce.

`delegationAddress` was already configurable, so a consumer could point delegation at the v0.9 implementation while the module kept signing for and submitting to the v0.8 EntryPoint, with nothing validating the pair. That half-configurable state is what this PR closes.

## Backwards compatibility

`entryPointVersion` is optional and construction-time only (consistent with `delegationAddress`). Omitting it resolves to the same account class, EntryPoint address, delegation implementation, signatures and nonces as before.

The strongest evidence is that **all 103 pre-existing unit tests and all 32 integration tests pass unmodified** — those tests assert concrete values, not shapes: `sendUserOperation` called with `ENTRYPOINT_V8`, `fetchAccountNonce` with `ENTRYPOINT_V8`, `pm_supportedERC20Tokens` with `[ENTRYPOINT_V8]`, and the exact user-operation signature `0xe9739f74…8736f1c`.

The public type surface is unchanged. `UserOperationV8` stays exported and stays accurate under v0.9, because abstractionkit declares `interface UserOperationV9 extends UserOperationV8 {}` — structurally identical, so no signature needed widening.

`types/` was hand-edited to mirror the source. Verified by emitting to a scratch directory and diffing: the additions match `tsc` output exactly, and the pre-existing hand-added override declarations (`getBalance`, `getTokenBalance`, `defaultWaitTimeout`, `verify`, `getFeeRates`) are preserved.

### One intentional behavior change

Construction now throws a `ConfigurationError` when `delegationAddress` is one version's reference implementation while `entryPointVersion` names the other:

```
delegationAddress 0xa46cc63e… is the reference implementation for EntryPoint v0.9,
but entryPointVersion is '0.8'. An implementation only accepts user operations from
the EntryPoint it was built for: set entryPointVersion to '0.9', or point
delegationAddress at a v0.8 implementation.
```

That combination cannot work — it is exactly the state consumers were patching around, and today it surfaces as an opaque `AA24` after a bundler round-trip. Only the two known reference addresses are compared; a custom `delegationAddress` is still accepted on either version and is not checked.

## Related Issue

Origin discussion (cross-repo): tetherto/wdk-wallet-evm-erc-4337#112 — where EntryPoint configurability was raised and this module was identified as the right target for v0.8/v0.9 support. Note that thread assumed the `0.3.8 → 0.4.0` bump was a prerequisite; it is not, as above.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] This change requires a documentation update

## How Has This Been Tested?

- `npm run lint` — clean.
- `npm test` — 114 passed (103 pre-existing untouched + 11 new).
- `npm run test:integration` — 32 passed against a local Alto bundler + mock paymaster on EntryPoint v0.8.

New unit coverage: version resolution for both versions (account class, EntryPoint address, and the paymaster token-quote RPCs), rejection of an unsupported version, both directions of the delegatee/version mismatch, acceptance of a custom delegatee on either version, and submission plus nonce reads against the v0.9 EntryPoint.

The signing test asserts real values in both directions — the same user operation signs to `0x8d1f1832…42a11b` under v0.9 and explicitly **not** to the v0.8 signature — pinning the domain separation that was previously silent.

**Not covered:** an end-to-end run against a bundler that actually serves EntryPoint v0.9. The integration suite runs Alto on v0.8, so v0.9 is verified at the module boundary (correct class, address, domain and nonce source) but not on-chain. Validation against a v0.9-serving endpoint before this ships would be worth having.

author: paulalbert1
body:
## Why

The Scopus producer already asks PubMed whether each document exists there, twice (ingest step 3, weekly `recheck_open_scopus`), and `_pubmed_esearch` already returns the matched PMID in `idlist` — the wrappers reduced it to a bool and threw it away. Worse, a *title-only* heuristic hit (`<title>[ti] AND <surname>[au]`, unquoted) silently auto-dismissed open rows: 345 rows carry `note LIKE 'auto: now in PubMed (title match)%'` today, and nobody adjudicated them. This is Layer 1 of the PM #951 design (handoff `docs/HANDOFF_2026-09-01_951-dup-adjudication-and-scopus-coauthor-backfill.md`, Part 1): persist the match, keep the heuristic ones open for a curator.

## What changes

- `setup/alter_authorship_review_add_matched_pmid_v2.7.sql` — (1) `CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci`: the table was created with no `COLLATE` and resolved to `utf8mb4_general_ci`; every join target is `unicode_ci`, and `ar.external_id = SUBSTRING(ea.article_id, 8)` raises `ERROR 1267 Illegal mix of collations` today (reproduced 2026-09-01; same bug v1.8 fixed for `external_article`). (2) `matched_pmid BIGINT`, `matched_pmid_source ENUM('scopus','doi','title')`, `matched_pmid_at DATETIME`, `matched_pmid_verdict ENUM('same','distinct')` + `ix_matched_pmid`, `ix_doi`.
- `update/aar_universe_scopus.py` — `_pubmed_pmid()` reads `idlist[0]`; `doi_in_pubmed` / `title_in_pubmed` / `resolve_no_doi` return the PMID (int) or `None` (same truthiness, names unchanged). Ingest: DOI hits are still dropped; **title hits are now kept and written with `matched_pmid`/`_source='title'`**. Recheck: DOI hit → dismissed as before, now with the PMID in the columns and in the note (`… PMID <n>`); **title hit → columns set, row stays open** (`status`/`note` untouched). The SELECT adds `matched_pmid IS NULL`, which excludes both already-flagged rows awaiting a verdict and rows a curator marked `distinct`, so the producer never re-flags either. Selftest extended (49 checks, offline).
- `update/aar_db.py` — the three producer columns are in `_INSERT_COLS` only, never `_REFRESH_COLS` (rolling windows re-upsert a document ~11×; a refresh would clobber a flag or an answered value). `matched_pmid_verdict` is curator-owned and in neither list. DDL string updated.
- `setup/table_authorship_review.sql` — same columns/keys and `COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci` for fresh installs.

Behaviour change accepted deliberately: `resolve_no_doi` no longer consults `isbn_in_pubmed` for `pub_type='Book'` (it can only return a bool, not a PMID). Those books (3.8% of a 26-doc probe) now fall to the title search and get *flagged* rather than silently dropped — the safer direction for this feature. `isbn_in_pubmed` stays (tested) for a future `source='isbn'`.

## Apply order — DDL first, then merge

A merge auto-deploys the CronJob image, and the first upsert after that names the new columns; if the table lacks them, **both AAR lanes** (Scopus and PubMed, same `aar_db.upsert`) fail with 1054 until the migration lands (caught by `run_all.py`, reporting unaffected, but that week's lanes are lost).

1. Outside the 14:30 UTC `reciterdb` CronJob window and curator hours (`CONVERT` is ALGORITHM=COPY; table is 76.5 MB / 30,015 rows — seconds, but it locks).
2. Pre-check, run 2026-09-01 13:58 UTC: `SELECT author_key COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci k, COUNT(*) FROM authorship_review GROUP BY k HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` → **0 rows** (unicode_ci folds more characters equal; a collision would fail `uq_author_key` during the CONVERT).
3. `mysql … reciterdb < setup/alter_authorship_review_add_matched_pmid_v2.7.sql`
4. Merge this PR.

## Not in this PR (decisions / follow-ups)

- The 345 title-match rows already auto-dismissed are untouched. Reopening them into the new PM view is a one-liner (`UPDATE authorship_review SET status='open', resolved_at=NULL WHERE source='scopus' AND status='dismissed' AND note LIKE 'auto: now in PubMed (title match)%'`); the next Sunday recheck would then fill `matched_pmid` for them. Proposed as `fix_…_v2.8.sql` only if wanted.
- Pre-existing drift: prod has `accept_conflict` + `idx_authorship_review_accept_conflict` (PM-owned) that neither `table_authorship_review.sql` nor the `aar_db.py` DDL declares.
- PM #951 Layer 2 (adjudication panel, `verdict` action) is a separate PR in ReCiter-Publication-Manager.

## Verification

- `python3 update/aar_universe_scopus.py --selftest` with DB/NCBI/Scopus env vars removed: SELFTEST PASS (49 OK / 0 FAIL). `py_compile` clean on both modules.
- Independent fresh-context review: PASS_WITH_NOTES — DDL identical across migration / table SQL / `aar_db.py` DDL; paper trace of the recheck for (i) DOI row resolving, (ii) first title hit, (iii) same row a week later, (iv) after `distinct`, (v) after PM dismissed with `same`: no path re-flags, re-dismisses, or writes a curator field.
- No SQL was executed by this change; the migration is hand-applied per the order above.

## What this merge is
`main_patched` → `module/container-queue` at height 239. Upstream adds plugin MCP server support to the agent-runner, a signal-cleanup fix in the poll-loop, container-plugin materialization, the `containerStartedAtMs` heartbeat fallback, and the host-lifecycle registry (`onHostStart`/`onHostShutdown`/`startHostModules`/`stopHostModules`) as a breaking replacement for the `onShutdown`/`getShutdownCallbacks` pattern in `response-registry.ts`.

## Resolutions

### `container/agent-runner/src/index.ts`

<details>
<summary>ours vs theirs vs chosen</summary>

**ours (`module/container-queue`)** — imports `runPollLoop` and `requestGracefulStop` from `poll-loop.js`.

**theirs (`main_patched`)** — imports `resolvePluginServer` and `McpServerConfig` (plugin support) from new files, drops `requestGracefulStop` from `poll-loop.js`.

**chosen** — ours for the `ActiveContainer` interface and `activeContainers.set` (the queue requires `spawnedAt`, `heartbeatMtimeMs`, and `hasOutstandingClaim`); theirs' `CONTAINER_PLUGINS_DIR` added to ours' imports; all needed imports unioned. `getContainerStartedAtMs` outside the hunk referenced `startedAtMs` (theirs' field name) but our interface uses `spawnedAt` — corrected to `spawnedAt`.

</details>

</details>

### `src/index.ts`

<details>
<summary>ours vs theirs vs chosen</summary>

**ours (`module/container-queue`)** — imports `migrateGroupsToClaudeLocal` from `claude-md-compose.js`, `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` from config, and `startHostSweep` from `host-sweep.js`; re-exports `registerResponseHandler` and `onShutdown` from `response-registry.js`; signal handlers call `void initiateShutdown(...)` directly.
