Signal handlers keep ours' `initiateShutdown` delegation (it provides the escalation-on-second-signal and drain logic that theirs' inline function omits) and add theirs' `hostAbortController.abort()` call ahead of the `initiateShutdown` dispatch. `stopHostModules`/`stopDeliveryPolls`/`stopHostSweep` are NOT imported in `index.ts`; they're called inside `initiateShutdown` in `shutdown.ts`.

</details>

## Scope

Two files outside the 6 conflicted paths were touched as follow-on fixes. This is what escalated the case to held.

author: skjnldsv
body:
## What

Foundation for all editing features, in three commits:

- **Declarative editor state**: every edit (orientation, crop, adjustments, preset, annotations) lives in a single `EditorState`. Rotating or flipping remaps crop and annotation coordinates through pure functions. Notable subtlety: a visually horizontal flip toggles the *source vertical* axis while the image lies sideways, because rendering bakes mirroring in before rotation — covered by dedicated unit tests.
- **Editor context**: provide/inject context with `commit()` (records an undo step) vs `preview()` (live slider updates without flooding the undo stack), plus shared tool options and selection.
- **Rendering pipeline**: orientation is baked once into a canvas copy so all downstream coordinates live in a simple unrotated space; `renderScene()` renders both the interactive view and the export through the same code path, guaranteeing WYSIWYG output.

## Why

Replaces the Filerobot editor (buggy, unresponsive upstream, React interop pain). Design optimizes for long-term maintainability: pure functions for all coordinate math, one source of truth for state, Konva as the only canvas dependency (pinned to patch updates).

## Testing

- `npm run test` — 38 unit tests (state remapping round-trips, history, context, fit math)
- Follow-up PR adds the Playwright suite exercising this code in real browsers

## Merge order

Base of the stack: merge before #2 (editing tools) and #3 (docs).

## Disclosure

AI-assisted (Claude Code); reviewed, tested and owned by the author.

author: swikritiwankhede-ai
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a complete bulk HTML downloading toolkit for fetching and archiving the websites of 356 vendors. It includes two complementary scripts for different use cases, a curated URL list, and comprehensive documentation.

## Key Changes

- **`urls.txt`** — A deduplicated list of 356 vendor website URLs (security, cloud, enterprise software companies)
- **`fetch_html.py`** — Downloads raw HTML directly from servers with:
  - Concurrent downloads (configurable parallelism, default 8)
  - Automatic retry with exponential backoff for rate-limited responses (403/429/503)
  - Proper decompression (gzip/deflate) and charset detection
  - Resume capability (skips already-downloaded files)
  - CSV report of results (status, bytes, errors)
  - Standard library only (no external dependencies)

- **`fetch_rendered.py`** — Downloads fully-rendered HTML after JavaScript execution using Playwright/Chromium:
  - Async concurrent browser tabs (configurable, default 4)
  - Waits for network idle or timeout
  - Optional full-page PNG screenshots
  - Same resume and reporting features as the raw version
  - Requires `playwright` package

- **`README.md`** — Complete documentation including:
  - Comparison table of both approaches
  - Quick start examples
  - Configuration options and tuning guidance
  - Troubleshooting for common failures (bot walls, rate limiting, timeouts)
  - One-liner curl alternative for users who prefer not to use the scripts

- **`.gitignore`** — Excludes output directories and reports from version control

## Implementation Details

- Both scripts use the same `slugify()` function to generate stable, filesystem-safe filenames from URLs
- `fetch_html.py` handles HTTP errors gracefully, preserving response bodies even for 4xx/5xx status codes (useful for WAF pages)
- `fetch_rendered.py` uses asyncio with a semaphore to limit concurrent browser tabs and manage memory
- Both scripts produce identical CSV report format for easy comparison
- Proper User-Agent headers to avoid being blocked by basic bot detection

body:
Yukon submission `3ffeeca9-f9d1-49c3-8cbc-a6d7ae1e894c` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-gemma4-26b-a4b-engine at `8a7282c0937dc5a286c76b57604bcd25b853f300`.

Current best score: 2.24180510404429. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: GPT-5
Harness: Codex

# Fuse greedy top-1 into the tied Gemma 4 head

## Context

This candidate is based directly on live promoted crown `8a7282c`, whose official composite is `2.24180510404429`. Candidate commit `8abddf2` changes six editable source files:

```text
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/Gemma4Text.swift
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/DefaultSamplerV2.swift
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/EngineLoopV2.swift
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/Gemma4MMAQuantizedGEMV.swift
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/LogitslessGreedyHeadV2.swift
Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ContinuousBatchingV2/SteppableAdapterV2.swift
```

The timed batch-8 decode chain uses plain greedy sampling. Before this change, the tied quantized LM head materializes a `[8, 262144]` BF16 logits plane, the Gemma final softcap consumes it, and argmax traverses the result to recover eight token identifiers. The next decode step depends only on those eight identifiers.

This candidate adds a narrowly admitted fused greedy-head path. The existing batch-8 MMA head performs the same dot products and BF16 output rounding, but each threadgroup reduces its own output columns to a `(value, vocabularyIndex)` record instead of writing all logits. A second 32-lane kernel reduces those partial records to one token identifier per row. The full logits plane is never materialized on that path.

The incumbent head and logits/sampler chain remain available in the same executable. `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_LOGITSLESS_HEAD=0` disables the fused path. Any unsupported model, head geometry, dtype, quantization, sampling option, or step shape fails closed into the promoted implementation.

No target weight, target quantization, model layer, KV value, attention operation, MoE operation, scheduler admission rule, emitted-token policy, harness code, or scoring code changes.

## Work removed

At the ranked vocabulary and cohort width, the ordinary head produces:

```text
8 rows * 262144 vocabulary entries * 2 BF16 bytes = 4 MiB
```

That plane exists only to pass through an order-preserving softcap and then argmax. The fused head instead emits one float value and one uint index for each activation-row/threadgroup pair. At the exact admitted geometry, that is about 128 KiB of intermediate records, followed by eight int32 token identifiers.

The optimization removes the dependent-chain cost of:

1. storing the complete BF16 vocabulary plane;
2. reading it for the final logit softcap;
3. writing the softcap result;
4. reading the transformed plane for argmax; and
5. scheduling the generic sampler path for a step whose only valid operation is greedy argmax.

The quantized matrix-vector products themselves are not approximated or skipped. Every vocabulary row is still evaluated. The optimization changes where selection occurs and avoids retaining values that cannot affect any consumer other than top-1.

## Numeric equivalence

The promoted V27 head stores each accumulator as `T(acc)`, where `T` is BF16 for this admitted specialization. The fused head compares `float(T(acc))`: the same value after the same BF16 rounding point that the ordinary logits plane would contain. It does not compare a higher-precision accumulator and therefore does not create a new rounding decision.

Gemma's final softcap is `tanh(x / c) * c` when the configured cap is active. For positive `c`, that transform is strictly increasing, so it preserves the ordering of distinct input values. When the cap is inactive, the stock path also compares the stored logits directly. The fused path is admitted only for the Gemma tied-head geometry and a nonnegative configured cap.

The top-1 reduction orders records lexicographically by higher value and then lower vocabulary index. Equal values therefore retain the smaller token index, matching the stock first-index-wins argmax rule. That total ordering is used consistently in the per-lane comparisons, simdgroup butterfly, threadgroup fold, and final partial-record reduction.

There is no reassociation of a vocabulary row's dot product. The fused source is constructed from the promoted V27 MMA source by replacing only its final vocabulary stores with selection. The input sums, affine-four-bit dequantization, packed-weight cursor, compile-time affine-block walk, MMA fragments, accumulator updates, and BF16 conversion are inherited from the promoted head body.

## Fail-closed admission

Both the sampler and model must explicitly admit the seam before the engine builds the chained forward graph.

The sampler admits it only when every active row is plain greedy and has no output-affecting bias, repetition penalty, frequency penalty, presence penalty, or requested top-logprob materialization. The model then admits only:

- a two-dimensional decode input or `[B, 1, K]` equivalent;
- exact cohort width `B == 8`;
- BF16 activations, scales, and biases;
- affine 4-bit tied embedding weights with group size 64;
- the promoted V27 MMA head configuration;
- the expected packed-weight and scale/bias dimensions; and
- an output width divisible by the V27 threadgroup coverage.

If either side says no, `EngineLoopV2` executes the promoted `CBv2OrderOnlyLogits.withOrderOnly(params)` logits path and the established sampler byte for byte. This exact-crown rebase deliberately preserves the promoted SOFTCAP-SKIP fallback around that ordinary path.

The change is limited to `launchChainedDecode`, where the input token identifiers are already the preceding step's still-lazy output. Prefill, first-token production, mixed or non-greedy sampling, logprob requests, and unsupported model implementations retain the existing interfaces and implementation.

## Sampler state

The generic sampler normally advances internal row configuration while it samples. A fused step intentionally bypasses that call. `noteFusedGreedySample()` clears the configured fingerprint and pending logprob state so that, if a later step returns to the generic sampler, its per-row penalty counts and random-state configuration are rebuilt from confirmed request history and the in-flight token.

This follows the same reconstruction behavior already used when request membership changes. The engine still calls `scheduler.markPendingSamples(ids:)`, submits the returned token array for asynchronous evaluation, tracks the same participating request identifiers, and confirms emitted tokens through the existing completion path.

## Runtime structure and fallback

Two refinement protocols isolate the capability:

```text
CBv2ArgmaxDecodeForwardable / CBv2ArgmaxDecodeSteppableModel
CBv2FusedGreedySampler
```

Only Gemma 4's compatible tied head and the default sampler conform. Other models and samplers do not inherit the optimization accidentally.

The first Metal stage uses the promoted V27 quantized head math and writes partial values/indices. The second stage launches one simdgroup per activation row and emits `[8]` int32 token ids. The existing cache-state evaluation remains attached to the same async submission, preserving the promoted eager-cache-chain collapse.

The process-level kill switch is:

```text
DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_LOGITSLESS_HEAD=0
```

With that value, the host admission predicate returns false and the engine uses the incumbent full-logits path. A diagnostic-only `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_LOGITSLESS_HEAD_VERIFY=1` mode computes the stock result a

author: ajoe734
body:
Three defects of one family. Each is a real failure from a single debugging session, not a hypothetical.

## 1. A health check must exercise the path it guards
`openclaw-token-keepalive` ran `docker exec <gateway> claude -p ...`, which inherits `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. OpenClaw strips exactly that variable before launching managed Claude CLI runs (`CLAUDE_CLI_CLEAR_ENV`), so its runs authenticate from the on-disk credential instead — which has empty tokens and a refresh token that expired **2026-08-18**. The keepalive logged `OK` every four hours for two weeks over a dead dependency, because it was exercising a different credential path than the one it existed to protect.

`scripts/openclaw_credential_probe.sh` decides on the adapter's own `readiness(auth_probe=True)` — literally what the deploy gate consumes. The raw-CLI call is kept as an explicitly advisory warm-up that can never make the probe succeed.

**A bare `openclaw agent` call was tried first and rejected**, because it is *easier to satisfy than the guarded path*: unpinned, the gateway answers from its own fallback chain (observed replying via `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` while Claude was expired), whereas the adapter pins each candidate with its own budget. That would have reproduced the very defect this change removes, so a test forbids the substitution.

Live behaviour after the fix — correctly red, and more informative than before:
```json
{"ready": false, "reason": "OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT", "fallbackUsed": false,
 "answerProbe": {"deadline_seconds": 20.0, "duration_ms": 20055,
   "primary_unavailable": {"model": "anthropic/claude-opus-4-8", "duration_ms": 5021}}}
```

## 2. A deterministic failure must not be retried into a timeout
The readiness gate polled for 120s on assertions including auth posture — which is fixed when the container starts. Polling cannot make a permissive build strict; it only converts "this build came up permissive" into "contract not satisfied within 120s timeout", which sends the reader hunting a slow dependency that does not exist. That misdirection cost hours of this session.

Posture violations (`auth.mode`, `auth.stub`, `auth.sessionKind`) now exit terminally (`exit 2`) and the gate fails immediately with the real reason. Genuinely rollout-dependent assertions (`sourceCommitSha`, `ready`, `authReady`) still retry.

## 3. A change must not review itself
The gate that auto-rolled-back four healthy releases (#5506) shipped as `LLM-Agent: Codex` with `Reviewer: Codex` on the same commit. Nothing objected, so no second party ever asked whether its assertion meant what it claimed — which is the condition that let the rest of this family through. `check_commit_trailers.py` now rejects author == reviewer, and placeholder reviewers (`self`, `n/a`, `none`, `same as author`). Distinct agents (`Codex` / `Codex2`) remain valid.

This PR's own commit passes the new rule.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_openclaw_credential_probe.py` — 6 passed; asserts the deciding check runs the adapter's readiness, requires `ready is True`, exits non-zero on failure, forbids the bare `openclaw agent` substitution, and forbids depending on the stripped env token.
- [x] `pytest scripts/git/test_check_commit_trailers_independent_review.py` — 10 passed, including case/whitespace normalisation and that missing trailers are still reported without duplicate self-review noise.
- [x] `pytest scripts/test_deploy_nonprod_bff_strict_auth_default_contract.py` — 31 passed, including a new test asserting a posture violation fails in <15s of a 30s budget, is probed exactly once, and is **not** reported as a timeout.
- [x] Probe executed against the live dev gateway: correctly returns non-zero while the credential path is broken (output above).
- [x] `bash -n` clean on both modified shell scripts.

Related: #5506 (removed the offending assertion), #5507 (declared which readiness fields may block a release).

author: marcosach
body:
Closes #189

The partition that absorbs flow the engine never placed is made unspoofable, and the disjointness rule the Σ-invariant rests on is enforced at registration instead of assumed.

## What landed

- **`__unattributed__` is uncollidable.** The literal moves from `adapters/store/_records.py` to `domain/position.py` — three layers must agree about it and `engine`/`app` may not import an adapter (ADR-0032) — and both `StrategyConfig` and `StrategyHost.register` refuse it as a `strategy_id` (ADR-0043 §2).
- **Symbol ownership is disjoint, and enforced.** ADR-0034's rule was documented and unenforced. `StrategyHost.register` now refuses a second strategy declaring an owned symbol, naming both strategies and every colliding symbol at once, because the remedy is a separate account and a reader cannot pick which strategy to move without them.
- **`hypothesis`: Σ over every partition equals the account net**, per symbol, under an arbitrary interleaving of fills across strategies and sides, with a restart at an arbitrary point and an unattributed partition present throughout. The oracle is the test's own signed sum of the fills it fed, never a re-fold of the projection's partitions — which would be green by construction.
- **The scoped facade cannot reach the unattributed partition**, which `account_net()` still counts. Reached through a restart rather than a synthetic write, because that is how the partition actually arrives.

## From the deepening review

Ran `/improve-codebase-architecture` over the slice before opening. It surfaced one candidate worth building and one policy gap:

- **`SymbolOwnership` (`domain/ownership.py`), and a second gate at config load.** The disjointness rule had one gate, at registration — the right gate for a strategy the composition root never saw, and the wrong *only* gate for a configured overlap: `build_engine` opens the store, resolves the leverage book and constructs the venue **before** its registration loop, so a typo'd `TICKWRIGHT_STRATEGIES` created a database file (or a live signing exchange) on its way to being refused. `AppConfig` now refuses it at load, every offender in one pass. The two gates cannot share an exception — pydantic needs a `ValueError` where the registry raises `InvariantViolation` — so what they share is a `domain` value holding the index, the collision sort and the wording. Same split `LeverageBook` makes between its dead-entry check and its `Exchange.start()` bound.
  `traded_symbols` was documenting the gap rather than closing it; its `dict.fromkeys` dedupe is now unreachable from a valid config, and the test that pinned two strategies on `BTC` as legal config was rewritten onto three symbols.
- **Docs-sync.** Three documents described this slice's own gate in the future tense — ADR-0038 "that gate does not exist yet", ADR-0018 "to be enforced by this registry", the module map "unenforced today" — and ADR-0034 named the registry as the single place the rule is refused. All four are append-corrected. `CONTEXT.md` gains **Symbol ownership**.

Three further leads from the review were opened and retired rather than presented: `_owners`/`_symbols` drift (deriving on demand moves the cost, it does not concentrate), the two scoping expressions in `PortfolioProjection` (a key lookup and a filter, and #228's code), and "20 verbatim `StrategyHost(...)` constructions" (21, in six forms, varying where the tests need it). One lead is real but deferred: the `strategy_id=None` arm of `position()`/`open_positions()` has no production caller today — **adjacent to #178**, which is what will write and read that partition in production. Narrowing is not available (`str | None` is ADR-0038's partition key), so there is nothing to pre-factor.

## Scope note

The property's subject is the **construction**, not the venue link. ADR-0034 states the invariant in three terms, `Σ(per-strategy signed size) = account net = venue szi`; this suite is about the first equality only. The `= venue szi` half has no paper counterpart — the in-process venue holds no position state to disagree with — and arrives with the live reconcile cadence. The test's own module docstring says so, so a reader does not over-read it.

## Verification

`1044 passed, 29 skipped` (Postgres and live-testnet tiers auto-skip locally), `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy` (171 files), `lint-imports` 7 contracts kept.

author: antone4628
body:
The cache fingerprint governs both the mesh cache and the SEM preprocess cache, and the discretization determines the numbering itself: ContGal shares interface nodes, DiscGal duplicates them, so npoin and connijk differ for otherwise identical inputs. Without :AD in the fingerprint, switching the discretization inside one case directory can load a cache built under the other numbering — neither cache filename carries a discretization marker.

This is a latent correctness bug independent of the DG work: it affects any user switching :AD in place, and bites hardest on exactly the A/B comparisons used to show a change is behaviour-neutral.

One commit, keys-only — `:AD` added to `_CACHE_FINGERPRINT_KEYS` with a rationale comment in the annotated-key style. No schema bump needed: the key-list length comparison in `_cache_fingerprint_matches` invalidates existing caches once by itself. Behaviour-neutral for numerics; `AdvDiff/2d` (ContGal) regenerates once, then cache-hits on the second run.

This is the standalone fix from our August thread (your item 6). The CIdescription.md key-name note from the same thread turned out to be already resolved by the CI rework, so it's not included.

author: stevenmburns
body:
Part of #760 (unit 3 of the n_qp arc). The momwire half — the AK half carries
the probes and their new results.

#674's study ran entirely at a fixed `n_qp_pair = 4`, and on a crossing node the
cross-edge quadrature error is **first order** in that knob. Re-derived across
the axis it held fixed — affordable now that #762 tiled the kernels — its
conclusions do not survive.

## The foundational finding is gone

probe1's *"the K>2 composition error is clean first order under uniform
refinement at ε̃ = 1"* is the observation the whole issue was built on. At
converged quadrature **there is no composition error**:

| rung | \|fan − truth\| at q=8 | at q=32 |
|---|---:|---:|
| s1 | 0.0544 | **0.0000** |
| s2 | 0.0224 | 0.0001 |
| s3 | 0.0121 | **0.0000** |
| s4 | 0.0073 | **0.0000** |

The first-order ladder (p = 1.09, 1.17, 1.18) was measuring quadrature.

## The attribution is gone, and it was user-visible

`_ABOVE_IS_DOMINANT` told users *"the above arm's interface-adjacent mesh is the
dominant term"*, on probe2's rise-only 0.2214 Ω against mono-only 0.0171 Ω:

| `n_qp_pair` | mono-only | rise-only |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 0.0171 | **0.2214** ← what the claim was built on |
| 8 | 0.0007 | 0.0540 |
| 16 | 0.0003 | 0.0082 |
| 32 | 0.0002 | **0.0001** ← no asymmetry left |

Both arms sit at ~1e-4 Ω once quadrature converges. There is no dominant member
to name, so the message no longer names one.

## The dominant mesh axis inverts

Soil-A fan, `|base − fully graded|` against a far-mesh doubling on the same rung:

| `n_qp_pair` | node grading | far-mesh ×2 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | **10.4101** | 0.0215 |
| 8 | 4.4967 | 0.0968 ← today's default |
| 16 | 1.5628 | 0.1182 |
| 32 | 0.3025 | 0.1227 |
| 64 | **0.0782** | **0.1224** |

The far-mesh term is a *real* effect, stable at ~0.12 Ω, that q=4 hid entirely.
It overtakes node grading between q=16 and q=32. #674 concluded the node mesh
dominates; at converged quadrature the far mesh does.

## What the warning still says, and why it is not just deleted

At the shipped default of 8, grading the node **is** worth ~4.5 Ω, so the advice
is actionable and correct in direction. What was wrong is the *explanation* — it
is not a mesh convergence class — and the *omission*: raising `n_qp_pair` is the
other lever and past q≈16 the bigger one. That could not have been suggested
when the warning was written, because the kernels refused `n_qp > 8` until #762.

So the message now names two levers instead of one, drops the withdrawn
attribution, and cites #760 beside #674.

## Tests

The gate deck is unchanged and still warns. Its test now pins that the message
cites #760 and that `"dominant term"` is **absent** — a withdrawn claim should
fail loudly if it comes back. The `_FAN_GRADES` provenance comment and the
coarse-anchor docstring carry the correction rather than the old numbers; the
grading itself is untouched, because it still earns its place at the shipped
order.

`make gates` green on all seven lanes (test 4240 · pynec 10 · integration 2384 ·
slow 255 · crossgate 7 · memgate 47), warning counts at baseline.

## 目的（推奨)

ADR-0027 の公開面（Easy Auth + BFF + backend internal ingress）を Terraform で実装し、internet から直接到達できる面を frontend のみにする（Issue #194。系列の正本は `docs/operations/frontend-sse-execution-plan.md`）。

## 変更内容（推奨）

- **frontend image 経路**: `frontend/Dockerfile` 新設（Next.js standalone・node 24.18.0-slim・非 root・secret 焼き込みなし）+ `next.config.ts` に `output: "standalone"`。cutover runbook §2 を 3 イメージ（backend / backend-ops / frontend）の `DEPLOY_SHA` 共有に拡張（ADR-0027 決定 7）
- **frontend Container App**（`ca-felisaichatbot-dev-front`）: `min_replicas = 1`（決定 9）、`BACKEND_ORIGIN` env（決定 3）、`frontend_container_image` 変数（空なら未作成 = fail-closed bootstrap 第 1 段を成立させる）、安定 FQDN output `frontend_app_fqdn`（決定 8）
- **authConfigs**: azurerm 5.1.0 に該当リソースが無いため **AzAPI provider 2.12.0 の `azapi_resource`**（API `2025-07-01` stable）で子リソースとして管理（決定 1）。`excludedPaths: ["/readyz"]` で外形監視経路のみ未認証で通す
- **backend internal ingress 切替**: `backend_ingress_external` 変数（既定 true）。false で internal 化と `BACKEND_ORIGIN` の internal FQDN への付け替えが **1 回の apply で完結**する
- **`CHAT_API_KEY_CONFIG_CHECKSUM`** を frontend / backend serving 両 template に同一値で適用（ADR-0027 付随する決定）
- **手順の正本化**: `vnet-integration-cutover.md` §7（fail-closed bootstrap 3 段 = 決定 6、`READYZ_URL` 付け替え = ADR-0026 の順序、rollback、checksum 収束）、`entra-easy-auth-setup.md`（Entra 側のユーザー実行手順 = ADR-0012 の境界）
- ADR-0027 の Accepted 化 + 追記（#183 実測一致・実装確定事項）、ADR-0013 追記（`-front` 予約）、台帳 §A/§B、`production-readiness.md` §1「`/chat` の公開面」・§7「フロントエンドの配信」（execution plan §4 の同時更新ルール）

## 影響範囲（推奨）

- **対象**: `frontend/`（Dockerfile・next.config.ts のみ。アプリコード変更なし）、`terraform/ephemeral/`、`docs/`
- **非対象**: `LLM_PROVIDER` 切替・`AZURE_OPENAI_*`・seed / backfill・レート制限・SLO 数値（Issue #194 の対象外）

## PRラベル（必須）

- **type**: `type:infra`
- **area**: `area:infra`
- **risk**: `risk:high`
- **cost**: `cost:small`

<details>
<summary>影響メモ（必要時のみ）</summary>

**コスト根拠**（小/中/大の場合）: frontend 常駐 1 replica の目安 0.0769 USD/日（ops コンテナの 2026-08-29 課金実測の転用。frontend 自身の値は未実測 = ADR-0027「影響」のとおり実測で確定させる）+ ACR ストレージ増分（frontend image 数百 MB・Basic 枠 10 GiB 内）
**リスク根拠**（Medium/Highの場合）: `terraform/**` の変更 + 公開面の切替（厳密運用）。bootstrap 窓は ADR-0027 決定 6 の fail-closed 順序で塞ぐ

</details>

## 可観測性/検証 *条件付き*

**外形監視（readyz-probe）を殺さない設計**: backend を internal にすると現行 `READYZ_URL`（backend FQDN 直接）は到達不能になる。対処は **probe 対象を frontend の `/readyz` 透過 proxy（#193 実装済み）へ付け替える**（ADR-0027 決定 8）。`/readyz` は authConfigs の `excludedPaths` で未認証のまま通し、ADR-0026 の URL 契約（`^https://[^/]+/readyz$`）に適合するため workflow の変更は不要。切替は ADR-0026 の順序（probe 停止 → apply → 新 URL 検証 → `READYZ_URL` 更新 → probe 再開）で行い、**internal 切替（§7-5）より前に完了させる**（§7-3）。切替前後の probe 成功は apply セッションで実測し `docs/verification/` に記録する（別 PR）。

- ローカル実測済み: frontend image の docker build / 起動 / `GET /` 200 / `/readyz` proxy 動作 / principal 無し `POST /api/chat` 401（fail-closed）
- `terraform fmt -check` / `terraform validate`（azapi 2.12.0 で init 済み）/ `npm run lint:md` / frontend lint・test 99 件 / `check:bundle-secrets` すべて green

## ロールバック *条件付き*

`vnet-integration-cutover.md` §7-6 が正本。すべて Terraform 変数の戻しのみで完結する（`terraform destroy` / `state rm` 不使用）:

1. backend external への復帰: `TF_VAR_backend_ingress_external=true` で apply（`BACKEND_ORIGIN` も同じ apply で external FQDN へ戻る）
2. `/chat` 遮断退避: `TF_VAR_chat_disabled=true` で apply
3. frontend 破棄（fail-closed の最終退避）: `TF_VAR_frontend_container_image=""` で apply
4. `READYZ_URL` の戻しは ADR-0026 の順序で（frontend が残る限り戻し不要）

<details>
<summary>テスト結果/検証手順</summary>

- `terraform -chdir=terraform/ephemeral validate` → Success
- `npm run lint:md` → 0 issues（85 files）
- frontend: eslint 0 / vitest 99 passed / next build（standalone 出力確認）/ `check:bundle-secrets` OK
- docker build + コンテナ起動 smoke（上記）
- apply 後の実地検証（bootstrap 3 段・匿名拒否・`AADSTS50105` の対・internal 到達不能・probe 生存）は `vnet-integration-cutover.md` §7 の手順どおり実施し、`docs/verification/` に別 PR で記録する

</details>

## メモ（レビューポイント）

- `azapi_resource` の `body` スキーマ（`authConfigs@2025-07-01`）と `parent_id` の結線
- bootstrap 窓（frontend 作成〜authConfigs 適用）を `chat_disabled = true` で塞ぐ順序が §7-1〜§7-4 に固定されていること
- internal 切替後の `BACKEND_ORIGIN` を `http://<internal FQDN>` + `allow_insecure_connections = true` とした判断（ADR-0027 追記に根拠。internal FQDN への https は既定証明書のカバレッジを公式に断定できない）

author: chardot
body:
## Description

`VineBottomSheetTileMenu` was a bottom-sheet menu variant that no screen could reach. This PR deletes it and removes its row from the design-system component table, leaving a pointer to what to use instead.

It landed in #1014 (2026-01-21) as a second menu shape beside `VineBottomSheetActionMenu`, and never acquired a caller. It was also never added to the package's `bottom_sheet.dart` barrel, so its name was not even in scope for app code, which imports `package:divine_ui/divine_ui.dart` — reaching it would have required a deep `src/` import that nothing does. A repo-wide search finds no reference outside the file itself; `mobile/pubspec.yaml` is the only dependant on `divine_ui`, and the package declares no `part` directives, so there is no indirect route in either. Nothing about the running app changes.

Unreachable meant unmaintained, and it had drifted badly:

- **Inverted colours, from the original commit.** The tile colour reads `isDestructive ? <normal text> : <error red>`, so a destructive "Delete" renders in the normal colour while a harmless "Edit" renders red — the exact inverse of the doc comment's "Destructive actions are displayed in red". Present in #1014 and carried verbatim through the #6467 token migration.
- **Destructive labels could not have been red regardless.** #6467 additionally pinned the title to `colors.primaryText`, so the computed tile colour never reached the label.
- **It throws on first show, and has since two days after it landed.** The component passes `expanded: false`, which at the time correctly suppressed `VineBottomSheet`'s `if (expanded) Expanded(child: body) else body`, leaving its own `Flexible` body valid. #1037 (2026-01-23) removed that gate and wrapped the body unconditionally; from that commit on, the `Flexible` collides with the enclosing `Expanded` and Flutter raises "Competing ParentDataWidgets". Today the same unconditional wrapper lives in `_ScrollableContent` (`vine_bottom_sheet.dart:553`), reached whenever `scrollable` is left at its default `true`; `VineBottomSheetActionMenu` passes `scrollable: false` and is unaffected. This was a change underneath the component, not an oversight in it — and with no caller and no test, nothing reported the breakage.
- **A dead return contract.** `show()` is typed `Future<String?>` and accepts `selectedValue`, but the tiles invoke `data.onTap` directly without popping a value, and `selectedValue` is never read.

Deleting beats fixing here. `divine_ui` is a strict 100%-coverage package, so repairing it would mean writing tests for a component with no consumers — coverage minted for dead state. Both jobs it could do are already covered by live, tested components: `VineBottomSheetActionMenu` for icon-and-label action lists, and `VineBottomSheet.show<T>` with private tiles popping a typed result for bespoke menus (`comment_options_modal.dart`, which returns a sealed `CommentOptionResult`, is the worked example). The premise of #1014 — that a second menu shape was needed — was never realised in the seven months since.

**Related Issue:** None. Found while auditing `divine_ui` for unused surface.

## Out of Scope

- The live bottom-sheet variants (`VineBottomSheetActionMenu`, `VineBottomSheetSelectionMenu`, `VineBottomSheetPrompt`) are untouched. The action menu is the only other component with an `isDestructive` flag and its ternary is correct, so no sibling carries the same defect; the other two have no destructive concept.
- No ratchet or baseline regeneration is involved: no baseline references this file, and the design-system ceilings scan `mobile/lib`, not `mobile/packages`.

## Verification

- `flutter test --coverage` from `mobile/packages/divine_ui` — 977 tests pass. Coverage is unchanged by this diff: the file had no test importing it, so it never appeared in `lcov.info` at all. (One line in `divine_heart_text.dart`, untouched here, reports uncovered under a plain local run; the package is green under CI's `very_good test --optimization` run on `main`.)
- `flutter analyze` clean for the package and for the app (`lib test integration_test`).
- Repo-wide `git grep` for the type names and the filename returns nothing outside the deleted file.
- The defects above were confirmed by rendering the component in a throwaway harness (not committed) — the colour inversion and the ParentDataWidget exception are observed, not inferred.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🧹 Code refactor
- [x] 📝 Documentation

author: jbdamask
body:
Closes #289. Refs #295. Adds [ADR-0018](docs/adr/0018-a-tool-file-is-a-sibling-of-a-pack-file.md).

## What this does

Rocky Surf had skills for authoring a whole Surge Pack and for adding a cloud, but none for the
unit people trade most often: a single tool. This adds `register-a-tool`, plus the artefact that
makes a tool shareable at all.

**Most of the "personal tools registry" the issue asked for already existed.** The `tools` table,
`/api/v1/admin/tools` CRUD and the Tools page have been there since the SPA port, with `sourceFile`
as the seam — non-null means a `packs/*.yaml` owns the row and boot rewrites it, null means it was
created here. What was missing was an artefact at tool granularity, and a name for the split the UI
already implemented. So the registry work here is mostly naming and sharing, not new storage.

### The format

A **tool file** is `version: 1` plus a list of tools, reusing `toolSchema` **verbatim** — so a tool
moves between a pack file and a tool file as a copy, not a translation.

- `GET /api/v1/admin/tools/:toolId/export` renders one for any tool, file-backed included, and
  strips `sourceFile`.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/tools/import` takes one back, writes `sourceFile: null`, and **refuses** an id
  a file-backed tool owns — the boot reconcile would undo that win at the next restart anyway, so a
  409 that explains itself beats a silent revert.
- `bootstrap` stays in the shared shape for interop, and `true` is refused on import in `lint.ts`'s
  own words.
- A pasted **pack** file is answered with a message naming the right door, rather than
  `Unrecognized key: "pack"`.

### Import is paste/upload only — no URL arm

Deliberate, and the one place the two formats differ. A pack records where a URL import came from
(`registrySource`/`registryUrl`/`registrySha256`), because #88 established that "where did this
shell that runs as root on my boxes come from?" is the question an operator needs answered. The
`tools` table has no such columns, so a URL arm would install root-privileged shell while being
structurally unable to say anything true about its origin. Follow-up issue filed for the columns.

### A bug found on the way

`servers.tools` — the explicit per-server selection that overrides a pack's list — was never
validated. The plan resolver drops an id it cannot find, which is correct when re-rendering an old
row and wrong as the answer to a fresh request: a create naming a misspelled tool **launched a
machine, billed for it, and quietly installed less than was asked for**. It now 400s before the
provider is touched, mirroring the existing `checkTools`.

### Scope

A tool reaches a box **only through a pack** (owner ruling). Pack personalisation — adding a tool to
chosen packs, to all packs, the modded-official-pack UI — is #295, and none of it is here. **No
migrations.**

## How this was verified

- Full gate green: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r test`
  (core alone: 78 files, 1561 tests).
- **The new validation tests were checked against a sabotaged build** — disabling the `tools` check
  turns exactly the three intended tests red, so they are not passing for free.
- **The skill's verification recipe was run against the real CLI**, not asserted: the wrapper pack
  lints clean with no `--base-packs`, and passing a wrong `--base-packs` reproduces the exact
  "unknown tool" failure the reference documents. No harness change was needed — `pack check`
  already resolves base tools against the bundled packs.
- New tests: tool-file round trips including block-scalar edge cases (trailing whitespace, tabs,
  CRLF, a script line that itself parses as YAML), cross-installation export→import byte identity,
  the file-backed 409, the pack-file redirect, `bootstrap: true`, unknown-key and `sourceFile`
  rejection, `servers.tools` validation, and an end-to-end register → pack → `snapshotInstallPlan`
  emitting `tool:<id>` in the right band.
- `scripts/check-skills-index.mjs` now fails the lint if a skill directory is not listed in the
  skills README — it caught its own motivating bug, the Help page saying "two skills" while three
  shipped. That count is now gone from the page entirely, per
  `docs/memories/2026-08-13-measured-numbers-in-prose.md`.

Docker smoke was not run for this PR: it changes no pack file and no bootstrap step.

body:
[AUTO-ESCALATED: cold read rejected 2x] — The src/modules/host-rpc/index.ts change (onShutdown → onHostShutdown, response-registry.js → host-lifecycle.js) appears in the resolution diff but has no corresponding conflict hunk and is not listed among the conflicted paths. Either this file had a conflict that was omitted from the case materials, or the resolver introduced an out-of-band edit. Provide the conflict hunk for this file or justif

## What this merge is
`module/agent-group-contributions` → `module/host-rpc` at height 239. Upstream adds the post-delivery hook (`registerDeliveryBatchPreview`), the `containerStartedAtMs` heartbeat fallback in the stuck-container SLA check, plugin MCP server support in the agent-runner, a signal-cleanup fix in the poll-loop, and the host-lifecycle registry (`onHostStart`/`onHostShutdown`/`startHostModules`/`stopHostModules`) as a breaking replacement for `onShutdown`/`getShutdownCallbacks` in `response-registry.ts`.

## Resolutions

### `container/agent-runner/src/index.ts`

<details>
<summary>ours vs theirs vs chosen</summary>

**ours (`module/host-rpc`)** — imports `runPollLoop` and `requestGracefulStop` from `poll-loop.js`.

**theirs (`module/agent-group-contributions`)** — imports `resolvePluginServer` and `McpServerConfig` (plugin support) from new files, drops `requestGracefulStop` from `poll-loop.js`.

**chosen** — union: keep `requestGracefulStop` from ours (still used by our graceful-drain path) and add `resolvePluginServer` + `McpServerConfig` from theirs.

</details>

### `container/agent-runner/src/poll-loop.ts`

<details>
<summary>ours vs theirs vs chosen</summary>

**ours (`module/host-rpc`)** — sets `currentQuery = null` in the `finally` block.

**theirs (`module/agent-group-contributions`)** — removes the abort-event listener (`config.signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abortActiveQuery)`) in the `finally` block.

**chosen** — both: both cleanups belong in `finally`. No semantic conflict.

</details>

### `src/container-runner.ts`

<details>
<summary>ours vs theirs vs chosen</summary>

**ours (`module/host-rpc`)** — imports `ContainerQueue`/`EvictionCandidate` and `getSession`; `ActiveContainer` interface has rich liveness fields (`spawnedAt`, `heartbeatMtimeMs`, `hasOutstandingClaim`); `activeContainers.set` fills all five fields and calls `queue.releaseReserve`.

**theirs (`module/agent-group-contributions`)** — adds `CONTAINER_PLUGINS_DIR` import; `ActiveContainer` simplified to `{ process, containerName, startedAtMs }` with no queue fields; `activeContainers.set` uses the simplified shape.

**chosen** — ours for the `ActiveContainer` interface and `activeContainers.set` (the queue requires `spawnedAt`, `heartbeatMtimeMs`, and `hasOutstandingClaim`); theirs' `CONTAINER_PLUGINS_DIR` added to ours' imports. `getContainerStartedAtMs` (added by theirs outside the hunk) referenced `startedAtMs` but our interface uses `spawnedAt` — corrected to `spawnedAt`.

</details>

### `src/delivery.ts`

<details>
<summary>ours vs theirs vs chosen</summary>

**ours (`module/host-rpc`)** — `for (const msg of deliverable)` — iterates only non-paused messages.

**theirs (`module/agent-group-contributions`)** — adds a `batchPreviewHooks` loop over `deliverable` before per-message processing, then changes the delivery loop to `for (const msg of undelivered)`.

**chosen** — theirs' batch preview hooks block added (using `deliverable` for the preview map, consistent with the delivery loop); delivery loop stays `for (const msg of deliverable)` to preserve the paused-channel filter. Theirs' change from `deliverable` to `undelivered` in the loop is not adopted — no evidence the paused-channel guard was moved elsewhere.

</details>

### `src/host-sweep.test.ts`

<details>
<summary>ours vs theirs vs chosen</summary>

**ours (`module/host-rpc`)** — test name `'returns kill-ceiling when heartbeat older than the idle backstop'`; declares a `heartbeatMtimeMs` local variable that is never used (dead code from a prior refactor).

**theirs (`module/agent-group-contributions`)** — test name `'returns kill-ceiling when heartbeat exceeds the absolute ceiling'`; no dead variable.

**chosen** — theirs: cleaner name and no dead local. The assertion body is identical once the dead variable is removed.

</details>

### `src/host-sweep.ts`

<details>
<summary>ours vs theirs vs chosen</summary>

**ours (`module/host-rpc`)** — imports `isContainerRunning`, `killContainer`, `recordContainerLiveness`, `wakeContainer` from `container-runner.js` plus `EVICTION_TIMEOUT` from `config.js`; passes `heartbeatMtimeMs: hbMtimeMs` to `decideStuckAction`.

**theirs (`module/agent-group-contributions`)** — imports `getContainerStartedAtMs`, `isContainerRunning`, `killContainer`, `wakeContainer`; adds `containerStartedAtMs: getContainerStartedAtMs(session.id)` to `decideStuckAction`; removes `recordContainerLiveness`/`EVICTION_TIMEOUT`.

**chosen** — union of import sets (all of ours' functions are still called; `getContainerStartedAtMs` from theirs is needed for the fallback feature; `EVICTION_TIMEOUT` stays because it's used at `ABSOLUTE_CEILING_MS = EVICTION_TIMEOUT`); `heartbeatMtimeMs: hbMtimeMs` from ours (already computed at line 329 — calling the function twice would double the `fs.statSync`); `containerStartedAtMs: getContainerStartedAtMs(session.id)` added from theirs.

</details>

## Scope

One file outside the 6 conflicted paths was touched as a follow-on fix. This is what escalated the case to held.

**`src/modules/host-rpc/index.ts`** (owned path for `module/host-rpc`): The `onShutdown` function was removed from `response-registry.ts` by upstream's lifecycle migration. This file imported `onShutdown` and called it to register the RPC server shutdown handler. Replaced with `onHostShutdown` from `host-lifecycle.js` — the direct equivalent under the new lifecycle API.

The owner should confirm: is this migration to `onHostShutdown` acceptable as written, or should it be restructured differently?

## Verification
Typecheck passed (`pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit`) after all fixes. Tests ran via `report-case`. Cold-read rejected twice due to the out-of-scope owned-path change; case held per doctrine.

body:
## Summary

- Document the corrected authentication and startup behavior, including the exact `x-sn-apikey` header, authentication precedence, startup validation, stdio launch, working-directory behavior, and process restart requirements.
- Document the read-only attachment split: `attachment` provides reads, while upload and delete require the separate `attachment_write` group and runtime write gates.
- Document the read-only `analysis` capabilities for submitted RITM variables and bounded journal history.
- Document inherited `describe` field resolution, child overrides, provenance, selection, and pagination.
- Rewrite the README as the complete operator and tool reference, and update `INSTALL.md` as the focused installation and troubleshooting guide.

## Security and compatibility

- API-key mode sends `x-sn-apikey` and does not combine it with Basic Auth.
- ServiceNow API-resource policies, row ACLs, and field ACLs remain the authorization boundaries. MCP package selection does not grant access.
- Sensitive RITM answers are masked. Missing variable metadata causes conservative masking.
- Reference and List Collector values remain raw identifiers. Multi-row variable set payloads are not retrieved or decoded.
- Read-only verification did not perform ServiceNow writes.
- The guides cover Python 3.12-3.14, MCP SDK v2, `uv` source checkout, and managed-package launch considerations.

## Verification

Reviewed work was verified with:

- `uv run pytest` — 894 passed.
- Focused authentication, startup, package, attachment, analysis, inherited-describe, dictionary, audit, and record-write tests — passed.
- `uv run ruff check .` — passed.
- `uv run ruff format --check .` — passed.
- `uv run mypy src/` — passed.
- `uv build` — passed.
- Markdown structure, links, anchors, fenced blocks, tables, examples, and cross-file claims — validated.
- Live MCP verification used read-only calls only and performed no ServiceNow writes.

**점수는 단 1점도 바꾸지 않았다.** 문자열 교체 3곳 + relicNames 배열 스키마 수정뿐이며, 기존 검증 3종이 그대로 통과하는 것이 그 증거다(아래 실행 결과).

### 커밋 ① logic.js — 문구 모순 해소
같은 카드에 `+0.8 소진 빌드에 적합`과 `-0.9 사혈 카드라 소진 빌드와 안 맞음`이 동시 표시되던 문제(실측 24/289장). 두 문구는 서로 다른 신호(태그 시너지=효과 vs builds=소속)에서 나오며 점수 합산은 의도대로다. 문구만 층위가 구분되게 교체:
- 216행: `X 빌드에 적합` → `X 덱에서 효과가 잘 맞음`
- 336행: `Y 카드라 X 빌드와 안 맞음` → `원래 Y 빌드용 카드 (현재 덱은 X)`
- 874행(제거 추천): 어투 통일 `빌드 밖 카드 — 원래 Y 빌드용 (현재 덱은 X)`

## Summary
- **Feed GitHub**: root cause trovata e verificata contro l'API reale — l'Events API tronca l'oggetto `pull_request` (niente `title`, niente `html_url`, niente flag `merged`; l'`action` restituito è ora `"merged"`, non `"closed"`) e restituisce `PushEvent.payload.commits` vuoto per i push fatti tramite API (come un merge via GitHub API, non un `git push` diretto). L'API rispondeva 200 ma il payload non conteneva mai i dati attesi, quindi il feed restava sempre vuoto. Sostituito con l'endpoint `/commits`, che espone sempre `message` e `html_url`.
- **Salti "finti"**: la fisica a gravità del salto automatico (introdotta nella PR precedente) era corretta ma non aveva nessun feedback d'impatto sui rimbalzi — a differenza del lancio manuale, che ha squash/suono/animazione "dropped" a ogni atterraggio. Senza quel riscontro tattile il movimento, per quanto fisicamente corretto, si leggeva come un galleggiamento innaturale. Aggiunto lo stesso linguaggio visivo/sonoro del lancio (squash 1.32/0.7 sul pavimento, squash 0.75/1.3 sulle pareti della zona, animazione `dropped`) a ogni rimbalzo sopra soglia.

## Test plan
- [x] `node --check script.js`
- [x] Feed GitHub verificato con dati REALI dell'API (`/commits` reale, salvati e rigiocati via route mock): 8 commit filtrati/deduplicati correttamente, merge commit esclusi
- [x] Confermato via curl diretto che `api.github.com` risponde 200 con lo shape atteso
- [x] Playwright: durante un salto automatico, `--mascot-squash-x/y` passa a `1.32,0.7` e la classe `dropped` si attiva — prima restavano sempre a `1,1`/assenti
- [x] Playwright: traiettoria del salto ancora ad arco reale (sale poi scende), rimbalzo di riposo confermato dopo l'atterraggio
- [x] Hugging Face/Hacker News non raggiungibili dal sandbox di test (policy dell'ambiente, non del sito) — non toccati in questa PR, nessuna regressione attesa
- [x] Nessun errore console

author: twcook
body:
The repository said **MIT** in its `LICENSE`, its badge, and five places in prose, while the organisation README and semanticdatacharter.com both said **Apache-2.0**, and every sibling implementation (`sdcvalidator`, `sdcgovernance`, `sdcreceipt`) ships Apache-2.0.

An enterprise legal reviewer reading those surfaces together finds an unresolved licence conflict on the reference model itself, which is unquantified IP risk sitting on the one artifact the whole stack points at.

## Why Apache-2.0 and not MIT

§3. A reference model is only worth adopting if adopting it is safe, and the express patent licence from every contributor is the part that says so. MIT grants no patent rights at all.

That the tooling was already Apache-2.0 while the model it implements was not is the wrong way round.

## Changed

- `LICENSE` — full Apache License 2.0 text, copyright `2025 Axius SDC, Inc.`
- `README.md` — badge, licence section, and the file-tree comment
- `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/FAQ.md`, `sdc4/examples/README.md`

Also corrects the copyright holder: `LICENSE` named Axius SDC, Inc. while the README's inline text named "Semantic Data Charter", which is the specification, not the legal entity.

## Not changed

**No schema, model, or normative content. SDC4 remains frozen.** This is repository licensing only.

## Loose end

`sdc5-planning` has `sdc5/examples/README.md` still reading "All examples are MIT licensed." That file does not exist on `main`, so it could not be swept here. It needs fixing on the next `main` → `sdc5-planning` merge.

Surfaced by Timothy Lee's advisory review, 2026-09-01.

author: posidev-coding
body:
## The bug

Every public room the reader joined last Saturday was still stacked in **Where you play** this week, above their own groups, labeled "Public room · this Saturday". A public room is a *transient* contest — one Saturday, then it's over — so carrying it forward tells the reader they are already seated in this Saturday's public contests, when the whole point is that a fresh week starts with the decision unmade.

The `past` flag was read off the week id:

```php
'past' => $group->isRoom() && $group->week_id !== $weekId,
```

2026's Week 1 holds **two** Saturdays (8/29 and 9/5), so a room that played 8/29 still satisfied `week_id === $weekId` on the Tuesday after. Reproduced in the dev database: rooms 17/18/19 all carry `week_id = 94` with slates dated `2026-08-29`, while the card being sold is 9/5.

## The change

**`past` is read off the room's own Saturday**, compared to the card being sold — the rule every other read on this screen already follows (`.ai/rules/views-livewire-support.md`). `cards()` picks up the room contests' slate Saturdays in one lean query (dates only, no eager loads, and only when the reader holds a public seat at all).

The Saturdays come back as **date strings**: `slates.saturday` casts at the app's timezone while the active Saturday is an ET midnight, so comparing the two as instants makes the same Saturday four hours "earlier" and files a *live* room under played.

- `roomCards` keeps only rooms still on the card; new `pastRooms` collects the played ones and never renders as cards.
- A room with **no slate at all** is still not past — its card was never published or was taken away, which is `group.room.no_card`, a different sentence. Never infer "played" from a missing row.
- **Nothing is deleted.** The membership, the room's leaderboard and its URL all outlive it.

The played rooms leave behind **one door to History** — already the screen that holds every settled week, already in the Picks strip — carrying the count and a Voice line in all three registers that says the rule out loud. `picks.whereplay.subheading` stops promising "every seat you hold" and says what the stack now is.

`group-card`'s "Saturday played" branch stays as a guard rather than a display path, so whoever renders a past card next inherits the right words instead of the lie.

## Verified

- Full suite green: **2,507 tests, 8,625 assertions**.
- Three tests in `PickemHomeTest` cover it: the split-week case (the actual bug), a room whose whole week is behind us, and a reader whose only room is live — who sees no door at all.
- **Broken back**: reverting `past` to the week-id rule fails the split-week test with `pastRooms` empty. It fails for the right reason.
- Checked at 390px in the device harness with the three rooms temporarily seated — only the private group renders under Where you play, with the History door beneath. The temporary memberships were removed afterward.

## Known gap

History lists **settled** entries, so a room joined but never picked in leaves no row there — which is why the door's line says "your settled weeks are in History" rather than promising those specific rooms. Making an unplayed paid seat recoverable is a separate change to History's query.

author: kenams
urunge
body:
Closes #219

비밀번호 상한을 32 → 30 으로 조정하고, 이름 칸에 「한글·영문만」 규칙을 추가합니다.

공백을 허용하지 않습니다 — 「김 진형」과 「김진형」이 같은 사람인데 다르게 저장되면
관리자 콘솔 검색에서 갈립니다. 영문 이름은 붙여 씁니다.

이름 검사는 **제출 시점에만** 합니다. 이메일 칸처럼 입력 시점에 지우면 한글 IME 조합 중인
낱자가 찍는 족족 지워져 한글을 아예 입력할 수 없습니다.

두 화면에 복사돼 있던 이름 검사를 `shared/lib/name.ts` 의 `validateName` 으로 합쳤습니다
(`validatePhoneNumber`·`validateBirthDate` 와 같은 방식).

**마이그레이션 없습니다.** DB 컬럼은 그대로입니다.

## 착수 전 실측 — 기존 이름 2건이 걸렸고, 고치고 진행했습니다

새 규칙은 회원가입뿐 아니라 **마이페이지 「기본정보 수정」도 같은 검사를 탑니다.**
규칙을 어기는 이름을 가진 기존 회원은 **이름에 손도 안 댔는데 전화번호 저장이 막힙니다.**
그래서 먼저 세어봤습니다.

```
전체 29명 / 새 규칙 위반 2명
  id=50  name='verify-ok'      email=login89@example.com   status=SUSPENDED
  id=51  name='verify-locked'  email=locked89@example.com  status=SUSPENDED
```

조사해 보니 **실사용 계정이 아니라 E2E 시드 계정**이었습니다.

- 같은 초에 일괄 생성됐고 이메일이 `login89`/`locked89` — 이슈 #89 작업 때 만든 것
- `login-real-api.spec.ts:15-16` 이 이 이메일을 픽스처로 쓰지만 **이름은 참조하지 않습니다**
  (이메일·비밀번호·상태만 씁니다)
- 이 이름을 생성하는 코드가 저장소에 없습니다 — 수동으로 만든 로컬 데이터입니다

**두 계정의 이름을 `검증정상`·`검증정지` 로 고치고 진행했습니다.** 고친 뒤 위반 0건을 확인했습니다.
마이페이지 수정 경로만 예외로 두는 방안은 두 화면의 규칙이 갈리게 되어 택하지 않았습니다.

> ⚠️ **제 로컬 DB 기준입니다.** 운영이나 다른 분들의 DB에 실사용자 이름이 걸릴 가능성은
> 확인할 수 없었습니다. 배포 전에 같은 쿼리로 한 번 확인해 주세요.

## ⚠️ HTML `pattern` 을 쓰지 않은 이유

이메일 칸은 `pattern` 을 쓰지만 이름 칸에는 쓸 수 없습니다.

- **한글 조합이 깨집니다** — 조합 중에는 값에 `ㄱ` 이 들어 있어 타이핑 내내 「형식 불일치」가 됩니다
- **문구를 못 고칩니다** — 브라우저 기본 문구는 「요청한 형식과 일치시키세요」입니다(#181 에서 겪음)
- 다른 칸은 칸 아래 문구인데 이름만 말풍선이 뜹니다

`sanitizeEmailInput` 처럼 입력 시점에 지우는 방식도 쓰지 않았습니다. **한글을 아예 못 칩니다.**
이 차이를 `name.ts` 주석에 남겨 두었습니다.

## ⚠️ `UserUpdateRequest.name` 은 선택 필드입니다

그냥 `AfterValidator` 를 붙이면 「이름을 안 보낸」 요청이 `None` 을 검사하다 죽습니다.
그러면 이름을 건드리지 않고 전화번호만 바꾸려는 사용자가 **저장 자체를 못 하게 됩니다.**
같은 파일의 `phone_number` 선례대로 `optional_after_validator` 를 썼고, **회귀 테스트로 고정**했습니다.

## 서버·프론트 공백 처리

서버 DTO 가 `strip_whitespace=True` 라 검증기는 이미 다듬어진 값을 봅니다.
프론트도 `trim()` 후에 검사하고, **검사한 값과 같은 값을 보내도록** `name.trim()` 으로 맞췄습니다.
안 맞추면 프론트만 거부하고 서버는 받아주는 상태가 됩니다.

## 검증

### 테스트

`test_name_rules.py` 8건 추가. 허용 5종(`김진형`·`KimJinhyeong`·`김Kim`·`AB`·`홍길`),
거부 7종(공백·숫자·낱자·한자·이모지·하이픈·특수문자), 앞뒤 공백 trim, 마이페이지 거부/허용,
그리고 **핵심 회귀 방지** — `name` 없이 `phoneNumber` 만 보내는 요청이 성공하는지.

E2E 1건 추가 — 잘못된 이름이 **입력 시점에 지워지지 않고** 제출 때 오류가 뜨는지.

### 기존 테스트 중 새 규칙에 걸린 픽스처

지우지 않고 이름만 규칙에 맞게 고쳤습니다.

- `app/tests/alarm_apis/helpers.py` — `알람 API 사용자` → `알람테스트사용자`
- `app/tests/med_apis/helpers.py` — `영양제 테스트 사용자` → `영양제테스트사용자`
- `entry-home-auth.spec.ts` — `신규 사용자` → `신규사용자`
- `signup-real-api-contract.spec.ts` — `테스트 회원` → `테스트회원`
- `api.mock.ts` — `RxVita 사용자` → `RxVita사용자`

(관리자·영양제·OCR 쪽 이름은 `validate_name` 을 타지 않아 그대로입니다.)

### 브라우저 실측

```
[한글 IME 조합]  ← 가장 중요
  조합 중 "ㄱ" -> "ㄱ"      입력 시점에 지워지지 않음
  조합 중 "기" -> "기"
  조합 중 "김" -> "김"

[제출 시점 검사]
  김 진형      -> 값 유지 / 오류 표시 O
  김진형2      -> 값 유지 / 오류 표시 O
  ㅋㅋㅋ       -> 값 유지 / 오류 표시 O
  金鎭亨       -> 값 유지 / 오류 표시 O
  KimJinhyeong -> 오류 없음

[비밀번호 30]
  회원가입 40자 -> 30      로그인 40자 -> 40 (상한 없음)

[마이페이지]
  이름 그대로 두고 전화번호만 저장 -> 성공
  이름을 「김 진형」으로 저장       -> 막힘
```

### 명령

- `pytest app` — **586 passed**, 실패 0
- `pytest app/tests tests` — **702 passed**, 3 failed (기존)
- `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` — 통과
- `tsc --noEmit` — 통과
- `playwright test` — **134 passed, 실패 0**

프론트 실패가 0이 된 것은 main 에서 들어온 `helpers/mode.ts` 가 실 API 전용 스펙을
건너뛰게 만들었기 때문입니다. 백엔드 3건은 기존 실패입니다
(`test_async_ocr_migration`, `test_user_settings_...`, 사이드바 CSS — 다른 담당 구역).

[AUTO-ESCALATED: checks failing] — cannot be fixed within the case's named files (src/cli/resources/groups.create.test.ts, container/agent-runner/src/poll-loop.test.ts)

The gate-fix case was derived at main_patched height 169 (`c3f1b0fa`), but both failing tests are already fixed at height 239 (`a815c7af`). The worktree arrived clean; no edit was made. Owner action: verify that `pnpm test` and `bun test` are green at the current tip, then close this PR.

## What is broken

**`pnpm test`** (host): `src/cli/resources/groups.create.test.ts` — `ncl groups create --folder orphan` (no `--name`) passes at height 169 because the handler has `const name = (args.name as string) ?? folder`, silently using the folder slug. The test expected `ok: true` and accepted it; a second, stricter test expecting `ok: false` on folder-only args does not yet exist at that height.

**`bun test`** (container): `container/agent-runner/src/poll-loop.test.ts` — `expect(nudges).toHaveLength(2)` fails; only 1 nudge is emitted. Root cause: `taskBlockNudged` is never reset between task runs, so the second task turn is silently skipped. The test timed out at 8 s without ever reaching the assertion (10 s deadline = 10 s vitest timeout).

## The fix (`main_patched`)

### `src/cli/resources/groups.create.test.ts`

Already fixed by PR #102 (`ca6ae304`, merged at `fffea883`): `groups.ts` changed to `if (!name) throw new Error('--name is required')`, and the test updated to add a second case (folder-only args) — both expecting `ok: false`. No edit is needed here.

### `container/agent-runner/src/poll-loop.test.ts`

Already fixed by PR #99 (`becc101b`): `poll-loop.ts` gained `taskBlockNudged = false` at the follow-up task dispatch path so the second turn always nudges. PR #110 (`3e61ebd4` / `cda19713`) then extended the test deadline to 15 s and the vitest timeout to 20 s, ensuring the diagnostic throw reaches the assertion on slow CI runners. No edit is needed here.

## Scope

This is a GATE FIX: it repairs a pre-existing defect, it resolves no merge conflict. The worktree was clean on delivery — no files were changed. The entire fix lives in the merged branch history (PRs #99, #102, #110).

## Verification

## Summary

body:
Ari's direction: when an address is listed wrongly, it's better for the publication to correct it in their own database — so the next export stops flagging it — than to teach this system to ignore it, and that option should be on every Voice question.

**What changed**

- Every question the publication's office can answer now carries **"We will correct this in our own system — the next export won't have it"** (`will_fix_at_source`), replacing the two per-kind variants that said the same thing.
- The choice carries its own lifecycle, closing a hole it would otherwise open: every other answer is a standing fact, so an unchanged question stays answered when it re-arises — but a will-fix answer is a *promise about the next export*. If the same question arises again at all, the fix didn't land, so it **reopens regardless of the fingerprint**, and the card says "You said this would be corrected in your system, but this week's list still shows it." Fixing the source stays the happy path: the question never re-arises and the next clean apply retires it.
- Pinned in rls.sh (62/62); node tests 99/99; build and lint clean. Migration already applied to production.

author: gaborbernat
body:
[`sanitizer-address (2/8)`](https://github.com/tox-dev/peryx/actions/runs/33390601731/job/99488178147) failed in the failover case from #1958. OpenRaft gives a vote RPC 300 ms. That case put three Raft cores, three HTTP listeners, and their clients on Tokio's one-thread test runtime, where AddressSanitizer overhead serialized vote senders with their HTTP receivers; both survivors missed replacement elections throughout the 10-second observation window.

Peryx processes run listeners and consensus on separate runtimes. Four Tokio worker threads give the failover case the same scheduling shape under instrumentation while leaving election and observation limits unchanged. The case keeps the original assertion that a committed control-key release survives leader loss.

author: saedx1
body:
## Problem

The CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` response was a **fixed list**. supabase-js
adds request headers over time, and the current one — `x-supabase-api-version` —
was **not** in the list, so browsers blocked the preflight of *every* cross-origin
request (auth, rest, functions, storage) with:

> Request header field x-supabase-api-version is not allowed by
> Access-Control-Allow-Headers in preflight response.

Same-origin apps never send a preflight, so this stayed latent until a backend-only
app with a separate browser frontend hit it.

## Fix

Reflect the preflight's `Access-Control-Request-Headers` into
`Access-Control-Allow-Headers`, falling back to the known supabase/PostgREST set
(now including `x-supabase-api-version`) when the preflight names none. This keeps
CORS correct for any supabase-js version without chasing new header names.

Only `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` changes — origin gating and the
never-set `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` are untouched.

## This matches Supabase's own behavior

- **Kong** (Supabase's gateway) configures the CORS plugin with no `headers` field,
  so Kong **reflects** `Access-Control-Request-Headers`.
- **PostgREST** reflects the requested headers too (`src/library/PostgREST/Cors.hs`).
- **GoTrue** uses a fixed list but explicitly added `X-Supabase-Api-Version` after
  hitting this exact bug (`supabase/auth#1589`).

## Security

Reviewed: safe. `Allow-Headers` doesn't gate response reads (that's `Allow-Origin`,
unchanged) and doesn't authenticate. With no `Allow-Credentials` and bearer-token
auth (no ambient cookies), reflecting the requested header *names* grants a
cross-origin page no capability it didn't already have; RLS still gates all data.
Go's `net/http` rejects CR/LF in response header values, so the reflected value
can't split headers.

## Tests

`internal/adapter/http/middleware_test.go`: a preflight with
`x-supabase-api-version` gets it reflected back; the no-requested-headers path
serves the known fallback set. Full `http` package tests + `go vet` pass.

author: hbleiberg
body:
Two improvement-loop sessions on one branch, each at full 5-iteration budget. **S308 continued here because PR #215 was still open and unmerged** (verified via the API before any work, per protocol).

**Six decision gates asked across the two sessions; all six answered, none deferred.**

---

# S308 — Pass I (first-load & empty-state), clean, and it closed an open question

## Iteration 1 — the pass

I's mechanical gates have now run clean **eleven consecutive times**, so the value was never going to be in re-running them. The S308 pointer supplied two weighted arms aimed at S307's own freshly-shipped surfaces, plus one open question — and the question got an answer.

| Arm | Result |
|---|---|
| Mechanical gates — 26 virgin loads (13 pages × EN/HE, empty localStorage **and** IndexedDB) | 0 pageerrors / 0 same-origin failures / 0 4xx / 0 raw i18n keys, `lang`+`dir` **26/26**; both detectors proven able to fire |
| S307's decision footer on a genuinely virgin profile, 4 cells | Store measurably **absent** beforehand; a **real click** on "Use in IvritSuite" writes `Reuben` at **exactly 12,608 bytes — the served file's own size** |
| Cross-tool payoff, same profile | The dictionary's picker shows a **"My Fonts" / "הגופנים שלי" header first**, Reuben its first option, 12 → 13 |
| `uiLang`/`darkMode` import on a profile that never chose a language | `null/null` → `he`/`1` → reload renders `lang=he dir=rtl dark=true`. `xx`, `../en`, `HE`, `''`, `en-US` rejected; `he` accepted; `darkMode` takes only `'1'`/`'0'` and `'0'` survives |
| **The open question** | **Answered with receipts** — see below |

**`_ivLangOk`'s `['en','he']` fallback is live on one path and dead on the other.** With `/js/i18n.js` blocked, `importAllSettings` throws `ReferenceError: I18n is not defined` at its *own* `confirm(I18n.t(…))` before ever reaching the `uiLang` line, and stores nothing — the fallback is unreachable there. `IVRIT_CFG.apply` reaches it with `window.I18n` undefined and works. First observation of that fallback firing, and its one real carrier is the `.ivrit` restore — which is also the suite's preferred backup mechanism, so the coverage sits on the right path.

## Iteration 2 — switching language no longer renames the font you are looking at

Found while grounding the micro-feature. `#fontPreviewTitle` carries `data-i18n` and `openFontPreview` overwrites it with the font's **name**, so `applyStaticI18n` put the generic "Preview" back: a teacher comparing fonts who switched to Hebrew watched **"TzviScript" become "תצוגה מקדימה"**, losing the one label saying which font was on screen.

Fixed first, so the feature landed on correct ground. The by-line was the firing control — it re-localized correctly throughout, proving the modal was alive and only the title was being stomped. Closed-modal control passes.

## Iterations 3–4 — micro-feature: compare fonts without leaving the preview

Gate 1; the maintainer chose the pointer's first offer. Two chevrons step through the gallery, so the decision happens where the specimen and licence already are. `filteredFonts()` extracted as the single definition of "which fonts are on screen right now", read by both grid and modal, so the stepper can never reach a hidden font or stop short of a shown one. Ends disable rather than wrap; under two matches the group hides; stepping deliberately does **not** re-select the sample field, so typed text survives a walk; a chevron disabling at either end hands focus to its sibling. **84 lines**, inside the fence.

**RTL measured, not eyeballed** — the screenshot misled on first read. In Hebrew prev sits at x=645 and next at x=561: the order mirrors *and* both glyphs flip. No new localStorage key and no IndexedDB, so nothing to register in AllTools or `.ivrit`.

## Iteration 5 — a translation key nothing has ever read

The suite's last untranslated cell, and the fix was the opposite of the one the S259 measurement implied. `worksheet.layout.title_default` is referenced **nowhere**: every other `worksheet.layout.*` key has exactly one use site, this one had zero, nothing builds it dynamically, and it was minted in the first localization commit and never wired. It was meant for the worksheet title default — printed output, which correctly stays a literal.

So the key goes, with the allowlist entry that existed only to excuse it. `build-locales` now reports **"all 5120 keys translated in every language"** for the first time — controlled by blanking a real Hebrew cell and watching the detector name it.

## The method yield — a fourth "the probe lied" rule, wearing a shipped P1's face

Measuring "is IndexedDB empty?" with `indexedDB.open(name)` and **no version** *creates* the database at v1 with no object store; the app's own `open(name, 1)` then gets no upgrade event and every write throws `NotFoundError`. That made "Use in IvritSuite" fail in all four cells with the page's own genuine error toast — on a feature shipped the session before. It reads as a regression. The tell: total identical failure in every cell while the same steps pass when run directly.

---

# S307 — Pass D (Torah Trainer), clean in every arm

Its first dedicated performance profile since S184/S185 (~122 sessions). Control first: a real `page.click` on a 450 ms busy loop produced `[452]`, so every zero is earned. S297 handle assertions caught **two false zeros before they counted** — `loadParsha` and `showReading` do not exist.

| Arm | Result |
|---|---|
| Cold load, 8 cells | **0 blocks >200 ms at either rate** (max 142 ms) |
| Full parsha — 176 verses / 2,688 words / 4,631 nodes / 325 KB | 735 ms @1×, 910 ms @4×, **0 longtasks** |
| Karaoke paint, 1,200 ticks | **4 µs/tick @1×, 10 µs @4×** |
| `clearKaraokeHighlight` over 2,688 words | 0.8–5.2 ms — the code comment's "cheap" claim, verified |
| Idle 10 s (the projected-board arm) | **0 longtasks, 0 DOM mutations** |
| Leak check, 60 re-renders | **None** — post-GC listeners flat at 1,070, Δ0 |

Plus the font-preview decision footer (`ff977f9`), printed chrome made uniform across all six chrome pages (`848fed9`), and `hebrewBlender_lang`/`darkMode` registered at all five AllTools sites with `uiLang` validated on import (`62f07ab`).

---

## Housekeeping

`sw.js` v625 → v626 → **v627**. `FONT_MAKER_VERSION` stays 5.37 — neither session touched the Font Maker. `check-i18n` (all four gates), `check-inline-js`, `update-llms-txt --check`, `check-ledger --vs origin/main` (conservation *and* structure) all clean; `update-sitemap` run last. Final 26-load suite-wide regression after every change: 0 pageerrors, 0 raw keys, `lang`+`dir` 26/26.

## Two protocol conventions ratified at S307 — the skill file still does not carry them

1. **A fix for a defect a discovery pass found is cap-exempt**, like the pass itself. This retroactively settles the S306 `resources.html ×3` dispute: it was not a breach, and `afb5f3b` should not be reverted.
2. **The printed-chrome boundary is closed** — a future chrome page copies one line rather than re-litigating it.

## For the maintainer

Merge when ready, then confirm the `pages build and deployment` run concludes `success` — deploy only happens on merge to `main`.

One thing worth knowing for next session: **`resources.html` has been at or over its 2-per-session cap for four consecutive sessions** and is by a wide margin the most-worked surface in the suite. The ledger's S309 pointer says to skip it unless a pass lands there on its own merits.

author: professor3333
body:
Structured logging, request correlation, response timing, connection PRAGMAs, and the four endpoints that complete the read surface. **153 tests.**

## The gap this phase closed

The 500 handler built a deliberately uninformative body — and then **discarded the exception**. The traceback was written nowhere, which made every 500 unresolvable and the opaque body indefensible rather than merely unhelpful. It now logs with `exc_info` against the same `request_id` the body carries. `test_traceback_reaches_the_log_but_not_the_body` asserts both halves together, because either one alone is a bug: an opaque body with no logged traceback is negligence, and a traceback in the body is a leak.

## Observability

One JSON object per line on stdout. A `ContextVar` carries the request id, so a log call anywhere in the request — including inside `repository.py` — is correlated without threading a parameter through every signature.

```jsonc
{"ts":"…","level":"INFO","logger":"jobsapi.access","message":"request",
 "request_id":"a3199c…","http":{"method":"GET","path":"/jobs","status":200,"duration_ms":2.9}}
```

Timing uses `perf_counter`, not `time()` — a wall clock adjusted mid-request can run backwards and produce a negative duration.

## Connection

`PRAGMA query_only` alongside `mode=ro`, so "this service never writes to `jobs.db`" is enforced in **two independent places** — removing one doesn't silently remove the guarantee. `temp_store = MEMORY` because a container with a read-only filesystem can't spill a sort to disk.

## The remaining surface

**`/jobs/{id}/changes`** — the interesting one. `job_changes` holds **32.8 MB** of description diffs, single values up to 30,646 characters. Values are truncated to 200 chars **in SQL**, not in the response model: filtering at serialisation would still have paid to read them off disk. `old_length`/`new_length` report true sizes and `truncated` says whether anything was cut, so a client is never misled. Measured on real data — job 72's six changes are ~92 KB raw, **3.4 KB served**.

An unknown job is a `404`, not an empty list: "never changed" and "does not exist" are different facts.

**`/sources`** — a bare array, deliberately unlike `/jobs`. Eight sources, nothing to paginate, no `total` worth carrying. `LEFT JOIN` so a source with jobs but no run row still appears. `last_run_status` can read `running` indefinitely, and that's reported as-is: this service cannot tell a live run from an abandoned one by querying, because the discriminator is a `-journal` file on disk.

**`/runs`** — **no `duration_seconds`.** Build 2 stamps `finished_at` from the same value as `started_at`, so it would be `0.0` for every completed run. A number that is always wrong is worse than an absent one; both timestamps are returned raw so the client can see the equality itself. Upstream bug, not laundered here.

**`/stats`** — per-field coverage, which is the honest counterpart to "NULLs never satisfy a filter". Real values: `posted_at` 100%, `description` 99.19%, `location` 97.84%, `remote` 63.64%, `seniority` 50.82%, `salary_min` **31.47%**.

## A bug the tests caught

`extra="forbid"` was on `JobFilters` rather than `Pagination`, so `?colour=red` was a 422 on `/jobs` and **silently ignored on `/runs`** — contradicting what `docs/api.md` already promised. Moved to the shared base, so the rule is true everywhere at once.

author: msyavuz
body:
### SUMMARY

Deployments that attach their own metadata to charts and dashboards — an owning team, a catalogue entry, a cost centre — have no way to make it survive an export/import round trip. The only options today are forking the export commands or monkeypatching their internals, both of which break silently on upgrade.

This adds two optional config hooks, alongside the existing `EXTRA_OWNERS_RESOLVER` and `AFTER_ASSET_CREATE`:

- `EXTRA_ASSET_EXPORT_FIELDS(model, asset_type) -> dict` — serialised under the `extra` key of the exported YAML
- `EXTRA_ASSET_IMPORT_HANDLER(model, asset_type, extra)` — called once the asset exists on import

Everything is namespaced under a single `extra` key rather than merged at the top level. The import schemas reject unknown fields (marshmallow defaults to `RAISE`), so one declared field per asset type preserves that strictness while leaving the payload shape free to evolve without further schema changes.

### BEFORE/AFTER SCREENSHOTS OR ANIMATED GIF

No UI. With `EXTRA_ASSET_EXPORT_FIELDS` configured, the exported YAML gains:

```yaml
slice_name: Revenue by region
...
extra:
  owning_team: analytics-platform
```

With neither hook configured, exported files are byte-for-byte unchanged.

### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS

`pytest tests/unit_tests/commands/extra_asset_fields_test.py` — 6 cases covering both hooks, a hook returning `None`, an empty `extra` being skipped, and the schemas accepting the field.

End to end: set `EXTRA_ASSET_EXPORT_FIELDS`/`EXTRA_ASSET_IMPORT_HANDLER` in `superset_config.py` per the docs added here, export a chart or dashboard, confirm the `extra` block, then re-import and confirm the handler is called with the mapping.

### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

- [ ] Has associated issue: No
- [ ] Required feature flags: None — both hooks default to `None`
- [ ] Changes UI: No, backend only
- [ ] Includes DB Migration: No
- [x] Introduces new feature or API: two optional config hooks, documented in `docs/admin_docs/configuration/configuring-superset.mdx`
- [ ] Removes existing feature or API: No

Verified locally: 1364 passed / 2 xfailed across `tests/unit_tests/{commands,dashboards,charts}`, and `pre-commit run` clean including mypy.

body:
Design pass 3 of 4. Stacked on #539.

## Line length

Explanatory text inside cards had no maximum width and ran to **169–176 characters a line** on a wide screen.

I measured the result with a `Range` against the rendered text rather than trusting an estimate — the detector's own heuristic said 87 where the real count was 76. At `66ch` the same paragraphs break at **65–66 characters**, inside the band a reader can track without losing the line.

Page descriptions keep their existing `60ch`; they were already constrained, and churning them would only add a second number.

## Capitals

Definition labels drop `uppercase` and move to 12px. Capitals are for short markers — `Время события (ISO, с часовым поясом)` at 37 characters is a sentence the reader decodes letter by letter.

## One chip

## What Problem This Solves

Existing Google or Google Vertex credentials/configuration did not restore the bundled Google plugin when `plugins.allow` was restrictive. After an upgrade, the configured provider could therefore remain silently unavailable and its models appear unknown.

Fixes #135221.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google manifest owned `google`, `google-gemini-cli`, and `google-vertex`, but its automatic activation metadata listed only `google-gemini-cli`. Users with a Google API/auth profile, a `models.providers.google` entry, or Google Vertex auth will have the Google plugin enabled and appended to an existing restrictive allowlist. Explicit plugin denial or disablement remains authoritative. Unconfigured bundled plugins are not added.
