author: dakakiki
body:
Found while testing the new multiselect: **filtering by four or more
categories took four minutes.** Three took one second.

Measured on the 18.5k-product dev catalogue:

| terms | products | before |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1,544 | 235 ms |
| 2 | 3,074 | 888 ms |
| 3 | 4,596 | 1,016 ms |
| 4 | 6,192 | **241,386 ms** |
| 5 | 7,698 | 305,837 ms |
| 6 | 9,231 | 352,387 ms |

## Cause

`term_relationships` is keyed by `term_taxonomy_id`, not `term_id`, so
asking it for terms meant joining `term_taxonomy` inside the membership
subquery. That two-table subquery is what the optimiser gets wrong.

`EXPLAIN` shows the plan flip exactly at the fourth term:

- **3 terms** — drives from the small term set, reaches `posts` by primary
  key (`eq_ref`).
- **4 terms** — materialises the subquery, scans it whole (`type=ALL`), and
  `p` degrades to `type=range` over 38,834 rows `Using join buffer (Block
  Nested Loop)`.

## Fix

Resolve the term ids to `term_taxonomy_id`s first — one small indexed
lookup, the same approach `term_slugs()` already uses for variation
attributes. The membership subquery then reads a single indexed table,
which plans correctly however many terms are given.

| terms | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 1,016 ms | 915 ms |
| 4 | **241,386 ms** | **975 ms** |
| 5 | 305,837 ms | 1,030 ms |
| 6 | 352,387 ms | 1,774 ms |

Identical counts throughout; only the plan changed.

## Alternatives measured and rejected

Still timing out past three terms: `DISTINCT` in the subquery, `GROUP BY`,
and wrapping it in a derived table to force materialisation.

Worked, but rejected: `STRAIGHT_JOIN` pins join order for every filter
shape the engine builds; an explicit derived-table `JOIN` would turn a
WHERE-fragment design into a JOIN builder. Both are a lot of blast radius
for something one lookup fixes.

## Behaviour

`NOT_EXISTS` now shares the negative branch with `NOT_IN` — with the ids
resolved they are the same query. A term id that does not exist resolves to
an empty set, which the clause answers honestly: "has one of these" matches
nothing, "has none of these" matches everything. Both are covered by new
tests, along with `NOT_IN`, because that empty case is an easy place to
silently drop the condition and match the whole catalogue instead.

242 tests green (3 new), PHPCS clean.

author: imilinovic
body:
> **Review view — do not merge this on its own.** These commits land through **#4727**, which carries all six. This PR exists so this one change can be reviewed and discussed separately.

Caches the label-filter verdict per (label step, node) for the duration of one `path.expand_config` call.

**How.** Reading a node's labels copies the vertex out of storage and then re-reads the label list once per label. A path-scoped uniqueness rule re-enters the same node once for every path that reaches it, and the verdict is identical every time, so the walk was re-deriving one of a few thousand answers millions of times. `PathHelper::CachedLabelBools` keeps it.

Keyed on the step as well as the node, because the label sequence repeats and the same node gets a different verdict at different depths — a new e2e test (`test_expand_config_label_step_per_depth`) pins that, and fails if the step is dropped from the key. Skipped entirely under a graph-wide uniqueness rule, which reaches each node once and would only ever write to the cache.

**Why.** 12.5s to 8.3s on a 4425-node topology, unchanged results. Costs memory bounded by (label steps x nodes visited).

Stacked on #4721.

**Intent** — third pass of the branding work. `tailwind.config.js` remaps fourteen palettes onto the monochrome ramp but not `red`, `green` or `emerald`, so those kept rendering as real colour everywhere: 135 class usages plus around 200 hardcoded hexes and `rgba()` tints across 125 files — red error text, green success ticks, amber warnings, a red-to-green password meter, red and green call buttons.

author: rifont
body:
Second defect blocking the standing release pull request, found once [#67](https://github.com/taucad/nanoraster/pull/67) cleared the first one and the workflow could reach its next step.

## What breaks

`release:prepare` runs the full `nanoraster:quality` gate, whose `docs` target drives Playwright's chromium over the built documentation routes. The shared `setup` action installs no browser, and this job never added one:

```
browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at
  /home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-.../chrome-headless-shell
```

The gate therefore failed on the environment rather than on anything about the release. `ci.yml` has always installed that browser for the same gate; only this workflow was missing it.

## The fix

One step, in the same position and with the same command CI uses:

```yaml
- uses: ./.github/actions/setup
- run: pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
```

`docs-site/scripts/test-built-routes.mjs` imports `chromium` only, so chromium alone is the right install — matching CI rather than widening it.

## Verification

Confirmed against the failing run that the browser was the only remaining blocker: `nx` already resolves the six pending plans to **0.5.0**, and every other gate in that run passed before `docs:routes` was reached.

author: valardragon
body:
## Summary

- sort theta-compressed Pasta lookup inputs with one cached canonical representation per value
- retain those sorted representations for the lookup permutation merge walk
- allocate per-input sort workspace during table-plan preparation, alongside advice preparation
- preserve the comparison-sort fallback for non-Pasta fields

This follows #302, which introduced the canonical-key table sort. Pasta field Ord converts values out of Montgomery form during each comparison. Caching the canonical representation changes that work from repeated conversions during O(n log n) sorting and O(n) merging to one conversion per input value.

## Performance

Isolated instrumentation of the six input lookup jobs in a two-Action Orchard proof on Apple M4 measured aggregate CPU time as:

| Work | Existing | Cached keys | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Input sorting | 1.013 ms | 0.418 ms | -58.7% |
| Merge walk | 0.326 ms | 0.138 ms | -57.6% |
| Combined | 1.339 ms | 0.556 ms | -58.4% |

This saves about 0.78 ms of CPU per two-Action proof. These are aggregate CPU timings across six independently scheduled lookup jobs, not a claim of 0.78 ms multicore wall-clock latency.

### Exact-head single-core Orchard benchmark

Control was current main at 77a58c6 and candidate code was cfb4f38. The current head, 5e407e9, differs only by the required changelog fragment. Both were independently built in release mode with Rust 1.97.1 on mac-os-1, an Apple M4. The real steady-state two-Action Orchard prover ran with exactly one Rayon worker in a warm A/B/B/A rotation. Proving-key construction, preparation, and proof verification were outside the timed samples.

| Revision | Run 1 | Run 2 | Mean |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Current main | 407.42 ms | 408.35 ms | 407.89 ms |
| PR #305 | 407.28 ms | 407.07 ms | 407.18 ms |

The PR point estimate is 0.71 ms, or 0.17%, faster. The per-process Criterion confidence intervals overlap, so this is directional rather than a statistically separated result. There were no competing benchmark processes and macOS reported no thermal or performance warnings.

Earlier end-to-end A/B measurements did not resolve a reliable multicore latency change on an otherwise-idle M4 with 10 workers or AMD Linux VM with 6 workers. The expected multicore benefit is reduced proving CPU, worker occupancy, and contention rather than a demonstrated idle 10-core latency reduction.

For two Orchard Actions, the six input workspaces add 490,080 bytes of temporary sort metadata, approximately 479 KiB. Their allocation overlaps advice preparation and the storage is released after lookup preparation.

## Correctness

- the canonical little-endian representation ordering is checked against field Ord for both Pasta fields
- exhaustive small-vector tests compare success, failure, and exact permutation output against the previous BTreeMap algorithm for both Pasta fields
- non-Pasta fields retain the existing Ord sort and merge path
- evaluator registration and transcript ordering are unchanged

## Validation

- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- git diff --check
- cargo test -p zakura-halo2-proofs --lib --all-features (149 passed)
- cargo check -p zakura-halo2-proofs --lib --no-default-features
- RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 cargo test -p zakura-halo2-proofs --lib plonk::lookup::prover
- cargo test -p zakura-orchard --release circuit::tests::round_trip_fixed -- --exact

Strict all-features Clippy under Rust 1.98 remains blocked by existing warnings on main; it produced no new diagnostic in the changed code.

## API surface

No downstream-public or pub(crate) API changes.

Internally, the pub(in crate::plonk) prepare_table_plan helper gains a circuit-count argument so input sort workspace can be allocated during the existing preparation overlap. All new fields and helpers are private.

author: maritagabisonia
body: Adds server-side protection for staff and student areas. This is not UI-only: the check runs on every request. ## Behavior - `/dashboard` and `/dashboard/*` require a logged-in user. Otherwise redirect to `/login`. - `/admin` and `/admin/*` require a logged-in user whose `profiles.role` is `admin`. Logged-in students (and anyone else) are redirected to `/not-authorized`. - Unauthenticated visitors to `/admin` are sent to `/login` first. ## How Next.js 16 uses `src/proxy.ts` instead of `middleware.ts`. Session refresh and the redirects live there. The `/dashboard` and `/admin` layouts call the same checks again so a page cannot render without passing them. Placeholder pages: - `/dashboard` — “Dashboard” - `/admin` — “Admin” - `/not-authorized` — “Not authorized” An admin can only see `/admin` after their `profiles` row has `role = 'admin'`. author: huzex87
body:
## Problem

After a merchant connected their WhatsApp number, the dashboard prompted them to connect again on every return. The "connected" state was inferred from `business_config.whatsapp_number` — a mutable JSON field that the Settings page clobbers (it saves `business_config` by spreading a possibly-stale local copy), and the connect route never error-checked that write. So the connection looked like it dropped.

## Fix

Use the durable `whatsapp_phone_bindings` row (which the inbound webhook already treats as the routing source of truth) as the authority for connection status:

- **`GET /api/whatsapp/connect`** — returns the tenant's active binding (with a `business_config` fallback). The dashboard fetches this on mount, so the connection survives across sessions and isn't affected by unrelated settings saves.
- **`DELETE /api/whatsapp/connect`** — explicit disconnect: deactivates the binding and clears `business_config.whatsapp_number`. The connection stays put until the user does this.
- **`POST`** now error-checks the `business_config` write instead of failing silently.
- **Dashboard** reads the durable status, adds a **Disconnect** button (replacing the ambiguous re-sync), and formats the number without doubling `+234`.

## Tests / checks
- `tsc --noEmit` = 0, ESLint = 0 on changed files, `next build` = 0.

## Note
The Settings page still overwrites `business_config.whatsapp_number` when saved from stale state; connection status no longer depends on it, but I can also make that save preserve the field in a follow-up if you'd like.

author: gouarin
body:
A macOS lane froze 9% into the suite and held its runner for 65 minutes
until the run was cancelled; the job's cleanup named the orphans -
`xctrace` and `DTServiceHub`. In the same workflow run, the other macOS
job finished the same suite in 3m32s. Re-running lands on a healthy VM,
which is what made this look like infrastructure.

It is not. `tests/test_cli.py` checks the command line - exit codes, the
Run directory, the JSON payloads, the naming cascade - and every one of
its runs was launching the platform's real profiler around a process that
exits immediately. On macOS that is `xctrace` plus the Instruments
service: twelve seconds a test, and now and then a hang with no ceiling
anywhere to end it.

Those tests now take the documented no-collector path, through the site
configuration the conftest fixture already owned. The module drops from
104 s to 1.3 s, the whole suite from 121 s to 21 s on an M5 Max, and the
number of real profiler launches in tier 1 falls from nine to one - the
`--record` test in test_corpus, which is the one that has to launch a
real collector to mean anything.

The tests job also gets `timeout-minutes: 15`, so that a hang fails a
job rather than holding a runner for an hour, and the testing page states
the choice: one real launch, the rest replayed.

The product side of this is issue #121: a collector that never returns
hangs `nunatak run` with nothing in the log, and that decision - which
invocations deserve a ceiling - is not a test fix.

author: imilinovic
body:
> **Review view — do not merge this on its own.** These commits land through **#4727**, which carries all six. This PR exists so this one change can be reviewed and discussed separately.

Replaces the iterative-deepening driver behind `bfs: true` with a single breadth-first walk. This is the large one in the stack.

**How.** Breadth-first order was produced by re-running the whole depth-first walk once per depth, each pass keeping only paths of exactly that depth. That re-derives every shorter path on every later pass, and the passes do not stop where the answers do — they continue while any node is still reachable at that depth, which on a graph whose long paths never reach a terminator is most of the cost.

`RunPathScopedBfs` walks it once over a tree of partial paths. A path-scoped rule lets a node sit on many paths at once, so the tree holds an entry per partial path rather than per node. Uniqueness walks the parent chain instead of consulting a visited set. Each entry keeps the relationship it was reached by, so rebuilding a path is a walk up that chain. Retires the pass-depth machinery it replaces.

**On the memory/time trade this makes.** An earlier revision of this branch kept only ids per entry and rebuilt a path by searching each node's relationships for a matching id. That is much leaner, and it is fine when few branches are returned — but it costs ~2.8us per returned path, and a shallow unfiltered expansion returns nearly every branch it visits. Measured, that revision took a 1.65M-path expansion from 0.95s to 5.59s: a 6x regression, entirely in the rebuild, with the traversal itself measuring *faster* than the code it replaced. Holding the relationship removes it.

**Why.** Deep and selective is what this is for: 17.5s to 0.57s on a 4425-node topology, the same 732 paths with the same contents. The shallow 1.65M-path expansion is 1.27s against 1.51s on master, so it stays ahead of where it started while giving up some of the per-visit savings the earlier commits in this stack won there. Peak memory over idle on that query is 71MB against master's 56MB — the cost of holding the relationships.

Two new e2e tests pin the guarantees the rewrite has to keep: breadth-first ordering under `limit`, and a node appearing on several distinct paths under `NODE_PATH`. Both pass against the unpatched module too. 133 path e2e tests pass.

Stacked on #4722.

author: cleytonmendest
body:
## O que muda

Os três eixos que nunca tiveram escala ganham token, nome e linter — com os valores tirados do que o código já fazia, não de gosto.

Fatia 1 de [#29](https://github.com/cleytonmendest/elizabeth/issues/29): passos **1, 2 e 4** da issue. O passo 3 (drenar o resto) fica para as próximas.

### O número que decide a questão

Não é a quantidade de valores. É este: **`text-xs uppercase` — um papel visual só, o rótulo curto em caixa alta — carregava QUATRO trackings diferentes** (`0.12em`, `0.14em`, `0.16em`, `0.18em`). Mesmo tamanho de fonte nos quatro, então não é compensação óptica. É tentativa e erro sedimentada, e é o que autoriza colapsar.

### A issue mediu metade do problema

Ela contou **só os valores entre colchetes**. As classes stock do Tailwind não aparecem no linter, porque a regra `tokens` procura `algo-[valor]`:

| Eixo | A issue diz | Medido agora |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Letter-spacing | 5 valores, 68 usos | **10 valores, 152 usos** (`tracking-tight` 45x, `widest` 16x, `wide` 15x, `wider` 2x eram invisíveis) |
| Proporção | 4 valores | **6** (`4/5` e `21/9` faltavam) |
| z-index | 3 valores | **7** (`z-0`, `z-10`, `z-40`, `z-50` faltavam) |

Ou seja: 78 ocorrências eram invisíveis para a medição **e** para a regra ao mesmo tempo.

### As escalas

```js
letterSpacing: { title: '-0.025em', label: '0.18em', hero: '0.3em' }
zIndex:        { base: 0, raised: 1, above: 2, sticky: 10,
                 overlay: 40, drawer: 50, modal: 9999 }
aspectRatio:   { portrait: '3/4', product: '2/3',
                 landscape: '4/3', ultrawide: '21/9' }   // video (16/9) já é do Tailwind
```

**Tracking são três papéis, não dois.** A issue previa dois. O código mostra três: `hero` (0.3em) aparece 4 vezes e sempre no mesmo papel — kicker de 11px sobre mídia de destaque, em `video`, `image-banner`, `slider-image` e `countdown-timer`. Uso consistente e restrito é o oposto do ruído que justifica colapsar, então ele sobrevive como degrau próprio.

**z-index é nomear sem renumerar.** Uma escala "limpa" (10/20/30…) foi considerada e descartada: a página de uma loja Shopify hospeda app de terceiro que não conhece nossa escala. O `modal: 9999` é feio e fica — é alto de propósito.

Detalhes e alternativas descartadas no [ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-escalas-de-tracking-z-index-e-proporcao.md). *(A issue pede "ADR 0002", mas esse número já é a taxonomia de labels; a numeração é sequencial e nunca reutilizada.)*

### Só migração que não move pixel

**236 trocas**, e cada uma foi provada comparando a declaração da classe antiga no CSS de antes com a da nova no CSS de depois:

| | antes | depois | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tracking-tight` → `tracking-title` | `-.025em` | `-.025em` | idêntico |
| `tracking-[0.18em]` → `tracking-label` | `.18em` | `.18em` | idêntico |
| `tracking-[0.3em]` → `tracking-hero` | `.3em` | `.3em` | idêntico |
| `z-0/[1]/[2]/10/40/50/[9999]` → nomes | 0,1,2,10,40,50,9999 | iguais | idêntico |
| `aspect-[3/4]`, `[2/3]`, `[4/3]`, `[16/9]`, `[21/9]` → nomes | iguais | iguais | idêntico |
| `rounded-lg` → `rounded-theme` | `.5rem` | `var(--radius-theme)` | **8px = 8px hoje** |
| `rounded` → `rounded-theme-sm` | `.25rem` | `var(--radius-theme-sm)` | **4px = 4px hoje** |

As duas últimas são o objetivo, não um desvio: os 87 `rounded-lg` deixam de ser literais e passam a obedecer `settings.radius_style` pela primeira vez. Hoje isso é invisível; deixa de ser no instante em que a lojista escolher 0px, 4px ou 16px.

### A regra vem junto

Sem ela a escala é sugestão. Dois checks novos pegam degrau **stock** nesses eixos — foi exatamente essa porta aberta que deixou o raio chegar a 50/50.

Verificada nos dois sentidos: planto `z-30` → acusa 1; troco por `z-above` → volta a zero; planto `tracking-widest` a mais → sobe para 34.

Pegou um falso positivo meu no caminho: `consent-tracking-api`, nome de API da Shopify dentro de um `<script>`. Resolvido com `(?<[-\w])`, o mesmo remendo da regra `radius`.

### Dois defeitos que a migração expôs, corrigidos

A regra `radius` já existia com dois problemas que só ficaram visíveis quando os outros itens saíram da frente:

1. Acusava **`rounded-br-none`** mandando usar `rounded-none` — que tiraria os quatro cantos. Conselho errado, e dívida que ninguém conseguiria pagar.
2. Reportava **`rounded-tl-[600px]`** como `"rounded"` — nome que não existe naquela linha — duplicando o que o check `arbitrary` já dizia com o nome certo.

13 casos de teste cobrindo a regra corrigida, todos como esperado (`rounded-br-none` passa, `rounded-br-lg` acusa).

## Verificação

- [x] `npm run gate` verde — 87 testes, 14 mutantes mortos, nenhuma violação nova
- [x] `npm run test:e2e:gate` — 14 passando
- [ ] Testado no editor com um color scheme claro **e** um escuro — *pendente, e agora vale mais que antes: com os 87 `rounded-lg` migrados, mexer `settings.radius_style` deve mudar o tema inteiro*
- [ ] Strings novas existem em `pt-BR` **e** `en.default` — *não se aplica: nenhuma string*

Conferido também que nenhuma das 236 trocas caiu dentro de `{% schema %}`, `<script>` ou `<style>`, e que nenhum JS manipula as classes renomeadas (senão renomear no Liquid quebraria comportamento).

## Baseline

Total: **377 → 341**

A cobertura do linter cresceu e o total **caiu** — 45 violações pagas contra 10 itens novos de dívida revelada. A catraca passa pelo caminho normal (`total ≤ base`), sem usar a exceção de "uma regra mudou neste PR".

`tokens` cai de 130 para 94 itens. A issue pede que chegue a 0; vale dizer que **isso não sai só destes quatro eixos** — dos 94 que sobram, ~60 são one-off de layout (`w-[25px]`, `basis-[42%]`, `shadow-[...]`) e 6 são hex de marca, que pedem exceção justificada, não token.

## Decisão estrutural?

Sim — [ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-escalas-de-tracking-z-index-e-proporcao.md).

### O que ficou de fora, e por quê

Migração que **muda pixel** não entrou junto com a que não muda, para o diff ser revisável como uma coisa só:

- 33 usos de `tracking-wide`/`wider`/`widest` e 23 de `0.12em`/`0.14em`/`0.16em`/`0.2em` — todos convergem para `tracking-label`, mas cada um move o espaçamento
- `aspect-[4/5]` (1) e `rounded-md` (2), sem equivalente exato
- O piso tipográfico de 12px (`text-[10px]`, `[11px]`, `[8px]`) — que a issue mede mas não lista entre as ações, e que esbarra em legibilidade, não só em token
- `portrait` (3/4) e `product` (2/3) continuam com nomes separados: unificá-los mudaria a forma de todo card de produto em toda página de coleção. É decisão de design, não limpeza de dívida

**Um limite honesto:** o critério de aceite da #29 diz "nada muda visualmente onde não era para mudar", mas o mecanismo que provaria isso — a baseline de regressão visual do style guide — **ainda não existe**: o PNG de referência nunca foi commitado e o teste se declara pulado. Esta fatia contorna a falta escolhendo só migrações byte-idênticas, que dá para provar pelo CSS compilado. A fatia seguinte, que move pixel, depende daquela baseline para ser mais que uma promessa.

author: javi11
body:
## Why

Callers sweeping many ids often learn mid-sweep that some ids no longer matter — a file already past its missing-segment threshold, say. Today the only way to act on that is to chunk the sweep and re-decide between chunks.

But `StatMany` clamps `Concurrency` to `len(messageIDs)`, so a wide sweep needs a large chunk, and a large chunk means coarse early-termination granularity. **Sweep width and early-termination granularity are therefore in direct tension**, and the caller has to give up one of them. AltMount hits this in both its sweep sites: `internal/usenet/validation.go` and the import fast-fail probe both chunk by their concurrency bound purely to get an abandon point.

## What

`StatManyOptions.Skip func(messageID string) bool`, consulted immediately before each id is dispatched. The caller passes every id in one wide call and abandons ids as their verdict settles — no chunking, no tradeoff.

The production change is 8 lines: the option field, and a check in the dispatch loop placed after the index and context checks. It uses `continue` rather than `return`, so a skipped id does not retire the worker.

## Contract change worth reviewing carefully

**A skipped id emits no `StatManyResult`.** This is consistent with the existing behaviour for ids left undispatched by cancellation, which `StatMany` already documents — but it means `Skip` introduces a *second* reason the result count can fall short of the input count, and a caller assuming 1:1 would silently mishandle skipped ids.

Both `Skip`'s and `StatMany`'s doc comments now say this explicitly rather than leaving it implied.

`Skip` is called concurrently from every dispatch goroutine, so it must be safe for concurrent use — also documented.

## Test plan

- [x] Written first, red phase confirmed by compile failure before the field existed
- [x] Skipped ids produce no result; non-skipped ids all do; result count is exact
- [x] **Wire-level assertion**: the skipped id never appears in the server's command log — proving no STAT was sent, not merely that no result surfaced
- [x] A `Skip` that flips partway through stops further dispatch (`Concurrency: 1` makes the cutoff deterministic)
- [x] `Skip == nil` behaves exactly as before — regression guard for existing callers
- [x] Concurrency safety: `Concurrency: 128` with a mutex-guarded closure, under `-race`
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` exit 0; `make test-race` green (212 tests/subtests)

## Compatibility

Additive only. Existing callers passing no `Skip` are unaffected.

author: osherelhadad
body:
**Merge order: this must land before #172.** `feat/inventory-hierarchy-0901` fails the
390 px constraint on the Inventory tab without the two `tools.css` commits here — measured on
that branch by actually removing them (`clippedOff 48`, `+159 px`), not by simulating it.

Six commits: two defect fixes, two cheap wins, one comment correction. Measured with the
sweep harness (`perf.mjs` / `shots.mjs`) throughout, on a copy of the seeded corpus with
both janitor rules disabled (`--dashboard-retention 0 --dashboard-max-bytes 0`).

## 1. Three tabs scrolled the page body sideways at 390 px. Now zero.

`index.html:583` wrapped the keep-alive live table in `<div class="scroll-x">`, and
`.scroll-x` is defined in **no stylesheet** — `grep -n 'scroll-x' dash/ui/*.css` returned
nothing. The working class is `.tblwrap` (already on `main`). Computed `overflow-x` was
therefore `visible`, an 1114 px table sat in a 390 px body, and the page scrolled sideways,
which the design brief forbids outright.

Overflow audit, all 17 tabs, dark, 390×844:

| tab | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| keepalive | body **+753 px** | no |
| kvcache | body **+16 px** | no |
| strategies | body **+183 px** | no |
| tools | body **+159 px** (see §2) | no |
| 13 others | no | no |

Three fixes, and only one of them was the rename:

- **keepalive** — `.scroll-x` → `.tblwrap`, *and* the ladder table at `app.js:8722` was
  appended bare. Fixing the live table exposed the ladder at +179 px.
- **kvcache** — wrapping `kvcache.js:1173` was not enough. A grid child defaults to
  `min-width: auto`, so the new `.tblwrap`'s own parent refused to shrink and the table
  pushed the column instead of scrolling inside it. `.grid-2 > * { min-width: 0 }` is the
  actual fix, matching the `.panel > *` / `.card > *` rules two lines above.
- **strategies** — not a table at all. A `<select>` is as wide as its widest option and a
  `<fieldset>` will not shrink below its own min-content, so one long option made a 544 px
  fieldset in a 390 px viewport. `fieldset { min-inline-size: 0 }` plus
  `max-width: min(520px, 100%)` on the form controls.

**Process note: fixing the biggest overflow reveals the next one.** Two of the three tabs had
a second defect hidden behind the first, so the audit has to be re-run after each fix rather
than once at the end.

## 2. Inventory (`tools`) — 48 elements were clipped out of reach

Found by re-running the audit after the seeded corpus grew to 16,444 requests: the tab only
breaks once the tool tables have rows, so the earlier sweep on a sparse corpus called it
clean. Two grid tracks flooring at min-content — `.inv-group`'s implicit auto track taking
its width from the longest line of the `white-space: pre` removal snippet, and `.cg-item`'s
`1fr` track taking it from an unbreakable name like `mcp__sentry__analyze_issue_with_seer`.
The `@media (max-width: 560px)` block re-declares the same track, so it has to agree or it
wins at 390 px. `minmax(0, 1fr)` in all three places.

    clippedOff    48 -> 0      unreachable content, the audit's worst category
    bodyScrollsX  +159 -> no   body.scrollWidth exactly 390 at 390px

Not a defect, for whoever picks up the rest: the `span.comp-name.trunc` findings on this tab
are deliberate. `style.css:572` is `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` and
`tools.js:961,1073` carry the full value in a `title`, so the name is truncated on purpose and
recoverable. Same shape as the `.vh` false positive in the harness README's §6 list.

The residual 138 px is also closed, in a third commit. It sat unattributed because the
audit's two checks answer different questions, which is worth recording: `overflowPage`
compares **bounding rects**, while `bodyScrollsX` reads `body.scrollWidth`, which includes
descendants' **scrollable overflow region**. A box with `overflow-x: visible` whose content
overflows keeps its own rect inside the viewport, so a rect scan finds nothing at any
tolerance. The predicate that finds it is `left + max(scrollWidth, width) > viewport`, and it
**must** skip any element with a scrolling ancestor or every cell inside a `.tblwrap` reads as
page overflow — the mistake two of us made independently.

It named `.inv-removal-fold > summary { white-space: nowrap }` (`tools.css:202`) holding
"Remove just mcp__postgres__describe_table", one unbreakable 414 px line. The nowrap is
deliberate — the fold also sits in a table cell, where wrapping stretches the row — so the
override is scoped to the narrow breakpoint and placed **after** the original. Same
specificity, and a media query adds none, so an override in the earlier `@media` block at
:102 silently loses; that cost a build to discover.

**All 17 tabs now pass the constraint**, `body.scrollWidth` exactly 390 at 390 px, verified
twice per theme with the tables populated (1,556 text nodes, 115 items — a run reporting 24
nodes is an empty render, not a pass).

## 3. The embedded assets are served gzipped

`dash/ui.go` set `Cache-Control`, `ETag` and a CSP and never looked at `Accept-Encoding`, so
~705 KB of JS and ~91 KB of CSS went over the wire raw on every load. Compressed once at
process start with stdlib `compress/gzip`, served from memory, raw as the fallback. No build
step, no dependency, no CDN.

**This is a WAN win, not a local one.** On loopback the four scripts cost ~31 ms of DCL but
~99 ms of main-thread CPU, 98% of it `app.js` — compression is not the local bottleneck,
execution is. At 1.6 Mbit/s and 150 ms RTT, 1440×900, 5 cold loads, median (range):

| | FCP | DCL | js+css wire |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| before | 1276 ms (1272..1284) | 4388 ms (4383..4392) | 760K |
| after | 600 ms (592..684) | 1570 ms (1550..1584) | 232K |

Independently measured end to end at 5 Mbit: 831 KB → 252 KB, ~1,362 ms → ~412 ms.

| asset | raw | gzip -9 | brotli -11 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| app.js | 473222 | 145814 | 119037 |
| tools.js | 108553 | 33414 | 28021 |
| kvcache.js | 76175 | 23211 | 19823 |
| campaigns.js | 46744 | 14176 | 12162 |
| style.css | 74610 | 19754 | 16658 |
| tools.css | 12415 | 3919 | 3260 |
| kvcache.css | 4586 | 1862 | 1492 |
| index.html | 55749 | 15762 | 13251 |
| **total** | **852054** | **257912 (−70%)** | **213704 (−75%)** |

**Brotli is deliberately not shipped, and this should not be re-opened:** Go has no stdlib
brotli, so it means a new third-party dependency in a product whose whole constraint is that
it works air-gapped with no CDN and no build step — for 5 percentage points of ratio over
gzip. Bad trade.

Caching correctness, since this is the part that breaks quietly:

- `Vary: Accept-Encoding` on **every** asset response, not only compressed ones. A shared
  cache that stored the raw body under an unvaried key would later hand it to a client that
  asked for gzip, and vice versa.
- A distinct `"<v>-gzip"` ETag. A different `Content-Encoding` is a different representation,
  so it needs a different validator, or a cache revalidating with one can 304 a raw client
  into a compressed body.
- `gzip;q=0` is an explicit refusal and is honoured.
- Compressed once at init, not per response: the bytes never change for the life of the
  process, so a `gzip.Writer` per response would burn CPU to produce an identical body.

One caveat, documented at the site: `net/http`'s `serveContent` skips `Content-Length` once
`Content-Encoding` is set, so compressed assets go out chunked and show no download progress.
Do not "fix" it by setting `Content-Length` — `ServeContent` answers a Range request with a
206 whose body is only the requested slice and will not overwrite a length we set, so a
full-body length there is a broken response rather than a missing progress bar.

## 4. `defer` on the four scripts — shipped, and it is NOT a speedup

DESIGN §4.3 item 2 says `defer` "removes all ~380 ms of throttled parse+eval from the
pre-paint path". **Measured, it does not.** A deferred script still runs before
`DOMContentLoaded` and still before first paint if the paint has not happene

body:
## Summary

Adds the workspace-level design and lock for a new Fundamental State Forecasting research family.

Child PRs:

- `alpha-research` #51: reusable PIT-safe targets, persistence baseline, expanding walk-forward Ridge/XGB-regressor OOS runner, forecast evaluation, purge/embargo utilities, and forecast+valuation scoring
- `strategy-research` #15: exploration thesis, literature map, experiment gates, catalog entry, and lifecycle documentation

`portfolio-backtester` is intentionally unchanged. The first portfolio experiments will reuse its existing public signal/backtest and incumbent-requalification capabilities.

## Design

The research flow is:

```text
canonical PIT annual fundamentals
        ↓
future one-year fundamental targets
        ↓
persistence / Ridge / XGB expanding-window OOS forecasts
        ↓
OOS fundamental evaluation
        ↓
forecast fundamentals + current valuation
        ↓
portfolio-backtester research backtest
```

This PR adds:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-01-fundamental-state-forecasting-design.md`
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-01-fundamental-state-forecasting.md`
- gitlinks for the two child feature branches

The MVP remains `exploration`, `production_eligible=false`, and adds no `strategy-app`, `strategy-pipeline`, `targets.json`, or execution wiring.

## Verification evidence

The pure alpha-research module was verified in an isolated local harness because the current sandbox cannot resolve `github.com` and therefore cannot build the private repository's full `uv` environment. Repository GitHub Actions are disabled by policy.

Fresh focused verification:

```text
PYTHONPATH=/mnt/data/fsf_tdd python -m pytest -q /mnt/data/fsf_tdd/tests/test_fundamental_state.py
.......... [100%]
10 passed in 0.75s

python -m py_compile ...
exit 0

custom 100-column check
fundamental_state.py lines>100: []
test_fundamental_state.py lines>100: []
```

The TDD/review cycle caught and fixed three meaningful regressions: pooled-vs-within-period rank IC semantics, multiple targets sharing one source column, and the absence of an executable leakage-safe walk-forward baseline path.

## Full gates still required

These were not run in this sandbox and are not claimed as passing:

```bash
# alpha-research
scripts/dev/run_tests.sh lint
scripts/dev/run_tests.sh typecheck
scripts/dev/run_tests.sh all
scripts/dev/run_tests.sh maintainability

# strategy-research

python src/research_contracts/smoke_contracts.py
python scripts/run_quality_checks.py --profile hard
python scripts/run_submodule_checks.py --profile smoke
```

## Merge order

Per workspace policy, merge the child repository PRs first. Then refresh this PR's gitlinks from the temporary feature commit SHAs to the resulting `main` commit SHAs and run the top-level local gates before merging the workspace PR.

author: rockymadden
body:
## Problem

`uip maestro flow node add` generates the node id from `--label` plus a counter, and has **no `--id` flag**. The skill documented this as only "Inserts node into `nodes` array with a generated `id`".

With no stated derivation, an agent will hard-code a *guessed* id in a `$vars` reference inside the same `&&` chain as the `node add` that creates the node. The guess is unverifiable at that point, and a wrong one is invisible: `flow validate` does not check expression correctness, so the flow reports **Valid** and faults only at runtime.

Observed in the `skill-flow-bellevue-weather-simulated` coder-eval (weighted score 0.333, gating criterion failed):

- `--label 'Normalize Bellevue conditions'` → `normalizeBellevueConditions1`
- decision node, same chain → `"expression": "$vars.normalizeConditions1.output.temperatureF > 60"`

```
uip maestro flow validate  → Status: Valid
uip maestro flow debug     → [400302] Error evaluating outgoing flow expression from gateway
                              (edge_warmerThan60F1_true_writeNiceDaySummary1_input)
                             [400302] ... _false_writeJacketSummary1_input
                             [400001] No condition for an outgoing flow was met (warmerThan60F1)
```

One wrong word. Everything upstream ran clean (trigger, HTTP 200 from open-meteo, normalize script returned real values).

## Changes

**`references/author/editing-operations-cli.md`** — new `### Generated node IDs` section:
- derivation rules and a 4-row example table, plus a scope guard so the section cannot be read as licensing `node add` for OOTB nodes (rule #9)
- the counter is **always** appended, starting at `1`
- `--label` is mandatory in practice: without one the CLI picks its own base name and it is *not* the type's last segment (`core.action.http.v2` → `httpRequest1`)
- the counter increments against **ids already in the file**, hand-authored ones included, so the id is **not a pure function of the label**
- capture recipe (`--output-filter "Node.Id"`, PascalCase)
- the prohibition
- caveat: a digit-leading label produces an id that breaks rule #12, and validate accepts it

**`references/author/greenfield.md`** — T1 said "capture it from the chained output", which is advice. Now a prohibition: all `$vars` references belong in T2, written against the ids T1 returned.

**`SKILL.md` rule #11** — extended. The rule already owns "a bare node reference resolves to `undefined` at runtime"; the wrong-`<nodeId>` case is its sibling. This matters because the failing agent read `SKILL.md` in turn 1 and never opened `editing-operations-cli.md` before authoring — documenting only in the reference file would not have prevented the failure.

+31 / -4 across three files.

## Verification

Derivation probed directly against `uip` 1.202.0, not inferred from the artifact. Every documented example reproduced on a clean flow. Three findings changed what got written:

- **No `--id` flag exists** (`node add --help`), so "capture the id" is the only available guidance.
- **The counter is not a pure function of the label.** With a hand-authored `handMade1` present, `--label "Hand made"` yields `handMade2`. An agent that knows the algorithm perfectly still cannot predict the id.
- **The response path is `Data.Node.Id`, PascalCase.** `--output-filter "Node.id"` silently returns `Data: []`.

Self-review then caught a third: I had written "no label → last dot-segment of the node type", generalized from one coincidental sample (`core.logic.merge` → `merge1`). It is wrong — `core.action.http.v2` → `httpRequest1`, `core.trigger.scheduled` → `scheduledTrigger1` — and `registry get` does not expose the real source, so the doc now states the observed behavior instead of asserting a mechanism. `--id` also confirmed to fail loudly (`unknown option '--id'`), not be silently ignored.

Also corrected two claims from an earlier draft: accented letters are **dropped**, not transliterated (`café münchen` → `cafMNchen1`), and `Fetch data (v2)` → `fetchDataV21` (`v2` plus counter).

Gates: `skills:check-links` ✅ · `skills:validate` ✅ (both flavors) · `check-skill-verbs.py` ✅ no new findings.

The `studioweb` flavor replaces `greenfield.md`'s entire `project-creation` block, so that edit does not reach it — another reason the rule needed to be in `SKILL.md` and the CLI reference as well. No flavor override required updating.

## Out of scope

This is one of several fixes identified from the same eval failure. Deliberately **not** included:

1. **A `$vars` reference-integrity check** in the finalize step. The durable fix, and it belongs in `uip maestro flow validate` (a dangling `$vars.<id>` is statically decidable from the file alone) rather than in a skill-authored shell check.
2. **The rule #9 vs rule #10 tension.** Rule #10 rewards collapsing work into one chained Bash; `node add` is the only node-CRUD surface that fits a Bash chain, so the batching rule quietly pushes toward the CLI path rule #9 forbids for OOTB nodes. The eval agent used `node add` for all seven OOTB nodes despite having read `SKILL.md`. Worth fixing in the CLI: `node add` should reject user-owned node types.
3. **The author-terminates-at-validate vs graded-on-debug mismatch.** The skill forbids `flow debug` as a validation step, so an agent that follows it cannot self-verify what the grader measures.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: clubanderson
body:
Fixes #5420

Part of #4907. Follows #5502 (T30), which rewrote `poll.go`; this extends that file rather than the shape described in the issue text.

## What was broken

`Client.Events` (#5059) and the Events pane (#5060) were both complete and both tested in isolation, and the pane still showed `waiting for data` forever — nothing called the client or delivered `panes.EventsMsg`. This adds the one missing wire.

## Shape

`fetchEvents` resolves to `panes.EventsMsg` **directly** rather than to an app-level message. `fetchGovernor` and `fetchTokens` exist in their indirect, cached form because their pane's frame is a JOIN of two independently failing endpoints, so a message sent straight from one fetch would carry a zero for whatever the other knows. An `EventsMsg` is complete the moment `/api/audit` answers — nothing to join, nothing to cache — so routing it through the model would add a hop that could only lose or reorder data. This is `fetchAgents`' shape, for `fetchAgents`' reason.

`panes.EventsMsg` therefore needs **no case in the app's `Update` switch**: it reaches the pane through the existing default `broadcast`. `app.go` is unmodified. `TestEventsReachThePaneThroughTheRootUpdate` pins that, because adding a case that forgot to broadcast would compile and pass every poll-level test while silently freezing the pane.

The returned slice is passed through untouched — the client returns newest-first and `panes.Events.replace` re-finds the operator's anchor by value.

## The error contract — the crux

Two outcomes that are one blank pane if conflated:

- **Failed read** returns `fetchErrMsg`, which the app swallows. Prior rows and scroll position survive *by construction*, not by the pane remembering to hold them.
- **Successful empty list** returns a real `EventsMsg`. It marks the pane loaded and renders `no events yet`.

`panes.Events` cannot distinguish either from `EventsMsg{Events: nil}` — it sets `loaded` and replaces rows for both — so the distinction has to hold at the message level.

`/api/audit` is the only poll read requiring read-write or owner access, so **403 is the expected state for a read-only token**, not an error condition. It travels the same nonfatal `fetchErrMsg` path as any other non-2xx and does not terminate the TUI. No new error chrome was added; `fetchErrMsg` already carries `source` for whichever later task surfaces it.

## Mutation evidence

Per #5388's standard, every assertion was proven capable of failing. Each defect was introduced, the specific test confirmed failing, then reverted.

| # | Defect introduced | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Failed read returns `panes.EventsMsg{}` instead of `fetchErrMsg` | **CAUGHT** — `TestFailedAuditReadPreservesPriorEvents` and `TestForbiddenAuditDoesNotStopTheOtherPanes` FAIL; `TestSuccessfulEmptyAuditMarksThePaneLoaded` still PASSES |
| M2 | Successful empty list suppressed into a `fetchErrMsg` | **CAUGHT** — `TestSuccessfulEmptyAuditMarksThePaneLoaded` FAILS; the two failure-path tests still PASS |
| M3 | App reverses the newest-first feed | **CAUGHT** — `TestEventsArriveNewestFirstUnreordered` + `TestNewerEventsPreserveTheAnchoredScroll` FAIL; `TestStartupPollFillsTheEventsPane` still PASSES |
| M4 | `fetchEvents` unwired from `poll()` | **CAUGHT** — 4 wiring tests FAIL; the root-delivery test still PASSES |
| M5 | Client fetches activity rows from `/api/events`, **and the harness serves audit rows there** so the fetch succeeds | **CAUGHT** — `/api/audit was read 0 times, want exactly 1` + `the poll made 1 request(s) to /api/events for activity rows` |

The complementary PASS results matter as much as the FAILs: they show M1/M2 are caught by *different* tests, so the failed-read and successful-empty paths are independently sensitive rather than one check double-counted.

Two notes on how that evidence was produced, since the brief asked for explicitness:

- **M5's first form was a false negative.** Simply repointing the client at `/api/events` made the fetch 404, so the test's own vacuity guard (`the poll delivered no events at all; the endpoint assertions below would be vacuous`) fired first and masked the endpoint counter. The counter assertion was unproven until the harness was also patched to *serve* audit rows on `/api/events`, making the misrouted fetch succeed so only the counter could catch it. The guard worked correctly; it just meant the assertion behind it needed a sharper mutant.
- **An earlier scripted mutation run reported M1 as a false PASS.** Shell heredoc quoting mangled the replacement pattern, so the patch silently no-op'd and the run tested unmutated code. Every mutation in the table above was subsequently applied via a tool that fails loudly on a non-matching pattern, and each was confirmed present in the file before running.

`TestNewerEventsPreserveTheAnchoredScroll` also caught a wrong assertion of my own: I initially asserted the newest entry becomes visible after a refresh, but for a scrolled-back operator the correct behaviour is that it does *not* — it lands above the viewport. The test now asserts the anchored frame is byte-identical and proves the refresh landed by scrolling back to the top.

## Cadence — expected gap, T32's to close

This uses the **current** refresh machinery and adds no competing timer. As #5502 documented, with SSE connected the poll stretches to `sseReconcileInterval` (60s) and the SSE payload carries no audit data — so in a healthy session Events refreshes every 60s rather than 5s. That is expected here and is exactly what T32 (#5421) fixes. Not addressed in this PR.

## Scope

`src/pkg/tui/poll.go` and `poll_test.go` only. Events pane rendering and the SSE parser are untouched, as are `app.go` and everything under `src/pkg/dashboard/` (#5492's territory).

- `go build ./...` from `src/` — clean across the module
- `go test ./pkg/tui/...` — all four packages green
- `gofmt -l` clean, `go vet ./pkg/tui/...` clean

## Summary

In line drawing mode, typing `Space` on a frame character inserts a cell at that column in every row of the surrounding table so columns stay aligned. When the column contains a horizontal line the new cell is filled with the same-weight line character so the border remains continuous. The action triggers when the frame is under the cursor or immediately after it, and it only widens the table in overwrite mode so `Insert` lets you type spaces inside cells as usual.

Pressing `Enter` to the right of the last frame character of a table row inserts a new row that carries the vertical lines of the split row (on a bottom border the new row is inserted above it), and the action is bound to both aliases of the Enter key code. Drawing a single line over a double one now sets the axis being drawn to the active weight on both sides, so a single line visibly replaces a double line while crossings preserve the other axis weight.

author: jessesandberg
body:
## Description

This PR updates the morphology-aware internal-structure detector from #99 to use a **unified evidence model** rather than treating bright vesicles, dark filaments, and dark-edged bubbles as mutually exclusive biological classes.

The detector now combines complementary image evidence into one authoritative structured mask:

- compact positive-residual regions,
- compact negative-residual regions,
- dark and light curvilinear/ridge evidence, and
- enclosed-boundary evidence.

This addresses failure modes seen in the newer test videos where the same physical internal structure can present with different contrast or morphology. In particular, filled dark circles no longer need a neutral interior to be detected, light-bordered/curved tubules can contribute through supported light-ridge evidence, and the final measurement no longer depends on deciding whether a feature should specifically be called a bubble, vesicle, or tubule.

The individual evidence channels are retained for diagnostics, but connected components of their merged union are the actual measured structures. Region output therefore reports `structure` plus an `evidence_types` field describing which proposals support each region.

Several false-positive controls are included in the unified detector:

- Structure proposals seed only within a conservative interior margin whose width accounts for the configured ridge-filter support, reducing persistent detections caused by the outer membrane/shadow.
- Compact bright and dark proposals may grow outward through connected supporting signal so genuine structures near that conservative seed boundary are not artificially clipped.
- Ridge filtering itself remains confined to the conservative interior to avoid reintroducing the parent-membrane response.
- Secondary opposite-polarity/ridge/boundary evidence near accepted compact bright regions is suppressed to prevent background-subtraction halos from enlarging structures.
- Once an enclosed bubble is accepted, redundant nearby evidence is suppressed so optical ringing does not produce an additional structure skirt.

This branch also incorporates the intervening VesMod work needed to keep the long-lived #99 feature branch current, including the shared validation/object-invariant changes from #122/#123 and related EdgeMod/VesEdge updates. Merge conflicts in `internal_structures.py` were resolved by preserving the unified detector and applying the newer shared-validation architecture to its expanded configuration rather than reverting to the older detector implementation.

## Usage Changes

The `vesedge internal-structures` command remains the entry point and the overall output-file family is unchanged.

Behavior and interpretation changes:

- `structure_masks` is now the authoritative union of all supported internal-structure evidence.
- `light_region_masks`, `dark_region_masks`, `dark_filament_masks`, and `bubble_region_masks` are retained as diagnostic evidence channels rather than mutually exclusive biological classifications.
- `sample_regions.csv` reports connected union regions as `structure` and records contributing proposal types in `evidence_types`.
- Frame/video summaries continue to report the union structured-area measurement while retaining channel-specific values for diagnostics.
- Filled dark compact regions can now be detected directly rather than requiring a dark enclosing edge around a neutral interior.
- Curvilinear detection considers both dark and supported light ridge evidence.
- The effective structure-seeding boundary automatically accounts for the maximum configured ridge scale.
- The default filament scales extend through 10 px and the default bubble-closing distance is increased to 4 px.

The shared-validation merge also normalizes accepted NumPy scalar configuration values to native Python numeric types and applies the common validation vocabulary to the expanded `InternalStructureConfig`.

No checkpoint format is changed, and internal-structure analysis remains a measurement step rather than an additional VesEdge QC/rejection rule.

## Todos

- [x] Merge compact bright, compact dark, curvilinear, and enclosed-boundary evidence into one authoritative structure mask.
- [x] Detect filled dark compact structures without requiring a neutral bubble interior.
- [x] Add supported light-ridge evidence for light-bordered/curved internal structures.
- [x] Preserve diagnostic evidence channels while removing dependence on biological class assignment.
- [x] Add `evidence_types` to merged region output.
- [x] Suppress outer-membrane/shadow responses using a ridge-scale-aware conservative seed boundary.
- [x] Allow high-confidence compact structures to grow beyond the conservative seed boundary when supported by connected signal.
- [x] Suppress background-subtraction halos around accepted compact bright structures.
- [x] Suppress redundant optical/ridge evidence around accepted enclosed bubbles.
- [x] Update CLI defaults and internal-structure documentation for the unified detector.
- [x] Merge the shared validation/object-invariant work into the unified branch without losing the newer detector implementation.
- [x] Apply shared validation to the expanded unified `InternalStructureConfig`.
- [x] Add regression coverage for unified configuration validation/normalization.
- [x] Confirm the complete test suite passes on the final merged branch.

author: l2succes
body:
Follow-up to #162.

That PR was correct: `add_push_tokens.sql` shared version `20260630000001` with `add_message_snooze.sql`, so only one of the two was ever recorded as applied. Giving it a unique version fixes a real collision.

But renaming a migration that has **already run** leaves a file no database claims. The next `supabase db push` sees `20260630000002` as unapplied and runs it — and

```sql
CREATE TABLE push_tokens (...)
```

fails against every environment where `push_tokens` already exists, which is all of them.

This makes the second run a no-op instead of a failed deploy: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, and the RLS policy dropped before it is recreated.

Worth knowing: Railway's start command is `bun run dist/index.js` with no migration step, so nothing ran automatically when #162 merged. The hazard is latent until someone next pushes migrations.

body:
## Summary

Adds support for declaring which months a single contribution transaction covers when it pays multiple months at once (e.g., R$ 70 for an overdue month + R$ 60 for the current month). This enables accurate monthly reconciliation and proper linking of payments to their corresponding months.

## Key Changes

- **New DocType `Contribuicao Mensal Detalhe`**: A child table for `Transacao Extrato Geral` that lists the months covered by a transaction, with value and overdue status for each month.

- **Service functions for month breakdown**:
  - `get_competencias_por_transacao()`: Retrieves declared months for transactions
  - `get_competencias_transacao()`: Returns formatted month details for display
  - `definir_competencias_transacao()`: Validates and saves month declarations, with sum validation against transaction value

- **Updated reconciliation logic**:
  - `get_recebimentos_por_associado()`: Now distributes transaction values to declared months instead of using implicit retroactive clearing
  - `get_transacoes_do_associado()`: Expands transactions with detailed months into separate rows per month
  - Both functions now query `Contribuicao Mensal Detalhe` to include transactions with declared months in the period

- **Automatic payment record management**:
  - `_upsert_pagamento_contribuicao_mensal()`: Creates or updates `Pagamento Contribuicao Mensal` records for each declared month
  - `_update_pagamento_contribuicao_mensal()`: Handles both detailed (multi-month) and legacy (single-month) transactions
  - Payment records are now linked to the transaction via `transacao_extrato` field

- **MCP API endpoints**:
  - `competencias_transacao()`: Read declared months for a transaction
  - `definir_competencias_transacao()`: Set/update month declarations with simulation support
  - `listar_pagamentos_contribuicao_mensal()`: List payment records with filtering and pagination
  - `atualizar_pagamento_contribuicao_mensal()`: Update individual payment records

- **Validation and normalization**:
  - Month format validation (AAAA-MM pattern)
  - Sum validation with 0.01 BRL tolerance
  - Duplicate month detection
  - Automatic normalization to first day of month
  - Beneficiary requirement check

- **Test coverage**: New test file `test_transacao_contribuicao_meses.py` covering month declaration, validation, reconciliation, and payment linking.

## Implementation Details

- SQL queries updated with table aliases (`t.`) for clarity and to support joins with `Contribuicao Mensal Detalhe`
- Existing transactions without month details continue to work with legacy behavior (single month from `mes_competencia`)
- Month declarations are optional; empty list removes detailing and reverts to legacy mode
- All payment record updates respect existing permissions and validation rules

author: xdoubleu
body:
## Summary

Root-cause per issue #1334's own investigation comments: **Web Test** and **API Test** on `main` were both already fixed by #1332 (the flaky `apps/feeds` race and the stale `ObservabilityClient` mock-call-count assertion) before this PR was opened — confirmed by re-checking the latest `main` workflow run, which is green. What remained open in #1334 was the smaller hygiene bug the issue's own comments identified: a backwards `t.Cleanup` registration order in three `apps/shoppinglist` integration tests.

## The bug

`TestGetPlanIngredientGroups_ReturnsGroups`, `TestGetMealPlanExportItems_RecipeAndGroupAttribution`, and `TestGetMealPlanExportItems_ExcludesGroup` each registered a plan-delete cleanup *before* a recipe-delete cleanup. `t.Cleanup` runs LIFO, so the recipe delete fired first and hit `plan_meals_recipe_id_fkey` (the plan's `plan_meals` row still referenced the recipe, since `plan_id` cascades on delete but `recipe_id` does not — `api/apps/recipes/migrations/00001_init.sql`). The error was silently discarded (`_, _ = testDB.Exec(...)`), so the tests still passed but the recipe row was never actually cleaned up.

## Fix

Reordered `t.Cleanup` registration in all three tests so the plan delete (which cascades `plan_meals`) runs first, then the recipe delete. The discarded error is now asserted via `require.NoError`, so a similar ordering bug can't silently swallow a real failure again.

## Verification

- `make test` (api) — full suite passes, including the three fixed tests run fresh against a clean database.
- `make lint` / `make lint/fix` (api) — clean, no issues.
- `npm test` (web) — 254 suites / 2091 tests pass, confirming `ObservabilityClient.test.tsx` (already fixed by #1332) is green.

Fixes #1334

author: isizono
body:
## 何が変わるか

プラグイン名は `cc-memory` から `calm` に改称済みだが、ユーザー/AI向けに注入・表示される案内文の一部が改称前の名乗り・参照のまま残っていた。

- MCP instructions（RULES）冒頭の製品名、および「内部識別子は本文に出さない」節の製品名表記
- RULES 末尾の使い方skillへの導線が、実在しない旧名のskill参照になっていた（実在するのは calm 名前空間のskill）
- SessionStart hookが注入する「この一覧は◯◯ hookが決定論的に…」の注記中の製品名
- SessionStart hookのDB異常検知メッセージ中のskill参照も同様に旧名のままだった
- preblock_hookが内部ID漏出を検知してAIに返すdeny理由メッセージ中の製品名
- db-recoveryスキルのfrontmatter descriptionが案内するskill参照も同様
- habits投影ファイル（`~/.claude/rules/`配下の自動生成ファイル）の見出し・本文中の製品名

標準ユーザー（開発者本人以外）は毎セッションこれらの案内文を受け取っており、旧名の呼称や存在しないskillへの誘導をそのまま受け取っていた。今回、案内文中の製品名呼称と、skillの名前空間参照を現行のものに揃えた。

## なぜ要るか

skill参照が解決できない名前空間を指したままだと、案内に従おうとしたAIが実在しないskillを探すことになる。案内文中の製品名の不一致も、ユーザー体験としてのブランド一貫性を損なう。

## 触っていない箇所

- ファイルパス・ディレクトリ名（`~/.cc-memory/`、`cc-memory-habits.md` 等）・環境変数名・ロックディレクトリ名・ログパス: ファイルシステム/OS層の識別子であり、案内文の呼称とは別レイヤーのため対象外
- `_PROJECT_NAMES` のようなプロジェクト名判定用タプル、relayのstream/identity名: 過去互換性や内部識別のための値であり、案内文の呼称ではない
- `src/main.py` 内の各MCPツールのdocstring（RULES以外の箇所、例: `export_material`・`relay_publish`等の説明文）中の製品名表記: これらもAI向けではあるが、今回の修正依頼が明示的にRULES文字列に限定していたため対象外とした。触るとすれば別途の変更として切り出すのが妥当
- `src/services/habit_projection.py` の `_METADATA_PREFIX`（投影ファイル先頭に書き込まれるHTMLコメント形式のメタデータマーカー文字列）: これはユーザーが読む案内文ではなく、`read_file_state` が `text.startswith(_METADATA_PREFIX)` で投影ファイルの破損判定に使う機械可読フォーマット識別子。ここを変更すると、既存ユーザー全員の投影ファイルが次回セッションで「メタデータ欠損＝破損」と誤判定され、強制的に書き換えが走る（内容自体は変わらないが不要な書き込みが発生する）。呼称統一とは別種の変更になるため見送った
- docs/spec配下でdoc-sync-convention.mdが監視対象と定めている3文書（db-schema.md / mcp-tools.md / components.md）: 今回の変更はこれらのwatch対象トリガー（migration・ツールシグネチャ・構成変化）に該当しないため更新不要
- tests/配下のその他多数の `cc-memory` 文字列（プロジェクト名判定・ファイルパス・relayのstream/identity名としての用途）: 案内文の呼称ではなくテストフィクスチャ上の識別子であり対象外

## テストが保証すること

author: matt-taylor-tech
body:
Follow-up to #7, found by running it against a live tenant.

## The numbers did not add up

A real Enforce run reported:

```
Disable candidates: 86  (applied 2, deferred 86)
```

86 candidates, 2 applied, 86 deferred. That cannot be true of 86 accounts.

`$disabled` counted **every** disable, including the two that were interim disables of
*delete* candidates. `$disablesDeferred` counted only unactioned **disable** candidates. Each
figure was right on its own terms, and the summary line mixed them.

This matters more than a cosmetic slip: that job log is the audit record for account changes.
If its arithmetic is wrong, nobody reading it later can tell what the job actually did.

## The fix

Interim disables get their own counter, incremented from the row's `Action`, and are reported
only on the `of which` line under Delete candidates. The planned figure used in the warning
is renamed `$interimPlanned` so it cannot be confused with what was applied.

The same live run now reads correctly: `applied 0, deferred 86`, with `of which: 2 were
disabled while they wait to be deleted` below.

## Checks

- Two new tests pin the arithmetic — applied plus deferred must equal the disable candidate
  total — covering both the case where every disable slot goes to delete candidates and the
  case where the two queues share a run. **Both fail against the old counting.**
- Suite: **112 passed, 0 failed.**
- PSScriptAnalyzer clean.

author: hugovl1013
body:
Two changes on top of the previously merged review branch.

## Live 30-year Treasury risk-free rate
The Sharpe, CAPM and Fama-French calculations used a hard-coded 2.5% risk-free rate. They now pull the current 30-year US Treasury yield (Yahoo `^TYX`) through a shared cached helper (`get_risk_free_rate`), with a 2.5% fallback if the quote can't be fetched so nothing crashes. The Beta/Sharpe/CAPM section now prints the rate actually used and whether it was sourced live or fell back, so the assumption is transparent instead of hidden in the code.

Note: the rate is applied uniformly (USD 30Y) to every ticker, including non-USD benchmarked names — a known simplification versus matching the risk-free to the benchmark's currency.

## Dark-mode sidebar fix
The custom sidebar CSS hard-coded a light gradient background without a matching text color, so on a dark Streamlit theme the sidebar text rendered white-on-white and was unreadable. It now uses Streamlit's own `--secondary-background-color` theme variable, so the sidebar tracks whichever theme is active. Verified in both light and dark color schemes.

author: kirillcustom
body:
## Что было не так

Первый шаг рабочего цикла в README — «Make changes directly in `node_modules/some-package`». На Linux и в CI это молча портит общий кеш bun, а вместе с ним и все остальные проекты на машине.

Измерено на bun 1.4.0:

| | до `edit` | после `edit` |
|---|---|---|
| `nlink` файла в `node_modules` | 2 | 1 |
| inode файла и записи кеша | один и тот же | разные |
| правка редактором доходит до кеша | **да** | нет |
| чистая установка в третьем проекте | приезжает с чужой заплатой | чистая |

На macOS умолчание — `clonefile`, копия своя с самого начала, и там воспроизвести нечего. На Linux умолчание — `hardlink`, и там воспроизводится всегда. `--linker isolated` не спасает: инод файла в `node_modules/.bun/…` тот же, что в кеше.

`create` от этого не страдал никогда — он диффает против собственного кеша эталона. Портился кеш пользователя, за пределами проекта, и без единого слова.

## Как это делают соседи

| | что происходит перед правкой |
|---|---|
| `bun patch` | перезаписывает папку пакета копией из кеша — комментарий в их коде так и говорит, «cuz it could be hardlinked»; при изолированной раскладке отцепляет симлинк на общий стор и падает, если не смог |
| `pnpm patch` | править в `node_modules` не даёт вовсе: распаковывает пакет в `node_modules/.pnpm_patches/<pkg>@<ver>` |
| `yarn patch` | то же во временном каталоге |
| `bunch-package` до этого PR | ничего — шаг оставался человеку |

## Что стало

`bunch-package edit <package>` заменяет каждый разделённый файл пакета копией самого себя: те же байты, те же права, свой инод.

- каталоги обходятся рекурсивно; симлинки и всё, что не обычный файл, не трогаются;
- содержимое читается байтами, поэтому `.node`, `.wasm` и картинки переживают;
- файл, у которого инод и так один, не переписывается — незачем менять время правки;
- пакет, чей реальный путь уходит за пределы проекта (изолированный стор bun), — отказ вслух, а не запись в общий стор;
- пакет, который патчит сам bun через `patchedDependencies`, — отказ, как в `create`;
- всё это под замком `apply`: тот пишет через временный файл и перестановку, и без замка копия, прочитанная мгновением раньше, легла бы поверх только что применённого патча.

## Чем подтверждено

| проверка | норма | результат |
|---|---|---|
| сюита | 0 fail | **149 pass, 0 fail** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | чисто | чисто |
| корпус `run.ts` — совпадение с patch-package | все сравненные | **287 из 287** |
| корпус `run.ts` — совпадение с кодом до правки | все сравненные | **287 из 287** |
| корпус `idempotent.ts` | 0 NOT-idempotent | **287 idempotent, 0 NOT-idempotent** |
| сквозная проверка на `ms@2.1.2`, `--backend=hardlink` | кеш цел | nlink 2 → 1, кеш цел, `create` дал ожидаемый патч |

Пять патчей из 292 в этот прогон не сравнивались: пакет не поставился из реестра (`tonweb`, `nextra`, `react-scripts`, `pastel`, `wa-sqlite`). Отсюда 287, а не привычные 291. `@radix-ui+react-dialog+1.1.6` даёт `apply-failed` — как и раньше, и ровно так же он отказывает у patch-package: код выхода 1 у обоих, деревья совпадают.

### Мутации

Все шесть покраснели:

| мутация | тест, который упал |
|---|---|
| разрыв отключён (`nlink <= 1` → `>= 1`) | detaches the package so editing it no longer changes the cache |
| содержимое читается как utf-8 | carries binary content through byte for byte |
| режим не переносится | keeps the executable bit |
| не-файлы больше не пропускаются | leaves symbolic links as links |
| проверка выхода за проект снята | refuses to detach through a link that leaves the project |
| проверка чужого патча снята | refuses a package bun patches itself |

Седьмая мутация — снятая проверка `isSymbolicLink()` — **выжила**: она дублировала `!entry.isFile()`, а тест на симлинки проходил случайно, из-за порядка обхода каталога. Дубль убран, тест переписан на ссылку, ведущую наружу пакета, и теперь мутация его убивает.

## CI

`engines` обещает bun >= 1.0.0, а команда читает `nlink` и `realpath`; сюиту на 1.0 и 1.1 не прогнать. Поэтому дымовое задание на 1.0.36, 1.1.45 и 1.2.23 теперь создаёт хардлинк рядом с пакетом, зовёт `edit` и проверяет, что иноды разошлись, а содержимое цело.

## Чего этот PR не делает

Правки в отдельном каталоге (путь pnpm, `create --from <dir>`) здесь нет: она рвёт связь с `node_modules`, где живут все прочие команды, требует своего файла состояния и меняет весь рабочий цикл. Разрыв на месте закрывает измеренный отказ, ничего не ломая.

## Objectif

Retirer l'affichage du gamma de `app.html` en conservant le calcul intact dans la chaîne. Préparer la migration des couches gamma vers `radon.html`, sans la faire.

**PR non auto-mergée** — contenu public modifié, revue avant mise en ligne.

## Inventaire des surfaces gamma d'`app.html` et destination

| # | Surface | Détail | Destination |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Popup au clic** — bloc « Domaine ionisant », colonne Gamma | libellé (`dose gamma ambiante (cosmique + terrestre)` / `dose cosmique au sol`), valeur `nSv/h`, badge 3 états (● ancré / ◐ extrapolé / ◆ en cours) avec son `title`, points de confiance (`●●○`/`●○○`), tooltip ⓘ des repères UNSCEAR, ligne de détail `X nGy/h terrestre (plage lithotype …) + Y nSv/h cosmique` | **RETIRÉ** |
| 2 | **Popup** — pied du bloc ionisant | `Fond naturel Corse : 75–150 nSv/h · Niveau de référence radon : 300 Bq/m³` | **moitié gamma RETIRÉE**, moitié radon conservée |
| 3 | **Panneau « Mon lieu »** (`myPlaceRenderSummary`) | ligne « Dose gamma ambiante (ordre de grandeur) » + pastille de statut (Ancré / Extrapolé / Cosmique seule) | **RETIRÉ** — non nommé au brief, cf. écarts |
| 4 | **Popup** — intitulé « Domaine ionisant » | — | **CONSERVÉ** tel quel, cf. justification |
| 5 | **Mode Expertise** — curseur `w_I`, indice composite | l'indice est affiché, la valeur gamma ne l'est jamais | **CONSERVÉ** (`GELÉ-001a`) — cf. point d'honnêteté |
| 6 | **Export CSV expert** | `gamma_dose_rate_nSv_h`, `expert_w_I`, `expert_n_I_normalise` | **CONSERVÉ** (consigne explicite) |
| 7 | **Couches togglables du domaine ionisant** | aucune vivante : `b-openrad` (Gamma citoyen OpenRadiation) est mutée depuis le 2026-08-30, le chip de filtre « Ionisant » aussi | **RIEN À FAIRE** |
| 8 | **Entrées de légende / sous-titres mobile** | aucune : `LEGEND_CORE_IDS` ne contient aucune couche gamma ; `LEGEND_HTML.openrad` existe mais est inatteignable (couche mutée) | **RIEN À FAIRE** |
| 9 | **Panneau « ? » / repères documentaires** | `LAYER_DOC_ANCHORS.openrad` → `/cadre-scientifique.html#gamma-ambiant`, inatteignable pour la même raison | **RIEN À FAIRE** |
| 10 | **Clés i18n** `gamma_label_*`, `gamma_badge_*`, `gamma_conf_*`, `gamma_reperes_tooltip`, `myplace_gamma_*`, `pill_gamma_*` | orphelines après ce diff | **CONSERVÉES** pour le portage vers `radon.html` — même patron que `b-openrad` |
| 11 | **`_geoLastPoint.gamma_nSvh`** | objet écrit et jamais relu (aucune autre occurrence dans le fichier) | **NON TOUCHÉ** — pas de nettoyage non demandé |
| 12 | **Chaîne de calcul** (`calcGammaAmbient`, `calcTerrestrialGamma`, `GAMMA_TERRESTRE_PAR_LITHOTYPE`, `GEO_SUSC_GRID`, boost `POINTS_CHAUDS_RADIO`) | — | **INTACTE**, servira au portage |

## Deux choix éditoriaux à valider

**L'intitulé « Domaine ionisant » est conservé.** Le radon *est* un rayonnement ionisant, et le domaine garde deux membres dans le modèle — un seul est désormais affiché. Le renommer « Radon » laisserait entendre que le domaine ionisant se réduit au radon, ce qui serait faux.

**Le repère « Fond naturel Corse : 75–150 nSv/h » part avec la colonne.** C'était un repère de lecture pour une valeur qui n'est plus affichée ; le garder seul aurait laissé un ordre de grandeur sans rien à quoi le rapporter. Le repère radon (300 Bq/m³) reste, il porte sur la seule grandeur encore exposée.

## Ce qui n'a pas bougé

- `calcGammaAmbient` et ses dépendances : appel inchangé, au même endroit ; `domains.ionizing.gamma` reste peuplé (composants `cosmic_nSv_h`, `terrestrial_nGy_h`, `terrestrial_status`, plage, label — tous intacts).
- `computeExpertComposite` : `w_I = 0,2`, indice sur trois composantes, bornes `GAMMA_nSv_h: [50, 250]`, formule. `GELÉ-001a` et `NCRP-001` non touchés.
- Radon : bloc, classe, plage Bq/m³, mention de l'arrêté du 27 juin 2018, repère 300 Bq/m³.

## Vérifications

- `contrast-panels` : **0 critique / 0 AA** — cliquet 0/0 tenu.
- `extract-and-check-js` : 16 blocs, **0 échec**.
- Rendu en direct (`/app`, point granitique Bastelica 42,00/9,05) : **zéro occurrence** de `gamma`/`nSv`/`nGy` dans le DOM rendu du popup et de « Mon lieu ».
- Calcul relu en direct au même point : dose **210,2 nSv/h**, composants complets (`terrestrial_status: "ancre"`, plage 86,8–176,1 nGy/h), composite **0,954**, `n_I` **0,801**, poids **0,4 / 0,4 / 0,2**.

author: nathandela
body:
Investigation + live experiments for the owner ask: an automatic compaction on a working session must present itself as mid-task context maintenance and the flow must continue afterwards.

**Live-verified on codex 0.151.0** (second app-server client on a throwaway session running a 3-part task):

- `thread/compact/start` takes `threadId` only — no instructions parameter. The framing therefore rides the continuation prompt (proven sufficient: full narrative continuity across two compactions), with launch-time `-c compact_prompt=...` documented as an owner option.
- Codex's native `thread/queue/add` **defers behind a running compaction and auto-starts the queued message 31ms after `contextCompaction` completes** — provider-enforced serialization of exactly the ordering we need. At idle the queue drains instantly (~20ms), so enqueueing before the compact write would race it — the design enqueues on `provider_compacting`.
- `clientUserMessageId` does **not** dedup → at-most-once stays daemon-owned (same sidecar + write-boundary pattern as the compact dispatch).

The note proposes the v1 design (ADR-023 amendment 2 candidate): continuation enqueued by the same guard worker, durable marker, attended-skip, fixed prompt with a "if already done, don't start new work" clause, additive `continue_after_compact` setting defaulting on with automatic dispatch.

Docs only — no behavior change.

author: danfuzz
body: From: Agent working on behalf of @danfuzz (Claude Opus 5) An ex-post-facto review of #6633 — the rule the doc-comment arc applied — found two cases its text does not decide, and a census turned each into a population. ## The two gaps **An overload set with no implementation.** The rule says a set is one declaration and the blank line closing it "goes after the implementation". A set declared in an `interface` or in ambient `declare` form has none, so the sentence never reached it. Such a set is an overload set all the same, and closes after its last signature. The text also said no blank line falls "between them", of the signatures and the implementation; it now says between one part of the set and the next, and says that the implementation body's own statement spacing is not what that means. **The formatter-exempt constructs are three, not two.** `deno fmt` strips a blank line between two items of a type parameter list exactly as it does between two items of a parenthesized list. No documented type parameter exists in the tree today — a shape-independent sweep of 4456 files under `packages/` found five candidates, all false positives on reading — so this correction is forward-looking. An enumeration asserting itself exhaustive is what makes it worth fixing now rather than when the first one arrives. `skills/cf-review` carries the overload sentence and takes the same correction. ## The four code sites A census found eight implementation-less overload sets. Four already conform or carry no doc comment; four were waiting on these two sentences. - **`packages/api/index.ts`** — `IKeyable.key` and `IKeyableOpaque.key` each carry a blank line mid-run that **#6655 inserted**. The detector that drove the sweep stops extending an overload set when the next signature opens its generic list on the line below, so it reported these sites as *missing* a line rather than as places a line must not go, and the sweep obeyed the tool over the rule. Both blanks reached the served `commonfabric.d.ts` verbatim, so that file is regenerated here; the regeneration diff is exactly those two lines. - **`PresenceSocket.addEventListener`** and **`Hasher.digest`** gave every signature its own doc comment, which cannot survive a set with no blank lines in it — each comment would lose the blank line above it that §"The blank line above" requires. Both fold to the one-comment-and-`//`-labels form that §"Where one goes" already asked for. ## Verification `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `deno check`, `check-docs` (596 blocks), `check-skill-facts` (49 documents), `check-commonfabric-types` (up to date), and the `content-hash` and `static` suites. Every added line is within 80 columns. The formatter claims here were probed rather than assumed, but **off-pin**: this machine has `deno` 2.9.6 where `mise.toml` pins 2.9.4 and `mise` is not installed, so `tasks/check.sh` refuses the toolchain by design. ## 📋 Description

Helps public visitors discover information sheets from the LG onboarding checklist and aligns user-facing copy with the “information sheets” terminology.

This PR builds on `integration/one-pagers`, which already exposes information sheets from the About mega menu and footer. This change adds the missing onboarding checklist entry point and renames “Guides and fact sheets” to “Information sheets” across the public and admin UI.

---

## 🔖 What type of PR is this? _(check all that apply)_

- [x] 🍕 Feature
- [ ] 🐛 Bug Fix
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor
- [ ] 📦 Chore (Release)
- [ ] ✅ Test
- [ ] 🔥 Hot Fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation

| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| 📑 Design / Figma    | <!-- Paste link -->                                                  |

## ✨ Features / Changes Introduced

- Add an **information sheets** link to the LG onboarding checklist (`/onboarding-checklist-page-for-lg-adopting`) in the “Learn more” section, routing to `/info-documents`
- Rename user-facing copy from **“Guides and fact sheets”** to **“Information sheets”** across:
  - Public catalog page (title, empty state, intro default)
  - Super-admin management screens and site configuration card
  - About mega menu label/description
  - Footer link text
- Update related spec fixtures and example strings to match the new terminology

---

1. Open the LG onboarding checklist page (`/onboarding-checklist-page-for-lg-adopting`)
2. Scroll to the **Learn more** section
3. Confirm the new copy includes a link labeled **information sheets**

6. Open the About mega menu and confirm the entry is labeled **Information sheets**
7. Visit a page with the footer (e.g. `/contact`) and confirm the footer link reads **Information sheets**
8. As a super admin, open **Configuration management → Information sheets** and confirm the screen title/description use the updated terminology

- All info-document UI copy consistently says **Information sheets**

**After this change:**
