author: lesdylan
body:
## Summary

Fixes #105 — `hellish: syntax error near unexpected token `('` at every ssh login on a
Debian box — plus the family of "lexing ahead of execution" siblings found sweeping the
same syntax, detector-first:

- **exec_string chunking** (`exec_string3.c`/`exec_string4.c`): eval and the dot builtin
  now lex/parse sourced text in hazard-clipped chunks like the main input driver, so
  `shopt -s extglob`, alias definitions and nested sources affect how the REST of the
  same file lexes. bash-completion 2.11 and 2.14 both load silently now (the login chain
  is hellish sets BASH_VERSION → ~/.profile sources ~/.bashrc → sources bash_completion).
- **`shopt` joined the batch hazards** (`rl_multi_line2.c`) — same staleness on the
  script/file path.
- **Extglob in `[[ ]]` without the shopt** — lexer (`tokenizer.c`) and matcher
  (`builtin_dbracket2.c`) arm extglob for conditional operands, bash 4.1 semantics.
- **`eval --`** options terminator; **`complete`** `-e/-g/-j/-s/-u` action letters and
  silent `-D` default specs; **`shopt`** honest answers for real-but-unimplemented bash
  option names (query off / `-u` ok / `-s` loud), never success-while-doing-nothing.

## Detectors (red before the fixes, green after — permanent)

- `tests/login_bashrc_chain_test.py` — the whole profile→bashrc→completion chain in a
  pty (glob-discovered → `interactive` + `allocator` CI jobs).
- `tests/scripts/42_shopt_extglob_midfile.sh`, `43_alias_source_chain.sh`,
  `44_dbracket_extglob.sh` — byte-for-byte vs bash 5.3.9 across file/source/eval paths.
- Plugin corpus: bash-completion row promoted `unsupported` → **`loads`** (floor 80
  definitions), with `BASH_COMPLETION_COMPAT_DIR` pinned so the verdict tests the file,
  not the machine's drop-ins.

## Verification

- golden suite: 4323/4323 debug + release
- `tests/run_scripts.sh`: 112/112 (three new scripts)
- `tests/hard/run.sh`: 17/17
- `make pty-test`: green including the new chain test
- `cd tests && ./verify_alloc.sh`: both heaps identical, zero leaks
- `make plugin-corpus`: all passed, bash-completion at `loads`
- `make arena-stress`: clean
- `make norm`: passed

Closes #105

author: ayushkbhatia
body:
Wave 3 of the Africa fittings sprint. Plan: `~/.claude/plans/africa-fittings-sprint.md`.

## What this wave is

Waves 1 and 2 were horizontal — identify a thread, buy it well. This one is **vertical**: one article per industry that actually runs hydraulics across the markets we ship to.

| Article | The argument |
|---|---|
| `copper-mine-hydraulic-fittings` | A mine is two hydraulic populations — fleet fails mechanically, plant fails chemically |
| `gold-plant-hydraulic-fittings` | Zone the plant before writing a stock list; chemistry decides material |
| `oilfield-fittings-in-west-africa` | Rig-side flow equipment and plant hydraulics are two supply chains; split the order |
| `agriculture-and-construction-fittings` | The one-workshop-covers-everything case; variety is the constraint |
| `quarry-and-crusher-fittings` | Vibration is the whole problem — joint count beats hose grade |
| `water-well-drilling-rig-fittings` | Stocking a machine that moves; failures cluster after a rig-up |
| `port-and-terminal-fittings` | Salt air plus no maintenance window; stock for opportunity, not failure |
| `sugar-mill-and-agro-processing-fittings` | The calendar governs; survey in-season, order for the shutdown |
| `buying-fittings-in-south-africa` | Local supply is usually right — the four cases where it is not |
| `factory-and-fixed-plant-fittings` | The one place the thread population is a choice; standardise at hose changes |

Each is written **from the equipment, not from a country**. A copper concentrator asks the same questions in Zambia as in Chile; what makes it a Zambian article is the lane, the resupply distance and the imported fleet mix — one paragraph and a link, not the headline. No article is titled "hydraulic fittings supplier in X"; that stays with `/markets/{slug}`.

## The cap change

`blog-cross-links.test.ts` market-card budget **12 → 18 articles**, as instructed, with the reasoning written into the test rather than just the number changed. Eight of these ten carry a card because eight genuinely are about a place; the quarry and drilling-rig pieces carry none. Site-wide: **16 of 18**.

The test comment now states the standard to apply before spending more of the budget: *is this article ABOUT that country, or is it an article with a country bolted onto it?*

## New hub

`hydraulic-fittings-by-industry` rather than spreading the cluster across `maintenance-reliability` and `machine-down` — ten sector pieces would have diluted two clusters that each mean something specific, and left the sector cluster with no page of its own to rank. Ships with `bodyBlocks` and a focus keyword.

## What it refuses to publish

Production statistics, reserve figures and market shares — unmeasured. Any named mine, plant, port or operator as a customer. Any claim of local presence or stock outside Dubai.

The **South Africa** article is the honest one: it says plainly that local supply is usually the right answer there, and names the four cases where importing is not. Pretending otherwise would be obvious to any reader in that market.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` green (6/6). Imported to production 2026-09-01.

Blog **123 → 133 published**, **13 → 14 categories**. All ten carry the delivery-reach section.

author: bigdataaytee
body:
Item 4 of the third field report: **stop shipping untested paths.**

> Add emulator UI tests for: grant a folder → grid renders; tap a photo → viewer; tap a video → plays; relaunch after grant → grid renders. The "launches" check must run these, not just reach RESUMED.

## Stacked on #26

Base is `claude/crash-loop-fix`, not `main`. Two of these journeys are the crash-loop fix asserted on a device — on `main` they fail, which is the point. Merge [#26](https://github.com/BigdataAytee/trim-gallery/pull/26) first and this retargets to `main` cleanly.

## The journeys

`androidApp/src/androidTest/.../GalleryJourneyTest.kt`:

| | Journey | What it would have caught |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Grant a folder → the grid renders | the crash on grant: the grant row now exists before any media row points at it, and the night pass is scheduled |
| 2 | Tap a photo → the viewer opens | "tapping a photo closes the app" — the negative rectangle reaching `Modifier.size` |
| 3 | Tap a video → it plays | the video-tap crash, and a viewer drawn above a player that never starts |
| 4 | Relaunch after a grant → the grid renders | the crash loop, and the fast start |
| 5 | A startup that fails → recovery, and no retry | the loop half of the crash loop |

(5) is beyond what you asked for. It is the recovery screen from #26, which has never been drawn on a device, and your rule was that nothing counts until it has.

## Three things that make these worth having

**The database is the real one.** Opened through `AndroidSqliteDriver` and its callback, so `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is in force exactly as on your phone. The crash loop was a foreign key that the JVM driver leaves off — a journey test on a permissive database would certify the same bug a second time. In memory, so a run leaves nothing behind.

**Only the platform edges are faked**, and each is something an emulator cannot supply: the system picker's grant, a tree of your own files, WorkManager. Everything above them is the app — the picker's result handling, the grant row, the scan, the diff, the grid, the viewer, ExoPlayer. The picker's *result* is driven through `LocalActivityResultRegistryOwner`, so every line from the result onwards runs for real; its UI is another app's and driving it would break whenever Android's file browser changes.

**A green job is checked for having run them.** `pixelSmokeAndroidTest` is green when it runs zero tests, when a filter excludes a class, and when everything skips — which is the same shape of failure as the whole report. `.github/assert-journeys-ran.py` reads the instrumentation result XML back and fails unless each journey is present and passed.

Journey 3 asserts the player reaches `STATE_READY` and is actually playing, over the golden H.264 clip with its real AAC track, read off the `PlayerView` on the main thread.

## What else changed, and why

- `GalleryTestTags` in `shared/feature/gallery` — the grid, a tile and the viewer answer to a name. Finding a tile by position or by the words in it breaks whenever the layout or wording changes, and a UI test that breaks for unrelated reasons gets deleted.
- `GrantedFolders.grants`/`take` are `open`, and nothing else is. That is the one place the picker's answer is stood in for.
- `AndroidDatabase.create` takes a `name`, so a test can ask for an in-memory database through the production driver rather than opening its own.
- `androidApp/src/smoke/AndroidManifest.xml` declares `androidx.activity.ComponentActivity` — one line, in the CI-only variant, so **no installable build carries it**. androidx publishes a whole artifact (`ui-test-manifest`) that does nothing but add that line; this avoids the dependency.
- `ui-test-junit4` from the same group and version as every other Compose module here (you authorised this one in the last report).
- Detekt: `TooManyFunctions` excludes test sources, same reasoning and same source sets as the `LongParameterList` exclusion already there.

## What this does *not* do

- The **job name stays "App launches on a device"**, because renaming a required check breaks branch protection until it is re-pointed. It now runs the journeys; say the word and I will rename it.
- The system picker's own UI is not driven. Everything from its result onwards is.
- The tests use `file://` refs, not SAF document URIs — without a persisted permission there is no document to address. Coil, the frame extractor and ExoPlayer all go through the same `ContentResolver` either way.

Item 3's numbered status list follows, once CI says which of these actually pass.

author: bart-aig
body:
Eleventh run of trading day 2026-09-01. **No order placed in either book.** Zero drift, broker-first reconciliation.

## What this run measured

QQQ printed the session's first genuine **structural** confluence — spot 711.715 against a 50-day SMA of 711.5868 (+0.128, +0.018%). It also passes the 2026-08-25 fast-average test: on a flat index the 50d path is 711.59 → 711.06 → 711.02 → 711.05 → 710.95 over five sessions, i.e. ~0.5 points of drift over a TACTICAL hold against a ~2-point profit target. Most levels this arc has tested failed that test; this one does not.

Both candidate vehicles were **quoted** on the nearest board clearing the DTE-7 floor (2026-09-11, 10 DTE):

| contract | mid | spread | delta | OI | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QQQ 09-11 705P | 4.630 | 1.30% of mid | −0.3435 | 34,015 | $463.00 |
| QQQ 09-11 716C | 5.775 | 0.87% of mid | 0.4347 | 670 | $577.50 |

Both clear the ≤3%-of-mid TACTICAL liquidity gate with room. **Neither is affordable against $302.10 deployable.**

## Finding

**Deployable ≥ the band floor is not the same claim as "a compliant vehicle exists", and only the second is the gate.** The TACTICAL band is $300–1,000 and deployable is $302.10, so the band arithmetic reads *satisfied* — but at current spot, IV and DTE no 0.40–0.60-delta contract on a penny-wide index chain prices under $302.10. The cheapest measured is $463. The put's gap understates it: at −0.3435 delta it is below the band, and the in-band 710P is dearer.

Detector recorded (`_BAND_FLOOR_REACHED_IS_NOT_VEHICLE_AFFORDABLE`) so the next run **quotes** rather than infers, with an explicit note not to inherit the $463 figure.

**Honest scope: this changed no decision.** There was no fire — QQQ sat *on* the level, not through it, so the two-bar price clause was unsatisfied in both directions — and the 2026-08-26 regime capstone independently bars a QQQ scalp whose hold window (flat by the 09-02 close) contains tonight's PANW/DELL/CRDO/MDB prints. Three independent grounds; only this one was measurable to a number.

## Book state

All six equities underwater at 15:45Z — ROST −0.78% / LLY −1.39% / PNC −3.23% / MDLZ −0.53% / MMM −1.25% / GD −1.55% — so the profit-banking gate fails book-wide and no mechanical exit is available. Nearest target is MDLZ 64.70, 3.9% away. Nothing green-enough, so no SET TRAILING STOP alert fires. Hedge SPY 2026-11-20 700P marks $546 vs $749 (−27.1%), ~80 DTE, backstop-exempt.

Capital: total $3,966.63 | cash $552.10 == `unleveraged_buying_power` (no margin extended) | reserve $250 | **deployable $302.10**. Equity throttle 1 of 3 (GD 13:36Z); options 0 of 8; realized options P/L $0.00 vs the −$400 cap.

author: d3smondwong
body:
Replaces the left sidebar below 1024px with the designed phone chrome: a profile chip strip that **is** the header, drop-down birth-record / account panels, and a 3-item bottom tab bar.

Both chromes render unconditionally and CSS picks one, so `children` — the whole chart tree — is built once. Branching in JS would either duplicate it or flash on hydration, since the server snapshot cannot know the viewport.

## Fixes three things that were unreachable on a phone

| | Why |
|---|---|
| Creating a profile | the `+` was gated on `!isCollapsed` |
| Signing in / out | `.sidebar-login-btn` was `display: none` below 1024px |
| Deleting a profile | the sidebar's trash icon was hover-only opacity — on touch, invisible but tappable |

## Drops the 85px icon-rail tier (768–1023px)

It showed no labels and carried the first two bugs above, so the bottom nav covers that range strictly better. With it go the `isCollapsed` flag and its ten branches, the logo swap, the 3-letter name truncation and a whole media-query block.

The sidebar is now a fixed **210px** rather than `12%`, which had no clamp and resolved to 123px at 1024px — too narrow for "Compatibility" (truncated) and "AI Oracle Chat" (wrapped to three lines).

## Four pillars on one row at every width

Was 2×2 below `lg`. The width comes out of the cards' own padding and type sizes, not out of dropping any label. Where a label genuinely cannot fit, the break is applied uniformly to all four columns rather than letting one wrap alone. Thresholds are measured, not guessed, and documented at each site.

## Pre-existing bugs found and fixed along the way

- **Rooting chip.** `w-3/5` left it 86.4px of content while "Moderately Rooted" needs 97px, so that one chip wrapped and pushed every row below it 14px high in that card — including the gap between the branch caption and the void chip. Now 75% with `min-w-fit`.
- **Day-master card.** Its 2px border (vs 1px) made its content box 2px narrower, enough to wrap "HEAVENLY STEM" in that column alone. Its padding is now 1px lighter to compensate.
- **Hydration mismatch.** The four analysis cards seeded state from `window.innerWidth`, which disagrees with the server HTML.

## Other changes

- Tabs controlled from `?tab=` so a view is deep-linkable and Back-navigable
- One shared `useMediaQuery` replaces five hand-rolled resize listeners that sat at four different breakpoints (640 / 720 / 1024 / 1024 → 768 / 1024)
- Explicit `viewport` export; `dvh` and `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`
- Four hardcoded English header labels now go through `translations`
- Deletes two dead CSS rules — `.sidebar-profile-name::before` and the positional `> div:nth-child(2)` — neither of which ever matched

## Deliberately not included

`Edit profile ›` from the design frames. There is no update path in the codebase (only `deleteProfileAction`; create is `POST /api/chart`), so the row would be a dead control.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint` reports one error, in `lib/authContext.tsx`, verified pre-existing by stashing this branch and re-running.

Driven with Playwright at 375 / 430 / 440 / 789 / 900 / 1000 / 1024 / 1100 / 1280:
- all four pillar cards on one line with identical internal geometry (section labels, glyphs, captions, chips and toggles within 1px)
- chip strip → birth record: strip does not move, tab bar hides, chart stays behind
- sign in/out and create-profile reachable at 375px
- `?tab=insights` deep-links, survives reload, Back returns to Four Pillars, invalid values fall back
- no horizontal overflow at any width tested

author: kundakarlabp
body:
## Root causes
1. Normal-depth scoring used `abs(depth_imbalance)`, so an asks-heavy negative option-book imbalance could receive the same +2/+1 depth confirmation as bid-side pressure.
2. LIVE OrderFlow could still publish context bonus/veto when the canonical execution quote readiness contract rejected the quote (for example a spread wider than the live maximum).
3. After distinct persistent fresh microstructure invalidated a stale direction bias, final metadata still published the old direction as a full veto and withheld confirmation.

## Corrections
- Score depth only when its signed pressure supports the candidate domain/side; publish `depth_supports_side` and `strong_depth_supports_side`.
- In LIVE, use the live OrderFlow spread limit for the spread-quality score rather than the 12% shadow/research allowance.
- Gate context influence with `context_quality_eligible`, requiring canonical quote readiness, valid depth, non-stale data, and live context-age validity.
- After persistent reversal confirmation, use the validated microstructure side as effective context alignment and suppress the stale-direction veto.
- Apply the same fail-closed principle to LIVE LTP/depth-missing fallback context: diagnostic signal can remain, but it cannot contribute bonus/veto.
- Make the existing source-inspection context-role test quote-style agnostic while preserving its semantic assertion.

## Preserved invariants
- `allow_orderflow_trigger = False` remains structural; OrderFlow is context-only.
- No entry threshold, daily drawdown, risk sizing, contract selection, broker path, stop/target, or order behavior is loosened.
- Existing positive signed-depth shadow behavior remains 10/10 with bounded bonus 3.0.

## TDD / validation
- RED proven on test-only head `9073db8bb7253e5ae114ea70f5f02ed7ca400a1b`: the new persistent-reversal contract failed before implementation.
- Final head `639c6f496d7d2f7c6e424a1d5b4637304714e2a8` passes:
  - full pytest suite

- One unrelated MDM timing/log-throttle assertion failed on the first full-suite attempt and passed on the targeted rerun; the PR changes no MDM/tick files.

author: lberserq
body:
Stacked on #51610

### Changelog category

* Improvement

### Description for reviewers

Implements the KQP/WLM side of the Memory Quota 2.0 interface from #51610: `GetMemoryAvailability()` reports real node and pool headroom, and `isOptional` quota requests are refused under memory pressure instead of being treated as mandatory.

The branch is `main` plus a local merge of `dq_memory_quota_2`, so the PoC's files appear in the diff. Review the last two commits only: `cc8b2a491d2` (implementation) and `73b0a7b68c7` (review fixes); after #51610 lands this rebases to a small diff.

- **`IKqpResourceManager::GetTxMemoryAvailability(tx)`** replaces the stub `spilling ? 0 : 1'000'000'000`. Returns `0` while the tx's spilling cookie (node or pool) is set — the yellow zone; otherwise `min(node headroom, named-pool headroom)` in bytes, with the cookie and the headroom read under the same RM lock. Never negative for now: there is no reclaim signal in the code yet, a single comment marks the slot.
- **Optional quota** in `TMemoryQuotaManager::AllocateExtraQuota` and `TChannelQuotaManager::AllocateQuota`: with `isOptional == true` the request is refused without error in the yellow zone (checked lock-free even when the channel already holds quota) or when it exceeds current headroom or RM cannot grant it. The mandatory path is unchanged. The pre-flight compares against full headroom, so an optional grant may still move the tx into the yellow zone; the zone is then reported on the next call.
- **Counters** `RM/OptionalQuotaDenied` and `RM/OptionalQuotaDeniedBytes` (bytes as requested by the task, not the rounded RM ask), incremented through one null-safe helper so test stubs without counters do not crash.

Tests in `kqp/rm_service/ut/kqp_rm_ut.cpp`: `OptionalQuotaDeniedAtYellowZone` (exact idle availability → yellow zone entered via real allocations → availability 0 → optional denied with counter deltas, mandatory still granted), `OptionalQuotaDeniedWhenExceedsPool`, `FreeQuotaSymmetryAfterOptionalGrant` — no internal state is poked; the spilling cookie flips through the public allocation path. `executer_actor`, `ut/channels`, `node_service` build clean.

```text
ResolvedIntent
→ exact bounded DelegatedWork

author: astronauteweb
body:
## Ce qui n'allait pas

Un rail ordinaire n'avait **aucune physique** : une polyligne que seul le traceur de faisceau consultait. Le corps la traversait sans rien sentir, quel que soit son état. Seul un **conduit** (le drapeau `conduit`) avait un tube — et aucun tableau livré n'en pose. En jeu, un rail n'était donc qu'un dessin.

## La règle

Tout rail a un corps. **Ce qui le franchit : le plasma, rien d'autre** — c'est-à-dire de la vapeur sur une ligne de champ dont l'arc est engagé. L'eau, la glace **et la vapeur ordinaire** butent.

Ce qui distingue encore le **raccourci** (`conduit`) est ailleurs et reste entier : lui seul, arc engagé, laisse en plus ignorer le *décor* et franchir une paroi. « Arc » et « ouvert » sont donc devenus deux qualités distinctes du tube — sans quoi un arc courant sur n'importe quel rail aurait fait de chaque rail un contournement d'énigme, et le raccourci ne se mériterait plus.

Deux épaisseurs, et chacune est celle qu'on dessine : le conduit garde son tube de convoyage (`plasmaRailRadius × 2,5`), le rail ordinaire prend sa **bande de capture** (`plasmaRailRadius`), celle que le calque trace déjà. Le dépôt s'est fait avoir une fois dans l'autre sens — « le tube mentait sur sa taille », collision sur 150, dessiné sur 60.

## Le piège, signalé par le concepteur et vérifié

La sortie de l'état plasma. Le nuage voyage **sur** l'axe, donc dans la paroi ; l'instant où l'arc tombe il redevient vapeur ordinaire, que la ligne refuse. Deux mesures ont dicté la solution.

**Une paroi qui pousse le gaz le catapulte à la longue.** La vitesse se lit `(prd − pos)/dt` : repousser la seule position prédite *ajoute* de la vitesse, et le répéter à chaque pas la pompe. Mesuré : la vapeur pressée contre une ligne finissait à **37,8 u** de l'axe, au-delà des 30 où le faisceau s'ionise — elle ne pouvait plus allumer ce qu'elle voulait franchir. **Le verrou de #304, revenu par une autre porte.** La position d'origine est donc alignée sur la même hauteur normale : la composante rentrante tombe à zéro, la tangentielle est gardée. Le gaz est arrêté, pas chassé.

**L'épaisseur.** Le gaz bute sur un cœur à 0,9 du rayon de capture — assez fin pour qu'il reste toujours de la vapeur dans les 30 unités où le faisceau s'ionise, assez épais pour qu'on ne le tunnelise pas. Un premier essai à 0,5 laissait passer un nuage lancé à 700 u/s.

### Mesuré, rail vertical de rayon 30, corps lancé à 700 u/s

| | résultat |
| --- | --- |
| eau | **0 passée**, repoussée, centre à x = −573 |
| glace | **0 passée**, centre à x = −756 |
| plasma | **37/37 passées** |
| vapeur pressée contre la ligne | la plus proche à **27,0 u** de l'axe (capture à 30), 40 u/s — elle flotte, pas soufflée |

Et la condensation **sur** la ligne — le joueur qui lâche la touche en plein voyage — est une expulsion bornée comme celle d'un conduit : aucune particule ne reste dans la paroi, et le pic reste très loin des 2861 u/s de l'expulsion non bornée.

## Le dessin

**Ce qui bloque se dessine comme tel.** Le rail se montre en paroi dès qu'il barre, et ne redevient la ligne de champ pointillée que là où il laisse vraiment passer : arc engagé **et** corps gazeux.

> ⚠️ **Cela s'écarte de la consigne littérale.** La demande disait « conserver le design actuel en vapeur » — elle a été écrite quand la vapeur passait. Depuis la correction, elle bute aussi, et un rail qui barre en gardant l'air d'un passage serait le piège même qu'on veut retirer. C'est **une ligne à changer** si la lecture littérale est préférée.

**Les coudes se raccordent.** Les deux arêtes étaient tracées tronçon par tronçon : au sommet, les droites décalées se croisaient au lieu de se rejoindre — encoche à l'intérieur du virage, trou à l'extérieur, diagonales parasites en travers de la bande. Le contour se calcule maintenant d'un seul trait, avec un **raccord d'onglet** (bissectrice des normales, allongée de 1/cos(θ/2), bornée à trois épaisseurs pour qu'un angle aigu ne fasse pas jaillir une aiguille).

**Les bouts se referment en demi-lune.** Le tube est une capsule : arête, demi-cercle, arête. Le cercle entier rapporté au bout posait un anneau en travers de la paroi, qui n'existe nulle part dans la collision.

Plus un **biseau** (le chant, comme la tranche des solides dans le décor) et une **veine** claire au milieu : même figée, la ligne reste une ligne de champ.

## La bascule, en électricité, dans les deux sens

Chaque rail garde sa valeur courante, qui court vers sa cible en un tiers de seconde — c'est cet écart qui donne son temps à l'éclair. L'intensité vaut `4·v·(1−v)` : nulle aux deux bouts, maximale à mi-chemin. **Une seule formule, et l'effet joue à l'ouverture comme à la fermeture** sans qu'une ligne ait à savoir dans quel sens on va.

Trois filaments serpentent le long de chaque tronçon, re-tirés trente fois par seconde, sur un cœur blanc qui court toute la ligne ; aux sommets, un éclat plus vif — c'est là que le champ force le plus. Le traceur d'éclair existait déjà (rayon vivant, sursaut de victoire) ; il remonte simplement avant le dessin des rails.

Une sonde de plus, dans la lignée de `__sim` et `__laserEtat` : `__railsEngages`. Sans elle, jouer la bascule à l'écran demandait de réussir l'énigme à la main.

## L'impact sur les tableaux livrés, mesuré

Les trois tableaux à rail les posent tout en haut de la salle — corps du rail à partir de y = 30, 70 et 110. La route du départ (−950, 0) au sas (y ±120) passe **dessous**, avec 780 à 860 u de hauteur libre.

La preuve de traversée (`generateur.accessible`) ne compte pas les rails, et c'est voulu : ce sont des portes d'**état**, comme la grille, la membrane et le rideau qu'elle ignore déjà toutes. Un commentaire le dit sur place.

**Ce que je n'ai pas vérifié** : je n'ai pas rejoué les trois énigmes de bout en bout. Si l'une demande de monter un corps gelé au-dessus du rail, il le gênera désormais.

## Les commandes

Neuf tests neufs, dont trois sur la seule sortie de l'état plasma. Un d'entre eux mesurait le mauvais axe — le rail est vertical, je comparais des ordonnées — et passait donc à vide ; corrigé.

`dev` a été rattrapé dans la branche (7 commits, dont l'écran LA DESCENTE) et la combinaison est vérifiée :

```
pnpm type-check   # 0 erreur
pnpm test         # 742 tests verts
pnpm build        # propre
```

Vérifié à l'écran, salle 20 : les quatre états (paroi en liquide, ligne ouverte en plasma, la bascule à 60 ms dans les deux sens) et les trois coudes de l'arche.

author: fdurand
body:
# Description
With a fixed TTL on the pfdhcplistener rate-limit cache, every endpoint that renews its DHCP lease in the same wave gets a cache entry that expires in the same second — so the entire population re-floods the pfqueue `pfdhcplistener` queue in one synchronized burst every `dhcp_rate_limiting` cycle. Observed on a lab server with ~30k clients on a 300s lease and `dhcp_rate_limiting=610s`: ~19k tasks landing at once per cycle, with the tail of each burst aging past the 300s task TTL ("Data not found for task" drops).

This jitters the suppression window by ±25% (`add_jitter($rate_limiting, $rate_limiting/4)`), so expirations spread across the cycle and de-correlate further every cycle. The average window stays at the configured value, and the minimum (75%) stays well above the renew interval so suppression still works. Also runs the config value through `normalize_time()` so `type=time` values like `610s` are handled properly instead of via numeric coercion.

Measured on the lab server (peak queue depth per cycle): 19,335 → 9,596 → 4,890 over three consecutive cycles, with zero drops from the second cycle on.

# Impacts
- pfdhcplistener packet rate limiting: per-packet cache TTL becomes `dhcp_rate_limiting` ±25% instead of exact; behavior with `dhcp_rate_limiting=0` (disabled) is unchanged.
- pfqueue `pfdhcplistener` queue inflow shape on short-lease networks.

# Delete branch after merge
YES

# Checklist
- [n/a] Document the feature (no new configuration; documentation.conf already describes dhcp_rate_limiting)
- [n/a] Add OpenAPI specification
- [n/a] Add unit tests (sbin daemon path; validated with perl -c and three measured cycles in production-like load)
- [ ] Add acceptance tests (TestLink)

# NEWS file entries
## Enhancements
* pfdhcplistener jitters its DHCP rate-limiting cache window (±25%) so short-lease networks no longer re-flood pfqueue in one synchronized wave every dhcp_rate_limiting cycle

author: mrbinnacle
body:
Executes **item 1** of the #368 ruling. Does not close #368: items 2 (Path C migration) and 3 (threshold re-derivation) are not built, and the detector's strict xfails are unchanged.

## What lands

`docs/INVARIANTS.md` §8. The estimand of record is the **discordant table** (McNemar/sign-test convention); half-update remains the interim operational stopping heuristic; the section carries the measured sensitivity that is the entire justification for keeping it.

## It records the corrected claim, not the flattering one

The ruling first argued tie dilution is monotone toward 0.5. **Its own amendment falsified that.** A sweep over `w, l in [0, 60]`, `t in [1, 80]` found **80,011 grid points where half-update RAISES** `P(rate > 0.60)` relative to drop-ties — loss-leaning cases pulled up toward 0.5, worst `w=0, l=2, t=7` at `0.0996` against `0.0640`.

Writing §8 around the original argument would have documented a claim the project had already measured as false, in the file whose job is to be the tracked anchor for load-bearing rules.

What survives is narrower, and it is a receipt:

| Gate | Result on the swept grid |
|---|---|
| PASS (`P >= 0.95`) | **Zero** crossings that drop-ties keeps below the gate — tie encoding cannot mint a false KEEP there |
| FAIL (`P <= 0.05`) | **Three** escapes (first `w=0, l=3, t=5`, `0.0527` against `0.0256`), all to INCONCLUSIVE, never to PASS |

So the cost is a delayed verdict, not a claim-integrity failure — bounded by the grid, not proven in general. §8 says so in those terms.

## Two things §8 makes explicit that were implicit before

- §1 presented the half-update encoding without qualification. It now points at §8.
- The locked `0.60/0.95/0.05` thresholds were calibrated against the blended rate and **do not transfer** to the conditional parameter `P(full wins | discordant)` unexamined. Re-deriving them is part of the migration and must be pre-registered before a production run consumes it.

## The xfails are untouched

`tests/test_halfupdate_tie_sensitivity.py` still fires 7 xfails. The ruling's acceptance is that they resolve when the encodings agree — after migration. Loosening them to close this ticket is precisely what that acceptance forbids, so they stay red-by-design.

## Verification

`scripts/drift_check.py` PASS (13 contracts) · `tests/test_receipts_index.py` 14 passed · the tie-sensitivity detector unchanged at 46 passed / 7 xfailed. Documentation only; no production code touched.

*Revisit if:* a production design exceeds the swept grid (`w, l > 60` or `t > 80`) — re-run the sweep before relying on the PASS-gate zero; or a tie-heavy axis shows the practical-significance inversion, where rare-but-real wins are drowned by ties in a way that matters operationally. That is an effect-size floor question for the Gate-2 net-lift bounds, not a reason to resurrect the blended rate.

author: guyvdbroeck
body:
`FrontendSession::build_run` short-circuits only when preprocessing leaves no
variables. A refutation is not that case: `reduced.cnf` is by design an explicit
contradiction over the ORIGINAL variable count, because DIMACS cannot portably
spell the empty clause. So a refuted run went on to select a spec and build a
full vtree over a formula whose answer the record already gives —
`PreprocessRecord::unsat` says "The count is 0 and no compilation is needed".
Construction gets a share of the wall that is left (by default a third of it, at
least 90 s and never past the run deadline), so the longer the caller's budget,
the more of it a refutation spends building a vtree nothing will compile.

`RunVtree` gains a third variant, `Refuted`, and `build_run` returns it as soon
as the record says the instance was refuted — before selection, before
construction. `built()` is `None` for it, so `write_to_dir` writes the bundle
alone and names no vtree files, and the command-line summary reports the verdict
where the vtree lines would be.

API note: `RunVtree` is public and this is a new variant, so an exhaustive match
on it needs the new arm.

主な病理:

author: rootkiller6788
body:
A Constant whose values are ml_dtypes.float8_e4m3fnuz was getting exported to ONNX as FLOAT8E4M3FN. The lookup table in dtype_to_onnx mapped fnuz to "FLOAT8E4M3FN" (looks like a copy-paste of the line above it), so the type enum was silently wrong. Anything reading the exported weights later would interpret the fp8e4m3fnuz bytes as fp8e4m3fn, which gives different numbers for most values.

This shows up as soon as you touch the tensor: either create a Constant with fp8e4m3fnuz values, or import an ONNX model that has a FLOAT8E4M3FNUZ initializer and access `.values` (which forces LazyValues to load into a numpy fnuz array), then export.

Fixed the mapping to FLOAT8E4M3FNUZ and added a regression test that checks the exported data_type and that the raw bytes round-trip. Verified with the onnx-graphsurgeon test suite (tests/test_exporters.py and tests/test_importers.py pass; the remaining failures in test_examples.py are a local no-python3-in-bash environment issue, unrelated).

author: zcsizmadia
body:
Closes #9. Also closes the gap that made everything else unreachable: install created a distro, but **nothing served the pipe**, so `docker` had no way in.

- **`hawser proxy`** serves the pipe in the foreground and relays to the distro, path translation on by default. A supervising Windows service is v0.2 (#3); this is the v0.1 way to run the bridge.
- **Pipe selection never takes the default pipe from Docker Desktop.** Hawser prefers `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` when it''s free and serves its own when it''s held, so trying Hawser stays a zero-risk experiment. Presence is probed by *dialing* — a pipe exists only while a server holds it, so checking for the path would be meaningless.
- **`internal/dockerctx`** manages the `hawser` context through the docker CLI rather than by writing `~/.docker/contexts` metadata directly. That layout is an implementation detail Docker has changed before; hand-writing it would make Hawser the thing that breaks next time.
- **Uninstall restores the previous selection before removing the context** — docker refuses to remove the context in use, and leaving the user on a context that no longer exists would break every subsequent docker command. That''s the opposite of "nothing else on the system was modified".
- **A missing docker CLI is typed and non-fatal.** The engine still works over `DOCKER_HOST`, so a working install is never rolled back over a missing convenience.

**One fix found by watching it run:** relay failures were logged at Debug, so an engine that was down looked like the bridge doing nothing at all. They''re Warn now — `filterClosed` already drops the ordinary ways a client hangs up, so what remains is a real fault the operator should see. Confirmed: `warning: connection failed error=read response: unexpected EOF` instead of silence.

**Verified against real WSL and the real docker CLI on a machine running Docker Desktop:**

```
serving pipe pipe=\\.\pipe\hawser_engine
  reason=\\.\pipe\docker_engine is already served by another engine (likely Docker Desktop)
docker context ready context=hawser host=npipe:////./pipe/hawser_engine
```

`docker context ls` showed all three contexts coexisting, `docker --context hawser version` reached the relay, and uninstall removed the context leaving `desktop-linux` selected and Docker Desktop untouched.

Also set the repo About text and topics, as requested.

author: kphurley7
body:
## MERGES LAST - keep this PR in draft

This spec change must NOT be merged until webdev PR #34100 has landed and the
feature is launch-ready. `grid-api` main feeds the nightly docs sync and the
Stainless public docs/SDKs, so merging early would publish an endpoint that
does not exist yet. Leave it as a draft until then.

## What

Adds `POST /stablecoins/{stablecoinId}/request-grid-enablement`, matching the
endpoint added in webdev #34100.

The endpoint is how a platform asks Lightspark to approve a registered
stablecoin as a Grid settlement currency. It records the request only: it moves
`gridOperationsStatus` from `NOT_ENABLED` to `PENDING_APPROVAL` and returns the
updated `Stablecoin`. Lightspark drives the remaining `ENABLING` and `ENABLED`
steps.

- No request body, and no `Idempotency-Key` header. The call carries no payload
  to disagree about, so a repeat request while the stablecoin is already
  `PENDING_APPROVAL` is an idempotent `200` that changes nothing.
- `ENABLING`, `ENABLED` and `DISABLED` belong to the Lightspark-driven
  workflow and are refused with `409`
  `STABLECOIN_GRID_ENABLEMENT_NOT_REQUESTABLE`, so a stale request cannot walk
  an in-flight or live token backwards.
- `403` when the caller does not own the stablecoin, `404` when it does not
  exist.

## Files

- `openapi/paths/stablecoins/stablecoins_{stablecoinId}_request-grid-enablement.yaml` (new)
- `openapi/openapi.yaml` - path entry
- `openapi/components/schemas/errors/Error409.yaml` - adds
  `STABLECOIN_GRID_ENABLEMENT_NOT_REQUESTABLE` to the code table and enum
- `openapi.yaml` / `mintlify/openapi.yaml` - regenerated bundles (`make build`)

## Difference from the vendored copy in webdev #34100

The path object here is identical to the vendored one. The one addition is the
`Error409` enum entry: the vendored copy documents the `409` response but never
adds `STABLECOIN_GRID_ENABLEMENT_NOT_REQUESTABLE` to the enumerated 409 codes,
and generated clients hard-reject an unknown error code. Worth mirroring back
into the webdev vendored spec.

## Verification

- `make build` regenerates the bundle cleanly.
- `make lint` passes (0 errors); no warning or info references the new path or
  operation.
- The regenerated canonical bundle's new path object compares equal to the
  vendored one in webdev #34100.

author: djnsty23
body:
Three fixes from one Brain session, each with its measurement.

## auto-brain could dispatch to existing sessions and nothing else (8.146.0)

Step 2 said a repo with no session was "not a session to brief" and to leave
starting one to the user. Step 5 offered `send_message`, which reaches existing
sessions only. `allowed-tools` declared neither that nor `spawn_task`.

So for a session-less repo the skill left two paths, ignore it or work it
inline. `[measured 2026-09-01]` a coordinator told to run the fleet took the
second across four repos in one session, and two branch collisions followed,
both from the coordinator writing to refs a briefed session was pushing to.

Step 2 now routes a session-less repo to a task chip and says not to work it
inline. Step 5 carries both mechanisms with the tier cap, the
one-chip-per-verifiable-unit rule and the stand-alone prompt requirement ported
from `brain`, which already had all of it.

The auto-archive paragraph in `brain` asserted a per-operator toggle was on. It
was turned off the same day. It now gives the probe that answers it, plus why
the setting is hazardous for this role: the archive keys on any PR a session
record is linked to, including one it merely merged, so a coordinator is
archived by its ordinary work.

## brain mandated a tool it did not declare (8.147.0)

Same defect, in the skill that documents the correct behaviour: step 4
instructs `spawn_task` while `allowed-tools` declared neither it nor
`send_message`, `AskUserQuestion` or `Monitor`.

A crude scan puts the rate at 15 of 63 skills. That number is unverified and
carries false positives by construction, since the detector cannot separate an
instruction to use a tool from a mention of one. Only these two are confirmed by
hand. A gate with a stated instruction-versus-mention rule is queued separately.

## The ownership section buried real sessions (8.149.0)

`[measured 2026-09-01]` three branches carried 11, 13 and 21 untitled,
unaddressable rows. Those 45 buried the 8 real sessions well enough that a
reader took the section for a 53-session fleet.

Three or more such rows now collapse to one counted line with the idle range.
Collapsed rather than dropped, so the count stays challengeable, and the branch
still declares how many sessions share it. An addressable session is never
collapsed whatever its title, and neither is a titled one.

Scenario I covers it, opening with a control that asserts the session-record
seam really produces an addressable session, so the rest cannot pass vacuously.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 90/90 suites. `test-brain-brief`: 134/134 assertions.
- Mutation-tested twice. The first attempt broke the COUNT while the
  never-collapsed assertion still passed, so it proved nothing about the
  property under test. Emptying the shown list instead fails the control and the
  safety assertion together.
- Full `npm run gate` runs before this leaves draft.

8.148.0 is deliberately skipped: it is reserved for a concurrent session whose
branch was unpushed when a collision was caught.

author: t-kalinowski
body:
## Summary

High-parallelism transcript runs could fail when tests inferred worker, relay, or response state from short wall-clock windows. Managed R resolution could also use pak's five-second subprocess startup limit, which is too short when the host is oversubscribed.

This change replaces those scheduler assumptions with causal checkpoints and gives pak's asynchronous resolver subprocess a 60-second startup allowance.

## User-facing changes

- Managed R requirements no longer fail only because pak's resolver child takes more than five seconds to report readiness under host load.
- MCP inputs, outputs, and lifecycle semantics are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Publish fixture markers atomically and observe them with kqueue, FIFO, sideband, and process-state checkpoints.
- Gate stdin ownership, idle input, completion, replacement startup, partial frames, and relay retirement before asserting their results.
- Replace Python and R poll-count assumptions with public input boundaries or worker-private FIFOs.
- Verify that the pak startup timeout overrides an inherited value and start a fresh poll before releasing a blocked automatic resolver.

## Notes

The complete transcript suite passed with 32 jobs on a 16-core macOS host. `scripts/check` also passed.

author: songlong0506
body:
## Bệnh

Ca thật, đọc từ AI Call Log `BAChat 2026-09-01 13:07:15` (dự án quản lý khóa học bắt buộc). Lượt 38 BA hỏi:

> *"…ngoài việc **khóa học hết hạn**, còn có trường hợp nào khác cần xử lý không? Ví dụ như nhân viên nghỉ việc, chuyển phòng ban, hay khóa học bị hủy…"*

Người dùng trả lời (nghỉ việc + chuyển vai trò). Hai lượt sau, BA phát lại đúng khung câu ấy:

> *"…ngoài việc **nhân viên nghỉ việc và chuyển vai trò**, còn có trường hợp nào khác cần xử lý không? Ví dụ như khóa học bị hủy, hay nhân viên chuyển phòng ban…"*

Câu cũ nằm sẵn trong khối *"Các câu hỏi BẠN ĐÃ HỎI — TUYỆT ĐỐI KHÔNG phát lại"* gửi lên model, và phanh tất định vẫn để nó đi qua.

## Bốn tầng đã hụt, và chỗ sửa

**1. Hai phía của phanh dùng hai phép thử khác nhau — phanh không chạy lần nào.**
`AskedQuestionHistory.Collect` nhận diện lượt hỏi bằng *"có chip HOẶC có dấu hỏi"*, còn `BAChatService.ApplyRepeatedQuestionBrake` bằng *"có chip HOẶC cờ câu-mở"* — mà cờ ấy chỉ bật khi câu chứa một cụm xin-kể (`NarrativeCues`: "kể giúp", "mô tả"…). Cả một lớp câu hỏi **không chip và không mang cụm xin-kể** vì thế được ghi vào sổ nhưng không bao giờ bị soi lại. Trong buổi đó, gần một nửa số lượt BA (12, 14, 16, 20, 26, 28, 30, 38 và lượt cuối) có hình dạng này. Comment ở `Collect` khẳng định hai phía dùng chung điều kiện — không đúng.

→ Cả hai phía nay gọi chung `AskedQuestionHistory.IsAskingTurn`.

**2. Kể cả khi chạy, phép đo tương đồng cũng hụt.**
Model giữ nguyên khung câu **VÉT** và chỉ thay vế liệt kê bằng chính câu trả lời vừa nhận. Đo lại bằng đúng thuật toán `QuestionCore` + `IsRepeat`:

```
core A: ngoài việc khóa học hết hạn, còn có trường hợp nào khác cần xử lý không?
core B: ngoài việc nhân viên nghỉ việc và chuyển vai trò, còn có trường hợp nào khác cần xử lý không?

containment = 0.750  (ngưỡng RepeatContainment = 0.80)  ✗
jaccard     = 0.522  (ngưỡng RepeatJaccard     = 0.60)  ✗
```

Dưới **cả hai** ngưỡng. Hạ ngưỡng thì chặn oan hàng loạt câu đào sâu thật (rationale đo đạc ở `RepeatJaccard` giữ nguyên, không đụng tới), nên bắt bằng **hình dạng**: `IsSweepRepeat` đòi ba điều kiện cùng đạt — câu mang một cụm VÉT ("nào khác", "gì nữa"…, hai chữ, không nhận "nào" đứng một mình), có vế liệt kê ngăn bằng dấu phẩy, và **đuôi sau dấu phẩy cuối** trùng khít với đuôi một câu vét đã hỏi (dài tối thiểu bằng ngưỡng đo mờ). Câu vét TIẾP trên câu trả lời vừa nhận (*"ngoài hai báo cáo này, còn cần báo cáo nào khác không?"*) có đuôi khác nên đi qua.

**3. Bản đồ bao phủ đánh `[RÕ]` khi mới trả lời 2/3 ca BA tự nêu.** — đây là chỗ chặn từ gốc.
Chuẩn `[RÕ]` của nhóm «Luồng ngoại lệ» chỉ đòi *"ít nhất một tình huống hỏng kèm cách xử lý"*, nên dòng lên `[RÕ]` dù *chuyển phòng ban* và *khóa học bị hủy* chưa ai đụng tới. Thiệt hại kép: `[RÕ]` vừa **cấm** BA hỏi lại nhóm, vừa xóa luôn mẩu `gap` — thứ duy nhất chỉ đường hỏi tiếp. Không còn gì hợp lệ để hỏi (hai nhóm còn mở đều bị prompt khóa "để cuối"), BA phát lại chính câu vét ấy.

→ `requirement-coverage.v4.md`: "ít nhất một" là **sàn** cho ca người dùng tự kể, không phải giấy phép đóng nhóm khi câu hỏi của BA đã nêu đích danh mấy ca mà câu đáp chỉ xử lý một phần. Mỗi ca nêu tên là **một vế** (nối vào luật "đếm vế" sẵn có), và `gap` phải gọi **TÊN** các ca còn treo.

**4. Tác dụng phụ phải chặn trước.** Vì phanh nay soi cả lượt không chip, vế hỏi *"Anh/chị thấy mình hiểu vậy đã đúng chưa?"* bỗng trở thành khoá so khớp. Nó dài hơn ngưỡng "vế hỏi quá ngắn" nên ngưỡng đó không đỡ, mà hai lượt CHỐT LẠI hai điều khác hẳn nhau vẫn kết bằng đúng câu ấy ⇒ trùng khoá tuyệt đối giữa hai lượt không liên quan. Xử bằng đúng cơ chế sẵn có: giữ NGUYÊN cả `message` làm khoá. Nhận diện hẹp ở cả hai vế (cụm xác nhận phải đứng CUỐI, và cả vế hỏi phải ngắn hơn 56 ký tự sau chuẩn hoá) để **kịch bản mẫu** và **ví dụ tính thử** — hai thứ prompt bắt buộc phải chở đủ dữ kiện, đều dài trên 90 — vẫn được đem so bình thường.

## Ngoài phạm vi PR này

Lượt sinh ra response đó lẽ ra **không hỏi gì cả**: system message `[8]` là `## LƯỢT NÀY: BÀY BẢNG LUỒNG NGHIỆP VỤ (bắt buộc)`, model trả `flowMap` rỗng, và `BAChatService` fail-open (`if (draft.FlowMap.Count > 0)`) nên lượt bảng rơi xuống thành lượt chat thường — model phải tự nghĩ ra câu hỏi để lấp. Fail-open là thiết kế cố ý ("một lượt hỏi thừa rẻ hơn một lượt câm") và cổng mở lại ở lượt sau, nên PR này không đụng tới; ghi lại ở đây vì nó là thứ tạo ra khoảng trống mà câu vét lấp vào.

## Kiểm chứng

`dotnet test` — **2017 passed, 0 failed**. Test mới:

- `AskedQuestionHistoryTests` (+6): bắt đúng cặp câu vét của ca thật, và chốt rằng nó nằm ngoài tầm phép đo tương đồng (hai phanh không thay thế nhau được); không chặn câu vét TIẾP; bỏ qua câu không phải vét và câu có đuôi cụt; hai lượt chốt lại khác nhau không bị coi là một; ví dụ tính thử kết bằng cụm xác nhận vẫn được đem so; `IsAskingTurn` đếm câu hỏi không chip nhưng không đếm lượt tóm tắt.

- `CoverageSweepQuestionRuleTests` (mới): giữ luật "đếm ca đã nêu" và chuẩn `[RÕ]` của nhóm ngoại lệ không trôi khỏi prompt.

author: lobantseff
body:
## What changed

- serialize stale first-page refreshes ahead of pagination and keep detail selection tied to image identity
- clear failed refresh and update-check lifecycle state so later work is not blocked
- save full-resolution images in the background instead of blocking the UI thread
- let image loads and saves fall back to the network when the cache cannot be read
- discard corrupt cached image bytes and retry the network once, even when cache cleanup fails
- make disk-cache eviction strictly LRU and surface file-removal failures

## Why

The audit found several reachable failure paths where the UI could freeze, pagination could be misordered or permanently blocked, and cache failures could prevent images from loading or saving. These changes keep background work terminal on both success and failure, make stale-cache replacement deterministic, and keep the cache an optional optimization.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo test --locked` (160 passed)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`

author: mutugiii
body:
Fixes #16664

Survey responses uploaded from myPlanet carried no top-level `team`, so Planet's `submissionsByParent` view could not attribute them to the team they were recorded for and they never counted towards that team's survey submission count.

Two gaps caused it:

- `createExamSubmission` set `teamObject` and `membershipDoc`, but both are `@Ignore` on the `Submission` entity, so Room dropped them. The persisted `teamId` column was only ever written by the sync path on the way down, so the team linkage did not survive the local write.
- `serializeSubmission` — the serializer behind every completed survey upload — emitted no `team` key at all. The sibling `getExamUploadPayload` does, but it is wired to a `type = 'exam'` query that surveys never reach.

Persist `teamId` at creation time and resolve it back into a top-level `team` object at serialization time, preferring the in-memory `teamObject` when present. Submissions with no team serialize exactly as before.

Refs open-learning-exchange/planet#10232

author: bigcatmellow
body:
Implements `work/notes/2026-09-01-6.9-slice2-execution-level-design.md` §3 (design PR #230, reviewed).

## What

Takes a matched `LOAD`-classified Skill from the **"activation"** level (SKILL.md body, #221) to the **"execution"** level per roadmap §6.9 ("scripts/references/examples only if needed").

- `runtime/skills/format.py`:
  - `SkillDescriptor.resource_sizes: tuple[(relpath, byte_size), ...]` — recorded at discovery (one `stat` per resource, no read) and reconstructed in `load_skill` from already-verified bytes; added to the identity checks.
  - `load_skill_resource(descriptor, relative_path) -> bytes` — exact bytes of one declared `scripts`/`references`/`examples`/`assets` file. `relative_path` must be in `descriptor.resource_paths` (that allowlist rejects `SKILL.md`, undeclared paths, absolute paths, `..` traversal); `_verified_snapshot` hash-checks the whole directory first. Deterministic single named file — not search/retrieval. Exported from `runtime.skills`.
- `runtime/context_builder.py::_select_skills` — inside the existing `LOAD`-only branch, after the SEC4 capability DENY and after the body attach: `item["execution_resources"]` — an ordered `{path, kind, size_bytes}` listing, **no content**, no filesystem read here. Any build error → fail-closed `item["execution_resources_withheld_reason"]` (mirrors #221's `body_withheld_reason`). `coverage["skill_execution_resources_listed"]` counts them.
- `runtime/flow_start.py` — step-2 docstring updated.
- `CAPABILITY_CHECKLIST.md` — 6.9 / S6 / 6.11 evidence text. **No status flip** (all stay IN PROGRESS).

**Not included:** §4's optional body byte-budget ceiling — the design leaves it as an implementer/coordinator call and says ship §3 independently.

## Manifest key naming

Per luve's #230 review note: the size key is `size_bytes`, not `bytes`, so a reader cannot mistake it for content.

## Robustness note (Part-A-style ceiling)

`load_skill_resource`'s allowlist (`relative_path in descriptor.resource_paths`) is the actual gate; the whole-directory hash check is defense-in-depth against post-discovery drift. The new `resource_sizes` identity-check in `load_skill` is **redundant** with that hash check (any resource-size change already changes `content_sha256`, since size is folded into the hash) — confirmed by mutation testing (see below), kept anyway for consistency with the existing `resource_paths` identity check.

## Tests

`tests/test_skills_format.py`: `resource_sizes` at discovery + activation, identity-change on size drift, `load_skill_resource` exact bytes / rejects undeclared+traversal+`SKILL.md` / post-discovery drift / empty when no resources.
`tests/test_context_builder.py`: `LOAD` Skill carries the manifest with no content + counter; no-resource Skill → no key; `WITHHOLD`/`DENY` → no manifest; manifest-build failure is fail-closed.

## Verification

Per the coordinator's updated protocol (machine-wide pytest contention) — **targeted modules only, run twice, both green; full suite delegated to CI**:
```
python3 -m unittest tests.test_context_builder tests.test_skills_format tests.test_skills_catalog tests.test_skill_capability_manifest
```
→ 105 tests, OK, twice. `python3 -m runtime.smoke` → exit 0, twice.

Own mutation testing on the new logic (targeted modules, ≤4 muts/call, `git diff HEAD` clean between calls): **7 killed / 8**. `format.py`: st_size→0, allowlist-inverted, hash-verify-skipped all killed; the `resource_sizes` identity-check drop is a confirmed **equivalent mutant** (see robustness note above). `context_builder.py`: size-lookup-broken, always-attach, drop-one-kind, fail-closed-marker-dropped all killed.

Did NOT self-review. @mepo to dispatch independent reviewer.

author: neksa
body:
The hooks pinned ruff 0.9.0 and black 25.1.0 while the project runs ruff 0.15 and black 26.5, so `pre-commit run --all-files` failed on six UP038 violations for a rule current ruff no longer has. Hooks that disagree with CI are worse than no hooks.

Pins now track pyproject, and those `isinstance` calls take single arguments rather than one-element tuples. Adds whitespace, end-of-file, YAML, TOML, merge-conflict and large-file checks.

The exclusion list is load-bearing: the first run stripped trailing tabs from the MAF fixtures and broke `test_real_maf_with_short_row_completes`, because those trailing empty columns *are* the padded-header case from #91. Data, fixtures and vendored assets are excluded.

Incidental whitespace fixes to LICENSE, docs/Makefile and four .rst files — all verified content-identical, the Makefile's leading tabs intact and the docs still building with 0 warnings.

Deliberately unlabelled: tooling hygiene is not worth a release on its own.

Also done outside this PR, on the repo settings:
- `protect-main` gained `required_linear_history` — we always rebase-merge, so it costs nothing and blocks an accidental merge commit.
- New `protect-release-tags` ruleset on `refs/tags/v*` against deletion and non-fast-forward. `v1.1.0` was unprotected; anyone could have moved or deleted it.

author: weisiang329-eng
body:
## 白话文

老板问：**「为什么有些单明明送完了，还留在 In Production？」**

先更正我自己 —— **我上一句话讲错了。** 我说「送货完成，销售单状态不会自己动」，那是错的。

**规矩早就有**（`so-delivery-sync.ts`），而且跑了好几个月。我错在：我只 grep 了交货单那个档案，看到里面没有「写销售单」，就下结论 —— 但那个「写」在它呼叫的另一个共用档案里。**我回答了另一个问题。**

## 真正的原因

那条规矩是在**交货单换状态的时候**才会跑。所以一张单如果货都出了、但**交货单一直停在 DISPATCHED、没走到 DELIVERED**，那条规矩根本没被叫到过。

**这是「补资料」的问题，不是「没有规矩」的问题** —— 两者的修法完全不同。

## 量出来的

```
公司 2 —— 每一行都送完、却还没进 Delivered：14 张
  全部卡在 IN_PRODUCTION
  它们的交货单状态：DISPATCHED 10、DELIVERED 4
```

那 4 张交货单**已经是 DELIVERED**，销售单就是没跟上 —— 那是真的漏掉了。

## 已经修掉 7 张

用的是**早就存在**的 `backfill-2990-delivered-dos`（它记着老板自己的裁示：「我们开了 DO 就是 consider 出货 delivered 了」）：

```
APPLIED: 3 DO(s) -> DELIVERED, 7 SO(s) advanced.
```

用**另一支独立的程式**重新量（不是拿写入的那支自己报）：

```
之前：14 张，交货单 DISPATCHED 10 / DELIVERED 4
之后： 7 张，交货单 DISPATCHED 7
```

## 剩下 7 张要老板决定

`2990-SO-2606-015`、`-016`、`-028`、`-035`、`-049`、`2990-SO-2607-005`、`-011`

它们的**交货单全部停在 DISPATCHED**。老板那句裁示是为「从 2990 搬进来」那批讲的；这 7 张不在那批里。

**问题很单纯：DISPATCHED 算不算已经送到？**

- 算 → 我把交货单推到 DELIVERED，销售单自己会跟（一分钟）
- 不算 → 那它们留在 In Production 是对的，等司机回报才动

我不敢自己决定，因为如果货其实还在车上，推过去就是假的送达。

## 这个 PR 本身

只有**唯读**的量测程式 + 它的工作流。SELECT，不写任何东西。它把「没有规矩」和「规矩没被叫到」分开报 —— 这两个我今天亲自搞混过一次。

公司 1 报 0，但那是**下限**：它只看得到有绑到销售行的交货行，旧单的交货行可能没绑。

body:
## What this PR does

Merges the full rebuild of HireSmart AI (phases 0–5) plus the final bug-fixing pass that took the CI suite to **11/11 test files green** (backend + frontend-contract).

### Production bugs fixed in the final pass

| # | Bug | Impact before fix |
|---|-----|-------------------|
| 1 | `buildPublicJobFilter` is async but was never awaited in `publicJobs` and the alert scan | **Public job search ran with no filter at all** — drafts, rejected and closed jobs were visible to everyone; alerts matched against every job |
| 2 | `alertScanService` imported `Job` as a named export (it's a default export) | Alert scans crashed silently — **job alerts were never delivered in production** |
| 3 | `v1AdminController` imported `Membership` without destructuring | **All admin moderation endpoints returned 500** — approve/reject was completely broken |
| 4 | `validate` middleware rejected bodyless JSON requests (`req.body === undefined`) | `POST /admin/moderation/jobs/:id/approve` with no payload failed 422 |
| 5 | `SearchHistory` TTL index was created with milliseconds instead of seconds | `create-indexes.js` crashed on boot — server could not start on a fresh database |
| 6 | Job alerts were created for the literal user `"any"` instead of the candidate | Alerts/notifications never reached the candidate |
| 7 | Recommendation snapshots excluded only *applied* jobs, not *saved* ones | Saved jobs kept appearing in "recommended for you" |
| 8 | `relatedJobs` matched only the source job's `requiredSkills` | Jobs sharing only preferred skills were never surfaced as related |
| 9 | `jobDto` omitted moderation status | Job owners had no way to see pending/rejected status + reason for their own listings |

Also: SRV-lookup DNS fallback for Atlas (`db.js` — public-resolver retry, then DNS-over-HTTPS with full TLS verification) for networks that block port-53 SRV queries, documented in the README.

### Test suite

- 11 test files in `server/test/` run per-file (isolated processes, shared CI Mongo service): `aiProvider`, `alerts`, `app`, `marketplace`, `matching`, `moderation`, `productionCore`, `resumeAnalyzer`, `snapshots`, `srvFallback`, `v1Workflow`
- `run-tests.js` relays a per-file failure tail + summary annotation to GitHub Actions
- Test-only `serverError` block in 500 bodies (`NODE_ENV=test` only) so CI can see the real stack
- Last run: **all 11 files passed** — [run 33308724416](https://github.com/anastai8704/HireSmart-AI/actions/runs/33308724416)

### Client-facing notes

- `jobDto` gained an additive `moderation` field (status/reason/reviewedAt — `reviewedBy` deliberately omitted); no client changes required
- All fixes are server-side; existing clients are unaffected by the API changes

author: jonah-stephans
body:
Closes #30.

## The probe gate, cleared before anything was written

The brief made this issue conditional on re-running probe E against the current build. Two probes, Claude Code 2.1.221, headless `claude -p`, a scratch project with one hook block:

- **`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` at exit 0 on `PostToolUse`/`Task|Agent` still reaches the orchestrator.** The hook appended to a marker file first, so *the hook did not run* is excluded. The orchestrator quoted the message back verbatim, rendered as `PostToolUse:Agent hook additional context: <message>`.
- **The `PostToolUse` payload carries `.tool_input.prompt` with the dispatch first line intact.** The event arrives with `tool_name: Agent` and `tool_input` keys `description, prompt, run_in_background, subagent_type`, and `prompt` split on the first newline gave back `devpath slice: devpath/demo/slices/01-thing.md`. That second probe is not in the brief and it is the one that decides whether the block can read anything at all.

Both were run in this session rather than inherited from the issue.

## What changed

**The menu tables the rule.** *A built slice is critiqued before the walk moves on*, verdict `not hard; a block still ships`, mechanism naming block 8 and both its limits. No fifth verdict category, and no existing row's verdict is touched — the diff shows no removed table row.

**Block 8.** `PostToolUse` on `Task|Agent`, exit 0, `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`. It reads the slice path off the fixed first line as blocks 2 and 3 do, and everything after that off disk: `done: true` with no `fix_cycles:` line, which is Integrate's step 3 test 2 asked at the moment the dispatch is due instead of at the merge gate. Its prose carries the two limits in the open — it fires on every ordinary builder return by design, and it cannot tell a deliberate hand-back from a forgotten dispatch — plus why neither `SubagentStop` nor `Stop` is the event.

**The demonstrated-failure paragraph records both failures**, and says the second is the one that argues for the block. The generalisation it closed on, *that pairing is the answer everywhere in this design*, becomes *almost everywhere*: the artifact backstop answers at the merge gate, and block 8 is a third answer rather than a guarantee.

**All five count sites move by one.** The `summary`, the *Ten properties* line, the *Four of those ten rows* paragraph, *Three of the eight parse the dispatch first line*, and `tests/schema.sh` check 2's header.

## Two judgment calls worth your eye

**`tests/hooks.sh` gains check 6, which the acceptance criteria did not ask for.** Check 5 exists because block 4's `jq -n` message is a program nothing else on the build runs, and *before this check, a jq program error in block 4 shipped green*. Block 8 is the second such program, and it fires far more often than block 4 does. Shipping it untested would reproduce exactly the defect check 5 was written to prevent, one block over. It selects block 8 by content (`fix_cycles` is in no other command), runs it against five fixtures, and asserts the wrapper. Four mutations confirm it bites: wrong wrapper key, the `fix_cycles` test deleted, the `[ -f ]` guard deleted, and — the one that does **not** go red — deleting `[ -n "$SLICE" ]`, which is redundant with `[ -f ]` for every state a session produces. I kept both clauses anyway, because the `[ -n ]` form is what blocks 2 and 3 carry and the block claims to parse the first line the way they do. **It shipped without check 5's other half**, which is the first item below.

**The block carries a `[ -f "$SLICE" ]` clause the brief did not specify.** Without it a first line naming a path that is not there still exits 0 silently, but the `done` grep writes *No such file or directory* to stderr on the way. One sentence after the fence says so.

Out of scope and untouched: the re-review gap, blocks 4 and 7's exit paths, any new front-matter field, the `depends_on` walk, the commit rule, the contamination rule, and Build's *a repo that wants certainty adds a hook of its own* callout, which still reads right — this is still a paste menu and `devpath` still ships none.

## What review added

Two findings, both applied on `f6aff95`, both test-side — README is byte-unchanged by them.

**Check 6 asserted the wrapper and not the `exit 0` under it.** It was built as check 5 one block over
and copied the fixtures without the test that made check 5 worth writing: break `jq` underneath the block
and see whether it still exits 0. Deleting block 8's trailing `exit 0` shipped the whole suite green,
against a README that claims the property outright — *It ends `exit 0` whatever `jq` did, for block 4's
reason*. **The asymmetry is the argument**: block 4's typo costs one write, and block 8's is exit 2 at
`PostToolUse` — a blocking error — on every ordinary builder return, which is every slice of the walk.
The check reuses check 5's `badjq` stub rather than standing up a second one.

**Nothing tied a block's registration key to the `hookEventName` its wrapper emits.** Moving block 8 to
`PreToolUse` shipped green: the harness would route its message nowhere, and *it cannot deny* — which the
new menu row's verdict rests on — would stop being true with no test noticing. **Block 8 is the first
block here whose sold property is a negative**, which is what makes this worth closing now rather than
never. It went into `tests/schema.sh` check 2 as an assertion rather than a tenth check, so no count
moves. Blocks 4 and 8 are the two carrying a wrapper; the rest emit none and are skipped rather than
exempted — said in the comment, so a block that starts emitting one is not silently outside it.

## Tests

`for t in tests/*.sh; do sh "$t"; done` clean. `schema.sh` now reports 8 hook blocks parsing (the number is derived, not pinned), and `hooks.sh` still finds exactly two commands enumerating `devpath/lessons/`.

**Updated off `main` on `7b07c58`**, so this ran against #24, #25 and #119 rather than the base it was cut from. Nothing in those three moved what block 8 reads: a `blocked` pause carries no `done: true` so the block is silent on it, #25's retry worker on a refused commit leaves `done: true` with no `fix_cycles` so it fires, and #119's third dispatch return already carries `fix_cycles` so it does not.

**Both new checks were run red before they were run green**, which is #119's rule:

| mutation | check that catches it |
| --- | --- |
| block 8's trailing `exit 0` deleted | `hooks.sh` — *exited 3 rather than 0, so a typo in its message denies every builder return* |
| block 8 re-registered as `PreToolUse` | `schema.sh` — *is registered under PreToolUse and its wrapper names PostToolUse* |
| block 4's registration renamed to `Stop` | `schema.sh` — *is registered under Stop and its wrapper names PostToolUse* |

author: cayerbe
body:
Resolves decision **0006** — record only, no spec or verifier changes (step 1 of 4 from the design thread). **`status: proposed → accepted`, `decision_date: 2026-09-02`.** **Do not merge** until reviewed.

## Resolutions
- **Q1 — Question B posture: B2 rejected.** "Enforced only at chain-write" is rejected as the standard's posture: under B2 revocation becomes a property of each integrator's diligence and a relying party can infer nothing from a revocation — incompatible with the reconstruction claim. B2 stays an accurate description of geiant *today* (an *is*, not an *ought*).
- **Q2 — conformance: enforce-or-label.** A conformant consumer either enforces liveness or declares itself non-enforcing and **labels its output** — with the label **normative**, **must-propagate**, and **stripping/failing-to-propagate non-conformant**. Without propagation, a non-enforcing output is re-served one hop down unlabeled and B2 returns silently.
- **Q3 — record structure: cross-reference, not subsume.** 0005 (speaks-for) · 0006 (honours) · v4 edge (expresses) — separate decisions, separate timelines.

## Left open, deliberately
- **New sub-question (open):** how is the non-enforcing label made **structurally hard to drop**? It describes the verifier's *mode*, not the attestation, so it can't sit in the attestation's signature. Candidate: a **signed verification result** (new signed artifact type + key management). A must-not-strip rule alone is honour-based — the very integrator diligence Q1 rejects. **Must be designed before the label field lands in the spec.**
- **Question A (open, implementation):** permit vs deny principals absent from `agent_registry` is **not** decided by this acceptance — it's a geiant implementation choice tracked in `geiant#11`. The acceptance is scoped to the standard's revocation posture.

## Recorded
`cgr-verify` as built in #89 is a **non-enforcing** verifier (honours held edges, does not seek). Under this resolution the reference should become **enforcing** — it becomes the de facto reading for `@geiant/core` and the read surface. (That's a later step; not in this PR.)

Scope: only `0006` + the decisions README index row. No spec/corpus/verifier changes.
