author: talchain
body:
## What this closes

CEE **PR #1309** ships a second AI pass that judges a freshly drafted model and may **redraw** it, attaching the rejected original to `_diagnostic_trace.draft_quality.discarded_graph`.

The owner's requirement:

> *"A repair pass that silently hides bad drafts destroys the only signal we have about draft quality. We need visibility of the original graph produced and what the system does to fix it. Otherwise we're flying blind."*

The data reached the wire and then **died in the UI's debug export**.

## The gap, confirmed at the bytes

`buildDebugBundle` does not spread `_diagnostic_trace` — it **ENUMERATES named keys** (`exportBundle.ts:3410-3417`):

```
llm_calls · prompt_identity · zone2_assembly · tool_policy
provider_resolution · structured_output_config · streaming_metrics · fallback_trace
```

`draft_quality` was **not among them**, so the export dropped it.

**Contrast control:** the same `rg` probe found all eight enumerated keys present, so the absence is a real read, not a blind instrument. Upstream is clean — `useDebugData` passes the whole trace through as `Record<string, unknown>` verbatim, so the enumeration was the **only** drop.

**This is the same key-naming silent drop CEE had just closed one hop further in, reappearing one hop further out.** CEE's own PR description predicted it: *"the UI's `exportBundle.ts` spreads eight named `_diagnostic_trace` keys … surfacing it in the export needs a one-line UI change."*

## Full graph vs summary — decided, not silently truncated

**Carried VERBATIM and WHOLE.** Reasons, in order of weight:

1. **A summary cannot answer the question.** The requirement is to see *the original graph produced*. A verdict plus coverage counts tells you a redraw happened, not what was wrong with the model. CEE already ships the summary alongside (`first_coverage`, `second_coverage`, `second_verdict`, `second_outcome`) — the graph is the part that is not otherwise recoverable.
2. **The size is affordable.** Measured across real fixtures in this repo, a drafted graph is **~26–43 KB of JSON** (14–20 nodes, 23–39 edges). The record rides **only** the rare turns that actually spent a redraw, and the bundle is a diagnostic artefact downloaded on demand.
3. **`_diagnostic_trace` is a declared passthrough** — *"UI must not transform"*. A UI-side summary would have to encode CEE's shape, which is exactly the producer/consumer drift this estate keeps paying for.

If the size ever does become a problem, that is a CEE-side decision about what to put on the wire — not a truncation to make silently here.

## The two twins — failing on DIFFERENT assertions

One alone proves nothing.

| Twin | REDs on | Proves |
|---|---|---|
| **CARRIES the rejected draw, whole and verbatim** | deep equality + sentinel node labels present in the serialised bundle | it arrives, and arrives **whole** |
| **does NOT fabricate a record when the pass did not redraw** | `expected undefined to be null` | a no-redraw turn does not grow an **invented** record |

RED-first, source reverted HEAD-relative (never index-relative), spec left in place:

```
RED   4 failed | 34 passed (38)
        × defaults all v2.0 sections to null
        × bundle shape matches v2.0 schema
        × CARRIES the rejected draw, whole and verbatim   ← line 528, toEqual
        × does NOT fabricate a record ...                  ← line 556, toBeNull
GREEN 38 passed (38)   — same collected count, nothing vanished
```

Without the second twin, an implementation shipping `?? {}` — or one reporting a discarded draft on *every* turn — passes the first twin perfectly.

**The `null` rung is load-bearing and deliberate.** Three states that are not interchangeable: a populated record = the pass redrew; `null` = the trace was read and held no record; key absent = v2 sections off. `null` is what distinguishes *"no redraw happened"* from *"the UI dropped it"* — and dropping it is the defect being closed.

The anti-fabrication twin also carries its own **contrast control** (the sibling keys DID populate from the same trace) and **pins its precondition in-test** (`expect(trace.draft_quality).toBeUndefined()`).

## ⚠ Deployed flag posture — what I could NOT establish

**This is the part that decides whether the requirement is actually met, and I could not settle it.**

- `_diagnostic_trace` is gated on `config.features.diagnosticTraceEnabled` — `booleanString.default(false)`. **It defaults FALSE** (`config/index.ts:625`). The whole trace builder short-circuits (`v5-diagnostic-trace.ts:542`).
- **`render.yaml` / `render-staging.yaml` do not mention `CEE_DIAGNOSTIC_TRACE_ENABLED` at all.** Contrast control: the same probe finds `LLM_PROVIDER` in both files, so this is a real absence. Per standing doctrine the YAML is a partial, drifting subset and **proves nothing either way** — the Render dashboard is authoritative.
- **CEE reports the real posture only as a startup LOG line** (`server.ts:448-453`, `event: config.startup_health`, field `diagnostic_trace`). There is **no HTTP route** that exposes it. Reading it needs Render log access.
- **I have no Render credentials** (none in env, no CLI, no config files). **So I could not establish the current deployed posture, and I am not going to infer it.**

**What I *can* offer is a dated behavioural witness, and it is only that.** Five live staging captures in this repo (4–8 Aug 2026) carry a **real, populated** `_diagnostic_trace` — 14 keys, `llm_calls` non-empty. So the flag **was ON in deployed staging as of 8 Aug 2026**. That is a witness about a build ~3.5 weeks old, not about today's, and the flag may have moved since.

> **Plainly: if `CEE_DIAGNOSTIC_TRACE_ENABLED` is OFF in deployed staging, this PR changes nothing the owner can see.** The requirement is not met by merging this alone.

**What must still happen before the owner can see a discarded draft on the deployed build:**
1. Confirm `CEE_DIAGNOSTIC_TRACE_ENABLED=true` on the CEE staging service (Render dashboard, or the `config.startup_health` log line) — **someone with Render access must do this**;
2. `VITE_DEBUG_BUNDLE_V2` on for the UI (defaults ON in staging, OFF in production);
3. Merge + deploy this;
4. Drive a draft that actually **triggers a redraw** and export the bundle. Nobody has witnessed the redraw path end-to-end yet — CEE #1309 shipped at rung **TESTED**, with *"no real LLM call has been made"* stated in its own description.

**Rung for this PR: TESTED.** Not deployed, not journey-witnessed.

## Adjacent finding — NOT fixed here (reporting, not expanding)

The 8 Aug live captures show CEE already sends **six more** trace keys the export also drops by the same mechanism: `benchmarking`, `claim_safety`, `correlation_ids`, `environment`, `exit_path`, `trace_version`.

I have **not** touched them — that is a different requirement and belongs in its own change. The durable fix for the whole class is to stop enumerating and carry the trace verbatim, but that is a mechanism change with its own review (the block is deliberately explicit today), so it should be decided rather than smuggled in here.

## Gates — and a correction CI forced, recorded rather than tidied away

**First push went RED, and the reason is worth keeping.**

`Typecheck Gate Self-Test` failed on its **green control**:

> `FAIL  no added-diagnostics notice on a clean tree — did NOT expect text "NOT in the identity baseline appeared", but the gate printed it`

and `Staging Gate` failed **solely** because of it (`tsc`, `vitest`, `vitest-summary`, `build` were all green).

**Cause, measured rather than assumed.** `diagnosticTrace` is `Record<string, unknown>`, so each read is `unknown`, which TS widens to `{}` under `??` and will not assign to the declared `unknown[] | null`. That mismatch is **pre-existing** — verified at pristine `staging`, where the same TS2322 sits at line 3180. Adding `draft_quality` changed the property count in the whole-object diagnostic's message (`49 more` → `50 more`),

author: alexu-a
body:
## What this does

Three connected fixes that came out of a transcript analysis of ~1,200 local sessions (Jul-Sep 2026):

### 1. The hooks' warnings never reached the model - fixed
Every v1 helper emitted `{"continue": true, "additionalContext": "..."}` at top level, which Claude Code does not honor (only `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` is injected). Across all analyzed transcripts, not one warning ever reached the model. All hooks now emit through the documented channels: `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` for Claude plus `systemMessage` for the user - visible in the terminal **and** the desktop app. PreCompact cannot inject context at all, so compact-gamble's Claude-facing instruction moved to the post-compact UserPromptSubmit hook, honestly documented.

### 2. TTL-aware idle-tax and idle-autosave (v2)
Claude Code subscription sessions now normally run on the **1-hour** prompt-cache TTL (2x writes -> a ~20x cold-vs-warm penalty at a 60-minute cliff), dropping to 5 minutes only in usage overage; measured: 99.7% of main-thread cache writes on 1h. Both helpers now read the TTL actually in effect from the last assistant message's `usage.cache_creation` breakdown instead of hardcoding 5 minutes:

- **idle-tax** measures idle from the last API call (not the last prompt), prices the re-write from the real cached context size and model, and warns from 15 minutes before expiry.
- **idle-autosave** arms a 45-minute window on the 1h TTL (4 min on 5m), and its handoff call is stripped to ~250 input tokens / **~$0.002** (haiku, `--effort low` pinned in env, no tools/MCP/skills/user settings, one-line system prompt) vs $0.18 with the default system prompt loaded. Auth-shaped answers are detected and retried without a stale `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before falling back.

### 3. New helper: usage-report
Zero-token, stdlib-only scan of `~/.claude/projects` transcripts into a markdown report: desktop vs terminal $/turn, cache read/write/output split, cold resumes priced, delegation audit (explicit-model rate, opus/fable share, teammate attribution), headless-job tally by spawner, week-over-week, and a calibration line against Claude Code's own `totalCostUSD` (1.00 median on the author's machine). `/usage-report` on demand plus a weekly SessionStart background refresh.

Docs updated throughout (READMEs, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md hook contract + testing sections, install-all.sh, dated notes on the historical measurement docs).

## Test plan
- `idle-tax/test.sh` - 22 fixture cases (both TTLs, expiring/expired, fallback, sidechain noise, overrides, corrupt transcript): pass
- `usage-report/test.sh` - 16 fixture cases over a synthetic transcript tree: pass
- idle-autosave worker run end-to-end against a synthetic transcript with a live minimal haiku call (rich handoff produced; auth-retry path exercised)
- All hooks re-validated as JSON emitters; live-installed and observed delivering via the new channels in a real session

## Update: Claude Fable 5.1 (pushed after opening)

Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`, the default Fable model since Claude Code 2.1.257) prices cache **reads** at 0.025x base input instead of the standard 0.1x; writes and TTLs are unchanged, so the TTL detection in this PR is unaffected. idle-tax and usage-report now look the read multiplier up per model: warm-hit figures on 5.1 drop 4x and the cold-vs-warm ratio becomes 80x (1h) / 50x (5m), with the same absolute cold cost. Fixture coverage added for both (23 + 17 passing). Source: platform.claude.com pricing page footnote, verified 2026-09-01.

body:
## Summary
- **Postflop ganha categoria e marcador de faixa** (Preflop já tinha, Postflop não): Turn/River C-Bet %, Fold to Turn/River C-Bet %, Donk Bet % e WSD %/W$SD % ganham marcador; Check-Raise Flop/Turn/River % ficam só com o ponto de categoria (sem marcador — sem referência confiável pra uma faixa "ideal"). Nova categoria **"resultado"** pras métricas de showdown.
- **Régua bem mais visível**: trilha de 4px→8px, zona saudável em verde bem mais opaco, marcador vira bolinha de 14px com halo colorido (verde/amarelo/vermelho) e borda no tom do card, em vez de um traço de 3px quase invisível.
- **Números revisados** com base em consenso comum de material de treino/HUD — cada faixa em `PREFLOP_REFERENCE`/`POSTFLOP_REFERENCE` tem comentário dizendo se é um valor com consenso, uma faixa construída em torno de uma média de população, ou heurística antiga sem revisão (nada de fonte inventada). Isso permitiu marcador novo em WSD%/W$SD% e nos 3 recortes de Fold to Steal, e apertar Steal%/ATS (35-55%→30-40% 6-max). Nenhum desses números é o motor GTO do produto — são referência de contexto, documentado no código sem nomear sites externos.
- **Torneios redesenhado**:
  - Filtro de buy-in (Até R$10/R$10-50/R$50-200/R$200+) com o mesmo `FilterChip` do resto do produto — filtra Total Games/ROI/ITM/Lucro total e a lista de premiação.
  - "Resultado em torneios" troca a grade antiga por `StatCardGrid` (ícones, hover, verde/vermelho por sinal em ROI%/Lucro).
  - Lista de premiação (`TournamentPayoutsPanel`) era uma coluna de linhas full-width com vão vazio enorme em telas largas — vira grid de 2-3 colunas, o card aberto ocupa a largura toda pro formulário.

author: oitalorabelo
body:
## O que muda

Adiciona o conjunto de 279 sitios candidatos a vertiporto no municipio de Sao
Paulo, em duas camadas, e o pipeline em R que o reproduz do zero a partir das
duas fontes publicas. Saida em `dados/tratado/locais_candidatos.csv`, criterio
e limitacoes em `docs/CANDIDATOS.md`.

## Por que

O enunciado 2.3 poe a montagem do conjunto como a primeira decisao do projeto e
o 2.5 a lista entre os diferenciais de um grupo para outro. A camada de
helipontos da o custo de implantacao baixo; a de estacoes de metro entra porque
o 2.2 diz que o acesso terrestre domina a cadeia porta a porta, e um sitio sobre
estacao nasce com esse trecho resolvido. As duas entram no mesmo conjunto de
decisao com custo distinto, o que deixa o trade-off para o modelo em vez de
resolvido na montagem.

Nenhum candidato e um vertiporto: `apto_triagem` registra apenas a triagem
possivel com o cadastro de helicoptero da ANAC, e a confrontacao com as normas
de projeto de vertiporto fica como pendencia aberta.

## Registros

- `tar-j6qe32` Montar conjunto de locais candidatos
- `fon-n0fj83` Cadastro de helipontos privados da ANAC
- `fon-8xmejy` Estacoes de metro do GeoSampa
- `dec-5hbw2z` Conjunto de candidatos em duas camadas
- `dec-0cmfmg` MTOW de referencia de 3,2 t como limiar de elegibilidade
- `dec-hs0npv` Agrupamento espacial a 150 m entra como coluna, nao como filtro
- `dec-v5jmkk` Candidato e sitio de implantacao, nao vertiporto
- `pen-n7woa1` Confrontar o conjunto com as normas de projeto de vertiporto
- `ia-808yms` IA na montagem do conjunto, aceito parcial

## Como verificar

- `Rscript app/01-baixa-candidatos.R && Rscript app/02-locais-candidatos.R`
  reproduz os 279 sitios (244 aptos na triagem, 233 agrupamentos a 150 m)
- `Rscript -e 'print(lintr::lint_dir("app"))'` sem lints
- `./gov rebuild && ./gov auditoria` selo VERDE, rastreabilidade 100%, 0 orfaos
- `python governanca/scripts/valida_estrutura.py --base origin/main` exit 0
- `./gov contexto tar-j6qe32 --raio 2` mostra a cadeia completa da tarefa

## Ponto que pede atencao do grupo

O limiar de MTOW nao e continuo: a 3,0 t sobram 183 dos 185 helipontos e a 3,2 t
sobram 150, porque 3,0 t e o valor de projeto mais comum das coberturas da
cidade. Sao 35 dos 185 helipontos, cerca de um quinto da camada e 13% dos 279
sitios, que entram ou saem pela aeronave de referencia escolhida. O parametro
esta no topo de `app/02-locais-candidatos.R` para a analise de sensibilidade do
4.4.

author: ahrav
body:
## Summary

- Add Topic 53 models for NVMe submission and completion queues, Linux `blk-mq`, effective queue depth, throughput, bandwidth, residence time, and batched CPU cost.
- Add a fail-closed exact-source Linux experiment that compares one-thread 4 KiB `O_DIRECT` reads at queue depth one and eight, with eight balanced whole-process blocks and a separate depth-one A/A control.
- Publish compact records from the required Arm host and runtime-resolved `xxl` host while retaining full read-only sealed receipts outside Git.

## Measured evidence

Both accepted campaigns built source commit `82c98a25eb4ad31fd9e18fc8d8f9463dab6854d7` from path-limited archive SHA-256 `44085d1001f8566bdf0f7a58af509b8b7acb1f633c09f1f7c218a88ab85e4c45`. Each host ran 64 fresh processes: 32 for depth one versus depth eight and 32 for the depth-one A/A control. Each process completed 8,192 verified 4 KiB direct reads and accounted for exactly 33,554,432 process read bytes.

- Arm, `dev-dsk-ahrav-2b-7dc7bd93.us-west-2.amazon.com`: q8/q1 `7.9964512444`, 95% whole-block interval `[7.9884234853, 8.0044870708]`; A/A `0.9993467115`, interval `[0.9985551620, 1.0001388885]`.
- x86-64, alias `xxl` resolving at run time to `dev-dsk-ahrav-2c-32182091.us-west-2.amazon.com`: q8/q1 `6.9555130563`, interval `[6.3123869095, 7.6641629498]`; A/A `0.9989588512`, interval `[0.9969766750, 1.0009449683]`.
- Both A/A controls passed the fixed point and interval acceptance rules. Independent validation reported `pass: true`, `sealed: true`, and `measurement_usable: true`.

Both paths used XFS over guest-visible Amazon Elastic Block Store NVMe devices. These results apply to the exact hosts, source, binaries, workload, device paths, and run windows. They do not prove queue occupancy, a one-to-one Linux AIO to NVMe completion mapping, local flash, or an Arm-versus-x86 or CPU-vendor effect.

## Primary sources

- https://nvmexpress.org/wp-content/uploads/NVM-Express-Base-Specification-Revision-2.4-Ratified-2026.07.31.pdf
- https://nvmexpress.org/wp-content/uploads/NVM-Express-NVMe-over-PCIe-Transport-Specification-Revision-1.4-Ratified-2026.07.31.pdf
- https://docs.kernel.org/block/blk-mq.html
- https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/iostats.html
- https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/io_submit.2.html
- https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/io_getevents.2.html
- https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html
- https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/statx.2.html

## Validation

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins --examples`
- `cargo test --workspace --doc`
- `cargo bench --workspace --no-run`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- 13 focused receipt tamper and synthetic-integration tests
- Bash syntax, ShellCheck, and warning-clean native C builds on both required hosts
- compact bundle `SHA256SUMS` verification
- independent revalidation of both read-only sealed receipts from the exact archived validator
- exact remote-head verification before publication


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

This adds Topic 53 curriculum, a bounded Rust cost model, and a reproducible Linux experiment for NVMe and `blk-mq` queue depth. Before this change, the repository lacked both a documented queueing model and controlled evidence for comparing depth-one and depth-eight direct reads.

## Why it was needed

The topic needed to explain how application concurrency, Linux `blk-mq`, device queue capacity, IOPS, bandwidth, residence time, and batched CPU cost relate. It also needed a controlled experiment with strong provenance and validation.

The measurements are scoped to the specified hosts, binaries, workload, devices, and run windows. They do not prove queue occupancy, one-to-one Linux AIO-to-NVMe completion mapping, local flash, or CPU-vendor effects.

## How it works

The Rust library validates inputs and computes:

- Effective queue depth.
- Concurrency-limited IOPS.
- Bandwidth from IOPS and bytes per I/O.
- CPU cost for batched submission and completion.

The native probe performs aligned 4 KiB cached and `O_DIRECT` reads with Linux native AIO. The process runner starts fresh processes for fixed scenarios, records benchmark results and system counters, checksums data, and writes `COMPLETE.json` only after all attempts succeed.

The host runner:

1. Validates the source archive, host, filesystem, page size, and block-device topology.
2. Builds and fingerprints the native probe.
3. Records host, kernel, storage, cgroup, binary, and assembly evidence.
4. Runs controls and depth campaigns.
5. Analyzes the campaign.
6. Verifies source immutability and cleanup.
7. Validates and seals the receipt.

The analyzer rejects malformed, duplicate, incomplete, inconsistent, or non-finite evidence. It groups results into fixed four-process blocks and computes geometric-mean q8/q1 ratios with a Student-t interval.

The independent receipt validator rechecks source hashes, archive safety, provenance, host and device metadata, build identity, controls, campaign accounting, snapshots, analysis, cleanup, and sealed manifests.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[New and changed: Rust cost model] -->|planning inputs and validated results| B[New: native AIO probe]
  B -->|per-process JSON results| C[New: process campaign runner]
  C -->|campaign artifacts and journals| D[New: strict analyzer]
  D -->|analysis and acceptance result| E[New: host runner]
  E -->|receipt and manifest| F[New: independent receipt validator]
  F -->|validation certificate| G[New: published measurement records]
```

The published campaigns used 64 fresh processes and verified 4 KiB direct reads. The q8/q1 ratios were 7.9964512444 on Arm and 6.9555130563 on x86-64. Both A/A controls passed, with `pass: true`, `sealed: true`, and `measurement_usable: true`.

## Key decisions

- The experiment uses exact archived source and native binaries to bind results to reproducible inputs.
- Fresh processes and balanced four-process blocks reduce process-history and ordering effects.
- A separate depth-one A/A control checks measurement stability without treating it as a depth comparison.
- Validation fails closed when evidence is missing, reused, unsafe, inconsistent, or incomplete.
- Large raw receipts remain outside Git. The repository stores compact manifests, hashes, validation outputs, and measurement records.
- The results use application-level behavior and recorded metadata as evidence. They avoid unsupported claims about lower-level NVMe behavior.

## Review focus

- Check queue-depth, block-grouping, and statistical acceptance invariants in `analyze.py`.
- Check alignment, completion accounting, checksum, residency, and process-counter checks in the native probe.
- Check cleanup, immutability, archive extraction, device-topology, and host-validation paths in `run_host.sh`.
- Check that `validate_receipt.py` independently derives and verifies campaign results instead of trusting analyzer output.
- Check that published measurements retain their stated scope and limitations.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `topics/053-nvme-blk-mq/Cargo.toml` | Defines the non-publishable Rust package and example target. |
| `topics/053-nvme-blk-mq/README.md` | Explains NVMe, `blk-mq`, queueing models, formulas, and experiment limits. |
| `topics/053-nvme-blk-mq/examples/nvme_costs.rs` | Demonstrates the planning cost model. |
| `topics/053-nvme-blk-mq/src/lib.rs` | Implements validated queue-depth, IOPS, bandwidth, and CPU-cost calculations. |
| `topics/053-nvme-blk-mq/experiment/README.md` | Defines the workload, controls, execution, evidence, and acceptance rules. |
| `topics/053-nvme-blk-mq/experiment/nvme_aio_depth_probe.c` | Runs aligned cached and direct native-AIO reads and emits structured results. |
| `topics/053-nvme-blk-mq/experiment/run_processes.py` | Executes fresh-pro

author: jeffmhopkins
body:
## What & why

Schedules **`docs/plans/SDR_RADIO_PLAN.md`** (a USB software-defined radio as a new sensor feeding pipelines that already exist) and ships its first wave, **S0a — the debug USB probe**: answer *"is the dongle there, what exactly is it called, and is anything holding it?"* from the debug console, with no terminal and before building anything the answer might invalidate.

The insight that makes S0a cheap: **naming a USB device is a sysfs read, not a device operation.** `/sys/bus/usb/devices/` is not namespaced and Docker already mounts the host's `/sys` read-only into every container, so this needs **no device passthrough, no privileges, and no `sdr` container**. Only *using* a dongle needs `/dev/bus/usb`. That lets the hardware be verified before the wave that depends on it is built.

**Code**

- `supervisor/usb_devices.py` — reads the bus, folds each device's interface drivers back onto it, flags the RTL2832U family by USB id. `scan()` carries `sysfs_readable` alongside the device list, because apart they lie: an empty list means "no devices" only if we could look.
- Supervisor `GET /usb`, mirroring `/metrics` — the supervisor is already the only container that reads `/sys`.
- Api `GET /api/debug/sdr` proxies it and returns a **verdict**, not a dump: `found`, `ready`, a one-line `summary`, a `next_step`. The distinction that matters is **found-but-not-ready** — a dongle claimed by the kernel's DVB-T driver (`dvb_usb_rtl28xxu`) is the expected first result on a stock Ubuntu box, and the verdict names the blacklist rather than leaving the reader to know it.
- An `sdr` command in the debug console, so it is one dropdown pick (CLAUDE.md rule 10 — the owner runs this box remotely, with no terminal).

**Plan + docs**

Promotes the plan out of `docs/proposed/` to `docs/plans/` with a ROADMAP slot, splits S0 into S0a (this) and S0b (host enablement + sidecar, still the blocking on-box gate), and records the closed GUI gate for the omnibox tuner (`docs/mocks/sdr-tuner/`, three interactive mocks; owner chose the bottom sheet, now carrying a BINDING SPEC header).

**Not yet verified against real hardware.** This container has no USB — the reader correctly returns an empty list rather than raising, which exercises the degradation path but is not proof. The probe is meant to be run on the box after this deploys.

## Checklist

- [x] **Tests land with the code** — `supervisor/tests/test_usb.py` (10: sysfs parsing, interface folding, driver dedup, absent sysfs, malformed attrs, the route + its auth) and `backend/tests/unit/test_debug_sdr.py` (7: every verdict branch — unclaimed/ready, DVB-claimed, other-driver, not-found, unreadable sysfs, missing product string, missing device node). No new tables, so no RLS isolation test; no LLM calls involved.
- [x] **Non-negotiables honoured** — no LLM calls, no file I/O, no DB access added. The probe is a read through the existing pinned supervisor client; the `stream.py` SSRF guard is untouched and un-widened.
- [x] **`scripts/dev-setup.sh` updated** — not applicable: no dependency, tool, or setup step added (stdlib only). S0b's host enablement will add one, and that is called out in the plan.
- [x] **Docs reconciled in this PR** — plan promoted `proposed/` → `plans/` with waves split and status flipped to In progress; ROADMAP slot added; `DEBUG_ACCESS.md` documents the new route; `SERVICES.md` records the supervisor's `/usb` read; both plan indexes updated; `Last verified` bumped on each touched doc. `scripts/docs-freshness.sh` green (0 errors, 0 warnings).
- [x] **CI green before merge** — locally: supervisor 155 passed, backend debug units 103 passed, frontend debug-console 5 passed, ruff + pyright + tsc + biome clean. Awaiting CI.

author: enerlens
body:
## Le symptôme

`Sites militaires` affichait **Error loading** sur chaque vue. La couche avait raison de le dire : `/api/military-installations` renvoyait `503`, et son `refresh()` lit `status >= 400` comme un échec. La panne était en dessous.

## Trois défauts empilés

**1. `overpass-api.de` rendait un `406 Not Acceptable`** — une page Apache nue, sortie de son filtre anti-abus, qui ne correspond ni au détecteur de rate-limit ni à celui d'erreur d'exécution. Mesuré le 2026-09-01 depuis cette machine, même requête, en alternance pour neutraliser la charge serveur :

| agent | 406 |
|---|---|
| `gods-eye-view-overpass-proxy/1.0` (ancien) | **8 / 11** |
| `gods-eye-view/1.0 (+…)` (conventionnel OSM) | **0 / 11** |

**2. `fetchOverpassPayload` traitait tout 4xx comme une réponse finale.** Il ne tournait vers le miroir suivant que sur 429/5xx, donc le 406 arrêtait la chaîne au premier miroir — trois miroirs sains non interrogés en dessous. C'est le vrai défaut : les sondes caméras et réseau électrique tournent déjà sur `status >= 400`, ce qui explique que ces couches aient tenu pendant la même panne.

**3. `/api/overpass` mettait en cache tout ce qui était sous `< 500`.** Le 406 était donc écrit en mémoire *et* sur disque sous un TTL de 7 à 30 jours, puis reservi en `HIT` sans jamais réinterroger l'amont. Une mauvaise minute en amont aurait coûté un mois à toutes les couches Overpass. Rien n'était encore empoisonné sur disque ici (0 entrée sur 53), mais le cache de la couche partait dans la même direction.

## Le correctif (`vite.config.js`)

- Nouveau `overpassAttemptDisposition()` — un 4xx est un verdict de **miroir**, pas de requête, donc il fait tourner la rotation. Une requête réellement malformée remonte toujours : tous les miroirs la rejettent, rien ne la surclasse, l'appelant récupère le 4xx.
- `OVERPASS_USER_AGENT` partagé, en forme conventionnelle OSM, utilisé par les trois appelants Overpass (proxy, caméras, réseau électrique).
- Cache **succès uniquement** (`< 400`), et un 4xx rejoint les 5xx pour servir le dernier bon état depuis le disque à tout âge.

## Vérification

A/B sur clés de cache neuves, même serveur, d'affilée :

| vue | avant | après |
|---|---|---|
| Paris | 200 *(disque chaud)* | 200 · 111 éléments |
| Lyon | **503** | 200 · 21 |
| Marseille | **503** | 200 · 23 |
| Nantes | **503** | 200 · 4 |

Dans le navigateur la couche rapporte `status: "ready"`, `error: null`, entités dessinées — Quartier de Croy, BA107 Villacoublay, le Mont-Valérien, le Fort de Rosny.

Six tests de régression dans `src/data/overpassProxy.test.mjs` épinglent la rotation de façon déterministe : un 406 passe au miroir suivant ; tous-4xx remonte quand même ; le rate-limit surclasse le refus ; un miroir qui lève n'arrête pas la chaîne. Suite complète verte (**4114 tests**), build de production propre.

## À savoir séparément

Les trois autres miroirs (kumi, lz4, private.coffee) répondaient tous 502/504 pendant cette session — `overpass-api.de` était le **seul** en bonne santé. C'est pourquoi ce filtre a frappé si fort, et c'est un argument pour revoir la liste des miroirs dans un autre PR.

## 概述
修复 2 个高危漏洞。

## 改动点

### #4 私密板块元数据与成员列表未授权泄露（IDOR）
- 文件：`backend/src/boards/service.ts`、`backend/src/boards/routes.ts`
- 问题：`GET /api/boards`、`GET /api/boards/:slug` 泄露私密板块；`GET /api/boards/:slug/members` 无鉴权返回任意板块成员列表。
- 修复：新增 `visibleBoardRows` 可见性过滤（全局 mod/admin 全见，其余仅 public 或已加入），三个接口均接入，私密板块对无权限者返回 404。

### #5 trustProxy 无条件信任 X-Forwarded-For（限流绕过 / IP 伪造）
- 文件：`backend/src/config/env.ts`、`backend/src/app/server.ts`、`deploy.sh`、`backend/.env.example`
- 问题：`trustProxy: true` 无条件信任，攻击者可伪造 X-Forwarded-For 绕过按 IP 限流。
- 修复：新增 `TRUST_PROXY` 配置，默认 false（直连公网安全），deploy.sh 部署时在 nginx 反代后设为 true。

## 验证
- `pnpm build` 通过；`vitest --pool=threads` 39 测试全绿

## 影响
- 后端 + 部署脚本/配置示例；无迁移。
- deploy.sh 自动写入 `TRUST_PROXY=true`；手动部署需在 .env 自行设置。

author: heydemoura
body:
## Proposed changes

* Raise the AI admin page test suite's async-utility timeout (`configure( { asyncUtilTimeout: 10000 } )`). The suite renders the whole admin app, whose boot chains several mocked requests through effects; under coverage instrumentation on a loaded CI runner that settle can exceed testing-library's 1-second default, so `findBy*`/`waitFor` assertions fail on timing rather than behavior. Observed as repeated `Code coverage (JS)` failures on unrelated PRs (twice consecutively on #51521, e.g. `host-off: shows the host-off notice…` rejecting after the file already ran for ~77s) while trunk's less-contended runs pass.
* Test-only change; no production behavior affected.

## Related product discussion/links

* Surfaced by the Code coverage (JS) failures on #51521.

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?

No.

## Testing instructions

* `pnpm run test-gui _inc/client/ai/test/main.jsx` from `projects/plugins/jetpack` — all 24 tests pass.
* The timing sensitivity is reproducible in the old code by lowering the default (`configure( { asyncUtilTimeout: 100 } )`): the async assertions fail exactly the way CI's instrumented runs do.

author: freaxnx01
body:
## Summary

`classify-turns.sh` picks the agent's turn budget from the issue body — 160 turns for a 6+ task enriched plan, down to a 50-turn default when it finds no plan at all. It detected the plan with:

```bash
printf '%s' "$ISSUE_BODY" | grep -qi '^## Implementation Plan'
```

`grep -q` exits the moment it matches, so `printf` is usually still writing. It dies of `SIGPIPE`, and `set -o pipefail` turns a **successful match into a false condition**. The script takes the `else` branch and reports `no Implementation Plan section found`.

Because it depends on how much body is left to write when grep quits, it only bites **large enriched issues — precisely the ones that need the biggest budget.**

## Evidence

Hit for real on #280: an 8-task plan that had earned 160 turns got 50, hit the cap, and lost the run — $1.84 and every uncommitted edit. From that run's log:

```
classify-turns.sh: line 85: printf: write error: Broken pipe
chosen: 50 (heuristic: no Implementation Plan section found)
```

Measured on the real 57 KB body: **42/100 runs mis-classified** before, **0/200** after. (The stderr message is not reliable — where `SIGPIPE` isn't ignored, `printf` dies silently and the only symptom is the wrong budget.)

## Changes

- `scripts/classify-turns.sh` — feed both greps by here-string; no pipe, no race
- `tests/fixtures/issue-body-large-plan.md` — the real #280 body, 57 KB
- `tests/run-script-tests.sh` — regression test asserting **25 consecutive runs** all pick 160

The repeat matters: a single run reproduces less than half the time, so a one-shot test would pass against the broken script.

## Testing

- `tests/run-script-tests.sh` — 480/480 pass
- `shellcheck -x -e SC1091` — clean on both files
- Fails reliably on the pre-fix script; passes after

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass
- [x] No new vulnerable deps
- [x] No secrets
- [x] Test fails before the fix and passes after

author: mgrin
body:
Third wave of the mirror scrub, after #389 and #390. Those two cleared everything
`check-oss-prose.ts --scan` reports; this clears what it structurally cannot.

## Why the scan misses these

It fires only when a scope word and a measurement share **one sentence**. So it
never sees `N of M`, a bare percentage, an un-grouped count, or a figure sitting a
line or two away from the production language rather than beside it. A
paragraph-level sweep over the `oss-eligible` set found roughly 90 further sites
across ~100 files. Every file was confirmed present upstream, with a
must-be-present control on each check so a blind negative could not read as "not
there".

## A second class, worse than any count

The same sweep found **four real on-chain wallet addresses and one transaction
hash**, carried in 15 files as both comments *and* test fixture values. A count
leaks a fact about a database; an address is a permanent link between this
repository and a real person's holdings.

They are replaced with clearly synthetic stand-ins of the same shape, applied
consistently across every file that referenced them. The EIP-55 mixed-case pairs
stay case-differing pairs, so the casing-insensitivity tests still exercise the
thing they were written for.

Public token-contract addresses (WETH, USDC, USDT, the Aave pool, the CoinGecko
well-known table) are untouched — those are public infrastructure and load-bearing.

## What is deliberately kept

Figures that do not measure a running deployment: upstream API limits, code
constants, regex quantifiers, browser and bundle measurements, self-hosting docs,
market prices, dates and vendor names.

## Scope and safety

- **No behaviour change.** Every non-comment line in the diff is a test fixture
  value — a synthetic identifier or quantity — or a trailing SQL comment.
- **Eight migrations change comments only.** Each one's executable SQL is
  byte-identical, proven by diffing with full-line and trailing comments stripped.
  Their recorded sha256 values change; nothing they do changes.
- `OSS_ALLOW_FIGURES=1` was set, and the assertion it asks for is true: the
  quantities on the added lines were invented for these fixtures. They carry ten
  fraction digits because that is the wire format being modelled, and every value
  in that format trips the check however round it is.

## Verification

Gated on the private port of the identical tree (per-run database isolation lives
there):

```
gate-db: PASS · exit 0 · 10391 tests across 754 files · HEAD 60c0cb1d3, tree clean,
5 written mid-run, bytes unchanged · base 7526258d1 unchanged (confirmed against the remote)
```

All 112 files here are byte-identical to that gated tree, checked file by file.
`bun run type-check`, `bun lint:fix`, `bun run docs:check` and `bun run deps:unused`
are all clean.

Opened as a draft until the private port lands.

author: grotegehaktbal
body:
Two commits, both from things that turned out to be wrong in the docs rather than in the code.

## The `*.pages.dev` addresses are a second copy of the site

A Pages project is always reachable at `<project>.pages.dev` as well as at its custom domain, and that address serves these same pages — the duplicate-content problem `riemersmaict.nl` had, from a hostname nobody chose to publish. Cloudflare already sends `noindex` on preview deployments; it does not on the project's own production `*.pages.dev`.

Every canonical tag already names `priemersma.nl`, which is most of the answer. `public/_headers` is now the rest of it:

```
https://:project.pages.dev/*
  X-Robots-Tag: noindex

https://:version.:project.pages.dev/*
  X-Robots-Tag: noindex
```

**The scoping is the safety-critical part, not a detail.** `:project` and `:version` are placeholders Cloudflare fills from the request's hostname, so these match `<project>.pages.dev` and `<hash>.<project>.pages.dev` and nothing else. The same header leaking onto the real domain would take the site out of Google, so that is checked rather than assumed: serving the export locally shows the security headers present on `/en` and no `X-Robots-Tag` anywhere on the site's own pages.

`docs/CLOUDFLARE.md` had this written down as something that needed the project's name filled in before it could be added. It does not — `:project` is a real placeholder in Cloudflare's matcher, not a stand-in. The doc is corrected with it.

## Cloudflare Pages reports as a check, not a deployment

The same file said Pages creates a GitHub *deployment* and appears in the Deployments panel. It does not: it posts a check run named "Cloudflare Pages", beside CI.

That is wrong in a way that sends you looking in the wrong place. This repository's Deployments page and the Environments beside it are populated by a host that *does* create them, so it still shows a stale production pointing at a `vercel.app` URL while Cloudflare's own green tick sits in the checks. Corrected, with a note that those leftovers can be deleted under Settings → Environments.

## Verified

`typecheck`, `lint`, 21 unit tests, `build:static`, the size budget, `check:export` and 23 smoke checks — all green.

author: raporipo
body:
## Summary

Expands the bilingual exploration on religious worldviews and normativity from a compact outline into a more fully argued article.

### Structural changes
- groups the 16 sections into four larger parts: decomposition of religion, theological bridges, identification of divine goodness, and worship/non-theistic comparisons
- upgrades the page from Exploration v0.1 to v0.2

### Major additions
- NOMA placed in a broader Barbour / Stenmark / Brooke-style history of science–religion classification, with a move from institution-level separation to claim-level non-conflation
- clearer local-atheism / global-atheism distinction and genealogical undercutting of religious evidence
- historical typology of religion as power/efficacy, sanction, normativity, and value-identity rather than a single linear progression
- expanded Plato / servile fear / Shaftesbury / Kant / Mill treatment of sanction versus genuine normativity
- deeper Huck Finn analysis using represented normative structure versus true normative structure
- detailed C→B treatment: divine command, divine nature, natural law, creation/authority, and God as perfect knower
- expanded distinction between God communicating reasons, evidentially supporting them, generating them, and sanctioning compliance, including Murphy's authority/compliance distinction
- six routes for identifying divine goodness, with their distinct epistemic and bridge problems
- expanded apophatic tradeoff between falsification resistance and discriminatory/action-guiding content
- detailed treatment of four major responses to the Evil-God Challenge and a broader alien-value comparison
- evil and divine hiddenness reframed more fully as identification problems
- richer decomposition of worship, sacredness, gratitude, allegiance, and fittingness
- expanded Buddhism, Confucianism, Zhuangzi, and Shinto comparisons

Japanese and English versions are kept structurally aligned.

author: pyup-bot
body:
### Update [django](https://pypi.org/project/django) from **4.0** to **6.1**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.1
   ```
   ========================

*August 5, 2026*

Welcome to Django 6.1!

These release notes cover the :ref:`new features <whats-new-6.1>`, as well as
some :ref:`backwards incompatible changes <backwards-incompatible-6.1>` you'll
want to be aware of when upgrading from Django 6.0 or earlier. We've
:ref:`begun the deprecation process for some features
<deprecated-features-6.1>`.

See the :doc:`/howto/upgrade-version` guide if you're updating an existing
project.

Mainstream support is expected to end in April 2027. Extended support is
expected to end in December 2027.

Python compatibility
====================

Django 6.1 supports Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14. We **highly recommend**, and
only officially support, the latest release of each series.

.. _whats-new-6.1:

What's new in Django 6.1
========================

Model field fetch modes
-----------------------

The on-demand fetching behavior of model fields is now configurable with
:doc:`fetch modes </topics/db/fetch-modes>`. These modes allow you to control
how Django fetches data from the database when an unfetched field is accessed.

Django provides three fetch modes:

1. ``FETCH_ONE``, the default, fetches the missing field for the current
   instance only. This mode represents Django's existing behavior.

2. ``FETCH_PEERS`` fetches a missing field for all instances that came from
   the same :class:`~django.db.models.query.QuerySet`.

   This mode works like an on-demand ``prefetch_related()``. It can reduce most
   cases of the "N+1 queries problem" to two queries without any work to
   maintain a list of fields to prefetch.

3. ``FETCH_RAISE`` raises a :exc:`~django.core.exceptions.FieldFetchBlocked`
   exception.

   This mode can prevent unintentional queries in performance-critical
   sections of code.

Use the new method :meth:`.QuerySet.fetch_mode` to set the fetch mode for model
instances fetched by the ``QuerySet``:

.. code-block::

    from django.db import models

    books = Book.objects.fetch_mode(models.FETCH_PEERS)
    for book in books:
        print(book.author.name)

Despite the loop accessing the ``author`` foreign key on each instance, the
``FETCH_PEERS`` fetch mode will make the above example perform only two
queries:

1. Fetch all books.
2. Fetch associated authors.

See :doc:`fetch modes </topics/db/fetch-modes>` for more details.

Database-level delete options for ``ForeignKey.on_delete``
----------------------------------------------------------

:attr:`.ForeignKey.on_delete` now supports database-level delete options:

* :attr:`~django.db.models.DB_CASCADE`
* :attr:`~django.db.models.DB_SET_NULL`
* :attr:`~django.db.models.DB_SET_DEFAULT`

These options handle deletion logic entirely within the database, using the SQL
``ON DELETE`` clause. They are thus more efficient than the existing
Python-level options, as Django does not need to load objects before deleting
them. As a consequence, the :attr:`~django.db.models.DB_CASCADE` option does
not trigger the ``pre_delete`` or ``post_delete`` signals.

Mailers
-------

The new :setting:`MAILERS` setting supports configuring multiple email backends
with different options, similar to existing mechanisms for :setting:`CACHES`,
:setting:`DATABASES`, :setting:`STORAGES`, and :setting:`TASKS`::

    MAILERS = {
        "default": {
            "BACKEND": "django.core.mail.backends.smtp.EmailBackend",
            "OPTIONS": {"host": "smtp.example.com", "use_tls": True},
        },
        "marketing": {
            "BACKEND": "example.third.party.EmailBackend",
            "OPTIONS": {"region": "africa-1"},
        },
    }

You can select a mailer with the new ``using`` argument to :ref:`email sending
<topic-email-sending>` functions, or obtain an email backend instance with
:data:`mail.mailers[alias] <django.core.mail.mailers>`. See
:doc:`/topics/email` for more details.

:setting:`MAILERS` is not yet enabled by default in existing projects. It will
replace :setting:`EMAIL_BACKEND` and related ``EMAIL_*`` settings in Django
7.0. Until then, the older settings will continue to work but will issue
deprecation warnings: see the list of :ref:`email deprecations
<mailers-deprecations>` below.

You can opt into the new feature at any time before Django 7.0; see
:ref:`migrating-to-mailers`. To ease the transition,
:data:`mail.mailers["default"] <django.core.mail.mailers.default>` works with
either :setting:`MAILERS` or the deprecated :setting:`EMAIL_BACKEND` setting
defined. The deprecated :func:`~django.core.mail.get_connection` function will
also return an instance of the default mailer when :setting:`MAILERS` is
defined.

Minor features
--------------

:mod:`django.contrib.admin`
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* The admin site login view now redirects authenticated users to the next URL,
  if available, instead of always redirecting to the admin index page.

* The admin's ``FilteredSelectMultiple`` widget now uses ``<optgroup>``\s to
  preserve :ref:`named groups <field-choices-named-groups>` (e.g.
  ``choices=[("Group", [("1", "Item")]), ...]``).

* When :attr:`.ModelAdmin.list_select_related` is ``False`` (the default),
  the change list now selects only the foreign key fields specified in
  :attr:`.ModelAdmin.list_display`, rather than all foreign key fields. This
  should improve performance for models with many foreign key fields.

* The :attr:`~django.contrib.admin.ModelAdmin.delete_confirmation_max_display`
  option allows customizing how many objects are displayed on admin delete
  confirmation pages and inline protected deletion errors before the remainder
  is truncated. The default is ``None`` (no truncation).

* In order to improve accessibility of the admin change forms:

  * Form fields are now shown below their respective labels instead of next to
    them.

  * Help text is now shown after the field label and before the field input.

  * Validation errors are now shown after the help text and before the field
    input.

  * Checkboxes are an exception to the above changes and continue to be
    displayed in their original layout.

* :attr:`~django.contrib.admin.ModelAdmin.list_display` now uses boolean icons
  for boolean fields on related models.

* The new ``location`` keyword argument of the
  :func:`~django.contrib.admin.action` decorator specifies which admin views
  the action is available on. The action is available on the admin change list
  page by default. It can also be available on the admin change form. See
  :ref:`admin-action-availability` for details.

* The new ``description_plural`` keyword argument of the
  :func:`~django.contrib.admin.action` decorator specifies a human-readable
  description for actions on the admin change list page. Defaults to the
  ``description`` value. This is useful when the action is available on both
  the admin change list and admin change form.

:mod:`django.contrib.auth`
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* The default iteration count for the PBKDF2 password hasher is increased from
  1,200,000 to 1,500,000.

* :attr:`.Permission.name` and :attr:`.Permission.codename` values are now
  renamed when renaming models via a migration.

* The new :attr:`.Permission.user_perm_str` property returns the string
  suitable to use with :meth:`.User.has_perm`.

:mod:`django.contrib.gis`
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* The :lookup:`isempty` lookup and
  :class:`IsEmpty() <django.contrib.gis.db.models.functions.IsEmpty>`
  database function are now supported on SpatiaLite.

* The new :lookup:`num_dimensions` lookup and :class:`NumDimensions()
  <django.contrib.gis.

body: ## Problem Wren glance miss on prod (`c5eee0c` / PR #11): on the miss overlay, COPY PROMPT sits **beside** TRY AGAIN and appears **green** at rest. Wren expects COPY to be quiet/muted and stacked under TRY AGAIN — not a second green button next to it. **Root cause:** `.overlay-btn--copy` was declared *before* `.overlay-btn` in CSS. Both are single-class selectors, so CSS source order means the later `.overlay-btn` rule wins — `background: var(--green)` overrides the muted `rgba(255,255,255,0.1)`. Additionally, both buttons were `display: inline` (default) and COPY came before TRY AGAIN in JSX, so they rendered side-by-side with COPY first. ## Fix ### `app/globals.css` - **Moved** `.overlay-btn--copy` (and its `:hover`/`:disabled` variants) **after** `.overlay-btn` so the muted background wins by source order. - **Added** `display: block` on `.overlay-btn--copy` so it stacks vertically like Cancel. ### `app/page.tsx` - **Reordered** JSX: TRY AGAIN (green primary) → COPY PROMPT (muted) → Cancel — matching the expected visual hierarchy. ## Unchanged - Title "Open Grok Bot to finish." and Lane's paste hint line stay. - Prompt is still not displayed on screen. - TRY AGAIN stays the green primary button. - Cancel still stacks under, Escape still dismisses, no remint. - Connecting… overlay unchanged. - `grokbot://app/v1/open` deep link unchanged — CONNECT is still one tap. - No 1:1 URL. author: dylanjeffers
body:
## Problem

Album track rows render a release date of **12/31/69**. Reported again this week on https://audius.co/SIRMYKE/album/cabanne-place-vocals-single, whose single track shows 7/26/26 on its own track page.

The API returns the entry as:

```json
{ "track_id": "NQl5AV8", "timestamp": 0, "metadata_timestamp": 1787494865 }
```

`timestamp: 0` → `dayjs.unix(0)` → 12/31/69.

The client half of this was fixed in AudiusProject/audius-protocol#14579, which restored a `|| created_at` fallback. This PR fixes the write path that produces the zero in the first place, so the server stops depending on every client to defend against it.

## Root cause

`canonicalizePlaylistEntry` emitted `time` only when the incoming entry carried a parseable number:

```go
if t, ok := pickJSONInt(entry, "time", "timestamp"); ok {
    out["time"] = t
}
```

No key is persisted when the client omits it. `dbv1.PlaylistContentsItem.Time` in the api is a bare `float64` with no `omitempty`, so a missing key deserializes to the zero value and re-serializes as `"timestamp": 0` — indistinguishable downstream from a genuine zero.

Its sibling a few lines away in `playlist_create.go` already does the right thing for the analogous field:

```go
releaseDate := releaseDateOrDefault(params.MetadataString("release_date"), params.BlockTime)
```

## Fix

`time` is now always emitted, in precedence order:

1. the client-sent value, when positive;
2. the time this entry already carries in the stored row;
3. `params.BlockTime`.

A zero is treated as absent rather than honored — unix 0 is never a real add-time, and the paths that produce it are ones that never set the field. This also means the fix covers both possible on-disk shapes, which matters because the public API cannot distinguish them (I could not reach Metabase to confirm which one these rows actually hold).

Step 2 is what keeps the update path honest. Without it, a metadata-only edit to an affected playlist would restamp every entry with the edit's block time rather than preserving the real add-times. Step 3 is skipped when `BlockTime` is itself unset, where emitting nothing beats stamping year 1.

## Scope

Write path only. **Rows already damaged still need a backfill** — this makes new and edited playlists self-healing, but does not retroactively repair `cabanne-place-vocals-single`. Happy to follow up with a migration; it wants its own review since it rewrites production JSONB.

Still not pinned: which client write path drops the field. Every SDK path requires `timestamp` (zod `z.number()` in both the Create and Update schemas) and all web create paths set it, so the damage is arriving from somewhere else. The floor makes that question non-urgent rather than answering it.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` and `go vet` clean on `pkg/etl`
- [x] `TestNormalizePlaylistContentsJSON` extended — missing / zero / negative timestamps all floor to block time, including the exact `{track_id, timestamp: 0, metadata_timestamp: N}` shape from the reported album
- [x] New `TestNormalizePlaylistContentsJSONPriorTimes` — prior value carried forward, client value still wins, a prior zero is not carried forward
- [x] New `TestNormalizePlaylistContentsJSONZeroBlockTime` — no floor available, no key emitted
- [x] Full `processors/entity_manager` suite passes against a clean PG 16 (265s, all green)

body:
## Tier 1 · Increment F — bulk user actions

`POST /admin/users/bulk` applies one action to many in-org users at once and returns a **per-user partial-failure report**.

```json
{ "action": "deactivate|reactivate|role|reset_password", "user_ids": [1,2,3], "role_key": "she_officer" }
```
-> `{ ok, action, succeeded, failed, results: [ {user_id, ok, message}, ... ] }`

- **Reuses the single-user helpers** (`_target_user` org-scoping, `_active_super_admins`, `auth.revoke_user_sessions`/`issue_auth_token`) — the merged single-user routes are left **untouched** (no regression risk to A/C).
- **Guards re-checked per user against LIVE state** committed each iteration, so a batch can never remove the final active super-admin; self-deactivate and last-super-admin demotion are blocked mid-batch too.
- Each sub-action **audited** exactly like its single-user counterpart, tagged `bulk:True`, so per-user audit history stays consistent.
- JSON body; capability-gated (`admin.users.manage`); ids de-duped; batch capped at 500.

### Tests
`test_bulk_actions.py` (9) — validation (unknown action, empty ids, bad role, non-admin 403); deactivate partial-failure report (ok + not-found + self) with session revocation; last-super-admin protected in batch; role assign; role demotion of last super-admin blocked; reset_password sets must_change + issues one token each + revokes sessions + queues one email each. Additive route; full SQLite suite run as the gate.

author: amir-r25
body:
## Summary

Apple has released a python sdk enabling developers to utilize their local foundation models: https://github.com/apple/python-apple-fm-sdk

The framework is an agentic harness with enabling chat, streaming, structured output, and tool calling. Many of these are handled internally via their C bindings so we cannot access them the same way we utilize litellm. However, we can bring support for **chat/streaming chat** and **structured** output extraction. 

### Caveats:
- This will only work on macbooks with XCode 26.4+ installed 
- The Apple SDK returns no token counts or cost. `MessageInfo` reports `latency` (measured locally) and `model_name`;
        `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_cost`, and
        `system_fingerprint` are `None`. Aggregations over mixed-provider
        sessions treat Apple runs as "unknown usage"
- These are documented in the docs

## Type of change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Refactor / chore / build / tests

## Checklist

- [x] Lint & format pass (`ruff check . && ruff format .`)
- [x] Tests added/updated and pass locally (`pytest tests`)
- [x] Docs updated if user-facing behavior changed
- [ ] Breaking changes include migration notes

## Notes

Example:
```python
import asyncio
import railtracks as rt
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from datetime import datetime
from rich import print

class Attendee(BaseModel):
    """Details of a single attendee mentioned in the text."""

    first_name: str = Field(description="First name of the attendee.")
    last_name: str | None = Field(None, description="Last name of the attendee. Leave None if not stated.")

class Event(BaseModel):
    """Details of a single scheduled event mentioned in the text."""

    name: str = Field(description="Short name of the event.")
    date: datetime | None = Field(None, description="ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) if stated, else null.")
    start_time: str | None = Field(None, description="24h HH:MM if stated, else null.")
    location: str | None = Field(None, description="Venue or room, else null.")
    attendees: list[Attendee] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Named people.")


ExtractionAgent = rt.agent_node(
    name = "Apple FM Extraction Agent",
    llm = rt.llm.AppleFMLLM(),
    # llm = rt.llm.OpenAILLM("gpt-5.4"),
    system_message = "You are a helpful assistant that can extract structured information from text about Apple FM.",
    output_schema = Event,
)

flow = rt.Flow(
    name = "Apple FM Flow",
    entry_point = ExtractionAgent
)

USR_PROMPT = """
Hi team, 
quick update on the Q3 planning offsite. 
We've moved it to Thursday, October 9th, 9:30am–4pm,
 at the Harbourview Centre (room 2B). Priya Raj will run the morning session on roadmap tradeoffs, 
 and Marcus Lindt is covering budget after lunch. Lunch is catered, let me know by Sept 26 
 if you have dietary restrictions. Dan can't make it in person but will join the afternoon by video.
"""

async def main():
    resp = await flow.ainvoke(USR_PROMPT)
    print(resp.structured)
    print(await flow.ainvoke(USR_PROMPT))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

    resp = flow.invoke(USR_PROMPT)
    print(resp.structured)
```

author: codihuston
body:
## Intent

Add truenas_user (and, since the API couples them, a minimal truenas_group) resources to this provider fork.

Binding decisions made before implementation:
- Passwordless/key-first by DEFAULT: the happy path creates users with password_disabled or SSH-key auth. An optional password is accepted as a WRITE-ONLY-style input, sent on create/update, never stored in state and never read back; drift on it is explicitly undetectable and must be documented as such.
- QUALITY BAR: this fork must stay upstream-portable to deevus - their conventions and doc style exactly, zero homelab assumptions, no filler comments, idiomatic terraform-plugin-framework.
- Schemas derived from the LIVE API only (repo tooling / midclt against the acceptance box), not from memory or guesswork.
- Build like the sibling task: follow internal/resources/cron_job.go's CRUD pattern and the repo's mocked-client unit-test conventions. Fields: the practical user.create/update surface (username, uid optional/computed, full_name, group/groups, home + perms, shell, ssh public key, smb, locked, password_disabled, sudo_commands*). Import by id. Required/optional/computed derived from the API schema.
- Acceptance target: TrueNAS SCALE 25.10.6 at 10.0.10.4, pool tank. Create/read/update/import/delete real users there.
- Done means: unit green, acceptance green, docs generated, coverage >= baseline (baseline was 89.8% total / 90.0% resources; the branch is at 90.3% total, 97.4% services).

Decisions and tradeoffs made while implementing, all derived from probing the live 25.10.6 API:
- truenas-go v0.5.0 (latest) has NO user/group service, so UserService and GroupService were written in internal/services following truenas-go's own service shape (opts struct -> params map, wire response -> user-facing struct, *_service.go plus *_service_iface.go carrying the interface and mock) so they can be lifted upstream unchanged. This is deliberate, not a layering violation.
- password is implemented as a real terraform-plugin-framework WriteOnly attribute (framework 1.17 / Terraform 1.11+), paired with password_wo_version as the re-send trigger. Because write-only values are absent from state, Update sends the password only when password_wo_version changes. Undetectable drift is intentional and documented.
- smb defaults to FALSE, deliberately deviating from the API default of true, because TrueNAS rejects password_disabled for SMB users and silently adds them to builtin_users - both wrong for the key-first default. Documented. ValidateConfig rejects smb + password_disabled at plan time so the API error surfaces during plan.
- uid and gid are RequiresReplace because the API rejects both on update (verified: 'user_update.uid: Extra inputs are not permitted').
- home asymmetry, verified on the box: with home_create the API treats home as the PARENT and creates <home>/<username>, then REJECTS that same parent on a later update ('The specified path is a ZFS pool mountpoint'). So home stays a stable config input, the server's real path is exported as the computed home_path, and Update sends home_path unless home actually changed. home/home_create/home_mode are inputs TrueNAS never reports back, so drift on them is undetectable; Read seeds home from the server on import.
- group and groups take group ENTRY IDs, not Unix GIDs. ValidateConfig requires exactly one of group or group_create (treating an unknown group as set, so a reference to another resource is legal).
- groups is Optional+Computed with no default so TrueNAS-managed membership (builtin_users under smb) does not cause perpetual drift; sudo_commands* use an empty-list default so removing the attribute clears them.
- group.create/group.update return only the entry ID, so GroupService reads the group back after writing (user.create/update return the full object and do not need this).

Verification performed: full unit suite green; and against the real box at 10.0.10.4 via a dev_overrides Terraform, the whole lifecycle - create, empty plan, update, empty plan, import, converge, destroy - plus the write-only password paths (secret absent from state, changing it alone yields an empty plan, bumping password_wo_version re-sends it) and the smb+password_disabled validation error. Docs generated with tfplugindocs from new templates plus runnable examples.

Out of scope / deliberately not done: no terraform-plugin-testing acceptance harness was added - this repo has none today and mise run test-acc matches zero tests, so introducing that framework unilaterally was judged against the upstream-portability bar. A pre-existing golangci-lint 'unused: int64Ptr' finding in internal/resources/virt_instance_test.go is untouched and not mine. fm-ensure-agents-md.sh's CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md rename was deliberately reverted as unrelated repo-wide scope; the durable knowledge went into the existing CLAUDE.md instead.

## What Changed

- Adds `truenas_user` and `truenas_group` resources (`internal/resources/user.go`, `group.go`) with full CRUD plus import by ID, registered in `internal/provider/provider.go`. The user schema is key-first by default: `smb` defaults to `false` (deviating from the API default), `password` is a framework write-only attribute paired with `password_wo_version` so it is sent on create and re-sent only when that version changes and never stored in state, `uid`/`gid` are `RequiresReplace` because the API rejects them on update, `home` stays a stable config input while the server's actual path is exported as computed `home_path`, and `ValidateConfig` rejects `smb` + `password_disabled` and requires exactly one of `group`/`group_create` at plan time. `groups` reconciliation ignores `builtin_users` one-directionally to avoid perpetual drift.
- Adds `UserService` and `GroupService` in `internal/services` (service + iface/mock files, shared `errors.go`, wired into `TrueNASServices`) covering the `user.*` and `group.*` namespaces that truenas-go v0.5.0 does not implement; the group service reads the entry back after create/update because those calls return only the entry ID.
- Adds unit tests for both resources and both services against the repo's mocked-client conventions, plus shared account test helpers; adds tfplugindocs templates, generated `docs/resources/{user,group}.md`, runnable examples, and README/index/CLAUDE.md notes.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The four prior fix rounds landed correctly — SSH key revocation works, the whitespace-normalization inconsistency is closed, the password/version pairing is enforced at plan time, the example no longer orphans a managed group, and the `builtin_users` exemption is now genuinely one-directional (I traced stored-loses-builtin, server-adds-builtin, non-builtin addition/removal, unset, and explicit-`[]` through `sameGroups` and all produce the right set) — but this is 4200 lines of new resource code whose most intricate logic, the group reconciliation and its `group.query` dependency, exists only because of the fix rounds and has never run against real hardware.

## Testing

Built the provider from branch head and drove it with the real Terraform CLI against the live TrueNAS SCALE 25.10.6 acceptance box, exercising the builtin_users reconciliation (both the previously-failing smb + explicit groups apply and the one-directional exemption under refresh), ssh_public_key set-then-revoke including the on-disk authorized_keys file, the whole create/plan/update/import/converge/destroy lifecycle with the pool-mountpoint home asymmetry, the write-only password rotation semantics checked against /etc/shadow, and both plan-time validation errors; the targeted user/group unit tests were run alongside. Everything passed, the stand-in evidence from the prior round was removed and replaced with the real transcript, and all test users, groups and directories were cleaned off the server.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Real-hardware acceptance transcript (10.0.10.4, TrueNAS SCALE 25.10.6)</summary>

```text
# tru

author: nick-potts
body: ## Why People who already sit on the server should be able to found a Cluster there. `sudo ployz machine init` is that path. Remote `ployz machine init user@host` stays the laptop path. ## Scope `ployz machine init` with no DESTINATION now talks to `/run/ployz/ployz.sock`. It installs `ployzd` through `provision_local` unless `--no-install`. After a fresh local install it retries the first dial with `reconnect_direct`, because there is no remote `ployzd dial-stdio` waiter. Remote destinations still parse as SSH, still run `provision`, still save an SSH connection. The stub error `local machine initialisation is not implemented` is gone. The CLI deviation is renamed `local-machine-init`. Help text says this Machine or a remote machine. Destination stays optional. Out of scope: `--local`, rewriting config under `SUDO_USER`, extracting an enrollment module, local `machine add`. ## Tradeoffs Omitted destination is the mode. A new flag would duplicate the optional positional the freeze already allowed. Config still writes under the process `HOME`. `cloud enroll` does the same. After sudo, later `ployz` as the unprivileged user can still hit the unix socket if that user is in the ployz group. ## Blast Radius CLI only. No daemon RPC change. `machine init user@host` is unchanged. `cloud enroll` is unchanged. ## Verification Dispatch tests, uid 1000, no `/run/ployz/ployz.sock`: - `local_machine_init_requires_root_to_install` passed. Error is `run this command with sudo`. - `local_machine_init_without_install_dials_the_unix_socket` passed. Error is `all 1 connections from Direct failed`. - `clap_tree_matches_all_frozen_command_pages_and_declared_deviations` passed. - `scripts/check-product-paths.sh` passed. Real binary: - `ployz machine init --yes --storage none --no-dns --no-ingress` exited 1 with `run this command with sudo`. - Same command with `--no-install` exited 1 with `all 1 connections from Direct failed`. - `ployz machine init --help` shows `[destination]` and "this Machine or a remote machine". Happy-path root install plus a live `ployzd` is not covered here.

# One-time setup privilege and helper resilience fn-4 shipped the plugin-owned distraction list, always-on off-space site block, and listener-owned reload. A quality pass then found helper-resilience gaps. > **Spec:** [fn-7-one-time-setup-privilege-and-helper](https://github.com/DanielKillenberger/omarchy-distraction-space/blob/a93e9368463c17ab444aa1d6cd91c4b3d115fb35/.flow/specs/fn-7-one-time-setup-privilege-and-helper.md) > **Branch:** `fn-7-one-time-setup-privilege-and-helper` → `origin/main` > **Tasks:** 3 completed > **R-ID coverage:** 6/6 evidenced > **Render lens:** `.flow/artifacts/fn-7-one-time-setup-privilege-and-helper/pr.html` (v1 currentness preserved — open locally in a browser; regenerable) ## TL;DR - Privileged setup should ask for sudo once; after that, list save, reload, placement, and site-block apply stay on non-interactive sudo, and a failed job, window event, overlapping reload, or notify must not kill the helper. - Hardened `setup` so one interactive sudo pins a trusted path, atomically installs the 0755 wrapper, visudo-validates a uid-only 0440 grant, and revalidates immediately before rename. - NetworkWorker now records a failed `_run` and stays accepting; overlapping reloads take one in-process lock across the full transaction so last-good writes stay consistent. - `process_socket2_line` skips a raising window query or move so later events still run; `notify()` OSError absorb is covered next to the existing missing/nonzero test. ## Not in this PR (by design) - fn-4 product behavior stays: owned list, exclusive listed windows, always-on off-space site block, intercept banner, focus lock unchanged. - This spec does not re-open fn-4 list membership, banner copy, or expand-map work. - Splitting the helper into multiple modules and extracting shared test fixtures are not required to close this spec. - Tests that reach internal worker state may stay; tightening them is optional. - Uninstall remains a documented teardown of the privileged helper and grant, not a second interactive product flow. - …and 3 more (see [spec](https://github.com/DanielKillenberger/omarchy-distraction-space/blob/a93e9368463c17ab444aa1d6cd91c4b3d115fb35/.flow/specs/fn-7-one-time-setup-privilege-and-helper.md)) ## The change, top to bottom One setup sudo installs a trusted-path nft wrapper and uid-only grant. author: ramotte11-ops
body:
## Résumé

Couche applicative serveur au-dessus de la primitive atomique de Mission 011A. **Code only** : aucune migration, aucune policy RLS, aucune action Supabase distante.

> **Correctif de revue (commit `31d500b`)** — la première version résolvait l'Owner par email avec `.ilike()`, ce qui livrait l'adresse à SQL **comme un pattern**. Corrigé en égalité exacte. Détail en fin de description.

## La frontière qui structure cette mission

`redeemAuthenticatedEntitlement()` est un **service interne serveur, et rien ne l'appelle**. Aucune route, Server Action, formulaire ou page d'activation : **connaître un UUID d'entitlement ne doit jamais suffire à obtenir un mémorial**. Le mécanisme qui résoudra une clé/preuve autorisée vers un `entitlementId` est une mission ultérieure.

Les deux identités en jeu sont traitées différemment à dessein : `identity` est la session réelle établie côté serveur, `entitlementId` est une référence opaque venant de l'appelant de confiance. **Il n'y a aucun paramètre `ownerId`.**

## Sécurité Owner — `lib/entitlement/resolve-owner.ts`

Une règle structure tout : **une adresse email identique n'est jamais une preuve d'identité.** Une ligne Owner peut préexister ; la reprendre parce qu'un email correspond reviendrait à donner les mémoriaux d'une famille à quiconque peut recevoir du courrier à une adresse voisine. Le seul lien jamais *créé* est entre un auth user et une ligne Owner **neuve**.

| Cas | Situation | Résultat |
|---|---|---|
| A | `auth_user_id` déjà lié | réutilisation (l'email n'est même pas lu) |
| B | rien de lié, rien en travers | création |
| C | Owner non lié au même email | `ownerLinkConflict` |
| D | email lié à un autre auth user | `ownerIdentityConflict` |
| E | anonyme / sans email / malformé / **non confirmé** / sans id | refus, zéro lecture DB |

Le contrôle porteur du cas E est `email_confirmed_at` : sans lui, `email` n'est qu'une chaîne non vérifiée, et `owners.email` est unique — l'accepter laisserait une adresse non vérifiée squatter l'identité d'un vrai acheteur.

**Concurrence (cas B)** : garantie par le schéma existant. L'insert est tenté, `23505` est traité comme « quelqu'un est arrivé avant », puis relu pour déterminer le cas réel. Deux premières redemptions simultanées ne peuvent pas créer deux Owners.

## Offer / Skin — réutilisation de Mission 006

`offerId → OFFERS → memorialType` + `allowedSkins → Memorial`. Un skin autorisé → automatique (les 5 offres V1). Plusieurs sans sélection → `skinSelectionRequired`, **jamais `allowedSkins[0]`**. Skin non autorisé → refus. Tous **avant** la RPC.

**`planEntitlementActivation()` n'est délibérément pas la porte ici** : elle décide aussi le statut, ce qui depuis 011A appartient à la base sous verrou de ligne. Le réutiliser dupliquerait la règle, rouvrirait la course check-then-act que 011A ferme, et **casserait l'idempotence**.

## Adapters

Ports étroits suivant la convention du dépôt. Les adapters sont le **seul** endroit qui connaît les SQLSTATEs de 011A (`HH404/HH403/HH409/HH500`) : aucun code, message SQL, hint ou stack ne franchit cette frontière — assertion testée. Une erreur non mappée **rejette** plutôt que de devenir un refus qu'un appelant prendrait pour une décision.

## Correctif de revue — lookup Owner par email

**Le risque était réel, et ma justification initiale était fausse.** postgrest-js fait `searchParams.append(column, \`ilike.${pattern}\`)` : la valeur part **verbatim** comme pattern SQL. Or `%` et `_` sont légaux dans une partie locale d'email (RFC 5322 atext) *et* sont des jokers LIKE/ILIKE. Donc `foo_bar@example.test` matchait le `fooXbar@example.test` d'un **inconnu**, à une frontière d'identité. Conséquences démontrées par les nouveaux tests contre l'ancien code : refus définitif d'une personne légitime dont l'adresse contient `_` ; `%@example.test` matchait tous les Owners d'un domaine (oracle d'existence *et* échec de `.maybeSingle()`) ; et PostgREST traite en plus `*` comme alias de `%`, donc l'échappement aurait dû être correct sur deux couches.

Mon argument d'alors — « un `eq` simple manquerait la ligne avec laquelle il entre en collision » — était le mauvais arbitrage. Manquer une ligne est un **échec sûr** (l'INSERT reste refusé par `lower(email)`, donc refus, jamais prise de contrôle). Matcher la ligne d'un inconnu ne l'est pas.

**Correction : plus aucun opérateur de pattern.** `findByEmail` utilise `.eq()` sur une adresse normalisée, `create()` écrit la même forme normalisée — lectures, écritures et l'index `lower(email)` s'accordent. En défense en profondeur, l'adapter écarte toute ligne dont l'email n'est pas exactement l'adresse demandée. Les règles A/B/C/D et la stratégie insert → `23505` → relecture sont **inchangées**. Aucune migration.

`lib/entitlement/owner-email-lookup.test.ts` teste l'**adapter réel** dans la **résolution réelle**, sur un store en mémoire qui applique les vraies contraintes de `owners` et implémente la **vraie sémantique SQL ILIKE** — une régression vers un opérateur de pattern y sur-matche réellement. **Vérifié** : en restaurant `.ilike()`, 10 tests échouent (dont « an underscore in the address cannot match a stranger's owner ») ; 24/24 passent sur le correctif. Le harness enregistre la sémantique moteur : contre PostgreSQL réel, `email ilike 'foo_bar@…'` matche l'inconnu, `lower(email) = lower(…)` ne matche personne.

Revue ciblée du reste du périmètre : aucun autre `like`/`ilike`/comparaison par pattern en code applicatif, et aucune valeur fournie par Auth utilisée comme pattern SQL.

## Tests — 300/300 Vitest (76 nouveaux), 71/71 DB (11 nouveaux)

Scénarios A→P couverts, dont les deux chemins de course de la résolution Owner, la matrice offre/skin sur chaque offre V1 réelle, le retry idempotent, et une assertion qu'aucun résultat ne porte autre chose que `status`.

**Le test P est appliqué, pas affirmé en commentaire** : `server-only-boundary.test.ts` parcourt le vrai graphe d'imports depuis chaque module `"use client"` et échoue si l'un atteint le client service-role ou un repository serveur. Il s'arrête aux modules `"use server"` — coupure réelle de Next.js. `import "server-only"` a été considéré puis écarté (paquet non installé, aucune dépendance ajoutée). `lib/supabase/env.ts` n'est volontairement pas sur la liste interdite (partagé avec le client anon ; clé lue via `process.env` dynamique sur une variable non-`NEXT_PUBLIC_`) — propriété assertée directement. Le test se protège contre un succès vide.

Le harness prouve **au niveau schéma** ce dont `resolve-owner.ts` dépend : second Owner sur le même `auth_user_id` rejeté, second Owner au même email rejeté, email ne différant que par la casse rejeté, Owner sans `auth_user_id` possible et non écrasable, plusieurs Owners non liés coexistant, et un Owner fraîchement créé qui redeem de bout en bout via la vraie RPC.

## Hors périmètre (volontairement)

Aucune page d'activation ni route, format/générateur de clé, Etsy/webhook/OAuth, checkout, Admin, dashboard, UI Builder, sélection langue/contexte, slug, publication, Pet, Pro, email. Le rattachement à un Owner **préexistant** reste non construit : `ownerLinkConflict` / `ownerIdentityConflict`, pour un mécanisme sûr hors bande ultérieur.

## Checklist

- [x] Lint, TypeScript, build : verts
- [x] 300/300 tests Vitest
- [x] `scripts/db/test-local.sh` : 71/71
- [x] **Aucune migration** (diff vide sur `supabase/migrations/`)
- [x] Aucune policy RLS créée ou modifiée
- [x] Aucune action Supabase distante, aucun secret, aucune nouvelle dépendance
- [x] Aucune mission ultérieure anticipée
- [x] Pas de fusion — en attente de validation
