author: wyckit
body:
`ConcurrentPublishAndRetire_NeverUnpublishesALivePlacement` and its duplicate-count sibling failed roughly **2 runs in 3** on CI, including on `main` at the v2.0.0 release commit.

## It was contention, not a defect

The failure message was already honest: *"the storm ran out of time before completing its rounds, so it proved nothing."* Neither test ever observed a violated invariant — the storm is bounded by a round count **and** a 60s wall clock, and on a contended shared runner the clock won.

The distribution across three consecutive runs settles it:

| Run | Failed | Passed |
|---|---|---|
| PR #24 | net10.0 | net8.0, net9.0 |
| PR #25 | — | all three |
| main @ `8541450` | net8.0, net9.0 | net10.0 |

A real bug does not migrate between target frameworks run to run.

## Why not just raise the timeout

That moves the threshold without removing it — the next slower runner fails again. The storm's actual requirement is *enough rounds to have a fair chance at a narrow window*, not *exactly 6000*. So the round count is now an aspiration and the oracles are stated against what actually ran:

- `RunRetirementStorm` returns the completed round count.
- The live-entry oracle asserts `completed * adders`; the duplicate scan walks `completed`.
- A **floor** of a quarter of the requested rounds preserves the guard-the-guard property the old hard failure provided — a storm that did almost nothing still fails loudly rather than passing vacuously.
- Budget 60s → 120s, and the `WaitAll` deadlock detector re-derived as `budget + 60s` so it stays strictly longer than the budget it backstops.

## The subtle part

The cutoff is decided once by worker 0 and published **before** the barrier, so every worker makes the same decision for the same round. Deciding per worker would tear a round in half — the remover seeding while the adders skip — and the returned count would then describe rounds that only partly happened, which is precisely the quiet inaccuracy the oracles cannot tolerate.

## Verification

Both new paths were exercised by temporarily shrinking the budget, since neither had ever been tested:

- **40ms** — cuts mid-storm. Tests pass and the oracles hold against the partial count.
- **1ms** — yields 0 and 109 rounds. Both tests fail on the floor with the new message, proving it is live rather than dead code.

Full suite green at the restored budget: **1696 passing on net8.0, net9.0 and net10.0**.

body:
## Por quê

Três frentes que apareceram juntas ao fechar o cutover dos domínios.

## 1. `esper.ws` ainda serve uma cópia do site

`https://esper.ws/` devolve 200 com o conteúdo completo, servido pela Vercel — conteúdo duplicado competindo com `www.ricardoesper.com.br`. A Hostinger não pode aplicar o 301: só tem o registro do domínio e o e-mail.

`scripts/esper-ws-to-cloudflare.sh` cria a zona na Cloudflare, replica os registros do Google Workspace, troca os apontamentos da Vercel pelo padrão originless (`AAAA 100::` proxiado) e cria a Redirect Rule 301 com caminho e query preservados. Para antes da troca de nameserver e exige confirmação dos registros de e-mail.

O DKIM é publicado em dois segmentos TXT e o segundo começa com um espaço dentro do base64. É replicado byte a byte, incluindo o espaço — normalizar quebraria a assinatura sem erro visível, com o e-mail apenas começando a cair em spam.

## 2. O "12 países" ainda estava no ar

Número inventado no commit `5f1385d`. Eu já tinha removido de nove lugares, mas dois escaparam: a página de imprensa, sob o rótulo "fatos verificáveis" para jornalistas, e o contador da home. Ambos estão em produção neste momento.

No lugar entra `COUNTRIES_VISITED = 74`, informado pelo próprio Ricardo — biográfico e sustentável numa entrevista, diferente de "atendidos", que era corporativo e falso.

Aproveitando o herói: "5 empresas fundadas" acertava por coincidência e "3 certificações elite" estava errado — são 5. Ambos agora derivam de `career.ts` e `credentials.ts`.

## 3. Grafo de identidade

O Twitter não é mais usado e saiu do `sameAs`, do press kit e das tags `site`/`creator`. Um perfil abandonado no grafo aponta o buscador para um lugar vazio ou contraditório. O card de preview em si continua — X, Slack e WhatsApp usam essas tags.

Também alinhados ao domínio canônico: o `metadataBase` do layout raiz (armadilha latente, não dano ativo, já que `metadata.ts` gera URLs absolutas), o rótulo das imagens Open Graph e a bio longa do press kit, que dizia a jornalistas que ele escreve em `esper.ws`.

Removido `src/lib/schema.ts`: substituído por `metadata.ts` em `f8a0ca4`, não importado em lugar nenhum, e carregava uma cópia divergente do grafo apontando para o domínio preterido.

## Validação

`tsc --noEmit` limpo, `next lint` sem avisos, 46 testes passando. CI verde nos quatro checks.

## Fora do escopo

Não desativa a Vercel — ela segue como rollback do cutover.

author: jestyr27
body:
## Why

The 2026-09-01 layout probe of the prod n8n VM invalidated the cutover premise in `complete-n8n-composable-deployment`: prod n8n is not the legacy monorepo `deploy.sh` path. It is a standalone rootless-podman compose project (queue mode: n8n + worker + Postgres 16 + Redis) running n8n **2.8.3** via a `:latest` pull frozen six months ago. Two consequences the change didn't cover:

1. Its `.env` spells the encryption key `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (compose maps it to `N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), so neither the pre-seed nor the cutover guard could ever verify the one value that matters most.
2. The composable stack declares different volumes, so an env-only cutover would boot an **empty database** — six months of workflows left behind.

## What

- **Live-name aliases, declared once** — `platform/playbooks/vars/n8n-stateful-keys.yml` is the single manifest of the stateful keys, their live spellings, and their OpenBao fields. `deploy-n8n.yml`'s guard and `seed-n8n-secrets.yml`'s extraction both consume it, so the two halves of the cutover cannot disagree. A live file carrying both spellings is refused as ambiguous.
- **Standing upgrade tooling (design D7)** — `backup-n8n-db.yml` (timestamped `pg_dump`, owner-only 0700 dir, file umask'd 0600, parameterized container so the cutover can aim at the legacy project) and `restore-n8n-db.yml` (explicit `-e n8n_dump_file=` only, `--single-transaction` + `ON_ERROR_STOP`, app containers restarted in an `always:` block so a failed restore never also leaves the service down). This is the runbook for every future n8n version bump, not a one-shot: backup → bump `n8n_image` → guarded deploy → restore on failure.
- Both new plays import `preflight-target-group.yml` — an empty group otherwise reports SUCCESS having written no dump, right before a one-way migration.
- Semaphore templates with survey vars (`Restore n8n DB` is unlaunchable from the UI without one), (Dev) and (Local) variants, and a generic `local-dev.sh run <playbook>` subcommand.
- OpenSpec artifacts revised: D6 (verified prod layout), D7 (standing tooling), amended rollback plan (legacy = the standalone compose project, stopped never destroyed until close-out).

## Proof

- Guard behavior proven by a new **behavioural BATS test** running the real shared task against fixture env files: alias match passes, alias mismatch refuses, cross-spelling duplication refuses, plain-key mismatch refuses.
- Seed extraction fixture-run: legacy spelling seeds cleanly; a file with both spellings is refused with names only.
- Backup + restore executed end-to-end through local Semaphore on the pinned 2.25.7 stack: dump verified, `--clean` drop-and-recreate restore, containers cycled, `/healthz` 200, row counts intact.
- 537 BATS + 100 pytest green; ansible-lint (production profile), yamllint, shellcheck clean; security review of the branch found no exploitable findings.

## Notes for review

- `no_log` is deliberately absent from the backup/restore data paths — dump content never enters the run record (redirects), and hiding a restore failure would be the opposite of safety.
- Generic `pg-dump/restore` shared tasks were considered and deferred (rule of three — n8n is the first instance); the shape to extract toward is noted in the design.

author: prasadtalasila
body:
## Summary

Two independent, file-disjoint issues from `plans/code-review-2026-09.md`, bundled in one PR because they can be worked on in parallel with no shared code.

**Fixes #508** (M-49, m-50, m-51, m-68):

- `chitragupta/references_ieee.py`:
  - BibTeX's `and others` truncation now renders as "et al." instead of a literal author named "others".
  - A single-hyphen page range (`pages = "1-10"`) now gets an en dash, matching the doubled-hyphen form.
  - `_title_part`'s trailing-period strip now skips an abbreviation shape (`U.S.`) instead of stripping every trailing period unconditionally.
  - `_VENUE_FIELDS`'s comment and lookup order now agree: `booktitle` is checked (and wins) first, so a dual-field `@inbook` entry's stray `journal` field no longer silently wins over the correct container title.
- `chitragupta/references_renumber.py`: a single-key group with a locator (`[@doe2020, p. 33]`) now renumbers to `[3, p. 33]` instead of nesting a second bracket (`[[3], p. 33]`). `renumber` split into three focused helpers (`_group_edits`/`_locator_edits`/`_bare_key_edits`) to stay under the 25-statement ratchet after the new logic landed.
- `chitragupta/bib_reader.py`: `_parse_authors` now recognises an author-list separator split across a wrapped line (bibtexparser preserves the original line wrapping) as whitespace, not only a literal `" and "`.
- `chitragupta/dedup.py`: bib_reader's `"Untitled"` missing-title placeholder, and any punctuation-only title, both normalise to empty and are excluded from title-matching, so entries missing a title no longer collide into one falsely-flagged duplicate bucket.

**Fixes #513** (m-82):

`chitragupta/retrieval.py::_tokenize` drops any word of 1-2 characters on both the index and query side, so a query built entirely from such terms (`AI`, `ML`, `5G`, `QA`) returns empty with nothing to explain why. Took the CLI-warns branch from the issue's two proposed options, not the bound-lowering one: lowering the floor to 2 would need an `_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (re-tokenizing the whole cached index and changing every existing query's ranking), while the warning is self-contained and fully testable. Added `retrieval.short_query_terms()` and wired a stderr warning into `retrieval_cli.main()` for both `search` and `evidence`, naming each dropped term. Documented in `docs/CORPUS-SEARCH.md` and `docs/CLI.md`.

PATCH (`6.53.33` -> `6.53.34`; the six other open PRs already claim `6.53.33`, so this avoids the collision).

## Test plan

- [x] New failing-first tests for every finding in `tests/test_references.py`, `tests/test_bib_reader.py`, `tests/test_dedup.py`, `tests/test_retrieval.py`.
- [x] Full suite: `.venv-full/bin/python -m pytest -q` — 4292 passed, 68 skipped, the same 17 pre-existing failures as an unmodified checkout of this worktree (missing `config.toml`, confirmed identical on `origin/main` before any change).
- [x] 100% line+branch coverage on every touched module (`references_ieee.py`, `references_renumber.py`, `bib_reader.py`, `dedup.py`, `retrieval.py`, `retrieval_cli.py`).
- [x] `pylint --rcfile=.pylintrc chitragupta scripts .claude/hooks` — 10.00/10, exit 0.
- [x] `ruff check chitragupta scripts .claude/hooks tests` — clean (one pre-existing finding in `tests/test_spec_align.py`, unrelated to this diff, left untouched).
- [x] `ruff format --check chitragupta scripts tests bench .claude/hooks` — clean.
- [x] `poetry check` — exit 0 (pre-existing deprecation warnings only).
- [x] `tests/test_code_standards_scan.py` — clean; no new offender (the `renumber` split keeps it under the ratchet).
- [x] `markdownlint-cli2` on both touched docs — 0 issues.
- [x] OpenCodeReview (`open-code-review:delegate-review`, LLM-free): 10 of 12 changed files reviewable (`docs/CLI.md`/`docs/CORPUS-SEARCH.md` excluded, `unsupported_ext`). ## Summary
Fixes Snyk Container finding `SNYK-DEBIAN11-LIBXML2-10350665` (CVE-2025-49794, CWE-825 expired pointer dereference in libxml2 XPath/schematron parsing, CVSS 9.1) in the Debian 11 layer pulled in by `Dockerfile:2 FROM node:18.13.0` (`libxml2 2.9.10+dfsg-6.7+deb11u3`).

```diff
-FROM node:18.13.0
+FROM node:22.23.2-bookworm
```

Why Node 22 rather than a newer 18.x tag (the approach used by sibling base-image PRs #118/#120/#147-#150/#253-#255):
- The Debian fix for this CVE is `2.9.14+dfsg-1.3~deb12u3` on bookworm (`+deb11u8` on bullseye). Node 18 is EOL and its images stopped being rebuilt in spring 2025 — the last `node:18.20.8-bookworm` image (docker-library/repo-info, created 2025-03-27) ships `libxml2 2.9.14+dfsg-1.3~deb12u1`, which is still vulnerable. No `node:18.*` tag closes this finding.
- `node:22.23.2-bookworm` (rebuilt 2026-08-25) ships `libxml2 2.9.14+dfsg-1.3~deb12u6` (≥ deb12u3 fix). Same tag as #256, so the two PRs agree if both merge (one-line conflict on `FROM` with the 18.x sibling PRs).
- Snyk's suggested `node:18.20.5-alpine3.19` was not used: it is also a frozen EOL image, and `routes/index.js` shells out to ImageMagick `identify`, which the alpine node images don't ship.

`NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider` in `npm start` remains valid on Node 22 (OpenSSL 3). Could not `docker build` here — the Docker registry is off this session's network allowlist.

Note: the finding is filed against `COG-GTM/educational-platform`, but that repo has no Dockerfile; the traceability block names `COG-GTM/nodejs-goof` as the source repo and the quoted `FROM node:18.13.0` is this file.

body:
Closes #4

## What this ships

The Windows data collector, built to ADR 0001 as amended by #405.

- `src/boostgauge/collector.py` — `SystemSnapshot`, `Thresholds` (defaults are #7's, verbatim: conpty 30/60, memory 60/80, processes 300/500, handles 30000/50000), `normalize` and the normalized-max `composite` with `driver`, the `DataCollector` base, `make_collector()` platform switch, and `CollectorThread` — a daemon that polls every `interval` seconds onto a `queue.Queue`, keeps `latest`, and survives a failing tick.
- `src/boostgauge/collectors/windows.py` — `WindowsCollector`. **The sweep is one `NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation)` call**, parsed once into `(pid, name, handle_count)` rows. ConPTY count, process count and handle count are predicates over those rows. `cmdline` is read per row, via psutil, for exactly the rows the sweep identified as Python interpreters — the Unleashed session predicate (ruling #239). Memory via `psutil.virtual_memory()` (ADR 0001 §2.6).

## The four test hooks ADR 0001 §4 names, all present

| hook | test | what it pins |
|---|---|---|
| stubbed single call | `tests/unit/test_collector.py::test_all_four_metrics_from_one_sweep` | one sweep call yields 10 rows, 3 console hosts, 7205 handles, 2 sessions; `cmdline` read only for pids 201/202/203 |
| source-level pin | `tests/unit/test_collector_source_pin.py` | no `psutil.pids` / `process_iter` / `Get-Process` / WMI in any collector module; exactly one `NtQuerySystemInformation(` call site |
| live cross-check | `tests/integration/test_windows_sweep_crosscheck.py` | sweep vs psutil on the running machine: rows ±1, console hosts ±1, handles within 1 % — churn retried, not tolerated |
| benchmark | `tests/benchmark/test_sweep_cost.py` | mean CPU per full `collect()` tick < 20 ms (1 % of a core at 2 s); measured ~2 ms here |

Plus literal-value tests for `normalize` (0 → 0, 15 → 30, 30 → 60, 45 → 80, 60 → 100, clamped both ends on the conpty band), the composite's max-and-driver, tie order, and the thread's stop and error paths.

```
20 passed in 4.31s
ruff: All checks passed!
```

## Not in this PR

- #7 will feed `Thresholds` from the config file and hot-reload them; the collector already takes them as an object.
- `MacCollector` / `LinuxCollector` — `make_collector()` raises `NotImplementedError` naming the platform.

Version 0.2.0 → 0.3.0.

author: bioszombie
body:
## Summary

Allow a release to be published entirely from GitHub Actions without requiring a local Git workstation, while preserving the existing four-platform build and release pipeline.

## Manual release path

- Add a required `version` input to the existing **Build & Release** workflow.
- Manual releases must be dispatched from `master` and enter the version without the `v` prefix (for example `2.1.0`).
- All four standalone executables build and pass the existing real JPEG -> WebP verification before any release tag is created.
- Only after those builds succeed does the release job validate the requested version against `imgconvert.__version__`, verify the commit is reachable from `master`, reject duplicate tags, and create `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` on the exact workflow commit.
- The same run then generates checksums, creates provenance attestations, and publishes the GitHub Release.

## Why the same workflow publishes

GitHub suppresses most follow-on workflow events caused by the repository `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so a tag created by one workflow cannot be relied upon to start a second normal tag-push workflow. The manual path therefore creates the tag late and continues publication in the same Build & Release run. No PAT, GitHub App private key, or long-lived release secret is required.

Local version-tag pushes remain supported and use the same release publication steps.

## Concurrency

Manual releases use a separate non-cancelling concurrency group from normal `master` push builds, preventing a later push from cancelling a release after it has begun.

## Documentation

Update distribution, development, and security documentation to describe browser-driven releases, the late tag-creation invariant, duplicate-tag refusal, and the local-tag alternative.

## Validation

Source CI is green on Python 3.13, Python 3.14, and Static and dependency checks.

The Build & Release PR run is also green on Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS Intel, and macOS Apple Silicon. Each job still installs the locked toolchain, builds the one-file executable, executes the JPEG -> WebP verification contract, and uploads the temporary Actions artifact.

`Publish GitHub Release` correctly skipped on the pull-request event. The actual manual publication path becomes available only after this workflow is merged to `master`, because GitHub only accepts `workflow_dispatch` for a workflow present on the default branch.

author: briananderson1222
body:
## User outcome

The path to a Linux Station install that needs no C++ toolchain. This PR proves the delivery layout works, ships the digest-pinned staging channel and the attested CI build workflow, and records the risk decisions (glibc floor, musl, spawn-helper). It deliberately commits **no binary**: an artifact built on this contributor machine would not be attested, so the manifest ships empty and every Linux install today behaves exactly as before (compile from source). Once a maintainer runs the new workflow and lands its artifacts via the documented consuming PR, `npm run dependencies:install` on linux-x64/linux-arm64 (glibc) stages the pinned prebuild, upstream's own `scripts/prebuild.js` exits 0, and node-gyp — and therefore g++/make/python3 — is never invoked.

## Issue and closure condition

- Issue: #1245 — Closes #1245
- Closure condition satisfied by this PR: the `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/` layout is proven to work end-to-end on real hardware (the single most load-bearing claim in the issue); an attested linux-x64 + linux-arm64 build workflow exists following `release.yml`'s attestation pattern; a fail-closed, digest-pinned staging mechanism connects committed artifacts to `node_modules/node-pty`; the glibc baseline, musl decision, and spawn-helper risk are each explicitly handled; the allowlist entry reflects the prebuild channel; the named docs are updated.

**One issue premise did not survive verification:** the issue proposes placing artifacts into `prebuilds/` "via the existing `patches/` mechanism". That mechanism is patch-package, and patch-package cannot represent or apply binary-file changes (its patch parser handles text hunks, renames, and mode changes only). The digest-pinned `packaging/node-pty-prebuilds/` channel + lifecycle staging in this PR replaces that leg of the proposal; everything else in the issue's shape (no fork, no vendored package, upstream's own loader and install hook) holds and is proven below.

## Documentation impact

- Affected public docs and generated sources (exact repository-relative paths):
  - `README.md` §Install — states the Linux-only C++ toolchain requirement (previously silent) and the prebuild channel that removes it.
  - `docs/guides/development.md` — new "Source Prerequisites" section with the per-platform toolchain truth and the `npm_config_build_from_source` opt-out.
  - `CONTRIBUTING.md` §Make a change — points at those prerequisites.
  - `packaging/node-pty-prebuilds/README.md` — the artifact channel's trust chain, scope decisions, and refresh policy (new trust surface, documented at the surface).
  - `Dockerfile` — comments marking the toolchain layer as droppable once artifacts land, plus `COPY packaging/node-pty-prebuilds` so in-container staging works.
  - `docs/user/getting-started.md` is deliberately NOT touched here: PR #1257 (#1244, filed alongside) already adds the per-platform toolchain statement to §Before You Install; amending the same paragraph from a second main-based branch would only manufacture a conflict. The consuming PR that lands actual artifacts must update it (and `README.md`/`Dockerfile`) to the post-prebuild wording.
- Intentional NOT_VERIFIED platform/UI claims retained or introduced: see table.

## Evidence

### Exact commands and receipts

All local runs on Linux arm64 (Ubuntu 24.04 PRoot on Android, glibc 2.39 host), Node v24.20.0:

**The required layout proof (real hardware, real artifact):**

author: haninaguib
body:
Closes #532

## What changed

An operator with several `gh` logins on the engine host can now say which one a project acts as, from either add-project form.

- **Engine — host account listing.** New `GET /api/github/accounts` (`GhAccountsController` / `GhAccountsService` under `engine/.../github/`) returns the `github.com` accounts from `gh auth status --json hosts`, with the active flag, in gh's own order. Read per request, so an account added with `gh auth login` while the engine runs shows up on the next open. Empty list, never an error, with no accounts or no `gh`. Gated as authenticated by one new `SecurityConfig` matcher (`/api/github/**`) — the chain ends in permit-all, so without it the host's logins would be public; a `@SpringBootTest` route test proves the gate.
- **Engine — create and import.** `POST /api/projects` and `POST /api/projects/new` accept an optional `githubLogin`. When set, `ProjectCheckoutService` resolves `gh auth token --user <login>` first, stores it encrypted as the project's own token (#81), and only then proceeds: the import's `git clone` is unchanged (URL, SSH alias and key decide its identity); the create path runs `gh repo create` and the first `git push` with `GH_TOKEN` set to that token through the process environment, never on a command line. An unknown login marks the project FAILED with a WARN naming the login before any repository, clone, or workarea exists. Absent `githubLogin`, behaviour is byte-for-byte the old one; the ambient `gh auth token` fallback (#513) stays.
- **Client.** Both forms carry a "GitHub account" select fed by the new endpoint, preselecting the active login. With zero logins each form shows a `gh auth login` hint; the create button is disabled (also until the list has loaded), the import button stays enabled and the request then carries no `githubLogin` at all.

## Verified

- `GhAccountsServiceTest` (7): the reference `gh auth status` shape → logins with active flag; one login; `{"hosts":{}}`; a non-`github.com` host only; gh not runnable; unparseable output; an account without a login — the last five all yield an empty list.
- `GhAccountsControllerTest` (2) and `GhAccountsRouteIntegrationTest` (2): JSON shape; 401 unauthenticated, 200 with a login session.
- `ProjectCheckoutServiceTest` (+7, 40 total with #531's): with a stub `gh` script, import with a login stores that account's token encrypted and clones unchanged; an unknown login fails before any clone, WARN names the login with gh's real stderr wording; a blank login never invokes gh; `createRepoAndPush` with a login runs `repo create` with `GH_TOKEN` (recorded by the stub) and the push with `GH_TOKEN` (captured by a pre-receive hook in the local bare remote) and stores the token; an unknown login there creates nothing; no login runs gh with no `GH_TOKEN`. All 25 pre-existing cases unchanged.
- `ProjectControllerTest` (+2, 28 total): both endpoints forward `githubLogin`.
- Composition with #531 (`createRepoAndPushRunsTheWorkflowScopeGateOnTheChosenAccountsToken`): with a chosen account, the workflow-scope gate judges that account's token (stored first), refuses before `gh repo create`, and names the stored per-project token in its WARN.
- Client specs: 7 new popup specs (both forms list accounts and preselect the active one; one login; zero logins → hint, create disabled, import enabled with no `githubLogin`; create held disabled until loaded; chosen login sent on import and on create; failed request treated as no accounts), 3 new `ProjectsService` specs, and the three `app.component` specs that mount the popup now flush its request.

Results at this commit (rebased onto #531, PR #534): `./mvnw -B test` → BUILD SUCCESS, engine 604 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors, client 655 of 655 specs green inside the `client` module's `npm run test:ci`; `./.t-workflow/scripts/consistency-check.sh`, `check-manifest.sh`, `check-record.sh`, and the plan-gate all OK; `protected-paths.sh --stdin` over the diff exits 1 (no protected surface); `git grep GH_TOKEN -- engine/src/main` shows environment-map use only.

## Open

- Human checks from the plan: a live two-account create on real GitHub (creator and pusher are the chosen account; `gh auth status` still shows the same active account afterwards), a live import of the SSH-alias repository with the work login listing its issues, and a look at the hint wording and select placement.
- #531 (PR #534) merged to `main` mid-task and conflicted here; resolved by rebasing (seven hunks, both test-only seams now on one nine-argument constructor). In `createRepoAndPush` the chosen account's token is resolved and stored before #531's scope gate runs, so the gate judges the token the bootstrap push will actually use. Recorded in the task record's Deviations.

author: jordangrieve
body:
Two landing-page fixes. The first is a live 500 on `main`; the second is the alignment issue you spotted.

## 1. `/` was returning 500

```
@clerk/clerk-react: You've passed multiple children components to
<SignInButton/>. You can only pass a single child component or text.
```

The header and hero CTAs had the nesting inverted — `<Button asChild>` wrapping `<SignInButton>` — so Radix `Slot` handed `SignInButton` a child set it rejects. Clerk's contract is the reverse: `SignInButton` wraps exactly one child.

```diff
-<Button asChild>
-  <SignInButton forceRedirectUrl="/onboarding" />
-</Button>
+<SignInButton forceRedirectUrl="/onboarding">
+  <Button>Sign in</Button>
+</SignInButton>
```

**Why CI didn't catch it:** `/` is a dynamic route — it branches on `SignedIn`/`SignedOut` — so `next build` never renders it, and there's no e2e coverage of the public landing page. Typecheck, lint, 39 tests and the build were all green with a hard 500 on the front door. It surfaced on the first real page load.

## 2. Header didn't line up with the page

The header was full-width with `px-4` (16px gutter) while every section below used `container` (32px gutter, max 96rem), so the logo sat flush left while the hero and footer were centred and inset.

The border stays full-width — only the content is constrained now, matching the footer.

**A wider issue found while fixing it.** `container` is a custom utility in `globals.css`:

```css
@utility container {
  margin-inline: auto;
  padding-inline: 2rem;
  max-width: 96rem;
}
```

It already supplies `mx-auto` and its own padding — but every call site was written `container mx-auto px-4`, making `mx-auto` redundant and silently overriding the intended 2rem gutter down to 1rem. So *every* section was rendering a narrower gutter than the design intends. All four call sites now use `container` alone.

The hero's `max-w-3xl` also moved from the section onto an inner div: applied to the container element it was overriding `max-width` and changing the gutter, rather than just narrowing the text measure.

| Element | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<header>` | `px-4`, full-width content | border full-width, content in `container` |
| Hero `<section>` | `container mx-auto px-4 … max-w-3xl` | `container` + inner `max-w-3xl` |
| Two `<section>`s | `container mx-auto px-4` | `container` |
| `<footer>` | `container mx-auto px-4` | `container` |

## Verification

`typecheck` 0 · `lint` 0 warnings · `test` 39 passed · `build` passes, 10/10 static pages.

Verified at runtime too, which is what mattered here: dev server against real Neon + Clerk credentials, `/` returns **200** and renders. `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` 200, `/app` correctly 307s to sign-in.

## Not in this PR

The persistence/progress backend work hasn't started — this branch was originally cut for it, then re-scoped and renamed once the landing page turned out to be broken.

body:
## Summary

Adds a NixOS-codified Prometheus textfile exporter for the Satisfactory dedicated server (wolveix/satisfactory-server docker container on shikisha). Scrapes the built-in HTTPS REST API on loopback (`127.0.0.1:7777`) every 30s.

### Metrics
- **Unauthenticated** (HealthCheck): `satisfactory_up`, `satisfactory_health`, `satisfactory_api_latency_seconds`
- **Bearer token** (QueryServerState + EnumerateSessions): player count/limit, game running/paused, tick rate, session uptime, tech tier, save count + newest save timestamp

### Files
- `nixos/modules/monitoring/satisfactory-exporter.nix` — new module (systemd timer + oneshot service writing textfile metrics)
- `nixos/modules/monitoring/dashboards/satisfactory.json` — Grafana dashboard (server status, players, tick rate, latency, session uptime, save table)
- `nixos/modules/monitoring/grafana.nix` — wire dashboard + stale-save alert rule
- `nixos/shikisha.nix` — enable the exporter
- `flake.nix` — import the module for shikisha

### Security
- API is loopback-only; exporter runs on the host and reaches the container via 127.0.0.1
- Metrics exposed via the existing node-exporter textfile collector, which is already Tailscale-gated
- API token is **optional** (`services.satisfactory-exporter.apiTokenFile`); module builds cleanly without it. Wire it to a sops secret to enable admin metrics (players, saves).

### Test Plan
- Exporter script validated against a mock Satisfactory API (HealthCheck, QueryServerState, EnumerateSessions) — output confirmed valid Prometheus textfile format
- Embedded Python syntax-checked
- Dashboard JSON validated
- **Not** full `nixos-rebuild` tested (no nix toolchain in this environment) — recommend a build check on shikisha before merge

## Notes
- The docker container itself is not yet part of the NixOS config (out of scope); this PR only adds monitoring for the existing deployment.
- Data backups, NixOS-managed container migration, and a management dashboard with quick actions are tracked as separate follow-ups.

This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and publish to npm yourself or [setup this action to publish automatically](https://github.com/changesets/action#with-publishing). # Releases
## @gtbuchanan/eslint-plugin-agent-skills@1.0.0

### Major Changes

- 79c96d0: Gate skill length on tokens rather than lines

  `configs.recommended` now caps both `SKILL.md` and
  `**/skills/*/references/**/*.md` with `agent-skills/max-tokens` at 5000,
  and applies `agent-skills/max-lines` to neither. The rule still ships, so
  a repo wanting the spec's 500-line figure can wire it explicitly:

  ```js
  {
    files: ['**/skills/*/SKILL.md'],
    rules: { 'agent-skills/max-lines': ['warn', { max: 500 }] },
  }
  ```

  Both rules proxy for how much context a skill costs to load, and tokens
  measure it directly. At the ~10-14 tokens per line typical of prose
  skills, 500 lines works out to 5200-7000 tokens, so the token cap is the
  one that fires. The line cap leads only below ~10 tokens per line, where
  it reports formatting — semantic line breaks and dense lists raise a line
  count without changing what the agent loads.

  The 300-line cap on `references/` had no upstream basis: the spec's third
  tier is "Resources (as needed)" and `skill-creator` calls bundled
  resources "unlimited, loaded as needed". The 5000 there is a backstop for
  a reference file costing more to load than the instructions tier it was
  split out of.

### Patch Changes

author: 1ikeadragon
body:
Our load balancer health checks currently have to traverse the full auth chain, so every probe lands in the auth logs and adds latency to what should be a trivial liveness check. `--gcp-healthchecks` covers the GKE case but hardcodes the Google probe UA and the root path, so it is no help for anything else.

This adds `--ping-user-agent` so operators can nominate the probe identity their infrastructure actually uses. When it is set, the health check middleware answers matching probes directly instead of passing them further down the chain.

Defaults to empty, so behaviour is unchanged unless you opt in.

Verified against our staging ALB with the target group health check configured to send a custom UA. `go build ./...` passes and the new middleware tests cover both the path and user agent cases.

author: jgfoster
body:
## The defect

A `<lambda>` traceback frame underlined its **caller's** call site rather than the lambda body. The two frames sit on the same source line, so the columns are the only thing that tells them apart — and Grail gave them the same ones:

```
  File "t.py", line 8, in baz2
    return (lambda *args: foo(*args))(1,2,3,4)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^
  File "t.py", line 8, in <lambda>
    return (lambda *args: foo(*args))(1,2,3,4)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^     <-- CPython: ~~~^^^^^^^ under foo(*args)
```

A frame's span is recovered by scanning the generated Smalltalk backwards from the ip for the last `___curPos___ := #(...)` store. A lambda body is an **expression**, not a statement, so no store was emitted inside its block: the scan ran past the opening bracket to the enclosing statement's store. Every lambda in every Grail traceback was affected — sort keys, callbacks, `map`/`filter`.

## The fix, and why it is two halves

The store is both a runtime value and a source literal, so recording the lambda's span needs care in both directions:

- **Runtime.** The block declares its own `___curPos___`, **shadowing** the enclosing scope's temp. GemStone permits that (verified one and two levels deep). Without it a lambda called from inside a `try` leaves its own span standing for the frame that catches.
- **Text.** The scan knows nothing about block nesting, so a store inside `[ ... ]` is also found by every later ip in the *enclosing* frame. The enclosing store is put back after the closing bracket as a Smalltalk **comment** — `_sourceAtIp:` reports comments verbatim, and a lambda is an expression, so there is no statement position there for a real one. A line break before the `]` is load-bearing: without it the restore shares a line with the body and the body's own ip finds it. The emitted text looked correct at that point and the frame was still wrong.

Skipped where the body has no full span — a bare constant answers a nil `endLine`, and a literal the parser cannot read records nothing while still displacing the enclosing store.

Every `___curPos___` emitter now routes through `AbstractNode >> ___emitCurPosStore___:on:`, which records what it wrote, so the restore reinstates whatever was actually standing: `For`, `With` and the `except*` finish all refine the statement's store with a narrower span.

## Tests

`tests/python/lambda_frames.py` — 5 checks, agreeing with CPython 3.14.6 — driven by `PythonTests>>LambdaFrameTestCase`. Each half is covered by checks that can see it go: four fail with the restore disabled, the fifth (the catching frame) fails with the shadowing disabled. Measured both ways rather than assumed.

## Verification

Re-run in full after rebasing onto #780 (walrus in a lambda) and #782 (lazy genexp), both of which touch the same codegen. `LambdaAst.gs` conflicted with #780 on the block's temp declaration; resolved so a lambda declares its walrus targets **and** its `___curPos___`, and `lambda: (n := 1) + n` still answers 2 leaving an outer `n = 99` alone.

- `check_python_fixtures.sh`: **4664 OK / 40 XFAIL** across 291 fixtures
- `run_tests.sh`: **6321 run, 6321 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors**
- full `run_cpython_suite.sh` + `check_cpython_regressions.sh`: **0 regression(s), 1 improvement(s)** — `test.test_traceback` FAIL/6 → FAIL/3

`docs/CPython_Suite_Scoreboard.md` is left at the committed CI-measured baseline.

## Two separate defects this uncovered, not fixed here

Both are pre-existing — confirmed by reverting `LambdaAst.gs` alone and re-measuring — and both deserve their own change:

1. **A frame from another module names the catching module's file.** `___codeForMethod___` takes the filename from the catching code object, and its own comment admits it is wrong across a module boundary; PR #781 exempted `<module>` frames and nothing else. Since #781 also made `linecache` win over the embedded line, the frame now prints whatever line *N* of the *caller's* file happens to be, with a caret line under it. Any multi-module program is affected. The fix has a shape: a method's own module class knows its path.
2. **A nested `def` whose body holds a lambda is misnamed `<lambda>`.** The frame-name scan resolves a name from the line alone, and both sit on one line. Now that the two frames carry *different spans*, that is the discriminator a fix could use.

Adds «Κοιλιακοί · Ημέρα Β», a second abs block so abs can be trained on another day with different exercises instead of repeating the same routine. Rebased onto the current LiftMate main (the earlier version of this branch was written against the pre-rename codebase and conflicted).

It deliberately covers what the Bruce Lee routine leaves out:

| Exercise | Region |
|---|---|
| Άρσεις γονάτων σε κρέμαση | lower rectus, full range |
| Ανάστροφες κάμψεις | lower rectus (floor alternative) |
| Κάμψεις ποδηλασία | upper rectus + obliques |
| Πλάγια σανίδα | lateral chain, isometric |
| Pallof Press | anti-rotation — absent from the classic routine |
| Dead Bug | deep core, breathing-friendly |
| Hollow Hold | whole rectus under tension |

Each exercise carries the same fields as every other one (cue, works, how, careful, video term), so the detail sheet and technique video work unchanged.

**Generalising extra blocks from one to many**: `ABS_BLOCKS` keyed per block with `ABS_EX_ALL` for the library and muscle-group maps; `liftmate.abs` now stores an array of block keys per day, reading the legacy `1` value as the Bruce Lee block so no existing setting is lost; one toggle button per block, rendered with `sc-for`; and removal now keeps the logged sets of the remaining blocks instead of resetting the workout.

Verified in a headless browser: both buttons toggle independently, storage reads `{"fitbox|l1":["bl","b2"]}`, removing one block leaves the other's exercises in place, and the legacy `1` value still shows the Bruce Lee block enabled. Service worker cache bumped to liftmate-v4.

author: callanplays
body: ## Problem Turning Auto-Track off left the radar icon on the project row. `treeRows()` caches the built Projects rows and only rebuilds when one of its keys changes (manual `treeRevision`, parse revision, alias revision, or the house/trust/cache fingerprint). The icon's colour and tooltip are per-frame thunks, but whether the icon and its spacer exist is structural, and auto-track membership was in none of the cache keys. ## Fix Instead of another `bumpTreeRevision()` at the mutation site, the persistence store now owns a revision per document: - `PersistedValue.revision()` moves on a successful `set()`, a `reset()`, or a TTL re-read whose raw contents differ from the last read. Unchanged polls do not bump, so the 2s alias TTL causes no per-poll rebuilds. - `treeStatusFingerprint()` includes `getAutoTrackRevision()`. - `aliases.ts` drops its hand-rolled counter for the store one. This also picks up an alias edited on disk (another client, a text editor), which the old counter missed. - `readJsonSettingsFile` returns the raw text so the store can compare re-reads. Audit of every other structural input to `buildTreeRows`: house uuid, trust, cache statuses, aliases, parses are covered by the fingerprint or a revision; local UI state bumps at every mutation site; queue membership, jump flash, and auto-track paused state are thunks. Auto-track presence was the only gap. ## Tests - revision increments on a successful set and not on a failed write - TTL re-read bumps only when contents changed - `getAutoTrackRevision()` moves on `toggleAutoTrackSource` ## Verification - `npm test`: 713 passed, 1 skipped; `npm run verify` and `npm run build` clean - Live in the Prism 1.8.9 instance: icon appears instantly on enable and disappears instantly on disable, no `/ct reload` between Note: `git diff` shows `store.ts` as binary because of a pre-existing stray `\0` byte in the file; `git diff -a` shows the change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

## Summary
- `DispatchConfig` gains `dispatch.tiers.<tier>` — a full spawn spec (`{command?, model?, prompt?}`) per escalation tier, so `mechanical`/`mid`/`strong` can each run a different agent CLI (e.g. `opencode` for the cheap tiers, `claude` as the rescue tier), not just a different `--model` flag on one shared template.
- `resolveDispatch` pre-resolves every tier once per tick; any field a tier's spec leaves unset falls back to the existing `command`/`tier_models`/`prompt` shorthand — a pre-#527 config with no `tiers` key resolves identically to before (no on-disk migration, resolution-time fallback only). Config schema moves to 1.4.0, 1.3.0 remains loadable.
- The stall/escalation ladder (`enterRecovery`) now redispatches with the NEXT tier's own resolved command, so a unit can start on one CLI+model and be rescued on a different CLI+model.
- `JournalEvent` gains typed `cmd`/`model`/`log` fields; `spawned`/`redispatched`/`fix-dispatched`/the batch report-agent's `report-dispatched` events all record the actual agent binary and model used. `runs.jsonl`'s per-dispatch entry sources the same tier-resolved command/model.
- `cli/src/commands/sched.ts`'s `start` skips claude/opencode auto-detect once `dispatch.tiers` is configured (with a diagnostic warning when that would silently fall back to the built-in claude template for an unconfigured tier).

Closes #527

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1 `dispatch.tiers` allows a full spawn spec per tier; `tier_models` + top-level `command` remain valid as the shorthand and migrate transparently — met `packages/sched/src/types.ts:479,507`, `packages/sched/src/dispatch.ts:366-381` (`resolveTierDispatch`)
- [x] AC2 The ladder redispatches with the next tier's own command — met `packages/sched/src/engine.ts` (`enterRecovery`'s `redispatched` journal + `spawnUnit` reading `ctx.dispatch.tiers[entry.tier]` via `resolveTierSpawn`)
- [x] AC3 `spawned`/`redispatched` journal events and `runs.jsonl` entries record both agent CLI and model — met `packages/sched/src/types.ts` (`JournalEvent.cmd`/`.model`), `packages/sched/src/engine.ts` (`recordDispatchRunLog`)
- [x] AC4 Report/mechanical tier can point at the cheapest CLI+model independently of mid/strong — met `packages/sched/src/engine.ts` (`spawnReportAgent` via `resolveTierSpawn(ctx.dispatch, tier, issue)`)
- [x] AC5 Tests: config migration; a fake two-CLI ladder in the integration harness — met `packages/sched/src/__tests__/persist.test.ts` (round-trip + migration), `packages/sched/src/__tests__/integration.test.ts` (real two-CLI ladder: mid dies, strong completes), `packages/sched/src/__tests__/engine.test.ts` (unit-level two-CLI ladder + per-tier prompt wiring)

## Test plan

- 7-agent tiered review (DRY, Security, Supportability, Maintainability, Documentation, Convention/Contract, Conformance) ran on the full diff; 10 findings applied (incl. wiring a previously-dead per-tier `prompt` override into the actual spawn path), 0 escalated

Repairs **CERT-678 (BLOCK, strike one)** on `158b2232`.

> The cue appears only on EventCard and generic FuturesCard Variant A. Threshold, leaderboard, Variant B, and ComparisonCard paths remain silently personalized with no explanation. Helper tests pass 33/33 and build/typecheck/identity/merge hygiene pass, but **there is no render-path guard**.

## What changed

**The cue now reaches eight paths** — the four the block named (threshold heatmap, outcome-distribution leaderboard, FuturesCard Variant B, ComparisonCard) plus two it did not:

- **GuessCard** — `app/discover/page.tsx:1338` renders `<GuessCard item={gi.item!}/>` *instead of* `<DiscoverCard>` for a guess slot. That is a real feed position holding the same personalized item every other card gets.
- **FuturesCompactRow** — `_public_member_item` strips only underscore keys, so bundle members keep `personalized`/`multiplier`/`personalization_reasons`.

**The render-path guard** (`__tests__/components/forYouCueRenderPaths.test.tsx`, 94 assertions) has two halves:

- **Part 1 — behaviour.** All eight paths rendered three times each: boosted (cue present), downranked (cue absent — the original defect), anonymous (absent). Each case asserts the marker of the path it *meant* to render.
- **Part 2 — enumeration from source.** Every item-taking component, every `<article>` root inside them individually, every dispatch destination, and cross-stack: the item types `feed.py` marks `personalized` are exactly `{event, futures}`. Every scan raises rather than passing when it cannot parse.

**Mutation battery** — 11 applied, 11 killed, control green (`artifacts-ux-p252/mutation_battery.sh`, rsync copy, needle count asserted before each write, restore verified by md5). Mutants **I** (a fifth uncovered `<article>` root) and **K** (`feed.py` personalizes a `tournament` item) attack the *enumeration* rather than a call site already covered by Part 1.

Unchanged: UX-P248's two-condition rule (`multiplier > 1` **and** a nameable positive reason). Mutants G and H prove it stays fixed on all eight paths.

body:
## Descrição

Fecha a issue #132. `docs/architecture.md` §13 foi escrita pela issue #39
antes do deploy real acontecer no Railway (backend) e na Vercel (frontend).
Esta PR atualiza a seção com o resultado real e três problemas descobertos
e verificados ao vivo durante o provisionamento desta sessão.

Closes #132

## Mudanças Realizadas

- Marca a seção como refletindo um deploy já feito, não mais um roteiro
  hipotético.
- **Volume do Postgres:** monta-lo direto em `/var/lib/postgresql/data`
  trava o `initdb` num loop de crash (`lost+found` de um volume novo não é
  diretório vazio) — documentado o fix (`PGDATA` num subdiretório do
  volume).
- **`railway up --path-as-root`:** publicar assim a partir da raiz do repo
  excluiu `app/storage/` silenciosamente do build (interação ruim com
  `.gitignore`), mesmo com `.dockerignore` correto — documentado o comando
  confiável (`cd backend && railway up`, sem a flag).
- **`railway run` não alcança o banco:** ele roda localmente, não dentro do
  container — não resolve `*.railway.internal`. Corrigido tanto na seção de
  seed (que já citava o comando errado) quanto na de migrations manuais
  (mesmo erro, nunca antes exercitado de verdade) — o comando certo é
  `railway ssh`.
- **Imagem Docker customizada de Postgres:** ao contrário do addon oficial
  do Railway, não gera `PGHOST`/`PGUSER`/`DATABASE_URL` sozinha — documentado
  como compor e registrar a `DATABASE_URL` manualmente.
- **Rewrite de SPA:** menciona `frontend/vercel.json`, sem o qual
  `/r/:qrToken` (o link do QR Code físico) dá 404 direto no CDN da Vercel.
- Remove a linguagem de "passo pendente/manual" de `VITE_API_BASE_URL` e
  `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` — já estão configurados de verdade.

## Impacto

Documentação apenas — nenhum código alterado.

## Validação

- `/code-review` (mínimo exigido para mudança trivial) rodado duas vezes:
  a primeira revisão pegou uma contradição real entre a seção nova de Seed
  e a seção existente de Migrations (as duas usavam `railway run`, que não
  funciona) — corrigida antes deste commit.
- Cada claim nova foi verificada ao vivo contra o projeto Railway real
  durante esta sessão (não é suposição): reproduzi o crash do Postgres, a
  correção com `PGDATA`, o `ModuleNotFoundError` do `--path-as-root`, e
  confirmei que remover a variável `PORT` do serviço do backend não quebra
  nada (a claim original da doc sobre isso já estava certa).

## Observações

Sem dependência de outra PR. Sem risco de deploy (só documentação).

author: zcsizmadia
body:
Implements the core of #39: one long-lived `hawser supervise` process owning both the pipe server and an engine reconciler, with `start/stop/restart/status` as real commands. `hawser proxy` stays as foreground debug mode.

**Desired-state driven, and that''s the design decision worth reviewing.** `hawser stop` records intent in a file the loop honors — without it, the health loop would helpfully restart the engine the user just stopped. A file rather than a control socket because it also works when no supervisor is running, which is exactly when `hawser start` needs somewhere to leave its instruction. Corrupt state fails toward *running*: an engine silently kept down reads as "Hawser is broken."

**Crash recovery verified on real WSL, zero clicks:**

```
wsl --terminate hawser-sup
engine right after kill:      stopped
engine after supervisor tick: running
docker version               -> server 29.7.2
```

Sleep/resume needs no special handling *by construction* — a resumed machine fails the next health check and is repaired like any crash. Backoff is exponential (2s→60s cap) so a crash loop can''t hammer WSL, and resets on observed health.

**Boundaries, from the #35 incident:** stop terminates only Hawser''s own distro; there is deliberately no wider primitive. Single instance via a per-install named mutex (`Local\`, hashed state dir) — the OS releases it if the process dies, which is the property a PID file can''t offer without staleness heuristics.

**One bug found by running it** (the sixteenth this project has caught that way): `runStart` resolved the install''s distro to verify it exists, then discarded it — so it polled the *default* distro name and reported a timeout while `hawser status` said running. Plus one self-inflicted lesson: you can''t rebuild a binary that''s currently running as your own supervisor.

13 new tests; **the 13-stage acceptance suite is still green end to end** with the supervisor in the tree.

**Deliberately deferred within #39:** autostart-at-logon (registering logon tasks without a console flash has real Windows subtleties worth a focused change) and the Event Log sink.

author: cameronfreer
body:
A Borel `G ⊆ X × Y` with at most one `y` above each `x` names a partial function. This packages the standard facts about it — Borel domain, measurable partial value map — so consumers never restate the argument.

```lean
structure BorelFunctionalGraph (G : Set (X × Y)) : Prop where
  measurableSet_graph : MeasurableSet G
  functional : ∀ {x y z}, (x, y) ∈ G → (x, z) ∈ G → y = z
```

The mathematics is Mathlib's — Lusin–Souslin — so the contribution is the reusable boundary, not a new theorem.

### Borel domain

```lean
theorem measurableSet_domain (h : BorelFunctionalGraph G) : MeasurableSet h.domain :=
  h.measurableSet_graph.image_of_measurable_injOn measurable_fst h.injOn_fst
```

No subtype is involved. `MeasurableSet.image_of_measurable_injOn` asks for `InjOn`, and `InjOn Prod.fst G` *is* the functionality hypothesis — `injOn_fst` is the one-step translation.

### The projection is a measurable embedding

```lean
theorem measurableEmbedding_proj (h : BorelFunctionalGraph G) : MeasurableEmbedding (proj G)
```

Restricting the projection to `↥G` turns `injOn_fst` into the global injectivity required by `Measurable.measurableEmbedding`; `MeasurableSet.standardBorel` supplies the standard-Borel structure on `↥G`. This is where the subtype enters, and not before.

### `equivDomain`, with a transparent forward map

```lean
noncomputable def equivDomain (h : BorelFunctionalGraph G) : ↥G ≃ᵐ ↥h.domain
```

Built explicitly with a transparent forward map, so the forward coercion is definitionally the projection; measurability of the inverse comes from `MeasurableEmbedding.measurable_rangeSplitting`.

```lean
theorem coe_equivDomain (h : BorelFunctionalGraph G) (p : ↥G) :
    ((h.equivDomain p : ↥h.domain) : X) = proj G p := rfl
```

That `rfl` is what the value specifications below rest on.

### The value map, identified

```lean
noncomputable def value (h : BorelFunctionalGraph G) (x : ↥h.domain) : Y
theorem measurable_value  (h : BorelFunctionalGraph G) : Measurable h.value
theorem value_mem         (h : BorelFunctionalGraph G) (x : ↥h.domain) : ((x : X), h.value x) ∈ G
theorem value_eq_of_mem   (h : BorelFunctionalGraph G) {x : ↥h.domain} {y : Y}
    (hy : ((x : X), y) ∈ G) : h.value x = y
```

`measurable_value` alone would not be usable: a measurable map with no stated relation to `G` identifies nothing. `value_mem` says the selected value is the one the graph names; `value_eq_of_mem` is uniqueness in the form callers actually apply, and follows from `functional` once `value_mem` exists.

### Hypotheses

```lean
[MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y] [StandardBorelSpace Y]
```

Both standard-Borel instances are needed: one for countable separation of the target, and both together for the product `X × Y` that Lusin–Souslin takes as its source. The purely combinatorial lemmas `omit` them.

### Boundary

Deliberately **not** included:

- no `X → Option Y` and no junk-valued totalization — both derive from the subtype form, and which one is wanted should be fixed by the eventual unique-expansion / functional-graph consumer, not guessed now;
- no model theory — the only import is `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.Basic`;
- no blueprint node — with no consumer yet, the mathematical role this plays is not yet settled.

### Verification

- `lake build InfinitaryLogic InfinitaryLogic.Everything :blueprint :blueprintJson InfinitaryLogicWIP` — 2758 jobs.
- All 15 discovered guards + `checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`.
- Warning gate: 5 allowlisted, all still present; the new module is warning-free. Headline axioms standard-clean.
- Sorry-free.

**Release impact: additive — the next release is v4.1.0.** Nothing existing changes; `Descriptive` gains one module.

Does not close any issue.

author: ktautkus-svg
body: ## Why On live Cloud Run PWA (main at ~49636a5, tree restored to `e4e534b` via #24), **Dokumentų importas / Importuoti maršrutą** shows: `Error: Error code 1: cannot rollback - no transaction is active` Clients that already migrated through courtyard park-memory may still have `user_version` 28 and/or a leftover explicit transaction from the original BEGIN-wrapped v28 blob. Current main expects schema 27 and expo-sqlite’s `withTransactionAsync` always runs `ROLLBACK` in `catch` even when no transaction is active ([expo/expo#49281](https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/49281)), so the real failure is replaced by this SQLite noise. ## Root cause **(A) + (C)** — not nested app-level transactions as the primary bug. 1. **expo-sqlite always ROLLBACKs in catch.** If `BEGIN` failed (leftover txn) or the task already `COMMIT`ted, `ROLLBACK` throws `cannot rollback - no transaction is active` and masks the original error. Import’s `ExcelImportRepository.savePreview` and `CreateDraftRouteWithStops` both use `withTransactionAsync`. 2. **Leftover schema 28 after #24.** `migrateDatabase` currently throws when `user_version > 27`. Partial v28 also left `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` without `COMMIT`. ## What this does - Keep `SCHEMA_VERSION` at **27**. No courtyard park-memory, no v28 migration blob. - Treat **28** as a compatible leftover: open the DB, leave unused `location_park_memory` / `park_*` columns on disk, do not read or write them. - On open: install a safe `withTransactionAsync` (BEGIN outside try; ROLLBACK only if a transaction is active; recover leftover nested BEGIN) and abort an orphan transaction. - Web import writes stay serialized (Codex `4d16657`): the queue now runs through `withSafeTransactionAsync` + `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. - Google routing spend-control changes from `4f8b5f3` are kept as-is. - `ensureRouteReturnColumns` uses idempotent ALTERs instead of nested `withTransactionAsync`. - Strip unused `park_*` columns from PWA backup/restore and cloud snapshots so schema-27 peers do not fail INSERT. ## Rebase Rebased onto latest `origin/main` (`4d16657`). Conflict was only `src/database/migrations.ts` install hooks; both installers are kept. ## What this does not do - Does not restore courtyard GPS park-memory (#21/#22), Google auth harden, or the steering-frame commit. - Does not change routing scoring or revert spend controls. ## Site data After this lands, leftover-v28 PWA clients should import **without clearing site data**. A hard refresh may still be needed to pick up the new JS bundle. ## Verification (after rebase) - `npx tsc --noEmit` passed - Focused + Codex regression tests: **7 files, 51 passed** (`sqlite-transaction`, `legacy-schema-compat`, `serialized-web-transactions`, `route-snapshot-apply`, `service-rate-limit`, `cache-security`, `cloud-run-deploy`)

author: pkloehn1
body:
Closes #131
Closes #142

PR4 of CP1 per [docs/ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/paragon-stats/paragon-stats/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md), and the last one: **merging this cuts v0.4.0 and completes the Parsing engine milestone.**

The PRD has claimed since day one that the logs are the source of truth and everything is recomputable from them. Nothing tested it. Recalculation *is* re-running the fold — there is no second recompute engine and there will not be one — so what #131 needs is not a feature but a proof, and the proof found a defect.

### The defect

`SessionTracker` sorted sessions with an unstable `List.Sort` keyed on `Start` alone. Sessions sharing a start second could come back in either order, and that is ordinary input: a pulse-opened sliver and the banner behind it land in the same second (the operator's own character-swap capture produced exactly that), as do back-to-back relogs. Small runs hid it — introsort falls back to a stable insertion sort at ≤16 elements — but a 906-session corpus does not.

It also made the engine's central claim untestable: batch closes sessions a file at a time, live watch closes them interleaved per tick, so the same lines produced two different session lists depending on how they arrived.

**The only production change in this PR** is the sort key: start, then account, then character, then open order. The first three are properties of the content, so order never depends on which file or tick delivered a session; open order is only consulted within one account, where it is identical on both paths. Comparison is ordinal — `Comparer<string>.Default` is culture-sensitive and would have traded one nondeterminism for a machine-dependent one.

### Acceptance criteria, each with the test that discharges it

| AC (from #131) | Test |
|---|---|
| Recalculation is re-running the fold, no separate engine | no new engine exists; `LogReplayer.Replay` builds a fresh tracker per call |
| Determinism, field by field | `Two_replays_of_the_same_files_are_identical_field_by_field` |
| Order independence across unrelated accounts | `Unrelated_accounts_interleaving_does_not_change_the_result` |
| Live equals replay | `Live_watch_reproduces_the_batch_replay_of_the_same_logs` and `Live_watch_matches_batch_when_the_logs_arrive_in_pieces` |
| On-demand recalculation from the CLI, nothing cached | `Cli_rerun_recomputes_from_disk_with_no_cached_state` |
| (ordering contract itself) | `Sessions_sharing_a_start_second_order_by_account_then_character_then_open_order` — 18 tied sessions, past the insertion-sort fallback |

No new CLI surface: batch replay already re-reads disk and folds from scratch, so a `--recalculate` flag would be a synonym for the default and would imply the plain run serves something cached.

### Review wave (four blind lenses at frozen `36ef756`: correctness, pattern cohesion, security, product)

The correctness lens found a real hole in the guarantee this PR closes CP1 on. A tailer stops at 50,000 lines per poll; the watcher polled every file each tick, so an account with a backlog on an older log had its **newer** log read first, folding late lines into the wrong session (the idle-close guard cannot catch them - the time delta is negative). Reachable by starting `--watch` shortly after midnight rollover following a >50k-line farming day. Measured before the fix on the new regression test: **50,103 experience instead of 51,000**. Fixed by having the tailer report `HasMore` and the watcher hold an account's newer files back until the older one catches up; other accounts keep streaming.

Also folded in: ordinal comparison now spelled the codebase's way, the case-insensitive-keys vs case-sensitive-sort nuance documented, both same-second tie pairs named, the CLI fixture corrected to keep per-account chronology, README precision (`no computed results are cached` - config.json does persist the game-root *path*), and each equivalence test now says whether it carries the ordering claim or is plumbing.

Accepted with reasoning rather than fixed: `Sequence` int overflow (needs 2^31 sessions; the process OOMs first), sort CPU on a crafted many-session file (introsort bound, and the sort runs only when `Sessions` is read - the 500ms watch loop reads `Open`), and the note that these tests are not *policy* tests (a symmetric collection regression would pass them - `MaliciousLogTests` remains that guard).

One disclosure the earlier body omitted: this branch also carries commit `0995d65`, which re-encodes `MaliciousLogTests.cs` - raw ESC/BEL/NUL bytes replaced with C# escapes so the file stops being a binary blob to git and diffs normally. Same assertions, verified byte-for-byte equivalent.

## Evidence
- 177 tests green (8 new); **no existing test needed editing** — the same-second regression anchor in `RobustnessTests` stayed green untouched.
- 100% line coverage held; `dotnet format` clean.

author: drokhinson
body:
## Why

Six things using the importer turned up, plus the onboarding step that tells anyone it exists.

## 1 · First-run gains a fourth slide

The importer was invisible to a new account — you'd have to open Settings for no reason to find it — and first-run is the one screen everybody passes through. Purely informational: no fields, no write, one **Continue**.

Placed **after** Link BoardGameGeek, and that's the point: someone who just tapped Skip there because they don't use BGG is exactly who a note importer is for.

The deck's panel count used to live in **four** places — the track width, the transform, and `.ob-slide`'s width *and* flex-basis in CSS — so adding a slide meant changing all four or watching the track settle on two half-slides. It's now one `PANELS` array whose length drives the width, the transform, and an `--ob-panels` custom property the stylesheet reads. The two duplicated slide-order literals collapsed into that same array.

## 2 · The run card no longer flips, and now looks like a stack

A flip promises a scorecard, and a run of identical plays has none to show — that's its whole claim. Tapping opens a sheet instead, which is where the one thing you can do with a run lives.

**Losing the flip is what fixed the crisscross.** The edges were `inset: 6px -5px -5px 6px; z-index: -1`, which pulls the top and left borders *inward* so they draw across the face — and the z-index couldn't push them back, because `.play-card__inner` is `transform-style: preserve-3d` and so makes its own stacking context. Hence borders crossing the card rather than a stack behind it. They're now same-size copies of the card translated down-right under an opaque front, with `transform-style: flat`, which costs nothing once nothing rotates.

The caption reads as a sentence — **"You won all 58"**, not "Won all 58 You". It's one flex child, because `.win` is `inline-flex` with a 5px gap and a bare span would render the name and the rest as two items with that gap between them.

## 3 · Deleting an import, at two levels (migration `006`)

`import_batch_id` joins 005's `import_group_id` — one per **import**, one per **run** — because there are two different regrets:

| Regret | Unit | Where |
|---|---|---|
| "That run is wrong" | the run | its own card's sheet |
| "That whole parse was wrong" | the import | a new Settings list |

The second can't be expressed as a series of run deletions, since an import also writes one-offs that carry no group at all.

Both RPCs are owner-scoped in their `WHERE` clause and report `deleted: 0` rather than 403ing — saying "not yours" would confirm somebody else's batch exists. `imported_at` is stamped server-side; a client clock is the one value here nobody should have to trust.

`bgb_feed_plays` also returns `import_group_id` now. 005 returned the *count* without the id, which let the feed say "58 plays" and gave it no way to act on them.

## 4 · You can be one of the players

`GET /play-partners` returns buddies and ghosts and **never the viewer**, because every other caller has already seated them — in Gather you're at the table by construction. In the importer you're not, so a note recording your own name had no way to become you, and every imported play landed with the importer absent from their own history and, worse, from their own wins.

The viewer is now the first candidate, labelled **You**, and their own display name auto-matches before any buddy is considered.

## 5 · A run's size is editable — in review, before the write

A misread tally is cheapest to fix while it's still a draft. Growing clones the run's first play with a fresh id (which *is* the `client_key`, so an added play is a new play, not a duplicate of one already sent); the anchor is never the row removed, so correcting 58 → 44 → 46 doesn't close the row being edited each time.

## Verification

**SQL was run, not read** — baseline + `003`–`006` into a scratch Postgres 16, then a fixture of two batches, two runs, one-offs, live plays, and a second user's import:

- Deleting a run removed exactly its 5 rows and took their `play_players` with them (27 → 22 seats).
- Deleting the batch removed the remaining 5 and left the live plays and the other batch alone.
- Stats fell 20 → 15 → 10, by exactly the deleted counts.
- The other user's 7 rows were untouchable — both calls reported `0`.
- `bgb_list_imports` named the right games and counts per batch.
- `bgb_log_play` stamps the batch and `imported_at` for an import, and neither for a live log.

**Browser at 390×844, both themes** — 46 assertions across three suites:

- **Deck (13):** walks five panels, every offset a whole multiple of 20%, counter reads Step 4 of 4 then All set, Back hidden on step 1 and the finale only, the slide fires no request, the skipped-everything ledger line still holds.
- **Stack (18):** no back face, doesn't flip, opens its sheet, delete gated by the confirm surface and cancel deletes nothing, edges card-sized and offset down-right only, no 3D context — **screenshot-inspected in both themes**; an ordinary card still flips.
- **Importer (15):** the viewer auto-maps and is the first "You" candidate, run resizing grows/shrinks/clamps without dropping its anchor, and the payload carries one shared batch id across all chunks with unique `client_key`s.

**Not run here:** migration `006` still needs applying in the Supabase SQL Editor, and the parse path still hasn't hit live Gemini (no key in this environment).

## Docs

`STRUCTURE.md` (data model, endpoints, screen flow, header entry), `db/schema/boardgamebuddy.sql`, `db/functions/boardgamebuddy.sql`.

body:
## Summary
CI-8 of `docs/changes/web-frontend/plan.md`. Closes #126.

## Files
- `TaskForm.tsx` — create/edit, React Hook Form + Zod, mirroring `docs/openapi.yaml`'s request constraints exactly. `priority`'s `""` is the server's own "not specified"/"leave unchanged" sentinel — never sent explicitly: an untouched field is omitted from the body entirely (tested: the request body literally has no `priority` key when none was chosen). A `409` redisplays the same form with a generic conflict message, with the user's own edits still intact — no diff UI, since `Task.Version` is `json:"-"` server-side (per `context.md`'s finding), so there's nothing to diff against.
- `TaskStatusControls.tsx` — mirrors `internal/task/service.go`'s `legalTransitions` table client-side to disable illegal buttons, **and still handles a real `409`** from the server on a click the mirror itself considered legal — tested by deliberately faking exactly that mismatch (a stale-mirror scenario, e.g. another tab moved the task first). Disabling illegal buttons is a UX nicety, never a substitute for the server remaining the authority.
- `TaskItem.tsx` — **not in CI-8's file list**, a necessary decomposition of what `TaskList` would otherwise carry entirely itself (display + status controls + edit modal + delete confirm modal), same kind of documented deviation as CI-6's `RequireAuth`/`App.test.tsx`. Delete confirmation is a real modal that **blocks the DELETE request until explicitly confirmed** — tested that zero requests fire before the confirm click, not just that a dialog renders.
- `TaskList.tsx` — wires `TaskItem` per row, a "New task" entry point (available even in the empty state, so creating the first task isn't blocked by it), and one success `Toast` surface shared across create/update/delete — issue #126's own added criterion ("feedback de sucesso em toda mutação"), beyond `plan.md`'s literal text.
- `useTasks.tsx` gains `addTaskLocally`/`updateTaskLocally`/`removeTaskLocally` — every mutation response already carries the updated `Task`, so patching the array in place avoids throwing away pagination state a full `reload()` after every edit would lose.

## The three things plan.md/#126 explicitly asked to prove
1. **Illegal transitions are disabled, and a real `409` is still handled anyway.** Two separate, both-tested claims — a disabled button proves the mirror; a deliberately-faked `409` on a click the mirror considered legal proves the server stays the authority.
2. **Delete requires explicit confirmation, not a toast-with-undo.** Tested directly: opening the confirm dialog fires zero requests; only the dialog's own Delete button does.
3. **`priority` is never sent as `""`.** Tested by inspecting the actual serialized request body.

## Verification
```
npm run typecheck    # clean
npm run lint           # clean (2 accepted warnings, both pre-existing from CI-6/CI-7 —
                        # useAuth.tsx's Fast-Refresh note and useTasks.tsx's fetch-on-mount note)
npm run test            # 158/158
npm run build             # clean
```
Also: built the app for real, served via `vite preview`, reached over real HTTP (200).

body:
## Summary
- Release Markdown preview responders (Cmd+F find field/field editor, text editor, and preview WebView) when the panel leaves the focused pane.
- Invalidate deferred Markdown find-focus requests at the same panel lifecycle boundary so a stale overlay cannot reclaim first responder after a pane switch, hide, or close.
- Keep the existing `BrowserPanel` responder-yield path for the diff viewer find bar, with focused coverage for both viewers.

## Why this is the shared boundary
`Panel.unfocus()` is already invoked by the workspace and Dock selection transactions used by directional/index keyboard focus, pointer selection, CLI focus-pane/surface operations, split/move, replacement, and close paths. `MarkdownPanel.unfocus()` now owns the Markdown-specific responder invariant: when this panel is left, no Markdown find field/field editor, text editor, or preview WebView remains the AppKit first responder. The fix is not in one shortcut handler. `BrowserPanel.unfocus()` provides the corresponding path for browser and diff-viewer content.

## Validation
- Test-first commit: [`849148a017`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/commit/849148a017). The original test-only red proof is [E2E run 33499320678](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/33499320678), which failed on the intended responder-handoff assertions.
- Fix commit: [`652bb80c4c`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/commit/652bb80c4cf4d41adf81d81298858d98c8211db8).
- Hosted focused responder suite [E2E run 33604063491](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/33604063491) passed all three tests, and tagged build [reload-build run 33604063843](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/33604063843) passed on the immediately preceding synchronized fix SHA (`dd618176b4`). The current synchronized HEAD is `652bb80c4cf4d41adf81d81298858d98c8211db8`; no additional build was started in this continuation per the stop-at-CI-green instruction.
- Full CI dispatch [33615068658](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/33615068658) passed migrations, workflow guards, sidecar, React, and related gates but failed only in the pre-existing web-test baseline (Freestyle shell-repair/pricing/supervisor tests). Those unrelated TypeScript/test fixes were intentionally not imported into this Swift/AppKit PR.
- `./scripts/check-pbxproj.sh`, `./scripts/lint-pbxproj-test-wiring.sh`, `python3 scripts/check-package-resolved-policy.py`, and `git diff --check` pass. The test wiring lint checked 739 test files.
- `cmuxTests/PaneFocusFindResponderTests.swift` is 222 lines; `Sources/Panels/MarkdownPanel.swift` is 751 lines. The requested `scripts/swift_file_length_budget.py` and `.github/swift-file-length-budget.tsv` are absent from current main (removed upstream), so no budget file was created or changed. `.github/swift-warning-budget.tsv` was not touched.
- No user-facing strings or shortcuts were added, so localization and shortcut registries require no changes. Visual CUA typed-keystroke evidence remains unavailable because the fleet host lacked the required Accessibility/Screen Recording permission; the in-process AppKit responder tests directly assert the first-responder invariant.

## Trade-offs
- The invariant stays at the existing `@MainActor` panel lifecycle boundary, which keeps keyboard, pointer, CLI, split, and close entrypoints on one path. The cost is a bounded AppKit window/responder-chain lookup during focus transitions.
- The regression tests use deterministic in-process AppKit/WebKit responders instead of a pixel-only UI test; this verifies the exact responder state without adding timing sleeps. The prior hosted run proves the suite executes; a fresh post-rebase build is intentionally deferred.
- The full CI baseline failures are reported rather than masked or repaired with unrelated web changes; this leaves the PR blocked by repository-wide baseline health until that upstream work lands.

## Review status
- Both CodeRabbit inline threads are replied to and resolved; the single audit table is [comment 5505131905](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/pull/11512#issuecomment-5505131905), re-checked against the current HEAD.
- The PR is conflict-free/mergeable, with `lawrencecchen` review still requested. This continuation stops before merge and before another build.
