author: key4ng
body:
## Description

### Problem

Every K3 tool call whose parameter schema uses `$ref` fails with a 500.

Each argument of a K3 tool call is compiled as its own standalone grammar document, but `build_args_format` embedded each property's subschema on its own while the `$defs` block stayed at the root of the tool's parameter schema. A `$ref` such as `#/$defs/Node` is a pointer from the root of the document it appears in, so once the subschema was lifted out the pointer dangled and the grammar compiler rejected the **entire tool call**:

```
json_schema_converter.cc:3370: Cannot find field $defs in #/$defs/Node
  xgrammar/grammar.py:365 from_structural_tag
→ ValueError: Invalid structural tag specification.
→ SMG: {"code":"start_generation_failed"}
```

`grep '$defs' crates/tool_parser/src/parsers/kimi_k3.rs` returned nothing before this change.

A second, quieter symptom: a property that is *only* a local `$ref` carries no `type`, so it fell through to the permissive shape and the argument was left completely unconstrained.

### Solution

Introduce `RootDefs`, carrying the `$defs` / `definitions` blocks alongside the parameter schema, used in two places:

- **Attach** the blocks to any subschema embedded as a `json_schema` grammar, so local pointers inside it still resolve. A subschema that carries its own block keeps it, and only schemas that actually reference something pay the extra bytes.
- **Resolve** a property that is nothing but a local `$ref`, so it is typed and constrained by the definition it names. Resolution follows a single hop, which keeps a `$ref` cycle from looping; a recursive definition still compiles because the block travels with the schema for the compiler to expand.

Both `$defs` (2020-12) and `definitions` (draft-07) are supported, the `$dynamicRef` / `$recursiveRef` spellings pull the block across too, pointers into a definition subpath such as `#/$defs/group/items` resolve, and a pointer with nothing to resolve against falls back to the permissive shape rather than emitting a grammar the compiler will reject.

Note that the second bullet is a strict tightening rather than part of the crash fix — the minimal fix is the attachment alone. It is covered by tests, but happy to drop it if reviewers would rather keep this PR to the bug.

## Test Plan

- `cargo +nightly fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p tool-parser --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test -p tool-parser` — 26 suites pass, including 9 new cases covering nested refs in array items, bare-`$ref` properties, recursive definitions, definition-subpath pointers, draft-07 `definitions`, `$dynamicRef`, ref-free schemas left unpadded, and dangling refs.

**End-to-end against the real grammar compiler.** The walle validator cases that the [Kimi-Vendor-Verifier](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier) runs were wrapped exactly as its own `wrap_schema_as_parameter_property` wraps them (which lifts the case's `$defs` to the wrapper root and nests the body under `properties.value` — the shape that triggers this bug), fed through `build_structural_tag`, and compiled with xgrammar:

| | Grammars compiled | Failed |
|---|---:|---:|
| before | 382 / 424 | **42** |
| after | 424 / 424 | **0** |

42 fixed, 0 newly broken. The failing suites match those observed against a live deployment — TestReferences (18), TestEnforcerCases (16), TestNestedDefsDepth (4), TestRefInProperties (2), TestRequired (2).

For context, the live run of `tests/tool_call_json_schema` against Kimi-K3 on SMG + vLLM 0.27.1 (gRPC) reported 368 passed / 40 failed, and every one of those 40 failures was this defect.

author: alexdross
body:
## What was actually wrong

`npm run test:api` failed 2 of 197 assertions on `origin/main` @ `a3f6bdd`, both in `tests/api/rpc-seed.test.mjs` (lines 252 and 262), both `expected 194 to be 167`.

**These were stale hard-coded corpus counts, not a persistence defect.** They were the only two transcribed cardinalities left in that suite; every other count already derived from `seedCorpus.mjs`. `src/roiData.js`, `src/upcomingData.js` and `src/propPicksData.js` are bundled *live* data and are the sole inputs to `migrateV0ToV1`, so the corpus grew as `main` kept refreshing them after Gate 3. `main` had already fixed this same class of staleness in the offline contract suite (`53a1066`, "Make repository contract tests data-driven"); the API suite never followed, because nothing in CI ran it.

No SQL, migration, RLS policy, RPC, repository, domain rule or application data was touched. The production bundle is byte-identical before and after this change.

## Proof it is not a persistence defect

All **194** stored computed-profit rows recomputed through `app_private.settlement_for` — the same function grading uses in production, not a reimplementation written to agree:

```
rows=194  value_mismatches=0  bit_mismatches=0  max_deviation=0  union_mismatches=0
outcome split: won=118, lost=73, void=2, push=1
```

Zero value mismatches, zero `float8send` bit mismatches, maximum deviation exactly `0`, zero settlement-union mismatches.

## Current harness corpus

Derived independently in JavaScript from the bundled data and cross-measured in PostgreSQL after a clean seed; the two agree exactly.

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| events | 21 |
| bouts · prediction runs · assessments · tracked positions | 205 each |
| prediction snapshots | 327 |
| market snapshots | 204 |
| props | 11 |
| migrated parlays | 0 (by design — see below) |
| seed-ledger roots | 216 |
| graded / pending runs | 195 / 10 |
| computed-profit rows | 194 |
| uncomputable settled rows | 1 |

Internally consistent: 195 + 10 = 205 · 194 + 1 = 195 · 205 + 11 + 0 = 216.

Cardinalities are now **derived at run time and cross-checked against PostgreSQL** rather than transcribed. The exactness of the recomputation is unchanged: the four zero checks are preserved verbatim, and `expect(Number(total)).toBe(COMPUTED_PROFIT_ROWS.length)` guards them from silently covering a subset if the corpus grows again.

## The harness corpus is not the production corpus

The harness deliberately passes `parlayEntries: []`, so `SEED_STORE.parlays` is empty by construction. **That is a test-harness choice, not deletion of production data** — the entries in `parlayData.js` are untouched — and it is why `ROOT_COUNT` reduces to prediction-run and prop roots alone.

**Gate 5 must rebuild and reconcile the complete latest migration input, parlays included, before seeding anything hosted.** This suite proves seed fidelity for the harness corpus and does not stand in for that step. Both files now say so explicitly.

## CI

Adds a second job, **`Database and API`**, on its own `ubuntu-latest` runner (30-minute timeout, inheriting the workflow-level `contents: read`). It installs with `npm ci --include=dev`, sets up the CLI via `supabase/setup-cli@v1` pinned to the committed **2.110.0**, starts a **local, unlinked** stack with the committed `npm run db:start`, runs `npm run test:db` and `npm run test:api`, and tears down in an `always()` step that cannot change the job outcome.

No project ref, no `supabase link`, no `--linked`, no hosted credentials, no production data, no repository secrets. The change to `ci.yml` is **purely additive** — the existing "Test and build" job is byte-identical with its original 15 steps.

## Credential hygiene

- **Startup and teardown output is suppressed** (`>/dev/null 2>&1`). Necessary, not cosmetic: on a successful start the CLI prints the anon key, the service-role/secret key, the JWT secret and the database URL. Redirection leaves the exit status untouched, so a failed start still fails the step.
- **The workflow never invokes `supabase status` itself.** Failure-only diagnostics are limited to container names/status and the Postgres log.
- **`supabase status -o json` *is* executed**, inside `npm run test:api`, by `tests/api/helpers.mjs` — it needs the REST URL, anon key and JWT secret to mint the GoTrue-shaped tokens that exercise the real authenticated path. An earlier draft of the plan claimed the command was never run in CI; that was false and is corrected in this diff.
- **Status failures are sanitized.** Command failure, unparseable JSON and missing fields each throw a hand-written message that names fields but never values, with no `cause`, stdout, stderr or child-process error object attached. Verified: `cause`/`stdout`/`stderr` all `undefined`, zero own enumerable properties, no credential substrings.
- **`status()` returns a frozen three-field allowlist** — `REST_URL`, `ANON_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET`. The CLI returns 9 fields; the other 6 (`API_URL`, `DB_URL`, `GRAPHQL_URL`, `PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SECRET_KEY`, `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`) are discarded, not merely unused. Previously the whole parsed object was returned, handing every importer the service-role key and the database URL. A regression assertion pins the exposed key set by name inside an existing test, so the suite is still 197 tests.

## Enforcement, stated honestly

`main` is **not** branch-protected. `Database and API` runs as its own check on pull requests and pushes to `main`, so its result is visible on every PR, but a red check does **not** mechanically block a merge. **During this rollout it must be treated as required by hand.** Enforceable gating would need a branch-protection rule or a repository ruleset; neither is configured, and configuring one is deliberately outside this change.

## Plan reconciliation

`docs/STAGE_7_PLAN.md` gains a dated **"Pre-Gate-4 baseline synchronization audit — 2026-09-01"** section carrying the current corpus and recomputation result. Historical Gate 1/2/3 measurements are **retained, not rewritten** — rewriting 167/178/182 to 194/205/216 would falsify what was actually tested when those gates landed. Wording that could be misread as describing `main` today is relabelled as historical instead.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run test:api` | **197/197** across 11 files |
| `npm run test:db` (pgTAP) | **174/174** across 3 files |
| `npm test` (offline) | **773/773** across 51 files |
| `npm run probe:browser` | pass |
| `npm run build` | pass |
| workflow structural validation | **25/25** |
| canonical fingerprint (two clean resets) | 856 lines, `60b497405f1fdb2eb24797f22e5bdd801423947621f98537348d3d443e1e79cd` |
| `git diff --check` | clean |
| bundle leak check (14 probes) | all 0 |
| source maps in `build/` | 0 |
| bundle digests vs. pre-change | byte-identical |

The fingerprint is unchanged in both directions, which is the evidence that no SQL moved.

author: jameskorzekwa
body:
## Intent

Prevent the Docs Source workflow from appending an unlisted asset to validated J2K web channel releases. Those releases use an exact three-asset inventory, and the extra docs archive makes every later release smoke test and managed update fail closed.

## Non-goals

This does not relax the updater inventory check or change docs packaging for upstream releases, main-branch docs changes, or untagged manual runs.

## Affected surfaces

- `.github/workflows/docs-source.yml`: skips release events and manually supplied tags containing `-j2k.`.
- `tools/channel-release/workflow-contract.test.mjs`: records both exclusions as release-channel contracts.
- `packages/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`: documents that docs archives are not attached to validated J2K channel releases.
- No rendered web, desktop, VS Code, or mobile behavior changes.

## Repository guidance

| Guidance | Why it applies | How the change complies |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | This changes release configuration and its documented contract. | The diff is limited to the owning workflow, contract test, and docs. |
| `communication-style` | Applies to all written output. | Documentation states the concrete release exclusion without generic filler. |
| `openchamber-change-discipline` | This is an external release contract and failure-path fix. | The updater remains fail-closed; the producer stops mutating the validated inventory. Focused contract and docs checks cover the changed behavior. |
| `packages/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` | Owns the docs-source publication contract. | The trigger and output descriptions now match the guarded workflow. |

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `node --test tools/channel-release/workflow-contract.test.mjs` | Passed, 9 tests. |
| `node scripts/docs/validate-docs.mjs` | Passed, 460 pages and 46 sidebar links. |
| `git diff --check` | Passed. |

The GitHub-hosted event guard has not yet run against a published release; the contract test verifies both automatic release and manual tagged-dispatch guards statically.

## Visual evidence

No visual evidence applies. The diff changes release automation and documentation only; it cannot alter rendered application UI.

## Risks and failure behavior

A matching J2K docs-source run is skipped before checkout, packaging, upload, or website dispatch. Normal docs publication paths remain unchanged. Rollback is reverting this commit, but doing so would let future docs-source runs invalidate the J2K channel inventory again.

Addresses #52

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to the deepface HTTP client and reqwest dependency features; behavior change is additive session stickiness with existing `reassign_required` fallback if affinity is lost.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Enables HTTP cookie persistence** on `FaceVerifierClient` so load-balancer stickiness survives from enclave assignment through follow-up API calls.
> 
> Workspace `reqwest` now includes the **`cookies`** feature, and `FaceVerifierClient::new` turns on **`.cookie_store(true)`** on the shared `reqwest::Client`. author: riscfuture
body:
The only way anything left this app was an `NSSavePanel` behind the macOS Print menu
group. iOS and visionOS had no export path at all, so a student could not AirDrop a
finished FRAT to a CFI and a club member could not mail one to a safety officer — on the
two platforms a pilot is most likely to be holding while filling one out.

The report already renders everywhere: #11 moved `FRATReport` and `FRATReportView` into
`Shared`, so `pdfData` draws its one-page vector PDF on every platform. What was missing
was a `Transferable` conformance and somewhere to tap. `FRATReport` now exports a single
`FileRepresentation`, and `ResultsView` carries a `ShareLink` in its toolbar, which
surfaces it in all three layouts — the iPhone tab, the iPad detail column, and the Mac
window. On macOS this is purely additive; **Print** and **Export FRAT as PDF** are
untouched.

### Why a PDF and not a re-openable assessment

The conformance uses `exportedContentType:` rather than `contentType:`. The latter
overload also demands an importing closure, which would declare that the app can read an
arbitrary PDF back into a questionnaire.

Re-opening a shared assessment sounds appealing and is a trap for the same reason.
`QuestionnaireData` is 22 bare `Bool`s and an `ApproachType`, and five of those answers
are defined by *per-device* threshold settings, so a sender's “surface wind greater than
15 kn” would silently become “greater than 25 kn” on the recipient's device, while
`RiskCategorizer` re-bucketed the rest against the recipient's rating and hours — an
authoritative-looking risk category for a flight nobody is flying. The PDF is the right
artifact precisely because it is inert and self-describing.

Skipping the custom UTI also skips the only real build cost here:
`UTExportedTypeDeclarations` is an array of dictionaries with no `INFOPLIST_KEY_`
equivalent, and every target generates its `Info.plist`.

### Temporary files

Each export writes into its own temporary directory so the file can keep the name
`FRATReport` suggests; services that copy it, like Mail and AirDrop, read that name off
disk rather than off the transfer representation. Nothing deletes it. The system copies
out of the file *after* the exporting closure returns, so there is no moment we could
safely reap it, and the temporary directory is the system's to clear.

### Incidentals

`Transferable` refines `Sendable`, and a `Sendable` conformance has to be declared
alongside the type, hence `struct FRATReport: Sendable`. The `periphery:ignore` comments
on `init`, `suggestedFileName` and `pdfData` are gone: they existed only because the
report had no caller outside `#if os(macOS)` while the scan runs against an iOS simulator,
and the share sheet gives all three a real one.

### Verification

Builds clean on macOS, iOS Simulator and visionOS. Unit tests 20/20 on macOS — two new,
covering the temporary file's name, its single rendered page, and that two exports the
same day do not collide. UI tests 28/28 on iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5. `swift-format lint
--strict` clean; `periphery --strict` reports no unused code. The exported PDF was opened
and checked as a readable one-page document.

author: juliarvalenti
body:
Closes #71.

Email has had a renderer for the format it actually arrives in — HTML — since `server/mailtext.ts`. Chat, notes and everything an agent writes arrive as **markdown**, and until now those surfaces showed the syntax raw. `sdk/markdown.ts` is the sibling renderer.

## The constraint, baked in

The output is **view nodes, never ANSI**. A raw `\x1b[1m` inside a `TextRenderable` miscounts the row's width and corrupts OpenTUI's layout, so piping `glow` through a view was never an option however good it looks in a shell. Every line is a `text`/`row`/`col`/`box` the host already draws — which also means it themes itself: name a role in `theme()` and one `config.toml` recolors every document kona renders. A test walks the whole tree and fails on an escape, or on any node kind outside the vocabulary.

The second constraint is **width**. A styled line is a `row` of spans, and the host can word-wrap one `text` node but not five side by side and keep them in order — so the wrapping is ours, span-aware, before any node exists. Long paragraphs wrap, a URL with nothing to break on is split, nothing is truncated.

## The surface

```ts
renderMarkdown(md, { width })   // the document as nodes — what a view wants
markdownToText(md, { width })   // the same render, flattened — a record row,
                                // a dash card, a desktop notification
cleanMarkdown(md)               // the cleanText() pass, run by both
```

It reads ATX and setext headings, emphasis, strong, strikethrough, inline code, links, images and autolinks, bullet/ordered/task lists (nested), blockquotes, fenced and indented code, thematic breaks and GFM pipe tables. Reference links, footnotes and raw HTML read as their literal text rather than disappearing.

Two options earn their keep:

- `breaks: true` — a single newline is a line break, what GitHub, Slack and a human typing into a notepad mean by enter. Off by default (CommonMark re-wraps a paragraph to the frame).
- `maxLines` — cap a preview and end with a dim `… N more lines`.

Emphasis maps onto what a terminal actually has: strong is brighter (`theme().key`), em is a tint (`alt`) rather than dim — dim would invert the emphasis — code is text on the field fill, links take the accent with their URL appended dim, struck text is dim.

## Where it plugs in

- **mycelium** — a message renders as markdown under its sender's gutter, so an agent's plan reads as a list and its command as a fenced block. Its local `wrap()` goes; the renderer owns wrapping now.
- **notes** — the reader renders the body, with `breaks` so a line you typed stays a line (a grocery list is still a grocery list).
- **storybook** — the gallery gains a markdown section, which is where a component proves it draws.

The Webex message reader is its own companion issue, so it is not wired here; `rss` item bodies arrive as HTML and already go through the mail path.

```
   22:14  coder        plan:

                       • parse to blocks
                       • wrap span-aware
                       • no ANSI, ever

                        sh
                        bun test tests/markdown.test.ts
   22:18  kona         │ no ANSI, ever

                       agreed — see the issue
                       (https://github.com/juliarvalenti/kona/issues/71)
```

## Testing

- `tests/markdown.test.ts` — 21 tests over the platform module: the no-ANSI guard, wrapping a 60-word paragraph and an unbreakable URL, every block shape, inline styles and escapes, hard vs soft breaks, `breaks`, `maxLines`, the empty document, an unterminated fence, and purity.
- New snapshot fixtures in `applets/notes` and `applets/mycelium` render markdown through the **real host** and assert the syntax never reaches the screen; storybook's gallery fixture gained the same.
- `bun test` (618 pass, 0 fail), `bun run check` clean, `bun run shots` re-run (storybook's shot moved by one scrollbar thumb).

`sdk/markdown.ts` sits beside `sdk/components.ts` rather than in `server/` because it emits view vocabulary and no `server/` module ever has; it is listed in the plugin ABI table in CONTRIBUTING.md.

author: blove
body:
PR #932 changed exactly three files under `apps/website/src` and ran **41** `Cockpit — e2e` lanes. Two independent scoping defects stacked.

## 1. The cockpit shell claimed the e2e matrix

`apps/cockpit/project.json` carried `scope:cockpit-e2e`. But the matrix dispatches `nx e2e` for the standalone Angular cap apps under `cockpit/**`, and:

- **0 of 40** caps depend on the `apps/cockpit` Next.js shell (checked against the nx project graph)
- no workflow anywhere runs the shell's own `e2e` target

So the tag could never select real work — only over-select. And it did: `apps/cockpit` statically depends on `apps/website`, so a website-only PR made the shell nx-affected and flipped `cockpit_e2e` true. From that run's `CI scope` log:

```
Affected projects (3):
  website [scope:website, scope:website-e2e, type:app]
  cockpit [scope:cockpit, scope:cockpit-deploy-smoke, scope:cockpit-e2e, scope:cockpit-examples, type:app]
  scripts [scope:scripts-tests, type:tooling]
cockpit_e2e=true
```

## 2. A cap was only matchable by its Angular name

A cap is two independent nx projects — the Angular app that owns the `e2e` target and the python backend — with no edge between them. `cockpit-matrix.mjs` matched affected projects on `cap.angular` only, so a python-only cap change attributed nothing, which `main()` reads as "nx found no cap" and answers with the full fleet.

## Measured, before → after

| change | lanes before | lanes after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| website-only (#932 `base..head`) | 41 | **0** — the dispatcher's `if:` gate is now false |
| python-only cap change | 40 | **1** — the cap that changed |
| `libs/chat` change | 40 | **40** — unchanged, no coverage lost |

(40 vs 41 is drift in the cap count since that run, not an effect of this change.)

## Notes

- The python sibling's nx name is read from its own `project.json` rather than derived from the path. A convention-derived guess would fail open to the full fleet without ever reporting that it guessed.
- The emitted matrix JSON keeps its exact `{angular, python}` shape; `pythonName` is internal to attribution.
- The shell still builds and tests on a website change — it consumes that code. Only the cap e2e matrix is descoped.

## Tests

Both new spec groups were confirmed **failing before** the fix:

```
not ok 1 - apps/cockpit is not tagged scope:cockpit-e2e
not ok 2 - a website-only change leaves cockpit_e2e false
# SyntaxError: ... does not provide an export named 'isCapAffected'
```

After: `node --test` over all six suites 125/125, `nx test scripts` vitest 71/71 (baseline), `nx lint scripts` clean. No new spec *file*, so `scripts/vite.config.mts` `exclude` and the ci.yml `node --test` invocation need no change.

## Left alone deliberately

`scope:cockpit-examples` and `scope:cockpit-deploy-smoke` on the shell are also broad, but those jobs are cheap and already self-scope (`Cockpit — build all examples` correctly logged "No affected cockpit angular projects" on #932). Separately: `apps/cockpit` has an `e2e` target that no workflow runs — worth a look, but not this PR.

author: stevenmburns
body:
Razor was CLI-only; this puts it in the solver tab strip. **One lane, not two.**

## Which lane, and why only one

`RazorSolver` serves two quadrature rules off one class — `n_qp_path` Gauss–Legendre nodes per wing, or NEC-5's identified two-point centroid trapezoid (momwire#316). momwire now names them `razor` and `razor-2p` (momwire#785).

Only the two-point lane is offered here. Measured on the ByDipole1 ladder (`scripts/bench_bydipole1_bases.py`, AK#1085), the GL rule's advantage **evaporates by N≈192** — the two agree within 3% of each other's self-convergence at N=384 having been 2× apart at N=12 — while costing **~10× the wall time** (momwire#780). A knob that buys nothing on any mesh a person will sit and wait for is not a knob. The GL lane stays on the CLI and the constructor, where paying for it is a deliberate choice.

## A new roster capability: `_BackendSpec.bound`

The picker previously mapped a name to a **class**, which cannot express a *lane*. `bound` carries constructor kwargs — the shape momwire's own deck roster and this CLI's basis variants already use — and `_make_momwire_engine` applies them **after** the request's `model_options` so they win: `razor-2p` stays the two-point rule whatever a client sends, or the label on the tab stops describing what ran. Gated by a test.

It serves **no numeric knob on purpose**: `n_qp_path` is the only quadrature knob razor has and it is *ignored* under this rule (momwire's own docstring), so serving it would render an inert control.

`default_n_per_wire=40` — higher than bspline's 30 because this basis converges slower (~16× the mesh for the same self-convergence on that ladder), and **even**, because a centre-fed deck wants a knot at the feed for it.

## No momwire release needed

The binding lives here, so this does not wait on momwire's roster gaining the name — which matters, because antennaknobs pins `momwire==0.45.0` **exactly** and that predates it. momwire#785 aligns the two rosters but is not a prerequisite.

Also adds `razor-2p` to the CLI basis variants beside the deprecated `razor-nec5`, which keeps working with an identical binding.

## Test plan

- [x] `uvx ruff@0.16.5 check .` and `format --check .` — clean (621 files)
- [x] Full suite — 3893 passed, 28 skipped
- [x] Served-roster pin updated (order, labels, panels, options schema, mesh defaults, capabilities)
- [x] New gates: the bound kwarg cannot be overridden from the wire, and no inert `n_qp_path` control is served

author: juliasilge
body: There's no rush on this; it's fine to wait to review/merge until after we branch. Fixes #11020 The SSH, WSL, and Dev Containers extensions each declared their own "Download URL" setting. All three had the same purpose and the same default, which also duplicated `serverDownloadUrlTemplate` in `product.json`. Typing "Download URL" in the Settings editor showed three entries, and it was easy to set the wrong one. This adds a single setting, `remote.serverDownloadUrlTemplate`, and reads it from all three extensions. It is registered in core rather than by one of the extensions, so it exists whether or not a given remote extension is enabled. The key sits in the `remote.*` namespace, so the Settings editor groups it with the other remote settings: Its default is the empty string, not the CDN URL. An empty value means "not set", which is what lets a local or dev build fall through to `product.json` and download a server that matches it. The three per-extension settings are deprecated but still work, and take precedence when set, so nobody loses the behavior they configured: The Settings editor hides a deprecated setting until it has a value, so a fresh profile now shows one entry instead of three. Two implementation notes: - Both settings are read with `inspect()` rather than `get()`. The deprecated settings ship a non-empty default, so `get()` cannot tell "the user asked for the CDN URL" apart from "the user asked for nothing", and only the second case may fall through to `product.json`. - That fall-through was unreachable before this change. `get()` always returned the manifest default, so for SSH and WSL neither `product.json` nor `DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_URL_TEMPLATE` was ever consulted. Both are reachable now, which is why `serverSetup.ts` is touched. Those two hardcoded defaults pinned the quality to `dailies`, and they now match the manifest defaults they stand in for. Dev Containers gains the `product.json` step, which it never had. The extensions cannot import from each other or from `src/vs`, so the resolution helper is copied into each one. A test asserts the copies stay identical and that the key they spell out still matches the one core registers. This branch also enables Vitest for `extensions/**`, which is what makes the helper testable at all, in a separate commit. Adding a test inside an extension requires excluding it from that extension's build, or it ships inside the extension with an unresolvable `vitest` import. That is documented in `.claude/rules/vitest-tests.md` and in the author-vitest-tests skill. ### Release Notes #### New Features - Added a single Download URL setting, `remote.serverDownloadUrlTemplate`, shared by the SSH, WSL, and Dev Containers extensions. The three per-extension settings are deprecated, and still take precedence where they are already set. (#11020) #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:remote-ssh @:remote-wsl The WSL suite already sets the deprecated `remote.WSL.serverDownloadUrlTemplate`, so it exercises the precedence rule directly. Dev Containers has no e2e tag, so that call site is covered by unit tests and manual checks only. #### Manual validation with a local Docker container This verifies which URL is actually requested. A dev build is the right harness, because its `product.json` has no `quality` or `commit`, so the default URL is unreachable. That is the problem this setting exists to solve! 1. Build the image and start a container, from a checkout of `positron-builds`: ```bash docker build -t remotessh -f dev/remote-ssh/Dockerfile --build-arg NODE_VERSION=$(cat ../positron/.nvmrc) . docker run -d --name remotessh -p 3456:22 remotessh ``` 2. Install your public key. Use `docker cp` rather than `ssh-copy-id` to skip the password prompts, then fix the owner, because `docker cp` keeps your host UID and sshd refuses a file it does not own: ```bash docker exec remotessh mkdir -p /root/.ssh docker cp ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub remotessh:/root/.ssh/authorized_keys docker exec remotessh chown -R root:root /root/.ssh docker exec remotessh chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys ``` Add a `dock` host to your `~/.ssh/config` (`User root`, `Hostname localhost`, `Port 3456`), then confirm `ssh dock` works. If you have used this container before, clear the stale host keys first with `ssh-keygen -R "[localhost]:3456"`. 3. Make sure `~/.positron-server` does not exist in the container, so a download is attempted: ```bash docker exec remotessh ls -d /root/.positron-server # expect "No such file or directory" ``` 4. Log the requested URL. The extension writes the install script to the **Remote - SSH** output channel, which is UI only, so a shim in the container gives a record you can read directly: ```bash docker exec remotessh sh -c 'mv /usr/bin/wget /usr/bin/wget.real; \ printf "#!/bin/sh\nprintf \"%%s\\\\n\" \"\$*\" >> /tmp/download-urls.log\nexec /usr/bin/wget.real \"\$@\"\n" > /usr/bin/wget; \ chmod +x /usr/bin/wget' ``` 5. Run each case below in a dev build. Both keys are application-scoped, so they go in the dev build's user settings (`~/.vscode-oss-dev/User/settings.json`), not workspace settings. For each one, run _Remote-SSH: Connect to Host..._ and choose `dock`, then read `/tmp/download-urls.log` with `docker exec remotessh cat /tmp/download-urls.log`. | Case | Settings | Expected URL | |---|---|---| | 1 | neither key set | `https://cdn.posit.co/positron/undefined/reh/arm64/positron-reh-linux-arm64-.tar.gz` | | 2 | `remote.serverDownloadUrlTemplate` only | `https://unified.test/linux-arm64.tar.gz` | | 3 | both, with distinct hosts | `https://legacy.test/linux-arm64.tar.gz` | | 4 | deprecated key removed, unified set to `""` | the case 1 URL again | Use `https://unified.test/${os}-${arch}.tar.gz` and `https://legacy.test/${os}-${arch}.tar.gz` as the values, so you can tell which key won and so the template variables are visibly substituted. What to expect: - The literal `undefined` in the case 1 URL is correct, not a typo. A dev build has no `quality` in `product.json`. - Every case fails to connect, with `There is no available Positron server with version for linux aarch64`. That is expected here! The download is after the part under test, and the message reports the version rather than the URL, so it looks identical in all four cases. Read the log, and don't be worried about the error. - Case 3 needs the deprecated key typed into `settings.json` by hand, because it is now hidden in the Settings editor until it has a value. That behavior is worth confirming while you are there, along with the strikethrough and the deprecation notice once it is set. Tear down with `docker rm -f remotessh`.

author: vicenteliu
body:
Walkthrough 03 closed on a connection this repo had never made: company information lives in five categories, four of which can carry a recovery objective, and **the reason the fifth cannot is the same reason monitoring coverage is a statement about a subset.** Both stop at the edge of the inventory.

That is a good line and it was in the wrong place.

## The rule it broke

`walkthrough/README.md`: *"If a sentence needs a fact no source holds, the fact gets written into the material first — the walkthrough is never where something first appears."*

Both halves existed. `the-stack/06` says coverage is measured against an inventory; `the-reference-office.md` says you cannot set a recovery objective for a system you have not inventoried. **The sentence joining them did not exist anywhere.** So a spoken script was load-bearing for an argument, which is exactly what that rule prevents.

It now lives at the end of *Can you monitor everything?* in `the-stack/06`, mirrored into `docs/zh/`, where it can be cited and checked. The script says it downstream.

## Two more things the same audit found

**An invented measurement.** *"The alert that would have fired eleven minutes before the first person walked up"* — a plausible-sounding number in a list of otherwise concrete things, with nothing behind it. Every other figure in those 102 beats traces to a source; that one traced to me wanting a rhythm. Now: *"before anybody walked up"*, which is true and scans the same.

**An off-by-one decade.** `build-out/01` dates the change at 2015; from 2026 that is eleven years, so *"ten years ago"* was wrong in the direction that sounds right. *"A decade ago"* makes no arithmetic claim.

## Why no checker caught these

None of the three could have been. The counts check added in `1ad5809` guards numbers **the repo states about itself**. These are numbers **a script states about the world**, and the only thing that finds those is reading the script against its sources — which is what `sources:` in the front matter is for, and why the freeze fingerprints exist.

`python3 check.py` — **all 27 pass**. Three walkthroughs still hold.

author: fdaviddpt
body:
## What

Closes #244 (part 2 of #233). At session end, when this session fired jit-context entries and nothing under `.claude/jit-context/` was written, name them: `N entries injected this session, none updated. Fired: 1. bridge.md (last edited 170d ago) ...`.

#233's own comment explained why this did not ship with parts 1 and 3: the `shown` marks record what was **injected**; nothing recorded that an entry file was **edited**, so `writes == 0` was not derivable. This PR builds that signal and nothing else.

## How

- **`scripts/post-tool-hook.sh`** (new) -- a `PostToolUse` hook, matcher `Write|Edit` in `hooks/hooks.json`. Parses `tool_name`/`file_path`/`session_id` with the same shared awk JSON macros every hook here already uses, and when a Write or Edit lands on a real, non-traversal path under `$JIT_BASE`, drops an existence-only marker `edited-<session>.txt` beside the `shown` marks -- no path, no content, no count.
- **`scripts/stop-hook.sh`** (new) -- a `Stop` hook. Reads the existing `vocab-shown`/`path-shown` marks (already written by the three pre-existing hooks) and the new edit marker. Three states: entries fired and the marker is present -- silence (healthy); entries fired and it is absent -- the numbered list, with `last edited Nd ago` reused from the existing `jit_scan_entry_ages()` **for display only**, never to decide the fired-vs-edited question itself; state directory unavailable -- explicit **could not tell**, never rendered as the silent/healthy case.
- `scripts/session-start-hook.sh` extended to age out the new marker the same way it already ages the `shown` marks.
- `README.md` and `.claude/jit-context/paths/00-manual/hooks.md` updated for the new hook count and the new Stop-hook behaviour.

## The trap this deliberately does not reach for

`jit_scan_entry_ages()` reads filesystem mtimes and inherits #243: a fresh `git clone` resets every mtime to checkout time, so a signal built on it would answer "nothing was updated" on a session where everything was. The edit marker is a second, independent, real signal (an observed Write/Edit) for exactly that reason -- never a second read of the age table.

## Self-review

Spawned an Explore reviewer and the oss:auditor, both against the first commit. One real bug fixed in a second commit: the fired-entry dedup scan in `stop-hook.sh` re-scanned its whole accumulator on every marker line with no size cap (unlike `JIT_LAYERS_MAX`/`JIT_ENTRY_AGES_MAX` elsewhere in this codebase) -- bounded at 500 with the overflow named rather than dropped, and a new test (`test-stop-hook.sh` section H, 600 entries) drives it. Also fixed stale "four hooks" prose left in two more places in `hooks.md` after the first commit only updated one. Two other findings were argued down with reasoning in the agent report: a claimed case-pattern glob-injection risk in `post-tool-hook.sh`'s path prefix test (empirically false -- quoting a variable in a bash `case` pattern makes it literal) and a marker write that does not check its own redirect's exit status (real, but the same accepted posture every other marker write in this codebase already takes, and adding retry/error-propagation would be a second new mechanism this issue's own maintainer decision explicitly rules out).

**below-bar, not filed:** a case-sensitive path-prefix match in `post-tool-hook.sh` would miss a `file_path` that differs only in case from `$JIT_BASE` on a case-insensitive filesystem (Windows/macOS default) -- but this whole plugin already matches paths case-sensitively, byte for byte, as a stated, deliberate design decision (`pre-path-hook.sh`'s own top-of-file comment, #76), so this is consistent with the established norm rather than a regression this diff introduced.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash tests/test-post-tool-hook.sh` -- new, 17 assertions, red before the hook existed
- [x] `bash tests/test-stop-hook.sh` -- new, 22 assertions (incl. the dedup-bound section), red before the hook existed
- [x] `bash tests/test-inert-without-tree.sh` -- extended to drive both new hooks through the tree-less contract
- [x] `bash tests/test-assertion-helpers.sh` -- both new suites declare their `jit-drive:` coverage
- [x] `bash tests/run-all.sh` -- full suite green, twice (once per commit)
- [x] `python3 .oss/assemble_changelog.py --check` -- ok

author: alpcaner
body:
## Summary

Closes #1902.

Every prerelease tag declared itself as its GA version, so an rc checkout was indistinguishable from the release it was a candidate for — `ALP_VERSION_STRING`, `alp_version_string()` and the build-plan `sdkVersion` all read identically.

**Root cause, confirmed not assumed:** `bump_version.py`'s `SEMVER_RE` and `alp_lock`'s version regex *already* tolerated a SemVer prerelease suffix. What blocked it was `release.yml`'s tag-verify step requiring `metadata/sdk_version.yaml`'s `version:` to equal the tag's **stripped** core exactly — making a suffixed `version:` impossible to declare. That forced the "bump metadata to bare GA, let only the git tag carry `-rcN`" convention, which is the defect.

## Both directions now closed

Review caught that the first pass only closed the GA direction: tag `v0.16.0-rc2` against `version: 0.16.0-rc1` still passed both checks, so an rc2 build self-reported as rc1 — #1902's own defect, surviving. A third guard now fails when tag and metadata both carry a suffix and they differ.

## Test plan

`tests/scripts/test_release_tag_verify.py` extracts the workflow's **own** `run:` text (never a retyped copy, following `test_release_changelog_slice.py`'s precedent) and runs it against a 6-case table plus the exact reviewer repro. 7 tests.

Proved sensitive: with the six production files stashed, 6 of 7 new prerelease tests fail; the one that passes is `update_version_h`'s already-correct behaviour, matching the "already half-supports it" finding.

One correction made while writing it: the step's `::error::` lines are plain `echo` with no `>&2`, so they land on **stdout**. Asserting on `stderr` would have passed locally on Windows (where the suite skips) and failed on every CI runner.

`docs/release-policy.md` gains the rc two-step, so an operator following the doc verbatim actually exercises the fix.

## Scope

- [x] Build/CI, docs, tests. `include/alp/version.h` doc-comment only — `abi_snapshot.py --diff` confirms **ABI unchanged**.

## Process

Authored on an isolated worktree branch, independently reviewed by a separate
agent running this repo's gates, then the reviewer's confirmed findings fixed in
follow-up commits. Findings that could be refuted with evidence were reported and
left alone rather than "fixed".

Not bench-tested: nothing here touches silicon behaviour.

body:
## Summary

- `#2218` wrapped `POLICY_OVERRIDE_NOUN_SOURCE` in a hyphen-boundary
  guard so a hyphenated compound like `idd-workflow-notes.md` no
  longer false-positives Check 3 (trust/safety), but left
  `POLICY_OVERRIDE_VERB_SOURCE` on a bare `\b`. A hyphen still counts
  as a word boundary there, so an ordinary compound noun ending in a
  listed verb -- e.g. `#2213`'s own title, "duplicate-evidence-skip
  check" -- still matched "skip" and wrongly failed `trust_safety`.
- Several regex-lookbehind revisions each let some flag-prefixed
  directive evade detection at a fixed lookbehind distance. The fix
  drops the lookbehind entirely: `POLICY_OVERRIDE_VERB_SOURCE` reverts
  to its original bare alternation, and a new
  `isOrdinaryHyphenatedCompoundVerb` classifier (called from
  `findPolicyOverrideMatch`, alongside the existing negation check)
  walks the token containing the verb back to its own true origin in
  JS -- a genuine compound always begins with a word character there;
  a flag token never does.
- Several follow-up rounds refined the walk itself: gating the
  classifier on the verb not sitting inside a masked code range (so a
  code-wrapped directive key stays detectable, while a bare
  un-code-wrapped compound-looking key stays deliberately excluded --
  it is byte-identical in shape to `#2213`'s own case); walking a
  fixed `[\w-]` run rather than growing an ever-incomplete punctuation
  boundary list (closing a gap on directives that directly abut prose
  punctuation with no whitespace, without breaking dotted/colon-joined
  flag names); and stopping the walk at an unspaced double hyphen
  directly preceded by a word character, which is prose punctuation
  (a typewriter em/en dash) rather than a compound joiner.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test tests/suitability-triage.test.mts` -- 243/243
      pass, including 12 tests added across this PR's review rounds
      covering: the `#2213` compound-word false positive, a
      freestanding verb still failing next to an unrelated hyphenated
      mention, hyphen-prefixed single and multi-word flags, an
      underscore-suffixed compound staying excluded, a verb as a
      non-first flag component, a non-hyphen flag prefix, a
      code-wrapped bare key staying detected, a bare unquoted
      compound-looking key staying deliberately excluded, a verb
      directly abutting prose punctuation with no whitespace, a flag
      name that itself contains a dot or colon, and a verb separated
      from a preceding word by an unspaced double hyphen.
- [x] `pnpm run build` regenerates `scripts/suitability-triage.mjs`.
- [x] `pnpm run lint:minimum` passes clean (typecheck, biome, dprint,
      full `node --test tests/*.test.mts` -- 4526/4526, cspell,
      markdownlint).

Refs #2218, #2213

author: vladimirrott
body:
## Why the middle digit

[#312](https://github.com/lacs-project/sysknife/pull/312). `npx sysknife-setup --claude --no-prompts --daemon-mode=system` is the automation one-liner in `docs/quickstart.md`, and it now exits 3 where it exited 0. No signature changed. A run that used to succeed now reports failure, and `docs/release.md` already counts that as a break, with v0.9.0 as the precedent: the wizard started refusing a malformed `.mcp.json` it used to overwrite, and that moved the middle digit too.

System mode is a two-phase install by design, so a non-zero exit is the honest answer. Anyone scripting that line under `set -e` will see it stop, which is the point of the issue it closes.

Nothing else in this batch breaks. `ApprovalPolicy::new` gained a parameter but `sysknife-cli` publishes no library. `rmcp` 2 to 3 is a binary's dependency. The preview request gained an optional field, and both directions of that skew are covered by tests.

## What ships

Sixteen changes, four from three outside contributors and seven from Dependabot.

**Two secrets stopped being readable by anyone on the host.** #316 moved every provider API key out of the VM harnesses' process arguments, proved by argv canaries rather than by reading. #326 moved CI off Node 20, which reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30, and pinned three lint tools that were being installed unpinned in a job holding the workflow token.

**A way to run with no human, that says so in the chain.** #329 adds `--dangerously-skip-approval`. It lifts the approval gate and nothing else, needs a second key in the environment, and the daemon writes the fact into the transaction's `warnings_json`, which is inside the row's Ed25519 signature. Scrubbing it makes `audit verify` report that row `Broken`.

**The audit chain became exportable.** #318, contributed by @danial-razi, writes the signed rows as JSON with the linkage and signature bytes, and states in `docs/cli.md` that an export inherits the confidentiality of the database it came from.

**Three gates stopped reporting verdicts they had not earned.** #313 and #317 on the Postgres contract, and #330 on six review findings including a guard that matched a variable by name and so could not see the same bug renamed.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --locked`: 1820 passed, 5 skipped.
- `scripts/check_release_versions.sh v0.11.0`: fifteen version sites, fifteen internal pins, five JSON manifests.
- `scripts/release_rehearsal.sh --check`: preflight passed for v0.11.0 on x86_64.
- `scripts/ci-local.sh`: PASS.
- Postgres contract under podman: `running 11 tests`, 11 passed.

Merging this does not publish anything. The signed tag does.

author: jadegate-mayor
body:
> **Stacked on `feat/federation-owner-label` — citadel's half, gp-0uj, PR #5.** This PR targets that branch so the diff shows only the fence; once #5 merges into `integration`, retarget this one to `integration` (mayor coordinates). Nothing here is installed or rolled out by this PR.

## The loop this closes

2026-09-01 23:00 CST — a jadegate `houmanoids-www` pool worker's startup claim (`gc hook --claim`) acquired **citadel's** bead `hw-57b63` out of the SHARED federated `hw` store. Citadel's lease lapsed every ~5 min (their gp-e8z heartbeat identity split). Jadegate's reconciler then saw an `in_progress` bead whose assignee was a session it had never heard of, **released it as an orphaned pool assignment**, counted it as demand, spawned a seat, and the seat's startup claim wrote lease+assignee **before any lane rule could run**. Every tick, until the rig was suspended (jg-n3plw4; same class as 2026-08-25).

## The convention (citadel gp-0uj; fit contract accepted by jadegate 2026-09-02)

- Every bead a federated city creates carries `owner:<identity>`, where identity is **`city.toml [federation] identity`** — an explicit opt-in key validated lowercase (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`) at config load, deliberately *not* the workspace name (citadel's is literally `city`). Labels are compared as **exact strings**, no trimming, no case folding.
- `handoff:<identity>` is written only by an explicit cross-city sling; a bead may carry several.
- Legacy unlabeled beads stay claimable. An unset identity means **not federated: nothing stamped, nothing refused**.
- Citadel's half (`feat/federation-owner-label`) is emit-only: the two create doors, `gc ready --label`, `gc maintenance owner-backfill`, and the vocabulary in `internal/federation`. **This PR is jadegate's half: one refusal rule, wired at every write that takes ownership of a bead for this city.**

## The rule — `federation.MayClaim(labels, thisIdentity) (ok, reason)`

In order: identity unset → ok (fence off) · no `owner:*` → ok (legacy) · any `handoff:<thisIdentity>` → ok (the override) · every `owner:*` names `thisIdentity` → ok (own) · otherwise **refused** — a foreign owner, a *mixed* owner set (two cities asserting ownership is a conflict, not a licence — one interpretation choice not spelled out in the contract; flagged for citadel), or a bare `owner:` with no value.

| labels (identity `jadegate`) | result |
|---|---|
| *(none)* | ok (legacy) |
| `owner:jadegate` | ok |
| `owner:citadel` | **refused** |
| `owner:citadel` + `handoff:jadegate` | ok |
| `owner:citadel` + `handoff:boomtown` | refused |
| `owner:citadel` + `handoff:boomtown` + `handoff:jadegate` | ok |
| `owner:citadel` + `owner:jadegate` | refused (mixed) |
| `owner:` | refused (malformed) |
| `Owner:Citadel`, ` owner:citadel` | ok — not owner labels (exact strings) |
| `owner:Jadegate` | refused — value ≠ identity (exact strings) |
| anything, identity unset | ok (fence off) |

`federation.ClaimRefusalLine(beadID, reason)` puts the bead id in front, so **every site logs the identical greppable line**, values Go-quoted when not a single printable token:

```
cross-city-fence refused bead=hw-57b63 owner=citadel this_identity=jadegate missing=handoff:jadegate
```

## The three call sites

**(a)+(b) `gc hook --claim` — which *is* the pool worker's startup claim protocol** (`cmd_hook.go`: "runs the standard startup claim protocol"), so one wiring covers both. Two layers:

- **Layer 1** — `fenceCrossCityHookCandidates` in `tryHookClaim` (`cmd/gc/cmd_hook_claim.go`): filters the decoded candidate set once, on the labels the work query returned, upstream of every tier that can serve or mutate a bead — adoption (`hookClaimExistingAssignment`), ready promotion (`claimFirstReadyHookAssignment`), the fresh-claim CAS (`claimFirstEligibleHookCandidate`), and the class-route escalation around them (`classRoutedHookClaimOps`). Zero I/O.
- **Layer 2** — `installCrossCityWriteFence` (installed in `tryHookClaim` after `applyDefaults`) wraps the hook's two write seams, `ops.Claim` and `ops.AssignContinuation`, with an authoritative re-read of the *one* bead about to be written through the `ReadWorkMeta` seam (class-routed, so a binding-resident bead is read from its binding). Adoption gets the same re-read (`hookCrossCityRefusedBeforeServe`) before serving, resolving a bead the current leg cannot find through the class route and then **every other work leg of the unscoped fan-out** (`hookClaimOps.WorkLegs`, threaded from `cmdHookWithOptions` *before* `scopeFederatedHookStores` pins the query to the primary; legs told apart by dir **and** env via `sameHookStore`). Layer 2 closes what layer 1 cannot see: a `work_query` projection that omits labels, and a label changed since the snapshot.
- **Nothing runs unverified.** A refusal is `errCrossCityFenced` — skipped as no-work, never `claims_errored`, never a fail-closed exit. A read *failure* surfaces as the seam's own error and is handled exactly as the write failing there would be: not-found (held in another leg) is skipped and the loop moves on to the leg that holds it; anything else is a `claims_errored` skip, or the ready tier's fail-closed exit. An adopted bead no leg holds, or a leg that cannot be read, fails closed (exit 1, seat kept). The demand/claim divergence classifier (`demand_divergence.go`) treats a fenced trigger as benign.
- **Off without an identity.** No `[federation]` → layer 1 and 2 inert, nothing logged. That is also the mode every direct `doHookClaim` caller (the legacy hook tests) runs in.

**(c) The reconciler's re-route — `releaseOrphanedPoolAssignments`** (`cmd/gc/pool_session_name.go`), the engine of the loop: the same `MayClaim` runs before any liveness gate spends a read, a foreign bead is left exactly as it is, and the same line goes to the reconciler's log. The reconciler's second ownership write, the retired-session re-home (`reassignWorkAssignedToRetiredSessionBead` and its `Info` twin, `cmd/gc/session_beads.go`), applies the same rule so a pre-fence contamination is never handed on to a successor — and so does the API's named-session continuity re-home (`internal/api/session_resolution.go` `reassignOpenWorkAssignedToSession`, identity from the server's config; codex r6). `cmd/gc/cross_city_fence.go` holds the one identity accessor (`federationIdentity(cfg)`). The class route is armed with the **unscoped** fan-out too (`observeWorkLegs(ops.WorkLegs)`), so a not-found in the pinned primary is checked against the work legs before it opens the binding escalation (codex r6).

**Files the bead pointed at and why they are not the fence**

| file | role | why not here |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/hooks/hooks.go` | provider hook wiring | not the claim; the claim is `cmd/gc/cmd_hook_claim.go` |
| `internal/beads/sqlite_store_claim.go` | relocated-class store's CAS | reached only via `claim_class_route.go`, downstream of the fenced set |
| `internal/beads/caching_store_reconcile.go` | read-side cache reconciler | no claim or assignee writes |
| `internal/dispatch/control.go`, `internal/api/handler_convoy_dispatch.go` | dispatch decoration | set assignee/`gc.routed_to` on **new** step beads (owned by this city); never claim an existing bead |

## Rollout notes (mayor, not this PR)

- jadegate's `city.toml` needs `[federation]\nidentity = "jadegate"`; until then the fence is off here.

body:
Lane K of the overnight consumer-side rebuild (charter T1 `660d2ca` §2). Nothing here merges, promotes or deploys — this is a pushed branch and a walked local production build.

Baseline first: `npm ci` (exit 0, 59 packages) then `npm run build` (exit 0) on untouched `196829c` **before a byte changed**.

---

## The EV table

| EV | Claim | Command | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| **EV-1** | the QR decodes to the governed scan landing | `curl -s localhost/ \| grep -o 'https://app.longevityvalley.ai/scan/dr-magfield/krpm'` | `https://app.longevityvalley.ai/scan/dr-magfield/krpm` |
| **EV-1** | no build can ship a doorway a phone cannot open | `node --test tests/standee.test.mjs` | 8 doorway assertions pass; every non-https / loopback / foreign override falls back to the canon |
| **EV-17** | 0 `localhost` in the served home chunk | `grep -c localhost .next/static/chunks/app/page-*.js` | `0` (baseline: `1`) |
| **EV-17** | 0 Telegram doorway in the served home chunk | `grep -o 't\.me/DrMAGfield_Bot' .next/static/chunks/app/page-*.js \| wc -l` | `0` (baseline: `3`) |
| **EV-17** | no name is captured | there is no input element on the page | the name prompt, the chat input and the voice playback are gone |
| **EV-17** | the voice route is gone | `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST localhost/api/kiosk/session` | `404` |
| **EV-17** | status is measured or says Unmeasured | served home text | `Lounge status · Unmeasured` |
| **EV-8** | the checkout is not reachable with the flag unset | `grep -o 'Online sign-up is not available' .next/server/app/rabbit-cup.html` | `Online sign-up is not available` |
| **EV-8** | the register endpoint is not downloaded | `grep -c 'rabbit-cup/register' .next/static/chunks/app/rabbit-cup/page-*.js` | `0` |
| **stamp** | the served page says which build it is | served home text | `drm-standee v2 · local · unknown` |

### RED → GREEN, per commit

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `f87e450` | **RED** — the standee's laws, 3 test files, all failing against the untouched build |
| `1a4b192` | **GREEN** EV-17 · EV-1 + the build stamp |
| `b10bbdd` | **RED** — EV-8 read from the served artifact, 3 of 4 failing |
| `85ad3be` | **GREEN** EV-8 |

```
$ npm run verify        # next build && node --test 'tests/*.test.mjs'
exit 0
ℹ tests 26
ℹ pass 26
ℹ fail 0
```

---

## What was retired, and what replaced it

**Retired.** The LED chat, the Agent 0 banner fetch to `http://localhost:3100`, the "Agent 0 Connected / Demo Mode" status, the name prompt, the voice playback, and `app/api/kiosk/session` with its `MINIMAX_API_KEY` dependency. The widget asked a walk-in for their name on a shared screen and posted it to its own voice route, which persisted nothing.

**Replaced by the standee.** Brand mark (inline SVG spiral vortex per DESIGN.md — no remote logo fetch to fail at the lounge), one QR, the canon ladder as plain text, Arie's WhatsApp line, and an honest status word. One primary action on the screen.

```
DR MAGfield
Experience Lounge · Kelab Rahman Putra Malaysia
Turn pain into pure performance.
RM65    Single session · 60 min   DRM-SINGLE-60
RM325   Package                   DRM-PKG5
RM1500  Package                   DRM-PKG7
What each package includes is confirmed at the lounge, not on this screen.
WhatsApp Arie Ong · +6012-659 5319
Scan to open the lounge page
https://app.longevityvalley.ai/scan/dr-magfield/krpm
This screen collects nothing. Scanning opens the lounge's own page on your phone.
Lounge status · Unmeasured          Sessions by appointment
drm-standee v2 · local · unknown
```

**The ladder prints no package session count, on purpose.** T1's ambiguity register AMB-1 still holds RM325 at 5 sessions (engine fixtures, served landing) against 6 (partnership canon "5+1"), and RM1500 at 7 against 7+1. A standee cannot resolve that, so it prints the canon price and the SKU and sends the question to the coordinator. A test enforces it.

**Env-only, no localhost default.** `NEXT_PUBLIC_DOORWAY_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_STANDEE_STATUS_URL` are the only inputs. The status endpoint has no default at all: unconfigured reads `Unmeasured`, never a fabricated "Connected".

---

## The census drove a design change

The first implementation refused loopback with a **denylist**. It worked. The bundle census still went RED:

```
✖ census: 0 occurrences of localhost in the served home chunk
  AssertionError: page-966dce912f5e96e9.js still embeds localhost
  2 !== 0
```

Both hits were the guard's own `'localhost'` string literal, minified into the chunk. **The guard minted the condition it measures** — and any future `grep localhost` on the served bundle would have read the cure as the defect.

Replaced with a positive **allowlist** (`*.longevityvalley.ai`, `*.vercel.app`): loopback loses by construction, no forbidden string ships, and foreign hosts nobody thought to deny are refused too. This is why the assertion is on the built bundle and not on the source — a source grep would have called the widget clean on 07-08 as well.

**One `localhost` remains anywhere under `.next/static/`**, and it is not ours:

```
$ grep -rl localhost .next/static/
.next/static/chunks/polyfills-78c92fac7aa8fdd8.js
```

That is core-js's WHATWG-URL polyfill implementing the file-scheme `localhost` rule, shipped by Next 14.2.5 itself. It is not a doorway and not reachable as one.

---

## EV-8 — quarantined, not retired

`/rabbit-cup` and `/rabbit-cup/success` render only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_RABBIT_CUP_ENABLED === 'true'`. The gate is a **lazy** import, so the fence holds in the bytes and not only in the render.

```
flag unset (default build):
  grep -o 'Online sign-up is not available' .next/server/app/rabbit-cup.html
    → Online sign-up is not available
  grep -c 'rabbit-cup/register' .next/static/chunks/app/rabbit-cup/page-*.js
    → 0
  grep -rl 'rabbit-cup/register' .next/static/chunks/
    → .next/static/chunks/687.f0e9239fa5d124f2.js     (present, never requested)

NEXT_PUBLIC_RABBIT_CUP_ENABLED=true npm run build:
  grep -c 'Online sign-up is not available' .next/server/app/rabbit-cup.html
    → 0
  the page chunk now references chunk 687 — the rail comes back whole
```

So it is a switch, not a deletion. The 388-line register form and the 165-line receipt view moved to `RegisterForm.tsx` / `ReceiptView.tsx` unchanged except for the component name and a quarantine header.

---

## Keith's doors — this PR decides neither

- **S-C · dispose of the legacy rabbit-cup rail.** This branch **quarantines** it (flag off by default, code intact, reversible by one env var). **Retire vs quarantine is yours.** If retire: delete `app/rabbit-cup/**` and the two fence tests. If quarantine stands: set nothing, and the flag stays off in production.
- **N12 · the repo is PUBLIC** (`longevityvalleykeith/dr-magfield-kiosk`), ungoverned by law. Unchanged by this branch. Nothing secret was added; the only phone number in the diff is the business line already published on `main` and on the landing site.

## Also for the morning, not decided here

- `app/globals.css` still carries the dead `.kiosk` / `.agent-panel` / `.name-prompt` rules. The standee uses a new CSS module on the same DESIGN.md tokens, and `globals.css` is **not** in this lane's file ownership, so it was not edited. A sweep is a one-line follow-up.
- `app/layout.tsx` metadata references `/manifest.json`, which does not exist in `public/` — a 404 on every load, present since before this branch. Lane K's layout mandate is "stamp only", so it was left alone.
- Next 14.2.5 has a published security advisory (the `npm ci` warning, and 46 Dependabot alerts on the default branch). Out of this lane's scope; flagged, not touched.

npm start -- -p 3411

author: alpcaner
body:
## Summary

Closes #1846.

`tas2563_init()` wrote its init sequence to the **broadcast** address `0x48`. On a bus where an INA236 also sits at `0x48`, that means codec init lands in the INA236's `CONFIG` register — one driver silently reprogramming another device.

The guard is in `addr_is_valid()`, which is the single choke point: every bus-touching entry point gates on `ctx->initialised`, so nothing can reach `0x48` any more.

Review found the guard was at the right layer but **documented a mechanism that was wrong**; the comments and commit message now describe what the code actually does. That is the same defect class as #1889 in the previous batch — a comment that misdescribes a guard is trusted by the next person debugging it.

## Scope note

The V2M/EVK `0x48` collisions (#1659, #1163) are separate, silicon-gated metadata questions and are deliberately **not** touched here. This is the driver-side refusal only. No I2C address value is changed.

## Process

Authored on an isolated worktree branch, independently reviewed by a separate
agent running this repo's gates, then the reviewer's confirmed findings fixed in
follow-up commits. Findings that could be refuted with evidence were reported and
left alone rather than "fixed".

Not bench-tested: nothing here touches silicon behaviour.

author: easly1989
body:
## Summary

Adds **Enable Banking** as a second bank-sync provider (after SimpleFIN, #309), covering **EU/EEA + UK** accounts via PSD2 open banking — on the same **bring-your-own-credentials** model, so the **project pays nothing and there's no fundraising**. The user registers their **own** Enable Banking application (a **free sandbox** to build/test, their **own production** app for real accounts — production is the gated/paid tier they bring themselves), pastes the **app id + RSA private key**, and connects banks. CloudBank stores the credentials **server-side (never returned to the client)** and signs every API call with a **JWT (RS256, `kid = app id`)**.

> This replaces the earlier idea of a fundraising drive for EU bank sync: with Enable Banking's free sandbox + a BYO-production model, the feature can ship now and each user supplies (and pays for) their own production access.

Closes #310 · part of #285

## Model (verified against Enable Banking's docs)

Per-wallet **config** (app id + private key), configured once → multiple **bank connections** via the OAuth-style flow: `GET /aspsps` (pick bank) → `POST /auth` (redirect the user to their bank) → callback with `code` → `POST /sessions {code}` (→ session id + account uids) → `GET /accounts/{uid}/transactions`. Linked accounts sync through the **existing import pipeline** (dedup + assignment rules — reused from SimpleFIN).

## Changes

**Backend**
- Migration `0025`: per-wallet `bank_ebanking_config` (app id + secret private key) + `bank_ebanking_auth` (pending OAuth state). Enable Banking connections **reuse `bank_connections`** (`provider='enablebanking'`, `access_url` = session id) with added `aspsp`/consent-validity columns.
- `internal/banksync`: an Enable Banking client — **hand-rolled RS256 JWT (no extra dependency)**; `/aspsps`, `/auth`, `/sessions`, `/accounts/*` — with the same **injectable HTTP transport**. `CB_ENABLEBANKING_BASE_URL` points it at a local stub for testing. The service: configure credentials, list banks, start auth, complete auth on callback, list remote accounts (+ balances), link/unlink, and **sync** — signed amounts (`credit_debit_indicator`), dedup by entry reference (hash fallback). `remoteAccounts`/`Sync`/`Remove` branch by provider.
- Wallet-scoped endpoints; openapi + generated types.

**Frontend**
- Bank sync page: **two provider cards** (SimpleFIN, Enable Banking). An Enable Banking config panel that **shows the exact redirect URL to whitelist**, the environment and app id; a connect flow (pick country + bank → redirect to the bank); a `/bank-sync/callback` route that finishes the connection. `en` + `it`.

body:
💡 What was confusing or wrong
The documentation for `PipelinePhaseMetadata` and `createShallowSnapshot` falsely claimed that `pure: true` would skip snapshotting, and heavily implied that limiting `touches` to an empty array would optimize snapshots away.

🎯 Who hits this and when
Any developer (human or AI) authoring a new pipeline phase and attempting to optimize it by declaring it pure or passing an empty touches array. They would expect zero snapshotting overhead, but would silently trigger a full deep-clone of all trackable entities.

🔬 How each claim was verified
- Read `runPipeline`: The `pure` property is never accessed on `phaseMeta`.
- Read `createShallowSnapshot`: The `touches` array is checked with `touches && touches.length > 0`. An empty array fails this check, causing it to fall back to `[...ENTITY_MAP_FIELDS]`.
- Verified via isolated scratchpad execution.

🐛 Any actual bugs discovered
The snapshotting fallback logic overriding both `pure` and `touches: []`. Scribe's job is not to fix it here, but the journal entry logs this trap.

author: jianminzhao
body:
…rce key

HeapDict::setting() couldn't distinguish two different reasons a slot can be empty for a key that exists in _source: a slot just created to shadow that key for the first time (already counted, no increment needed), versus a tombstone left behind by an earlier remove() or removeAll() (which already decremented _count, so re-setting it must increment). Both look identical -- empty slot, key present in _source -- so the increment was always skipped, leaving _count one too low after remove()-then-set() (or removeAll()-then-set()) on a source key.

That undercount corrupts kvArray(): it sizes its cache array from the (wrong, too-low) count(), then the correct iterator overruns it, an out-of-bounds write that HeapArray::setting()'s bounds check only catches in debug builds (#if DEBUG) -- in shipping builds it silently corrupts the heap. This is the root cause of the crashes reported in CBSE-23608 (VectorRecord::setRemoteRevision performs exactly this remove-then-set pattern on load-then-save of a synced document).

Fix: track whether the slot pre-existed the call (a tombstone) versus was just created (a fresh shadow of a source key), and increment count() in the former case.

Adds two regression tests (remove() and removeAll() variants) that fail with the old count() and pass with the fix; verified against the full Fleece test suite with no new failures.

author: simenb
body:
## Summary

Fixes #16420.

Webpack inlines `require('../package.json')` into each bundle. A release builds first and lets Lerna bump every `package.json` afterwards, so the published bundles carry the version from before the bump — `@jest/core@30.5.1` ships `"version":"30.5.0"` in its `build/index.js`, and `30.2.0` ships `30.1.3`. `jest --version` and `--debug` print that stale value. `jest-haste-map` and `@jest/transform` read the same constant into their cache keys, so those are labelled one release behind too.

29.7.0 was unaffected: that build emitted one file per module with a real runtime `require`. It regressed in #12348, which moved the build to webpack.

Marking the request external restores the runtime `require`. `webpackIgnore` is not an option — webpack honours it on `import()` and `new URL()`, not on CommonJS `require`; with the magic comment in place the output still reads `__webpack_require__(/* webpackIgnore: true */"./package.json")` and the JSON is still emitted as a module.

The external path is relative to the bundle rather than to the importing source file, so `logDebugMessages.ts` asking for `../../package.json` from `src/lib` lands in the same place as `version.ts` asking for `../package.json`. No source changes needed.

## Test plan

After `yarn build:js`, no `"version":"30.x.y"` literal is left in the `jest-core`, `jest-transform` or `jest-haste-map` bundles, and each contains `module.exports = require("../package.json")`.

Editing `packages/jest-core/package.json` to `99.9.9` *after* building, then running `node packages/jest-cli/bin/jest.js --version`, prints `99.9.9-dev` — the built output reads the file at run time.

`grep -rln 'require("../package.json")' packages/*/build/` matches only the three flat `build/index.js` files. The external assumes a chunk at `build/*.js`; the one nested entry in the build, `jest-jasmine2`'s `jasmine/jasmineLight.js`, does not touch `package.json`.

## What

The `@claude review` workflow now loads the Simple English plugin (https://github.com/AminBlg/SimpleEnglish, v2.0.0) and selects its `simple-english:simple-english` output style in `settings:`. This replaces the built-in `Concise` style. The reviewer gets the same skill and SessionStart rule hook the maintainer runs locally.

## How

- One extra `actions/checkout` step fetches `AminBlg/SimpleEnglish` at the v2.0.0 commit (`d9e52340…`) into `simple-english/`, beside `pr-head/`.
- `claude_args` gains `--plugin-dir ${{ github.workspace }}/simple-english`.
- `settings:` becomes `{"outputStyle": "simple-english:simple-english"}`.

## Why not the action's `plugins:` inputs

They run `claude plugin marketplace add` against the upstream HEAD with no pin, and a failed install aborts the review. The checkout is SHA-pinned like every `uses:` here, needs no network on the review path, and a pull request cannot alter it.

## What runs on the runner

The SessionStart hook (node) and the Stop hook (python3, advisory). The PostToolUse hook matches Write|Edit, which the reviewer is not allowed, so it never fires.

## Verification

- `uvx zizmor`: no findings. `actionlint` (with shellcheck): clean.
- `claude --plugin-dir <dir> plugin list` on CLI 2.1.257 loads the plugin as `simple-english@inline`. The action installs CLI 2.1.252, which has `--plugin-dir` (present since before 2.1.129 per the changelog).
- Not trialled from this PR: `issue_comment` runs the default-branch copy of the workflow. Verify on the first `@claude review` after merge. An output style that does not resolve degrades silently, so check the review's register.

Bump the plugin SHA by hand. Renovate does not track a `ref:` under `with:`.

author: chriszarate
body:
When the server sets an edit aside for a person to review, both engines now store it under the same name: `parked`.

## What changed

Before this change, the two engines that have a review lane used different names for the same kind of row in the room log:

- intent-log wrote `proposal` rows.
- de-rtc wrote `proposal-parked` rows.

Both now write `parked`. The `resolved` row that closes a parked edit is unchanged.

These are the code names for it:

- `WP_Intent_Log_Engine::UPDATE_TYPE_PARKED`
- `WP_De_RTC_Engine::UPDATE_TYPE_PARKED`
- `INTENT_LOG_UPDATE_TYPES.PARKED`
- `DE_RTC_PARKED_TYPE`

The browser wire inspector decodes the shared row type for both engines, since each engine stores different details inside it.

## Why `parked`

The glossary already uses "park" to mean exactly this: an edit that is saved but not applied, waiting for someone to decide. It also pairs naturally with the `resolved` row that closes it.

`proposal` could not be the shared name. In de-rtc, a proposal is an attempt by someone's browser to merge the whole document, so reusing that word for a parked edit would have been confusing.

## Things to know

- Rooms written before this change are not migrated. They keep their old row names. This is by design.
- The frozen intent-log core and its test vectors never named this row type, so they are untouched.
- The new name shows up in the browser wire inspector and in the `wp collaboration rooms` diagnostics.
- CHANGELOG.md, the glossary, and the engine comparison doc are updated.

## Testing

Existing Jest and PHPUnit tests are updated to the new row name.

author: open-coder-ai
body:
## What

Bumps the `agentseam` pin from 0.1.1 to 0.2.0 (the post-ACS release: canonical outcome word `escalate`, `ask` kept only as a deprecated alias) and fixes the incompatibility a pin-bump dry run proved, in the same PR — neither half is green alone. `src/chock/evidence.py` conflated two vocabularies: it validated `claims.json`'s `verdict` field (which records the **vendor's wire word** — claude witnesses `"ask"`, codex degrades and witnesses `"deny"`) against agentseam's **canonical** constants, and derived the fail-to-ask lift by `verdict == contract.ASK`. Under 0.1.1 that worked only because canonical and wire words coincided; under 0.2.0 (`contract.ASK` == `"escalate"`) it rejected the witnessed `"ask"` at load and would have silently turned a crashed guard's ask into a deny.

The fix makes the semantics explicit rather than coincidental:

- Each `claims.json` row now carries **both** the witnessed wire word (`verdict`, validated against a chock-owned wire vocabulary — `evidence.WIRE_VERDICTS` — which a live-runtime test recomputes from the fixtures) and an explicit **`honours` boolean**; `honours_ask` derives from the semantic field alone. Mutation tests pin that the old conflation cannot return: deriving by equality with any verdict constant (canonical or wire) fails one of the two pinned rows, and a canonical word (`"escalate"`) posing as a wire verdict is refused at load.
- Wire words stay wire data: no witnessed `"ask"` was rewritten.
- Where chock speaks **to** agentseam it now uses the canonical post-ACS words: `guard_runner.VERDICT_ASK` (`"ask"`) became `VERDICT_ESCALATE` (`"escalate"`), and the vendored dispatch uses `Decision.escalate(...) if outcome == ESCALATE`. Every vendored-runtime fixture now runs under `-W error::DeprecationWarning`, so a deprecated spelling cannot ship silently on any exercised path. `test_chocks_verdict_words_are_agentseams_own` is re-homed onto `contract.ESCALATE`/`contract.DENY`, keeping its intent (chock's stdlib-only literals cannot drift from agentseam's contract).
- Pin bumped in `pyproject.toml` and `requirements/brand-assets.in`; `brand-assets.txt` regenerated with pip-compile (hashes match PyPI's published 0.2.0 artifacts); `.chock/bin/*` runtimes regenerated via `chock sync --repo .`.
- **Frozen binary** (second commit, from CI's `binary (ubuntu-latest)` smoke failure): agentseam 0.2.0 loads `data/vendors/*.json` at import, while 0.1.1 shipped no data files — so the PyInstaller one-file binary built but died in `chock init` with `FileNotFoundError` from `agentseam._data.load()`. `packaging/chock.spec` now collects agentseam's data files (`collect_data_files("agentseam")`); reproduced locally first, and the full CI smoke sequence passes on the rebuilt binary.

**Behavior contract held**: crashed-guard handling is byte-for-byte today's on every agent — ask where ask (claude_code, vscode_copilot, cursor), deny where codex_cli degrades — proven by the unchanged intent of `test_guard_fail_to_ask.py`, and no day-one coverage word moves (`test_todays_words_all_clear_their_cap` unchanged and green). No chock version bump.

## Definition of done

- [x] `chock check` → 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 infos
- [x] `chock check --only matrix` passes; matrix updated in this PR if behavior changed (no behavior change)
- [x] `chock sync --repo . --check` clean (compiled artifacts match their manifests)
