body:
## Summary

Closes #1712. Closes #1855.

`--emit scaffold --template multicore-rpmsg` emitted a tree that **could not build**: no root `CMakeLists.txt`, no `prj.conf`, a referenced-but-unemitted `linux/src/main.c`, and a generated-dir path pointing outside the project. A scaffold that cannot build is worse than none — it looks like a starting point and is a dead end.

The failure sequence was established by **emitting a scaffold and trying to build it**, not by reading the emitter: `cmake -S . -B build` at the project root gives `does not appear to contain CMakeLists.txt`, and `linux/` gives `Cannot find source file`.

#1855 is the same area: catalog entries named alp-sdk-only paths bare in generated comments, so a customer scaffold referenced paths that do not exist for them.

## The over-correction review caught

The first pass fixed #1855 by rewriting bare paths to GitHub URLs — including paths that **are** part of the emitted tree. `multicore-mailbox` emits `peer/main.c` in the same envelope, yet `src/main.c` rendered that sibling as a github.com URL pointing out of the customer's project.

The rewrite is now aware of the scaffold's own emitted file set: an in-scaffold path stays a relative in-project reference, and only genuinely alp-sdk-only paths become URLs. A test emits a scaffold and asserts the in-scaffold sibling reference is not rewritten.

## Process

Authored on an isolated worktree branch, independently reviewed by a separate
agent running this repo's gates, then the reviewer's confirmed findings fixed in
follow-up commits. Findings that could be refuted with evidence were reported and
left alone rather than "fixed".

Not bench-tested: nothing here touches silicon behaviour.

author: frikkern
body:
## Two halves, both emitter-side

`chat_approval_html/1`, `chat_question_html/1` and `chat_plan_html/1` each read `approval_status` straight off the block and hand it to `chat_card_header/2` → `chat_status_label/1`, whose last clause is a catch-all `to_string(other)`. The folding function that *would* confine it — `chat_approval_status/1` (`pending | allowed | denied | canceled`, fail-open to `pending`) — sits a few lines below and was never called on this path, although all three **block builders** already use it.

The word then landed in a span carrying an **inline** `white-space: nowrap`. Being inline it beats every stylesheet rule, so no `paper-surface.css` change could ever reach it.

## Criteria

**0 — the html emitters fold `approval_status` through the known vocabulary before rendering.** Met, for all three (the row named plan + question; approval had the same hole and additionally branched its *title* on the raw value, so it is folded too — an unrecognized status now correctly still reads "Allow Bash?", i.e. still awaiting you).

**1 — the status span can no longer force one unbreakable line.** Met. `white-space: nowrap` is gone from `chat_card_header/2`, replaced by `min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere;` — the guard a shrink-to-fit flex item actually needs, since only `anywhere` reduces the intrinsic width the box is sized from and `min-width: 0` lets the item shrink below its content size at all. The same guard goes on the title span, which had none either. Pinned by a test asserting `refute html =~ "nowrap"` on all three cards.

**2 — a rendered 390px measurement shows `scrollWidth == innerWidth` for all three fixtures with a 44-character `approval_status`.** Met.

```
chrome-headless-shell 148.0.7778.167, container CSS transcribed from
api/assets/paper-editor/src/__narrow_render.mjs, status =
"awaiting-operator-decision-2026-08-24T11:23Z" (44 chars)

--- BEFORE (origin/main emitter) ---
FAIL  chat-approval  scrollWidth=433px  innerWidth=390px
FAIL  chat-plan      scrollWidth=450px  innerWidth=390px
FAIL  chat-question  scrollWidth=466px  innerWidth=390px

--- AFTER (this branch) ---
PASS  chat-approval  scrollWidth=390px  innerWidth=390px
PASS  chat-plan      scrollWidth=390px  innerWidth=390px
PASS  chat-question  scrollWidth=390px  innerWidth=390px

--- AFTER @320px ---
PASS  chat-approval  scrollWidth=320px  innerWidth=320px
PASS  chat-plan      scrollWidth=320px  innerWidth=320px
PASS  chat-question  scrollWidth=320px  innerWidth=320px
```

My before-numbers are 433/450/466 where the row recorded 450/483/475 — same defect, same direction; the delta is a different 44-character string and a different Chrome build.

**Instrument note.** The first run of this measurement reported `innerWidth=500px` for a `--window-size=390,900`: Chrome on macOS clamps its window to a 500px minimum, so every fixture "passed" against a viewport that did not exist. `chrome-headless-shell` honours the size. Anyone re-running `__narrow_render.mjs` with `BP_CHROME` pointed at full Chrome on macOS gets a silently vacuous green.

**Which half carries the geometry.** Measured separately: with the 44-char status still present and *only* the span clamped, all three already read 390/390. So the clamp is independently sufficient for criterion 2, and the fold is what closes the arbitrary-text hole (criteria 0 and 3). Neither is redundant.

**3 — a test reds when an arbitrary `approval_status` reaches the output unfolded, and the mutation lands.** Met, proven in **both** directions:

```
MUTATION 1 — revert the three folds, keep the clamp:
  47 tests, 3 failures
    1) chat_question_html/1 never lets an arbitrary status reach the output
    2) chat_approval_html/1 never lets an arbitrary status reach the output
    3) chat_plan_html/1  never lets an arbitrary status reach the output
  (the clamp test stays GREEN)

MUTATION 2 — restore the inline nowrap, keep the fold:
  47 tests, 1 failure
    1) the header carries NO inline white-space:nowrap — the declaration CSS cannot beat
  (the three fold tests stay GREEN)

RESTORED: 47 tests, 0 failures
```

The fold lives in the three html emitters and **nowhere else** — deliberately *not* doubled inside `chat_card_header/2` or `chat_status_label/1`. A second layer would make exactly this mutation not land, and a mutation that cannot land is not a catch.

A fourth test pins that the **known** vocabulary survives: `pending`, `✓ allowed`, `⊘ denied`, `— canceled` still render their labels on all three cards, so the fold is not a blanket neutralizer.

## Goldens

`api/test/support/fixtures/pd-parity/chat-{approval,plan,question}.golden.json` and their `js/packages/react/tests/fixtures/pd-golden/` mirrors are regenerated with `mix barkpark.portable_doc.gen_pd_parity`, which is the sole writer of **both** mirrors and writes them atomically — regenerating the api mirror alone would red the mirror-identity lock. Only `expectedHtml` moves; the `shape` projection (tag / class-set / `data-*` / text) is unchanged, which is why the JS renderer stays shape-equal without a source change. The generator rewrote all 64 types × 2 mirrors; only these 3 × 2 differed.

The `chat_golden_toolrows` fixture is **not** affected: its three chat card variants all carry `approval_status: "pending"`, already in the vocabulary, and it stores the block map + projection text, not rendered HTML. Its parity test is in the gate run below, green unchanged.

## Gates

```
mix test components_test.exs pd_golden_parity_test.exs component_golden_parity_test.exs
         view_edit_parity_test.exs chat_golden_toolrows_parity_test.exs
         chat_render_golden_test.exs chat_live_test.exs
  → 639 tests, 0 failures

mix format --check-formatted <the two files I touched>  → exit 0
scripts/studio-literal-check.sh                          → exit 0
```

Two earlier runs of that same set flaked under machine load — once on the sidebar byte-lock, once on six `argv-echo :binary fake` marker-file tests. Different tests each time, none touching this change, all green in isolation (`chat_render_golden_test.exs` alone: 8/0; `chat_live_test.exs` alone: 296/0) and green on the re-run above.

**Note on `mix format --check-formatted` repo-wide:** it exits 1 on `origin/main`, naming three files this PR does not touch and which are byte-identical to `origin/main` here. Pre-existing.

## Known gap, out of fence

`js/packages/react/src/blocks/chat.ts` carries the **twin of both defects** — `chatStatusLabel`'s `default: return status` and the same inline `white-space: nowrap` in `chatCardHeader`. The parity assertion is shape-only, so it can see neither. Outside this task's fence; needs its own row.

body:
## Why
Guard A (cross-surface consistency, measured THROUGH Raven) has been red on every parity run today:

```
DISAGREE gaps-axis-vs-type-counts   analyze?dimension=gaps byType: 8 · searchProjects?type=<same>: 7 ["Yield (rejected)"]
DISAGREE typed-rows-are-reachable   a type present on real rows: 6 · searchProjects?type=<that type>: 5 ["Yield"]
```

Reproduced through Raven's own codemode client: `scout.searchProjects({ type: "Yield" })` → `ok:false`, `error/0ms` (rejected client-side against their pinned catalog, spec 1.9.1; `Yield` shipped in 1.9.13). `type: "Wallet"` → ok in 479 ms. Our API serves 8 Yield rows directly. That is catalog lag on their side, not two of our surfaces disagreeing — exactly the class the guard rules say to report, not gate (`feedback_catalog_lag_is_not_drift`).

## What
- When Raven rejects a type probe, the guard asks our API directly (`/api/projects/search?type=T&limit=1`); a member we serve is printed as `catalog-lag` and not counted as a disagreement.
- Both count-pair snippets now return the full unreachable list with `(rejected)` / `(0 rows)` suffixes, so classification is per member (a `(0 rows)` entry still disagrees).

## Gate
Live run with `--gate`: **6 consistent · 0 disagreeing · 0 errored**, two `catalog-lag: ["Yield"]` lines. biome clean · `typecheck:scripts` 42, unchanged.

body:
The *Producing attestations* section named the producer but not the guard at the producer's elbow. An attestation is only as honest as the push that produced it, and the way a push gets dishonest in practice is a coding agent masking its failure — `git push … 2>&1 | tail -5` reports tail's exit status, so a rejected push reads as success. [amont-agent](https://github.com/fredericrous/amont-agent) refuses that command shape before it runs.

Framed honestly: independent of this verifier, related by author and by the shared conviction — trust what was verified, never what was reported.

Part of a three-PR set closing the cross-reference holes: fredericrous/amont#224 names all three companions on amont's front page; fredericrous/amont-agent#7 is the mirror-image line there.

author: jul-27
body:
Vier Punkte in einem Zug.

## 1. Formationswahl als Bild

Statt `TW · LV · IV · IV · RV · DM · DM · LA · OM · RA · MS` — vollständig, aber niemand setzt elf Abkürzungen im Kopf zu einer Aufstellung zusammen — steht jede Formation als Miniaturfeld mit elf Punkten da, Torwart in Gold. Dieselben Koordinaten wie das große Feld, die Vorschau stimmt also mit dem überein, was danach gespielt wird.

## 2. Ratings: 65 bis 96

| | vorher | jetzt |
|---|---|---|
| Spanne | 50–98 | **65–96** |
| Median | 58 | **70** |
| ≥ 90 je Liga | 8–11 | **8–14** |
| Anteil aller Saisonwerte ≥ 90 | 1,3–1,8 % | **1,0–1,3 %** |
| Anteil ≥ 85 | – | **3,7–4,9 %** |

Die Skala beginnt bei 65, weil jeder, der es in einen Kader der drei größten Ligen geschafft hat, Profi ist. Die Spanne ist dadurch enger, und der Unterschied zwischen Ergänzungsspieler und Star muss aus der Kurve kommen statt aus der Skalenbreite.

Wenige Einsätze drücken jetzt stärker (Boden von 0,55 auf 0,42). **Fehlende Einsatzzahlen dürfen aber nicht bestrafen** — Wikidata führt sie nur bei 73 % der Stationen, Matthäus und Xavi tragen gar keine. Wo sie fehlt, wird sie aus den Jahren geschätzt (25 je Saison), die immer vorliegen.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Bundesliga** | Neuer 96 · Lahm 96 · Ballack 96 · Lewandowski 96 |
| **Premier League** | Cech 96 · Terry 96 · Lampard 96 · Cristiano Ronaldo 96 |
| **La Liga** | Casillas 96 · Ramos 96 · Iniesta 96 · Messi 96 |

## 3. Die echte Liga

Die Elf trat gegen zusammengewürfelte Jahrgänge an — Bayern 2014 gegen Werder 1996 in derselben Tabelle. Jetzt spielt sie in der **Bundesliga 2025/26**, der **Premier League 2024/25** oder **La Liga 2025/26** und verdrängt dort einen zufällig gewählten Verein, damit die Liga wieder achtzehn bzw. zwanzig Mannschaften hat.

Die Saison 2026/27 gibt die Datenlage noch nicht her: Wikidata führt dort null Teilnehmer, in England fehlt sogar 2025/26. Sobald sie gefüllt ist, genügt ein erneuter Lauf des Skripts — ohne Codeänderung.

### Zwei neue Pipeline-Skripte

**`wikidata_league_clubs.mjs`** — 108 Vereine mit Saisonzugehörigkeit ab 2010/11 (P3450 Saison, P1923 Teilnehmer), 79 davon neu.

Wikidata führt für viele Vereine **zwei Einträge**: den Verein und die Männermannschaft. Ältere Saisons verlinken den einen, neuere den anderen — die Bundesliga 2025/26 verlinkt *ausschließlich* die leeren Hüllen:

```
FC Bayern München  Q15789     Fußballverein            824 Spieler
FC Bayern München  Q97905919  Herrenfußballmannschaft    2 Spieler
```

Ohne Auflösung hätte die neueste Saison achtzehn Vereine ohne einen einzigen Spieler. Aufgelöst über den Namen (unter Gleichnamigen gewinnt der mit den meisten Spielern); vier Sonderfälle — Heidenheim, Arminia Bielefeld, Holstein Kiel, Bochum — erscheinen nur in Saisons mit Hülle und werden über `P361` nachgebessert. Der Namensweg allein hätte Heidenheim nicht gefunden: Der Verein heißt dort „1. FC Heidenheim 1846".

**`wikidata_league_squads.mjs`** — deren Kader als datierte Stationen: **822 neue Spieler, 3.561 ergänzte Karrieren, 13.210 Stationen**, Bestand jetzt 32.359.

Geschrieben wird nur `cp`, **nicht `clubs`**: Das Feld führt die 47 Spielvereine mit Hexfeldern und Wappen, und die neuen sind ausdrücklich keine. Ein Eintrag dort würde Hex, Raster und Transferkarussell verändern, ohne dass jemand darum gebeten hätte.

### Sehen die Ligen echt aus?

| Bundesliga 2025/26 | |
|---|---|
| Spitze | Bayern 92,9 · Dortmund 79,4 · Leverkusen 79,1 |
| Keller | Heidenheim 60,3 · St. Pauli 59,0 |

Testlauf: Meister mit 81 Punkten vor Bayern (74), 87:26 Tore.

## 4. Saisonurkunde

Als **SVG gezeichnet** und per Leinwand in ein PNG mit **1800×2480** verwandelt. Ohne Bibliothek und ohne externe Bilder — deshalb bleibt die Leinwand sauber und lässt sich überhaupt auslesen. `html2canvas` hätte die HTML-Karte abgelichtet: weniger Arbeit, aber unschärfer und bei Schriften unzuverlässig.

Systemschriften, weil ein als Bild geladenes SVG die Webfonts des Dokuments nicht sieht — sonst stünde im PNG etwas anderes als auf dem Bildschirm. Keine Gesichter, nur Namen, Positionen und Jahre.

## Drei Fehler, die dabei auffielen

**Zidane war verschwenden — und mit ihm jede Saison vor 2010.** Seit `baueZiehungen` die Ligazugehörigkeit beachtet (damit Kaiserslautern 2020 nicht im Bundesliga-Topf landet) und die Ligalisten erst 2010 beginnen, war Real Madrid nur noch ab 2010 ziehbar. Für die 47 Spielvereine, bei denen Karrieredaten bis 1995 vorliegen, bleiben die Jahre davor jetzt offen. Die Beispielurkunde zeigt Lahm 2003, Frings 2001 und Herzog 1998.

**Drei vandalierte Wikidata-Labels kamen als neue Spieler durch.** Live in Wikidata heißt Wayne Rooney auf Englisch „El Perrito de la C", Juan Mata „Juan Mata Pata", Aubameyang „Pierre Cardin picha grande". Mein Skript fragte nur englische Labels ab; die deutschen waren sauber. Ursache behoben („de,en" wie der Rest der Pipeline), Folgen über `NAME_OVERRIDES` verschmolzen — jeder Eintrag per QID belegt, wie die Tabelle es verlangt.

**`teamStaerke` füllte dünne Kader mit 50 auf**, obwohl die Skala inzwischen bei 65 beginnt. St. Pauli stand dadurch mit 59 unter dem eigenen Skalenboden. Der Boden ist jetzt eine exportierte Konstante statt einer hingeschriebenen Zahl.

Dazu hat der Datenlauf 25 kuratierte Namenskorrekturen überschrieben — die Pipeline-Reihenfolge ist nachgeholt, und beide neuen Skripte stehen jetzt an ihrer Stelle in `refresh_all.mjs`, damit ein Vollabgleich sie mitnimmt.

## Geprüft

- **513 Tests grün.** Neu: die echte Liga (Vollzähligkeit, Gefälle, Verdrängung genau eines Vereins), das Auffüllen dünner Kader, die Klassenkurve auf der neuen Skala, die Schätzung fehlender Einsätze
- Drei Testfehler, die der Datenlauf ausgelöst hat, waren echte Befunde und keine Testartefakte — überschriebene Namenskorrekturen, inkonsistenter Datenstempel, eine Poolgrößen-Schwelle aus der Zeit vor den Ligakadern
- Im Browser durchgespielt: Ligawahl mit echten Saisons, Draft (erste Ziehung Werder Bremen 2001), laufende Simulation, Saisonkarte, Urkunde samt PNG-Export

body:
## 為什麼要記

這批頁面的維護知識目前只存在做過的人腦袋裡。下個月要更新時，光是找回各家上游的網址與解析方式就要重來一次，更麻煩的是那些不查就會錯的地方。

## 放哪

`docs/CHANGELOG_SOURCES.md`。`docs_dir` 指向語系目錄（`zh-TW` 等），所以 `docs/` 根目錄的檔案不會被建置成頁面，跟既有的 `docs/README.md` 同一層。已經跑過 `sh run.sh` 確認 `output/` 裡沒有多出這一頁。

## 內容

四塊：十二頁的上游對照表、七個會踩的坑、急迫程度分級的判準、寫作與流程的注意事項。

**七個坑裡有兩個這次真的踩到了：**

- MSRC 的嚴重度是每個受影響產品各記一筆，同一顆 CVE 平均對應五個多產品。直接數 Critical 會膨脹好幾倍，2026 年 8 月直接數是 721，以相異 CVE 計只有 134
- GrapheneOS 發布說明裡的「List of additional fixed CVEs」是 security preview release 提前套用未來數月公告的累積清單，誤讀成當月涵蓋範圍的話整頁數據就失去意義

其餘五個：Android 公告網址 2026 年起多一層年份目錄且 7 月起無明細、c-tor 的 ChangeLog 在 `main` 不是最新的要從 tag 讀、同一個安全釋出常有多個 TROVE 編號不能只挑前幾個寫、WebTunnel 沒有 ChangeLog、MSRC 的項目總數涵蓋整個產品線而 Windows 本體只佔一小部分。

**急迫程度那一節**記下六頁的判準基礎不同（有的看證據、有的看官方發布形式），以及哪些頁刻意不套標籤與原因。這是最容易在後續維護中被弄混的地方。

**寫作與流程**記三件事：術語解釋要寫在最新的條目（由新到舊排，寫在最舊那則讀者會先撞牆）、批次處理版本號要比對完整標題行（`7.10` 的正則會吃到 `7.10.1`）、front matter 的 `description` 含冒號空格會讓整組 YAML 解析失敗而 mkdocs 不報錯。

## CLAUDE.md

在「Docs 文件網站」那節加一段指引指過去，並把最容易誤判的那兩個坑直接寫在指引裡，這樣不點進去也知道要當心什麼。

## 驗證

- `docs_style_lint.py` 掃新檔案 0 error 0 warn，我加進 `CLAUDE.md` 的段落也乾淨（該檔既有的兩處分號違規不在這次範圍，且 `CLAUDE.md` 不在 CI 觸發路徑）
- `sh run.sh` 建置通過，`output/` 沒有多出頁面

author: rjrodger
body:
Publishing stopped halfway on 0.34.0, and the `master` → `main` rename took CI with it. This fixes both, updates the Pages render of `docs/`, untracks `.claude/`, and cuts `v0.34.1` so a release exists that went the whole way.

## What was wrong

**The release ended early.** npm serves `jostraca@0.34.0`, but there is no `v0.34.0` tag behind it and no `go/v0.34.0` at all — so the Go module never shipped 0.34.0 and is still on `0.33.1`. For Go the tag is not a record of the release, it *is* the release: the module proxy serves the module straight from `go/vX.Y.Z`. A workflow that published npm and stopped left one stack unreleased and looked green doing it.

It was also unrecoverable: a second run died on npm refusing to republish 0.34.0 before it reached anything that could cut a tag.

**Nothing that named `master` followed the rename.** `Test` and `Go tests` trigger on `master`, so neither has run since — every PR against `main` shows no checks at all. `make publish` pushes to `master` too, which fails *after* the bump, commit and both tags are already made locally.

**`docs/` renders as a site that links out of itself.** GitHub Pages builds `docs/` as the site root at [jostraca.github.io/jostraca](https://jostraca.github.io/jostraca/), so `../ts/`, `../go/`, `../test/spec/` and `../CLAUDE.md` resolve above the root and 404 there — while working perfectly in the blob view, which is why the repo's own link checker never saw them.

## What changed

**`publish.yml` now ends where a release ends.** Four jobs, in that order:

| job | does |
|---|---|
| `version` | resolves the version from the tag or the dispatch input; requires `ts/package.json` to declare it, and *reads* `go/jostraca.go` to decide whether this is a joint release or npm-only |
| `go` | `go build`, `go vet`, `go test` — this run is the only gate before `go get` can serve a new tag |
| `npm` | install, build, test, publish — after `go`, so nothing irreversible happens while a gate can still fail |
| `tag` | cuts `v$V` (and `go/v$V` on a joint release) at the tested commit, makes the Go release page, warms proxy.golang.org |

Every step skips work already done, so an interrupted release is finished by running it again rather than by unpicking tags — but a skip is never an unchecked assumption. An existing tag must peel to the commit this run tested, and a version already on the registry must carry a `gitHead` naming that same commit; otherwise the run stops rather than tagging a tree npm never published.

Which stacks ship is read from the tree, not asked for: `make publish` bumps both files, so Go gets its tag; `make publish-ts` deliberately leaves the Go const behind, so that path publishes npm alone and cuts no Go tag.

Splitting the job also takes the repo-write token out of the jobs that run project code: `tag` holds `contents: write` and runs nothing but git, gh and curl; the job holding the npm id-token keeps `contents: read`. The filename stays `publish.yml` — npm's trusted publishing is pinned to it.

**CI and the release push point at `main`**, named once in `RELEASE_BRANCH`. README links move to `blob/HEAD/`, GitHub's name for the default branch whatever it is called next; ten of them were in `ts/README.md`, which is what npm renders on the package page.

**`docs/`** gets a `_config.yml` (its own title and description instead of the repo name, and the theme it is already rendered with) and absolute `blob/HEAD` / `tree/HEAD` links for the five that climbed out of the site root. Links between doc pages stay relative — `jekyll-relative-links` rewrites those and the docs suite checks each one resolves.

**`.claude/settings.local.json` is gone and ignored** — one machine's tool permissions, carrying local `/Users/richard/…` paths in a public repo. `CLAUDE.md` stays; it is the contributor guide and the README links to it.

**`release v0.34.1`** bumps both stacks. The two `.d.ts` lines are the committed build catching up with `shape@11`, which adds `jsonSchema()` to the type these declarations inline.

## Review round

The Codex review raised four ways the run could still release something other than what it tested; all four were real and are fixed in `99e13c3` — the `npm`/`go` race, the npm-only path being rejected outright, an existing tag accepted wherever it pointed, and a published version matched on its number alone. Each gate was simulated against the live registry and remote before the fix was pushed.

## Testing

- `cd ts && npm run build && npm test` — 455 pass, 0 fail (includes the docs suite: executed snippets, style gate, link resolution)
- `cd go && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... -count=1` — ok
- `make -n publish V=…` and `make -n publish-go V=…` — recipes expand to `git push origin main …`
- Workflow gates simulated against the real remote and registry: missing tag cuts, matching tag skips, mismatched tag stops; unpublished version publishes, same-commit re-run skips, different-commit re-run stops; joint / npm-only / unreadable-const version detection each hit their branch

After this lands, dispatching `Publish` with `0.34.1` should end with npm at 0.34.1, tags `v0.34.1` and `go/v0.34.1`, a `go/v0.34.1` release page, and `go get github.com/jostraca/jostraca/go@v0.34.1` working.

author: jonahgabriel
body:
## OMN-17502 — a Bifrost lane can now declare a cloud execution locale

Fixes the omnibase_infra half of OMN-17502 per the operator ruling of 2026-09-01 (option 2). The onex-dev cluster lane is cloud-only by the beta's axiom 9 (cloud execution locale, BYOK). Until now the typed lane overlay could not say that: `ModelBifrostLaneOverlay` required **exactly** the three authorized lab backends, so the only schema-valid overlay for onex-dev was another lane's `.201`/`.200` bindings — endpoints that are refused from inside the namespace. When the fail-closed OMN-17150 renderer (#3120) reached that lane in the released `candidate-3a29fd2` image, the lane had no legal overlay at all and `omninode-runtime`, `-effects`, `-worker` went to CrashLoopBackOff.

### Design (three sentences)

An overlay now declares an execution **locale**: `lab` keeps today's exact-set, pinned-binding rules unchanged, and `cloud` declares zero local backends — an empty `backends` mapping *plus* the explicit `locale` field, so the absence is a stated fact and not a fallthrough (there is no default; any other combination is rejected naming the lane and the rule). For a cloud overlay the renderer emits the base contract's cloud backends and explicitly disables every local backend (`endpoint_url: null`, the shape omnimarket's `_load_bifrost_endpoints` skips) while keeping those ids **declared**, because `load_bifrost_delegation_config` (OMN-15628) refuses a contract whose `routing_rules`/`default_backends` name an id it does not declare and the base contract's `code_generation` rule names `local-coder`. `docker/lane-overlays/onex-dev.bifrost.yaml` is that overlay; the render stays fail-closed when `BIFROST_LANE_OVERLAY_PATH` is unbound, so OMN-17150 is not relaxed.

### What is NOT in this PR

* The omninode_infra k8s manifest half (binding `BIFROST_LANE_OVERLAY_PATH` + the mount that provides this file, AC-1/AC-2) — separate repo, separate PR, and it needs an omnibase_infra release + runtime repin off this version to take effect.
* AC-3 (`omnimarket-projection-api`'s missing topic) — the runtime provisions `onex.snapshot.projection.consumer-flow.v1` at boot (OMN-15832); it is the crash-loop that prevents it. Unblocking the boot is the fix; if it does not provision, that is a new finding with new evidence.

### Corrected false claim (item 4 of the brief)

`tests/ci/test_env_parity.py` justified shipping OMN-17150 without its cluster half with: *"the render itself only runs where BIFROST_CONTRACT_PATH is bound, so the pin travels with these knobs as one debt item — the cluster binding lands together with BIFROST_CONTRACT_PATH's or not at all."* That was already false. `BIFROST_CONTRACT_PATH` has been bound **non-empty inline on all three onex-dev runtime Deployments** since omninode_infra#792 (OMN-15628, 2026-08-01), a month earlier — so the cluster does render, the two halves did not travel together, and OMN-17502 is the consequence. This PR removes `BIFROST_CONTRACT_PATH` from `CONFIGMAP_DEBT_KEYS` (it is on the k8s runtime-family surface, so listing it as debt was itself a false claim) and adds `test_bifrost_render_knobs_are_classified_by_live_cluster_state`, which holds the true invariant mechanically: `BIFROST_CONTRACT_PATH` must be on that surface, and `BIFROST_LANE_OVERLAY_PATH` is either bound there **xor** recorded as debt — so the allowlist entry cannot outlive the gap it describes.

### Schema version bump (v2 -> v3) and the cross-repo consequence

`locale` is required with no default, so a v2 file is not a v3 file. The version is bumped rather than made permissive so an image/overlay skew in either direction fails naming the schema version instead of failing on a field whose absence used to be legal. omnimarket's OMN-15628 seam test constructs a v2 overlay; its lock pins `omnibase-infra==0.38.15`, so it updates when omnimarket repins — flagged here so the repin is not surprised.

Project version `0.38.17 -> 0.38.18`: `0.38.17` already built the released `candidate-3a29fd2` image, so shipping this change under the same version would alias two code states — exactly what the release-identity gate exists to prevent (the gate itself compares against published tags and would have passed at `.17`). Runner image identity lock refreshed with it.

### Evidence (dod_evidence)

**Cross-repo seam, proven live before landing** — renderer under test (this branch) + real omnimarket loader/reducer (`omnimarket==0.4.15`, the version the released image carries), rendering from the packaged omnimarket base contract:

```
--- cloud (onex-dev.bifrost.yaml) ---
  resolved backend ids: ['cloud-gemini-flash', 'cloud-gemini-pro', 'cloud-glm',
                         'cloud-glm-judge', 'openrouter-glm-flash', 'openrouter-qwen3-coder-480b']
  local rungs resolvable: []
  first_eligible_tier('code_generation'): cheap_cloud
  local endpoint_url values: {'local-coder': None, 'local-ds-v4-flash': None, 'local-heavy-reasoning': None}
  declared ids count: 11
  routing_rules backend refs resolvable: True
--- lab (dev.bifrost.yaml)  [control] ---
  local rungs resolvable: ['local-coder', 'local-ds-v4-flash', 'local-heavy-reasoning']
  first_eligible_tier('code_generation'): local
```

The contract **loads** through `load_bifrost_delegation_config` and **routes to cloud** with no local rung resolvable; the lab control proves the result is the overlay's doing. The executable form of this test belongs in omnimarket next to its OMN-15628 sibling (omnimarket depends on omnibase_infra, not the reverse, and this repo's venv-purity gate OMN-15620 refuses an omnimarket install into the test venv); it lands there at the next repin. The properties that proof depends on are held here by unit tests read out of the consumer, not assumed.

**Local gates (this branch, `52df0ff3b`)**

* `uv run ruff format src/ tests/` + `uv run ruff check src/ tests/` — All checks passed
* `uv run mypy src/ --strict` — Success: no issues found in 2926 source files
* `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` — 105 hooks, zero failures
* `uv run pytest tests/unit/runtime/ tests/ci/test_bifrost_lane_overlay.py tests/ci/test_env_parity.py tests/unit/models/test_model_serialization_roundtrip.py` — **5754 passed, 5 skipped**
* `scripts/ci/validate_runner_image.py` — `[PASS] image_identity` after regeneration

**Tests added (RED first — the model/enum did not exist when they were written)**

* model: cloud accepted; lab-with-a-missing-backend rejected naming lane + rule; cloud-listing-a-backend rejected naming lane + rule; lab-with-zero-backends rejected; `locale` required with no default; v2 rejected as not-v3.
* renderer: cloud render disables every local backend and keeps the cloud endpoint; local ids stay declared so every routing rule still resolves; cloud render with no cloud endpoint fails closed; a cloud lane with no `BIFROST_LANE_OVERLAY_PATH` still fails naming the lane.
* CI gates: `onex-dev.bifrost.yaml` is cloud with zero backends and contains no lab endpoint or backend id anywhere in the file; every committed overlay states an explicit locale; the lab overlays declare `locale: lab` + the exact active set.

Ticket: OMN-17502 (see also OMN-17150, OMN-15628).

## Summary

Closes #1731. Refs #1801 — **not closed here**, see below.

`ALP_SOC_NPU_ARENA_SRAM_KIB` is `0` on all nine SoCs, so the NPU-envelope check that consumes it was **dead**: it passed everything. A gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate, because its green is read as evidence.

No arena sizes were invented. Where a real per-SoC figure could not be sourced from a document we hold, that is stated and the dead check is made **loud** rather than left silently passing.

## #1801 belongs to #1470, not to this branch

The first pass added `metadata/schemas/npu-ops-v1.schema.json` here. Review caught that this is **not new work**: it is open PR #1470's schema, differing by two whitespace-only hunks, and #1470 has carried it since 2026-08-15 — before this branch was cut. I confirmed #1470 is still open.

Landing it here would have duplicated an open PR and created a second source for one schema. The schema is removed from this branch entirely; **#1801 should be closed against #1470**.

## Process

Authored on an isolated worktree branch, independently reviewed by a separate
agent running this repo's gates, then the reviewer's confirmed findings fixed in
follow-up commits. Findings that could be refuted with evidence were reported and
left alone rather than "fixed".

Not bench-tested: nothing here touches silicon behaviour.

author: scholtz
body:
## Summary

Addresses #823 (partially — theme 1's execution-level tests; the other 4 themes and theme 1's assembler-level sub-items remain open).

Phase 17's audit flagged the `match` opcode (v8, 0x8e) as having zero execution-level tests. Writing them (ported from go-algorand's `TestMatch`/`TestShortMatch`) exposed a real, previously-undetected bug.

## The bug

`op_match` popped its `n` case values **before** the match target — the reverse of go's actual stack effect (`"[A1, A2, ..., AN], B" -> ""`, target `B` on top, popped first). This meant `match` always compared the target against the wrong case index, silently selecting the wrong branch (or the right one only by coincidence) for any group of 2+ case values. Undetected until now because the opcode had zero test coverage at all.

## Fix

Pop the target first (matches go's `opMatch`, `eval.go:3041-3080`: `last := len(cx.Stack)-1; matchVal := cx.Stack[last]` before slicing off the n-element `matchList`), then pop the n case values.

## Also found: a second, unrelated bug

While porting go's tests (which use `;` as a statement separator, e.g. `zero: int 1; return`), I found that algod-rust's assembler treats `;` as a **comment delimiter** instead — silently discarding everything after it on a line, including real instructions. go-algorand's assembler treats `;` as a genuine statement separator. Filed as **#847**; this PR's tests are written one-statement-per-line to avoid that gap while it's unfixed.

## Testing

- TDD: `match_takes_zeroth_label_with_int_cases`/`_bytes_cases` and `match_takes_first_label_with_int_cases`/`_bytes_cases` were written first against go's `TestMatch` semantics and confirmed failing (4/6) against the old pop order.
- `match_falls_through_when_no_case_matches`, `match_with_single_case`, `match_truncated_program_is_rejected` (ported from `TestShortMatch`) round out coverage.
- Full `algo-avm` suite passes; `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy -p algo-avm --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p algo-avm` — all green (7/7 new tests, 0 regressions)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p algo-avm --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` — clean
- [x] Follow-up issue #847 filed for the semicolon-parsing bug; #823's acceptance criteria updated

author: nvuillam
body:
Combines two Renovate PRs that can only be merged together, and prevents the split from happening again.

## Updates

| Package | Change | Renovate PR |
|---|---|---|
| npm-package-json-lint | `10.5.1` → `11.0.0` | #8746 |
| npm-package-json-lint-config-default | `9.0.1` → `10.0.0` | #8790 |

`npm-package-json-lint-config-default` v10 is a major bump whose only content is "Update to npm-package-json-lint v11", so neither PR can be merged on its own.

Breaking change in npm-package-json-lint v11: the `--allowEmptyTargets` CLI option was removed, and behavior changed when no targets are provided. The `JSON_NPM_PACKAGE_JSON_LINT` descriptor never used that option and always passes `.` as target (`cli_lint_mode_project_extra_args_after`), so no descriptor change is needed.

## Renovate grouping

Added a `npm-package-json-lint` group in `renovate.json5` so both packages are raised in a single PR from now on.

Dependabot is not involved here: these two packages are pinned in `megalinter/descriptors/json.megalinter-descriptor.yml` and only tracked by the Renovate custom manager. Dependabot's npm scope in this repo is `/mega-linter-runner` and the test fixtures.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## What was broken

`POST /api/v1/23/home-remedies` returned **HTTP 500** for any complaint outside the six indexed keywords — e.g. `"sore throat"`, an empty string, or a client sending `symptom` instead of `complaint`:

```
POST /api/v1/23/home-remedies  {"complaint": "sore throat", "language": "bn"}
→ 500 {"success": false, "node": 0, "node_name": "gateway",
       "data": {"error": "Internal error; safe fallback — refer to physician.", ...}}
```

**Root cause:** Node 23's no-match path returned `risk_level: "unknown"`, which `AuraMedResponse.risk_level` (a `red|yellow|green` enum) rejects. The Pydantic `ValidationError` bubbled into the gateway's global handler, so the patient lost the *"no verified entry, consult a clinician"* answer the node had already produced.

## What changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `backend/core/schemas.py` | New `coerce_risk_level()` + `field_validator` on `AuraMedResponse.risk_level`: an off-contract node label degrades to `null` instead of failing the mandatory envelope. `ok()` echoes the dropped label as a `{"risk_level_unmapped": ...}` alert, so nothing is swallowed silently. |
| `backend/nodes/node_23_remedies/engine.py` | No-match path returns `risk_level: null` + `escalate_to_clinician: true` (never invents GREEN); accepts `symptom` as an alias for `complaint`; red-flag path now also sets `seek_emergency_care: true`. |
| `backend/api/edge_feedback.py` | Withheld home care is explicit: `{"home_care_withheld": true, "reason": "red_flag" \| "no_verified_entry"}`. |
| `backend/main.py` | `/health` now carries the disclaimer in the body too — the README promises the disclaimer on *every* response body; it was only in the header here. Caught by the new suite. |
| `tests/` | New **whole-gateway contract suite** walks all 31 OpenAPI routes asserting no 5xx, disclaimer in header **and** body, and an on-contract `risk_level`; plus Node 23 regression tests and envelope unit tests. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI runs the suite on Python 3.11 + 3.12 and verifies all 26 nodes stay routable. |
| docs | `docs/api-gateway.md` conventions + README test count / CI badge. |

## Verification

```
$ python -m pytest -q
131 passed, 1 warning in 0.76s        # was 38 passed
```

Regression proven against the pre-fix code (fix stashed, same request):

```
=== OLD code ===  status: 500 | {"success": false, "node": 0, "node_name": "gateway", ...}
=== NEW code ===  status: 200 | {"success": true, "node": 23, "risk_level": null,
                                 "data": {"served": false, "escalate_to_clinician": true, ...}}
```

CI's routing check locally: `OK - all 26 nodes routable across 31 OpenAPI paths`.

**GitHub Actions on this PR:** `pytest · Python 3.11` ✅ pass (14s) · `pytest · Python 3.12` ✅ pass (20s) — [run 33566097864](https://github.com/BFH-HAMID/AuraMed-Ai-Powered-Medical-Assistant/actions/runs/33566097864). (The local sandbox only has Python 3.11, so the 3.12 leg was verified by the workflow itself.)

## Safety contract

No triage semantics changed: RED still wins, the hard red-flag refusal in Node 23 still returns `risk_level: "red"`, and the disclaimer remains on every header and body. The only behavioural change is that a *missing* risk assessment is now reported as `null` + an explicit escalation flag rather than crashing the request.

## Summary
- removes automatic fullscreen entry when scoring starts, preventing Chrome's persistent fullscreen instructional banner during normal scoring
- attempts a best-effort landscape orientation lock only while the live scoreboard is active
- unlocks orientation again when leaving the scoreboard
- keeps the fullscreen button manual; when used, LoveAll retries landscape lock after fullscreen succeeds

- starts point haptic feedback on pointer contact for lower perceived latency, while preserving the stronger game-win haptic
- removes the haptic capability/diagnostic toast from the scoring path
- adds a small isolated scoring-layout stylesheet instead of expanding the main stylesheet
- bumps the service-worker cache and precaches the new scoring stylesheet so installed PWAs receive the update reliably
- adds regression coverage for manual fullscreen, landscape lock/unlock, pointer-down haptics, and center-divider swap placement

## Scope
No changes to badminton scoring rules, match history, persistence, setup, install flow, or game continuation logic. No new runtime dependencies.

body:
## Summary

Reconciles the next four source-ordered packages in `.github/plugins/azure-sdk-python/skills/` at Microsoft Skills pin `32cad4ee689c95c309e61aeefcbc6af356f1e6a7` while preserving individual exact-version evidence and complete-package review.

- `azure-ai-translation-text-py` — rejected unchanged, 13/20
- `azure-ai-vision-imageanalysis-py` — rejected unchanged, 12/20
- `azure-ai-voicelive-py` — rejected unchanged, 9/20; complete review includes bundled API/examples/models references
- `azure-appconfiguration-py` — rejected unchanged, 12/20

The batch reduces repeated repository bookkeeping without applying a family-level verdict. Each skill retains its own package-tree and `SKILL.md` identity, source-path freshness, dependencies, authority, portability, controlled tags, decisive state, rationale, and explicit `validation_status: not-run`.

The Voice Live package received deeper review because its bundled references add live audio/transcription, function/MCP tool calls, conversation mutation, synthesized voice/avatar output, and additional privacy/authority boundaries.

## Accounting after merge

- persisted third-party exact-version reviews: **244**
- Microsoft Skills companions: **72/189**
- Microsoft Skills gaps: **117**
- direct Python plugin slice: **13/40 complete**

README, System State, CURATION_QUEUE, INDEX and index.json are reconciled together. No repository runtime, CI, tests, generator, scanner, scheduler, monitor, or other active machinery is introduced.

author: roseoutllc
body: Adds a lightweight production probe workflow so AWS background-runtime verification no longer requires rebuilding the full Next.js image. It checks the deployed Lambda state, probes `location-search-profile-worker` and `search-phase13-maintenance` through the scheduler invoker, retries transient Lambda concurrency throttles, and prints only a sanitized response summary on failure. No scheduler state or database state is changed.
